# Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

July 1, 1972

President Park Chung-hee (朴正熙)


--- (p. 6) ---

*   The spirit of diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperation (協同) of the Saemaul Undong is a resource for national development (國家發展) that we cannot buy even with billions of dollars, and it is the most precious heritage (遺産) to be passed down to future generations (後孫).
*   I am confident that all the numerous meeting minutes (會議録), account books (帳簿), various statistics (統計表), and development plans (開發計劃) placed in the community centers (會舘) across the nation (全國) are clear evidence of the development of democracy (民主主義) in our country and will be a history (歷史) to be passed down to future generations (後孫).

— From the address at the 1977. 12. 9 National (全國) Saemaul Leaders (指導者) Conference (大會) —

# Saemaul Song

With vigor and cheerfulness

1. The morning bell has rung, dawn is breaking
   Everyone, let's rise and build our new village
2. Repairing thatched roofs, widening streams
   Everyone, let's sweat and build our new village
3. Helping each other, working together to achieve a bountiful harvest
   Everyone, let's unite our strength and build our new village
4. All of us joining forces to achieve the modernization of our nation
   Let's make our beautiful new country shine forever

## 〈Refrain〉
A village where we live well
Let's create it with our own strength

## Lyrics

With vigor

1. The vital energy of Mount Baekdu (白頭) protects this land
2. As the clear morning sun rises over the East Sea (東海)
3. The spirit of the Hwarang (花郞) who achieved the unification of the Three Kingdoms

The lofty spirit of Mount Hallasan (漢拏) has guarded our people
The towering Jukangsan, passing on the radiant fatherland (祖國)
Today, we inherit it with new hearts and spirits

The eternal Mugunghwa (無窮花) blooms, our history (歷史) that is as old as time
The shining cultural heritage (文化遺産) born of our people's sweat and toil
Let us create a new history (歷史) of glory (榮光) for our new fatherland (祖國)

Our wise people have lived through the modern era (近世紀)
With all our sincerity (精誠) from the Imjin (壬辰) era, let us preserve this path forever
Let us call out for a brilliant (燦爛) renewal (維新) that will last for all eternity (萬古)

# Stele Erected on Dotjae Road

## The Spirit of Saemaul

We, the residents of Hancheon-myeon (漢川面民), have endured countless hardships and immense inconveniences due to the rugged Dotjae Pass. With the spirit of Saemaul—self-reliance (自主), cooperation (協同), and community (郡民)—we have taken pride (矜持) in widening this road. Our aim is to shine a bright light from generation to generation (世世), perpetuating the spirit of Saemaul for eternity.

President Park Chung-hee (大統領) bestowed upon us a generous donation (下賜金), and Governor Kwang of Gyeongsangbuk-do personally visited the site to offer words of encouragement and a motivational grant (激勵金). We, the residents of Hancheon-myeon, express our deepest gratitude to all who have supported us. With these nine unwavering aspirations (意志), we will forever uphold this glorious monument (金字塔) and inscribe this pledge on a commemorative stele (記念碑) marking the opening of Dotjae Road.

September 30, 1977
The Residents of Balcheon-myeon

![A panoramic view of the road construction site. People are cutting through the mountain and clearing a path to build Dotjae Road.](/images/page_1_img_1.png)

Cutting through a 350m stretch of Cheonwonsan Ridge and constructing a 6km road. The age-old dream of not having to detour 42km to cover a straight 6km distance has finally been realized.

Under the scorching 37°C heat, residents carved through rock formations and filled in valleys, with 45,000 people mobilized annually.

![Residents of Hancheon-myeon working under the sweltering 37°C heat, cutting through rock formations and filling in valleys. They are using manual tools like pickaxes and shovels to build the road.](/images/page_1_img_2.png)

# Foreword

![Image: Portrait](/images/page_1_img_1.png)

Amidst backwardness, poverty, and despair, our people have a hidden history of shedding the 5,000-year-old shackles of poverty and building a land of abundance and hope. This is the history of modernization, where our parents, brothers, and sisters stood up with the banners of self-help, self-reliance, and cooperation in remote mountain villages, along the crashing seashores, and in towns and fields.

Truly, the 1970s were the decade of Saemaul, the decade of national revival, the decade of totality, and the decade of modernization.

Through seven years of the Saemaul Undong, our farmers achieved many accomplishments. They constructed 2.4 km of village roads per village, completed 46 large and small bridges per township, and finished a total of 7,845,000 projects. For these endeavors, tens of thousands of pyeong of fertile land was donated, numerous rural houses and walls were demolished and rebuilt, and our rural areas underwent a great transformation unprecedented in history.

This was made possible by the dedicated efforts of Saemaul leaders, who, without any compensation, tirelessly worked for their villages, regions, and the nation, and by the residents who, moved by their leaders' devotion, gathered in village halls, leaders' homes, or early morning fields and alleys to discuss and deliberate on village affairs. They worked together, making compromises and finding common ground, ultimately achieving these results through cooperation and effort.


--- (p. 24) ---

One village has, over the past 7 years, held over 200 meetings with the participation of all residents, holding at least 2 meetings per month. They successfully completed 147 projects.

This is the true practice of democracy and a testament to the democratic spirit of compromise and understanding taking root in our rural communities, leading to the establishment of excellent democratic practices.

In this way, we have compiled the first volume of "Footsteps of Glory" based on the meeting records kept in each village, documenting the progress of the Saemaul Undong at the village level. However, please note that the villages included in this volume are not necessarily the most outstanding ones. We plan to continue uncovering and publishing more exemplary cases in future volumes.

This historical record aims to preserve the living footsteps of our parents, siblings, and fellow villagers who have walked the path of the Saemaul Undong.

This book will not only make our descendants aware of the development of Korean democracy, which has grown from the grassroots alongside our villages, hometowns, and ancestors, but also instill in them our beautiful national spirit of loyalty to the country, filial piety to parents, and neighborly love. Simultaneously, we believe this book will serve as an opportunity for us to discover new courage, self-confidence, and a renewed sense of determination.

January 1, 1978
Minister of Interior, Park Chi-yeol

# Jeollanam-do (全南) Hwasun County (和順郡) Hancheon-myeon (寒泉面) Dotjae Road (道路) Construction (開設)

### 1. Village Overview (槪況)

#### a. History (沿革)

Hancheon-myeon (寒泉面) was originally named Geumo-myeon (金鰲面), derived from the alias Geumosan (金鰲山) of Yongamsan (聳岩山), a famous mountain in the original village. In the 15th year of King Injo's reign (仁祖 15年), it was renamed Hancheonnae-myeon (寒泉嶺內面) and Hancheonwae-myeon (寒泉嶺外面). In the year 4246 of the Dangi calendar (檀紀 4246年, corresponding to the 3rd year of the Taisho era, 大正 3年), the administrative districts were merged, and the two villages were combined to form Hancheon-myeon (寒泉面), which remains to this day. The current administrative district consists of 11 ri (個里) with 20 natural villages (自然部落).

#### b. Location (位置) and Conditions (與件)

**〈Location (位置)〉**
Geographically, Hancheon-myeon is located about 12 km south of Hwasun-eup (和順邑) along the national road from Gwangju (光州) to Goheung (高興). From Hwasun-eup, it is approximately 21 km west along a local road. The village is situated with Yongamsan, part of the Noryeong mountain range, as its backdrop. It borders Nam-myeon (南面) to the east, Chunyang-myeon (春陽面) to the south, Neungju-myeon (綾州面) to the west, and Hwasun-eup (和順邑) to the north, making it a mountainous village centrally located within Hwasun-eup.

**〈Conditions (與件)〉**
Although Hancheon-myeon is a backward village (落後面) with many mountains and limited arable land, it is rich in coal resources, producing an average of 23,000 tons of coal per month. The village is developing through agricultural income from pig farming, Hanwoo (Korean cattle), beekeeping, and other non-agricultural sources.
The village is divided by Dotjae, a 350-meter-high ridge of Cheonunsan in the center, creating distinct living areas, administrative districts, and ceremonial zones for the inner and outer regions. The inner region, where the village office is located, consists of 6 ri and 12 natural villages (1,124 households, 5,614 people), while the outer region has 5 ri and 8 natural villages (412 households, 2,350 people). The area ratio is 51:49, and the population ratio is 70:30 between the inner and outer regions. Due to these geographical peculiarities, residents of the outer region, while administratively part of Hancheon-myeon (寒泉面), have their living and ceremonial ties with neighboring Nam-myeon, leading to various vulnerabilities in administrative guidance and village unity.

## 2. Village Development Process (發展過程)

### A. Situation Before 1970 (70年 以前)

#### 1) Basic Environment (基礎環境)

- The rural (農村) structure consisted of thatched-roof houses (草家) with pillars like walking sticks and flowing rotten water, which accounted for 90%. In mining villages (鑛山村), there were no pillars, just clusters of houses. The village paths followed small streams (細川) and were winding. Fences made of rice straw or reeds would smell rotten when it rained, staining the collars of people's clothes.
- There were no farm roads (農路), not even roads leading into the village. Residents inside the mountain (嶺內) had to walk about 8 km to take a bus to Yeongju (綾州), and residents outside the mountain (嶺外) had to walk up to 10 km to neighboring Nam-myeon (南面). Especially on market days (市場日), which occurred every five days (5日), residents had to carry market goods on their backs and walk to Yeongju Market (綾州市場) or Nam-myeon Market (南面市場), facing considerable inconvenience.

#### 2) Income Level (所得水準)

- The farmland (農地) inherited from ancestors was 0.6ha per household (戶當), but due to the highland (高嶺) terrain, it was difficult to produce even 2 seok (石) per nyang (反) in an unscientific (非科學) manner.


--- (p. 36) ---

Farming was subsistence-level, barley was barely cultivated, and double-cropping was mostly limited to planting potatoes in spring. The cattle breeding business (韓牛增殖事業) and chili and tobacco farming through slash-and-burn agriculture (火田), selling firewood, and earning low wages at small mines were the only sources of income. The average annual income per resident was 250,000 won.

### 3) Mental State (精神狀態)
Living in poverty and ignorance, people had no aspirations to improve their lives, lacked unity, and were filled with laziness and envy. They lived day by day without hope for the future or a pioneering spirit, showing indifference and apathy.

### 4) Cultural Life (文化生活)
* Living under the dim light of oil lamps, residents could only read newspapers at government offices. The only news source was hearing weather forecasts from a radio in a neighboring village.
* In winter, wearing cotton pants, jackets, and blankets was considered luxurious. In summer, they wore hemp clothing. During the spring famine (春窮期), many had to sell firewood in neighboring areas like Yeongju (綾州) and Nammyeonjang (南面場) to buy food.
* Residents used traditional outhouses that were indistinguishable from manure pits. Despite being bitten by mosquitoes and fleas, they rested anywhere without shame or sadness, accepting their fate as if it were destiny.

### B. The Launch of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

#### 1) Motivation (動機) and Experimental Project (試驗事業) Results
* In the fiscal year 1971, experimental projects such as village community businesses were implemented but resulted in shoddy construction due to a lack of technology and resident cooperation. However, these projects instilled a sense of confidence in the residents that they could accomplish even small tasks if they worked together.
* Starting from the fiscal year 1972, the movement was fully launched, leading to today's achievements. The spring famine (春窮期) has long disappeared, thatched-roof houses have been replaced with tiled or slate-roofed ones, oil lamps have been replaced with electric lights, shoulder poles have been replaced with carts or tractors (耕耘機), and hemp clothing has been replaced with nylon or wool. Residents who previously had no access to news now receive it through television, and education levels have improved.


--- (p. 37) ---

Even the remote areas have changed so much that almost all middle and high school students attend school.

* Just 10 years ago, areas that required walking to the market now have buses running through each village. Just 5 years ago, our region, where farming was impossible without oxen, has now entered a mechanical age where farming is done with cultivators. Just 3 years ago, farmers were competing to harvest "six bushels" per paddy, but now they surpass "seven bushels," showcasing a new image of agricultural life. However, to achieve the early goal of 1.4 million won per household, the obstacle of Dotjae has been a hindrance to regional development. The residents of Hancheon-myeon, with their long-cherished dream of opening the Dotjae Road, have demonstrated the power of the Saemaul Undong, relying solely on the residents' determination of "We can do it" without technology, materials, or money. Through the Saemaul cooperative project, they have turned yesterday's obstacle into today's production road, directly linking it to household income and laying the foundation for exceeding the goal of 1.4 million won per household.

* Due to the obstacle of Dotjae, which is a 350m highland, residents outside the ridge had to walk 6km over a steep ridge to visit the town, and if they used vehicles, they had to detour through four towns and villages, covering a total of 42km. In 1966, an outpost was established outside the ridge to convenience the residents, but there are still vulnerabilities in agricultural business, postal services, rural guidance, transportation, and other related guidance work. Moreover, there is a lack of cooperation and differing opinions among residents inside and outside the ridge, hindering the unification of the town's opinion and significantly impeding town development. It was felt that the urgent task was to break through this steep Dotjae to promote regional development and achieve the total harmony of the town's residents.

* Everyone thought that Dotjae should be opened by someone's effort at some point. However, this long-cherished wish, which had been around for hundreds of years, required too much time to mature and be put into practice.

* On January 13, 1973, Jo Gyu-seon, who was then a delegate of the National Unification Democratic Congress, proposed that Gu Jae-u, then the town's head, consult with various agencies and prominent figures in the town to form the Dotjae Road Opening Promotion Committee. They submitted petitions and proposals to central and local authorities on behalf of the townspeople, but their efforts were in vain, and the collective opinion of the residents was dashed.

* After several attempts, it was the end of 1975. At that time, as part of the Saemaul Undong, Kim Jung-jin, the town's head, proposed to open the Dotjae Road through the Saemaul cooperative project. The Dotjae Road Opening Promotion Committee was reorganized, and a request was made to the county (County Magistrate Moon Byeong-u) to handle it as a pending county project. A reply was received that the request would be accepted, which made not only the promotion committee but all the townspeople overjoyed.

* On February 18, 1976, seizing this rare opportunity, the townspeople gathered for a town meeting. County Magistrate Moon Byeong-u mentioned President (大統領) Park Chung-hee's words, "We can do it," and proposed and encouraged turning this project into a Saemaul cooperative project, starting with making a path that people can walk on with the residents' efforts. With renewed strength, the townspeople firmly resolved to accomplish the task.

* Thus, the promotion committee members visited the Advanced Saemaul Model Site and sought advice from experts from various fields and strata.


--- (p. 38) ---

After consulting with experts, the initial preparations including route surveying and other tasks took about three months. Starting from May 14, 1976, approximately 6,500 participants, including 520 local residents and reservists, engaged in clearing the survey area, constructing a new road (excluding cliff areas) that was 2 meters wide and 2.5 kilometers long, and other groundwork for about two weeks.

- Subsequently, as the work continued, on January 19, 1977, the government recognized the determination and efforts of the local residents, as well as the necessity of the project, and selected it as an IBRD loan project, advancing it as a rural road construction project. However, due to the extremely rugged terrain with steep slopes and rocky areas, numerous obstacles were encountered.

- Despite these challenges and difficulties, the united efforts of the residents, pouring with sweat and toil, gained widespread attention through various mass media. President (大統領) took notice and, through Governor (高建), provided special support funds of 38.2 million won and 6,435 bags of cement on May 7, 1977, for the construction of the Dojae Road. Governor (高建) expressed gratitude for the President's generosity and promised to allow bus traffic once the road was completed, as well as dispatching technicians. He encouraged connecting the industrial road to increasing the residents' income, which further motivated the residents to strengthen their resolve.

2) Overcoming Challenges (隘路克服狀況)

- Initially, the project aimed for completion by the end of October 1977, but it was decided to finish two months ahead of schedule. Despite the intense summer heat, all residents endured and pushed forward. They leveled the steep slopes, created drainage channels, and laid sod transported from 230 li away, even up to 15 meters high, using large wooden stakes. The difficulty of the work was immense, and during the scorching heat of July and August, with no rain, 90% of the 18,200 m² of sod they had laid withered and died, leaving them helpless and even resentful of the indifferent sky.

- However, when the awaited rain finally came, it suddenly turned into a downpour (177mm), causing momentary joy. Yet, the sod they had laid with sweat and the embankments they had built (10,000 m²) collapsed, tearing at their hearts.

- The residents began to lose heart, and their initial enthusiasm waned. Additionally, various pests and diseases plagued their main occupation, farming, causing significant expected damage, making it difficult to find workers. Even the heavy machinery deployed frequently broke down due to the harsh rock-cutting work, compounding the difficulties.

- To overcome these challenges, officials from the county and village, along with the promotion committee, worked tirelessly, but to no avail. At this critical moment, the chairman of the promotion committee, Munhakgu (文學九), revitalized the atmosphere with an impromptu speech, reigniting their courage.

- Thus, even in the sweltering heat reaching 37°C, they hurried to complete the project, working late into the night with torches. Village head Kim Jungjin (金仲珍) and promotion committee chairman Munhakgu (文學九), along with a few other leaders, camped under trees on the mountain for several days, working through the nights.

- With the renewed efforts for the Dojae Road construction project, residents who had gone away and other concerned county residents provided encouragement and comfort, injecting vitality into the project. Additionally, the county authorities supported the project by providing dump trucks from nearby areas.


--- (p. 39) ---

The military provided crucial assistance with various heavy machinery such as bulldozers, compactors, and payloaders.
- Finally, a 6-meter-wide, 6-kilometer-long road was built on the rugged 350-meter-high hill. Buses could now run, eliminating the inconvenience of walking on steep mountain paths or detouring 42 kilometers through four towns (townships and townships).
- Since the discussion on opening the Dotjae Road on January 13, 1973, it took four years and eight months. From the start of actual work on February 9 to the completion on September 30, a total of 45,000 people and a total construction cost of 164,887,245 won (support fund 106,118,000 won, resident's share 58,769,245 won) were invested. The long-awaited opening ceremony was held, marking a new milestone for the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement).

### 3) Effects of the Dotjae Road Opening

- With the opening of the Dotjae Road, 2,300 residents from five villages and eight natural hamlets outside the ridge no longer had to endure the hassle of walking over the rugged Dotjae pass of Cheonunsan's 350-meter-high ridge or taking three bus transfers to travel over 100 ri to obtain a single official document.
- Moreover, the smooth transportation of coal mined from many mining sites (鑛業所) inside the ridge was ensured, and residents outside the ridge could easily find jobs, creating an opportunity to increase non-agricultural income (農外所得).
- Through this project (事業), residents learned and realized many things. They experienced the ordinary lesson that "where there is a will, there is a way," felt the great power of cooperation (協同) and unity, and gained a proud sense of accomplishment in leaving a glorious legacy for future generations.
- Therefore, a stele was erected on the ridge of the Dotjae pass in the middle of Cheonunsan, inscribing the following "Will of the New Community (新村意志)".

### Will of the New Community (新村意志)

We, the residents of Hancheon-myeon (寒泉面民), who had suffered countless hardships and inconveniences due to the rugged Dotjae pass, united with the Saemaul spirit (新村精神) of diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperation (協同). We worked hard from early morning to late night, holding torches to open this road. President (大統領) Park Chung-hee (朴正熙) granted us a subsidy, and Governor (道知事) Ko Keon (高建) visited the site to encourage us. We, the residents of Hancheon-myeon (寒泉面民), sincerely express our gratitude to all who helped us. To commemorate this glory, built by the green will of the New Community (新村) of the entire face (面民), we erect this monument for the opening of the Dotjae Road (開設).

1977. 9. 30 Hancheon-myeon (寒泉面) residents

### 4) Encouragement and Support for the Saemaul Cooperative Circle (協同圈) Project (事業)

- While the promotion of long-cherished projects (宿願事業) is usually carried out as a public pledge (公約事業) of a particular individual, the Dotjae Road (道路) opening project (事業) was achieved through the united (總) rise (蹶起) of all residents (住民), embodying the will (意志) of the New Community (新村).
- In addition to the face (面) citizens' assembly (面民大會), over 1,200 participants in the work site (現場), including Congressman (國會議員) Moon Hyung-tae (文亨泰) from this face (本面) and Hwasun (和順) County Magistrate (郡守) Moon Byeong-woo (文炳宇), received consolation (慰勞), encouragement, and on-site guidance (現地指導) from the heads of various institutions (機關) and organizations (團體). Moreover, newspapers such as Jeonnam Daily (全南每日), Jeonnam Ilbo (全南日報), and broadcasters like MBC (文化放送) and Christian Broadcasting (基督教放送) vividly reported on the progress of the construction (工事). Furthermore, MBC-TV and KBS-TV also broadcasted the event.


--- (p. 40) ---

The O Governor Ko Keon (高建) of this province provided on-site guidance and the provincial forestry bureau chief provided on-site technical support. The residents, overflowing with joy, shouted "Manse" and pushed forward with the project after receiving a special gift of 38,200,000 won and 6,435 bags of cement from Governor Ko Keon on behalf of His Excellency the President (大統領).

The provincial and county authorities played a significant role in problem-solving and technical support.

5) Land, Cash, and In-Kind Donations

Residents who worked hard received warmth and comfort from various sectors beyond the land they trod. In addition, residents demolished their front yards and houses for the Saemaul cooperative circle project, and construction companies also donated large sums.

6) Heartwarming Stories

a) First Story

In September 1977, the military unit (CAC Command (司令部)) supported the Hancheon-myeon (寒泉面) Dotjae Saemaul cooperative circle project, which is located in a remote and vulnerable mountainous area, with 3 units (臺) of heavy machinery (loaders and compactors, bulldozers) for 22 days as a civic service project. This significantly reduced the residents' labor burden and enabled the completion of the project within the scheduled period. The residents of this area are sending words of praise to the military unit (軍部隊) for their gratitude.

b) Second Story

Mr. Kwon Taeyeong (權泰永), the president of a civil engineering subcontractor, was moved by the residents' unity and determination to push forward with the project despite limited budget and residents' burden, even in the scorching heat of 36°C. He donated 25,000,000 won for construction costs to reduce the residents' burden, which resulted in the smooth completion of the project by the expected date.

### Ba. Achievements through the Saemaul Movement (事業)

1. Spiritual Aspect (精神面)

    The barriers of Dotjae were broken, and the divided village opinions (面論) were unified (統一), establishing a comprehensive system (總和體制). The cooperative spirit (協同心) of the residents (住民) discovered that the philosophy of action (行動 哲學) is to live well, have the village live well, and have the country live well.

2. Livelihood Aspect (生活面)

    Due to Dotjae, people inside (嶺內) and outside (嶺外) the ridge became as close as if they were within the same fence, traveling by bus. This has been a great help in administration (行政) and production (生產).

3. Production Aspect (生產面)

    *   The 42km detour was shortened to 6km, saving bus fare and time (時間), indirectly (間接) increasing income (所得), and
    *   The employment rate (就業率) of people outside (嶺外民) the ridge in the mining (鑛業所) facilities inside (嶺內) the ridge is high, increasing wage (勞賃) income (所得), and
    *   The blocked road is now operated (運行) by bus, bringing lively (生氣) activities. The Dotjae road (道路) is directly (直結) connected to an industrial (產業) road (道路), bringing vitality (活氣) to income (所得) source (源) development (開發).

# 4. Future Development Plans (開發構想)

a. Attraction of Saemaul Factories (工場)

To utilize the idle labor force (遊休 勞動力) of 500 households (家口) in Gwangsan Village (鑛山村) and increase income (所得), attract Saemaul factories (工場)
Target items (對象 品目): socks, gloves, clothing (衣類), agricultural machinery (農機具), smokeless coal (無煙炭)

## Na. Establishment of Livestock Farms (畜產團地)
Utilize vast wild grasses (山野草) to establish livestock farms (畜產團地).

## Da. Establishment of Economic Forests (經濟林)
Renew the current tree species of mixed forests to economic forests (經濟林) such as Japanese cedar, Korean pine, Paulownia, and Zelkova, and expand income sources (所得源).

## Ra. Establishment of Cash Crops (經濟作物)
1. Cultivate medicinal herbs (生藥), persimmon, chestnut, and jujube trees, high-quality horticultural crops, and flowers to increase income (所得).
2. Establish mulberry trees (닥나무류), an export product, in roadside and idle lands to aim for foreign currency (外貨) acquisition (獲得).

## 1. Village Overview
- 6 villages (Gudam (九潭) 1, 2, Gisam (箕山) 2, Sincheong (申城) 1, 2, Guhodong (九湖洞))

### A. History
During the Joseon Dynasty (李朝), this area was divided between parts of Yonggung County (龍宮懸) and Andong County (安東懸). After the Japanese annexation (日帝), it became Pungseo-myeon (豊西面) of Andong County (安東郡), with the Pungseo-myeon office (豊西面) located in Yugjang (六場). In 1934, administrative districts were reorganized, and it became Pungcheon-myeon (豊川面) of Andong County (安東郡), a status that continues to this day. This region (6 villages) has long been centered around the Kwang-san (光山) and Suncheon (順天) Kim (金氏) clans, a region with strong feudalistic (封建思想) ideas, weak unity, and underdeveloped villages.

### B. Location and Conditions
#### <Location>
* Located 29 km west of the Andong County Office (安東郡廳), and southwest of Pungsan-eup (豊山邑) along the provincial road, passing the Pungcheon-myeon Office (豊川面事務所). The villages of Gudam 1 and 2 (九潭) in the northern part of the Nakdong River (洛東江) border Jibong-myeon (知保面) of Yecheon County (醴泉郡), while the villages of Gisam 2 (箕山), Sincheong 1 and 2 (申城), and Guhodong (九湖洞) in the southern part border Sinpyeong-myeon (新平面) of Uiseong County (義城郡).
* Geographic conditions of Pungcheon-myeon (豊川面)
  Taking the Nakdong River (洛東江) as the center, the northern part is called Gangbuk (江北) and the southern part is called Gangnam (江南). The conditions are as follows:

#### <Conditions>
* With the Nakdong River (洛東江) in the center, these 6 villages share similar settlement patterns (聚落形態), clan compositions (氏族構成), and lifestyles (生活風習). However, a 400m-wide river (江) flows east-west (東西), dividing farmland (農耕地) of over 100 jeong (町) even though they belong to the same administrative district (行政區域). This separation has caused inconveniences in farming (營農), as well as in transportation (交通) during floods (洪水時) or freezing periods (結氷期), affecting students' commuting (通學) and the transport of agricultural products (農產物) and other farming materials (農資材).

## 2. Village Development Process

### A. Situation Before the 1970s

#### 1) Basic Environment

* The six villages divided by the Nakdong River (洛東江), which flows through the center, were situated along a 400m wide riverbed, relying solely on an old wooden boat as their means of transportation, leading a stagnant life.
* People were primarily focused on securing food, with no thought given to environmental improvement. The village had crumpled thatched-roof houses with mud walls, makeshift outhouses surrounded by bamboo fences, and narrow village paths too tight for even handcarts to pass through.
* Traditionally, the village lacked even fences, except for a few ancestral homes and old houses. Most houses were typical thatched-roof mud structures. Additionally, the village faced the threat of water damage during the flood season, adding to the residents' sense of insecurity.

#### 2) Income Level

* The villagers relied on rice and wheat cultivation on ancestral farmland, with an average of 1.0ha of cultivated land per household. However, the annual average income per resident was 250,000 won, making these villages the lowest-income areas in the region.

#### 3) Living Conditions

##### A) Mental State

* Despite living in ignorance and poverty, the villagers lacked the ambition to improve their lives. The mutual antagonism between the Suncheon Kim (金) and Gwangsan Kim (金) clans, along with the presence of other surnames like Jeong (鄭), Kwon (權), and Yu (柳), weakened the village's unity. Residents spent their days in idleness, envy, drinking, and gambling.
* Bound by rigid feudal ideologies, the villagers lacked hope for the future or a pioneering spirit. They lived in apathy and complacency.

##### B) Culture and Daily Life (Clothing, Food, Shelter)

* Electricity was unheard of; villagers lived by the light of pinewood torches or oil lamps. The old mud houses combined kitchens, barns, and chicken coops, resembling livestock dwellings. There were no public facilities, and children had to cross the river and walk 4km to attend the nearest elementary school in the town center.
* Parents, struggling to make ends meet, paid little attention to their children's education. It was common for schools to close during the summer flood season or winter freezing period. Moreover, the drowning of one or two students annually while crossing the river was accepted as an inevitable fate by the riverside residents.
* Without hospitals or even pharmacies, villagers had no means to rescue critically ill patients during floods or freezing periods. They passively accepted fate, enduring suffering and sadness without complaint.


--- (p. 49) ---

O And then, in 1962, residents from 20 villages in 4 related regions petitioned the Minister of Construction and the Governor, urgently explaining their situation and proposing the construction of a bridge. Additionally, in early 1975, a member of the National Assembly from the region and the Minister of Construction visited the area. However, the administrative authorities at the time received a report stating that constructing a bridge across the 400m-wide river was currently impossible, and the residents' hopes were dashed.

O Since then, bridge construction has been proposed as an election pledge during every National Assembly election, but it only served as a voting tactic for the candidates. However, constructing a bridge across the river was a long-standing aspiration for the residents of this region.

### The Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

#### 1) Motivation and Achievements of the Pilot Project

O News spread that the "Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)," initiated by President Park Chung-hee on April 22, 1970, was igniting like a spark across the nation, and this news reached this village as well.

O In 1971, the government supported a pilot project with 335 bags of cement, and the residents attempted to construct a small bridge and culverts. Although the construction was crude and substandard due to a lack of technical skills, they gained confidence and a sense of possibility for the first time.

O Subsequently, with confidence in the Saemaul projects each year, all residents made efforts, leading to the improvement of village roads, farm roads, and living environments. The village, which had been backward, began to show noticeable daily improvements.

O However, the residents, who had been steeped in feudal ideology and adhered to outdated customs, were reluctant to learn from others or broaden their horizons, living like "frogs in a well," unaware of the outside world.

O In 1976, after the completion of the Andong Dam upstream on the Nakdong River, the water depth in the downstream region of Gudam-dong became too shallow for wooden boat navigation. Residents installed a 300m-long log bridge, which was somewhat convenient for students commuting to school.

O Some residents felt satisfied with the installation of the log bridge, but soon after, due to the release of water from the dam for industrial water supply, the bridge would be lost or buried overnight, increasing the residents' anxiety. Moreover, the adjustment of the Andong Dam's water level, which varied by season, made it impossible to permanently install the log bridge and exacerbated the residents' inconvenience.

#### 2) Motivation for the Construction of Gudam Bridge

O Lee Chan-gyu, a delegate of the National Unification Democratic Front and a public doctor in Pungcheon-myeon, who has consistently dedicated himself to regional development and residents' health management, led the village heads and development committee members from six villages in the Gudam area on a study tour of advanced Saemaul villages in Mungyeong County, Gyeongbuk, and the advanced site of Bomun Bridge in Yecheon County in early 1976. He gained immense insights from this experience, broadening his perspective.

O After the study tour of the advanced sites, the village heads, Saemaul leaders, and development committee members from the area were filled with the courage to think, "We can do it too."


--- (p. 50) ---

Finally, on November 19, 1976, a residents' general assembly for the construction of the Nakdongdae Bridge was held, with Representative Lee Chan-gyu as the main driving force.

- At the residents' general assembly, Jeong Man-soo (current head of Pungcheon Post Office) was elected as the promotion committee chair by unanimous vote, and the name was set as the "Saemaul Gudam Bridge Construction Promotion Committee."
- A budget of 50 million won was estimated for the large-scale bridge construction spanning 360m across the Nakdong River. The plan was to secure 30 million won through donations from benefactors and sell 450 jeongbo of forest land, which had been preserved as communal property, to cover the construction costs. At this meeting, Representative Lee Chan-gyu donated 2.5 million won in cash, and Committee Chair Jeong Man-soo donated 2.3 million won.

## 3) Issuance of the Saemaul Gudam Bridge (九潭橋)

On December 30, 1976, residents of all ages united as one and braved the harsh cold of winter to work on the Nakdong River daily, despite the freezing winds, to collect stones and gravel for the construction of their lifelong dream project. Over 800 residents participated, determined to complete the project.

## 4) Overcoming Difficulties

- In August 1964, unprecedented heavy rains caused the Nakdong River to flood to its highest level, submerging over 100 households as a 3m-high dike collapsed. Residents trapped by the flood waters cried for help, and their relatives on the other side of the river could only watch and weep, unable to assist. The Gudam-dong Youth Association took the initiative and organized a special task force of skilled swimmers, including Zhang Jeong-hwan and 10 others, who rowed a ferry to rescue the stranded residents. Despite their parents' protests, the team set off, and the crowd cheered them on. Fortunately, a military helicopter arrived just in time to rescue the stranded residents, preventing any accidents. Witnessing this, all the residents lamented that if only a bridge had been built, both lives and property could have been saved. They blamed themselves for not being able to construct the bridge.
- The annual monsoon season from July to August brought heavy rains every year, making it necessary to cross the river by ferry six times a month for the market day. This caused significant inconvenience, and accidents were frequent as people rushed to board the ferry. However, the only solution was the construction of the Gudam Bridge. Residents decided to take action and petition the government.

*   First proposal: On October 1, 1964, to the Ministry of Construction, the Ministry of Home Affairs, and Representative Kwon Ohun (from the Gyeongsangbuk-do region) regarding Gudam (九潭)


--- (p. 51) ---

The Bridge Construction Promotion Committee, led by Chairman Lee Chan-gyu, was formed, and over 800 residents of Mongni signed a petition, but it was dismissed with the reason that "a huge budget would be required."

* 2nd Proposal: On November 1, 1968, the committee was reorganized with Chairman Kim Chang-su, and over 1,600 residents from the nearby four towns petitioned the Ministry of Internal Affairs, the Ministry of Construction, Gyeongsangbuk-do, and then-Rep. Kim Dae-jin, but it also ended in failure.
* 3rd Proposal: On July 15, 1971, the committee was reorganized with Chairman Kim Dong-gyu, and petitions were submitted to then-Rep. Kim Sang-nyun of the Republican Party and Rep. Park Hae-chung of the Democratic Party, but it was also rejected.

Reference: Original drafts of the petitions from the 1st and 2nd proposals were lost.

### 3rd Petition - Construction of the Nakdong River Bridge

Promotion Committee for the Construction of the Nakdong River Bridge in Gudam, Pungcheon-myeon, Andong-gun

As part of the modernization of our homeland, we are entering the first year of the third five-year economic development plan, which continues to progress without interruption. The Ministers of Internal Affairs and Construction are working tirelessly, and our people must also work unitedly without rest to achieve the great task of national revival.

President Park (朴大統領) also said in his March 1st Independence Movement Day address, "Let us achieve complete self-reliance so that we can join the ranks of advanced countries from the ranks of newly developing countries." The residents of Andong, Uiseong, and Yecheon counties are also working in line with this, and as part of the rural modernization project, we hope to construct a bridge over the Nakdong River between nine villages in Pungcheon-myeon, Andong-gun, and Gisandong to facilitate the cultivation and transportation of agricultural products from the 1,000 jeongbo of fertile farmland.

First, currently, to go to Daegu (126km) from Gudam, one must go through Andong, but if a bridge is constructed, the distance will be shortened by about 60km, which will greatly benefit the transportation of agricultural products to major cities. Excluding the summer, during the other three seasons, about 1,000 people cross the ancient stepping stones daily, but it is very inconvenient.

Second, on the other side of the river, there are 1,000 jeongbo of fertile farmland where main crops such as silkworm cocoons (50,000kg annually), peanuts (400 tons annually), watermelons, garlic, and apples (600 tons) are produced. Currently, these crops are transported by ferry, which causes confusion and water damage. However, during the flood season, transportation is cut off, and residents can only look at the water level of the river.

Third, Andong-gun Pungcheon-myeon Gudam-dong, which is the production area of special crops, is at the center of Andong-gun Pungcheon-myeon (2,000 households), Uiseong-gun Sinpyeong-myeon (1,500 households), and Yecheon-gun Homyong-myeon and Jibomyeon (1,500 households). If the distribution channels for agricultural products become smooth, income in this area will increase significantly. We sincerely hope that the Ministers of Internal Affairs and Construction will deeply understand the long-cherished wish of the residents of the three counties who are struggling in such living conditions and actively mediate the construction of the Nakdong River Bridge in this area.

July 15, 1971
Gudam-dong, Pungcheon-myeon, Andong-gun
Promotion Committee for the Construction of the Nakdong River Bridge
Chairman Kim Dong-gyu (金東奎)


--- (p. 52) ---

<4 myeon (個面). Myeon chief's (面長) opinion paper (意見書)>

### Opinion Paper (意見書)

The construction of a bridge across the Nakdong River (洛東江) in Gudam (九潭), Ilgisan (一箕山), Windcheon-myeon (豊川面), Andong-gun (安東郡), approximately 450m long, is a long-cherished project of the residents of Andong-gun (安東郡), as well as those of Homyong (虎鳴) and Jibo (知保) in Yecheon-gun (醴泉郡), and the residents of Sinpyeong-myeon (新平面), Uiseong-gun (義城郡). This bridge is a vital route for the daily commute of over 1,000 people from the three counties and is crucial for the smooth transportation of various agricultural products from the 1,000 jeongbo (町步) of plains around Ilgisan (箕山). We earnestly request that this long-cherished project of the entire community, the construction of the bridge, be realized at this opportunity.

July 23, 1971
Yu Byeong-ha (柳炳夏), Chief of Windcheon-myeon (豊川面長), Andong-gun (安東郡)

### Opinion Paper (意見書)

The bridge across the Nakdong River (洛東江) is an essential route connecting Sinpyeong-myeon (新平面), Uiseong-gun (義城郡), Windcheon-myeon (豊川面), Andong-gun (安東郡), and Yecheon-gun (醴泉郡), which is widely acknowledged. For Sinpyeong-myeon (新平面), this bridge is not merely a simple connecting path but a crucial major route for the transportation of various agricultural products and people, benefiting the entire area of Sinpyeong-myeon (新平面) and Anpyeong-myeon (安平面) in Uiseong-gun (義城郡). It is an absolute necessity for the three counties, and there is no need to reiterate this fact. We sincerely hope that the authorities will consider this situation and help fulfill the great long-cherished wish of the Sinpyeong-myeon (新平面) residents: the successful establishment of the Nakdong River (洛東江) bridge.

July 1, 1971
Lee Gyeong-bok (李敬馥), Chief of Sinpyeong-myeon (新平面長), Uiseong-gun (義城郡)

### Opinion Paper (意見書)

Uicheon Police Station (義城警察署) Sinpyeong Substation Chief (新平支署長) Seo Gab-deuk (徐 甲得)

### Opinion Paper (意見書)

Homyong-myeon (虎鳴面) is located at the southernmost tip (最南端) of Yangcheon County (釀泉郡), and its development (發展) hinges on transportation (交通), which is extremely inconvenient. For approximately the past 10 years, the long-cherished aspiration (宿願) of all residents (全面民) has been the construction of the Andong (安東)–Pungcheon (豊川)–Gudam (九潭) connecting road (間道路), which has been agreed upon and initiated by both sides (兩面). While this has resolved part of the long-standing issue (宿願事業), the residents of this area (本面民) now view the construction of the bridge (橋梁) across the Nakdong River (洛東江) in front of Gudam (九潭) as an incredibly motivating and significant project (重要事業).

If this bridge (橋梁) is constructed, it will facilitate the export (搬出) of agricultural products (農產物) produced in this area (本面) to Daegu (大邱), opening up new markets (販路) and increasing profits (增利). Additionally, it will ease the transportation (交通) of people and goods (人馬), significantly improving the income (所得向上) of all residents (全面民). This bridge (橋梁) is indispensable (必要不可缺) for the development (發展) of this region (故庄). We urgently request that the construction be completed as soon as possible (早速) and kindly ask for your prompt attention (急速善處) to this matter. Representing the residents (面民), we humbly submit this opinion (意見) with sincere hopes (懇切한 소망).

July 1971

Homyong-myeon Chief (虎鳴面長) Kim Seung-jae (金承在)
Homyong Substation Chief (虎鳴支署長) Park Young-soon (朴永淳)

### Opinion Paper (意見書)

The bridge (橋梁) across the Nakdong River (洛東江) in Gudam-dong (九潭洞), Pungcheon-myeon (豊川面), neighboring Andong County (安東郡), has long been a cherished aspiration (宿願事業) of the residents of Jibong-myeon (知保面). The location (場所) of the planned bridge (橋梁), Gudam-dong (九潭洞) in Pungcheon-myeon (豊川面), Andong County (安東郡), is a central artery (中央요로) connecting Andong (安東), Yecheon (醴泉), and Uicheon (義城) counties (3郡), which needs no further explanation (再言). For the residents of Jibong-myeon (知保面民) and the broader Yecheon County (醴泉郡) area (一帶), this bridge (本橋梁) is crucial for directly (直接) transporting agricultural products (農產物) and facilitating human traffic (人的交通) to Daegu (大邱). It is not merely a simple bridge (簡單) belonging to Gudam-dong (九潭洞) but an essential major artery (大要路) for the three counties (3個郡) mentioned above, without which daily life would be significantly inconvenienced (不便). Currently, 16,000 residents (面民) of the area are eagerly awaiting (渴望) the establishment (設立) of this bridge (橋梁) across the Nakdong River (洛東江) in the Gudam (九潭) region (地區). We humbly request (渴望) that the authorities (當局) consider (參酌) our dire circumstances (實情) and ensure (期必코) the successful completion (成功) of this project (事業).

July 24, 1971

Jibong-myeon Chief (知保面長) Yoon Chungsik (尹沖赫)

* On October 1, 1976, Representative (代議員) Lee Chan-gyu (李燦珪) of the Pungcheon-myeon (豊川面) Unification Democratic National Assembly (統一主體國民會議) took the lead in proposing that our region should now strive to become a wealthy village (富者 村落) where each farming household (農家 戶當) earns over 1.1 million won (110萬圓). He suggested that we should no longer rely on others but build a submerged bridge (潜水橋) with our own strength (力). He commissioned the county construction department (建設課) to design the project (設計), and the estimated construction cost (工事費), initially projected at around 300 million won (3億), was revised to approximately 90 million won (9,000萬圓) by the provincial technical support team (道 技術支援團).
* On November 9, 1976, a notice (案內狀) was sent out to convene a general assembly (住民總會) of the six villages (6個洞) on Gudam Market Day (九潭 市日). On November 19, 1976, at 2 PM, the first general assembly (總會) was held in the grand hall (大廳) of Kim Taek-yong's (金澤容) house in Gudam-dong (九潭洞), where a unanimous decision (滿場一致) was made to proceed with the construction (架設) of the bridge (橋梁). The project began with the collection of coarse aggregates (骨材), but it was later realized that collecting coarse aggregates (骨材) alone would not suffice, contrary to the resolution (決議) made during the general assembly (總會).


--- (p. 54) ---

Opposing residents (住民) continued to increase, nearly leading to the project's (架設) failure. However, Lee Chan-gyu (李燦珪), a respected assemblyman (代議員), took the initiative and contributed 2.5 million won (萬원) to the residents (住民) for the bridge construction (橋梁架設), which moved the residents (住民) and instilled in them a newfound confidence (自信感). The residents (住民) then took the lead in organizing a groundbreaking ceremony (起工式), which was attended by about 15 officials (機關長) from Andong City (安東市) and County (郡), along with approximately 800 nearby residents (隣近住民) on December 30, 1976, marking a historic commencement (着工式) of the Gudam Bridge (九潭橋) project (架設).

O In May 1977, as the foundation work (基礎工事) involving the installation of concrete circular forms (콘크리트 원형 파일) was underway and slab (슬라브) work began, an unexpected heavy rain caused the sand and gravel collected throughout the winter to be washed away in a single night. The entire region's (地域) residents (住民) gathered by the river (江), stomping their feet and lamenting the sky as they endured the night rain.

O Additionally, the release of 200 tons (屯) of water per second (每秒當) from the dam (「댐」) for downstream water supply (下流地域用水供給) hindered the progress (進度) of the construction (工事).

O To make matters worse, the initial plan (當初計劃) to register the communal village property (村落共同財產) of 450 jeongbo (正步) of wasteland (野山) under the joint ownership (住民共同名義) of the residents (住民) faced obstacles. Among the 28 owners (所有者), many had either passed away (死亡) or gone missing (行方不明), making it impossible to sell the land and causing significant delays.

O Nevertheless, the residents (住民) of the area (地域) refused to lose heart (失去勇氣) and remained determined (集念) to complete the Gudam Bridge (九潭橋).

5) Donations (誠金) from various sectors (各界)

O As news of the project (架設) spread from person to person (入口), Andong Broadcasting Station (安東文化放送局) launched the "Send Cement (洋灰) Campaign" (1口座 8,000원) for the Gudam Bridge (九潭橋) Saemaul Bridge Construction (橋梁架設), raising a total of 4,678,000 won (千원) from 127 donors (喜捨者). This outpouring of support (格勵與慰勉) further boosted the residents' (住民) morale (意欲).

O From January 1, 1977, to raise funds (誠金 醵出), the promotion committee (推進委員會) visited each household (戶別 訪問). Initially, no one was willing to donate (喜捨), and the prominent citizens (有志) suggested that the less affluent residents (零細 住民) should show their sincerity (誠意) first. However, the less affluent residents insisted on seeing the sincerity of the prominent citizens first, and neither side was willing to compromise (一步 的 讓步).

O The promotion committee (推進委員會) decided that to achieve the project's goals (事業 成就), the committee members (推進委員) should donate first (喜捨). The chairman of the promotion committee (推進委員長), Jeong Man-su (鄭萬洙), promptly donated 2 million won (萬圓), setting an example for the upper class (上流), middle class (中流), and lower class (下流層) to follow in fundraising (募金).

O Without a set standard (基準) for the donations (誠金 醵出), even the middle class (中流層) donated alongside the lower class (下流層), leading to another challenge (試練) and a temporary halt (中斷 狀態) in the fundraising efforts.

O The promotion committee (推進委員會) held a general meeting (總會) and decided to persuade (說得) the middle class (中流層) by convincing (說得) their close acquaintances (親知) one by one. They publicly announced (公開) the list of donors (喜捨者 名單) on the village bulletin board (揭示板) to maintain their dignity (自己 體面) and resolve the situation smoothly (無難히 解決). Ultimately, 662 people, including Representative Lee Chan-gyu (李燦珪) of the Unification Democratic National Council (統一主體國民會議), raised 32,590,000 won (千圓) in donations (誠金).

6) Administrative Support (行政 支援)

Initially, the temporary bridge construction project (九潭撟架設工事) in Gudam-gyo (九潭撟), which was being promoted as a Saemaul Undong project (事業 地區) by the county (郡), was approved by higher authorities (上部) as a cooperative project (協同圈 事業 地區) by the Ministry of Interior (內務部). The Ministry of Interior (內務部) allocated a special support fund (特別 支援金) of 20 million won (萬圓).

O The county magistrate (郡守) and deputy magistrate (副郡守) provided on-site guidance (現場 指導) every other day (格日制), while the Pungcheon-myeon magistrate (豊川面長) and related civil servants (關係 公務員) (county (郡) and myeon (面)) provided round-the-clock (不撤晝夜) on-site guidance (現場 指導).


--- (p. 58) ---

Thus, with officials and citizens united as one, exerting their utmost efforts, the construction of the nation's largest-scale bridge for the New Community Movement, the Gudam Bridge (length 360m, width 6.4m, connecting road 119m), was completed in just 9 months after the groundbreaking. On October 14, 1977, the Gudam Bridge Completion Ceremony was held at the site, attended by members of the National Assembly, related government officials, heads of relevant agencies, and all residents of the project area. Amidst a festive atmosphere, the bridge, embodying the residents' blood, sweat, and tears, as well as the great spirit of self-reliance, wisdom, and neighborly love of our nation, was opened to the public, reminding everyone of these values once again.

## 7) Effects of the Project

- 3 counties, 4 towns, 20 villages, approximately 20,000 people can utilize the bridge (Andong, Uiseong, Yecheon)
- Easier commute for 400 middle school students in the Gangnam area
- Shortening of the distance between Daegu and Andong by approximately 34km
- Elimination of division in Pungcheon-myeon
- Improvement of circulation structure for agricultural products
- Annual reduction of transportation costs for agricultural products by 50 million won
- Increase in land value
  - In the Gangnam area, 1,258 jeongbo increased by 500 won per pyeong, totaling an increase of 18 billion 80 million won
- Residents of Gudam 1 and 2 villages had approximately 35 jeongbo of farmland in the Gangnam area, paying an annual ferry fee of 400 seok (80 million won at the end of 1977) to 2 ferry terminals in spring and autumn. However, with the construction of the bridge, the ferry fee was saved

## 8) Heartwarming Stories and Exemplary Cases

Among the many heartwarming stories and exemplary cases related to the construction of the Gudam Bridge, a few are introduced here:

- On September 8, 1977, Dongjang Choi Cheong-woong (38) and 149 other residents (127 men, 23 women) from Ssangho-dong, Sinpyeong-myeon, Uiseong-gun, located 12km away from the Gudam Bridge, decided on their own initiative to participate in the construction of the nation's largest-scale New Community Movement cooperative project, the Gudam Bridge. They brought their own tools and extracted 3m³ of coarse aggregate.

### I. Joyful Moments

- When I proposed the bridge construction (架設) to Mr. Park Don-yang (朴敦陽), the county magistrate (郡守), and he actively (積極) promised to support (支援) it.
- On December 30, 1976, when we held the groundbreaking ceremony (起工式) with the heads (機關長) of departments in Andong City and County (安東市郡內).
- Whenever Andong K.B.S. M.B.C. broadcasting station (放送局) aired a broadcast (放送) about the cement (洋灰) donation campaign (運動).
- When the pile driving (파일 타설) for the bridge pier (橋脚) construction (工事) first began (始作).
- When Mr. Seo Jeong-wook (徐正勖), the county magistrate (郡守), frequently visited the site (現地) to comfort (慰勞) and encourage (激勵) us.
- When Kim Soo-hak (金壽鶴), the governor (道知事), visited the site (現地) to inspect (報告) the bridge construction (橋梁 架設) work (作業) and encourage (激勵) us.
- When Kim Sang-nyun (金尙年), the member of the National Assembly (國會議員), received a telegram (電報) confirming that 240,000 won had been secured (確定) for the Gudam Bridge (九潭橋) construction (架設).
- When neighboring (隣近) residents (住民) from other counties (他郡) voluntarily (率先) came to the Gudam Bridge (九潭橋) construction (架設) site (現場) to help (採取) with gravel (자갈) collection (採取).
- When 43 out of 45 spans (經間) of the bridge pier (橋脚) were completed (完了), and the remaining spans (經間) were left, the promotion committee (推進委員會) members (委員) held a ground-breaking ritual (告祀).
- On October 14, 1977, when we held the historic (歷史的) completion ceremony (竣工式) and opened (開通) the bridge for the first time (始作).

### II. Sad Moments

- On April 23, 1977, when heavy rain (暴雨) caused the Nakdong River (洛東江) to flood (氾濫), washing away (流失) some of the gravel (자갈) we had worked hard to place (일해 놓은).
- When the eldest son (長男) of Kim Dong-chun (金東春), the head (長) of Gudam 2-dong (九潭二洞), was injured (負傷) by getting caught (감겨) in an iron rope (쇠줄) in the mixer (믹사기).
- When Kim Song-mu (金松茂), aged 38 (歲), from Gisam 2-dong (箕山2洞), suffered a spinal fracture (脊椎骨折傷) while transporting (運搬) aggregates (骨材) with a power tiller (耕轉機) during the upper deck (上板) finishing work (作業), and was hospitalized (入院) at Seongso Hospital (聖蘇病院) in Andong (安東市內).

## 3. Residents' Assembly (住民總會)

### ◆ Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (1)

*   Agenda (議題): Promotion of Nakdong River (洛東江) Grand Bridge (大橋) and Gudam Bridge (九潭橋) Construction (架設)
*   Date (日時): November 19, 1976 (1976年(年) 11월(月) 19일(日))
*   Time (時): 14:00 (14時)
*   Location (場所): Kim Taek-yong's (金澤容) sitting room in Gudam-dong (九潭洞)
*   Attendees (參席人員): Lee Chan-gyu (李燦珪) and 50 others (名)
*   Absentees (不參人員): Kim Dong-gi (金東琪) and 27 others (名)
*   Chairperson (司會者): Lee Chan-gyu (李燦珪), Unification Democratic Party (統一主體國民會議) Representative (代議員) of Pungcheon-myeon (豊川面)

Chairperson (司會者): I am deeply grateful that so many of you have taken the time to attend today despite your busy schedules. For decades, we have promised to build a bridge over the Nakdong River (洛東江) to ensure fair prices for agricultural products and to facilitate transportation for about 1,000 households in nearby Sinpyeong-myeon (新平面), Uiseong County (義城郡), and the Gangnam (江南) region. However, we have failed to deliver on this promise, leaving us with an ancient ford that is only usable in winter and requiring ferry services in summer. This situation is truly regrettable.
Now, thanks to President (大統領) Park's (朴) decisive leadership, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is gaining momentum across the nation. Let us also take advantage of this cooperative district (協同圈) initiative to benefit the eight villages, with six of them selected for projects in 1977. Today, we have gathered to discuss and advance this proposal.
To proceed with the discussion, shall we elect a temporary chairperson (臨時議長) according to the meeting rules (會議規則) and proceed with the meeting?


--- (p. 62) ---

# Meeting Proceedings

**Jeong Do-sul (鄭道述):** This is an old aspiration of our village (古莊) that must absolutely be accomplished by our generation. Before forming the committee (委員), let us discuss and decide on the fundraising methods (募金運動) and the direction for promoting the project (事業推進), and then proceed.

**Kim Seo-yeon (金瑞淵):** All meetings should be conducted according to the meeting procedures (會議進行法) to maintain order and ensure smooth proceedings and decisions. I propose this.

**Kim Woo-hyun (金瑀鉉):** I agree to the proposal (改議).

**Chairperson (司會者):** Let us decide on Jeong Do-sul's proposal (鄭道述案) and Kim Seo-yeon's proposal (金瑞淵案) by a show of hands.

- Supporters of Jeong Do-sul's proposal (鄭道述案): 5
- Supporters of Kim Seo-yeon's proposal (金瑞淵案): 36

**Chairperson (司會者):** We will proceed according to the meeting procedures (會議進行法). First, let us elect a temporary chairperson (臨時議長). I have to leave temporarily as I have a patient waiting for me at the hospital (病院), so who would be a good temporary chairperson?

**Jeong Won-gyo (鄭元敎):** I nominate Kim Byung-gyu (金炳奎).

- Unanimously approved by applause (滿場一致).

**Kim Byung-gyu (金炳奎):** Although I am honored (蒙利者), as a public official (公務員), I can only assist from the side. I lack the ability and will decline.

**Kim Dong-seon (金東鮮):** What does the position matter in a meeting for a great cause (事業)? We just need someone to conduct the meeting (會議進行). Time is being delayed, so let us continue the meeting (續會). Please proceed with the meeting.

**All (全員):** There are no objections. Please proceed with the meeting. We request this by applause (再請).

**Kim Byung-gyu (金炳奎):** Then, I will only conduct the meeting (會議進行). First, please decide on the organization (部署) and the number of members (定員). I ask for your decision on this.

**Kim Dal-hyun (金達鉉):** It would be good to have 1 chairperson (委員長), 3 vice chairpersons (副委員長), 6 general affairs members (總務), around 10 committee members (委員) from each neighborhood (各洞), and 1 auditor (監事) representing each neighborhood (各洞代表).

**Kim Dong-seon (金東鮮):** Kim Dal-hyun's proposal (金達鉉案) is good, but I propose 1 chairperson (委員長), 6 vice chairpersons (副委員長), 2 general affairs members (總務), around 10 committee members (委員) from each neighborhood (各洞), and 6 auditors (監事).

**Kim Jin-sik (金珍植):** I agree to the proposal (改議).

**Temporary Chairperson (臨時議長):** There are no other proposers besides the proposer (動議者) Kim Dal-hyun (金達鉉) and the proposer (改議者) Kim Dong-seon (金東鮮), so let us decide by voting (票決).

- Supporters of the proposer (動議者): 11
- Supporters of the proposer (改議者): 37

Then, we decide on Kim Dong-seon's proposal (金東鮮案).

All show approval by applause (全員 박수(拍手)로 찬동(賛同)함).

**Temporary Chairperson (臨時議長):** Now that the organization (部署) is decided, how should we select the members?

**Kim Byung-gi (金炳基):** Let us nominate by oral recommendation (口頭呼薦) and approve by a show of hands (擧手). All show approval by applause (全員 박수(拍手)로서 찬동(賛同)함).

--- (p. 63) ---

Lee Chan-gyu (李燦珪): Emergency motion (緊急動議) for personal statement (身上發言).
I (本人) cannot represent both the company (業體) and the current assembly member (現代議員), so please recommend someone else (他人).

Acting Chair (臨時議長): Please nominate others (其外) as well. Let's proceed with a vote (票決) by show of hands (一同).
Acting Chair (臨時議長): 13 members (名) agree (賛同) with the proposer (動議者) Kim Du-yun (金斗潤)'s motion (案).
38 members (名) agree (賛同) with the proposer (改議者) Kim Taek-yong (金澤容)'s motion (案).
Thus, Jeong Man-soo (鄭萬洙) is elected as the chairperson (委員長).
As the current chairperson (現在委員長) is not present (不參), we will proceed with the meeting (會議) as is.
Next, please elect a vice chairperson (副委員長).
Jeong Do-sul (鄭道述): Since the village heads (洞長) of each village (各洞) are present (參席), let's entrust (一任) the election of the vice chairperson (副委員長) to the village heads (洞長).
Everyone (一同) shows agreement (賛同) by applause (拍手) with no objections (異議).
Acting Chair (臨時議長): With no objections (異議), I declare (宣布) the motion (案) carried (可決).
Thus, one vice chairperson (副委員長) will be elected from each village (各洞):
Kim Dong-gi (金東琪) from Gudam-dong (九潭洞), Jeong Do-sul (鄭道述) from Gisam 2-dong (箕山2洞), Jeong Yeon-ok (鄭然玉) from Sinseong 2-dong (申城2洞),
Kim Taek-yong (金澤容) from Gudam-dong (九潭洞), Kim Yong-bok (金容福) from Sinseong 1-dong (申城1洞), and Kwon Hyuk-rak (權赫絡) from Guho-dong (九湖洞).
Please show your approval (賛成) by raising your hands (擧手).
51 members (名) voted in favor (賛成) with no objections (異議), and the motion (案) is carried (可決).
Next, let's elect two general affairs managers (總務).
Kim Jin-sik (金珍植): I nominate Kim Dong-seon (金東鮮) and Choi Kwang-yeol (崔光烈) from Gudam-dong (九潭洞民) to handle all affairs (事務) and financial matters (經理).
Everyone (全員) shows agreement (賛同) by applause (拍手) with no objections (異議).
Acting Chair (臨時議長): With no objections (異議), confirmed by a show of hands (擧手表決), 51 members (名) agree (賛同), and thus, the two are appointed as general affairs managers (總務).
Next, let's appoint committee members (委員).
Choi Chang-yeol (崔昌烈): I propose that the village heads (洞長), who are well-versed (精通) in each village (各洞), appoint about 10 members (餘名) and receive approval (認准) from this assembly (本會).
Everyone (一同) shows agreement (賛同) by applause (拍手).
Acting Chair (臨時議長): With no objections (異議), I instruct (指示) the village heads (洞長) of each village (各洞) to report (報吿) their appointments (選任).
16 members (名) from Gudam 1-dong (九潭1洞), 14 members (名) from Gisam 2-dong (箕山2洞), 8 members (名) from Sinseong 2-dong (申城2洞),
19 members (名) from Gudam 2-dong (九潭2洞), 12 members (名) from Sinseong 1-dong (申城1洞), and 6 members (名) from Guho-dong (九湖洞) have been appointed (選任).
Is there any objection (異議)? Everyone (一同) shows agreement (賛同) by applause (拍手) with no objections (異議).
Acting Chair (臨時議長): The motion (案) is carried (可決) unanimously (滿場一致), and I declare (宣布) it so.
Next, let's appoint 6 auditors (監事).
Kim Dong-seon (金東鮮): It would be good to entrust (一任) the appointment (適任者) to the village heads (洞長).
Everyone (一同) shows agreement (賛同) by applause (拍手) with no objections (異議).
Acting Chair (臨時議長): I declare (宣布) Kim Dong-seon (金東鮮)'s motion (案) carried (可決).

Gudam-dong(九潭洞) Kim Du-yeon(金斗淵), Gisandong 2-dong(箕山2洞) Kim Jae-yun(金在允), Sinseong 2-dong(申城2洞) Jeong Yun-gyo(鄭允敎)
Gudam 2-dong(九潭2洞) Kim Yong-nak(金容洛), Sinseong 1-dong(申城1洞) Kim Chun-sik(金春植), Guho-dong(九湖洞) Kwon Oh-bong(權五峯) have been elected. Are there any objections? Everyone (一同) shows approval with applause (拍手).
