♦ Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (4)

**Date of Meeting (開催日時):** November 28, 1976
**Agenda (案件):** Decision on Excellent Village Special Support Project (特別支援事業) for 1976
**Number of Attendees (參席人員):** 39

**Saemaul Leader:** Thanks to your endless cooperation and efforts, we have been able to carry out various village development projects this year and achieve a bumper harvest. Our village's Saemaul project achievements have been highly evaluated, and we have been selected to receive support for the Excellent Village Special Support Project next year. I have called this meeting to discuss and decide on the project plan with all of you. Please share your good ideas on what kind of project we should undertake.

**Jo Don-haeng:** Now, our village has solidified the belief that we can do it and is wrapping up all village development projects. Regarding the cattle fattening (肥育牛) project we pushed forward with last year, we have built a communal barn covering 15 pyeong (坪) and have increased the cattle fattening business to 50 head. I think the cattle fattening project is good for increasing residents' income and creating communal assets for the village.

**Kim Jong-hyeop:** How much is the special support project budget (事業費)?

**Leader (指導者):** It is 1,500,000 won.

**Lee Gab-soon:** While the cattle fattening project is good, I propose purchasing a village farm to cultivate special crops for the Saemaul income project for women and aim to increase income.

**Jo Su-gil:** Our village has inconvenient transportation and lacks means to transport agricultural products, which causes significant losses in residents' income due to market margins in the agricultural product distribution process. I propose purchasing and operating self-reliant village vehicles, a characteristic project being promoted by Gyeonggi Province.

**Kim Jong-hoon:** After securing a farm for special crop cultivation and purchasing self-reliant village vehicles for communal income projects and village fund creation, we should operate the cattle fattening project, which is currently being promoted and directly increases income. I propose carrying out the cattle fattening project.

**Leader (指導者):** To summarize your opinions, please raise your hand if you agree with the farm purchase project.

Only Lee Seong-yun and 6 others raised their hands.

Next, please raise your hand if you agree with the self-reliant village vehicle purchase.

Only Kim Jong-dae and 4 others raised their hands.

The Excellent Village Special Support Project for 1976 has been decided to be the cattle fattening project and is hereby announced.

**Jeong Gi-yong:** Please explain the summary of the communal cattle fattening project promotion that has been carried out since last year.

**Leader (指導者):** Explanation of cattle fattening project settlement report (20 minutes)

**Kim Jong-sik:** Regarding the settlement report mentioned above, the income amount of 1,700,000 won should be used next year or the year after.


--- (p. 139) ---

It would be good to reinvest the profits (再投資) in operations (運營). In my opinion (本人意見), it would be ideal to implement high-income businesses such as ginseng cultivation (人蔘栽培) to further expand the village fund (基金) and distribute dividends (配當) to residents (住民) through the village savings bank (金庫).

**Leader (指導者)**: That is a good suggestion. Let us proceed in that direction. For today, I will conclude the meeting (會議) here.

Thank you.
♦ Minutes (會議錄) (5)

Date of Event (開催日時): April 11, 1977
Venue (開催場所): Saemaul Community Center (會館)
Agenda (案件): Promotion of Foreigners (外國人) Demonstration Village (示範마을) Business Plan (事業計劃) and Implementation (推進)
Attendees (參席人員): 43

**Leader (指導者)**: Thank you for taking the time to attend today. Now, our village has achieved a unified (渾然一體) Saemaul business (事業) through the efforts of all residents (住民), which has been highly praised. Currently, many domestic and international (國內外) dignitaries (人士) visit our village for inspection (視察) and consistently express their admiration (感銘) for the Saemaul Movement (運動), offering words of comfort (慰勞) and encouragement (激勵). The government (政府) has also taken note of these developments. Last year, they provided 1,000,000 won to support the completion of unfinished (未進) communal (共同) village projects (事業). This year, we have received 1,000,000 won in government (政府) support (支援).

**Jeong Gi-yong**: Could you please explain the necessary criteria (必要基準) for the foreign promotion (弘報) village (示範마을) projects (事業) for this year (今年度)?

**Leader (指導者)**: While the basic environmental (基礎環境) and production infrastructure (生産基盤) projects (事業) in the village have been completed, I believe that the residential environment (住居權環境) projects (事業), particularly kitchen (部엌) and toilet (變所) improvements (改良), and interior (內部) renovations (住宅), are still at a low level (水準). Unlike last year (昨年), individual (個人) residential (住居權) projects (事業) are now eligible for support (支援). Therefore, any project (事業) would be acceptable. However, based on what the Saemaul chief (新村計長) from the county office (郡廳) mentioned, I believe it would be appropriate to prioritize high-level (次元) residential environment (住居權環境) projects (事業).

**Lee Gab-soon**: Our members (會員) believe that this is an excellent project (事業). First, we would like to express our gratitude (感謝) for the government (政府) support (支援). Although the kitchen (部엌) improvements (改良) are mentioned, they are still traditional (在來式) and only the structure (構造) has been improved (改善) with cement (시멘트). If we pursue more cultural (文化的) and sophisticated (高級化) improvements (改良) and maintenance (整備), it would greatly enhance hygienic living (衛生生活).

**Jo Don-haeng**: What the women's association (婦女會長) president (會長) mentioned is certainly (勿論) valid. However, the walls (壁) still need painting (塗色), and the roofs (地붕) painted (塗色) 3-4 years ago have faded (退色), detracting from the village's scenery (景觀). Therefore, I believe it would be beneficial to include house (住宅) repairs (改補修), wall (壁) painting (塗色), and roof (地붕) painting (塗色) as well.

**Kim Yong-hak**: I believe this is a good project (事業), but how should individual (個人別) support (支援) and selection (選定) be handled?

**Saemaul Leader (指導者)**: We cannot support (支援) the entire (全體) quantity (物量) of projects (事業) with a budget (事業비) of 1,000,000 won. However, we also cannot support (支援) only a few (一部) individuals (個人). Therefore, I believe it would be appropriate to support (支援) roof (地붕) painting (塗色), toilet (變所) improvements (改良), and kitchen (部엌) improvements (改良) with the available funds (用).


--- (p. 140) ---

Estimate the total (總) amount (所要量) required and purchase (購入) it all at once. Allocate the average (平均) support (支援量) per household (全家戶), and let the remaining additional portion (追加分) be borne individually (個人別). It would be good if every household (全家戶) improves (改良) and gets organized (整備).

**Lee Gab-soon**: I agree (贊成) with the leader's words. Then, when should we start (着手) the project (事業)? In my opinion, it would be good to have the technicians (技術者) covered by the village's common fund (共同基金).

**Kim Jong-dae**: No. There are no separate technicians (技術者). It would be better to have those with experience (經驗) in the village serve (出役) in lieu of their individual (負擔) responsibility (代身).

**Saemaul Leader**: Let's start (推進) from April 6th and proceed (推進) together (共同). Please ask Jung Gi-yong, one of the development committee members (開發委員), to take charge (專擔) of this.

Today's village general assembly (總會) will conclude (以上) here. Thank you very much (大端).

# Yuldong (栗洞) Village, Geumsan-ri (金山里), Iljuk-myeon (一竹面), Anseong-gun (安城郡), Gyeonggi (京畿)

## 1. Village Overview

### a. History

- Approximately 570 years ago, the village was formed under the Wonju Won (元氏) clan and was called Iljuk-myeon (一竹面), Geumsan-ri (金山里) in the old Joseon Dynasty.
- In 1919, following an administrative district reorganization, it was renamed Yuldong (栗洞), Geumsan-ri (金山里), Iljuk-myeon (一竹面), Anseong-gun (安城郡).

### b. Location and Conditions

#### <Location>
The village is located 96 km from Seoul, 61 km from the Suwon Provincial Office (水原道廳), 28 km from the county office (郡廳), and 5 km from the town office (面所在地). School buses travel to and from the village twice a day.

#### <Conditions>
Located in the southeasternmost part of the county, 28 km from the county office, the village is bordered by Chungbuk (忠北) at a close distance to the east and is adjacent to Yul-myeon (栗面), Ichon-gun (利川郡) to the east. Surrounded by mountains on all sides, the village is situated in a mountainous area where residents primarily engage in rice farming (田作) over dry farming (沓作). The village is characterized by many small-scale farmers, with red pepper or flue-cured tobacco farming being the main agricultural activities.

### c. Basic Status

#### O Households and Population
There are a total of 65 households (戶), with 61 being farming households (94%) and 4 being non-farming households (6%). The total population is 358, with 185 males (52%) and 173 females (48%).

#### O Land Area
The total land area is 144.6 ha, with 90.6 ha being cultivated land (62.6%), 48.0 ha being forested area (33%), and 6.0 ha being other uses (4.4%). Of the cultivated land, 59.8 ha is rice fields (田) and 30.8 ha is dry fields (沓), with an average of 1.3 ha per household.

### Communal (共同) Property (財產)

The village's communal (共同) property (財產) includes a communal (共同) village farm of 1,000 pyeong (坪), a village hall (會舘) of 30 pyeong (坪), a village warehouse (倉庫) of 65 pyeong (坪), a purchasing and selling stand (購販張) of 10 pyeong (坪), a communal (共同) rice polishing facility (精米所) of 25 pyeong (坪), a communal (共同) bathhouse (沐浴湯) of 4 pyeong (坪), and a communal (共同) workshop (作業張) of 37 pyeong (坪), which make up the main assets of the village.

## 2. Village Development (發展) Process (過程)

### A. Situation (狀況) Before 1970 (年)

#### 1) Basic (基礎) Environment (環境)

*   Environmental (環境) projects (事業) included roof improvements (改良) for 9 houses (棟) and wall improvements (改良) for 7 sites (個所), totaling 75 meters of environmental (環境) work (事業).
*   The primitive (原始的) farming methods (營農) and the lazy (나태한) villagers' spirit (精神) involved backbiting others, envying success, and acting recklessly (沒知覺) with disrespect (不遜) towards elders.
*   When a guest visited a neighbor, they would be taken to a tavern and forced to drink alcohol, a disrespectful (不遜) behavior that was frequent.
*   The village relied on loans (장리빚) from neighboring villages to obtain white rice (白米) for winter provisions, and the following year's agricultural products (農產物) were used to repay the loans (장리빚). If not, they would obtain rice at high interest (고리 쌀) to maintain their livelihood (維持).
*   The cement (洋灰) supplied to each village, 335 bags (袋), was reportedly mismanaged due to the lack of leadership (指導者) and the village head's (里長) inability to coordinate (統率) the residents (住民). The residents (住民) allegedly used the cement for personal projects (自己) around their homes (家庭) and courtyards (뜰) or kitchens (부엌) in a makeshift manner (허술하게).

#### 2) Motivation (動機) and Trial (試驗) Project (事業) Results (成果)

*   The current (現) Saemaul (新村) leader (指導者), after completing 15 years (年間) of military (軍) service (生活) and working in Seoul, realized that urban (都市) life (生活) and office (職場) work (生活) were not the be-all and end-all of life (人生). He quit his job (職場) and returned to his hometown (故鄕) on February 9, 1972 (年月日), just as the Saemaul Movement (運動) was beginning to gain momentum (全國的) nationwide (全國的).
*   Upon returning (故鄕) to his hometown (故鄕), the current (現) leader (指導者) was deeply (太) disappointed (失望). The villagers (住民) were lazy (나태) and morally (精神) corrupt (썩어 빠진), gambling (賭博) with the tobacco collection fees (收納金) earned through hard work (피땀), drinking excessively (술), and wasting (소일) their days (日) without contributing (事業) to the village (村).
*   Witnessing (이러한) these issues (일), the leader (指導者) decided (決心) to educate (啓導) the villagers (住民) and embark on (事業) the Saemaul (新村) project (事業). On March 19, 1972 (年月日), he gathered (자리를 같이하여) four influential (有志) villagers (分) and like-minded (뜻) colleagues (동료) to discuss (議論) the future (앞으로) of Yuldong (栗洞) village (村). They resolved (결심) to develop (育成) the village (村) into a model (標準) rural (農村) community (村) and volunteered (自進) the current (現) leader (指導者) as the Saemaul (新村) leader (指導者).
*   On March 21, 1972 (年月日), a village general assembly (總會) was held, but only 15 people (名) attended (參席). That day, the meeting (의논) focused on (좌담) agricultural (營農) discussions (座談).


--- (p. 143) ---

On March 26, five days after the previous meeting, a village assembly was held again, with 49 attendees. During the meeting, several dedicated individuals and colleagues suggested that the village needed figures who would prioritize community work over personal life to drive its development. The current leader was put forward as a top candidate, and in the process, was elected as the leader of Yuldong Village.

### 3) Leader's Activities
- The leader began awakening villagers through personal example and action, prioritizing the village's affairs over personal matters. He started guiding each villager with sincerity.
- Some villagers who had initially refused to participate mocked him, calling him crazy or foolish. However, the leader did not give up and continued to help with both good and bad village tasks daily. Eventually, some of the opposing villagers changed their minds and started to cooperate.
- Emboldened, the leader consulted with a few intellectuals and, on March 21, 1973, held a village assembly to initiate the first project: electrification. Within two months, the village was brightly lit with electric lights, no longer relying on dim oil lamps.
- Not content with this, the leader sought to improve villagers' spirits by installing an amplifier. He visited a hometown chaebol (財閥) and requested a lamp, which was promptly granted. A 540,000 won amplifier was installed, and morning and evening broadcasts of patriotic songs and spiritual enlightenment began.
- In February 1974, the leader replaced the nominal village development committee and members of 4-H, the youth association, and the women's association with more dynamic figures. A villagers' assembly was held, and it was resolved that all villagers would participate in community projects.
- On February 12, 1974, the leader rented a bus at his own expense to take village development committee members and key figures on a field trip to exemplary Saemaul Undong villages. Upon return, they met with the town chief and agency heads, requesting support for Yuldong Village's development, which was readily granted. With this support, they began an environmental improvement project: roof renovation.
- Through the agricultural cooperative, they secured a loan of 300 million won, with villagers contributing an additional 400 million won, totaling 700 million won. However, due to opposition from some villagers, only 70% of the roof renovation was completed.
- To finish the remaining 42 roofs, the leader planned to mobilize youth association members to remove thatch from every house.

### 4) Overcoming Difficulties
- On March 21, 1974, upon returning from a trip to the agricultural cooperative and market to purchase materials, the leader heard that some villagers and youth association members had fought on the village roof.
- Thinking it unlikely, he returned home, only to find family members pleading with him to flee, as some villagers were reportedly armed with sickles and hoes, vowing to kill the Saemaul leader. Neighbors also advised him to escape for his safety.
- That night, at 12:30 AM, he returned home but couldn't sleep, tossing and turning. Suddenly,


--- (p. 144) ---

The villagers' shouts and the incessant ringing of the village bell echoed as if the world was about to end. It was 3:10 AM when we finally extinguished the fire and returned. Reflecting on the incident, I truly felt the immense difficulty of being a Saemaul leader. From that point on, complaints began to sprout among the families. My parents' words, chasing me to the workplace, were filled with curses, saying that helping others would lead to their starvation. The complaints were endless.

Not only that, but some villagers would come drunk, causing trouble, and saying things like, "You're ruining the neighborhood," "Why didn't you do the sewer project in front of so-and-so's house?" or "Are you going to feed us just because we're doing the Saemaul project?" The jeers and disturbances continued.

Despite this, I did not yield and persuaded them with all my conviction, seeking their cooperation. However, instead of responding, they became more resistant and caused more disturbances, making me want to give up and retreat. Each time, the village chief would come and encourage me, giving me the courage to push forward even stronger.

We bought a cheap mountain, and all 125 villagers participated in turning it into a field better than the existing ones. The following year, in 1976, we planted chili peppers as our first crop, earning a net profit of 89 million won, excluding farming costs.

In the first half of that year, the village was selected as the top village in the province for Saemaul Undong projects. On August 21, 1976, the Minister of Home Affairs awarded a commendation and a prize of 2,000,000 won, which was used for 300m of small stream improvement and the construction of one agricultural road bridge with a 7m span. Construction began in September 1976, and all projects were completed by November 5, 1976. This protected farmland and improved traffic for vehicles and residents, leading to increased income.

In the 1976 Saemaul Undong comprehensive review, the village was selected as an outstanding self-reliant village. At the national Saemaul Undong leaders' conference, the village received a cooperation medal from the President and a support fund of 1,500,000 won.

With the 1,500,000 won in support, the village built a 60 pyeong communal warehouse, storing 2,000 sacks of government grain and generating an annual income of 500,000 won.

**Village (마을) Organizations (組織) and Their (그) Activities (活動) Status (狀況)**

![Diagram: Village Organization Chart](/images/page_146_img_1.png)

The village organization chart has the following hierarchical structure:
*   At the top level are the 'Saemaul Leader (指導者)' and the 'Village Head (里長)' side by side.
*   Below them is the 'Village Development (開發) Committee (委員會)'.
*   Under the Village Development (開發) Committee (委員會) are four organizations: 'Youth Group (青年會)', 'Women's Group (婦女會)', '4-H', and 'Senior (老年) Volunteer Corps (奉仕隊)'.


--- (p. 147) ---

### Development Committee (開發委員會)
- Village resident decision-making, overall business operation, technical guidance (技術指導)
- Youth Association (靑年會): Promotion of Saemaul Undong (推進), agricultural improvement (營農改善), income increase (所得增大)
- Women's Association (婦女會): Rice-saving campaign (節米運動), purchasing and selling (購販事業), flower bed creation (花壇造成), labor service (勞力奉仕), home environment improvement (家庭環境改善), wholesome song promotion
  - Cleaning (淸掃) and environmental beautification (環境美化), labor service (勞力奉仕)
- Senior Service Corps (老年奉仕隊): Early cleaning (早期淸掃), flag raising (國旗揭揚)

### 4. Village General Assembly (住民總會)

* Meeting minutes (會議錄) (1)
    * **Date (日時)**: March 26, 1972
    * **Location (場所)**: Head of village's house (里長宅)
    * **Agenda (議案內容)**: Election of Saemaul leader (指導者)
    * **Attendees (參席人員)**: Total 65 people (名) attended (出席), 49 people (名) absent (缺席), 16 people (名)

Chairperson, the head of the village (司會(里長)): I have gathered you all here to discuss the plans for our village's Saemaul Undong (事業) and to actively promote the Saemaul Undong. We will now elect a Saemaul leader (指導者) to vigorously advance Yuldong village (栗洞마을). First, please explain the election method (選出方法).
Won Myeong-hui (元明姬): That is a great idea. Let's elect by secret ballot (無記名投票) rather than by show of hands (擧手方法).
Choi Byeong-mu (崔炳茂): What do you all think? Let's do it by secret ballot (無記名) instead of show of hands (擧手).
Chairperson, the head of the village (司會): As per your good suggestion, we will proceed with a secret ballot (無記名投票).


--- (p. 148) ---

**Saemaul Leader**: At the last meeting, we held an emergency meeting regarding the purchase of the communal farmland and discussed the expenditure of the deposit and the remaining balance. # Goyang2ri (高陽2里), Wolgot-myeon (月串面), Gimpo-gun (金浦郡), Gyeonggi-do (京畿道)

## 1. Overview of the Village

### a. History

*   Approximately 500 years ago, at the beginning of the Joseon Dynasty (李朝), this village is said to have formed as a small port connecting the maritime traffic between Incheon (仁川), Gaeseong (開城), and Seoul.
*   With a high mountain behind the village enveloping it, this village is cozy and sunny.
*   As this port village is located along the western coast (西海) of the Korean Peninsula, it has been called Goyangpo (高陽浦) Village from ancient times.

### b. Location and Conditions

**<Location>**

*   Located about 20 km northwest of the county office (郡廳), this rural village (農村) is situated 2 km west of the national road (國道) connecting Seoul and Ganghwa, adjacent to the western coast (西海).

**<Conditions>**

*   Although this village along the western coast (西海) had about 20 fishing households (漁家) 15 years ago, the meager catch (漁獲高) from small-scale coastal fishing (近海) led to a shift in occupations (轉業), and now there are no fishing households left. Currently, about 110 households primarily engage in agriculture (農業). While most farming households (農家) have traditionally relied on rice farming (水稻作), they began cultivating ginseng (人蔘) eight years ago, transforming the village into a major ginseng cultivation area (人蔘栽培) and significantly increasing household income (所得).
*   The farmland (農耕地) inherited from ancestors is thin and infertile (土薄), resulting in lower yields (收穫) compared to other villages. About 70% of the fields (沓) were previously unirrigated (水利不完全沓), but after constructing reservoirs (貯水沓) and installing irrigation facilities (揚水場), 90% of the fields are now irrigated (水利安全沓).

* There are 27 clans living here, with the Lee, Kim, and Park clans being the major clans.

### Characteristics

Before the 6.25 Incident, there were about 60 farming and fishing households, but after the incident, about 90 refugee households from Ongjin, Gaepung, and Yeonbaek counties settled here. Later, about 20 households from various regions across the country settled due to land reclamation projects. A total of about 170 households were scattered across five natural hamlets. However, after the armistice, about 60 households moved to Seoul, Incheon, and other areas. Currently, the village is still scattered, with non-farming households making up 30% of the population.

## 2. Village Development Process

### Before 1970

#### 1) Basic Environment

There was no access road from the national highway to the village, making it impossible for carts and other vehicles to pass through. The means of transportation were shoulder poles or women carrying goods on their heads.


--- (p. 155) ---

*   There were no farm roads (農路), so agricultural products (農産物) were transported using ox carts or bundles.
*   The small river (小河川) in front of the village was narrow and winding, so whenever heavy rain occurred, it would burst in dozens of places. There were no tiled houses (기와집); all were thatched houses (草家), and even those were not properly maintained, leaving ridges on the roofs. When it rained, stagnant water would flow down.
*   There were no toilets (便所) other than traditional ones (在來式), making it embarrassing for women to use them. There were no sewers (下水溝), bridges (橋梁), or culverts (暗渠), so whenever it rained, people had to wade through streams barefoot.

### 2) Income Level (所得水準)

*   Over 70% of the land was dry fields (天水沓), making it difficult to even transplant rice seedlings (移秧) if it didn't rain. The soil quality (土質) was poor, making it hard to harvest even 100kg from one jeongbo (단보).
*   30% of farming households (農家) were tenant farmers (小作農), and including 30% of non-farming households (非農家), 60% were stuck in poverty (零細狀) with no way out.
*   Crops (田作物) were limited to wheat, barley, and beans, with traditional farming (在來式 營農) repeated year after year. Non-farming households (非農家) worked in reclamation projects (干拓地 事業場) or did odd jobs, spending any money they earned on alcohol rather than trying to improve their lives. The village was known for mocking those who tried to work hard. At the time, the average household income (戶當 所得) was a mere 300,000 won.

### 3) Mental State (精神狀態)

The residents, scattered across five natural hamlets (自然部落), were completely disunited. They would argue and fight over minor issues, gather to gamble (賭博) and drink, wasting their household funds (家事). It was common for wives to report their husbands' gambling to the police (警察). The village was known for being the poorest in the area.

### 4) Cultural Life (文化生活)

There was no electricity (電氣), so people had to rely on oil lamps (燈盞) at night. There were only four radios (弘報物) for publicity (弘報物), and no households received newspapers (新聞).

## B. The Launch of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

### 1) Motivation (動機) and Trial Project Results (試驗事業의 성과)

*   When the village received 335 bags of cement in 1972, residents with no business experience (事業經驗) decided to undertake foundational projects (基礎 事業) like building a communal well (共同 우물), installing sewers (下水溝), and culverts (暗渠). However, due to insufficient technical guidance (技術指導), they did not achieve significant results (成果).
*   In 1973, the village resolved to expand the 2km village access road (進入路) to a width of 5m, a long-standing project (宿願事業). Initially, poor community unity (住民團合) made it difficult to mobilize labor (人員動員), requiring village leaders to visit each household repeatedly. However, persistent encouragement (督勵) from the village head (里長) and Saemaul leaders gradually increased participation awareness (參與意識). Once the project showed some progress (成果), all residents (全住民), regardless of age or gender (男女老少), were mobilized (總動員). Within two months, the 5m road was completed, allowing large vehicles (大型 車輛) to pass through. This brought immense satisfaction (보람) to the villagers, serving as the greatest motivation (動機) for the success of the Saemaul project (事業).


--- (p. 156) ---

*   Based on the cooperation and unity (協同團結) and the lesson that "if we do it, we can do it" gained from this project, the village quickly initiated the straightening of a 700m-long small stream (小河川) in front of the village into a straight river (直江).
*   On October 20, 1973, the village assembly established a promotion committee (推進委員會), and after obtaining approval for land use (土地使用) from the committee, the project commenced. Just one month after the groundbreaking on November 30, the 700m stream straightening project (直江工事) was completed.
*   This small stream improvement project (整備事業) was carried out with 1.1 million won supported by the county office (郡廳) and 2 million won contributed by the residents (including land and effort). Thanks to the Saemaul Undong, residents who had sweated to complete major projects that had been the villagers' long-cherished dream for decades, gained confidence in all projects. With the leader (指導者) at the center, the villagers united (協同團結) and accomplished in 1973 a total of 1,150m of small stream improvements (小河川) at three locations, 2,300 pyeong of communal farmland (共同畓) development (開畓), 5km of village access roads (進入路) and internal roads (安길), and 400m of farm roads (農路). Evaluated as an excellent Saemaul Undong beautification project, the village was promoted to a self-reliant village (自立마을) and connected to the 1973 Saemaul Undong total network (總連結), achieving the honor (榮譽) of promotion (昇級).
*   In 1975, with the support of 300 bags of cement and 0.5 tons of rebar (鐵筋) for the Saemaul Undong beautification, a 35-pyeong village hall (會館) was constructed. The interior facilities (施設) were completed for multipurpose use (多目的), including a management office and a 4-H hall (會館), and the hall was utilized as a Saemaul Undong education center (敎育場).
*   Additionally, a 6m-long small bridge (小橋梁) was installed over the small stream (小河川) in front of the village to allow the passage of horse-drawn carts (牛馬車) and farm machinery (耕耘機). A 5,000-pyeong Saemaul Undong fishing spot was developed communally (共同), generating an annual (年間) communal income (共同所得) of 500,000 won for the village.
*   Focusing on completing basic environmental (基礎環境) projects alongside the Saemaul Undong beautification, the residents improved the roofs of 16 houses and repainted the roofs of 55 previously improved houses. They also improved 75 poor-quality fences (不良 울타리), totaling 1,240m, thereby cleaning up and purifying (淨化) the village environment (環境).
*   In 1976, with the support of 400 bags of cement, a 45-pyeong communal workspace (共同作業場) was constructed. Of this, 20 pyeong was used as a sack factory (工場), and 25 pyeong was utilized as a communal warehouse (共同倉庫).
*   Meanwhile, with the support of 500,000 won in special assistance funds (特別支援金) for the second half of 1976, the village purchased an automatic weaving machine (自動入織機) for communal income-generating projects (所得事業). Installed in the newly constructed communal workspace (共同作業場), the machine produced sacks (가마니) using locally grown crops (穀草), generating an annual (年間) communal income (共同所得) of 1 million won for the village.
*   For welfare and hygiene facilities (福祉衛生施設), 1 million won in support (支援) was received in 1976 to complete primary (一次的) simple water supply (簡易給水) facilities for 50 households (號). This provided access to hygienically treated drinking water (飲料水) and improved living convenience (便利).
In this way, the unity (團合) and cooperation (協同) gained by the residents during the Saemaul Undong promotion process (事業推進課程) did not end with the Saemaul Undong beautification project. In 1976, for summer compost (夏季堆肥) production (增産), all villagers, young and old, mobilized (動員) even farm machinery (耕耘機) and vehicles (車輛). Through camping work (野營作業) and distant grass-cutting expeditions (遠征 풀베기 작업), they achieved remarkable results (巨揚한 실적), earning awards (施賞) as the most excellent village in the province (道內) for both the village and the women's association (婦女會) 4-H club fees (會費). They were even recommended for the central (中央) jury's grand prize (大賞).
*   The Saemaul Undong achievements (實績) accomplished by the village from 1972 to 1976 earned the village the title of the most excellent village (最優秀마을) and the Diligent Award (勤勉賞) from the Governor of Gyeonggi Province (京畿道知事) in 1976. Emboldened by this, the residents and leaders continued their unrelenting efforts in the 1977 Saemaul Undong, resulting in the construction of a 15-pyeong senior citizen's hall (敬老堂), 500m of waterways (導水路), two water pumping stations (揚水場), and one rest area (休憩所).


--- (p. 157) ---

The village achieved many accomplishments in the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) projects, including receiving 3.25 million won in funding for improving rural housing, which was used to renovate over 20 homes. The village was evaluated as an excellent village within the province and, at the 76th National Saemaul Leaders Conference, received 1.5 million won in special support funds from the President (大統領). These funds were used to establish a 600-kan ginseng processing facility as a communal income-generating project. In the effective year of 1980, the village aimed to achieve 5 million won in communal income. All work was carried out communally, further strengthening the residents' spirit of cooperation (協同心).

## 2) Activities of the Leaders (指導者)

O Since President (朴大統領) Park Chung-hee declared the Saemaul Undong in 1970, the village held a general village meeting in 1971 to discuss the implementation plan for the Saemaul projects and the selection of Saemaul leaders.
O On October 28, 1971, a general village meeting was held to establish a business plan for the use of 335 bags of cement. At this meeting, it was decided to construct three communal wells, a sewer system, and underground pipes. This first general village meeting was attended by 62 residents, each proposing projects.
O On November 13, 1971, a general village meeting was held to elect Saemaul leaders. Residents nominated several individuals they believed to be the most capable and with the strongest leadership qualities, and through a secret ballot, elected Mr. Jeong Young-Chae, who had experience as a 4-H volunteer leader and was the most active and had the strongest leadership among the young men in the village, as the first Saemaul leader of the village.
O The newly elected Saemaul leader, Jeong Young-Chae, was originally from Ganghwa (江華) and had graduated from a high school there. He had also served as the village's reserve forces platoon leader (小隊長), making him the most suitable candidate. He was appointed by an absolute majority as shown in the following voting results.

<Results of the Saemaul Leader Election (投票)>

| Name (姓名) | Jeong Young-Chae | Lee Beom-Ho | Min Seong-Ung | Im Yong-Ju | Jang Sun-Heum |
| :--------- | :------------- | :--------- | :----------- | :-------- | :--------- |
| Votes (得票數) | 32            | 22         | 8            | 7         | 4          |

O The first Saemaul leader, Jeong Young-Chae, dedicated himself to promoting the Saemaul projects and village improvement projects, contributing significantly to the development of the village. However, issues arose with the village's retail shops, and due to a lack of decisive action from the village head (里長) and lack of cooperation, he resigned from his position as leader on October 14, 1973. Since then, the village has changed its Saemaul leader five times, but it has consistently advanced its planned Saemaul projects ahead of schedule.

### <Reason for Becoming a Leader (動機)>

O On February 1, 1973, Lee Woo-Sang (李又相), who had returned from the military (軍), became a leader (指導者). With experience (經驗) as the village's 4-H President (會長), he was the most diligent (勤勉) and honest (誠實) young man (青年) in the village. He accepted the residents' (住民) invitation (勸誘) and took on the role with a firm resolve (決心) to do something for the village (村落).
O Since being appointed (選任) as a leader (指導者) on November 1, 1974, he, along with village head (里長) Park Yang-Won, has driven out the poverty (貧窮) and laziness (懶怠) inherited from the past, and put into practice (實踐) the Saemaul spirit (精神) of diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperation (協同). As a result, the unity (團結) of all residents (住民) has been strengthened, a Saemaul Community Center (會館) has been established to enhance education (敎育), a communal workspace (共同作業場) has been built, and an automatic loom (自動入織機) has been purchased to increase village income (所得). Today, the village has become an excellent Saemaul with a household income (戶當所得) exceeding 1,664,000 won (千圜).
O Since becoming a leader (指導者), he has fulfilled his mission (使命感) diligently (勤勉) and honestly (誠實), consistently promoting (推進) the Saemaul movement (事業). As a result, in July 1976, the village was selected as the best (最優秀) Saemaul in Gyeonggi-do (京畿道) for village beautification (部落), and the leader received a diligence award (勤勉賞) from the Gyeonggi-do governor (知事). On December 10, 1976, he received 1,500,000 won (千圜) from the President (大統領) at the National Saemaul Leaders Conference (大會) and was also awarded (表彰) by the Prime Minister (國務總理) as an excellent Saemaul leader (指導者).
O As the village became widely known (道內) as an excellent Saemaul (優秀), on May 9, 1977, its Saemaul activities (事業) were introduced nationwide (全國) through the KBS-TV "New Village, New Life" program (時間).


--- (p. 159) ---

### 3) Overcoming Difficulties (隘路克服) Situation (狀況)
○ After the implementation of the Saemaul Undong, the most challenging problem was in 1973 when the village decided to expand a 700m stream in front of the village to a width of 10m. A promotion committee was formed, and permission was sought for the inclusion of the relevant land. However, when it was discovered that 155 pyeong of land from the 500 pyeong owned by farmer Chae Su-won would be used for the stream project, the promotion committee, leaders, and village head repeatedly visited him to request his permission, but he firmly refused, posing a significant obstacle to the project. However, through the persistent efforts and persuasive appeals of two leaders, permission to use the land was finally granted. The other residents were so impressed by the resolution of this issue that they all willingly agreed, allowing the project to be completed as planned. As a result, the 700m stream access road and the expansion of 5.4km of farm roads, involving 7,000 pyeong of land, were successfully completed without any issues.

## 6) Heartwarming Stories (美談 佳話)

### <1st Class War Disabled Veteran Actively Participates in Saemaul Undong Despite Disability (不具)>
Yam Gyeong-yong (52 years old), a 1st class war disabled veteran residing in O village, actively participates in all Saemaul Undong projects and compost production despite his disability, leading by example not only for himself but also for his wife. His dedication has earned him praise from all villagers.

### <Senior Citizens (老人會) (Yushin Club (維新會)) Take the Lead in Outstanding Saemaul Construction (建設)>
Through the Saemaul Undong, all villagers of O village cooperated and united, achieving excellence in village beautification and compost production. On September 11, 1977, senior citizens organized the Yushin Club, and its 51 members gathered in front of the village community center at 5:30 AM daily, performed a brief attendance check, and then cleaned weeds along the riverbanks and roadsides, contributing to compost production and environmental improvement. Additionally, all senior club members actively participate in the Saemaul Undong's monthly large-scale clean-up events.


--- (p. 161) ---

On days when guests visited the village for tours, residents voluntarily participated in cleaning the 2km village entrance road and the surrounding lanes, setting an example for young people who might otherwise become lazy.

### 8) Notable Matters
#### a) Joyful Events

O In 1973, when the 2km village entrance road was widened to 5m, allowing large vehicles to reach the village, not only the leader but all the residents were deeply moved. In 1975, the completion of the 35-pyeong village community center allowed Saemaul leader Lee Woo-sang to hold the first wedding ceremony there, making the entire village even more joyous. Additionally, on October 5, 1977, using the 450,000 won earned from the village's collective farm established through the Saemaul movement, 131 village residents (51 senior members, 41 women's association members, and 39 other household heads) toured Seoul's major attractions by dividing into 5 tour vehicles after visiting the National Cemetery (顯忠祠), feeling the fruits of their 7 years of effort as a united Saemaul.
O Through the collective income generated from the 3,000-pyeong collective farm and the Saemaul fishing spot established by the Saemaul movement, the village reinvested in the Saemaul projects, resulting in no financial burdens on the residents. Moreover, even the village's miscellaneous expenses were covered by the collective fund, making it a village with no financial burdens on its residents.


--- (p. 162) ---

It is a village with a strong spirit of self-reliance (自立), capable of solving any difficulties without depending on others, within the village itself.

## 3. Village Assembly

### ◆ Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (1)

Date: December 1, 1971
Venue: Min In-gi's living room
Agenda: Election of Saemaul Undong Leader
Attendees: 73
Absentees: 47
Chairperson: Village Headman Lee Sang-ha

**Chairperson:** I am very sorry to have called you all here so suddenly today. The reason we have gathered for this village assembly is to elect a Saemaul Undong leader for our village. The Saemaul Undong leader, who will guide the Saemaul Undong projects, should be someone who can lead the village from the forefront, elected from each village across the nation. Their responsibility is indeed significant.

I kindly ask you all to elect the most capable leader.

**Im Yong-ju:** Is there an age limit for the leader position mentioned by the village headman?

**Chairperson:** No, there is no age limit. However, it would be preferable if the Saemaul Undong leader is relatively young.
Now, what would be the best method for the election? How about recommending candidates and then deciding by a show of hands?

**Min Gyeong-seon:** Yes, let's decide by a show of hands as the village headman suggested.

**Im Yong-ju:** Instead, I think it would be fairer to recommend a few candidates and then vote for them.

**Chairperson:** Please, someone else, share your thoughts.

임 Yong-ju: I recommend Mr. Jeong Young-chae.
Min Gyeong-seon: I think Mr. Lee Beom-ho should do it.
Jang Sun-heum: I recommend Mr. Min Seong-woong.
Chairperson: Is there anyone else? Alright, then, assuming there isn't, you have recommended three people. How should we proceed to elect one person out of the three?
Lee Geun-chun: It would be best to vote anonymously.
Chairperson: An opinion has been raised to vote anonymously. What do you think?
All: Yes, that would be best.
Chairperson: Then, we will vote anonymously, so please write down your names.
Chairperson: Now, I will announce the voting results.

Lee Beom-ho: 22 votes
Min Seong-woong: 8 votes
Im Yong-ju: 7 votes
Jang Sun-heum: 4 votes

With this, Mr. Jeong Young-chae has been elected as the Saemaul leader. Please welcome him with applause.
Chairperson: This concludes today's meeting. Goodbye.

# Gangwon (江原) Yeongwol County (寧越郡) Suju-myeon (水周面) Dowon 1-ri (桃源1里)

## 1. Overview of the Village

### Ga. History

* Originally belonged to Wonju County (原州郡) in Gangwon Province (江原道), but was incorporated into Yeongwol County (寧越郡) following the administrative district (行政區域) reorganization in 1906, becoming part of Seogu-myeon (西區面) (currently Jucheon-myeon (酒泉面)).
* In 1935, it was separated from Seogu-myeon (西區面) and became Dowon-ri (桃源里) in the newly established Suju-myeon (水周面). On January 10, 1962, the administrative district (行政區域) was reorganized, and Dowon (桃源) was divided into Dowon 1-ri (桃源1里) and Dowon 2-ri (桃源2里), leading to the current structure.
* The natural hamlets (自然部落) of this village consist of four hamlets: Bondon (本洞) and Jeomteo in the plain area (平野部), and Malguri and Gutongsan in the mountainous area (山間部). The village is said to have been called Dowon-ri (桃源里) since ancient times (太古的) because the flow of Jucheon River (酒泉江), which borders three sides of the village, forms a peach-shaped terrain (地形).

### Na. Location and Conditions

* Located approximately 24 km northwest of the Yeongwol County Office (寧越郡廳) in a mid-mountainous area (中山間部), and about 8 km southwest of the Suju-myeon (水周面) office.
* This village is situated in a narrow, remote mountainous area (山間奧地). Standing in the center of the village and looking around, you can see the rugged Taebaek Mountains (太白山脈), with Guron Mountain (구롱산) towering in the background. The ridges of Guron Mountain encircle the village like a screen, and the Jucheon River (酒泉江), about 200 meters wide, flows gently beside the farmland (農耕地), making the village resemble an island on land. The village exudes a tranquil and cozy atmosphere, embodying the typical (典型的) image of a prosperous rural village (農村).

### 2. Village Development Process (發展過程)

#### a. Development Situation Before 1970 (以前)

##### 1) Production Infrastructure (生産基盤施設)

O This village, although it has abundant water resources from the Jucheon River (酒泉江) flowing along three sides, lacked irrigation facilities (水利施設), suffering from severe droughts (早害) every farming season (營農期). During the summer rainy season, the lack of embankments (堤防築造) caused farmland (農耕地) to be lost, buried, and flooded, resulting in annual water damage (水害) to crops (農作物) that was immeasurable.

O The 200-meter-wide river (江) in front of the village, connecting it to other areas (外地), relied on a single small ferry for transportation, making travel extremely inconvenient. During the summer rainy season (雨期), transportation was completely cut off, leaving the village isolated, like an island.

O There were no roads (農路) connecting the village's main path (安길) to farmland (農耕地), only narrow, winding footpaths that could barely fit one or two people. All goods (物資) had to be carried by hand.

##### 2) Welfare and Environmental Facilities (福祉環境施設)

O The scattered houses (家屋) in the village were mostly thatched-roof huts (草家) with small, makeshift walls (壁體). No houses had walls reinforced with cement or lime (白灰). Most farmhouses (農家) had no fences, and structures like barns (畜舍), auxiliary buildings (附屬舍), and outhouses (便所) were poorly constructed with makeshift walls and roofs. The living environment (住居環境) was dire to say the least.


--- (p. 172) ---

It was so filthy that it was impossible to live, and there were no well or pump facilities, so they used river water as drinking water. All day long, women carried water in buckets to fetch drinking water, and it was common for them to spend the day doing so.

### 3) Income Level (所得水準)
*   The income level was also such that people relied on small plots of farmland inherited from their ancestors to grow small amounts of rice, corn, and potatoes as their main crops. No one attempted to cultivate high-income economic crops to increase their income. However, until the end of the 1970s, the average household income in this village was only around 300,000 won.
*   People recklessly destroyed forests to create slash-and-burn fields, planting and harvesting beans or mung beans, but they did not significantly increase their income. They indiscriminately cut down lush trees for firewood, showing no regard for protecting beautiful nature or having any attachment to their hometown. It was a pitiful, small-scale village filled with ignorance and apathy.

### 4) Living Conditions (生活狀態)
#### a) Mental State (精神狀態)
*   The mental state of the residents was also meaningless, as they accepted poverty as their fate and gave up on everything. There was no one who worked diligently and strived to live better.
*   They gossiped about others, were envious, and indulged in laziness and routine, wasting their time on alcohol and gambling. Every five days, when the market day came, they would flock to the Jucheon Market, about 20 ri away, with nothing to do but wander the market, drinking alcohol on credit, getting drunk, picking fights with anyone, and causing trouble.
*   Even more pathetic was the fact that from early spring, women would wander from mountain to mountain picking mulberry leaves to feed silkworms. When they sold the silkworms, they would spend all the money on alcohol at an inn along the way and come home drunk, making their wives cry. In the dead of winter, they would gather in the living rooms of various houses to gamble, squandering their meager assets in a single night. During the farming season, there was at least one household per year that had to leave the village.

#### b) Clothing, Food, and Shelter (衣食住)
*   The thatched roofs were rotten and sagging, leaking when it rained. The walls and ceilings were unfinished, so sitting against them would soil one's clothes. The floor was covered with straw mats, rough and uneven. If children played or ran inside, dust would fill the room, making it difficult to breathe. They lived without ever imagining electricity, using dim oil lamps that left the ceiling blackened with soot, and never cleaned the house all year.
*   They wore patched clothes, with holes in their socks revealing their toes, and their children's hands and feet were rough and black from not bathing. If someone wore black rubber shoes, the children would stare longingly, then silently lower their heads and walk away, their innocent hearts filled with pity and sadness.
*   Their diet consisted mainly of potato and cornmeal rice with plain radish soup all year round. If they carried and sold a few bushels of corn at the market 20 ri away, they might buy a handful of dried anchovies pickled in salt to grill and serve with their meal. The whole family, young and old, would be overjoyed, as if it were a birthday celebration.
*   It is now a long-forgotten memory, but every year during the spring famine, many households would run out of food, and the demand for high-interest rice loans would


--- (p. 173) ---

Living off borrowed money and barely making it through the year, the meager household was steeped in a backward and closed-off way of life.

## I. The Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

### 1) Motivation and Results of the Pilot Project

After news of the Saemaul Undong (Movement) in rural areas reached this village, the year 1971 passed with the village remaining as quiet as ever, showing no signs of reform or the spark of the Saemaul Undong (Movement).

However, by the following year, 1972, the fervor of the Saemaul Undong (Movement) had swept through the entire village. In the six years since then, the village of Dowon-ri has achieved truly remarkable development, both quantitatively and qualitatively, as well as in terms of results.

The village's achievements in its first year of the Saemaul Undong (Movement) included the construction of a 20-meter small bridge, the expansion of a road by 3 kilometers, and the installation of one communal laundry area.

Although the government provided 335 bags of cement and 1 ton of rebar for the pilot project, the construction of the small bridge was shoddy and substandard due to a lack of technical expertise and a lack of cooperation among the residents involved in the project. The road expansion project also faced numerous challenges and trials because it required incorporating valuable farmland into the road.

However, after completing the project, the residents gained a newfound confidence and motivation, realizing that they could accomplish anything and achieve success if they worked together wholeheartedly. This new sense of self-assurance and drive was the true harvest and achievement gained through the pilot project.

### 2) Selection and Activities of the Leader

Born as the son of a poor farmer and having only attended elementary school, Mr. Choe Won-gyu had always been determined to overcome the poverty passed down through generations and to leave wealth as a legacy for future generations. He was known in the village as a model young farmer who dedicated himself to his work with strong perseverance and diligence, eventually improving his living conditions to the envy of others.

It was only natural that Mr. Choe was elected as the Saemaul Undong (Movement) leader, given his background and achievements.

Mr. Choe's heart was always set on developing the village as quickly as possible and transforming it into a prosperous place. He was determined to overcome any difficulties and challenges that might arise until this goal was achieved.

From the moment the Saemaul Undong (Movement) began in the village, Mr. Choe set aside his own farming work and personal matters, devoting himself entirely to the development projects for the village's progress. He organized the Saemaul Youth Volunteer Corps to drive out gambling dens where villagers would gather in the winter to squander their assets. He also led daily morning clean-up efforts around the village, setting an example for the lazy residents and instilling in them a sense of diligence.


--- (p. 174) ---

1. They transformed unsanitary living environments (住居環境) into clean villages, sought out new agricultural techniques (農事技術) and income sources (所得源), personally learned and mastered them, and once successful, disseminated them throughout the village to boost residents' income (住民所得增大).
2. They also ensured thorough (徹底) self-defense (自衛) through Saemaul Undong activities to prevent infiltration by undesirable elements or thieves.
3. Through women's associations (婦女會), they vigorously promoted frugal rice-saving (節米貯蓄) campaigns, instilling a spirit of thrift (近檢節約) in daily life.
4. Thus, the activities of the leaders (指導者) were broad in scope and diverse.

### 3) Overcoming Obstacles (隘路克服狀況)

At the outset, the village road-widening project required securing 700 pyeong (坪) of land owned by about 10 households. Despite multiple village meetings (住民總會) and persuasive efforts, the landowners (地主) vehemently opposed the project, unwilling to part with their precious land (門前沃土). Daily visits to plead for understanding and cooperation often resulted in verbal abuse and alienated the community.

Ideally, purchasing all the farmland (農土) would have simplified the process, but the village lacked the funds (基金) for such acquisitions. At the time, Mrs. Eom Hwaja (嚴花子), a female Saemaul leader (婦女新村指導者), donated her own 434 pyeong (坪) plot of land to the village's communal property (共同財產) to facilitate the road-widening project. Similarly, Leader Choi, whose land constituted more than half of the required area, also contributed selflessly. Through persistent persuasion over nearly five months, they finally secured the land donations from the reluctant landowners.

However, once the project commenced, elderly and stubborn landowners took to the construction site, hurling insults and protesting that the Saemaul project (新村事業) would ruin the neighborhood (洞里). They argued that widening roads in an area inaccessible to automobiles was futile, causing work to halt on several occasions. Nonetheless, work resumed silently, and by late autumn, the once narrow and winding path was transformed into a straight, clear road. Villagers rejoiced, imagining automobiles traversing their streets, while the leaders who had toiled over the project were moved to tears.

Among the numerous challenges faced by the Saemaul project, another notable feat was the construction of the 160-meter-long (延長) Dowyon Bridge (桃源橋) by the villagers themselves, completed four years after its inception.

Constructing a bridge of such scale (規模) and technical sophistication (高度技術) solely with the village's resources proved daunting, both materially and manpower-wise. However, even slight rains would swell the river, preventing the 200-plus children from attending school, and every villager endured the inconveniences of poor transportation. United in their resolve, no one opposed the bridge project, and on February 5, 1973, they held a historic groundbreaking ceremony with 500 bags of imported cement (洋灰) and one ton of steel reinforcement (鐵筋). Armed with shovels and hoes, villagers tirelessly extracted aggregates (骨材) and excavated the foundation, though their work efficiency (作業能率) remained low.

Yet, enduring blistered hands, backbreaking pain, and relentless hardship, they persevered with tenacity and grit.


--- (p. 175) ---

In September of that year, they completed the first section of the bridge, standing 5 meters high, along with four bridge piers. The villagers continued their efforts in 1974, completing another section and four more piers, finishing the main structure. In 1975, they focused on installing the bridge deck, starting the work eagerly from the beginning of the year. Concerned about delays, they worked late into the night with torches and even brought schoolchildren to help gather gravel. Neglecting their farm work, each household contributed around 90 man-days of labor and 300,000 won in cash. The women's association also contributed funds from their savings, profits from the cooperative store, and 26 sacks of potatoes harvested from their communal farm. Despite their efforts, some villagers grew weary, and a few even suggested abandoning the project. Tragically, a flood in mid-August washed away their formworks and materials, leaving the villagers disheartened. However, driven by their leaders' determination, they resumed work in 1976, and by October, the massive Dowon Bridge, a lifeline for the 130 households and 700 villagers, was completed, a testament to their great cooperation.

### 4) Developmental Promotion of the Saemaul Undong

With the expansion of the village roads and the completion of the Dowon Bridge, this village began to see balanced and staged developments and improvements in various aspects of the Saemaul Undong, including production and income base facilities, communal facilities, and welfare environment enhancement projects. First, for production and income base facilities, they constructed a new 2 km bypass road with a width of 5 meters and built a 650-meter-long embankment along the river and installed a 160-meter-long improved bridge upstream of Jucheon River to enhance farmland protection and agricultural water facilities. They also constructed 430 meters of small stream improvement and 200 meters of waterways to create irrigated farmlands, contributing to increased grain production. Additionally, they opened 3.6 km of farm roads, enabling the transportation of agricultural and forest products by carts and tractors.

For communal facilities, they built a 57-pyeong welfare center combining a cooperative store, meeting room, and warehouse, which served as a versatile gathering place for the villagers. They also constructed a new communal warehouse for the storage and management of various agricultural materials. Furthermore, they built communal wells and laundry areas, significantly reducing the workload of the women.

For welfare environment enhancement projects, all 130 households carried out roof and housing improvements annually, completing them by the end of 1976. Over 40% of all houses repainted their roofs, greatly improving the living environment. Most fences were also upgraded to block walls and prefabricated fences, eliminating unsightly and unhygienic conditions.


--- (p. 176) ---

Kitchens and outhouses, previously absent, were now plastered with cement, making them very hygienic. Some houses even had their kitchens and outhouses tiled. Barns and auxiliary buildings were repaired and renovated, with their roofs and walls restored to a condition even better than the main house before development.

Electricity came to every home, bringing light to the world, and simple water supply systems were installed in kitchens, eliminating the inconvenience of women carrying water buckets. Soon, 25 households had telephones installed, allowing them to make calls from anywhere in the country while sitting in their rooms. Villagers who used to gather in the living room to gamble now enjoyed leisure time laughing while watching television.

Additionally, in the 33 hectares of communal wasteland, 8,000 trees of economic forests, fuel forests, and fruit trees were planted. Afforestation was carried out on the idle land along the river, turning the village into a lush and verdant place. These cultivated trees are expected to significantly contribute to increasing the village's non-agricultural income in the future.

The achievements of Daewon Village over the past six years of developing the Saemaul Undong were substantial, both in appearance and in substance. This is because all projects were directly linked to income. Residents who previously only cultivated low-income crops like potatoes and corn learned and applied new farming techniques, expanding the cultivation of chili peppers, garlic, tobacco, and specialty crops suitable for the local climate, thereby achieving high incomes. Through the application of imported soil and increased compost production, soil fertility was enhanced, leading to the expanded cultivation of unified system new rice varieties and remarkable increases in yield. Additionally, livestock breeding projects like Hanwoo (Korean cattle) and pig farming led to a rapid annual increase in farm income, gradually improving living standards. The average household income, which was only 400,000 won in 1970, reached 1.6 million won by the end of 1977.

Starting in 1972, this village actively promoted the Saemaul Undong and was elevated to the status of a self-sufficient village in 1974, just two years later. In 1974 and 1976, it received the honor of being granted special support funds from President (大統領). Moreover, both male and female Saemaul leaders were recognized for their activities and contributions, each receiving the Saemaul Medal.

5) Land and Cash Donation Situation

The present state of Daewon Village was made possible because residents deeply understood the true meaning of the Saemaul Undong and actively responded, while various sectors provided comfort, encouragement, and warmth.

### Cash Donation Contents (現金喜捨內容)
On July 17, 1972, the head of the Aeji-hyeon Ganggi branch (支部長) of the Korean Residents Association in Japan (재일(在日) 거류민단(居留民團)) (name unknown (姓名 未祥)) donated 3,060,000 won (千원) as Saemaul Undong funds (誠金).

### 6) Heartwarming Stories (美談佳話)
There are beautiful stories in the history of the Saemaul Undong in Dowyun (桃源) village that should be preserved for a long time.

#### a) Story 1 (第1話)
On July 17, 1972, the head of the Aeji-hyeon Ganggi branch (支部長) of the Korean Residents Association in Japan (재일(在日) 거류민단(居留民團)) who visited the motherland (母國) found the remote mountain village of Dowyun (桃源) and formed a sisterhood relationship (姉妹結緣). After hearing about the village development plan (開發計劃) through the Saemaul Undong (事業), he encouraged the residents (住民) and promised to donate Saemaul Undong funds (誠金). After returning to Japan (日本), this person personally remitted 3,600,000 won (萬원) to the village residents (住民) in the summer of 1973. The village residents (全住民) sincerely appreciated the large amount of money (巨額) sent from a foreign country (他國) wishing for the development (發展) of the motherland (母國). To repay the intention, the village built a welfare center (福祉會舘) with an area of 57 pyeong (坪) using 2,000,000 won (萬원) from the donated funds (誠金) and 1,000,000 won (萬원) from the residents (住民). With the remaining balance (使用殘額) of 1,060,000 won (萬원) from the donated funds (誠金), the village purchased 1,600 pyeong (坪) of communal farmland (共同田) and turned it into communal property (共同財産).

#### b) Story 2 (第2話)
In October 1972, the village residents (住民) expanded a 3 km road inside the village (안길) through self-reliance projects (自力事業). However, about 10 residents (住民) refused to contribute their land (土地) to the road expansion (擴張事業), putting the Saemaul Undong (事業) at risk of failure from the start (初擧). At that time (當時), Mrs. Eom Hwa-ja (嚴花子), who was actively involved as a female Saemaul Undong leader (婦女새마을지도자(指導者)), donated her own land (自己所有) of 434 pyeong (坪) in front of her house (門前沃土) to the village's communal property (共同財産), despite her not affluent living conditions (生活). This act surprised the village residents (住民) and moved those who had refused to donate land (土地), leading to the completion (完成) of the road expansion (擴張). This event served as a catalyst (契機) for the village residents (住民) to actively participate (參與) in the Saemaul Undong (事業).


--- (p. 178) ---

### Chapter 3

On February 15, 1973, the village residents held a groundbreaking ceremony to build a 160-meter-long Dowa Bridge (桃源橋). The next day, all residents worked together as one to extract aggregates and start excavating the foundation. No matter how hard they tried, their work efficiency did not improve, and they only felt exhausted. However, on March 5, 1973, Mr. Jang Jibong (張志鳳), the manager of Seongan (聖安) Mining Site (鑛業所), was moved by the villagers' hard work and dedication to the bridge construction. He provided two vehicles daily from the mining site to the construction site, which had been transporting raw stones. This allowed the villagers to easily secure 10 carloads of sand and 10 carloads of gravel. With this support, the residents worked even more diligently on the construction.

#### 7) Visits by Dignitaries

- On July 17, 1972, Mr. Kang Gi (姜琦), then chairman of the Aichi Prefecture branch of the Resident Association in Japan (在日居留民團愛知縣支部長) (name unknown), visited the village, established a sisterhood relationship, encouraged and comforted the residents dedicated to the Saemaul Undong, and donated 3,060,000 won.
- On October 2, 1973, Mr. Jeong Seokmo (鄭石模), then governor of Gangwon Province (江原道知事), visited the village, inspected the Dowa Bridge (桃源橋) construction site, encouraged and comforted the residents for their hard work, and gave them a monetary gift.
- On August 18, 1974, Mr. Yu Eunjae (柳恩在), then director of the Gangwon Provincial Agricultural Promotion Bureau (江原道殖產局長), visited the village, inspected and guided the Dowa Bridge (桃源橋) construction site, and encouraged and comforted the residents for their hard work.
- On November 16, 1976, Congressman Jang Seungtae (張承泰) personally visited the village and attended the completion ceremony of Dowa Bridge (桃源橋). He congratulated the residents on their efforts and presented 200 towels as a memento.

#### 8) Special Items

- On October 10, 1974, Mrs. Eom Hwaja (嚴花子女), a female Saemaul leader, received the Saemaul Medal at the National Leaders Conference held in Gwangju (光州).
- On December 10, 1976, Mr. Choi Won-gyu (崔元奎), a Saemaul leader, received the Saemaul Medal for Effort at the National Leaders Conference held in Daejeon (大田).
- In the August 1977 issue of the monthly magazine "Saemaul" published by Daehan Gongnon Society (大韓公論社), the village was introduced as an excellent Saemaul.
- On December 8, 1977, the village and leader Choi Won-gyu (崔元奎) were featured on the KBS-TV program "Nagojang Manse" as an excellent Saemaul, and their business achievements were broadcast nationwide.

**B. Achievements of Saemaul Undong**

1) Spiritual Aspect

Through Saemaul Undong, village residents have learned diligence, cultivated self-help spirit, and acquired the Saemaul spirit of mutual cooperation. They have completely reformed their closed consciousness structure, gained confidence, and felt the evidence of their capabilities.

2) Living Aspect

Scattered and dirty living environments have been rapidly improved and transformed along with income increase. Life stability in clothing, food, and housing has been established, and various cultural facilities are gradually being enhanced.

3) Income Aspect

With the development and expansion of high-yield new crop varieties, improvement of various farming techniques, selection of high-income crops, and mechanization of farming, income has increased by more than four times compared to before the Saemaul Undong.

## 3. Future Development Vision (發展構想)

To improve public health (保健衛生), we will gradually complete the necessary facilities (施設物) and strive to enhance the health (保健向上) of residents (住民). We will continue to pursue residential area (住居圈) environmental improvement projects (環境改善事業) to accelerate the realization (實現) of a cultural welfare environment (文化福祉環境). We will continuously supplement and improve (繼續補完整備) the underdeveloped production income (生產所得) base businesses (基盤事業). We will promote farmland improvement projects (耕地整理事業) to increase land utilization (利用度). Through village joint income projects (共同所得事業) and the expanded cultivation (擴大) of high-income (高所得) economic crops (經濟作物), we will improve farm income (農家所得). Thus, we will surely accelerate the construction (建設) of a prosperous and peaceful ideal village (理想農村) in Dowon (桃源) 1-ri (里) before the 1980s (年代).

<1980s (年代) Village Goals (目標)>
