## 4. Village General Assembly (住民總會)

**♦ Meeting Minutes (會議錄)(1)**

*   **Agenda (議題)**: Construction (架設) of a small bridge (小橋梁) and road expansion (擴張)
*   **Date (日時)**: December 26, 1971
*   **Location (場所)**: Home of Eom Hwaja (嚴花子)
*   **Attendees (參席人員)**: Choi Won-gyu (崔元奎) and 53 others
*   **Absentees (不參人員)**: Jeong Gyeong-seong (鄭圭性) and 19 others
*   **Chairperson (司會者)**: Saemaul leader (指導者) Choi Won-gyu (崔元奎)

**Chairperson (司會)**: Ladies and gentlemen! It is my great pleasure to have all of you gathered here today for the first time since our village was established. The reason I have called you all here today is not just any other matter. It is about the Saemaul Undong (運動) that is currently being carried out in various regions (各地). Each village is actively promoting (推進) Saemaul projects (事業). Our village should not just stand by and do nothing. I have called this meeting to discuss how we can also improve our village with the support (支援) from the government (政府).

I have checked with the local office, and it appears that our village has been included in the 1972 Saemaul beautification project (事業). The government (政府) will provide (支援) our village with 335 bags (袋) of cement (洋灰) and 1 ton of rebar (鐵筋). With these materials, we plan to first remove the stepping stones in the small stream (小河川) in our village and build a concrete bridge. We also plan to install a laundry area (設置) so that the women can easily do their laundry. Given this support (支援) from the government (政府), I feel grateful, and I would like to take this opportunity to widen and straighten the narrow and winding roads in our village so that cars can pass through. This is why I have called this meeting today.


--- (p. 181) ---

**Kim Guk-hyeon(金國絃)**: If we are to build a bridge, where do you plan to locate it?
**Chairperson(司會者)**: That issue should be decided after you all have decided where to place the bridge.
**Jeon Hak-jin(全學鎭)**: It would be easier to build a small bridge, and for our village, it is urgent. I think it would be best to remove the stepping stones on the current village farm road and build a bridge there.
**Chairperson(司會者)**: Please share your opinions as well.
**Lee Chang-no**: The leader said we should expand the village roads. If we do that, our land will be incorporated, so what is the plan for that?
**Chairperson(司會者)**: The plan is that the landowners should voluntarily donate the land that will be incorporated into the road after measurement.
**Lee Un-se(李云世)**: Then where should we widen the village roads?
**Village Head(里長)**: We should use the existing roads for expansion, straightening out the curved parts as much as possible and widening them.
**Lee Un-se(李云世)**: There are many landowners with more than 10 pyeong of land adjacent to the village roads. Will they all willingly donate their land?
**Lee Chang-no**: If the village roads are expanded, several pyeong of my land will be incorporated into the road, so I can't just give it away.
**Lee Un-se(李云世)**: Me too, I can't just give away my land.
**Kim Guk-hyeon(金國絃)**: My land will also be incorporated to some extent. I will decide as I wish, but my parents won't just let it be.
**Kim Do-ryong(金道龍)**: Let's put aside the village road issue for now and first decide on the small bridge and laundry area.
**Chairperson(司會者)**: Alright. Let's decide on the small bridge and laundry area installation first today, and then hold another meeting to decide on the rest. Where should we prioritize the installation of the small bridge and laundry area?
**Village Head(里長)**: In my opinion, it would be best to remove the stepping stones we are currently using and build a bridge there.
**Lee Un-se(李云世)**: If we build the bridge, the next issue of expanding the village roads will arise. I don't plan to participate in the bridge construction.
**Kim Guk-hyeon(金國絃)**: Let's start with the bridge and laundry area. If we don't agree from the beginning, we won't be able to do anything, and the relevant authorities will divert the support materials elsewhere. They won't support us in the future, and we will surely suffer losses.
**Chairperson(司會者)**: That's right. Let's think carefully about this and work together enthusiastically to start the project.
**Kim Do-ryong(金道龍)**: As the Village Head said, let's build the bridge at the current location and expand and properly install the laundry area at its current location.
**All(一同)**: Alright, let's do that.
**Chairperson(司會者)**: Any objections?


--- (p. 182) ---

Then, we have seen the location determination for the bridge construction and the laundry facility installation. How will we handle the labor burden?

Village Head: First, until the project is completed, every household should participate in the work with one person each. Also, not everyone should come out at once; instead, it would be better to form work teams and take turns working.

Kim Guk-hyun: That would be a good idea.

Moderator: Are there any objections?

All: None.

Moderator: Thank you. Then, we will conclude today's meeting here. I declare the meeting adjourned.

## Minutes (2)

Agenda: Village Road Expansion
Date: March 15, 1972
Location: Village Head's House
Attendees: Kim Guk-hyun and 61 others
Moderator: Saemaul Leader Choi Won-gyu

Moderator: Everyone, I am truly sorry to have to convene this meeting. We have been able to complete a small bridge (20m) and a communal laundry facility thanks to your active participation in the Saemaul projects. Today's meeting is about the issue of expanding the village roads, as previously mentioned. Please understand that the goal is to open a path for us all to live better, and I kindly ask for your active cooperation to conclude today's meeting with good results.

Lee Chang-no: So, you're saying we should give up our land? I can't do that. I won't, even if I die, so you all figure it out.

Lee Gi-hoon: Instead of just opposing, let's discuss this together. Didn't we see how beneficial the bridge and laundry facility were after we built them?

Lee Chang-no: You're only saying that because your land isn't involved, so don't spout nonsense.

Park Chan-ho: If you're going to expand the roads, go ahead. I won't participate in that.

Lee Un-se: If the leader insists on pushing this forward, buy my land and make the road.

Village Head: Everyone, please don't get excited and listen to me. For this road expansion, the total land required is 1,400 pyeong. Among this, Leader Choi owns 100 pyeong, Kim Hyun-ju 30 pyeong, Park Chan-ho 30 pyeong, Lee Chang-no 150 pyeong, Lee Un-se 190 pyeong, Won Cheol-sang 20 pyeong, Lee Myeong-hak 20 pyeong, and Jeong Gu-hyun 20 pyeong. Of course, it's regrettable to give up one's own land, but this is for the benefit of the entire village, so I kindly ask for your understanding and cooperation. Leader Choi has already donated the land for the road a long time ago. What could be so pitiful that the leader would offer his own land without hesitation? Everyone, please think carefully.

Kim Guk-hyun: Is this Saemaul project about taking other people's land? Is that what Saemaul is about?


--- (p. 183) ---

What benefit (利益) would there be for us if we did that? I can't do it.
**Lee In-guk (李仁國)**: Everyone! If landowners like you provide the land, I will prioritize everything else and work diligently on the road expansion project. From what the leader (指導者) has said, if the road is widened, we can buy handcarts or small tractors instead of carrying goods on our backs to make farming (農事) more convenient (便利). Of course (勿論), this is not to say that I won't do anything if my land is not included.

**Eom Hwaja (嚴花子)**: Everyone, I have been watching you all discuss today and have made a decision. I promise you all that in order for us to all live well, we must choose the bigger over the smaller. I will donate (喜捨) the 400 pyeong (坪) of land I own in front of my house to the village's communal property (共同財產). If the land issue for the road expansion (擴張) is not resolved, I will even sell this land to purchase land for the road expansion. But we must widen the village road.

**Host (司會者)**: Eom Hwaja (嚴花子) leader (指導者), thank you so much. I don't know how to express my gratitude (感謝). Everyone, let's all respond to this generous gesture.
**All (一同)**: (Applauds enthusiastically in welcome (歡迎))

**Kim Hyun-guk (金鉉國)**: I am moved (感動) by Mrs. Eom Hwaja (嚴花子) donating (喜捨) her own land to the village property (財產). And I feel ashamed of what I have done so far. Please forgive (容恕) me.

**Lee Chang-no (李昌魯)**: Everyone, I agree (同感). I have decided (決心) to offer my land. Let's expand (擴張) our village road.

**Park Chan-ho (朴燦浩)**: Actually (事實), I was not unaware that road expansion (擴張) was necessary. I will persuade my parents somehow and offer the land.

**Lee Un-se (李云世)**: Now that it has come to this, I have no reason (理) to oppose (反對). However, let's have the survey (測量) done accurately (正確) and proceed with the work.

**Host (司會者)**: Everyone, thank you so much (感謝).
**Village Head (里長)**: Now that everyone's will is united (團合), my mind feels lighter. Let's all work together to develop (開發) this village as quickly as possible.

**Lee In-gyu (李仁奎)**: Thank you, landowners (地主). I don't have any land to offer, but as long as I am in good health (以上), I will participate (參與) and work hard at whatever I can.

**Host (司會)**: Everyone, let's give a big round of applause to those who have willingly donated (喜捨) their own land.
**All (一同)**: (Applauds loudly in welcome (歡迎))

**Host (司會)**: Thank you again (感謝). Then, we have seen the decision regarding the village expansion (擴張). We will conclude today's meeting (會議) here. Landowners (地主), please sign (署名) and stamp (捺印) the meeting minutes (會議錄) to record (記錄) that you have agreed to the land use (使用) at today's meeting (會議). Thank you (感謝).


--- (p. 184) ---

# Minutes (會議錄) (3)

*   **Agenda(議題)**: Planning for 1973 Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) Beautification Project
*   **Date(日時)**: November 24, 1972, 13:00~15:00 (3 hours)
*   **Location(場所)**: Choi Won-gyu (崔元奎) Residence
*   **Attendees(參席 人員)**: 58 people including Park Il-yong (朴日龍)
*   **Chairperson(司會者)**: Saemaul Undong Leader Choi Won-gyu (崔元奎)

**Chairperson(司會者)**: Over the past year, our entire village has united and, in particular, set aside personal desires to donate our fertile land. Thanks to this, we have expanded our village roads, which were previously narrow and difficult to traverse, allowing carts to enter our village and even building a bridge to replace the old stepping stones. However, I believe there is still much to be done in our village. Let us not stop here. For a better tomorrow, let us plan and execute more projects next year. In this meeting with our village's responsible civil servant, Lee Bong-gyu (李奉奎), let us establish the 1973 Saemaul Undong project plan according to everyone's opinions. Please share your good ideas.

**Kim Kyung-man(金景萬)**: Our village is surrounded by a river, and during the rainy season, we cannot pass through. We must start building bridges to connect Dowon and Dochon.

**An Jong-geun(安鍾根)**: While building a bridge between Dowon and Dochon has been a long-standing dream of our ancestors, we will need cement, reinforced concrete, various materials, technicians, and a substantial budget. We should inquire with the responsible civil servant about the level of support the Saemaul Undong provides for such projects.

**Lee Bong-gyu(李奉奎)**: Currently, Saemaul Undong projects are springing up like wildfire across the nation. However, the government does not fully fund all these projects. The fundamental purpose of the Saemaul Undong is to support projects that are particularly burdensome for you, providing some materials, cement, and reinforced concrete. Please establish your project plans with the resolve to cover the entire project cost through your labor and contributions.

**Kim Ho-gi(金好起)**: If we build a bridge, will the government provide all the necessary cement and reinforced concrete?

**Lee Bong-gyu(李奉奎)**: Our local office also hopes to receive more support from you. We will request the higher authorities to provide as much cement and reinforced concrete as possible.

**Lee Myeong-hak(李孟學)**: Building such a long bridge would require us to dedicate the entire year to the project. Moreover, raising the necessary funds would be impossible, even if we sold all our belongings.

**Village Head(里長)**: It is understandable that you lack the courage. That is why we have been isolated whenever the river flooded, and we could not even sell our agricultural products at fair prices due to the lack of vehicle access. If we give up on building the bridge to save a few coins and spare ourselves, not only us but also our descendants will have to live like this forever. Let us gather our courage and build the bridge.

**Lee Un-jae, Lee Chang-no, Park Chan-ho, Kim Guk-hyeon(金國鉉)**: The Village Head is right.

**Leader(指導者)**: Let us think again, everyone. As the Village Head said, if we unite and build the bridge, we can...


--- (p. 185) ---

How can we ever escape the hardships of our lifetime and leave something so proud for our descendants? Let us all join forces to build the bridge.

Kim Do-yong (金道龍): I agree with the village head (里長) and the leader's (指導者) opinion, but it seems that everyone here lacks the courage to build the entire long bridge at once. I think it would be reasonable to plan to build only the bridge piers this year and postpone the rest for next year, advancing the project on a yearly basis.

All: That is a very good idea. We all agree.

Lee Myeong-hak (李孟學): Initially, I did not dare to agree and opposed it, but after hearing the village head (里長) and the Saemaul leader's (指導者) words, I think we must build the bridge. And as Kim Do-yong said, if we divide the project by year, it will be easier to work on it, and I will actively cooperate with the project.

All: Applause.

Leader (指導者): Then, with the agreement of all members (會員), it is decided that the bridge between Dowon and Dochon will have only the piers built by next year. If anyone has other opinions, please speak up.

Lee Gwang-im: This year, the roads within the village have been completed, but without roads connecting to the fields, we cannot even carry a single load of fertilizer, and during harvest, we have to carry everything on our backs. Let's start expanding and connecting the roads to the fields this winter.

Lee Seong-jae (李性在): That is a good idea, but if we combine the bridge and the roads, won't the workload (作業量) be too much?

Lee Gwang-rim (李光林): The bridge will start next year, and the weather is not too cold now, and farming is almost done. Instead of playing cards, let's start now and use our free time.

Leader (指導者): Making roads requires land (敷地), but where should we pave them? Last year, we had considerable trouble with the land (敷地) for the village roads, and I wonder if the landowners (地主) will respond (呼應).

Kim Guk-hyeon (金國絃): We have already offered the land in front of our houses, so what's a little bit of the fields? If we make roads through our own fields, won't it be much easier and more convenient to work? Even if the land decreases a little, can't we achieve a threefold harvest (倍所出) by carrying fertilizer (推肥) with a cart instead of on our backs?

Lee Myeong-hak (李孟學): I agree with Kim Guk-hyeon's (金國絃) opinion. The roads should be expanded and connected to the old roads (舊道路), taking the point next to Jiseo, the center of the cultivated land (耕地), as the starting point. It would be good to open them in a cross shape (十字形), with our fields on the right (右則) and Kim Dae-hyeon's (金大鉉) fields on the left (左則).

All: We agree with Lee Myeong-hak's (李孟學) opinion.

Leader (指導者): In that case, the roads will be built through the fields of Kim Do-yong, Lee Seok-jun, Kim Yeo-hyeon, Kim Ho-gi, Kang Sun-sik, Jeong Gyu-seong, An Jong-geun, and Hong Wang-pyo. I would like to hear their opinions.

Kim Do-yong, Kim Do-hyeon: How can we not offer our land when others are offering theirs?

Leader (指導者): What do the other members think?

Hong Wang-pyo (洪王杓) and 5 others: We will also donate (喜捨) without objection (異議).

Leader (指導者): Then, let's start the bridge construction earlier so that it does not interfere with next year's farming (農事).

Lee Gwang-rim (李光林): We should start before the ground freezes. Let's start tomorrow (來日) by placing ropes and working by each team (各班別) to determine the workload (作業量).


--- (p. 186) ---

Let's distribute the work so that all residents can work together to pave the roads.
**Leader (指導者)**: There's a suggestion to allocate work by team (班別). What are the team leaders' opinions on this?
**Lee Seong-jae**: To complete the work quickly, it's best to allocate tasks by team. Let's determine the workload proportional to the number of households in each team.
**All (一同)**: We agree.
**Leader (指導者)**: Then, after this meeting, let's allocate the workload by team and discuss the funding and labor mobilization for the bridge construction.
**Village Head (里長)**: We should categorize the shortfall in project funds as upper, middle, and lower based on living standards, estimate the budget once the support materials are confirmed, and have each household bear the cost. As for the start of work, since we can work even if the ground is frozen, let's start the road paving work as soon as the preliminary road work is finished.
**All (一同)**: We agree with the village head's opinion.
**Leader (指導者)**: I appreciate your absolute participation in the Saemaul Undong and your generous donation of land. I will now conclude today's meeting. Please sign and stamp the meeting minutes to leave a record for the future, and please participate in the allocation of the workload for the preliminary road work, team leaders. Thank you.

## Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (4)

On July 17 last year, the Aeji Local Branch of the Korean Residents Association in Japan, which has a sisterhood relationship with our village, sent us the promised Saemaul donation of 3,060,000 won. We need to discuss how to manage this meaningful donation, so please share your good ideas.

**Saemaul Leader (指導者)**: I agree, but currently, our village urgently needs a meeting room, as you all know. I think it's most urgent to design a separate warehouse, communal workspace, and meeting room to build a welfare center (福祉舘).

All residents (住民) in attendance: We agree with Mr. Kim Yeo-hyun's opinion.

Chairperson (司 會): Since you all unanimously approved the purchase of communal property (共同財產) and the construction of a welfare center (福祉舘), we will proceed with this decision. I will now ask Mr. Park Cheon-ho, who is present here, if he is willing to sell his land for the agreed amount.

Park Cheon-ho: How can there be a deal without negotiation? Rather than selling to someone else and regretting it, I will sell it to the village.

Chairperson (司 會): We have decided on the land purchase (土地買入). Where should we locate the welfare center (福祉舘)?

Kim Yeo-hyun: I think the most suitable location would be right next to Mrs. Eom Hwa-ja's house (宅), on the newly purchased land (新買入地). If we build a road in front of it, it would be perfect.

All residents (住民) in attendance: Agreed.

Chairperson (司 會): We will reconvene after the harvest to discuss the commencement of the welfare center (福祉會舘) construction. For now, let us adjourn this meeting. Please stamp or sign your attendance.

# Gangwon Province, Jeongseon County, Buk-myeon, Nam-pyeong-ri

## 1. Overview of the Village

### A. History

*   Nam-pyeong (南坪) Village has been inhabited for approximately 1,200 years by the families of three surnames: Byeon (邊), Baek (白), and Yu (劉), and Jeon (全). Over time, the Byeon and Baek families disappeared, and now the Yu and Jeon families are the dominant clans.
*   In 1936, the village was renamed from Sodok Village in Buk-myeon, Jeongseon County, to Nam-pyeong-ri, Buk-myeon.
*   In 1958, the Nam-pyeong Outpost (南坪出張所) was established in Nam-pyeong-ri, Buk-myeon.
*   On July 1, 1971, the administrative district of Nam-pyeong was divided into Nam-pyeong 1.2-ri.

### B. Location and Conditions

*   Nam-pyeong Village is located 6 km northeast of the Jeongseon County Office (旌善郡廳) in a mountainous area.
*   The village is situated along the upper reaches of the Namhan River (南漢江), specifically the 170m-wide Joyang River (朝陽江), which flows in front of the village.
*   Behind the village stands the Taebaek Mountains (太白山脈), making it a typical mountainous farming village.

### C. Basic Status

#### Households and Population

| | **Households** | | | **Population** | |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| **Total** | **Farming** | **Non-farming** | **Total** | **Male** | **Female** |
| 282 | 271 | 11 | 1,665 | 827 | 838 |

#### Village Common Property

| Community Center | Common Warehouse | Bathhouse | Paddy Fields | Land | Village Fund |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 building, 50 pyeong (坪) | 1 building, 40 pyeong (坪) | 1 building, 15 pyeong (坪) | 1.2ha | 240 pyeong (坪) | 281,000 won (千원) |

#### Cultural Facilities

| 196 households | 41 households | 34 households | 282 units | 42 households |


--- (p. 192) ---

## 2. The Development Process of the Village

### a. Situation Before 1970

Nampyeong (南坪) village was a rural area located 14 km away from the town center, consisting of 11 natural villages scattered along the ridges of fields. The winding village paths and the clustered thatched roofs, along with the leaning stone walls, made the village look untidy. The villagers relied on traditional farming methods, focusing on crop rotation, and barely managed to survive, with an average household income of only 300,000 won in 1970. Despite this environment, gambling and drinking were rampant, leading to the dissipation of wealth and many villagers moving to other areas. Cooperation was unthinkable due to envy and jealousy. At night, women would work under the dim light of oil lamps, spinning thread and sewing, and grinding grains with a foot-powered mill for the next morning's meal, often not going to bed until after midnight. There were no newspapers, and only two radios in the entire village, owned by wealthy families, from which all news was disseminated.

In terms of clothing and food, the villagers' attire was shabby, and skipping meals during the spring famine was a common occurrence. Corn and sweet potatoes were the main staples.

### b. Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

#### 1) Motivation and Experimental Project Results

In 1971, following President Park Chung-hee's proclamation of the Saemaul Undong, a wave of enthusiasm swept through Nampyeong village, and the government provided 335 bags of cement. Although the villagers were inexperienced and lacked organization from the planning meetings to the completion of the work, they learned the valuable lesson that hard work yields results. Through the experimental project, they expanded 300 meters of farm roads and 1,200 meters of village paths, achieving significant psychological and spiritual effects beyond the physical improvements.

#### 2) Leader's Activities

The Saemaul leader of Nampyeong village had spent over ten years as an elementary school teacher before deciding to live and work with the villagers, starting his farming life in 1969. That year, he was elected as the village head and, together with another leader, Yu Byeong-hoon (劉炳勲), dedicated himself day and night to the village's development and the construction of a new community. In 1975, he was appointed as the Saemaul leader by unanimous vote of the villagers and served as a Saemaul flag bearer. Despite facing criticism and accusations of having selfish motives, his unwavering perseverance and persuasive abilities drove the construction of a 170-meter-long large bridge, becoming a driving force for creating a new history.

#### 3) Overcoming Challenges

The development of Nampyeong village faced significant obstacles, requiring the village leader to exert considerable effort and endure hardships. The Soyang River (召陽江), an upstream tributary of the South Han River (南漢江), flowed in front of the village, blocking access. To cross the river, the villagers needed a car


--- (p. 193) ---

The inconvenience of using ferries or passenger boats made transportation immeasurably difficult. When it rained, the river would swell, making it impossible to cross, leaving the village stranded like an island. Students who couldn't go to school would just kick their feet, staring at the sky and the river. The geographical disadvantages weren't just about crossing the river. The national road from Jeongseon-eup (旌善邑) to Gangneung (江陵) passed through the village after the ferry terminal, but for about 7 km, it was formed like a steep cliff, always posing a risk of major accidents. This made travelers constantly anxious. In October 1975, the road was rerouted to avoid the dangerous mountains and river, making travel safer. However, the 1,600 residents of Nam-pyeong-ri (南坪里) lost their only route and became like an island village, feeling a sense of defeat.

To overcome these difficulties, leader Do Rak-hyung (都洛亨) gathered the residents' opinions and judged that the quickest way for our village to prosper was to build the Nam-pyeong Bridge (南坪橋). He visited Anmi-gyo (安味撟) in Daehwa-myeon (大和面), Pyeongchang-gun (平昌郡), which had already built a large bridge, with the development committee to learn from their experience. He was particularly moved by the residents' advice that maintaining initial enthusiasm and persevering until the end was most important. After the visit, the leader and his team held a general meeting of residents on December 17, 1975, and firmly resolved to build a 170-meter-long large bridge. They swore that those who did not participate in the project would lose their status as residents and immediately collected 7.7 million won and 300 pyeong of land as donations, sparking the bridge construction.

Finally, as all residents yearned for it, the massive bridge construction project that would create a great history for Nam-pyeong Village began. Despite the severe winter cold, all residents held a simple groundbreaking ceremony at the planned construction site on January 20, 1976, and vowed to successfully build the bridge. As the representative residents and the heads of Jeongseon-gun (旌善郡) offices dug the first shovel into the frozen ground, some residents were moved to tears, feeling that their long-cherished dream was finally coming true. Some young men even volunteered to showcase the skills they had learned during their military service.

The excavation work for the Nam-pyeong Bridge (南坪橋) foundation was particularly challenging as it required digging up to 7 meters to expose the water basin, making it twice as difficult as other bridge constructions, especially since everything had to be done manually. Installing one 8-meter-high bridge pier required 310 bags of cement and 1.5 tons of rebar, taking 35 days. To maximize efficiency, the work was organized into five departments under the committee chairperson: General Affairs, Supervision, Technology, Materials, and Mobilization. All households were divided into 27 work teams of 10 households each to participate in the work. The foundation work had to pass a precise inspection by the Technology Department, considering the heavy rainfall during the summer monsoon season, before proceeding to the next step. Sometimes, coal would appear during excavation, making the work as tough as digging through solid rock. To prevent losses of materials and maintain work efficiency during the summer when the river swelled, night work teams were organized using torches. Even those who didn't participate during the day voluntarily joined the night work, reducing the construction period by three months ahead of schedule. The bridge construction, a crystallization of sweat, cooperation, and wisdom, was completed in one year and two months after the start of construction.


--- (p. 194) ---

In October of 1977, the 10 piers of the bridge were completed, revealing their grand structure, and once the decking work was finished, a meticulous technical inspection was conducted on the reinforcement bar assembly to ensure perfect construction. By September of that year, the decking and abutments were all completed, showcasing their grandeur, and the automobiles and pedestrians passing by the bridge would momentarily stop and refrain from praising the natural challenge of the Nam-pyeong residents. The unity of the residents fostered through the bridge project instilled a sense of confidence that "if we do it, we can do it," and the wisdom of cooperation created a new myth through life education, leaving a legacy for future generations.

On October 22, 1977, a grand bridge 8 meters high and 170 meters long, which would adorn a page in the history of Nam-pyeong Village, was finally inaugurated amidst the cheers and blessings of all the residents. The residents were so moved that the inauguration site briefly became a sea of tears, and they caressed their calloused hands, unable to hide their joy. Yu Gyeong-ok, an 84-year-old villager, remarked that she could now cross the Joyang River, which she had previously only crossed by boat since her childhood, using this sturdy bridge, and she lingered on the bridge for a long time.

With the completion of the bridge, the traffic difficulties for the 1,600 or so residents were resolved, and the commuting of 160 middle and high school students, as well as the circulation of 1,200 tons of agricultural products and daily necessities, became smoother. Additionally, the train stop in front of the village was 6 km away, causing inconvenience, so a request was made to the railway authorities to install a temporary station connected to this bridge, resulting in the approval of the installation on February 28, 1977. The installation work was carried out as part of the Saemaul Undong, and the temporary station was opened on August 1, 1977, enabling middle and high school students who had been boarding in Jeongseon Town to commute.

Furthermore, 4 hectares of wasteland in front of the village and 42 hectares of barren fields that only produced corn were reclaimed, and 800 meters of embankments and a water intake facility were installed, two water pumps were purchased, and 3,800 meters of waterways were installed. As a result, 188 tons of grain were produced from the reclaimed land in 1977, expanding the income base. 1977 was also a year of trials for Nam-pyeong Village and a year of great historical transformation. Through environmental improvement projects, all farming households painted their roofs, and 374 projects, including the village entrance road, community center, communal warehouse, sewer, and housing improvement, were completed, making the village a pioneer in rural modernization. The village was even selected for the mid-month economic trend report in March 1978.

### 4) Developmental Promotion of the Saemaul Undong

Future development plans include expanding the embankments by 4,000 meters to reclaim 40 hectares of wasteland and expanding the breeding of Korean cattle to increase the number of cattle per household to more than three. Additionally, plans are to build a bridge connecting Buk-pyeong-ri and focus on income-increasing projects. Drawing on the experiences of overcoming the harsh conditions of a remote mountainous area with diligence and cooperation, the village aims to instill a sense of confidence and willpower in daily life and the belief that "we can live well too." With this in mind, the village has set a goal of 2.4 million won per household in the 1980s and is advancing with all its might through the Saemaul Undong.

## Ma. Achievements (成果) of the Saemaul Undong (新村運動)

### <Spiritual Aspect (精神面)>
The Saemaul Undong (新村運動) is a great leap forward (大躍進) movement (運動) for the nation (民族) and a movement (運動) to live well. The residents of Nampyeong Village are proud (自負) of and take pride (自負) in participating (參與) in this national (民族) movement (運動). Through the movement (運動), they gained experience (經驗), cultivated the strength (力量) to overcome (克服) any adverse conditions (惡條件), learned self-confidence (自信力) and potential (可能性), and gained the conviction (確信) that they can live well. They also cultivated the habit (習慣) of working hard (勤勉), learned and practiced the spirit (精神) of diligence (勤勉) and cooperation (協同), and made the Saemaul spirit (新村精神) the food (糧食) for their minds (心).

### <Livelihood Aspect (生活面)>
The old decadent (退廢的) customs (風習) were abolished (打破), ceremonies (儀禮) were simplified (簡素化), and consumption (消費) life (生活) was rationalized (合理化). Family (家族) planning (計劃) projects (事業), rice saving (節米) movement (運動), and improvement (改善) of dietary life (食生活) led to significant improvements (向上) in living standards (生活). By effectively utilizing (活用) idle labor (遊休勞動力) during the farming off-season (農閑期), income (所得) increased (向上) throughout the year (年中), allowing for improvements (改善) in clothing (衣) and food (食) structures (構造) according to one's means (分수). A culture (氣風) of mutual aid (相扶相助) was fostered (造成), helping the less fortunate (不遇) neighbors, leading to a stable (安定) and peaceful (平和) living environment (生活터전).

### <Income Aspect (所得面)>
In the face of adverse conditions (惡條件) such as limited land (土地), meager resources (貧弱資源), and mountainous terrain (山間地帶), it seemed as if hardships (試鍊) and poverty (貧困) were our destiny (宿命).


--- (p. 197) ---

The residents of Nampyeong (南坪) village, who had once left everything up to heaven, have learned and realized what it means to live well and how to achieve it, six years after the implementation of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement). They have learned that there should be no idle people, that diligence is necessary, and how much power can be generated through cooperation, all through their business endeavors.

When thinking back to a few years ago during the spring famine (春窮期), when they had to endure hunger, they cannot help but feel how fortunate their current (現在) living conditions are. Nampyeong (南坪) village has increased its per household income from 300,000 won in 1971 to 1,700,000 won in 1977, and is aiming for 2,400,000 won in 1980, with the entire village exerting its total force (總力) towards income-increasing endeavors.

## 3. Residents' General Assembly (住民總會)
* Minutes (會議錄) (1)
    * **Agenda (議題):** Establishment of Saemaul Business Plan (事業計劃)
    * **Date (日時):** Jan. 20, 1977
    * **Location (場所):** Nampyeong-ri (南坪里) Village Hall (會舘)
    * **Attendees (參席人員):** 97 people (名)
    * **Chairperson (司會者):** Yoo Byeong-hoon (劉炳勲)

**Chairperson (司會):** We will now commence the Nampyeong-ri (南坪里) Village General Assembly (마을總會). The reason we have gathered you all here today is to discuss the establishment of the Saemaul Business Plan (事業計劃). We must decide today, through this meeting (會議), how our village should develop, what businesses we should undertake, and in what order and manner we should proceed. I kindly ask that you all propose good ideas.

**Lee Yoon-young (李允榮):** There are countless tasks that need to be accomplished through the Saemaul Business (新村事業), but in my opinion, the most urgent task is the construction of farm roads (農路). Every year during the farming season, the narrow farm paths make it very inconvenient to transport crops, and since ox carts and horse carts cannot pass, much labor is required, and efficiency drops, making it difficult to increase the daily workload.

**Chairperson (司會):** Lee Yoon-young (李允榮) has proposed the construction of farm roads (農路). Please propose any other opinions you may have.

**Do Nak-chul:** While farm roads (農路) are urgent, I believe that the first priority should be the improvement of the stream (水河川) behind the valley, as it floods every summer, posing a danger to farmland and houses. We should start with the stream improvement project (整備事業).

**Chairperson (司會):** Do Nak-chul suggests that we first undertake the stream (水河川) improvement (整備). We will now hear the next proposal.

**Park Jong-ha (朴鍾夏):** I agree with both opinions. In addition, I propose that we also push forward this year with simple water supply systems (簡易上水道), public bathhouses (共同沐浴湯), communal storage facilities (共同倉庫), and bridges (水橋), among other things. Of course, undertaking many businesses will be a heavy burden, but the Saemaul Movement (運動) is about our village living well through our own hands, so why don't we try experiencing this trial (試鍊)?

**Chairperson (司會):** That is an excellent opinion. If there are any other good opinions, please speak up.

**Jeon Jae-il:** It would be good to establish the business plan (事業計劃) based on the proposals made so far.


--- (p. 198) ---

Ma Jong-seon: I agree.
All residents: I agree.

Chairperson: Then, please raise your hand if you agree to proceed with all the above projects together. (All residents raise their hands) We will confirm the project selection as such. Next, please propose the project costs, labor, and burden plans for these projects.

Lee Yoon-young: The land for the farm road will be donated by the relevant landowners, and the government will support the construction of the stream and warehouse, and the simple water supply system with cement. It would be good to proceed with the project using these materials.

Chairperson: That's a good opinion. However, I wonder if all the landowners will provide the land for the farm road.

Kim Gi-seong: How can one not provide the road that goes through one's own land?

Chairperson: Please speak up if you are a landowner.

All landowners: We will provide it.

Chairperson: Then, the Development Committee will first report the quantities and material requirements that they have identified. If there are any modifications or corrections, please let us know. Mr. Lee Dong-hoon will present the report.

Lee Dong-hoon: I will report only the project quantities and costs that were preliminarily planned by the Development Committee and proposed today.

## Minutes of the Meeting (會議錄) (3)

*   **Agenda (議題):** Bridge Construction (橋梁架設)
*   **Date (日時):** December 17, 1975
*   **Location (場所):** Nam-pyeong-ri (南坪里) Community Center (會舘)
*   **Attendees (參席人員):** 198 people (名)
*   **Chairperson (司會):** Do Rak-hyung (都洛亨)

Chairperson: We will now begin the general meeting of Nam-pyeong-ri (南坪里) residents. We will perform the national ceremony (國民儀禮). Please face the national flag (國旗). "Salute to the flag (國旗에 대하여(對하여) 경례(敬禮))" "Straight" and below will be omitted. Please be seated. The reason we have gathered you here today is to discuss the issue of constructing a bridge (橋梁), a long-standing wish of our Nam-pyeong-ri (南坪里). This bridge (橋梁) requires the participation of both Nam-pyeong 1 and 2 (南坪 1,2里), so residents from both villages have gathered here. Through the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동), we have gained skills, wisdom, and patience, which have given us confidence. Our neighboring village of Jang-yeol-ri (長悅里) has improved its farmland and village structure, making it much better than ours, which was once worse off. This has made us realize that we cannot just sit idly by. We held a joint meeting of the development committees from both villages and confirmed the approximate project cost (事業費) and feasibility (推進可能性). We also sent representatives from both villages to visit the Anmi-gyo (安味橋) construction site in Daehwa-myeon (大和面), Pyeongchang-gun (平昌郡) to learn about the issues and methods of progress (推進方法). Today, we will first decide on the construction of the bridge (橋梁架設) and hear your opinions. First, Mr. Do Nak-hoi will present the content of his visit and the basic plan for the bridge construction (橋梁架設).

Do Nak-hoi: Four representatives from the development committees of our two villages visited Anmi-gyo (安味橋) in Daehwa (大和), Pyeongchang-gun (平昌郡) two days ago. The bridge (橋梁) there is 120 meters long and 6 meters high, smaller in scale than the one we plan to build. Although there was government (政府) support, we were impressed by the residents' cooperation (協同) and diligent efforts. The most memorable part was the saying that the initial enthusiasm should not be allowed to fade until the end. We must be firmly resolved. The bridge (橋梁) we plan to build in Nam-pyeong-ri (南坪里) will be 170 meters long, 8 meters high, with 11 spans (經間), and will cost 60 million won (六千萬 원). According to the development committee (開發委員會), we plan to proceed with this project over two years by collecting donations (誠金), using village funds (部落基金), and government support materials (政府支援資材), with more than half of the project cost (事業費) covered by our labor (勞力).

Chairperson: That was the report from the development committee (開發委員會). While you are all aware of how much we need this bridge (橋梁) and the obstacles it causes in transporting agricultural products (農産物運送) and traffic (交通), we will now hear directly from Park Chun-ja (朴春子), a student at Jeongseon Girls' Middle School (女子中學校), about her difficulties in commuting (通學) in accordance with the order of proceedings (式順).


--- (p. 201) ---

**Park Chun-ja (朴春子) Student (學生)**: Good day. I am Park Chun-ja, a student commuting to Jeongseon (旌善) Girls' Middle School. Before I talk about the inconveniences of commuting, I heard a rumor that the adults of Nam-pyeong-ri (南坪里) are going to build a bridge (橋梁), and I was so happy I didn't know what to do. I've suffered a lot so far, but I thought that when my younger siblings go to middle school, they would have an easier time, and my heart was full. We commuting students leave the village at 5:30 AM and go to the ferry landing. In the cold morning, the boatman uncle would untie the frozen boat, and sometimes we would help untie the boat, and our gloves would get wet, and our hands would freeze. Also, if the students didn't gather enough, we would have to wait at the ferry landing, and the cold river wind would make our hands and feet feel like they were frozen and bursting. Also, in the summer, due to floods, we would be absent from school for about a week a month on average. I study hard, but because of the absences, I couldn't keep up with the other students. And after crossing by boat, we have to take the bus, but sometimes we would miss the bus because of the inconvenience of crossing by boat, and we would have to walk 25 ri (里) to school. I just hope that the bridge will be built as soon as possible, and when the bridge construction starts, I thought that we students could also help with easy tasks on Sundays or after school.

**Chairperson (司會)**: That's truly heartbreaking and a painful matter for our parents. Now, let's decide on whether to build the bridge. Please suggest a method for voting.

# Gangwon (江原) Yanggu County (楊口郡) Yanggu-myeon (楊口面) Dosari (都沙里) Village

## 1. Village Overview (槪況)

### a. History (沿革)

* In ancient times, the region was inhabited by the Yeomaek people. During the Goguryeo era (高句麗時代), it was called Yanggu County (楊構郡) or Yo-eunholcha County (要隱忽次郡). In the Silla era (新羅時代), it was known as Yangjin County (楊塵郡), and during the Goryeo era (高麗時代), it was renamed Yanggu County (楊口縣) and was subordinate to Chuncheon (春川) (present-day Chuncheon). In 1413, the 13th year of King Taejong's reign (太宗), Yanggu County (楊口縣) was established with a county magistrate (縣監).
* On August 15, 1945, with liberation (解放), the area was occupied under communist rule (共產治下). After the armistice agreement (休戰 協定) on July 27, 1953, it was recovered (收復). On November 17, 1954, it was transferred from military government (軍政) to civilian administration (行政引受) and became Dosari (都沙里), Buk-myeon (北面), Yanggu County (楊口郡). In 1962, following an administrative district revision (行政區域 改編) on November 21, it became Dosari (都沙里), Yanggu-myeon (楊口面), Yanggu County (楊口郡), as it is known today.
* The village was named Dosari (都沙里) because the clear sand and stones flowing together were said to purify the minds of those who saw them.
* After liberation (解放), under communist rule (共產治下), residents were harshly exploited by the North Koreans (北傀), leading to the village being called Dosari (盜使里). After its recovery (收復) in 1953, the village overcame numerous difficulties and was revived as a pleasant place to live, hence the name Dosari (都沙里).

### b. Location (位置) and Conditions (與件)

Dosari (都沙里) is a remote mountain village located 7 km north of the Yanggu County Office (楊口郡廳) and 17 km south of the Military Demarcation Line (民統線). It is a front-line village where the famous UN Hill (高地), a fierce battleground during the Korean War (6.25), is situated behind it, and where North Korean propaganda broadcasts (北傀 對南放送) can still sometimes be heard.

# 2. Village Development Process

### Ga. Situation Before 1970

1) Basic Environment
All 67 households in the village lived in thatched houses (초가집), with no main roads in the village, making it impossible even for handcarts to pass. Additionally, there was no bridge over the stream in front of the village, so even a slight rain would make it impossible to cross. Schoolchildren who had to go to school early in the morning would have to stand by the stream, stomping their feet and crying with their schoolbags on. Sometimes, children would even fall into the stream while trying to cross. It was a village that seems almost unimaginable by today's standards.

2) Income Level
The village had an average annual household income of 280,000 won, with 70% of households being absolutely impoverished (절량농가). Just a few years prior, each household could only cultivate 0.4 hectares of rice paddies, making it difficult to even have regular meals. During the spring hunger period (춘궁기), residents had to leave for other regions to work as day laborers. It was a village plagued by misfortune.

3) Living Conditions
a) Consciousness Structure
After liberation (수복이후), the village was composed of war refugees (전재민) who had gathered from various places. The villagers saw poverty as an inevitable fate brought by war, living in a state of resignation, saying, "What can we do in a place like this, right in front of the enemy?" They spent their days drinking and gambling. With seven bars in such a small village, it was known as a village with serious gambling problems and many bars, with strong factional consciousness and a sense of being left behind.

b) Culture and Daily Life (의식주 생활)
In the aftermath of the Korean War (6·25), it was almost surprising that people could live at all amidst the horrors and ruins. Villagers spent their nights huddled under the dim light of lanterns and candles, as the winter nights in the liberated area (수복지구) were long and deep. It was difficult to obtain even daily necessities, let alone newspapers and magazines. Villagers mainly used military surplus goods left over from the war, such as using helmets as well buckets and worn-out military boots as shoes. They wrapped themselves in old military blankets and overcoats, complaining about their lives.

### Na. Promotion of the Saemaul Undong

1) Development Motivation
After liberation (수복이후), war refugees (전재민) who had gathered from various places lived in a desolate and extremely poor village. The residents faced daily ridicule and criticism from neighboring villages due to their drinking, gambling, and fighting. On April 22, 1970, the "Saemaul Undong" was initiated by President Park Chung-hee (박대통령), igniting a spark of change in this frontline area (접적지구).


--- (p. 208) ---

The storm also hit Dosa-ri.
However, the residents turned a blind eye to it, and their habitual drinking and gambling continued as usual.
That winter, Lee Kang-seop (李康燮), a resident of this village, couldn't bear to watch the desperate situation of the village, which he had come to see as his fate. He rushed to where a gambling den was in progress, kicked open the door, and shouted, "Ladies and gentlemen! How much longer will you continue this? Let us all unite in harmony and eliminate empty rituals. Let us work diligently to escape poverty." However, instead of persuading the residents, he was beaten and spent a week in the hospital unable to rise. Undeterred, he judged that for this village to prosper, he needed to instill a sense of patriotism and cooperation in the outsiders who had come to this village, making them feel "This is my village, my hometown (故鄕)." He took the lead by setting an example, infusing the villagers with the will and belief that they too could live well, which became the driving force for today's development.

## 2) Activities of Saemaul Leaders and Overcoming Adversity

Lee Kang-seop (李康燮), the Saemaul leader of Dosa-ri, moved to this village in 1959 after completing two years of police service and six years of military service. He served as the chairman of the youth association and was elected village chief in 1964. Despite countless hardships and difficulties, he made tremendous efforts for the village and was an excellent pioneer of the Saemaul Movement.
In 1973, he was convinced that for this village to prosper, they should first reclaim the barren land around them to increase their land and income. He devised a reclamation plan for agricultural expansion.
He explained this plan to the village elders, but they opposed it, arguing that there were no irrigation facilities like reservoirs or weirs, the stream dried up all year round, making it impossible to irrigate the fields, and that their current difficult situation made such a huge task impossible. However, he did not back down and informed the residents that underground water flowed in the stream. He explained that if they installed a tunnel-like structure along the waterway, they could sufficiently irrigate the fields, and earnestly appealed to everyone to join him in promoting this reclamation project.
Persuaded by the persistent appeals of this leader, the villagers held a groundbreaking ceremony for the reclamation of barren land on December 18, 1973, despite the biting cold. In temperatures of minus 20 to 30 degrees Celsius, about 100 residents participated each day, blowing on their frozen hands to thaw them while installing tunnel-like structures according to the slope of the reclaimed land and removing large and small stones equivalent to 150 truckloads.
The transportation of stones for the ridges and dikes was carried out on a per-household basis. The men carried the stones using sleds and backpacks, while the women carried them on their heads. Due to the fierce snowstorm, some people hurt their waists from falling on the snowy ground, some suffered from frostbite, and others injured their fingers while digging stones out of the frozen ground.
With the stones they had painstakingly gathered, they made ridges for the fields and put in water, but the reclaimed land, which was only rocks and sand, could not retain moisture and fertilizer. Although they needed to use red clay for the fields, there was no one in the village who owned land suitable for digging clay, presenting another difficulty in securing a clay digging site.
He successfully obtained permission for clay digging after visiting a landowner six times, who lived 20 ri away,


--- (p. 209) ---

With a solemn resolve to complete the land reclamation before rice transplantation, regardless of any circumstances, the leader visited each injured resident at the work site at night and encouraged those working during the day, tirelessly transporting soil from the excavation site day and night.

O Suddenly, an unexpected cold snap halted the work, and the exhausted leader, who had been working non-stop, was bedridden with a nervous stomach disorder, forcing a temporary suspension of the soil work.

O During the 40-day suspension due to the cold, the residents did not rest for a single day, twisting straws to raise 900,000 won, which they used to purchase 50 carts to prepare for soil transportation.

O The following year, as the spring cold somewhat subsided, he led the residents back to the land reclamation site without fully recovering. Over 60 days, the soil brought to the reclaimed land amounted to 75,000 cartloads, equivalent to 3,000 truckloads.

O Transporting this enormous amount of soil solely by manual labor was grueling, with many collapsing from exhaustion and hunger. The villagers' creed: Courage! Perseverance! Nothing is impossible!

O As the residents' blood, sweat, and tears story of creating a new history for the village spread throughout the region, nearby military units joined in to help with the labor shortage, and about 200 students from Yanggu Comprehensive High School also assisted, boosting the residents' morale.

O A total of 4,000 participants endured immense hardships for five months, transforming 87,000 pyeong of wasteland into fertile fields. After connecting seven gullies to the newly reclaimed paddy fields and completing the first collective rice transplantation, the residents were so overwhelmed with emotion at the miracle of creating something from nothing that they could not leave the fields for a long time. Many grabbed the emaciated and roughened arms of the leader, shedding tears of joy and gratitude. The residents working in the newly reclaimed fields did not feel the hardship of the work or the scorching sun.

O Over the years, the barren land, eroded by floods and left desolate by war, had been covered only with pebbles and weeds. Witnessing this incredible miracle—where the barren land transformed into golden fields of swaying rice—residents embraced the practical philosophy of the New Community Movement: "If you do it, it can be done." They became filled with confidence that they could accomplish anything.

O That autumn, the residents, who had harvested 1,500 bundles of rice from the 87,000 pyeong of communal reclaimed land, danced joyfully at the threshing site, filled with boundless happiness.

### 3) Developmental Advancement of the New Community Movement

O Meanwhile, to protect the reclaimed land, which was achieved through the collective efforts of the entire village, from floods, the residents, without rest after completing rice transplantation, began constructing the embankment of the "Hwangyeongcheon" flowing along the reclaimed land. They completed 1,700 meters of sturdy embankment in just 45 days. While creating new farmland, the leader also signed a contract with nearby military units for the supply of radishes and cabbages, cultivating these vegetables on 54,000 pyeong of fields after harvesting barley, producing 500 tons annually and supplying them to the military, thereby earning an additional income of 6 million won.


--- (p. 210) ---

*   The village environment was also revitalized, completing projects such as roof improvements for all households, electrification for all households, village roads, simple water supply facilities, and establishing communal facilities like community centers, warehouses, bathhouses, communal workspaces, senior centers, and 4-H clubhouses.
*   Production and income-generating projects were also promoted, including the construction of 2,500 meters of farm roads, 8 small bridges totaling 110 meters, and communal livestock barns. Additionally, 10 hectares of village afforestation and one grain processing plant were established. The village collectively invested significant effort into these communal assets, amassing a total of 126.8 million won in communal property, creating a veritable paradise on earth.
*   This remarkable development was achieved through the dedicated efforts of Leader Lee, his unyielding phoenix-like conviction, and the unity and cooperation of the village residents, transforming the area into a leading village in the frontline region.
*   On January 5, 1975, during the monthly economic trend report, a successful case was reported, and the individual received the Saemaul Medal of Cooperation.
*   Additionally, from August 10 to September 30, 1973, for a total of 1 month and 20 days, he was selected as one of the nation's outstanding Saemaul leaders and visited rural areas in Japan for a study tour.

*   In 1972, Yu Geun-jae donated 56 pyeong of wasteland for the "Nutrition Improvement House."

5) Heartwarming Stories

## Village Organizations and Activities

*   The village organizations of Dosari (都沙里) include the Saemaul Farming Cooperative Association, the Agricultural Improvement Club, various crop teams unified into the Saemaul Farming Association, the Life Improvement Club, the Saemaul Women's Association, and the 4-H Club for youth.
*   The Saemaul Farming Association consists of all 77 farming households and is divided into sub-teams for vegetable crops, Hanwoo (Korean cattle), and leaf tobacco, each actively engaged in farming activities to increase income.
*   The executive members of the Farming Association are Chairman Lee Kang-seop (李康燮), Vice Chairman Kim Young-bok (金英福), and Secretary Lee Kang-jun (李康俊). The leaders of the sub-teams are Kim Sun-tae (金順泰) for vegetables, Yu Geun-jae (柳根在) for Hanwoo, and Lee Gi-pyo (李基杓) for leaf tobacco. Their activities include:
    *   The vegetable crop team cultivates 40,000 pyeong of vegetables, working together to save effort and produce collectively. They have a contract with the agricultural cooperative for joint sales. In November 1977, they sold 350,000 kg, earning a total income of 90 million won, significantly contributing to income growth.
    *   The Hanwoo crop team focuses on breeding activities, improving feeding and management, installing facilities in underground spaces, and preventing livestock diseases.


--- (p. 214) ---

### Livestock Barns
The village owns 1 communal livestock barn (共同畜舍) with a size of 50 pyeong (坪) and 55 individual improved livestock barns (個人改良畜舍) for 5 head (頭) each, with a total number of livestock being raised (總飼育頭數) of 126 head (頭). In 1977, the pure profit (純收益) amounted to 8,820,000 won. The tobacco cultivation group (葉煙草作目班) plans to have 20 households (戶) participate in 1978 to cultivate 45,000 pyeong of flue-cured tobacco (엽연초), aiming to lead the increase in farmers' income (農家所得增大).

- The Saemaul Women's Association (婦女會), led by President Kim Gyeong-sun (金敬順) with 46 members (會員), is organized and engaged in various activities such as operating the communal purchasing and selling market (共同購販場), saving rice (節米貯蓄), family planning (家族計副事業), and improving living environment (生活環境改善). The association's fund (基金) alone amounts to 1,100,000 won.
- The Dosari (都沙里) 4-H Club, led by President Lee Sang-gu (李相求) with 19 members (會員), is organized and actively engaged in farming improvement (營農改善活動), promoting village libraries (文庫), and emotional activities (情緖活動), advancing towards a healthy future (來日).
- Regarding the organization (組織) and activity (活動) status (狀況) of the village savings bank (金庫), the Dosari (都沙里) UN Village Savings Bank (金庫) has Mr. Lee Kang-seop (李康燮) as the chairman (理事長) of the bank. All members (會員) are fostering a frugal (勤儉) and thrifty (節約) lifestyle (生活風土). With a total capital contribution (總出資額) of 4,200,000 won, the bank plans to surpass 10,000,000 won by 1979.

## Ba. Achievements of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

Since its inception in 1971, the Saemaul Undong (運動) has swept through Dosari (都沙里) village more vigorously than any other place in the country. Spiritually (精神面), the village, once known as the poorest in the county (郡內) with a reputation for drinking, gambling (賭博), and fighting, has transformed into the best-living village. The villagers have developed an unshakable belief (信念) that "anything is possible" and have rooted self-reliance (自立精神). They have also learned the truth (眞理) of cooperation (協同) that one plus one is more than two. In terms of lifestyle (生活面), the old lazy and extravagant lifestyle (生活狀態) has vanished, replaced by diligence (勤勉), frugality (儉素), and thrift (節約). The villagers, no longer war victims (戰災民), embrace the spirit of pioneers (開拓者精神) and strive towards the dream of being the best in the country (全國). In terms of production (生產面), through communal work (共同作業), production (共同生產), and distribution (共同出荷), the village has not only saved labor (人力) but also increased the unit yield (單位收穫量) and improved income (所得). In terms of income (所得面), the average household income (戶當平均所得) has increased from 280,000 won in 1970 to 1,600,000 won in 1977, showing an enormous change with a sixfold (6倍) increase (增加). Today and tomorrow, the Saemaul Undong (運動) continues to move forward, striving to become an advanced village (先進的村里) that accelerates the realization of an ideal rural community (理想農村) in the 1980s (年代).
