Society (社會): After the construction of the communal cattle shed (共同畜舍), 155,200 won for purchasing 15 head of Korean cattle (韓牛購入資金) has been allocated to the main village (本部落). The main business expenses (本事業費) are short-term agricultural funds (短期資金). In the future, agricultural funds (農事資金) will be replaced with medium- to long-term agricultural special funds (農特資金). We need to purchase Korean cattle (韓牛) and manage the cattle shed (畜舍管理). However, pre-management (사양관리) is the main issue. If anyone has good opinions (意見), please speak up.
Lee Gi-pyo (李基杓): There is no objection to replacing agricultural funds (農事資金) with agricultural special funds (農特資金). In the near future, we must purchase 15 head of Korean cattle (韓牛), and before the construction of the communal cattle shed (共同畜舍), pre-management (사양관리) will be an issue. If anyone has good opinions (意見), please speak up.
Kim Sun-tae (金順泰): It would be better to temporarily entrust management until the completion of the communal cattle shed (共同畜舍).
Yoo Chang-bok (劉昌福): Let's think of good opinions (意見) for entrusted breeding management (委託사육).
Kim Sun-tae (金順泰): First, let's investigate the entrustment hopeful breeders (希望사육자) here. I think it is most reasonable to decide the breeding fee (사육비) based on the increase in body weight (增體量). If anyone has good opinions (意見), please speak up.
Kim Hee-seon (金熙先): I don't have any particularly good opinions (意見). I think entrusting breeding (委託사육) as Kim Sun-tae (金順泰) suggested is the most effective (第一効果的). And it would be better to decide the breeding period (사육기간) here.
Kim Sun-tae (金順泰): I think the breeding period (사육기간) should be until the completion of the communal cattle shed (共同畜舍).
All (一同): Agreed.
Society (社會): So, the breeding fee (사육비) will be decided based on the increase in body weight (增體量), and the breeding period (사육기간) will be until the completion of the communal cattle shed (共同畜舍). Next, please select the entrusted breeders (委託사육자).
Kim Young-bok (金英福): According to my current investigation (調査), Lee Kang-jun (李康俊) 1 head, Jeon Gi-cheol (全基哲) 1 head, Park Ho-young (朴浩泳) 1 head, Lee Bong-hwa 1 head, Kim Su-hyeop 2 head, Lee Gi-pyo (李基杓) 1 head, Lee Gyeong-hwa 1 head, Kim Jae-dong 1 head, Shin Jae-ho 1 head, Kim Jin-man 1 head, Baek Shin-jong 1 head, Hwang Il-gu 3 head, a total of 12 people (名) have expressed hope (希望), so I think it would be good to entrust them with breeding (사육).
All (一同): Agreed (unanimous decision (滿場一致)).
Society (社會): We will purchase cattle (소) for the 12 people (名) you have selected and entrust them with breeding (委託사육). Today's meeting will be adjourned. Please sign and stamp (署名捺印) the attendance list.

## Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (2)

Date (日時): April 1, 1974, 19:00~21:00
Location (場所): Village Community Center (會舘)
Agenda (議制): Special Support Project (特別支援事業) Construction of Village Communal Cattle Shed (共同畜舍)
Attendees (參席人員): 67 people (名)
Chairperson (社會者): Saemaul leader Lee Yeom-seop (李廉燮)
Recorder (記錄者): Main leader Kim Seong-jong (金聲鍾)

Society (社會): As a special support project (特別支援事業) for cattle sheds (畜舎), one building (棟) of 50 pyeong (坪) (for 15 head (頭用)) will be assembled. The total project cost (總事業費) is 1,500,000 won, with a grant (下賜金) of 1,260,000 won and a self-funded amount (自體負擔額) of 240,000 won. Please discuss the self-funded amount (自體負擔額).


--- (p. 216) ---

Kim Hee-seon (金熙善): The subsidy (하사금) should be used only for purchasing materials (자재구입비), and the self-funded amount (자체부담금) should cover the labor mobilization (노력동원) burden.
All: I agree (찬성).

Lee Ki-pyo (李基杓): For resident participation (주민노력참여), it would be best to have 3 people per household (호당) working in shifts (순위로 교대) with 20 workers per day (1일작업인원), rotating through teams 1, 2, and 3.
Chairperson (사회): Do you agree with Lee Ki-pyo's opinion (의견)?
All: I agree (동의).

Kim Sun-tae (金順泰): In case residents (주민) fail to participate (노력참여 불이행), they should pay 800 won in cash per day (1일당 800원 현금).
Chairperson (사회): Do you agree with Kim Sun-tae's opinion (의견)?
All: That's good (좋습니다).

Chairperson (사회): Then, the labor burden (노력부담) for building the communal livestock barn (공동축사) will be 3 days per household (호당 3일), with 20 people mobilized per day (1일당 20명씩) in shifts through teams 1, 2, and 3. Those who do not participate (불참) should pay 800 won in cash per day (1일당 800원씩 현금).

Kim Young-bok (金英福): After the barn is completed (축사준공후), there should be a manager (관리자) to reside and manage it (상주관리). What do you think?
All: There should be a manager (관리자).

Yu Chang-bok (柳昌福): I propose establishing a management office (관리처) for the communal livestock barn (공동축사) and paying the manager (관리자) a monthly salary (월급료) of around 20,000 won (2만원).
Chairperson (사회): Yu Chang-bok proposes having a resident manager (상주관리자) and paying a monthly salary (월급료) of 20,000 won. What are your opinions (의견)?
All: That's good (좋습니다).

Chairperson (사회): Please recommend someone for the manager (관리자).
Lee Kang-jun (李康俊): Park Byung-ho (朴炳浩), who lives in team 1, would be a good choice.
All: I agree (찬성).

Chairperson (사회): The manager (관리자) of the communal livestock barn (공동축사) has been decided to be Park Byung-ho (朴炳浩). Park Byung-ho, please make active efforts (적극노력) not to disappoint the residents' expectations (주민기대). Next, we will discuss the location (위치) and site (부지) for the communal livestock barn (공동축사). Please share your good opinions (좋은 의견).

Kim Young-bok (金英福): Since the communal livestock barn (공동축사) aims for intensive cattle raising (다두사육), it should be located (입지) where forage resources (초자원) are abundant and grazing (방목) is possible. In my opinion, I agree to build the barn (축사건립) in the Hanyang Valley (항영골). If you have any other good opinions (좋은 의견), please share them.
Chairperson (사회): Are there any other good opinions (좋은 의견)? Then, do you agree with Kim Young-bok's opinion (의견)?
All: I agree (찬성).

Chairperson (사회): The location (건립장소) for the communal livestock barn (공동축사) will be decided as Hanyang Valley (항영골). Next, please suggest where the barn (축사) should be built (들어설 장소).

Kim Sun-tae (金順泰): For intensive cattle raising (다두사육), while forage resources (초자원) are important, the location should also have easy access to water supply (급수용이). Therefore, I agree to build the barn (건립) in the current cornfield (옥수수밭) being farmed by Hwang Sun-jong (黃淳鍾).
Chairperson (사회): The location (장소) is the best, but since it is Hwang Sun-jong's property (소유), we should first invite Hwang Sun-jong to this meeting and listen to his opinion (의견). Then, we can either purchase the land (토지매입) or exchange it with the communal farmland (마을공동재산인 경작지).


--- (p. 217) ---

Under the condition that a livestock barn is to be built at that location, it seems appropriate.

Lee Gi-pyo (李基杓): I agree with the opinions presented by both of you. Then, let's invite Mr. Hwang Sun-jong (黃淳鍾) here.

All: We agree.

Hwang Sun-jong (黃淳鍾): I have heard and understood well. This is not for one person but for the village, and a project in which all residents participate. Moreover, it does not occupy a large area, so instead of the condition of selling or exchanging the land, if I donate the site and the income of the farmers increases, it would be better.

Kim Hee-seon (金熙善): Mr. Hwang Sun-jong (黃淳鍾) said he would donate the site. Let us all residents applaud and thank Mr. Hwang Sun-jong (黃淳鍾).

All: Welcome with applause.

Chairperson: The most difficult problem has been resolved by Mr. Hwang Sun-jong's (黃淳鍾) donation of the site. The location is determined to be Hwang Sun-jong's (黃淳鍾) field in Hangyeong-gol. Hwang Sun-jong, please sign and stamp the consent form for the donation of the site, and the attending residents, please also sign and stamp the meeting minutes. Thank you for today's meeting. I declare the adjournment.

### Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (3)

*   **Date (日時)**: May 1, 1974, 18:00~21:00
*   **Location (場所)**: Village Hall (會舘)
*   **Agenda (議制)**: Report on the completion of the joint livestock barn (畜舍) construction (建立) and settlement (決算)
*   **Attendees (參席 人員)**: 58 people (名)
*   **Chairperson (社會)**: Saemaul leader (指導者) Lee Kang-seop (李康燮)
*   **Recorder (記錄)**: Resident leader (駐在 指導者) Kim Jong-seong (金鍾聲)

Chairperson: With the cooperation of relevant agencies and all of you, a excellent joint livestock barn (畜舍) of 50 pyeong (坪) has been completed. We have convened this emergency general meeting (臨時 總會) to report on the progress of the project (事業) so far and to discuss the operation (運營) and management (管理) of the livestock barn (畜舍) going forward.

Lee Kang-seop (李康燮) (Development (開發) Committee Chairperson (委員長)): Report on the progress of the project (事業): If there are any objections during the report, please speak up.

All: There are no objections.

Chairperson: The financial report (決算) has been passed as there are no objections from all of you. Next, please share your good opinions (意見) on the operation (運營) and management (管理) of the joint livestock barn (畜舍) after the project (事業).

Yoo Chang-bok (劉昌福): To efficiently lead the joint project (事業), I agree that we should establish management (管理) regulations (細則) and operate (運營) and manage (管理) according to the regulations (細則).

Chairperson: Are there any other good opinions (意見)? Please speak up.

All: None.

Chairperson: Then, understanding that there are no other good opinions (意見), we will enact the management (管理) regulations (細則) here. We have a draft (草案) prepared in advance, so it would be good to discuss it one by one.


--- (p. 218) ---

# Rules for the Management and Operation of the Joint Livestock Barn

## ＜Purpose and Objectives＞
The purpose of this (本) business site (事業場) is to serve as a venue for the Saemaul Undong (運動) to instill the spirit of self-help (自助), self-reliance (自立), and cooperation (協同精神) among the villagers of Dosari (都沙里民), improve livestock farming techniques (飼育技術), and contribute to increasing farm income (農家所得).

1.  (Name (名稱)) This (本) business site (事業場) is called the Dosari Joint Livestock Barn (共同畜舍) in Yanggu-myeon (楊口面).
2.  (Ownership (所有)) The joint livestock barn (共同畜舍) and 15 head (頭) of Korean cattle (韓牛) are communal property (財産) of the village (部落).
3.  (Operation (運營))
    가. To operate (運營) this (本) business site (事業場) efficiently (效率的), the following managers (管理人) are appointed.
    O Manager in charge (管理責任): 1 person
    O Cowherd (牧夫): 1 person
    O Auditor (監査): 2 persons
    나. Duties (任務): The manager in charge (管理責任者) is responsible for (擔當) all aspects of the business (事業) and operation (運營), represents (代表) this (本) business site (事業場), and is in charge of (擔當) financial affairs (財政事務). The cowherd (牧夫) is responsible for (責任) protecting (保護) the joint property (共同財産) of the village (部落), which is the livestock barn (畜舍), and managing (飼養管理) the livestock (家畜). The auditors (監査) are responsible for (責任) auditing (監査) all operational (運營) situations (諸般狀況) at any time (隨時).
    라. Compensation (報酬) for managers (管理人)
    O The manager in charge (管理責任者) and auditors (監査) serve (奉仕) without compensation (無報酬).
    O The cowherd (牧夫) is paid (支給) a monthly (月) compensation (報酬) of 20,000 won, which will be increased (引上) as the business scale (事業規模) expands (擴張).
4.  Meetings (會議)
    Meetings (會議) are divided into regular general meetings (定期總會), extraordinary general meetings (臨時總會), and special meetings (特別會議).
    O Regular general meetings (定期總會) are held (定) twice a year (回), at the beginning (年初) and end (年末) of the year (年).
    O The beginning-of-the-year meeting (年初會議) establishes (樹立) the annual (年間) business plan (事業計劃), and
    O The end-of-the-year meeting (年末會議) reports (報告) on the annual (年間) business performance (事業實績) and settles (決算) the accounts.
    O Extraordinary general meetings (臨時總會) can be convened (召集) at any time (하시라도) if issues (問題) arise (發生) in the business (事業).
    O Special general meetings (特別總會) are convened (召集) centered around (中心) the Development Committee (開發委員會).
5.  These (本) regulations (規約) come into effect (施行) on May 1, 1974 (年月日).

Chairperson (司會): As mentioned above (以上), the management rules (管理規則) for the joint livestock barn (共同畜舍) and beef cattle (肉牛) business (事業) have been established (制定). If there are any corrections (고칠 곳) or additions (添加) to be made, please share (말씀하십시오) your opinions (意見).
All present (一同): None.
Chairperson (司會): Then, we decide (決定) to pass (通過) the management rules (管理規則) for the joint livestock barn (共同畜舍) and beef cattle (肉牛) business (事業) as mentioned above (위와 같이). Once again, we thank (感謝) you for your hard work (勞苦) during this time (동안). With this (以上), we conclude (마치겠읍니다) today's meeting (會議). Please stamp (捺印) the meeting minutes (會議錄) as you attend (參席).


--- (p. 219) ---

# Minutes (會議錄) (4)

*   **Date(日時):** October 10, 1975, 18:00
*   **Location(場所):** Village Community Center (會舘)
*   **Agenda(議題):** Economic Trend Report (經濟動向報吿) and Village Special Support Project (特別支援事業) Planning for Residents' General Assembly (住民總會)
*   **Master of Ceremonies(社會者):** Saemaul Leader Lee Kang-seop (李康燮)
*   **Recorder(記錄者):** Chief Village Leader Kim Jong-seong (金鍾聲)
*   **Attendees(參席人員):** 60 people

**Master of Ceremonies(社會):** Since the beginning of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動), with your strong will to live well, you have carried out the Saemaul project (새마을事業), resulting in our village, Dosari (都沙里), being selected as a successful case for the monthly economic trend report (經濟動向報吿). On November 5, we will have the honor of reporting this to His Excellency the President (大統領). This is all thanks to your strong belief and active participation in various projects. I would like to express my gratitude. Now, with this successful case report, we will receive 5 million won as the resident's wish project fund (住民宿願事業金). I have called you all here today to discuss how we should use this grant money. Please share your good ideas.

**Kim Young-bok (金英福):** The most urgent need in our village, Dosari (都沙里), seems to be a community warehouse (共同倉庫). Even though we have 50,000 pyeong of community farmland (共同沓), we lack a warehouse to store our produce. Therefore, I suggest we build a community warehouse (共同倉庫).

**Master of Ceremonies(社會):** Kim Young-bok (金英福) suggested using the grant money to build a community warehouse (共同倉庫). What do you all think?

**All (一同):** We agree to build a community warehouse.

**Master of Ceremonies(社會):** We have decided to build a community warehouse (共同倉庫). Now, could you please explain the profitability (收益性) of the community warehouse (共同倉庫)?

**Kim Young-bok (金英福):** If we build a community warehouse (共同倉庫), our village, Dosari (都沙里), will spend 186,000 won on storage fees in one year. Additionally, the net profit (純收益金) from storing our own farm produce and various fertilizers and materials will be 745,000 won, making the total annual profit (收益金) 931,000 won.

**All (一同):** We understand.

**Master of Ceremonies(社會):** Then, what should be the scale (建立規模) of the community warehouse (共同倉庫)?

**Yang Gwan-sun (梁寛淳):** I inquired at the county construction office (郡建設課), and they said it would cost between 600 and 650 million won to build a 60-pyeong community warehouse (共同倉庫). Therefore, I think we can build it by investing the 500 million won grant money and 150 million won from the residents' efforts.

**Master of Ceremonies(社會):** Do you all agree with Yang Gwan-sun's (梁寛淳) opinion (意見)?

**All (一同):** We agree.

**Master of Ceremonies(社會):** Then, we will build a 60-pyeong community warehouse (共同倉庫) as the grant money project (事業). This concludes today's meeting. Please sign and stamp the minutes (會議錄). Thank you.


--- (p. 220) ---

# Minutes (會議錄) (5)

*   **Date**: November 15, 1975, 19:00~21:00
*   **Location**: Village Community Center (會舘)
*   **Agenda**: Monthly Economic Trend Report (動向) and Village Grant (下賜金) Business for the Construction of a Joint Warehouse (倉庫)

*   **Chairperson (司會者)**: Lee Kang-seop (李康燮)
*   **Recorder (記錄者)**: Resident Advisor (駐在 導者) Kim Jong-seong (金鍾聲)
*   **Attendees (參席 人員)**: 65 people (名)
*   **Absentees (不參 人員)**: 5 people (名)

**Chairperson (司會)**: On November 5, 1975, our village was selected as an outstanding New Village nationwide (全國). We have the honor of reporting successful cases during the monthly economic trend report (動向). This is all thanks to your hard work and sweat. I would like to express my gratitude. For this report, the President (大統領) grant (下賜金) business (事業) will fund the construction of a joint warehouse (倉庫) (60 pyeong) in our village. The funds of 5,000,000 won will be transferred from the Governor of Gangwon-do (江原道) on November 19, 1975. The design (設計書) for the joint warehouse (倉庫) has been received from the county (郡). If you have any good opinions (意見) on promoting this business (事業), please speak up.

**Yang Gwan-soon (梁寛淳)**: For promoting this business (事業), the total construction cost (工事費) is 6,200,000 won, with 5,000,000 won being the grant (下賜金) and 1,200,000 won being the self-funded portion (自體 負擔金). First, we need to decide on a method to secure the self-funded portion (自體 負擔金).

**Lee Gi-pyo (李基杓)**: From a design (設計) perspective, the grant (下賜金) of 5,000,000 won should be sufficient for purchasing materials (資材). Currently, material prices are rising, but we can purchase them. Let's make efforts to cover the self-funded portion (自體 負擔金).

**Chairperson (司會)**: Do you agree with Lee Gi-pyo's opinion (意見)?

**All (一同)**: We agree (贊成).

**Chairperson (司會)**: Are there any other good opinions (意見)?

**All (一同)**: None.

**Chairperson (司會)**: We have agreed to cover the self-funded portion (自體 負擔金) through efforts (努力).

**Yu Geun-jae (柳根在)**: I would like to hear opinions (意見) on mobilizing labor (勞力).

**Chairperson (司會)**: If you have any good opinions (意見) on mobilizing labor (勞力), please speak up.

**Kim Sun-tae (金順泰)**: During the construction period (工事 期間), I agree to assign personnel (人員) required for the progress (進度) of the work to teams 1, 2, and 3 in rotation (輪番制).

**Chairperson (司會)**: Do you agree with Kim Sun-tae's opinion (意見)?

**All (一同)**: We agree (贊成).

**Chairperson (司會)**: If you have any other good opinions (意見), please speak up.

**All (一同)**: None.

**Chairperson (司會)**: We will proceed with the work in rotation (輪番制) for teams 1, 2, and 3. Next, if you have any efficient methods (方法) for managing the funds (資金), please share your opinions (意見).


--- (p. 221) ---

Kim Young-bok (金英福): I believe that the most efficient way to manage funds is to deposit all business funds in the name of the Agricultural Cooperative (農協) and use them for business expenses (事業費) as decided by the Development Committee (開發委員會). This would be an efficient method of fund management.

Chairperson (社會): Do you agree with Kim Young-bok's (金英福) opinion?

All (一同): We agree.

Chairperson (社會): Are there any other good opinions?

Kim Sun-tae (金順泰): I agree with Kim Young-bok's (金英福) opinion and would like to add something.

Chairperson (社會): Would you accept Kim Sun-tae's (金順泰) additional remarks as an opinion?

Kim Young-bok (金英福): Yes, I will accept it.

Kim Sun-tae (金順泰): There are two types of joint accounts (共同名義). First, in the name of all village residents (住民), and second, in the name of the development committee members (開發委員) elected at the general assembly (總會). Among these, I think it is more efficient and faster to operate under the name of the development committee members (開發委員), reducing complexity (複雜性) and promoting business (事業) progress. I agree to add that three development committee members (開發委員) should be selected to manage the funds jointly (共同名義).

All (一同): We agree (unanimously, 滿場一致).

Chairperson (社會): Please elect three development committee members (開發委員).

Kim Sun-tae (金順泰): I suggest Lee Kang-seop (李康燮), Yang Gwan-sun (梁寛淳), and Ryu Myung-hun (柳明勳).

All (一同): We agree.

Chairperson (社會): The three development committee members (開發委員) will jointly manage (共同名義) the business funds (事業資金). For the operation and management of the joint warehouse (共同倉庫), after completion (竣工), the general assembly (總會) will establish and implement an operation plan (運營計劃). If any issues arise during the construction period (工事期間), a meeting (會議) will be held to devise a solution (處理方案). The Development Committee (開發委員會) will be fully responsible for construction supervision (工事監督). That concludes today's meeting. Finally, please sign and stamp the minutes (會議錄). Thank you.

## ♦ Minutes (會議錄) (6)

*   Date (日時): January 20, 1977, 20:00-22:00
*   Venue (場所): Village Community Center (會館)
*   Agenda (議題): Fundraising Plan for Storage Warehouse (貯藏庫設置) Construction
*   Chairperson (司會者): Saemaul Leader Lee Kang-seop (李康燮)
*   Recorder (記錄者): Kim Jong-seong (金鍾聲), Chief Saemaul Leader
*   Attendees (參席人員): 59 people (名)

Chairperson (社會): The reason we have gathered for this village general assembly (總會) today is to share with you the results of my visit to the Ministry of Home Affairs (內務部) on December 2, 1976, where I met with the Minister (長官). The Minister praised your cooperation (協同) and unity (團結) in actively participating (參與) in the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) and developing our village into the best in the nation (全國最優秀). He encouraged us to continue our efforts in village development (部落開發) and promised to support our long-cherished project (宿願事業) of building a vegetable storage warehouse (菜蔬貯藏倉庫) with 1.5 million won (萬圓). Today, we have convened this general assembly (總會) to discuss the promotion of this project. If you have any good opinions on the establishment and promotion of the storage warehouse (貯藏庫設立推進), please share them.


--- (p. 222) ---

Kim Sun-tae (金順泰): First, please explain the effects of the project after the storage facility is installed.
Chairperson (社 會): The purpose of promoting this project is that although we supply 500,000 kg of vegetables to the military annually, we suffer damages due to surplus production, with 200,000 kg remaining. If we store them in winter and release them in spring, we can sell them at a higher price, and they can also be used as air-raid shelters, achieving dual effects. I believe you understand the circumstances of promoting this project. If you have any good opinions, please speak up.
Lee Mun-u (李冕雨): Yes, I understand your explanation. Then, please tell us about the scale of the project and the estimated project cost.
Chairperson (社 會): Yes, I will. The project name is Vegetable Storage Facility, the scale is 30 pyeong for one building, and the estimated project cost is 3,500,000 won, with 1,500,000 won as special support funds and 2,000,000 won as self-funded amount.
All (一 同): We understand (All agree).
Chairperson (社 會): The proposal for the Vegetable Storage Facility has been passed unanimously. Out of the total project cost of 3,500,000 won, 1,500,000 won is the support fund, and 2,000,000 won is the self-funded amount. If you have any good opinions on the measures to raise the self-funded amount, please speak up.
Yoo Chang-bok (劉昌福): For raising the self-funded amount, I agree to cover it with 1,000,000 won from the village fund and 1,000,000 won from effort burden.
Chairperson (社 會): Do you agree with Yoo Chang-bok's (劉昌福) agreement?
All (一 同): We agree.
Chairperson (社 會): Does anyone have any other opinions?
All (一 同): No other opinions.
Chairperson (社 會): Then, we will invest 2,000,000 won in this project with 1,000,000 won in cash from the village fund and 1,000,000 won from effort burden, as agreed by Yoo Chang-bok (劉昌福).
All (一 同): No objections (applause of agreement).
Kim Young-bae (金永培): I agree to entrust the Development Committee (委員會) with all matters during the project promotion period.
All (一 同): We agree.
Chairperson (社 會): We will promote the project as decided by you during the project period, entrusted by the Development Committee (委員會). I declare the closure of today's meeting. Finally, please sign and stamp the meeting minutes (會議錄).

# 4. Future Development Vision

Looking at the development vision of Dosari (都沙里) village, which has achieved prosperity through the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement):

- **Production (生産) Base Establishment (造成) Projects**
  - Install one reservoir of 3,000 pyeong and two irrigation channels of 500m each, and two improved furrows of 1,610m to create 45,000 pyeong of reclaimed land, expanding farmland.
- **Management Modernization (經營 近代化) Facilities**


--- (p. 223) ---

Improved livestock barns (5-head capacity) with 40 new buildings were constructed, allowing each farm household to raise 5 heads of livestock. Two agricultural product drying facilities were established, 20 buildings for drying tobacco leaves were constructed, and 50 stoves were installed. Additionally, 10 more cultivators (currently owning 13 units) were purchased, and one vehicle for transporting agricultural products was bought to boost both agricultural and non-agricultural income.

### For the income augmentation plan:

High-yield rice varieties will be cultivated across the entire area. Beef cattle breeding will be expanded by 300 heads, military supply vegetable farming will be increased by 50,000 pyeong, and tobacco cultivation will cover 45,000 pyeong. Additionally, the collection of forest products such as medicinal herbs, mushrooms, and acorns will be increased, and high-quality products will continue to be produced, with an annual production target of 10,000 units. Yanggu County aims to become the wealthiest village not only in the region but across the entire country.

### Once the above income-generating projects are completed, the village infrastructure improvement project will be undertaken to pave the way for constructing an ideal rural community.

### The annual income plan shows:

- 1977: 1,600,000 won
- 1978: 1,900,000 won
- 1979: 2,200,000 won
- 1980: 2,500,000 won
- 1981: 2,800,000 won

This will create a prosperous Saemaul Undong village to be passed down to future generations.

# Gangwon (江原) Myeongju-gun (溟州郡) Seongsan-myeon (城山面) Geumsan (金山) 2-ri

## 1. Overview of the Village

### Ga. History

*   During the reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, the area was part of the Four Commanderies and belonged to the land of Imdun (臨屯). In the era of Goguryeo (高句麗), it was called "Haseorang" (下西郞).
*   In the 16th year of King Gyeongdeok of Silla (新羅) (757 AD), Haseobu (下西府) was promoted to Myeongju (溟州), becoming the capital of Kim Ju-won (金周元), the ancestor of the Gangneung Kim clan (江陵金氏), and was also called GeonGeum (建金). In the 19th year of King Taejo of Goryeo (高麗) (936 AD), it was renamed Donggyeong (東京), and among the 12 myeons (面), it belonged to Seongsan-myeon (城山面). It was renamed Geumsan-ri (金山里) (Geumsan-ri) because many Kim clan members lived there.
*   On August 13, 1955, with the promotion of Gangneung (江陵) to city status, Gangneung-gun (江陵郡) was renamed Myeongju-gun (溟州郡), and the village was named Myeongju-gun (溟州郡) Seongsan-myeon (城山面) Geumsan (金山) 2-ri (里), a name that has persisted to the present.
*   The 1,000-year-old ginkgo tree with a circumference of 12 meters in the village center stands as a testament to the village's long history.
*   Nearby mountainous areas are home to centuries-old pine trees and other trees that attest to the theory of Ho Song-seol (李珥), as well as abundant forest and livestock resources.
*   The village is renowned for its scenic beauty, with cultural heritage sites that were once enjoyed by scholars, such as the Imgyeongdang (地方有型文化財 46號 臨溪堂). Even today, the scattered but neatly arranged traditional houses from the Joseon Dynasty (李祖時代) blend harmoniously with improved housing from the village improvement project, creating a picturesque blend of past and present.
*   Known as a cultural hub and a town of letters, the village has a strong Confucian tradition (儒學), with most residents holding conservative views but possessing cheerful and helpful personalities.

### Na. Location and Conditions

#### <Location>

*   Located 8 km west of Gangneung (江陵), this village is a plain settlement with the Yeongdong Expressway (嶺東高速道路) running in front of it. Across the river in front of the village lies the Junsan (准山) village of Gangneung City (江陵市).
*   To the west of the village, about 25 km away, stands Daegwallyeong (大關嶺), a mountain peak with an elevation of 800 meters, marking the boundary between Gangneung City (江陵市) and Myeongju-gun (溟州郡).

#### <Conditions>

*   The dense pine forests on the village's rear mountain and the countless persimmon trees that have been growing for 30 years within the village turn the entire village into a beautiful canvas of red persimmons in the autumn.


--- (p. 225) ---

Well-maintained farmland yields bumper crops year after year, bringing prosperity, and as it is adjacent to Gangneung City, 20 residents are employed at various agencies and organizations in Gangneung City, while middle and high school students commute to Gangneung City for school.

## 2. Village Development (發展) Process (過程)

### A. Situation (狀況) Before 1970 (70年 以前)

#### <Overview (槪況)>

- The legacy of defeatist attitudes (敗北意識) and despair (失意) inherited from ancestors, along with the continuous vicious cycle (惡循環) of poverty, led many residents (住民) to abandon rural areas (農村) and yearn for urban life (都市).
- This decline in farmers' (農民) production will (生産 意慾) and dispersal of labor (勞動力) became a major cause (主要 原因) of the annual occurrence of families facing food shortages (絶糧農家).
- As the 1960s (年代) began, President (大統領) Park Chung-hee's (朴 總統) steadfast belief (堅固 信念) in rural modernization (農村 近代化) laid the foundation for a new history (歷史) to be created in Geumsan (金山) village.
- With an unyielding will (不撓不屈 意志) toward national modernization (祖國 近代化) and in response (呼應), the residents (住民) of Geumsan (金山) village rose resolutely (決然) and their collective efforts (努力) began in 1969 (年), bolstered by the high rice price (高米價) policy (政策), to boost production (生産) and increase yields (增產).
- Through the special income-increasing project (所得增大 特別 事業) for farmers and fishermen (農魚民), Geumsan (金山) village expanded the beef cattle (肥肉牛) project (事業) annually (年次的) starting from 1968 (年度).
- Before 1970 (70年 以前), the village's form (形態) transitioned from traditional farming (過去 農事) for sustenance to commercial farming (農事) for profit (利潤).

#### <Village Environment (環境)>

- At the center of the village, an unpaved national road (非鋪裝 國道) wound through the area, with about 40 thatched houses (初家) scattered across the farmland (耕地), their mud walls blackened and covered in cobwebs (蜘蛛網).
- Adjacent to the kitchens (廚房) were dilapidated barns (外廐間), their thick excrement (排泄物) flowing into the courtyard (마당) and creating a quagmire (泥窪).
- Despite having fallow land (垡地) areas exceeding 20 times the house's floor area (建坪), the only path leading to the houses was along the rice paddy dikes (稻田 墘), with no farm roads (農路) and even rickshaws (人力車) struggling to pass through the increasingly eroded (侵蝕) and stagnant (沈滯) village entrance (進入路).

#### <Income (所得) Level (水準)>

- In Geumsan (金山) 2-ri (里) village, only 33% of households (農家) were self-sufficient (自立) in farming (營農), and while 67% of households (家口) relied on farming (農事) as their main occupation (主業), they were unable to achieve self-sufficiency (自立 營農). Additionally, 43% of farming households (農家) engaged in small-scale (小規模) farming (營農) of less than 0.5 hectares (0.5ha 以下), depending on rice cultivation (水稻作) and barley farming (大麥 農事) on sloped fields (斜坡 田) for their livelihood (生計).
- In the 1960s (年代), along with improvements in farming methods (營農 方法), the special income-increasing project (所得增大 特別 事業) for rural areas (農漁村) was implemented starting from 1968 (年度).


--- (p. 227) ---

Through the business of fattening cattle (비육우(肥肉牛) 사업), which was expanded annually (연차적(年次的)으로 확대실시(擴大實施)), the foundation was laid for significantly improving farmers' income (농가소득(農家所得)), reaching 285,000 won per household (호당(戶當)) by 1970. However, with this income, households were still struggling to make ends meet, and by spring, many were facing absolute food shortages (절량(絶糧) 농가(農家)).

### Mental State (정신상태(精神狀態))
- The residents of this village had, since the mid-19th century, been deeply influenced by Confucian scholars and yangban (권세가나 사대부) who looked down on physical labor (육체노동(肉體勞動)), leading to a generations-long (자자손손(子子孫孫)) aversion to labor among their descendants. This resulted in the bad habit of ensuring their children would not become farmers.
- The feudalistic (봉건사상(封建思想)) village of Geumsan (금산(金山)마을) had intense power struggles (세력(勢力) 다툼) and internal conflicts (씨족내(氏族內) 불화) among clans (씨족간(氏族間)), leading to frequent instances of drinking, swearing, and violence.
- It was not until the late 1960s that the residents' mindset began to change, influenced by the government's "human transformation" (인간개조(人間改造)) ideology, which aimed to reform the national spirit (국민정신(國民精神) 개조(改造) 사상(思想)).

### Cultural Life (문화(文化)생활(生活))
- The residents of Geumsan (금산(金산)마을) lacked a spirit of self-reliance (자주정신(自主精神)) and self-help (자조정신(自助精神)), blaming their poverty on ancestral inheritance (조상(祖上)의 유산(遺產)) and societal responsibility (사회적(社會的) 책임(責任)) rather than taking personal responsibility.
- It was only in the late 1960s that this mindset began to improve, with residents becoming less dependent on others and less reliant on luck. As urban civilization (도시문명(都市文明)) advanced, they began to appreciate its benefits and yearn for a more cultured life (문화(文化)생활). By 1970, the increase in cultural facilities (문화시설(文化施設)) showed the following trends:

### Clothing, Food, and Shelter (의식주(衣食住) 생활(生活))
- The roadsides, covered in white dust, were lined with thatch-roofed houses and outbuildings, where farmers lived in rags and filth.
- In winter, military blankets were considered luxury items, and during the hungry summer months (오뉴월 보릿고개), they survived on long-grain rice (장리(長利)쌀) or tree bark (초근목피).
- If a bumper harvest (풍년(豊年)) occurred, they had no time to enjoy rice before worrying about the falling rice prices.
- To afford necessities like rubber shoes, they had to carry firewood they had stolen to the markets of Gangneung (강릉시내(江陵市內)) at dawn.
- Opening the door, made from fertilizer sacks covered with paper, they would enter a room with three sleeping mats or straw mats spread on the floor.


--- (p. 228) ---

The village floor was marked with stripes from children's excrement.
○ The dark kitchen had its ceiling and walls blackened by smoke, and the adjacent livestock shed (畜舍) had cows' heads always poking inside, allowing flies from the cattle shed to freely move between the shed and the kitchen.
○ The cramped outhouse had wooden planks soaked in urine, which were also used as a storage shed (倉庫) for farming tools (農機具). This was the past way of life encompassing clothing, food, and shelter (衣食住), which people accepted as their fate (宿命).

## B. The Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

### 1) Motives (動機) and Experimental Project (試驗 事業) Results (成果)
○ For a long time, the villagers' distrust (不信), ignorance (無知), and laziness (懶怠), along with the jealousy that "if my cousin plows four inches of land, I feel pain in my back," and poverty, never left the village.
○ As the economic development plan (經濟開發計劃) progressed successfully in the 1960s (年代), signs of economic growth (經濟成長) and changes in the villagers' consciousness (意識) structure (構造) began to emerge, leading into the 1970s (年代).
○ On April 22, 1970 (年), President Park (朴大統領) proclaimed the Saemaul Undong (運動), which reached our village in 1971.
○ Kim Seon-gi (金善起), aged 52, who had dedicated himself to public service (公職) for years and returned to his hometown (故鄕) due to family matters (家事), took on the role of village chief (里長職). With a firm belief (信念) in turning our village into a prosperous one, he convened a general village meeting (住民總會) and initiated the Saemaul project (事業).
○ However, the villagers' latent jealousy (嫉妬), complacency (安逸), and divisions (分裂) remained unchanged. Kim (金氏), determined to dedicate himself to the village, decided to start with fostering the villagers' spirit (住民精神) and organized the "Saemaul Farming Association (營農會)" with about 20 young and middle-aged villagers (靑壯年), including Kim Seong-nam (金星南). They promoted six campaigns (運動):
* A village without idle people
* A village without gamblers
* A village without idle land
* A village without extravagance and waste
* A village that eliminates those who should not exist
* A village without superstitions (迷信)

They formed three guidance teams (指導班), assigned responsibilities to each team, and held multiple village meetings (部落會議) with the women's association (婦女會), 4-H clubs, agricultural reform (農改) leaders, and life reform (生改) leaders to successfully foster the villagers' spirit (住民精神) through persistent efforts (努力), which began to show results (反應).

○ Moreover, during the farming off-season (農閑期), they utilized the idle labor force (遊休 勞動力) to encourage the production of sacks and twine (紗). They held reconstruction (再建) competitions (競演大會) for each team (班別) and awarded mirrors (one per winner) from personal funds (私費) to the winners, creating a significant opportunity (契機) to promote agricultural side businesses (農家副業).

○ Based on the changing villagers' consciousness (住民意識構造), the first project (事業) they undertook was expanding and constructing facilities (構造物) for a 200-meter village access road (進入路) connecting the national road (國道) to the village (部落). Although this had been a long-standing village aspiration (宿願事業), the landowners (所有者) could not agree to donate their farmland (農耕地) for the access road (進入路). Thus, it was decided at the general village meeting (住民總會) to proceed as an experimental project (試驗事業) with government-supported (政府支援) cement (洋灰) totaling 335 bags (袋). They constructed two underground drainage pipes (暗渠) and installed four soil pipe systems (土管埋設) at four locations (個所).


--- (p. 229) ---

Work began in earnest.
*   Extending the 200m access road involved incorporating 100 pyeong of adjacent farmland into road land, requiring donations from 7 landowners. This was no easy task.
*   Despite this, Kim Seon-gi (金善起) managed to secure donations from Kim Yeol-gi (金烈起) and 4 other households through persistent persuasion and understanding. However, the remaining 3 households continued to refuse.
*   Remembering the proverb "Sincerity moves heaven," leader Kim (金指導者) worked with agricultural cooperative officials and village elders to individually persuade the remaining 3 households over 10 meetings, finally securing their donations. This allowed the construction of 7 structures and the extension of the 200m access road, involving 760 people and an investment of 2,500,000 won, successfully completing a major trial project that had previously seemed impossible.

2) Leader's Activities
<Leader's Activities>
*   Empowered, village head Kim (金氏) decided that there was no task the villagers couldn't accomplish together. Adopting the Saemaul spirit of diligence, self-help, and cooperation as his life motto, he took the lead in all matters. The villagers began rising earlier to clean the village access road, repair irrigation channels, and improve auxiliary buildings, transforming their surroundings. They drew up annual business plans and repeatedly revised them to outpace neighboring villages in development. They also requested support from relevant agencies and began work on the 1972 projects. To facilitate intra-village opinion coordination and strengthen driving force, Kim Jang-gi (金障起), a prominent village figure, was recommended as the male leader, and Kim Jeong-suk (金貞淑), the village women's association president, as the female leader. They were elected by village consensus, and various self-generated organizations were strengthened, leading to an integrated system.
*   That year's projects included, as supported projects, the construction of a 25 pyeong village community center and the early completion of roof improvements for 20 buildings, as well as, as self-supported projects, the stone paving of a 20m access road and the improvement of the national highway fence. These projects involved 128 villagers. In 1973, they undertook the expansion of the intra-village road by 120m, roof improvements, and the maintenance of agricultural water facilities, among other projects.
*   Accompanied by development committee members, they visited the Myeon (面) head and county magistrate multiple times to request the relocation and improvement of scattered houses within farmland and the planning of farmland reorganization projects. Fortunately, the government's development policy direction aligned with their needs, and in 1974, an enormous large-scale project was designated for Geumsan (金山) village.
*   Although many projects were planned by village consensus, given the village's actual circumstances at the time, it was truly challenging to ensure their successful implementation.
*   However, village head Kim Seon-gi (金善起), in consultation with Saemaul leaders and development committee members, decided to push forward with all projects and convened a village general assembly.
*   The project contents included improving 26 scattered houses within farmland into standardized thermally efficient houses while relocating them to the foothills in groups, farmland reorganization over 56ha, the maintenance of a 3600m stream, the repair of 36 houses, and house relocations.


--- (p. 230) ---

The attached houses (부속사(附屬舍)), wall improvement (담장개량(改良)), etc., were indeed major projects. When a village meeting (주민총회(住民總會)) was held to promote the projects, few residents responded positively. Those with slightly better housing structures were entirely opposed, while those with poor housing opposed the projects due to lack of financial resources (재력(財力)). The land readjustment project (경지정리사업(耕地整理事業)) faced strong opposition from the elderly, who had an emotional attachment to their ancestral land and argued that they had managed farming well without such projects.

The first village meeting (1차(次) 총회(總會)) ended without reaching a conclusion. Kim Seon-gi (김선기(金善起)), the leader, individually persuaded capable residents of the project's necessity and secured a few supporters before convening another meeting. With the efforts of the village development committee (이개발위원(里開發委員)) and supporters, more than half of the residents showed positive reactions, but the meeting ended without a conclusion. A third meeting (3차(次) 회의(會議)) was held with special guidance from the county (군(郡)) Saemaul Undong office staff, the county magistrate (군수(郡守)), and the village head (면장(面長)). It was decided to postpone the land readjustment project until autumn and prioritize housing improvement (주택개량(住宅改良)) and relocation (이주사업(移住事業)). To secure land (야지확보(垡地確保)), Kim, the village head (김이장(金里長)), offered 200 pyeong (坪) of his land, persuading most residents to agree on the projects, except for a few staunch opponents.

Thus began the great project that changed the village's history. Housing improvement and relocation were carried out with a loan of 600,000 won per unit (棟當) and a resident's share of 200,000 won, with the total project cost ranging from 300,000 to 500,000 won. To save on the budget (예산절감(豫算節減)), all materials were purchased collectively. Kim, the village head, devoted himself tirelessly, and the residents worked hard, completing 26 units of relocation, 33 units of new construction and repair of attached houses, and 2,700 meters of wall improvement by that autumn. Additionally, with partial support from the agricultural cooperative (농협(農協)), a communal kitchen and other projects like sewer installation, repair, and roof improvement were completed simultaneously.

However, the large-scale land readjustment project awaited the exhausted residents. Although the administrative agency had completed the project implementation plan and started the initial stages, some residents' strong opposition became more serious. The project progressed through village meetings and individual persuasion, but another major problem arose. The shallow soil and gravel land turned all farmland into gravel fields. With the farming season approaching, removing hundreds of tons of stones from the fields and planting seedlings seemed impossible.

The residents, exhausted and disheartened, turned to Kim, the village head, and the leaders for help. Through the county's mediation, they requested support from various sectors. As the saying goes, "Heaven helps those who help themselves," with the efforts of high school students and the reserve army platoon from five schools in Gangneung City (강릉시(江陵市)), the stone removal work was completed before the farming season, and support for seedling planting was also provided.

However, pursuing two major projects left the residents with significant debts, and complaints arose that their family assets were being squandered due to overly ambitious project planning and execution. Exhausted, Kim Seon-gi, the village head, and the Saemaul Undong leader Kim Jang-gi (김장기(金障起)) resigned from their positions.

### Leader Replacement

On July 1, 1975, a village meeting was held to elect successors for the village head and the Saemaul Undong leader. However, no one came forward to take over the complex task of completing the two projects, just as no one had three years earlier when a neighboring village had moved here.


--- (p. 231) ---

The current leader, Ham Yeon-go (35 years old), decided to take on the role and resolve all the issues to lead the village. The entire community unanimously elected him.

O Ham, who served as both the village head (里長) and the Saemaul leader, dedicated himself day and night to the convenience and problem-solving for the residents. He personally took the initiative to handle difficult tasks without relying on the residents, which inspired the villagers to participate vigorously in the Saemaul Undong again. In 1975, they completed the improvement of a 3,600m small river in the land consolidation area and self-reliantly promoted projects such as roadside fence improvement, kitchen improvement, and toilet improvement along the national road.

O That year, they received a special support fund of 100,000 won from President (大統領) for being an outstanding village and built a 25-pyeong (坪) community warehouse next to the meeting hall (會舘). In 1976, they completed the water supply facility for 36 households early, and promoted various welfare and income-generating projects such as creating living fences, expanding lanes, roof painting, installing amplifiers, introducing beef cattle, village seedling nurseries, planting fruit trees, and collective land improvement in the land consolidation area. They increased the per capita income from 950,000 won to 1,287,000 won and established a Saemaul savings bank, creating assets of 1,200,000 won within a year. As a result, the village was designated as the only foreign publicity target in the province in 1977, attracting many domestic and international visitors.

O In 1977, they paved the village entrance road (350m), constructed a waterway (100m), covered sewers (80m), introduced beef cattle (250 head), conducted test cultivation of sweet potatoes in paddy fields, planted improved persimmon trees, created a fund, promoted poplar tree planting, and improved the environment of all traditional toilets in the village by installing flush toilets and renovating kitchens with tiles. They also installed a postal telephone for the first time in the village's history, enhancing cultural life. Additionally, they received the national Saemaul commendation.

### 3) Overcoming Difficulties (隘路克服)

O In 1974, during the final stage of the land consolidation project, which was beyond the residents' capabilities, hundreds of trucks of excavated rocks and gravels piled up. Fearing that farming would be impossible if not completely removed before the farming season, the residents protested to the village head, Kim Seon-gi, demanding that he take full responsibility for their survival and assume all debts incurred from the housing relocation and land consolidation projects.

O Village head Kim collapsed from exhaustion. The county government, after extensive research, secured the active cooperation of the Gangneung Education Superintendent and the Gangneung Police Chief. They mobilized 1,300 high school students and 7,000 regional reservists from five local high schools to volunteer their labor. Like ants, they gathered the rocks, restoring the farmland before the farming season. Additionally, 12 local agencies participated in supporting the rice transplanting volunteers, demonstrating unity and revitalizing the discouraged residents.

O Although farming was resumed in the land consolidation area, the first-year harvest was less than half of the previous year due to the rocky soil. Thus, the theory that large-scale land improvement was essential for increased production resurfaced in the fall of that year, and countermeasures were discussed.


--- (p. 232) ---

To bring in at least 18,000 tons of soil to a 30-hectare area, 6 million won was required. While 3 million won from the county Saemaul income fund and up to 3 million won from residents were smoothly decided, the issue of securing the land for soil excavation remained unresolved. Despite searching everywhere and pleading with nearby landowners, the efforts proved futile. The successor leader, Ham, knew about a family-owned mountain from his previous residence. From that day, he visited elder family members to persuade and plead, eventually obtaining permission to excavate the land despite opposition from some family members. Immediately, heavy machinery was deployed, and the development committee members were assigned to work sites to push forward. As a result, the goal of bringing in 18,000 tons of soil was achieved within the set period. The following year, an additional 12,000 tons of soil and fertilizer were added. In 1977, the harvest per 3.3 square meters reached 480 kg, securing a second-place comprehensive award in the provincial high-yield assessment and earning a prize of 300,000 won. This reaffirmed the truth that the rewards of hard work are inevitable.

## 5) Heartwarming Stories

O Mrs. Kim Jeong-suk (金貞淑) (51), the women's association president of Geumsan (金山) Village's 2nd neighborhood, has been praised by the residents for her leadership role among women since 1971.
O After her husband retired from his teaching position in 1964, she took on the role with a strong desire to improve the residents' lives despite the difficult rural lifestyle. She also organized various forms of assistance to reduce the workload of the men.
O During the annual planting event, she operated a communal kitchen to help reduce the workload.
O Women took the lead in managing the village savings bank, implementing a policy of one account per family and promoting thrift. Starting with 16 members at the end of 1975, the village savings bank now has 130 members and assets of 500,000 won, truly becoming a Saemaul bank.
O In 1974, a communal kitchen was established with the help of Kim Chun-gi (金春起) and Ham Yeong-rim (咸永麟), who volunteered their carpentry and related skills. The residents still praise their beautiful hearts during village meetings.

### Ma. Various Organizations and Activity Achievements in the Village

#### <Saemaul Women's Association>

-   Along with 20-plus members, Kim Jeong-suk (金貞淑), the 51-year-old president of the Saemaul Women's Association, held regular weekly meetings to support struggling villagers through neighborhood assistance campaigns. From 1971 to 1976, they donated 3.5 *mal* of rice and 20 pieces of clothing to 21 people across 7 generations.
-   The association, along with 4-H members, produced over 30 tons of village compost in 1977, contributing to food production efforts.
-   The Saemaul spirit fostered by the women's association leaders encouraged village women to work diligently in the fields during the farming season and make the most of their leisure time by foraging or silkworm farming during the off-season.

#### <4-H Members>

-   Under the banner of the four-leaf "clover" symbolizing knowledge, virtue, labor, and health, 25 4-H members, led by Kim Nam-yong (金南龍), gathered regularly in the village. They acquired various promotional materials and technical education from the Rural Guidance Center to improve and elevate their lives, playing a guiding role.
-   From 1971 to 1976, they contributed significantly to various projects, including the renovation and repair of 38 houses, the construction and repair of 33 annexes, and the improvement of 2,700 meters of fencing. Their efforts were instrumental in the surrounding development projects for the completion of the Yeongdong Expressway in 1975, demonstrating unified leadership and a central role in promoting the village.

### Ba. Achievements through the Saemaul Movement

#### 1) Spiritual Aspect

-   The village experienced firsthand the core spiritual elements of the Saemaul Movement: diligence, self-help, and cooperation. They realized that to become modern villagers, they must possess the basic spiritual attitude of making correct judgments, living meaningful lives, and engaging in fulfilling activities.
-   Through the Saemaul Movement, they understood that no one else could improve their lives unless they built a foundation by uniting their strengths.

#### 2) Lifestyle Aspect

-   As spiritual development progressed, villagers naturally rejected superficial customs and embraced the practicality of home rituals. They came to value substance over form, respect rationality, and eliminate irrationalities, concluding that humans should live humanely.
-   With widened and well-maintained village roads and a scientific approach to farming, various crops and fruits appeared more abundant than ever. This fostered a culture of frugality and thrift among the villagers, helping them adopt the attitude of cultured individuals through the Saemaul Movement.

#### 3) Production Aspect


--- (p. 236) ---

*   The effects of implementing scientific farming (科學) from traditional methods (在來式) awakened the wisdom (智慧) of the farmers (農民) themselves.
*   Through Saemaul communal work (共同作業), the focus shifted from staple grain production (主穀生產) to livestock (畜產), high-quality vegetable (高等蔬菜) farming, and mulching (멀칭) of field crops (田作物). This helped overcome the backwardness (後進性) and precariousness (零細性) of the past, leading to the improvement (改善) and development (發展) of diversified farming techniques (多角營農技術) that allow for continuous production (生產) regardless of the season (季節).

## 4) Income Aspect (所得面)

*   As the Saemaul movement (事業) is directly linked (直結) to income (所得), production income (生產所得) projects (事業) have been carried out. During the farming off-season (農閑期), efforts have been focused on Saemaul beautification (事業), while during the busy farming season (農繁期), the emphasis has been on increasing income (所得增大). This has led to the sustained (永續化) development of the countryside (農村) with a spirit of self-help (自助) and self-reliance (自立). Projects such as collective farming (集團栽培), joint pest control (共同防除), compost production (堆肥增產), soil improvement (客土事業), land leveling (피뽑기), afforestation with fruit trees (有實樹造林), and sandbank afforestation (沙防造林) have been promoted annually (年次的), resulting in increased household income (戶當所得).
*   Consequently, in 1977, the income target of 1,630,000 won per household was exceeded, achieving 1,800,000 won.
*   In 1978, efforts are being made to reach an income of 2,000,000 won.

## 3. Future Development Vision (發展構想)

*   The main reason for the transformation of Geumsan (金山) village from its past state to a prosperous community is the dedicated service (獻身的) of the Saemaul leaders (指導者), their strong determination (執念), and the unity (團結) and cooperative spirit (協同精神) of the residents (住民), along with their frugal (勤儉) and thrifty (節約) culture. This is a natural outcome (結果) of these factors.
*   The transformed Geumsan village now attracts visits and study tours (見學) from all over the country (全國).
*   Ham Yeon-ho (咸衍鎬), the Saemaul leader, has designed the village's future development plan (事業計劃) with the conviction (信念) of making it the wealthiest (富者) village in the country (全國) during the 1980s (年代).

The villagers are diligently working towards increasing production (增產) today, guided by the wisdom (經綸) of President (大統領) and the spirit (精神) of the Saemaul movement, with the resolve (意志) that "it can be done."

# 4. Residents' Assembly (住民總會)
Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (1)

**Date (日時):** 71.12.24. 20:30
**Location (場所):** Kim Seon-gi's (里長) house, inner room
**Agenda (議題):** Village road expansion (擴張)
**Attendees (參席人員):** 72 people (名)
**Chairperson (司會者):** Kim Seon-gi (里長)

**Chairperson (司會者):** Good evening, fellow villagers. I apologize for calling you out so late. This is the first time all 72 villagers have gathered in one place.
The room is a bit cramped, but please bear with it and participate in the meeting seriously. I appreciate your understanding.
I have called you all here because the district office has provided us with 335 bags of cement. This cement is for our villagers to use with our own hands to improve our village environment (環境).
So, please discuss freely how we can effectively utilize these 335 bags of cement.

**Kim Young-rae:** It's great that we have cement. I think we should use it to exchange with city people for pipes (土管) to install in the waterways, as our ox carts (牛車) often can't pass when fully loaded due to the many waterways.

**Jeong Jin-cheol:** Instead of that, why don't we make the pipes ourselves and install them?

**Kim Young-rae:** No, we don't have the technology (技術) or equipment (器具) for that. Don't say things that won't work. Making pipes (土管) requires special (特殊) technology (技術).

**Kim Seong-nam:** Since we have precious cement, why don't we distribute it to each household to improve their kitchens (改良)?

**Kim Dong-gi:** It should be used for communal projects (共同事業), not for individual (個人) needs. Individuals should buy what they need themselves.

**Chairperson (司會者):** As Kim Dong-gi said, we cannot use it for individual (個人) purposes. We must use it for the village community (共同). Under the principle (原則) that cement is to be used for communal (共同) purposes, please share your thoughts on what we should do, Mr. Jeong Won-gyo.

**Jeong Won-gyo:** I think installing pipes (土管設置) is good, but if we must, we should widen the entrance road to our village. When ox carts (牛車) meet, there's no room to pass, and we often have to backtrack. It's inconvenient (不便) and how can we farm (農事) like this? And the cement we have can be used to widen the road and build structures (構造物).

**Chairperson (司會者):** What do others think about what Mr. Jeong Won-gyo just said?

**Kim Chang-gi:** No, widening the road will take up a lot of farmland. Who will give up their precious land for that?

**Elder Jeong (鄭老人):** Chang-gi is right. We should grow crops to harvest even one more grain. We shouldn't make roads with precious land.


--- (p. 238) ---

Whoever has land to spare, please speak up.
**Jeon Hye-cheol**: How much are we planning to widen the road? If we're widening the new road (新作路) up to Old Man Kim's house, it would be at least 200 meters.
**Moderator (司會者)**: As Mr. Jeon Hye-cheol said, the length would be 200 meters, and the road width (路幅) should be about 5 meters. You all have shared various opinions, and it would be great to widen the village entrance road (進入路) on this occasion. Last time, when we harvested cabbages, it took us all day to load them onto the car parked on the new road (新作路). The driver said it took a lot of time (時間) and demanded an additional 3,000 won, but we compromised at 1,500 won.
When widening the road, there might be concerns about the land to be incorporated (編入用地), but first, we need to consolidate (集約) the opinions of the villagers (里民) on the principle of widening the 200-meter village road to 5 meters.
Does everyone agree on expanding the village road (擴張)? Is there anyone who opposes it?
**Kim Young-rae**: Who would oppose doing good things for the village's development (發展)? The issue is that we all need to make mutual concessions and contribute land. Last time, I went to Naegok-dong (內谷洞), Gangneung-si (江陵市) for some work, and they had widened the roads very well. I asked the locals about it, and they said they did it themselves. Five people donated (喜捨) their land, and although there were discussions about compensation, everyone declined, so the project went very well.
**Moderator (司會者)**: Thank you for your kind words. Everyone agrees on expanding the village road (擴張), right?
**All in attendance (一同)**: We agree.
**Moderator (司會者)**: Then, 550 pyeong (坪) of land will be used for the road expansion. I will start by contributing 100 pyeong (坪) of land.
**All villagers (里民一同)**: Mumbling here and there.
**Moderator (司會者)**: If it's difficult to give a definitive answer (確答) right now, we can decide on the contribution while working. Please let us know when we should start the work. Additionally, we will use 355 bags (袋) of cement to build structures (構造物) for the village road expansion. Does anyone object?
**All villagers (住民一同)**: No objections.
**Jeong Won-gyo**: Since tomorrow is Christmas, it would be good to make the 25th the day for village road expansion (擴張) as a commemoration (記念).
**Moderator (司會者)**: Does anyone object to Mr. Jeong Won-gyo's suggestion?
**All villagers (住民一同)**: No objections.
**Moderator (司會者)**: Please gather at my house courtyard at 10 AM tomorrow. When you come, please bring your own shovels or hoes.
Thank you all for participating in this meeting (會議) so seriously. This concludes the meeting (會議). Thank you.


--- (p. 239) ---

## Minutes (會議錄) (2)

*   **Date(日時)**: April 15, 1972, 14:00
*   **Location(場所)**: Kim Seon-gi's House
*   **Agenda(議題)**: Summary of Village Entrance Road Expansion and Construction of Village Community Center
*   **Attendees(參席人員)**: 69 people
*   **Chairperson(司會者)**: Kim Seon-gi, Village Head (里長)

**Chairperson(司會者) (Kim Seon-gi, Village Head (里長))**: Good afternoon. It has been four months since our last meeting on December 24th of last year. I am glad to see everyone here again. I would like to express my gratitude to all residents who braved the cold winter to participate in the village road expansion project. Special thanks to those who contributed their land for the expansion. Now, our village looks much more open and pleasant when viewed from the new road.

Today, we will discuss the progress of the village road expansion and the construction of the village community center. First, I would like to report that out of 335 bags of cement, 280 bags were used for two underground drainage projects, and the remaining 55 bags were used for four pipe installations and stone wall construction. The cement was used entirely for these purposes, with none diverted elsewhere.

**Kim No-in**: At this moment, I propose we give a round of applause to Kim Seon-gi, Kim Young-rae, Jeong Jin-cheol, Kim Seong-nam, Jeon Hye-cheol, and Jeong Won-gyo for contributing their land to widen the village road.

**Chairperson(司會者)**: Let us show our appreciation with a big round of applause, as Kim No-in suggested.

**All Residents(住民一同)**: Applause to express gratitude.

**Chairperson(司會者)**: Next, I would like to discuss the construction of the village community center. This year, our village has received 500 bags of cement. I have informed the local party secretary about our plan to build a 25-pyeong community center. I would like to hear your opinions on this matter.

**Kim Seong-nam(金聖南)**: Chairman, that is an excellent idea. Currently, we hold meetings at your house, but it is inconvenient when we need to gather as a neighborhood or when we have guests. Moreover, managing village affairs is challenging due to the lack of a proper space. I believe that if we work together, just as we did during the road expansion, we can successfully build a community center.

**Jeong Won-gyo(鄭元敎)**: That is a great idea. However, can we build a house with just cement? What are the plans for obtaining labor and lumber?

**Chairperson(司會者)**: First, let us decide on the location for the community center through a consensus of the residents. Since the community center should be a place where all villagers can freely enter and use, it would be best to build it in the center of the neighborhood. For this, we need to secure a site of about 100 pyeong. In my opinion, the area near Kim Seong-nam's house in the first neighborhood would be suitable. What are your thoughts?


--- (p. 240) ---

Kim Seong-nam (金聖南): I'm not saying this just because I live in 1st Ward (1班), but considering both the location and the conditions for residents' use, I believe it would be best to build the community center in our ward.

Moderator (司會者): Kim Seong-nam (金聖南) suggests building the community center in 1st Ward (1班). Are there any other opinions? If not, we will decide to build it in 1st Ward (1班).

Residents (住民) all (一同): No objections.

Moderator (司會者): Then, we will decide to build the community center in 1st Ward (1班). If we build it in 1st Ward (1班), how should we determine the specific location?

Kim Dong-gi: Since 1st Ward (1班) has secured the community center, the ward leader can discuss the land issue.

1st Ward (1班) Ward Leader (班長): First, I am truly grateful that the community center will be built in our ward, Geumsan-ri (金山里). However, if I were to specify the location for building the community center, it would involve using farmland, which puts me in a difficult position. If I had land there, I would gladly donate it, but since all our farmland is at the foot of the mountain, it's not easy to spare. I'm not sure what to do.

Moderator (司會者): Does anyone have a good opinion on the community center land issue?

Residents (住民) all (一同): A moment of silence.

Kim Seong-nam (金聖南): Since the community center will be built in our ward, as a member of 1st Ward (1班), I have something to say. If the land is 100 pyeong (坪), even at the current market price of 2,000 won per pyeong, that's 200,000 won, isn't it? The area near where the community center will be built is my family's farmland and next to the road leading to the village. For the development of our village, I will gladly donate this jade field (玉田) that has been passed down through generations. However, I'm worried that my wife might object.

Residents (住民) all (一同): Applause and cheers expressing gratitude.

Moderator (司會者): On behalf of the residents, I express my gratitude to Kim Seong-nam (金聖南). We will aim to complete the community center construction by the end of this year. Together with the village development committee (里開發委員), we will make a concrete business promotion plan. I ask for the active participation of many residents in the construction of the community center. With that, I will conclude today's meeting. Thank you. Please go home safely.

Moderator (司會): Thank you very much for coming in such large numbers. Today is a meaningful gathering. We have completed the community center, which our neighborhood has long desired, and are holding this meeting right here. Until now, I, as the village head (里長), have been managing village affairs alone, but now we have the Saemaul Leader System (指導者制), and we need to elect male and female Saemaul leaders (指導者).


--- (p. 241) ---

I would like to express my gratitude for the various forms of cooperation you have shown me thus far. It would be good for our village to elect a Saemaul leader, just as villages across the nation are doing. Please share your opinions if you have any.

**Ham Yeon-ho (咸衍鎬)**: What are the main responsibilities of a Saemaul leader?

**Host (司會者)**: They will take charge of all Saemaul projects in our neighborhood. This includes managing Saemaul materials coming into our village, overseeing the expected Saemaul project funds, and generally overseeing all Saemaul projects in our neighborhood. The women's leader will be in charge of women's association affairs in our neighborhood.

**Kim Gi-seon**: They certainly have an important role as representatives.

**Host (司會者)**: Please share who you think is qualified to be the male or female leader.

**Host (司會者)**: It seems difficult for you to speak up. Let me suggest someone. In my opinion, Kim Jang-gi (金璋起) would be suitable. Kim Jang-gi has been helping with neighborhood matters alongside me in every way possible, and I believe he is the right person for the job. What do you all think?

**Jeong Jin-cheol**: That sounds good. I agree.

**All residents (住民一同)**: Unanimous approval with applause

**Host (司會者)**: Then, please come forward, Kim Jang-gi (金璋起), and say a few words.

**Kim Jang-gi (金璋起)**: Thank you. There are many people who work harder and are more active than me, so I am grateful to have been elected as the Saemaul leader despite my shortcomings. I believe that the success or failure of our village's Saemaul projects depends on how much we cooperate, not just on my individual efforts. I will do my best, but I greatly expect your cooperation.

Thank you.

**Host (司會者)**: Next, we will elect the women's leader. Please share your thoughts.

**Kim Jang-gi (金璋起)**: In my opinion, Kim Jeong-suk (金貞淑), aged 46, would be suitable. She is currently in charge of the women's association, so I believe she is the right fit.

# ❖ Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (4)

Date: June 8, 1974
Location: Village Community Center (會舘)
Agenda: Collective Resettlement (集團移住) of Residents (住民)
Attendees: 83 people (人員)
Chairperson: Kim Jang-gi (金璋起), Saemaul Leader (指導者)

Chair: Good day. Until now, I have spoken with you individually and while working in the fields, but today I have gathered you here to discuss the Saemaul project, which will significantly change the environment of our village. We propose changing the village structure as the Yeongdong Expressway (嶺東高速道路) will pass through our village.

Currently, there are 16 substandard houses (不良住宅) scattered within our farmland (農耕地), which not only look unpleasant but also hinder farming. You all know this well. Although it may be difficult to leave our long-time homes and the cost is high, the government is providing support funds (支援金), so we hope for your active participation.

Kim Young-rae (金永來): So, we are to completely dismantle and rebuild our houses on the hillside? That's no small task. They say building a house is like cooking a meal, and now we have to build 16 houses at once in our neighborhood. That's a huge undertaking.

Chair: As the Saemaul leader, this first project feels overwhelming. It's a task that must be done, but even I feel daunted. Three days ago, the county magistrate (郡守) visited and we roughly agreed on the houses to be resettled. Since the houses will be completely rebuilt, the support is 200,000 won (萬원) per house and a loan of 600,000 won (萬원). There will also be some self-funding required. Please discuss this seriously.

Park No-in (朴老人): When do we have to finish this? And what about the land for the new houses?

Chairperson: We must complete this by the end of October this year. The land should be secured on the hillside. In my opinion, since the current land will become farmland, we should consult with the landowner (山主) and seek their support.

Jeong Won-gyo: Why not improve the substandard houses at the foot of the mountain as well?

Ham Yeon-ho (咸衍鎬): We already have a problem rebuilding the 16 houses in the middle of the rice fields. Let's not complicate things further.

Chairperson: Let's discuss only the 16 houses. According to the county magistrate, the support funds are limited.

Kim Seong-nam (金聖南): Let's first establish the principles for our collective resettlement. The timing, methods, and selection of participants can be decided by the neighborhood development committee (里開發委員會).

All Residents: Agreed.

Chair: Then, we will adjourn the meeting. We will discuss the details individually later. Goodbye.

# Gangwon (江原) Samcheok County (三陟郡) Nogok-myeon (蘆谷面) Yeosam (閭三) Village

## 1. Overview of the Village

### Ga. History

- In ancient times, it was the country of Siljik (悉直氏)
- In the 23rd year of King Pasa (婆娑王) of Silla (新羅), it surrendered to the Silla Kingdom (新羅國), then was taken by Goguryeo (高句麗), and then restored to Siljik (悉直) in the 6th year of King Jijeung (智證王) of Silla (新羅). It was the first time a state (州) was established, and in the 8th year of Queen Seondeok (善德女王), the Jinju Dudo-bu (眞州都督府) was established. In the 5th year of King Muyeol (武烈王), it was changed to Bukjin (北眞), and in the 59th year of King Gyeongdeok (景德王) (760 AD), it was renamed Samcheok County (三陟郡).
- During the Goryeo Dynasty (高麗時代), in the 14th year of King Seongjong (成宗), it was changed to Cheokju (陟州), and in the 9th year of King Hyeonjong (顯宗), it was renamed Samcheok County Magistrate (三陟縣令).
- During the Joseon Dynasty (李朝), in the 2nd year of King Taejo (太祖), it was renamed a city (府), and in the 5th year of King Injo (仁祖) (1628 AD, the year of Jeongmyo (丁卯)), the city (府) was abolished and it was changed back to Samcheok County (三陟郡), which continues to this day.
- In 1936, the Samcheok Railroad (三陟鐵道) was built.
- In 1942, the Samcheok Development Corporation (三陟開發公社) was established along with various mining and industrial companies (各種鑛工業體) due to the excavation of bituminous coal (無煙炭採堀), making Samcheok County (三陟郡) one of the leading industrial counties (工業郡) in Korea (韓國) with a population (人口) of 300,000 in 5 towns (邑) and 5 townships (面).
- In the 25th year of King Sejong (世宗) (1445 AD), Shim (沈氏), a fallen citizen (落鄕民), first settled in Yeosam (閭三) Village, which was then called Yeosim (閭心). In 1954, it was renamed Yeosam-ri (閭三里), which continues to this day.

### Na. Location and Conditions

Yeosam (閭三) Village is located on a mountain (山上) at an altitude (海拔) of 350m, where the Taebaek Mountains (太白山脈) form a watershed (分水嶺), 12km southwest (西南) of the Samcheok County Office (三陟郡廳). Before the start of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동), it was a remote and isolated mountain village (山間奧地) that was completely cut off (完全孤立) from the outside world (外部) and was a backward (落後) village that was excluded (疎外) from civilization (文明).
