### Village Characteristics (特性)

Located at an altitude (海拔) of 350m in a basin (盆地) formed by limestone (石灰岩) strata (地層), the village does not have any streams (河川) or rice paddies (沓) as rainwater drains through a depression (沈降地) and does not accumulate within the village.

## 2. Village Development Process (發展過程)

### A. Situation Before 1970 (70年 以前 的 狀況)

#### 1) Basic Environment (基礎環境)


--- (p. 245) ---

The highland basin (高山盆地) had no roads (道路) connecting it to markets (市場), the town center (面所在地), or other neighboring villages, leaving it isolated (孤立) and underdeveloped (落後). The village was divided into 7 natural hamlets (自然部落) and 4 Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) teams, with no internal paths connecting the hamlets, making communication among residents difficult. All 70 households (戶) lived in thatched (草家) or earthen houses, and there was no water (水) in the village, making bathing impossible and requiring residents to collect rainwater or melted snow for laundry, living like primitive people (原始民). They had to travel 6km to neighboring villages for water.

## 2) Income Level (所得水準)
This village had an average household income (戶當平均所得水準) of only 190,000 won in 1970, living in a cycle of poverty (貧困의惡循環) and relying on potatoes and corn (옥수수) as staple foods (主食), supplemented by gathering wild plants (산나물) and herbs (藥草) for household income (家用財源). The village had abundant forest resources (林產資源), which they used to make firewood (장작) to sell at the Samcheok market (三陟市場), 12km away. However, at that time (當時), many residents had to leave for nearby coal mining areas (炭田地帶) such as Jangseong (長省), Hwangji (黃池), and Dogye (道溪) within the county (郡內) to find work, making it an unfortunate village (悲運의마을).

## 3) Living Conditions (生活狀態)
### a) Mental State (精神狀態)
Residents accepted the lack of water (물) and roads (길) as their fate (宿命), indulging in idleness (나태), drinking, and gambling (도박), leading to the village's increasing isolation (폐쇄).

### b) Cultural Life (文化生活) and Daily Life (衣食住生活)
Isolated (孤立) in the mountains (山間奧地), cultural life (文化的生活) was non-existent. There were only 2 radios (臺) in the village, and among the 30-plus residents (住民), half had never seen a train or car (自動車). Housing conditions were poor, with thatched roofs (草家) leaking rain, and residents primarily wearing hemp clothing (삼베옷) and straw shoes (짚신) as their best footwear (最高手段).

## b. Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동의推進)
### 1) Development Motivation (開發動機)
Yosasam Village was widely known as the most remote (最奧地) village in Samcheok County (三陟郡).
- The village had no water (水) in any of its 7 natural hamlets (自然部落), and residents had to cross mountains (山) to fetch water from a spring (용천수) on a distant hillside, taking 2 hours (時間) to carry one bucket (동이).
- The nearest elementary school (國民學校) was 8km away in Nogok-myeon (蘆谷面), making it difficult for students (學生) to commute (通學) in bad weather, and the low school attendance rate (就學率) resulted in a high illiteracy rate (文盲者).
- The village's isolation (폐쇄) and lagging development (發展) were seen as a natural fate (自然의宿命) imposed by its environment (自然).


--- (p. 246) ---

Among these, the most significant aspiration was the development of a 12km road connecting the village center with the Samcheok Market (三陟市場).

In such difficult circumstances, the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) became an opportunity to open new paths for the villagers who had lived there for 500 years, and all the residents firmly united with the shared resolve to "Let us live rightly."

## 2) Attracting a Branch School (分校誘致)

- Yeosam (閭三) village had been actively engaged in the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) under the leadership of Park Jae-myeong (朴載明), a determined leader.
- After being discharged from the military in 1962, Park Jae-myeong leveraged the revolutionary government's agrarian policies and spiritual purification movement to seek elements for village development and made extensive efforts.
- He first aimed to rectify the residents' spirits, which were steeped in decadence, laziness, and outdated customs, by organizing a life improvement club for the young generation in their 20s and guiding them to promote new agricultural spirits and healthy emotional lives.
- He also taught illiterate residents, who made up over 90% of the population, to read using his own silkworm room (蠶室) as a night school (夜學).
- With 150 residents who gained literacy from this initiative as the core, the villagers built a 40-pyeong (坪) schoolhouse by their own efforts in early 1965 and were approved to establish a branch classroom (分室) of Nogok National School (蘆谷國民學校), allowing them to hire one teacher.
- However, the residents were not satisfied with just a branch classroom for three years of schooling. They received a donation of 2,000 pyeong of forest land from village resident Jeong Taek-gwon (鄭澤權), and with all 5,250 residents working even through the night with torches, they carved out a 5-meter-high mountain to create the site. In August 1967, they were approved to establish Yeosam Branch School (閭三分校) with three classrooms and an 1,800-pyeong playground.
- Since the establishment of Yeosam village, in 1972, they experienced the joy of producing the first female graduate from the national school.

## 3) Achievements of the First-Year Pilot Project (初年度試驗事業의成果)

- In 1971, the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동), initiated by President Park Chung-hee (朴大統領), began to spread across the country, reaching even the remote mountain village of Yeosam (閭三).
- However, many residents, unable to break away from old habits, ignored the movement and indulged in decadence and idleness, such as drinking and gambling.
- The foundation for today's Yeosam village was built on the tireless courage and relentless determination of leader Park Jae-myeong (朴載明).
- At that time, as the village head (里長), Park initiated the first project: expanding the roads between the eight natural hamlets and widening the village roads, a long-standing aspiration. With all 2,700 residents united, they completed the expansion of a 2km road between hamlets to a width of 3 meters and widened a 1.2km village road in just 55 days of construction. This allowed them to use handcarts, bicycles (自轉車), and other means of transportation beyond just shoulder poles, enabling them to acquire the new civilization of mechanization previously seen only in plains villages and city surroundings. As the vitality of village development became evident through the Saemaul Undong, many residents gained a sense of possibility and confidence, thinking, "If we do it, we can do it."


--- (p. 247) ---

## 4) Activities and Obstacle Overcoming Situations of Saemaul Leaders

*   Park Jae-myeong (朴載明氏), the Saemaul leader of Yeosam (閭三) Village, was born on April 2, 1938, as the eldest son among six siblings of a poor farmer who had lived in this village for four generations.
*   He graduated from Samcheok Industrial High School (三陟工業高等學校), becoming the first high school graduate in the village.
*   After completing three years of military service, he ignored the advice to leave the mountainous village to find a good job and decided to become a worker for his hometown.
*   Park Jae-myeong (朴載明), the leader who succeeded in his first business, judged that the reason this village was poor was because the villagers had resigned themselves to the natural conditions given by nature as fate, and
*   He improved living conditions by bringing in water to solve the water shortage problem,
*   He opened a 12km road connecting the county office of Samcheok-gun (三陟郡) and the office of Nogok-myeon (蘆谷面) to escape isolation from the outside world, while
*   He tried to bring in electricity to expel oil lamps and pursue a culturally rich life, and
*   He devised a village development plan to cultivate medicinal herbs, including camphor (長腦), which can only grow in the soil of this village, to increase income.
*   He explained this plan to the village development committee and local elites, but they opposed it, arguing that the water source was 50m lower than the village, 2km away over the mountain, so water could not cross the mountain, and that it was impossible for the villagers to break through the 12km rocky road in dozens of years.
*   However, he did not retreat at all and persuaded the villagers that water could cross the mountain ridge due to water pressure caused by the drop, and that the opening of a 12km road could also be achieved if the villagers united and worked together, as there was a explosives technician with mining experience in the village. He earnestly appealed to the villagers to firmly unite and push forward together, saying that if they could not open the road in their generation, the village would forever remain a backward village excluded from civilization.
*   As the first business based on the determination of all villagers, they dug a well in a place where water could come out in the village, but they could not find groundwater.
*   The leader, who had commissioned a geological survey of the soil by the Geology Department of Hanyang University (漢陽工大), concluded that rainwater was drained through a depression or cave, and decided to bring water from Sangutgol, 2km away from the village.
*   Initially, the villagers took 35 days to lay a 1km water pipe along the mountain, but the water pipe could not be watered because it had to cross a high ridge. Then, after 25 days of cutting through the mountain waist, the construction was halted again as they hit a rock bed.
*   The leader, who encouraged the disheartened villagers, vowed that they would not be defeated in their first business, and decided to dig a cave to bring water no matter what.
*   However, it was not an easy task to break through the hard rock wall. It was like a human mole. While breaking through with a wooden lever, the cave collapsed several times, injuring hands and feet and threatening life.
*   On the 29th day of starting to dig the cave, they finally completed a 40m rock cave, allowing water to cross the ridge.


--- (p. 248) ---

And, the village had been using a shared water well located 800 meters away from the village, but in 1976, they made it possible for each household to have water by constructing a water collection well that could store 50 tons of water and, from there, women carried 40 loads of sand from 6 kilometers outside the village to the top of a 250-meter mountain to build a water distribution well. They laid a total of 5.5 kilometers of water pipes to each household, and once the water supply was perfectly established, the long-standing wish of the village residents, who had suffered from water-related hardships for 500 years, was finally fulfilled.

Upon completing the simple water supply system, the leaders and residents of the village, who had deeply realized the infinite possibilities and miraculous fruits of unity in the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), came to realize that the reason their village had fallen behind in the development of history was because they had resigned themselves to the natural heritage bestowed upon them as fate. They vowed to conquer the harsh nature to live well.

The biggest wish of this village was to open a 12-kilometer mountain road connecting the village to the market in Samcheok and the administrative center of Nogok-myeon.

Leader Park Jae-myeong (朴載明) had experienced more than anyone else the desperate sorrow and hardships of a village without roads.

He had commuted from elementary school to high school for 12 years, climbing and descending the mountain slopes.

For 500 long years, the stone path of this mountain, where the footsteps of his ancestors had passed, had been a painful memory that he felt every day, and there had been times when he blamed his ancestors.

Moreover, during his middle school days, his father had gone to buy salt on this stone mountain, slipped, and fell into a several-dozen-meter cliff, becoming paralyzed and leaving this world. When he thought that this was also due to the cursed stone mountain, the determination to break through the mountain and make a road grew within him.

Leader Park Jae-myeong (朴載明) held seven village meetings and persuaded the residents, saying, "If we cooperate, there is nothing we cannot achieve, and we will definitely break through the stone mountain path left by our ancestors in our generation and pass it on to our descendants."

On February 18, 1973, before the snow had even melted, they began the construction work on the frozen stone mountain with a relentless determination that even their ancestors had not dared to attempt.

However, the project did not go as smoothly as initially thought.

A total of 7,500 pyeong of land was required for the 12-kilometer road construction section, and 6,500 pyeong of it belonged to the residents of Jobi-ri, the lower village, and neighboring villages.

During the day, he had to guide the residents and push forward the work, and at night, he had to visit the landowners of the neighboring villages to request land donations.

However, the landowners consistently demanded payment for the land, and the leader was able to receive land donations on the condition that the residents of Yeosammaul (閭三마을) would help with agricultural work, and also by introducing matchmakers within the village.

Despite all the hardships, they managed to secure 6,500 pyeong of land for the road and push forward the work. However, they encountered another obstacle: 8 kilometers of pure rocky terrain that the residents' determination alone could not penetrate.


--- (p. 249) ---

That summer, three professors conducted a field survey and concluded that blasting work was difficult due to the road gradient reaching 40°, the enormous cost, the difficulty of transporting equipment, and the risk of student injuries. The leader persistently appealed to the principal for a week and finally obtained permission to blast only the rocks.

During the summer vacation, 30 students from Samcheok Technical College, led by Professor Kim Young-dal, participated in the work, personally dragging the compressor.

When the technical college students arrived at the foot of the mountain with their equipment, the morale of the residents, which had been lost, surged. All the residents were mobilized, and they pulled the compressor, weighing over 6 tons, up the steep 4 km mountain road in one go.

Moved by the residents' enthusiasm for the work, the students camped in the mountains during the vacation and even performed dangerous belt drilling.

The mountains and valleys echoed with continuous explosions, and after the blasting, the residents removed even more stones to avoid hindering the students' work. Women formed teams to prepare snacks and provided them at the work site.

On the other hand, grandmothers took care of infants in the nearby woods, and Kim Ok-sun, the wife of Jo Jeong-nam of the village (then 23 years old), came to the work site with her swollen body just seven days after childbirth, saying, "I can't stay at home because I feel sorry," which moved the residents and students to tears.

However, after a year of construction, a 4.5 km road was opened, but the residents, exhausted from overwork, decreased in number at the work site. To make matters worse, the leader was hospitalized with neurogenic osteomyelitis, and the work was temporarily suspended.

After two months of diagnosis, the leader, hospitalized at Samcheok Hospital in Gangwon Province, held a Development Committee meeting from his sickbed and urged the continuation of the work. However, the development committee members suggested abandoning the project midway, citing agricultural interference and residents' exhaustion from overwork.

On the 29th day of his hospitalization, the leader returned to the village with his unfinished recovery, leaning on his wife and a cane, determined to continue the work.

With a cane supporting his ailing body, the leader visited each household, persuading the residents that if they did not build the road in their generation, they would never escape poverty and suffering, and the village would become a backward, closed-off village from civilization. He appealed to them to return to the work site.

Under the Saemaul flag, the residents gathered again with new resolve and determination. This project was a spiritual achievement born from the indomitable spirit of the entire village, from young to old, embodying the Saemaul spirit of "I cultivate my own village."

The 12 km road connecting the county office of Samcheok County and the office of Nogok-myeon was completed in July 1976 amidst the gratitude of all the residents.

This project, spanning 3 years and 5 months, involved a total of 46,000 participants, from children to the elderly, who braved rain, snow, harsh cold, and scorching heat. This means that each household participated in the road construction work for 6 months every year.


--- (p. 250) ---

* This road, constructed with a subsidy of 8.2 million won, opened a road worth 120 million won. It is used by 2,700 residents from Yeosam Village (閭三마을) and four nearby villages. It is expected to save approximately 180 million won annually by transporting 680 tons or more of agricultural and forest products, as well as farming supplies, by automobile.
* Notably, the opening of the road led to a 7.5-fold increase in the price of the region's main product, forest products, from 8 won per unit to 60 won. The bulk joint distribution of specialty crops like garlic and chili peppers has significantly contributed to increased income and improved distribution structures.
* After completing the road construction project, Yeosam Village (閭三마을) embarked on bringing electricity to the village by banishing kerosene lamps.
* In 1976, with 5.7 million won from residents and 6.9 million won in government support, electricity was installed for 63 households, fulfilling another long-held aspiration of the residents following the provision of water and roads.
* This village has long been home to various medicinal herbs, including Korean ginseng (山蔘), known as a mountain elixir, which have been a source of income for the residents.
* Cultivated Korean ginseng, scientifically named Panax vietnamensis (長腦), differs from Panax ginseng (人蔘) in having a longer neck, slower growth rate, and nodes on its body indicating its age. Residents have cultivated it from seeds for about 120 years, but low germination rates limited its cultivation to a few residents until a leader developed a germination method, enabling 48 households to now cultivate a total of 600 pyeong (坪).
* The price of Panax vietnamensis is high, with 10-year-old plants selling for about 80,000 won and 15-20-year-old plants for around 200,000 won. Currently, the 600 pyeong of cultivation yields approximately 100 million won, serving as a unique source of income for the village.
* With the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) achieving long-held aspirations that even ancestors could not accomplish over 500 years and raising farm income, the village launched full-scale environmental improvement projects in 1976. They upgraded the roofs of 82 thatched houses, including annexes, to corrugated iron and slate, replaced unsightly fences made of pine branches with natural fences of Korean fir and four-season trees, and built 350 meters of stone walls to protect nature in areas prone to soil erosion as part of a natural conservation campaign. Additionally, they improved manure pits, kitchens, and stoves in each household, completing all facilities needed to adapt to 1980s cultural life.
* As Yeosam Village (閭三마을) was introduced nationwide as an outstanding Saemaul Undong village, it received 2 million won from the Interior Minister's Award for Excellent Saemaul Undong Villages in July 1976. In October, village leader Park Jae-myeong was awarded the Donggok Culture Award (東谷文化賞) in the social division for his contributions to local culture in Gangwon Province (江原道). On December 8, during the Monthly Economic Trends Report Meeting, the village had the honor of presenting successful Saemaul Undong cases to President (大統領) Park Chung-hee, receiving the Saemaul Medal for Cooperation, the Presidential Citation for the Village Community, and 5 million won in prize money.
* The village used the 5 million won prize money to establish a meeting hall, barbershop, potato crushing room, village savings bank, and a communal sales stand, among other facilities.


--- (p. 251) ---

The welfare facility for purposeful use was completed on July 8, 1977, and we are always mindful of the esteemed consideration of His Excellency the President (大統領) and strive for thorough utilization (活用).

## 6) Heartwarming Stories (美談佳話)

* During the mountain road construction (山間道路開設時) from 1973 to 1976, Kim Gwan-hyun (金官炫) (owner of Samcheok (三陟) Sawmill, now deceased), who resided in Namyang-ri (南陽里), Samcheok-eup (三陟邑), held a mountain spirit ceremony (山神祭) seven times to pray for the safety of the road construction.
* Samcheok Industrial High School (三陟工業專門學校) (Principal (學長): Lee Seong-gap (李成甲)) supported the project with compressors, drilling machines, and explosive techniques over four years (年間), with a total of 1,459 participants (延人員).
* All households in 16 villages of Nogok-myeon (蘆谷面) (Myeonlong (面長): Kim Seong-gi (金聲基)) volunteered for three days each year (年間) over four years (年間).
* Children from Yeosam Branch School (閭三分校) formed teams every evening to hold torches and assist with night work.

## Ma. Various Organizations and Activities in the Village

- In Yeosam (閭三) Village, the various organizations include a Youth Association (靑年會) with 35 members, a Development Committee (開發委員會) with 12 members, a Women's Association (婦人會) with 49 members, a 4-H Club (會) with 28 members, and a Christian Youth Service Association with 12 members. Notably, the 4-H Club is one of the outstanding 4-H Clubs in Samcheok County (三陟郡).
- The Youth Association (靑年會) and the 4-H Club (會) have taken the lead in cultivating special crops (特用作物) to increase income (所得). For the past 15 years, they have been cultivating large quantities of garlic and chili peppers, earning each household (戶當) over 500,000 won (萬圓) annually.

## Ba. Achievements through the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

### 1) Spiritual Aspect (精神面)

- Before the Saemaul Undong (運動) began, the village was mired in a vicious cycle of ignorance (無知) and poverty (貧困), with debauchery (頹廢) characterized by drinking and gambling (賭博).
- Through the Saemaul Undong (運動), residents gained confidence (自信) and courage (勇氣), realizing that unity (團結) could overcome any challenge. The resolution of Yeosam (閭三) Village's long-standing aspirations (宿願事業) is a spiritual (精神的) achievement.

### 2) Livelihood Aspect (生活面)

- Through the Saemaul Undong (運動), residents united to accomplish a 500-year-old aspiration (宿願事業):
  - The old saying (口說) that "marriage was difficult without water" has become a myth (神話).
  - Residents can now freely use water from the newly installed indoor plumbing (上水道) for laundry and daily needs.
  - Previously, agricultural products (農產物) were sold at low prices to merchants (商人) or carried to market as pack loads (等짐), but now they are transported by vehicle (車輛) for collective (共同) distribution (出荷), bringing convenience (便利) and increased income (所得).
  - Improved communication (疏通) with the outside world (外部) has freed the village from isolation (孤立), allowing residents to enjoy the benefits of civilization (文明).

### 3) Production Aspect (生產面)

- While the main crops (主穀) include barley, millet, potatoes, and corn (等), seed renewal (種子更新) has increased yields (收穫高) per unit area (段步當).
- Yeosam (閭三) Village's unique main products (主産物), such as camphor (長腦) and various medicinal herbs (藥草), are now produced in large quantities (多量).

### 4) Income Aspect (所得面)

- Road construction (道路開通) has increased the price of forest products (林産物) from 8 won (材當) to 60 won (萬圓), boosting income (所得) for this village rich in forest resources (林産資源).
- Large-scale cultivation (多量栽培) of garlic, chili peppers, and medicinal herbs (藥草) has improved land utilization (耕地利用度).
- By utilizing the abundant natural resources (初資源) around the village, each household (家庭) raises more than 3 head (頭) of Hanwoo (韓牛), increasing livestock income (畜産所得). In 1977, each household earned 1.6 million won (萬圓).

## Sa. Future Development Plans (發展構想)

- Yeosam (閭三) Village has completed all environmental improvement projects (環境改善事業) through the Saemaul Undong (運動).
- Going forward, the village plans to focus on increasing income (所得) to continue developing as a wealthy community (部者村).


--- (p. 255) ---

Currently cultivated camphor trees (長腦) will be expanded by utilizing the village mountain to select and expand new planting sites, and pasturelands will be developed to increase the number of Hanwoo cattle (韓牛), including fattened cattle (肥育牛). Additionally, the village plans to jointly purchase a truck with neighboring villages to collectively ship local products and increase income.

# 3. Residents' Assembly (住民總會)

## ♦ Minutes of the Meeting (會議錄)(1)

**Date (日時)**: February 25, 1971
**Location (場所)**: Yeosam Branch School (閭三分校) classroom (敎室)
**Agenda (議題)**: Road construction (道路開設) between natural hamlets (自然部落間) and widening of An-gil (安吉擴張)
**Attendees (參席人員)**: 57 people (名)
**Absentees (不參人員)**: 13 people (名)
**Chairperson (司會者)**: Village Head (里長) Kim Woo-hyun (金佑炫)
**Recorder (記錄)**: Seo In-seok (徐仁錫)

**Village Head (里長)**: I apologize for asking you to come here despite your busy schedules. Today, we have convened this village meeting (大洞會議) for several reasons, but primarily to discuss widening the narrow paths between the seven natural hamlets (自然部落), which are often impassable when it rains, and to consider constructing new roads where necessary. Although our living conditions have improved significantly in recent years, we still struggle with the inefficiency of carrying goods on our backs, and it is embarrassing to rely on such outdated methods. We must pave these roads eventually, so let us discuss and plan to do so this coming spring. Yesterday evening, I consulted with the development committee members at my home, and we agreed to hold this meeting today. Please share your valuable opinions to ensure that this discussion results in clear, well-lit roads connecting each village.

**Kim Sang-jung**: Could you explain where and how much we should widen the roads?

**Village Head (里長)**: Yes, as our seven natural hamlets (自然部落) have been connected for a long time, it has been quite difficult to traverse the village. Therefore, we propose widening and improving the roads connecting Seonmaeul, Eupseota, Daemaeul, Changbakkol, Saegigol, Bongcheon, and Heumok to a width of approximately 3 meters.

**Jeong Yeon-mo**: So, we are talking about widening the existing roads?

**Village Head (里長)**: Yes, that is correct. We aim to widen the currently narrow roads.

**Jeong Yeon-mo**: In that case, we will need additional land for the roads. Have you considered this?

**Village Head (里長)**: Yes, once this meeting confirms the road construction, we will discuss and determine the necessary measures.

**Park Jae-myeong (朴載明)**: As the Village Head (里長) mentioned, let us discuss the measures after confirming the road construction. Road expansion (道路擴張) is essential for our village. We must expand the roads to build a prosperous village (富村).


--- (p. 256) ---

# Village Head: What do you all think?
**Kim Jun-seok:** Widening the road is good, but there seems to be an issue with how we go about it. Let's first discuss the method.
**Village Head:** Then, let's consider that there is no objection to widening the road and discuss the method.
**Jeong Yeon-mo:** If we widen the road, a lot of my land will be taken up. I don't have enough spare land to just give away. If we calculate the land value at market price, perhaps, but...
**Seo Bong-cheon:** Listen here, don't just say it's not possible. Hear me out. It's true that everyone's land is precious, but how can we do good for the neighborhood if we start by being stubborn? Why would the village head hold meetings for the good of the neighborhood and run around every day if it weren't for a good cause?
**Park Jae-myeong:** That's right. I think we must widen the road. So, I will offer my 150 pyeong of fertile land. If my 150 pyeong of land becomes a meaningful road for all the villagers to use, how rewarding would that be, even if it's land passed down through generations.
**Village Head:** Thank you, Park. Really, thank you.
**Kim Jun-seok:** If Park, who isn't well-off, can offer 150 pyeong of his land, how can we just stand by? I will offer whatever amount of land is needed to widen the road.
**Village Head:** Thank you. Those whose land is significantly taken up have almost all offered it. Thank you.
**Jeong Yeon-mo:** My land will be taken up less than Park's or Kim's, but I'm sorry to say it's not possible. It's because this land was given to me by the main family when I started my household. I will also make a donation.
**Village Head:** Thank you.
**Kim Chang-hyeon:** You all are truly admirable. Offering your land for the village like this, our village will surely change. I've lived in this neighborhood for over 70 years, and I've never seen anything like this. Thank you so much.
**Park Chan-yong • Jeong Si-tak • Jeong Taek-gwon:** We also have some land taken up, so we can't not offer it.
**Village Head:** Please have Seo In-seok record the contents of this meeting and get signatures and seals after the meeting is over. Then, the land issue is resolved, but when and how should we start the work?
**Park Jae-myeong:** Let's form work teams by natural hamlet units and agree to pave from one's own village to three villages away. Since the large village has the most residents and the least amount of work, please cooperate with the people living in Changbakgol to pave the road coming down from Changbakgol.
**All:** Of course, let's do that. We agree.
**Village Head:** Then, when should we start?
**Jeong Yeon-mo:** As they say, pull out the ox horn in one go. Let's start tomorrow.
**Kim Chang-hyeon:** But we also have work to do at home, so let's give ourselves three days to tidy up the house, and start the work from the first of March.
**All:** We agree.
**Village Head:** Thank you. Are there any other opinions?


--- (p. 257) ---

동(同): No, there isn't.
Ijang(里長): Then, let's conclude today's meeting here. I have a jar of makgeolli at my house, so please come and have some. And for those who have donated land, please sign and stamp the meeting minutes at Mr. Seo Yeon-seok's place. Thank you.

## Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (2)

Date(日時): April 10, 1972
Location(場所): Village Community Center (會舘)
Agenda(議題): Establishment of a Simple Water Supply Facility (簡易給水施設) Business Plan (事業計劃)
Attendees(參席人員): 61 people
Chairperson(司會): Saemaul Leader Park Jae-myeong (朴載明)

Chairperson(司會者): I would like to express my gratitude for your continued efforts in the Saemaul Undong (事業). Although the weather is not good today, I am grateful that so many of you have come. The matter we will discuss today is to solve the chronic water shortage (食水難) that has been considered a fate (宿命) for generations through the Saemaul Undong (事業) by establishing a simple water supply (簡易給水) facility. However, our village is originally a highland basin (高地盆地), so the water source (水源地) is a problem. I will explain the installation plan (設置案) roughly discussed with the development committee (開發委員) and listen to your good opinions. If we proceed with the simple water supply facility (簡易給水施設), the water source (水源地) will likely need to be established about 2 km away, across the mountain, using the Yongcheon Stream in Sanggot-gol for a simple water supply system (簡易上水道).
Of course, there are many difficulties, but there is also potential. What do you all think?
Jeong Yeon-gyeong: No matter how good and successful the Saemaul Undong (事業) is, it's better not to make reckless remarks. Do you think our elders in the past were unable to fetch water in buckets?
Jeong Yeon-gi: If we proceed as discussed, how will that water cross this mountain pass and reach our village? How can we possibly achieve such a tremendous task given our circumstances? Please don't make the village foolish by acting recklessly.
Chairperson(司會者): Yes, those are good points. It is indeed difficult and seemingly impossible. However, we must resolve this issue. And no matter what adversity (逆境) comes in the future, we must solve it ourselves and make our village prosperous with our own hands.
Park Bu-yong: Everyone! If it's something you want to do, it won't be that easy, and if you don't want to do it, you won't be able to do it no matter how hard you try. If this project (事業) succeeds, how beneficial it would be? Our women wouldn't have to fetch water from miles away and could live comfortably, it would be hygienic, and it would also greatly help in agricultural cultivation (栽培).
Jeong Yeon-gyeong: Well, I won't drink that water, so those who want to do it should go ahead and do it well. I can't even manage tomorrow, let alone today, so why act like a lone hero (獨不將軍)...


--- (p. 258) ---

# Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (3)

**Date (日時):** January 20, 1973, 20:00
**Location (場所):** Village Hall (會舘) (Former Yesam Branch School (閭三分校))
**Agenda (議題):** Construction of a New Road (新設道路) Connecting the County Seat (面所在地) and Samcheok Market (三陟市場)
**Attendees (參席人員):** 65
**Absentees (不參人員):** 5
**Chairperson (司會者):** Park Jae-myeong (朴載明), Saemaul Leader (指導者)

**Chairperson (司會者):** Good evening, fellow villagers. I am truly sorry to have called you out on such a cold winter night.

I have gathered you here today because, as you all know, the Saemaul Undong (運動) is vigorously underway across the nation, yet it seems our village alone is asleep. Last time, I had some business in Yupeong-ri, Jeongseon County. There, I witnessed a scene that left me in awe. A mere 635 households were constructing an 8km-long farm road (農路) with their own hands. The residents of Nampyeong (南坪) village in Jeongseon County had suffered significant losses as their harvested crops rotted for two years because cars could not reach their village. They realized that their village could make money by allowing cars to enter and transport agricultural products (農產物). I was astonished to see that their situation was remarkably similar to ours.

As you all know, we cannot just sit idly by. Let us take a look around our village.

---

**Seo Bong-cheon (徐奉天) (Development Committee Chairperson (開發委員長)):** Let's all quiet down for a moment. Everyone's suggestions are good. Park Jae-myeong's (朴載明) proposal is not for personal gain but for the betterment of our neighborhood and our collective well-being. Let's not misunderstand each other. I'll buy everyone a round of makgeolli (막걸리) tonight, so let's clear up any misunderstandings and cooperate to get things done before the farming season starts. What do you say, friend? Are you planning to leave our village and never see me again... (laughter)

**Chairperson (司會者):** Everyone, I understand that this is a difficult and challenging task. However, we must succeed in this endeavor. We need to work together for our village and ourselves to overcome adversity and create a miracle for Yesam-ri (閭三里).

We will continue to research and develop good plans for this project. For now, let's start the work. What do you all think?

**All (一同):** Good, we agree.

**Chairperson (司會者):** Then, we will proceed under the assumption that everyone agrees. Starting tomorrow, please bring your tools and gather at the village hall (會舘). It's late at night, so please take care on your way home.

---

**Detailed Business Plan (事業計劃):** To be discussed and researched separately.

**Action:** Commence work starting tomorrow.

**Instructions:** Please bring your tools and gather at the village hall (會舘) tomorrow.


--- (p. 259) ---

Here the distance to Jobi-ri in the lower village is only 6km, but since it goes around the mountain slope, it's barely wide enough for one person to pass. Who would just wait for someone to build a road?

Of course, it will be hard work and require great effort, and it may seem daunting, but we will need to take several years to build this road. Since the mountains are all rocky, we will need machinery and explosives.

However, during my time as a leader, I will dedicate myself to overcoming these difficulties and building this road, so let's all cooperate and work together.

If we manage to build this road and cars can enter our village, your lives will change overnight. There are many bachelors in our neighborhood, but no girls want to marry into a village with no access road. Let's all join forces and work together.

**All Residents (住民一同):** A moment of silence

**Jeong Yeon-deok:** Leader (指導者), while no one will oppose what you've said as it is naturally something we must do for our village's development, it's not that simple. How can we build a 6km road through rocky mountains with just our bare hands? It seems like it would take 10 years even then. And during farming season, should we neglect our crops to focus on this?

**Kim Jae-cheon:** I agree with Yeon-deok. It's easier said than done. We'll just exhaust ourselves trying to build this road. That's the county office's job, not ours. No matter how much we hammer at the rock face, we won't make a dent. Let's not start something we can't finish and just give up.

**Seo Bong-cheon (開發委員長):** From what I'm hearing, everyone seems hesitant, but instead of just insisting it can't be done, we should explore possible methods. I also stopped by the county office on my way to Samcheok-eup (三陟邑), and they told me that this year's rural road development funds (農路開發事業費) have been allocated, but the target location (對象地) hasn't been decided yet. So, I think we should take this opportunity to apply for road construction subsidy funds (補助) and gradually build the road over several years. This opportunity could be a turning point for our village, a matter of life or death.

**Yoon Kyung-sik (4-H 會長):** As the development committee chair said, I also fully support the principle of building an access road (進入路) for our village.

Our 4H members (會員) will also eagerly participate in the road construction (道路) work alongside the adults.

**Host (司會者):** Thank you all for your excellent opinions. Regardless of whether we proceed with road construction (道路開設) or not, there is no disagreement that we want our village to prosper.

As the development committee chair (開發委員長) mentioned earlier, this year's rural road development (農路開發) budget is 250 million (萬) won. I proposed that our village should undertake the road construction (道路 事業) first.

The vice-mayor (副郡守) said he would come to our village to assess the feasibility (實現可能性). Let's not miss this opportunity and give it a try.

Since I graduated from Samcheok Technical College (三陟工專), I will negotiate with the school authorities (學校當局) to borrow a compressor, and the county (郡) will handle the road design (道路設計).

They say beginnings are half the battle, so shouldn't we at least give it a try?


--- (p. 260) ---

## ♦ Minutes (會議錄)(4)

*   **Date (日時)**: December 15, 1976, 20:00
*   **Location (場所)**: Yeo (閭) Sam-bun School (三分校) Classroom (敎室)
*   **Agenda (議題)**: Economic (經濟) Trends (動向) Report (報告), Saemaul (新村) Success (成功) Case (事例) Report (報告), and Construction (建立) of Multipurpose (多目的) Welfare (福祉) Community Center (會舘)
*   **Attendees (參席人員)**: 67
*   **Absentees (不參人員)**: 3
*   **Chairperson (司會)**: Saemaul (新村) Leader (指導者) Park Jae-myeong (朴載明)
*   **Guests (臨席)**: Nogok (蘆谷) Myeonjang (面長) Kim Seong-gi (金聲基)

**Chairperson (司會者)**: Good evening, fellow villagers.

I appreciate your efforts in coming out on this dark night. I am particularly grateful to our respected Myeonjang (面長) for attending this meeting. I believe today's village assembly holds significant meaning.

As you all know, I had the honor of reporting our village's Saemaul (新村) success case (事例) to President (大統領) Park Chung-hee (朴正熙) in Seoul on December 8, thanks to your support. During this meeting, I was fortunate enough to receive the Saemaul (新村) Medal (勲章) and a grant (下賜金) of 5 million (萬) won. I would like to express my gratitude once again. This is all our village's glory and the crystallization of your hard work. I would like to share this honor with all of you. Please take a look at the medal (勲章) and certificate (勲章證) as they are being brought in.
——At this moment, Park Mu-yong (朴武勇) looks at the certificate (勲章證) and comments that the seal on the medal (勲章) is extraordinarily large, saying he has never seen such a large seal before——

When I met President (大統領) Park Chung-hee (朴正熙), I was so nervous that I couldn't think straight. When he shook my hand, my vision went dark, and I felt cold sweat all over my body. I was deeply impressed by his extensive knowledge about our rural (農村) village. I look up to him for leading our country so well to this day. I will conclude my remarks on the meeting with President (大統領) Park Chung-hee (朴正熙) here and would like to hear from our Myeonjang (面長) next.

**Myeonjang (面長) (Kim Seong-gi (金聲基))**: Thank you. Thanks to your hard work in the Saemaul (新村) project (事業), I was also honored to meet President (大統領) Park Chung-hee (朴正熙) along with Leader (指導者) Park Jae-myeong (朴載明). Your efforts were broadcast nationwide through KBS-TV on December 8. While I am not sure how many villages nationwide have achieved such glory, out of 2,251 villages in Gangwon-do (江原道),


--- (p. 261) ---

It has been announced that we will become the third village.

That is, following Hwail-ri (花日里) and Susang-ri (上里) in Yangyang County (襄陽郡), Jangyeol-ri (悅里) in Jeongseon County (旌善郡), and Dosari (沙里) in Yanggu County (楊口郡), our Yeosam (閭三) village in Samcheok County (三陟郡) will become the next one.

Although there are many villages in Gangwon-do (江原道) that are wealthier than your Yeosam (閭三) village and have undertaken various Saemaul Undong (事業) projects, I believe that the reason our Yeosam (閭三) village has been granted this honor is because of the results achieved by your diligent efforts, self-help, and cooperative spirit. I hope that you will seriously discuss this matter, but I also hope that you will cherish the special grant money that has been bestowed upon you and determine a meaningful project for the entire community that will absolutely succeed and be completed. Once again, I would like to express my gratitude to you all.

**Kim Woo-hyun (金佑炫), Village Head (里長)**: I would like to express my gratitude to the town mayor (面長) and Mr. Park (朴), the instructor (指導者). Without the dedicated efforts of the Saemaul instructor (指導者), how could we have achieved today's joy! Let us use this opportunity to work even harder and make a pledge to do so.

**All Residents (住民)**: Applause

**Master of Ceremonies (司會者)**: Then, what kind of project (事業) will you undertake with the 5 million won (萬圓) grant money (下賜金) from His Excellency (閣下)?

**Kim Gu-bae (金九培)**: In my opinion, it would be good to build a multipurpose (多目的) welfare center (福祉會舘).
Our village needs a place like a community center (會舘). Even if we have a community center (會舘), it is currently the old Yeosam (閭三) branch school (分校) site, so it seems that a community center (會舘) is urgently needed. Therefore, if we combine a purchasing and selling place (購販場), a barbershop (理髮所), and a meeting room (會議室), and also build a sweet potato crushing (甘薯粉碎機) factory (工場) since sweet potatoes are produced a lot in our village, we can make starch and earn money.

**Lee Jae-young (李載榮)**: In my opinion, since there are many mountains (山) and grass near our village, I think it would be good to buy cows (牛) with that money and raise them together as a village (共同).

**Jeong Yeon-gi (鄭淵基)**: I agree with Mr. Lee Jae-young (李載榮). We have been working hard for three years (年) until our bones break, so if we build a village welfare center (福祉會舘), we will get sick again. I shudder at the thought of work.

**Residents (住民)**: Silence for a while.

**Park Chang-ryong (朴昌龍)**: In my opinion, it would be better to have a multipurpose (多目的) welfare center (福祉會舘) as Mr. Kim Gu-bae (金九培) suggested.
Is there a barbershop (理髮所) in the neighborhood, or is there any store (商店)? Let's build a nice house.

**Lee Jae-young (李載榮)**: If we build a community center (會舘), we will need a lot of sand, but how can we transport it from a place 6km away? People's strength is also a business. And what need is there for a modern (現代式) community center (會舘) in this mountain village (山谷)? It would be better to buy cows (牛) and raise them together.

**Master of Ceremonies (司會者)**: If you have any other opinions (意見), please speak up.

**Residents (住民)**: Silence for a moment.

**Master of Ceremonies (司會者)**: If there are no other opinions (意見), we will decide on the project (事業) based on the two issues raised by Mr. Kim Gu-bae (金九培), the multipurpose (多目的) welfare center (福祉會舘), and the Hanwoo (韓牛) breeding (飼育) proposed by Mr. Lee Jae-young (李載榮). Are there any objections (異議)?

**All Residents (住民) Together (一同)**: No objections (異議).

**Master of Ceremonies (司會者)**: Then, we will decide on the target project (對象事業) based on the community center (會舘) and the cow (牛) issue (問題).


--- (p. 262) ---

The decision-making method will be by show of hands.
First, please raise your hand if you support raising cattle.
— 8 people raise their hands —
Next, please raise your hand if you support building a multipurpose welfare center.
— 59 people raise their hands —
Therefore, 8 people support the cattle business, and 59 people support building a multipurpose welfare center. With the President's (大統領) grant, we will build a village multipurpose welfare center.
The 8 people who opposed building the multipurpose welfare center, please do not feel disappointed as this is the will of the residents. Please actively cooperate in the construction of the village center in the future.
We will negotiate with the county to have them design the center. Are there any objections?
Residents: None.
Host: Then, we will conclude the meeting. Once again, thank you all residents. Please go home safely. Before you leave, I have prepared a simple banquet, so please enjoy it on your way.

### Meeting Minutes (會議錄)

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Date | July 10, 1977 |
| Venue | Village Welfare Center (福祉會舘) |
| Agenda | Report on Economic Trends (經濟動向) and Report on the Settlement of Business (事業) Funded by the President's (大統領) Grant |
| Attendees | 65 people |
| Absentees | 5 people |
| Host | Saemaul Leader Park Jae-myeong (朴載明) |

Host: Please quiet down everyone. I suppose you are happy to be in this fine building.
This is all thanks to your tireless efforts. As you all know, we have gathered you today to hold a settlement meeting regarding the construction of this welfare center. First, please enjoy the food prepared by the neighborhood while we talk. I will now give a progress report.
Reporter: Leader Park Jae-myeong (朴載明)
This center was built using the 5 million won prize money given by President (大統領) at the economic trends report meeting on December 8 last year. Through a general meeting of residents on December 20 of the same year, it was decided to build this welfare center. Thanks to your active cooperation, construction began on December 18, 1976, and despite many difficulties during the winter, the center was completed on July 8 this year. The total construction cost was 78 million won, with 5 million won supported by the county and 280 million won contributed through the residents' labor.

The design was supported by Dongyang Architectural Design Office manager in Samcheok-eup (三陟邑), and the construction was carried out by U Won-myeong (禹元明) from Gyogari, Geundeok-myeon (近德面).


--- (p. 263) ---

The welfare center (福祉會舘) is a 50-pyeong (坪) multipurpose (多目的) facility with 25-pyeong (坪) for the community center (會舘), 8-pyeong (坪) for the purchasing and selling facility (購販場), 5-pyeong (坪) for the potato crushing room (粉碎室), 5-pyeong (坪) for the barbershop (理髮所), 5-pyeong (坪) for the kitchen, and 2-pyeong (坪) for the room. We have secured a good community center (會舘) for our village. The purchasing and selling facility (購販場) will be used as a communal (共同) purchasing and selling facility (購販場) to sell daily necessities, the potato crushing room (粉碎室) will be operated communally (共同) with a crushing machine supported by the army, and the barbershop (理髮所) will be operated by hiring a barber (理髮師).

With a total of 480 participants (延人員) mobilized (動員), I would like to express my sincere (眞心) gratitude once again for the construction (建立) of this welfare center (福祉會舘). I will now conclude this brief progress report (經過報告). If anyone has any questions (疑問), please speak up.

**Kim Gu-bae (金九培):** Everyone, including the leaders (指導者), has worked very hard (勞苦) so far. But do you have any plans (對策) for the operation (運營方法) and management (管理) of this welfare center (福祉會舘)?

**Chairperson (司會):** That's a good question. The management (管理) of this community center (會舘) will be decided after selecting (選定) a manager (管理人) and considering (參酌) your opinions (意見). As for the purchasing and selling facility (購販場) and the barbershop (理髮所), we do not yet have a concrete (具體的) plan (案), so we will discuss (相議) it separately. Does anyone else have any questions (疑問)?

**All villagers (住民一同):** No objections (異議).

**Chairperson (司會):** Then, please sign (署名) the meeting minutes (會議錄) and take care on your way home in the dark night.

◆ Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (6)

| Item   | Content                                 |
| :----- | :----------------------------------- |
| **Date (日時)** | August 10, 1977 (1977年8月10日)          |
| **Location (場所)** | Community Center (會舘)                       |
| **Agenda (議題)** | Installation (架設) of Village Electricity (電氣)           |
| **Attendees (參席人員)** | 63 people (63名)                             |
| **Chairperson (司會者)** | Saemaul Leader (指導者) Park Jae-myeong (朴載明) |

**Chairperson (司會者):** Thank you all for gathering here. I feel sorry for convening (召集) meetings (會議) too often, but isn't our united (團合) strength the one that completed (完工) a 12km road (道路) over several years (數年) despite various hardships (逆境)? You all have truly worked hard (勞苦) during the road (道路) project (事業) promotion (推進).

I believe our village now has the confidence (自信感) to accomplish (完成) anything. Now, I will explain (說明) why I asked everyone to gather here today.

With our united (團合) Saemaul spirit (精神), all residents (全住民) cooperated (協助) to install (設置) a simple water supply (簡易給水), and we have seen the historical (歷史的) completion (完工) of the farm road (農路), which has been the long-cherished dream (宿願) of everyone who has lived in our village so far. However, above all, I think we cannot live well without electricity (電氣), so after several days of deliberation (宮理), I listened to the opinions (意見) of the elders (長老) at the general meeting (總會) and decided to explore (摸索) a plan (方案) for the installation (架設) of electricity (電氣).

In fact (事實), I have visited several villages in the county (郡內) for personal (個人的) matters in recent days (幾日), but there are very few villages without electricity (電氣). Seeing that villages similar to ours have electricity (電氣) installed with televisions and record players (電蓄), I couldn't help but think that our village should also quickly install (加設) electricity (電氣). Since all the elders (長老) are gathered here today,


--- (p. 264) ---

Please ensure that we can definitely get electricity installed.

**Kim Jae-cheol (金在喆)**: That's a great suggestion. There probably isn't a single person in our village who hasn't thought about electricity. No matter what, we must get electricity installed.

**Kim Chang-hyeon (金昌鉉)**: Everyone's suggestions are good, but installing electricity is not a small investment. We can't avoid thinking about how we will bear the burden.

**Seo In-seok (徐仁錫)**: Actually, before starting the construction, we should investigate how much capital will be required, whether we can receive support from the government, and if there are technicians available to do the electrical work. Then we can start the project.

**Moderator (司會者)**: I've heard both of your points. Actually, I've been to the county and township for about 10 days to make plans and have done some rough designs. I heard that the total project cost will be around 13 million won. Out of that, we can probably get a loan of about 7 million won from the administrative authorities for the rural electrification project. That means we will have to bear a burden of about 6 million won, which is about 80,000 won per household. It's a heavy burden, but if we think about how we lived 5-6 years ago, scraping by on grass roots and tree bark, we can see how wealthy we are now. Let's help each other and use this opportunity to get the work done.

**Jeong Yeon-gyeong (鄭然景)**: But how can we bear such a large amount of money at once? Also, how will we repay the 7 million won loan? No matter how much better off we are than before, can we really bear the burden of the loan?

**Lee Jang**: Well, I've roughly looked into it. After installing electricity with the loan, we pay the electricity bill each month. We add a little to that and the entire village bears the burden equally over 25 years. So, receiving the loan isn't a big deal. It's the government supporting rural electrification.

**Park Chang-yong**: Let's make our village one where we can watch TV. We must do it. The later we do it, the more we'll fall behind other villages.

**Moderator (司會者)**: Are there any objections?

**All (一同)**: (Silence)

**Moderator (司會者)**: Then, let's make installing electricity the principle, and we must discuss and cooperate many times during the promotion of this project. We can't hold a general meeting of residents every time we discuss, and if we are to cooperate with related agencies and supervise the site, it would be good to form an electricity promotion committee to solve all arising problems and promote it. What do you think?

**Seo Yong-cheon ∙ Park Bu-yong**: That's good. Let's do that.

**Moderator (司會者)**: Then, how should we form the committee?

**Park Bu-yong**: One chairperson and four members, each a class leader, totaling five members should be enough.

**Yoon Gyeong-sik**: That suggestion is good, but there seem to be too few committee members. We have to discuss and decide everything representing the residents, but it seems that four or five members can't make a decision. At least seven or eight members are needed to collect the self-burdened funds, supervise the construction, and discuss with administrative agencies.


--- (p. 265) ---

### Meeting Minutes

**Seo Bong-cheon(徐奉千):** The idea of having the 4-H president(會長) seems reasonable. Let's form a promotion committee(推進委員會) consisting of 1 chairperson(委員長) and 7 members(委員), totaling 8 people(名), and entrust them with the task regarding the electrical work(電氣工事). (All in favor(一同贊成))

**Chairperson(司會者):** Then, who would be suitable for the chairperson(委員長)?

**Kim Jae-cheon(金在天):** Who else could it be but the current(現在) Saemaul leader(指導者)? There is also the village head(里長), but the village head(里長) has too many other tasks, so let's elect(選出) Saemaul leader Park Jae-myeong(朴載明) as the chairperson(委員長).

**All in favor(一同贊成):** We agree. (Applause)

**Chairperson(司會者):** I appreciate your support and will work hard, but I ask for your active(積極的) cooperation(協助). How about the members(委員)?

**Lee Jae-young:** As I mentioned earlier, let's recommend the 4 class leaders(班長) as members(委員), and reserve soldier platoon leader In Seok, 4-H president(會長) Yoon Kyung-sik, and development committee chairperson(開發委員長) Seo Bong-cheon, making a total of seven people as members(委員) to promote the project.

**Seo Bong-cheon:** I appreciate your words, but I have my own farming work(農事) and lack the ability(能力), so I would like to be excluded from the members(委員) if possible, following everyone's opinion(意見).

**Lee Jae-kyung:** This person, who isn't busy, right? Don't you know that leader Park(朴指導者) has been sacrificing(犧牲) for the village for several years(年) without even looking after his own(自己) work(事)?

**Kim Chang-hyun(金昌鉉):** Let's do as Jae-kyung suggests.

**Chairperson(司會者):** Are there any other opinions(意見)?

**All in favor(一同):** (Silent)

**Chairperson(司會者):** Then, let's elect the members(委員) as such, and tomorrow, the village head(里長) and I will visit the county(郡) to discuss(議論) and hold a promotion committee(推進委員會) meeting to devise(講究) a promotion plan(方案). Are there any other opinions(意見)?

**All in favor(一同):** None.

**Chairperson(司會者):** Then, let's proceed with the electrical business(電氣事業) in this manner and conclude the meeting(會議). Thank you. Goodbye. And please come to my house the day after tomorrow if possible, members of the promotion committee(推進委員).

# Chungcheongbuk-do (Chungcheongbuk-do)

◊ Yulyang-dong (Yulyang-dong), Sang-ri (Sang-ri), Cheongju-si (Cheongju-si)
◊ Sanseong (Sanseong), Naebuk-myeon (Naebuk-myeon), Boeun-gun (Boeun-gun)
◊ Sangnyegok-ri (Sangnyegok-ri), Cheongsan-myeon (Cheongsan-myeon), Okcheon-gun (Okcheon-gun)

--- (p. 268) ---

## Chungcheongbuk-do (Chungcheongbuk-do) Cheongju City (Cheongju-si) Yulyang-dong (Yulyang-dong) Sang-ri (Sang-ri)

### 1. Overview of the Village

#### a. History

- After the reign of King Yeongjo (英祖) of the Joseon Dynasty (李朝), the area was part of Yulbong-ri (栗峯里) in Bukju-naemyeon (北州內面), Cheongju-mok (清州牧).
- On October 1, 1915, it was renamed Yulhyeon-ri (栗峴里) in Sajumyeon (四州面), Cheongju-gun (淸州郡), and later changed to Yulyang (栗陽).
- On January 1, 1963, it was incorporated into Cheongju City (淸州市) as Yulyang-ri (栗陽里) due to administrative district reforms.
- On April 1, 1966, following the Ministry of Interior's (內務部) policy to unify city names, the village became known as Yulyang-dong (栗陽洞) Sang-ri (上里), a suburban village near the city.
- Around 1870, a member of the Seo (徐氏) clan from Daeseong (達城), Boeun (報恩), lost his family wealth to gambling and became a fire-field farmer (火田民), settling in this area.
- At the same time, a Kim (金氏) family from Gimhae (金海) also settled here as fire-field farmers, establishing the village.
- These residents supplied fire-fields (火田) and firewood (火木) from the dense forests to Yulbong Station (栗峯驛) to sustain their livelihoods.
- The village is located near the base of Baekhwasan (百花山), which is said to be a place where centipedes are prevalent. According to feng shui (風水地理說), if bitten by a centipede, chewing chestnuts (밤) can be effective. To suppress the power of centipedes, chestnuts should be revered, leading to the abundance of chestnut trees in the area.
- The village is named Yulyang (栗陽) because it is located in a sunny spot (陽地) with Baekhwasan (百花山) to the north, like a screen (屛風), and is called Yulsang-ri (栗上里) or Sang-ri (上里) village as it is the uppermost neighborhood.

#### b. Location and Conditions

##### <Location>

- Located in the northern part of Cheongju City (淸州市), the village is accessible by crossing Bamgoji (밤고개, a pass named for the abundance of chestnuts, but commonly known as Bangoji) towards Chungju (忠州) and ascending Yullyangcheon (율량천). It is situated about 2 km to the east towards Sangsan (上黨山城).
- The village is nestled in a cozy spot between the foothills of Sangsan (上黨山) and Baekhwasan (百花山).

##### <Conditions>

- Situated on the foothills, the village has infertile soil and lacks water sources, making it a barren land where vegetation struggles to grow. The gentle slopes are suitable for creating meadows (草地).
- The development of surrounding areas for meadow creation led to the promotion of dairy farming (酪農) using mixed feed (配合飼料), establishing the village as a dairy farming community centered around cattle.

## 2. Village Development Process

### Ga. Situation Before 1970

#### 1) Basic Environment
* The stream flowing from Baekhwasan (百花山) behind the village curves like a bow and flows in front of the village,
* The road built during the Saemaul Undong (再建國民運動) could barely allow one oxcart (牛車) to enter the village entrance,
* Inside the village, the roofs of thatched houses were so low that even bundles of firewood would get caught on the eaves, making it difficult to pass,
* The roofs were rotten and sunken, with weeds growing in the hollows, and when it rained, dirty water would flow down, creating an unsightly scene,
* Moreover, if it rained a little too much, the stream would overflow into the fields (田沓),
* And during droughts, there was no drinking water, forcing villagers to go 1km to the middle village (中里) to do laundry.

#### 2) Income Level
* The slash-and-burn fields (火田) cultivated by ancestors were the basis of life, with barley, beans, corn, and potatoes as main crops (主產物),
* The long-standing practice of tenant farming (貸田) meant that most of the harvested crops were given to landlords (地主) under the name of "doji" (地主),
* During the farming season (農事), food supplies would run out, forcing villagers to borrow rice (長利) from landlords in the neighboring middle village (中里),
* Special crops (特作) were limited to tobacco cultivation (煙草) in a few households, and this village was one of the poorest (零細) in the area (管內),
* It was during the Saemaul Undong (再建國民運動) that this village began to open its eyes to income-generating activities (所得事業),
* Through this movement (運動), some young men (靑年) in the village received government (政府) support in 1963 to install electricity (電氣) in 26 households (戶),
* In 1964, Seo Dong-gyu, Han Heung-won, and Kim Jin-eok (氏) became the first to import two dairy cows (各 2頭) each for trial breeding (試驗),
* They noticed that there were many areas suitable for creating pastures (草地) around the village (部落), making dairy farming (酪農) possible even for small-scale farmers (零細) with limited arable land (耕地),
* However, when they actually started raising dairy cows (飼育), they faced challenges such as lack of technology (技術), equipment (裝備), and insufficient government (政府) support (支援),
* Additionally, many residents (住民) opposed dairy farming (反對) due to economic (經濟的) considerations at the time (當時),
* When producing milk (牛乳), the producers (生産者) themselves would directly


--- (p. 271) ---

Visiting each household in the city to secure consumers and delivering daily at an early hour posed significant challenges. Additionally, the lack of awareness among residents about milk distribution and their limited financial means led to a reluctance to consume milk, which became a major factor in the stagnation of the dairy farming business. As a result, Han Kwang-won and Kim Jin-eok failed in their business and moved to the city. Only a few residents, who had gained new awareness, managed to increase the number of cows to 25 by around 1970. At that time, the average household income was 650,000 won.

### 3) Living Conditions
#### a) Consciousness Structure
Living in ignorance and poverty, people did not even think about improving their lives. They lacked unity and were lazy and envious. Two bars in the city were always bustling, and people would drink to quench their thirst without worrying about the cost of their next meal. One drink led to another, and soon they would spend the money meant for a load of firewood on alcohol. Arguments and even fistfights would break out among the drinkers, often escalating into family disputes or clashes between factions and clans. There was never a peaceful day.

On market days in Cheongju City, most people would sharpen their sickles not to go to work but to spend the day at the market doing nothing. Men and women alike would get drunk, loitering under the eaves of other people's houses, singing loudly, and behaving indecently, drawing disapproving glances from others. Taverns often turned into gambling dens, and fights would break out, leading to the seizure of ancestral land deeds. The wails and shouts of women made the village sound like it was in mourning. Such customs led to a decline in public morals and a loss of hope and pioneering spirit for the future. People preferred to stay out of other people's business unless it directly affected them. They were indifferent to good deeds and efforts to live better but were highly partisan during elections, which only fueled factionalism.

#### b) Culture and Daily Life
Residents here, who made a living by cutting firewood, could not afford a decent life. They could not even buy a newspaper or magazine. In winter, a gentleman would wear a cotton-padded pants and jacket, and a dyed military jacket, and be ready to visit his in-laws' house for the first time.

Looking at their houses, they were crawling shacks with doors plastered with fertilizer bags, crooked and twisted. Entering, one would find a dark room like a cave, and if the walls were covered with newspaper, it was considered high-class.

Another important point was that the village residents unconditionally opposed or were non-cooperative with anything the government did, whether good or bad. They had no contact with the neighborhood office, and if an official came on an inspection tour, they would create unnecessary trouble and be non-cooperative, to the extent that even the officials avoided visiting. The penetration of government policies was out of the question, and the village, which did not even think about the benefits of the government, was a backward village with no dream of development.


--- (p. 272) ---

## 1) Motivation and Results of the Pilot Project
* In 1970, news of the Saemaul Undong spreading across the nation reached this village. Kwun Jae-ha, who was the youth leader, visited the local office and requested the village head to support their Saemaul project by providing cement.
* Whether it was due to being the first to visit or the rare occasion of visiting a village with no prior contact, the village head agreed to support the administrative village unit with 335 bags of cement in 1971. Out of these, 30 bags were allocated for the pilot project.
* With the supported cement, the villagers constructed one underground drainage system along the village ditch. However, due to the lack of technical skills among the few participating residents, the construction was rough and shoddy. After the main project was completed, the villagers, who had not shown their faces during the construction, criticized the work, saying it was either well or poorly done.
* Consequently, no government support projects were assigned to the village in 1972.
* Nevertheless, the residents failed to reflect on their actions. They gathered at the local tavern, complained, and spent their days drinking, blaming Kwun Jae-ha, the youth leader, for the village's exclusion from the Saemaul project support. They showed no shame and wasted their time without awakening to the situation.

## 2) Selection of the Leader and Activity Status
* Although the village leader is typically elected at the general village assembly, the village head, aware of the residents' nature, believed that an election would not yield good results. Thus, Seo Jang-seok, who was then the class leader, was appointed as the village leader without the residents' knowledge.
* Seo Jang-seok, a high school graduate who had worked in agriculture before enlisting in the military, was deeply impressed by the Saemaul education he received in the military. He made sincere efforts to lead the village. However, from December 1, 1973, to September 30, 1974, during his tenure, Kwun Jae-ha, who was then the youth leader, actually handled all the administrative tasks and village guidance.
* Initially, Seo Jang-seok seemed to organize and guide the residents with enthusiasm. However, due to inconsistencies between his words and actions, as well as unclear accounting, the villagers' trust in him dwindled day by day. Eventually, he became a distrusted leader, and the village became more divided, filled with complaints.
* Seeing the village's situation, Seo Woo-seok, who was then the promotion committee chairperson, proposed holding a general assembly to formally elect a village leader. All residents responded positively and conducted a secret ballot, writing the names of their preferred candidates.
* Thus, on October 1, 1973, with the unanimous approval of all village residents, Kwun Jae-ha was elected as the village leader.
* Leader Kwun had only completed elementary school. At the age of 23, he got married while serving in the military. At 25, he became an itinerant peddler to earn money for his nephew's tuition. After several failed business attempts in other regions, he returned home and spent disheartened days amidst a large family. At the age of 33, he moved to this village with his six family members, possessing nothing. Through diligent and sincere efforts, he eventually secured 2,000 pyeong of fields and 2,300 pyeong of rice paddies.
* Upon his election as the village leader, he made a firm resolution to transform this village into a prosperous one, determined to achieve at least one meaningful result with his heavy sense of responsibility.


--- (p. 273) ---

He, who couldn't drink alcohol or smoke, first aimed to reform the spirit of the villagers who spent their days playing hwatu (a Korean card game) and drinking alcohol. He visited and persuaded one villager each day. Additionally, to develop the village's income sources, he consulted with Seo Sang-won, who was then serving as the village chief, and entrusted the Agricultural Extension Service with a detailed analysis of the soil quality and climate. The results indicated that the village was suitable for raising dairy cows, leading to active promotion and expansion of dairy farming. Simultaneously, he closely cooperated with the Cheongju Dairy Cooperative to vigorously advance the dairy cow introduction project and also pushed forward environmental improvement projects.

As the number of dairy cows increased to over 80, transporting the milk they produced necessitated the expansion of An-gil (a local road). On November 20, 1973, Upper-ri Village formed a sisterhood relationship with the Cheongju Lions Club. Lee Byung-seop, a club member and city councilor, acted as the mediator between club president An Seon-jun and village leader Kwang Jae-ha. The club members, composed of prominent local figures, visited the village to encourage and comfort the residents. They donated 250,000 won worth of children's playground equipment as a gift for the sisterhood, igniting the villagers' enthusiasm for the Saemaul Undong. The frequent visits from city officials, including the police chief and mayor, along with other prominent figures, fostered a mental transformation that drove the villagers to unite and participate actively in the Saemaul Undong.

### 3) Overcoming Challenges

The expansion of An-gil, which began in the harsh cold of December 1973, was arduous, requiring the moving of ancient boulders. Straightening the road involved demolishing houses, cutting down large persimmon trees (often yielding dozens of fruits each), and installing 210 meters of sewers to address the muddy conditions caused by rainwater and waste. Residents who faced the loss of their homes, courtyards, or trees were reluctant to agree. The construction began on December 1, 1973, with conflicts and opposition from affected residents. Cutting down old persimmon trees was particularly contentious, with one grandmother protesting that the tree, planted by her ancestors, would cause misfortune if felled. Despite these challenges, the leader took the initiative to cut down the tree, and the road expansion began. However, Kim Su-yeon (58), Seo Jeong-mok (55), and Kim Gab-chul remained opposed. The leader's persuasion, along with the efforts of Kim Man-su, a young club member who convinced his father Kim Gab-gwang to donate land, helped resolve the land donation issue. Seo Bong-sam also pledged to donate land for the road expansion.


--- (p. 274) ---

At last, even the residents who had initially opposed the movement began to respond, and the issue of land consolidation was resolved.
- While working daily to resolve the land issue, even late into the night, visiting each household to persuade them, Leader Kwon felt immense fulfillment regarding the Saemaul Undong when he heard Kim Man-su, a member, pleading with his father in a heart-wrenching manner. Moved by the united members' efforts, Leader Kwon vowed to work even more diligently.
- Living in his wife's village, he took great care in both actions and words, always taking the lead in village matters. This earned him the trust of the villagers.
- Once the road was built, a 210-meter-long sewer pipe was installed. Additionally, the female members, who had long suffered from their husbands' drunkenness, took the lead in persuading their husbands to stop gambling and drinking, successfully convincing two bars to close voluntarily.
- The village assembly decided to operate a village purchasing and selling center through the women's association.
- The Saemaul promotion body was reorganized, and tasks and projects were carried out by sector.

4) Developmental Promotion of Saemaul Undong
a) Operation of Night Classes
- Under the responsibility of the youth association president, the community center was utilized to provide nighttime group tutoring for 20 middle and high school students. After school, students who used to play and socialize began to show respect to adults and act properly in all aspects, thanks to the moral education provided by the guidance team.
b) Operation of Daycare Centers During the Busy Farming Season
- Under the responsibility of the women's association president, two volunteer caregivers were selected from the women's association and the 4H girls' club. A daycare center was operated for 50 preschool children using the community center and children's playground, providing protection and education. The women's association was responsible for providing snacks twice a day using the communal kitchen, ensuring the safety and development of the children and securing female labor during the busy farming season.
c) Joint Purchasing and Selling Business
- The purchasing and selling business, established with the women's association fund after the removal of bars, evolved into a village-wide market viewing movement. Female members took turns collecting order forms from each household, purchasing items in bulk at the market, and delivering them as ordered. This reduced unnecessary market visits and lowered prices. During holidays like Chuseok and Seollal, transportation by car was even used. Additionally, 150,000 won from the profit of building the community center was supported for its construction, and members saved rice in thrift rice jars to secure funds.
d) Operation of Saemaul Joint Work Teams
- Operated under the auspices of the youth association, the work team consisted of 36 members. This team undertook various tasks, including farming, land reclamation, soil mixing, land clearing, construction, and architectural projects, earning an average annual income of 130 million won.


--- (p. 275) ---

*   The improvement of work efficiency (作業能率) is not only promoting unity (團合) among all residents (全體住民), but also showcasing a more united (團合) face (一面貌) of the village (洞里). For the construction (建立) of the community center (會舘), 250,000 won (萬圓) of business funds (事業費) were covered by the profits (收益) from joint work (共同作業).

### Ma) Saemaul Women's Association Joint Work

*   The Saemaul Women's Association joint work team (共同作業隊), consisting of 45 members (婦女會員), primarily engages in agricultural work (農作物) such as weeding (김매기), harvesting (收穫), and sowing (播種) to save wages (勞賃) for the "One Bank Account per Member" campaign (會員 1通帳 갖기 운동). The 45 bank accounts (通帳) have become a source (源泉) of household economics (家庭經濟). As a result, work efficiency (作業能率) has improved, and idle labor (遊休 노동력) has been utilized.
*   In particular, these women would go to great lengths for money, as the saying goes, "See a ten won (圓) coin and run a hundred li (百里)."
*   Upon learning that the reserve forces (豫備軍) were conducting mobile training (機動 訓練) at Sangdangsanseong (上黨山城), they carried noodles (국수) up to the summit (頂上) of the mountain fortress (山城), which was over 30 li (里) away, to serve the reserve forces (豫備軍). From the unit commander (部隊長), they received an envelope of money (金一封) and a donation (募金) from the reserve forces (豫備軍) expressing their thanks (謝禮金). The total amount was twice (倍) the market price (市中 飮食값) of food (飮食), creating a sensation (話題).

### Ba) Dairy Farming Training

*   One of the reasons for the rapid growth (急成長) of dairy farming (酪農), currently (現在) with about 300 cows (餘頭), is that under the guidance (指導) of the rural (農村) guidance center (指導所) and the 4H Group (主管), activities (活動) such as dairy farming (酪農) technical education (技術敎育), collective disinfection (共同消毒) of barns (畜舍), and preventive inoculation (豫防 接種) of cows (젖소) have been mainly conducted. Even farmers (農家) who were initially opposed (反對) to dairy farming (飼育) education (敎育) participated (參與) in large numbers (多數).
*   Moreover, Leader Kwon (權指導者) promoted (推進) environmental improvement (環境改善) projects (事業) such as roof improvement (地붕개량) of 21 houses (棟), wall improvement (담장개량) of 550 meters, kitchen improvement (부엌개량) of 6 houses (棟), and toilet (便所) construction (建設) of 15 houses (棟) in 1974 (74년도). As a result, household chores (家事) were neglected (放觀), and farming (農事) was in a bad state (말이 아니었다). The usually quiet (平素) wife (婦人) became irritable (짜증을 내게 되었다), asking him to pay more attention (돌봐 달라고) to household chores (家事) instead of just focusing (열중) on village affairs (마을 일). This eventually led to marital disputes (夫婦 싸움) and family conflicts (內外 다툼).
*   One day, when Leader Kwon (權指導者) went to the field (들) alone, he saw that the young people (靑年) were weeding (매어주고) his rice paddies (논) and the women (婦女子) were weeding (김을 매고) his fields (밭). Upon learning the reason (事由), he found out that the villagers (마을 사람들) had voluntarily (자진) helped him because they had witnessed (目擊) that his excessive focus (열중) on village affairs (마을 일) had led to neglect (망치고) of his farming (農事) and family discord (家庭 불화). Moved (눈시울이 뜨거워 옴을 느끼고) by this, Leader Kwon (權指導者) became even more diligent (열심) in his work, and perhaps this is how the present-day Sangni (上里) was born (誕生).
*   Initially (當初), the 500 bags (袋) of cement (시멘트) provided (支援) ran out (바닥나자) halfway (도중), but the city (市) preemptively (미리) provided (支援) an additional (追加) 400 bags (袋), enabling the successful completion (成功적 완수) of the 1974 (74년도) project (事業).
*   In autumn, 3,000 chestnut trees (밤나무) were planted (植栽) on the mountains (뒷산) behind six villages (町), creating (造成) a chestnut tree housing complex (밤나무 단지).
