## 6) Heartwarming Stories
* On November 20, 1973, through the mediation of Lee Byung-seop (李秉燮), a member of the Lions Club, a sisterhood relationship was established. Chairman An Geo-jun (安璩俊) and all other members donated 6 units of amusement facilities and other goods worth 250,000 won to comfort and encourage the residents, awakening their dormant awareness and igniting the Saemaul Undong (事業). This left a profound impression. On June 4, 1975, they sent 56 sickles, and on February 10, 1976, they brought 50 shovels for the Saemaul Undong (事業), planted trees in the village, and spent a day with the children, further enhancing the village's enthusiasm. Additionally, on July 15, 1976, they sent a lectern (敎卓) and a platform (敎壇) worth 80,000 won for the village community center's completion ceremony, providing material and spiritual support that earned the residents' praise and joy.
* Apart from this, Seojusan Industry (西州產業), which exclusively collects the village's milk, donated 50 chairs, and Huang Seung-nak (黃承洛) from the city sent a large blackboard worth 50,000 won, along with contributions totaling around 200,000 won from many other individuals for the community center's completion ceremony.
* On February 15, 1977, all employees of the Cheongju branch (淸州支店) of the Korea Industrial Bank (韓國產業銀行) visited the village as part of a Saemaul Undong (事業) field survey and donated about 20 shovels.
* On September 10, 1977, Assemblyman Lee Byung-seop (李秉燮) donated 50,000 won, and on September 30, 1977, Yu Seung-yeol, the head of the Cheongju Dairy Cooperative (酪農組合長), visited the village and donated 20,000 won. Additionally, the city's administrative advisory committee members donated 10,000 won, and Nam Chung-hee (南忠熙), the head of the city's tax office (稅務課長), donated 5,000 won, among other significant donations and contributions.

## 7) Visits by Dignitaries
* On July 8, 1977, during an unofficial visit to Korea, U.S. Army Secretary Alexander, accompanied by his family, aides, and 15 others, visited the village with the guidance of National Assembly Member Min Hwang-sik (閔璜植) and his wife. They thoroughly observed the village's development and residents' lives, offering comfort and encouragement.
* In 1976, the mayors of Cheongju City (淸州市長) and Yeongdeungpo District (永登浦區廳長) visited for comparative inspections, and in 1977, the mayors of Chuncheon City (春川市長) and Suwon City (水原市長) also visited for comparative purposes.

## 8) Special Matters
### a) Joyful Events
* When the Lions Club established a sisterhood relationship and encouraged the residents
* When the children's playground was completed and children joyfully played on the playground equipped with amusement facilities donated by the Lions Club
* When the village received a presidential grant (下賜金) of 1 million won on December 10, 1975
* When a dairy cow purchased with the presidential grant (下賜金) on January 20, 1976 gave birth to a female calf. After several days of hard work to purchase a pregnant dairy cow, it gave birth to a female calf within a month. At that time, a male calf was worth around 5,000 won, while a female calf was worth at least 200,000 won, making the villagers' joy indescribable.
* When the village received a second presidential grant (下賜金) of 1.5 million won on December 4, 1976
* When the village won first place at the city level during the successful case presentation conference for leaders on October 12, 1976
* When Chungcheongbuk-do (忠淸北道) won first place at the June 4, 1976, competition festival
* When the village exceeded 1.4 million won during the Saemaul Undong (事業) grand festival on April 22, 1977, receiving a certificate and a mist blower as awards


--- (p. 278) ---

Indeed, all residents were happy that they could live well as a result of their hard work, especially when they received the award for their business (상사업비) of 500,000 won.

- When the documentary film "Mucheoncheon" was produced by the city in August 1977 and filming took place in Sang-ri Village, all villagers appeared in the movie.
- On September 20, 1977, at the Saemaul Undong Grand Plaza, I received the award for my business (상사업비) of 500,000 won from the President's (大統領) daughter, Geun-hye, and the day the Women's Association purchased and introduced a cow.
- On December 9, 1977, when the village received a grant of 3,000,000 won as a village simultaneously supported for economic trends report.

b) Sad events

- When trying to calm down an old lady who was cursing and making a fuss, saying that tree stumps would appear if old trees were cut down while making a village road.
- On May 26, 1977, at around 17:36, while all villagers were working on building new houses as part of the housing improvement project, Myung-ho (5 years old), the third son of Jung-hoon Lee from the village, and Heung-deok (5 years old), the third son of Dong-yun Seo from the village, drowned in a well while playing at a shared laundry area. At this time, all villagers could not hold back their sorrow because it was an accident that occurred while working at a Saemaul Undong (新村運動) site.
- On May 10, 1977, the provincial livestock hygiene service conducted a collective examination of the village's cows. However, five privately owned cows and one collectively raised cow were diagnosed with tuberculosis. After a re-examination and a third examination, the collectively raised cow of the village was ordered to be slaughtered on September 22. All villagers cried as if they were at a funeral, and even when trying to put the cow on the car, it would not get on. The villagers shed tears watching this. Although there was significant financial damage, as the cow was nine months pregnant, efforts were made to postpone the slaughter by one month and to arrange for isolation, but these attempts were unsuccessful. On September 23, when the cow was finally taken away, villagers cried and held onto the car, and some even lay down in front of the car to prevent it from leaving. All villagers wailed loudly as the cow was taken away, and they were even more heartbroken upon hearing that the calf was a heifer.

### Achievements through Saemaul Undong

1) Spiritual Aspect
*   Through Saemaul Undong, people were transformed into new human beings characterized by diligence, self-help, and cooperation;
*   They gained confidence in their abilities and developed gratitude towards their country and neighbors;
*   Through village general assemblies, they embodied Korean democracy.
*   With a heightened sense of historical mission, they actively cooperated with the government.

2) Livelihood Aspect
*   Farmers acquired dairy farming techniques and reformed agricultural methods, shifting from grain-based farming to diversified specialization in livestock, fruit trees, and special crops, leading to a rapid increase in income;
*   Farmers became proactive and diligent through effort and research;
*   Through thrift and savings, every household opened a savings account;
*   They practiced helping their less fortunate neighbors, understanding that their well-being was intertwined.

3) Production Aspect


--- (p. 281) ---

Through the large-scale introduction of dairy cows and cooperation with powdered milk factories, milk production increased significantly, leading to a sharp rise in income.
The successful introduction of dairy cows, funded by government grants, laid the foundation for the establishment of a village community fund.

### 3. Future Development Plans

- Expand income-generating businesses through cooperative dairy farming, while continuing to promote the introduction of 500 dairy cows.
- Establish one small reservoir to improve the irrigation rate from the current 56% to over 80%, enabling year-round farming.
- Actively promote the complete mechanization of agricultural machinery to pursue scientific farming.
- Purchase small trucks for the direct transportation of milk and feed.
- Install telephones to expand industrial information and medical services, aiming to achieve a welfare-oriented and modernized village.
- We will strive to pass on this legacy to future generations.

### 4. Village Assembly Meeting

♦ Minutes of the Meeting (1)

**Agenda:** Expansion of the village inner road
**Date:** October 10-20, 1973
**Location:** Home of Seo Jeong-mok (徐廷穆)
**Attendees:** Son Bok-gil and 55 others
**Absentees:** None
**Chairperson:** Leader Seo Jang-seok (徐長錫)

---

**Chairperson:** I apologize for convening this late-night meeting. Tonight's agenda includes the expansion of the village inner road, the establishment of a village fund, the improvement of dilapidated buildings, roof improvements, and the promotion of sewer coverage projects.

First, let me discuss the expansion of the village inner road. As you all know, our village is too narrow, and we have discussed this issue multiple times. This is the first time it has been formally raised at a village assembly. The promotion committee has drawn up an expansion plan.

I apologize for the late notice, but this is a matter of great importance for our village's future. Under the first-phase plan, the walls of Kim Jong-heon's house, as well as those of Kim Ju-yeon, Seo Woo-seok, Lee Jong-un, Kim Man-soo, and Choi Cha-rang, will be demolished. Additionally, the persimmon trees of Kim Su-yeon and Seo Woo-seok, and the persimmon tree of Kim Tae-young will be cut down. Parts of the houses of Seo Jeong-mok, Seo Woo-seok, and Kim Su-yeon will also be demolished.

**Kim Su-yeon:** Leader! May I have the floor? Just what is the point of expanding the village inner road if it means demolishing my house?


--- (p. 282) ---

Well, it's not fair to say that I should be the only one to suffer. I can't agree to that.
**Kwon Jae-ha**: I understand your point, sir, but considering how our village has been left behind and unable to develop in the past, those who have to give up their land or whose walls have to be torn down should show generosity and contribute. Otherwise, our village will continue to lag behind. I sincerely ask for your active cooperation for the development of our village.
The walls torn down for the village road expansion will be repaired by all the young members of our village.

**Host**: Yes, as Kwon Jae-ha, the youth leader, said, if the elders permit, tearing down walls, fixing houses, and other tasks will turn our village into a new community.

**Seo Bong-sam**: I understand. We will follow the leaders and the youth. Even if my land is taken, I'll be grateful if you make our village better.

**Seo Gyu-seok**: What are you talking about? I've lived here all my life. The alley is narrow, and I can't carry things or farm, but I can still live well as it is. I oppose this.

**Lee Beom-seop**: Uncle, what are you saying? Our neighboring villages have widened their roads, and tractors can pass through every house. Imagine being able to bring fertilizer or feed right to your doorstep. How can you oppose the young people who want to achieve what you couldn't in your youth?

**All villagers**: Right.

**Host**: Then, I assume everyone agrees. We will start the project tomorrow. Next, I would like to discuss the creation of a village fund. We have 10 bags of rice in the village. If we use 5 of them for the road expansion and other New Community Movement projects, what do you think?

**Kim Gap-gyu**: That rice has been saved by our ancestors for generations. Why should we use it? Don't you feel guilty about eating it all, let alone using it?

**Host**: Your point is valid, sir, but this rice was saved to help our village prosper. If we use it for this project, it might lead to more funds in the future. Please consider this and allow us to use the fund.

**Kim Seok-keun**: At my age, I want to see our village thrive. If we entrust our work to the young, we should also hand over economic control to them and let them manage it as they see fit.

**Seo Gyu-seok**: Then the young people can do as they please, and we won't know. If something goes wrong, they'll blame us. We old folks will leave.

**Lee Beom-ju**: Very well. Please entrust everything to the young people and let the elders retire.

**All young people**: Please entrust it to us.

**All elders**: Go ahead and do well.


--- (p. 283) ---

Host (社會者): Thank you very much. I apologize for being late.
Today's evening meeting will conclude as above, and we will commence the work starting tomorrow. I will now adjourn the meeting.
Attendees: Han Byeong-gyeong, Lee Beom-gyu, Seo Jeong-mok, Kim Gyeong-su, Park Sun-tae, Son Bok-gil, Lee Beom-seop, Seo Rap-seok, Kim Han-jun, Seo Nam-won, Kim Jeung-sik, Jeong Seong-ok, Seo Sam-bong, Lee Jong-un, Seo No-seok, Oh Chang-seon, Im Jong-han, Kim Su-yeon, Song Woo-young, Park No-cheon, Jo Deok-hee, Seo Nam-seok, Kim Jong-heon, Choi Cha-rang, Kim Han-su, Oh Young-won, Seo Hae-seok, Kim Dae-young, Kim Man-su, Kim Han-bok, Choi Byung-ho, Seo Gyu-seok, Kim Bo-young, Kim In-hwan, Shin Seung-hwan, Lee Wan-hee, Kim Yong-cheom, Ryu Yong-seong, Kwon Tae-u, Seo Jang-seok, Seo Jeong-seon, Jeon Jae-ha, Kim Seok-geun, Ryu Chun-bu, Na Byeong-rap, Seo Dong-gyu, Seo Sang-won, Won Gyeong-sik, Seo Dong-myeong, Seo Un-won, Han Beong-o, Kim Beong-su, Kim Jae-won, Seo Jeong-bong, Yoon Seok-gyu

Absentees (不參人員): Son Bok-gil and 7 others
Chairperson (司會者): Leader (指導者) Kwang Jae-ha

Chairperson (司會者): Dear villagers, thank you for gathering here despite your hardships. We will now hold a settlement meeting regarding the village road expansion project that has been promoted since October 1973.
Seo Sang-yun: First, I would like to express my sincere gratitude to the leader (指導者) and the promotion committee chairperson (推進委員長) as well as the village head (洞長) for their cooperation in the village road expansion construction. I am particularly grateful to the residents who donated land for the village road expansion. Without your support, this project would not have been possible.
Chairperson (司會者): As you all know, there have been many issues regarding the land incorporated into the village road expansion project. Even now, some elderly individuals, including grandparents and aunts, do not understand and are still complaining. Some have even come to my house to express their grievances. Please continue to understand and persuade each other to resolve these issues.
Kim Bo-young: Although 150 pyeong (坪) of our rice fields were incorporated into the project, causing significant economic and other losses, we did so for the sake of the village road expansion. Initially, there were many complaints during the construction, but now that the road is paved, we feel greatly satisfied.
Just as the chairperson said, even if there are some complaints about the incorporated land, let us cooperate with each other for the sake of our neighborhood.
All Residents (住民一同): Understood.
Chairperson (司會者): From today onwards, I hope that all grievances regarding the land incorporated into the village road expansion will be resolved, and that you will actively cooperate with the new village movement (새마을運動) in the future. I will now conclude today's meeting.
Attendees (參席者): Kwang Jae-ha, Han Byeong-gyeong, Son Bok-gil, Kim Jong-sik, Oh Chang-seon, Jo Deok-hee, Oh Young-wol, Choi Byung-o, Lee Wan-hee, Seo Jeong-seon, Seo Dong-gyu, Han Beong-o, Lee Beom-gyu, Seo Woo-seok, Lee Beom-seop, Jeong Seong-ok, Im Jong-han, Seo Nam-seok, Seo Hae-seok, Seo Gyu-seok, Seo Gi-seok

## Minutes of the Meeting (會議錄) (3)

> **Agenda(議題):** Selection of President (大統領) His Excellency's Special Support Project (特別支援事業)
> **Date(日時):** December 5, 1975, 18:00
> **Location(場所):** Mr. Kwon Jae-ha's (權在夏) inner room
> **Attendees(參席人員):** 42 people
> **Absentees(不參人員):** 14 people
> **Chairperson(司會者):** Leader Kwon Jae-ha (權在夏)

**Chairperson(司會者):** Thanks to our collective efforts, we have received 1,000,000 won in special support funds from President (大統領) His Excellency. Today, we have convened this meeting to decide how best to use this grant for our village. Please share one essential project that you believe our village urgently needs.

**Kim Jae-won(金在源):** Let's use the 1,000,000 won to build our village's long-awaited community center.

**Oh Chang-seon:** What about a dairy farming business (酪農事業) to increase income (所得增大事業) instead of a community center?

**Chairperson(司會者):** We have two proposals: building a community center and starting a dairy farming business. Are there any other suggestions? Mr. Han Bong-ho next to you, please share your thoughts.

**Han Bong-ho:** I believe purchasing dairy cows for income generation (所得事業) would be better. We also have 300,000 won in our village's joint fund (共同基金). What if we combine this with the grant to buy more cows and raise them collectively (共同) for the village?

**Chairperson(司會者):** If there are no other suggestions, we will decide between the two proposals—building a community center and purchasing dairy cows—by a majority vote (多數決).

**Chairperson(司會者):** First, please raise your hand if you support building a community center. 4 people. Next, please raise your hand if you support purchasing dairy cows. 38 people. By majority decision (多數決定), we have decided to purchase dairy cows.

**Chairperson(司會者):** We will use President (大統領) His Excellency's grant along with our village's 300,000 won fund to purchase dairy cows. We will inform you of the detailed implementation plan (細部推進計劃) later.

**Chairperson(司會者):** Are there any objections from everyone?

**All Residents(住民一同):** Agreed (贊同)

**Chairperson(司會者):** With that, we conclude the selection of the President (大統領) His Excellency's special support grant project (特別支援支金事業) and adjourn this meeting.

## Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (4)

*   **Agenda (議題):** Special Support Project (特別支援事業) Financial Report (決算報告)
*   **Date (日時):** January 25, 1977, 10:00 AM
*   **Location (場所):** Inside the Village Community Center (會館)
*   **Attendees (參席人員):** 45 people (including city guidance officer Lee Woo-seop)
*   **Absentees (不參人員):** 11 people
*   **Chairperson (司會者):** Guide (指導者) Kwon Jae-ha (權在夏)

**Chairperson (司會者):** We will now hold a meeting to report on the financial results of the dairy farming project (酪農事業), which was a special support project (特別支援事業) in 1975 and 1976, and to discuss the raising of cows.

First, we will hear the financial report from the head of the village, Mr. Seo Sang-won.

**Seo Sang-won:** In 1975, we purchased 3 cows with the special support fund (特別支援金), and they gave birth to 1 calf, making the total 4 cows. In 1976, we purchased 2 more cows, and they also gave birth to calves, increasing the total number to 7 cows. In 1975, we invested 100 million won (萬圓) from the special support fund (特別支援金) and 30 million won (萬圓) from the village fund (村基金). In 1976, we invested 150 million won (萬圓) from the special support fund (特別支援金) and 50 million won (萬圓) from the village fund (村基金), totaling 330 million won (萬圓). At the current market price, this amounts to 840 million won (萬圓) (120 million won (萬圓) per cow), which has been created as communal property (共同財產) for the village.

**Chairperson (司會者):** Mr. Seo Sang-won has just spoken about the dairy farming project (酪農事業) and the cows. The number of cows has increased, but it is difficult to raise them. Let's discuss this issue (問題).

**Kim Bong-su:** It would be good to appoint a communal cow raiser (共同飼育士) to take care of the cows.

**Kim Bo-young:** Mr. Kim Bong-su suggested appointing a communal cow raiser (共同飼育士). Where should the remuneration (報酬) for this person come from?

**Kim Bong-su:** It would be appropriate to pay the communal cow raiser (共同飼育士) from the milk sales revenue (販賣代金).

**Choi Byung-o:** How much is the milk sales revenue (販賣代金) per year (年)? And how much should the communal cow raiser (共同飼育士) be paid per year (年)?

**Seo Sang-won:** The average annual milk sales revenue (販賣代金) is 90,000 won (圓). After deducting the feed (飼料) and other expenses (其他經費), about 50,000 won (圓) remains.

**Kim Han-su:** It would be good to pay the communal cow raiser (共同飼育士) around 40,000 won (圓). I believe that neighboring villages (村) also pay around that amount.

**Chairperson (司會者):** Everyone has made some good points. Now, let's vote on whether we should appoint a communal cow raiser (共同飼育士) to take care of the cows.

Please raise your hand if you agree with this proposal.

**All Residents (住民一同):** Unanimous approval (贊成)


--- (p. 286) ---

Host: The next topic is the remuneration for the livestock keepers (飼育士). As Mr. Kim Han-su mentioned, let us take the example of the neighboring dairy farming village. Please raise your hand if you think it is good to give 40,000 won per month.

All residents: Unanimously in favor (全員 贊同)

Host: Then, we will have the dairy cows raised by a common livestock keeper (共同 飼育士) and decide to give a monthly remuneration (月報酬) of 40,000 won each.

Host: With this, we will conclude the special support (特別支援) business (事業) settlement report meeting (決算報告會議). Thank you.

# 1. Village Overview

## a. History

- During the Three Kingdoms period (三國時代), the remains of Baekje's (百濟) fortress (Old Guso Fortress, 老枯城) can be found, hence the name Sansung-ri (山城里). In 1947, the administrative district was reorganized and divided into two districts (1,2구).
- The village is named Jatmi after the walnut trees that grow abundantly on the mountain slopes.

## b. Location and Conditions

The village is located about 53 km southeast of the Chungcheongbuk-do (忠北道廳) Office in Cheongju (淸州), approximately 4 km from Boeun-eup (報恩邑) towards Cheongju, across the Boeuncheon River (報恩川), at the foot of Old Guso Mountain (老枯城). It is a mid-mountain village (中山間) at an altitude of 150m.

## 2. Village Development Process
### a. Situation Before 1970
#### 1) Basic Environment
* The thatched roofs passed down from ancestors, now crumpled and overgrown with weeds, would leak rotten water onto clothes whenever it rained,
* The Secheon stream flowing through the center of the village was a mix of various waste and garbage, breeding flies, mosquitoes, and maggots that would sweep away lives with infectious diseases,
* The village path was so narrow that one could barely pass by carrying a bundle of firewood, with trees on the verge of collapse lining the way.


--- (p. 289) ---

Fences and outhouses were all demolished,
O Drinking water (食水) was from open, unclean wells, and there were no farm roads (農路), not even roads leading into the village. The people were stuck in primitive agriculture (原始農業), unable to progress,
O Living each day listlessly (無氣力).

## 2) Income Level (所得水準)
O Fathers worked as hired hands in neighboring villages, while mothers served as live-in maids for wealthy landlords in Boeun County (報恩邑). Despite swollen backs and shoulders, they carried loads of wood in long lines to sell at the Boeun Market (報恩市場). On a good day, they might sell two sacks of barley rice.
O Most farming households (農家) with small plots of land (耕地) could only dream of scientific farming (科學營農). With an average household income (戶當所得) of 250,000 won, they struggled to support families of six or seven.

## 3) Living Conditions in the 1970s (70年度의 생활狀態)
### a) Mental State (精神狀態)
O Under the influence of the old yangban (兩班) society's unique customs (因習) and lazy thinking, people had never even considered improving their lives.
O Selfish (利己的) and exclusive (排他的) habits prevailed, with no sense of cooperation (協同心) among villagers.
O Men wasted their time (虛送歲月) drinking (飮酒) and gambling (賭博), living listlessly (無氣力).
O Stuck in old habits (因習) and stubbornness (頑固), they lacked hope (希望) for the future or a pioneering spirit (開拓精神), living indifferently (無關心) and expressionlessly (無表情).

### b) Culture (文化) and Daily Life (衣食住生活)
O Without electricity (電氣), residents lived by the dim light of oil lamps (호롱불), never experiencing a decent life (生活).
O Struggling to make ends meet, they couldn't afford radios, newspapers (新聞), or magazines (雜紙), living in darkness (暗黑).
O In winter, they wore hemp cotton pants and jackets with straw shoes (짚신).
O Most villagers had to sell loads of wood in the town market (邑內場) to buy food (食糧) to survive (延命).
O Inside their homes, they used fertilizer bags (肥料 空袋) and old rags to block drafts.
O The floor (房) was covered with straw mats (草席) or woven mats (멍석), where children grew up playing in filth (汚物).
O The outhouse (便所) was indistinguishable from the manure pit (堆肥場) or ash shed (잿간), barely standing.
O Dirty water from the manure pit (堆肥場) and livestock shed (畜舍) flowed into the courtyard, attracting flies and mosquitoes. Yet, the villagers lived on, feeling neither shame nor sadness.

## b. Promoting the Saemaul Undong (運動의 推進)
### 1) Motivation (動機) and Trial Project Results (試驗事業의 성과)
O Since President (大統領) Park Chung-hee declared the Saemaul Undong (運動) on April 22, 1970, the movement has spread like a flame across the nation (全國), igniting every corner (坊坊谷谷).


--- (p. 290) ---

However, this village showed no signs of change throughout the year of 1971, remaining in a state of indifference.

With the support of the government (政府), which provided 335 bags of cement (洋灰) and 1 ton of rebar (鐵筋) as a trial project (試驗事業), the village decided to construct a 57-meter-long bridge (橋梁) over Bochongcheon (報靑川) at the village entrance (入口). They completed only the bridge piers (橋脚) that year. The following year, they received an additional 500 bags of cement (洋灰) and 1 ton of rebar (鐵筋), along with a contribution of 500,000 won (萬원) from the residents (住民) and the participation of 750 residents (住民名). In just three months (個月), they successfully completed their first project: the main bridge (本 橋梁). Through this, the residents (住民), who had never known cooperation (協同), came to personally understand the power of cooperation (協同) and gained the confidence (自信感) that "we can do it."

## 2) Election (選出) and Activities (活動狀況) of the Leader (指導者)
Kim, the leader (金指導者), graduated from Boeun Agricultural High School (報恩農高) and was working at the Gosan County Office (槐山郡廳) in his hometown (鄕地) when he received a letter (便紙) from his aging father (老患의 父親) asking him to return to his hometown (故鄕). After resigning from his public service (公職生活) and returning home (歸鄕), he found that his family's situation (家庭環境) and the living conditions (生活狀態) of his neighbors had not changed at all from what his ancestors (祖上) had left behind. Determined to improve his hometown (故鄕), where his ancestors' bones were buried and where he himself would one day be buried, he struggled to find the courage (勇氣) to take action. During this time, he was asked by the local (管內) village head (面長) and neighborhood chief (里長) to serve as a leader (指導者) for the village. Taking this as an opportunity, Kim, the leader (金指導者), resolved to become a voluntary leader (自願的指導者職) with the firm determination (決心) to create a prosperous village.

## 3. Overcoming Difficulties (隘路 克服 狀況)
Inspired by the successful completion of the bridge construction (橋梁工事) as a trial project (試驗事業) in the first year (初年度), the village decided to establish a road leading to the national highway (國道) at the entrance (進入路). On December 6, 1973 (年月), a general meeting of residents (住民總會) was convened. When the issues of donating land (土地 喜捨) for the entrance road (進入路) and village roads (村里路), demolishing targeted houses (撤去對象 家屋), and removing walls (除去 墻) were announced, the meeting hall (會議場) instantly turned into chaos (修羅場).

Despite holding several more general meetings of residents (住民總會), the targeted individuals (對象者) consistently refused to participate (不參), and resistance (反發) grew. Desperate, Kim, the leader (金指導者), organized a youth and adult agricultural improvement club (靑壯年 農事 改良 俱樂部) with 24 members (名) from the 4-H club (俱樂部) he had organized in high school (高等學校) as the core (主軸), and resolved to take the lead in village development (村里 開發). He visited the targeted individuals (對象者) house by house (戶別 訪問) and made every effort to persuade (說得) them, eventually succeeding in obtaining the landowners' (地主) consent (承諾).

However, the issue of incorporating 80 pyeong (坪) of land (土地) for the entrance road (進入路) remained unresolved. Kim, the leader (金指導者), ultimately resolved the issue by exchanging his own fertile field (沃畓) of 100 pyeong (坪) through a written agreement (證書). Kim, the leader's (金指導者) persistent efforts (努力) and determination (執念) led to the widening of the narrow entrance road (進入路) and village roads (村里路) that had been passed down through generations (祖上代代).

With the newfound confidence (確信) that "we can do it" through collective effort (合力), Kim, the leader (金指導者), decided to persuade (說得) some of the reckless (沒知覺) youth and adults (靑壯年) who were wasting their days (日) on alcohol (酒) and gambling (賭博) to join the ranks (隊列) of the New Community Movement (新村運動). One night, after witnessing a farmer (農夫) lose all seven sacks (가마) of rice (米) he had earned as a farmhand (머슴살이) at a gambling den (賭博場) and subsequently engage in a marital dispute (夫婦 爭執), Kim, the leader (金指導者), and six members (名) of the village's agricultural improvement club (村里 農事 改良 俱樂部) visited the gambling den (賭博場) to plead (哀願) with them to return the money (錢) they had won. However, the individuals in question (對象者) retaliated (反發), shouting, "What business is it of yours?" (什麼 相關) and attacking them (襲擊), resulting in one of them (其中一人) falling and breaking an arm (一邊 팔).


--- (p. 291) ---

Kim, the leader (金指導者), once had his bones broken and was called to the police station (警察支署). However, after receiving warm admonition from the station chief (支署長), he returned and thought that the village's taverns should be eliminated first. With the cooperation of the women's association (婦女會), he successfully persuaded the tavern owners to close voluntarily.

There was also a time when, despite the saying that "heaven helps those who help themselves," the long-cherished goal of bridge construction (橋梁架設) was thwarted by untimely spring rains, causing the formwork and 50 bags of cement (洋灰) to float away, leaving the villagers disheartened.

Moreover, the small river (小河川) flowing through the center of the village was teeming with various filth, garbage, mosquitoes, flies, and maggots, yet the villagers merely watched. To awaken them, Kim, the leader (金指導者), visited the principal of Haegeum Elementary School (鶴林國民學校) and requested the organization of a hometown association (鄕友班) to conduct morning cleanups, which was successful.

One day, while the leader was waking up early to ring a bell and walking through the alleys to awaken the students for cleanup, a parent expressed concern, saying, "If you are going to bring the New Village movement to our town, you alone should be affected. Why do you make our children clean and disrupt their studies?"

Despite these difficulties, Kim, the leader (金指導者), decided to focus on increasing income through the cooperation of the villagers, the agricultural improvement club (農事改良俱樂部), and the women's association (婦女會). He arranged for the supply of high-quality vegetables (高等蔬菜) from various accommodations (接客業所) in Seokrisan (俗離山) in Daejeon (大田), which were usually supplied at high prices from outside, to be provided from their own village.

He leased 1,200 pyeong (坪) of personal farmland (土地)(田) and was cultivating high-yield crops such as green onions, cucumbers, tomatoes, and peppers with care when an unexpected strong wind (强風) destroyed the vinyl greenhouse, causing all the crops to suffer from frostbite (冷害), leaving the entire village disheartened once again.

Overcoming such difficulties, Kim, the leader (金指導者), visited house after house, urging and persuading the villagers to participate fully in village development (開發), saying, "This village is where our ancestors' bones are buried, where we should be buried, and where our descendants should live. It is our home."

This was the persistent determination of one leader that gradually became known to connect the impossible with the possible. It was also a moment when the longing of the local residents, who had only looked enviously at the prospering neighboring villages, began to unravel one knot at a time, opening a new chapter in history.

## 4) Developmental Promotion of the New Village Movement (事業)

- The villagers, through the New Village spirit (精神) of diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperation (協同), gained the courage (勇氣) to overcome trials (試錬) and hardships (苦難), the belief (信念) to break through stagnation (沈滯) and poverty, and the strength to envision a bright tomorrow with hope (希望) on the vigorous path (途程) of progress (躍進). They steadily promoted the following projects (事業).
- Relying on the successful construction (架設) of the 57m Bochungcheon (報靑川) bridge (橋梁),
- In 1973, they opened 1,200m of village access roads (進入路), 1,600m of farm roads (農路), and 1,500m of village inner roads (村內路), promoting the mechanization (機械化) of farming (營農) as well as the convenience of transportation (交通).


--- (p. 292) ---

Around the same time, a 500m small river (小河川) was renovated (改修) to prevent annual (每年) floods (洪水) from causing loss of farmland (農耕地), and residents (住民) who had not experienced the benefits (惠澤) of culture (文化) under the lamplight welcomed the early implementation of the rural electrification project (農漁村電化事業), spending the night (夜) joyfully as the entire village (動民) made a vow (道藥) for mental leap (道藥), not knowing what to do with themselves.

As communal facilities (共同利用施設) such as village halls (村會舘), children's playgrounds (兒童 놀이터), daycare centers (탁아소), and nutrition improvement houses (營養改善의 집) were established, the village's appearance (村面貌) was transformed.

Through environmental improvement projects (環境改善事業), wall improvement (擔墻改良) projects, roof improvements (屋改良), painting (塗色), plastering (灰壁), and slum improvement (不良住宅改良) were promoted.

Through residential area projects (住居圈事業), kitchens, toilets (便所), Jangdokdae (장독대), and composting sites (堆肥場) were renovated (整備), completely renewing the environment (環境).

As production infrastructure (生產基盤施設) such as communal warehouses (共同倉庫), communal workspaces (共同作業場), and communal barns (共同畜舍) were established, village communal income (村共同所得) increased.

Moreover, 1,500 persimmon trees (本) were planted (植裁) in village-owned (村所有) forests (林野), and 1,200 improved poplar trees (本) were planted (植裁) in idle vacant lots (遊休空閑地) to increase income (所得), while 92 greenhouses (棟) were installed (設置) to develop the village into a model village (示範村) that increases income (所得) through high-quality horticulture (高等園藝).

## 5) Land (土地) and Cash Donation Situation (現金寄捨狀況)

Villagers (洞民) who had stubbornly refused to include land (編入土地) and demolish attached buildings (附屬建物撤去) due to mutual antagonism (反目) and jealousy (疾視) now received comfort (慰勞) and warmth (溫情) from various sectors (各界) for the villagers (住民) who worked hard sweating and bleeding in this village with the Saemaul spirit (精神).

Residents (住民) also provided strenuous efforts (努力) for the Saemaul project (事業), generously offering their fertile land in front of their gates (門前沃沓) and cash (現金).

Moreover, the women's association (婦女會) provided meals (食事) to husbands (男便) working hard with rice (節米) saved through thrift (勤儉節約), and at the year-end (年末) Saemaul settlement (決算), all villagers (洞民) gathered in one place to hold a lavish banquet (宴席), settle the year's accounts (決算), and discuss the next project (事業).

## 6) Heartwarming Stories (美談佳話)

### a) First Story (第1話)

As the Saemaul Undong (事業) gained momentum and incomes improved, the village leader (指導者) and Agricultural Cooperation Chairman (農改會長) Choi Gi-hwan (崔奇煥) aimed to help the underprivileged neighbors.

*   They gathered opinions (意見) to assist Im Heon-suk (林憲淑), a beneficiary (對象者) of the village's livelihood protection (生活保護), who was begging (求乞).
*   They launched a campaign (運動) to build (建) a main house (干先) and 24 members (農改會員) of the Agricultural Cooperation (農改會) participated (參與), contributing 100,000 won (萬원) from their membership fund (會員基金) and receiving support (賛助) from local (部落) leaders (有志). They provided a cozy 15 pyeong (坪) home.
*   This act has been praised (稱讚) within the jurisdiction (管內) as a prime example (標本) of the village's warm-hearted (溫厚) humanity (人情).

### b) Second Story (第2話)

*   Inspired by the Saemaul Undong (運動), Im Woo-soo (林羽洙), a native (出身) of this village, donated (喜捨) 20 pyeong (坪) of paddy field (編入穀地) for road access (進入路).
*   To refine (醇化) the village's sentiments (情緖觀念) and help residents (住民) acquire (習得) various (各種) farming techniques (營農技術), he
*   On April 12, 1976 (年月日), delivered (直接傳達) 740 books (卷) including comics (만화) for children, educational (敎養) reading material (册字) for youth (靑少年), and various (各種) farming technique manuals (營農技術敎本). He also comforted (慰勞) and encouraged (激勵) the residents (住民).
*   On August 10, 1977 (年月日), the Seoul-based (在京) hometown association (報鄕會) organized (組織) a medical service (醫療奉仕) team (活動班) and provided (奉仕) medical care (醫療) to 360 patients (患者) within the jurisdiction (管內). They also received (受) a letter of appreciation (感謝狀) from the local county magistrate (管內郡守).

### 8) Special Notes (特記事項)

**a) Joyful Events**

*   On December 8, 1976, when we heard the news that President Park Chung-hee (朴大統領) had awarded us the Cooperation Medal (協同章) and granted us a special subsidy of 5 million won (500萬支援金)
*   When we watched the live broadcast from our village during the Monthly Economic Trends Report Meeting (月間經濟動向報告會) on December 8, 1976
*   When Park Jin-hwan and Kim Jong-ho, secretaries of the Blue House (靑瓦臺秘書官), and Kim Jun, the director (院長), and Gwak Jeong-hyeon, the deputy director (副院長), of the Saemaul Central Training Institute (中央硏修院) visited our village directly (直接) on November 23, 1976, and donated a radio (1台) and offered comfort and encouragement
*   During the Saemaul Undong (運動) Promotion General Mobilization Conference (促進總蹶起大會) in 1976, when National Assembly Member Yuk In-soo (陸寅修), who is from this area, gave us a precious pen and offered comfort and encouragement
*   During the Sports Festival (體育大會) held to commemorate the 7th anniversary (第7週年) of the Saemaul Undong (運動) on April 22, 1977, when we achieved the glory of ranking first (一位) among the 27 villages (27個村) in the county for both Saemaul achievements (實積) and sports scores (體育點數), and received a special subsidy of 500,000 won (50萬支援金) from Governor Jeong (鄭知事)
*   When Governor Jeong Jong-sak (鄭宗澤) met with the village leaders (指導者) during his New Year's inspection (年頭巡視) of Boeun County (報恩郡) in 1976 and offered comfort and encouragement
*   The joy of completing the Bochungcheon (報靑川) Bridge (橋梁), which our ancestors (祖上) had only ever seen, and holding the completion ceremony (竣工式) was shared by all the villagers (住民)

**b) Sad Events**

*   When the formwork and cement stored at the construction site (作業場) for the bridge construction (橋梁架設) were all washed away by the spring rains (春雨)
*   When the greenhouse (비닐하우스) for increasing income (所得增大) was destroyed by strong winds (强風), and the crops (作物) that we had carefully tended (精誠) suffered from winter damage (冬害) and died
*   When the young and middle-aged men (靑壯年) who had been gambling (賭博) were falsely accused (樓名) and the village leaders (指導者) were taken away by the police (警察) while trying to persuade them (說得)

## Ba. Achievements through Saemaul Undong (事業)

1) Spiritual Aspect (精神面)
- We have gained the courage (勇氣) to overcome trials (試鍊) and hardships (苦難) through the diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperation (協同) of the Saemaul Undong (運動).
- We have acquired the belief (信念) to overcome stagnation (沈滯) and poverty (貧困).
- Our community has transformed (改善) from one filled with human emotions (人情) and individualistic (利己的) society (社會) into a shared (共同) public square (廣場).

2) Living Aspect (生活面)
- Our village has renewed (一新) itself from its previously backward (落後) state.
- Our village has neatly organized (整備) its production infrastructure (生產基盤施設) and cultural welfare environment (文化福祉環境), allowing us to look forward to a hopeful (希望) tomorrow (來日).
- Our residents (住民) are cultivating ( 다져나가고) a lifestyle ethic (生活倫理) based on self-help spirit (自助精神).
- Our village residents (住民) have become thrifty (勤儉節約) farmers (農民) who practice (實踐) and think (思考).

3) Production Aspect (生產面)
- We have achieved a dramatic (劃期的) increase (增大) in income (所得) through advanced horticulture cultivation (高等園藝栽培) and expanded cultivation (擴大栽培) of unified rice varieties (統一系統 稻).

4) Income Aspect (所得面)
- Income (所得) before 1970 was only 270,000 won (千원), but by the end of 1977, it had increased to 2,023,000 won (千원) per household (戶當), more than seven times (7倍) the previous amount.

### 3. Residents' General Assembly (住民總會)

#### ◆ Meeting Minutes (會議錄)(1)

**Date (日時)**: January 6, 1971
**Location (場所)**: Im Hak-cheol's (林學喆) living room
**Agenda (議題)**: Bridge construction (橋梁架設)
**Attendees (參席人員)**: Choi Gi-hwan (崔寄煥) and 62 others; 4 absent (不參)
**Chairperson (司會者)**: Kim Wol-yeon (金月鍊) instructor (指導者)

**Chairperson (司會者)**: Thank you all for attending this meeting despite the cold winter weather. The main purpose of tonight's village meeting is to address the fact that our villagers (洞民) cultivate most of our fields in Hakseom yard, yet we lack a bridge over Bochongcheon (報靑川) in front of the village, which leaves us helpless during floods. The government has provided 335 bags of cement for the New Community Movement (事業用), so we have called this meeting to discuss what project we should undertake.

**Im Jun-cheol (林駿喆)**: May I say something? With the 335 bags of cement provided by the government, do you think we can build such a large bridge (橋梁) with our own strength?

**Instructor (指導者)**: Well said. First, let's hear from everyone whether building this bridge is a good idea or not.

**Im Dong-soo (林東洙)**: I am wholeheartedly in favor of building this bridge (橋梁). However, our village lacks both the technical expertise and the funds to construct such a bridge (橋梁).

**Instructor (指導者)**: It seems that both of you agree that building the bridge (橋梁) is a good idea, but it will be challenging as it is our first such project.

**Im Heon-man (林憲萬)**: May I add something? Fellow villagers, we must seize this opportunity to build this bridge (橋梁).

**Instructor (指導者)**: Let's take a vote. Please raise your hands if you agree with building the bridge (橋梁). 49 in favor. 14 against.

**Im Hak-cheol (林學喆)**: Since the entire village (洞民) has decided to build the bridge, please explain the business plan (事業計劃) to us, instructor (指導者).

**Instructor (指導者)**: Very well. The total project cost (總事業費) will be 1,300 bags of cement, 5 tons of rebar, and approximately 1 million won (萬) for other materials (其他資材代) and specialized labor (特殊技術人夫賃).


--- (p. 299) ---

**Im Hak-cheol (林學喆)**: How do you plan to secure the project funds (事業費) you mentioned earlier? Please elaborate.
**Leader (指導者)**: We plan to construct the bridge (本橋梁案) over a two-year (2個年) period. This year, we will set up the bridge piers (橋脚) and complete the superstructure (上部工事) next year. With this year's government support (政府支援) of 335 bags of cement (洋灰) and the village fund (洞里基金), we will purchase 500 bags of cement to install the bridge piers.
**Im Hak-cheol (林學喆)**: Now that we have decided to construct the bridge (架設), let's all villagers (部落民) work together to complete the project (本事業) before the rainy season (장마철).
**Leader (指導者)**: I kindly ask the development committee members (開發委員) and each team leader (各班長) to actively cooperate (積極協助) in the bridge construction (本橋梁架設).
**Im Dong-soo (林東洙)**: You mentioned constructing the bridge (本橋梁) over a two-year (2個年) period, but what if the government (政府) does not support (支援) us next year (來年) after we only set up the bridge piers (다리발) this year (今年)?
**Leader (指導者)**: If we work hard with sweat and tears, we will plead (哀願) our village's situation (사정) to the county (面 or 郡) and definitely secure the support (支援).
**Im Dong-soo (林東洙)**: But what if the county (郡) says they don't have money and refuses to support (支援) us at that time?
**Leader (指導者)**: The President (大統領) said that villages that unite and strive (努力) to live well will be prioritized (優先) for support (支援) over others. So, let's all work hard. With that, I will conclude today's meeting (會議).
According to the resolution (決議) of the village assembly (住民總會), please sign and stamp (署名捺印) this document. Im Cheol-soo, Im Hak-cheol, Im Jun-soo, Choi Ki-hwan, Song Seok-ju, Jang Jae-hyuk, Im Heon-sang, Lee Jae-ha, Lee Jong-rak, Kim Wol-ryeon, Choi Hak-bong, Im Heon-sang, Im Jun-cheol, Kim Gi-jong, Im Dong-soo.

## ♦Minutes (會議錄) (2)
Date: January 3, 1972
Venue: Im Gwang-cheol's (林光喆) living room
Agenda: Village road widening
Attendance: 61 present, 6 absent
Chairperson: Village head Im Gwang-cheol (林光喆)

**Chairperson (司會者)**: Thank you all for attending despite the cold winter weather. Our village has long wished to straighten and widen our winding access road (進入路) so that we and our descendants (後孫) can live well. We kindly ask all villagers (洞民) to help resolve (解決) this issue.
**Song Seok-ju (宋錫柱)**: Does the leader (指導者) really know and understand our village well enough to make such claims? Doesn't he know that the town mayor (面長) even came here but couldn't resolve the land issue and had to cancel it?
**Lee Jong-rak (李鍾洛)**: Hey, you young leader (指導者), you don't know how the world works. I've been carrying loads (등짐) and plowing fields (흙쟁기) while raising children at my age nearing 60. Why are you trying to ruin our village? I will never give up my land. Go ahead and do as you please.
**Leader (指導者)**: I have nothing to say. I have no intention of making life difficult for the respected elders of various villages, not even a bit (秋毫). If you all blame (怨望) me like this, I will say my final words.


--- (p. 300) ---

We have 700 pyeong (坪) of land here, and I will divide it all among you, but we must definitely pave the inner roads.

**Im Hak-chul (林學喆)**: Listening to you, the leader's (指導者) words seem quite fair. Didn't you see in the neighboring village last year how the young people demolished walls and houses to widen the inner roads? I also have land, but the criticism (攻駁) is too severe.

**Im Hun-sang (林憲想)**: Then, please share the plans for the access road (進入路) and inner road expansion (擴張) with us, leader (指導者) and village head (里長).

**Leader (指導者)**: It's not that I want to widen the inner roads just for myself. Please bear and understand everything.
*   The business (事業) plan (計劃) will involve incorporating less land and if a few people just bear and understand, it will be an easy task.
*   The access road (進入路) will be widened equally on both sides,
*   The inner village road will be widened straight from Im Sam-jun's (林三俊) house to Mr. Song Seok-ju's (宋錫柱) house, and the back road will pass by Mr. Im Jun-cheol's house, damaging and demolishing walls, sheds, jars, and persimmon trees, but if we widen both sides, many houses will be demolished, so please bear and understand. What do you all think?

**Song Seok-ju (宋錫柱)**: You're really bad, why do you have to demolish my house entirely? If you widen both sides equally, my house won't suffer much damage, but you really have some grudge against me, don't you?

**Im Hak-chul (林學喆)**: My annex is also half demolished, but shouldn't we do things in a way that causes less harm to more people? Why are you insulting the leader (指導者) and criticizing (攻駁) him by calling him bad?

**Song Seok-ju (宋錫柱)**: You can say that because you're rich (富者) after raising your children, but I absolutely won't accept it. If you want to, go ahead.

**Leader (指導者)**: Then, please raise your hands to decide whether to start this business (事業) or not. 48 people (名) are in favor (贊成), and 13 people (名) are against (反對). Let's start with the alleys of those who supported (贊成) in our Aehyangdan (愛鄕團).

**Im Hak-chul (林學喆)**: Let's adjourn (閉會) the meeting for tonight and start (始作) tomorrow. Later, let's all go to the houses of those who opposed (反對) and plead with them.

**Leader (指導者)**: Then, let's adjourn (閉會) the meeting.

Choi Hak-bong, Im Hun-man, Im Cheol-soo, Jang Jae-hyuk, Im Ik-soo, Kang Chung-geun, Lee Jong-nak, Im Dong-soo, Im Hak-soo, Kim Gi-jong, Im Hak-chul, Choi Gi-hwan, Song Seok-ju, Im Jun-cheol, Im Hun-sang, Song Gwang-young, Lee Jae-ha, Im Jae-man

### ♦ Minutes (會議錄) (3)

| Item         | Content                                 |
| :----------- | :----------------------------------- |
| Date (日時)     | 73. 1.7                              |
| Venue (場所)     | Im Hak-chul's (林學喆) living room (氏)           |
| Agenda (議題)     | Village seedling business (養苗事業)             |
| Attendance (參席)     | Attendance (參席) 48 people (名), Absence (不參) 19 people (名) |
| Chairperson (社會者) | Village head (里長)                             |


--- (p. 301) ---

# Village Head (里長) : We have convened today's evening meeting to discuss implementing a special project, Village Nursery (마을養苗), in our village to create a village fund (마을基金).
# Leader (指導者) : First, I would like to share a story about a village that succeeded in Village Nursery (마을養苗) during my Saemaul Education (새마을敎育). Through the efforts of the villagers, they were able to earn hundreds of thousands of won a year by growing poplar, side oak, persimmon, larch, and walnut trees. Let's try to increase our village income (마을所得) as well. There is a village that conducted an experimental project (試驗事業) this year by growing persimmon trees in their village nursery (마을養苗) and planting them on the back mountain (後山) of the village to generate profits (收益). Since we also have a hill (洞山) in our village, let's grow 3,000 persimmon trees and plant them on our hill, and sell the rest to make a profit (利益).
# Im Hak-cheol (林學喆) : That's a great idea. It's a very good thing to decide to plant them on the back mountain (後山) of our neighborhood.
# Leader (指導者) : Then, I would like to ask for the consensus (贊成與否) of the villagers (洞民). Everyone agrees (全員 贊). Then, I will explain the business plan (事業計劃). We will lease Im Hak-cheol's (林學喆) field to create a persimmon nursery (苗圃밭). The seed cost (種子代) required for this is 80,000 won (八萬圓), the grafting technology labor cost is 150,000 won (一五萬圓), the rental fee (賃貸料) is 50,000 won (五萬圓), and 50,000 won (五萬圓) is needed for sacks and pesticides (等). If we invest 100,000 won (一○萬圓) from the village women's association fund (婦女會 基金), how about that?
# Im Jun-cheol (林駿喆) : From what I heard from the leader (指導者), you only talked about the materials (資材) needed for the nursery (養苗), but how are we going to weed and take care of them?
# Leader (指導者) : The general laborers (普通 人夫) needed for weeding and taking care of them will be taken care of by the 4-H club president (會長) and the agricultural improvement club president (農事改良 俱樂部會長) of our village.
# Im Jun-cheol (林駿喆) : My child is also a 4-H member (會員), but he doesn't study (工夫) and when he comes back from school (學校), he says he has 4-H assignments (課題) and doesn't study (工夫), so I will not send my child.
# Leader (指導者) : You have made a good point. Our village children have received awards (賞金) from the guidance center (指導所) and the county office (郡廳) for being role models (模範) in 4-H compared to children from other villages (洞里). 4-H members (會員) studying (履修) assignments (課題) does not mean they cannot study (工夫). Please understand (理解) this.
# Im Hak-cheol (林學喆) : Then, let's have the villagers (洞里), 4-H, agricultural improvement members (農改會員), women's association (婦女會), and patriotic group (愛鄕團) work hard and work together to make an excellent village nursery (마을養苗).
# Leader (指導者) : Please state your agreement or disagreement (贊反) regarding what has been said.
# Choi Hak-bong : 4-H president (會長), agricultural improvement president (農改會長), and women's association president (婦女會長), please say something about this matter.
# Women's Association President (婦女會長) : We will be responsible for weeding the nursery (苗圃밭), so please do not worry.
# Leader (指導者) : Then, since the women's association president (婦女會長) will take the lead (率先) in being responsible for the village nursery (마을養苗) and weeding, how good is that. Let's all work hard based on the work plan (作業計劃書) to increase our income (所得). With that, I will conclude today's evening meeting. Thank you (感謝).

<Attendee Signatures (參席者 署名捺印)>
Im Cheol-soo, Im Ik-soo, Im Hak-cheol, Im Young-soo, Im Heon-man, Im Geum-soo, Im Yoon-cheol, Song Seok-ju, Im Heon-chang, Lee Jae-ha, Song Kwang-young Im Jae-man, Kang Chung-geun, Hwang Soo-chang, Kim Wol-yeon

## Minutes (會議錄) (4)

Date(日時): February 3, 1974
Location(場所): Im Cheolsu's (林喆洙) living room
Agenda(議題): Construction of Community Center and Warehouse
Attendance(人員): Attended (參席) 61 people, Absent (不參) 6 people
Chairperson(社會者): Leader Kim Moonryeon (金月鍊)

**Leader(指導者)**: Thank you all for coming out in this cold weather. I have called this meeting to discuss the construction of our community center and warehouse. Our village has been allocated 600 bags of cement and 1 ton of rebar. We have repeatedly requested the local cooperative office to approve the construction of a community center and warehouse. Now, let's discuss how many square pyong (坪) we should build and where.

**Im Dongsu(林東洙)**: It's wonderful that we can finally build our long-awaited community center. However, can we really build it with the cement and rebar provided by the government? Leader, could you please explain?

**Leader(指導者)**: We plan to build a 15-pyong community center and a 35-pyong warehouse, totaling 50 pyong, in the village square. However, while we have enough cement, we lack wood and other materials. I've estimated that we need special skills for carpentry and additional wood and materials. We plan to use the willow and pine trees from our village stream with permission, and we will seek donations from prominent villagers for the rest.

**Im Hakcheol(林學喆)**: I understand the leader's explanation. The annex and brick making will be handled by the village patriotic group, and stacking will be done by Im Jaehwan (林在煥) and Im Jaeman (林在萬) of our village, as they have the necessary skills.

**Im Jaehwan(林在煥)**: I have to take care of my elderly parents and cannot sacrifice too much for the Saemaul Undong. Please consider someone else.

**Leader(指導者)**: What else is there to leave behind besides one's name after death? If you work for our village, the villagers will not forget your efforts. Please consider it.

**Im Jaeman(林在萬)**: I also cannot do it, so please understand.

**Village Head(里長)**: Please help our village. Many villagers are present here, but if someone without skills tries to build it and it collapses, what will we do? Our village must work together to minimize cash burdens.

**Leader(指導者)**: Villagers, if both of you sacrifice too much for the village, it will be difficult. How about we take responsibility for summer planting instead? (Applause unanimous.)

**Im Jaehwan(林在煥)**: Thank you. If everyone insists I am necessary, I will try my best.

**Im Youngcheol(林榮喆)**: For the remaining funds, I will visit each household tomorrow to seek donations, so I kindly ask for your cooperation.

**Leader(指導者)**: It's getting late, so I will conclude the meeting. Thank you.

Im Youngcheol, Choi Ki-hwan, Lee Jae-ha, Kim Kijong, Song Seokju, Im Jaeman, Im Jaehwan, Im Juncheol, Im Yuncheol, Im Gwangcheol, Im Heonsang, Choi Hakbong, Im Hakcheol, Song Gwangyeong


--- (p. 303) ---

## Minutes (會議錄) (5)

| Category | Content |
|---|---|
| Date | April 20, 1974 |
| Venue | Im Cheol-su's (林喆洙) living room |
| Agenda | Proposal for the construction of a communal livestock barn (共同畜舍) |
| Participants | Attended: 46, Absent: 21 |
| Chairperson | Village head (里長) |

**Chairperson (社會者):** I have called this meeting to discuss the construction of a communal livestock barn (共同畜舍) using the special grant of 1,260,000 won bestowed by His Excellency the President (大統領).

**Leader (指導者):** For our village to increase its income by raising fattening cattle (肥育牛) using natural pastures (自然草地), high-quality vegetables (高等蔬菜), and byproducts (副産物), it is best to construct a modern livestock barn (現代式畜舍).

**Im Dong-su (林東洙):** That's a great idea. But what's the use of building a barn without the funds to buy cattle? Why don't we use the grant money to buy cattle and lease them to small farmers (零細農) for breeding (飼育), sharing the profits in a 4:6 ratio?

**Leader (指導者):** Well said. You know how the neighboring village of Sinam-ri (新含里) became wealthy by raising fattening cattle (肥育牛). It would be good to build an improved barn (改良畜舍), hire workers (人夫) to manage it, and raise cattle there.

**Im Hak-cheol (林學喆):** I think we should cultivate sweet potatoes, pumpkins, and hay (乾草) on the idle land (遊休地) behind our village, manage and harvest them together through the 4-H or farm improvement (農改) club, and use them for raising cattle.

**Leader (指導者):** All those in favor of building the barn, please raise your hands. (Unanimously approved.)

**Lee Jong-rak (李鍾洛):** Please explain the business plan to us, Village head (里長) and Leader (指導者).

**Leader (指導者):** The communal livestock barn (共同畜舍) will be constructed on an idle lot (空閑地) of 45 pyeong (坪) inside the riverbank (河川邊) of our village. The total cost (總經費) will be 2,000,000 won. I believe we can complete it before the busy farming season (農繁期) if we all work together. I ask for your active cooperation. This concludes today's evening meeting.

<Development committee members (開發委員) and team leaders (班長) sign as representatives>
Im Gwang-cheol (任光哲), Im Hak-su (任學洙), Song Seok-ju (宋錫周), Im Jeong-su (任正洙), Kang Chun-geun (姜春根), Im Hyun-sang (任賢相), Kim Gi-jong (金基鍾), Yoon In-gwan (尹仁寬), Im Heon-man (任憲萬), Hwang Su-chang (黃壽昌), Im Geum-su (任金壽)

## Minutes (會議錄) (6)

| Category | Content |
|---|---|
| Date | December 16, 1976 |
| Venue | Village community center (會館) |
| Agenda | Selection of projects and use of the President's (大統領) grant (下賜金) |
| Participants | Attended: 58, Absent: 8 |
| Attendees | Myeonjang (面長) Im Sam-jun (林三俊), Chief of General Affairs (總務係長) Kim Jong-gil (金鍾吉)


--- (p. 304) ---

# Village Meeting on Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) Project

**Village Head (里長)**: It is a great honor for our village that our leader, Kim Moon-ryeon (金月鍊), received a medal (協同章) from President Park (大統領) during the December 8th monthly economic trend report. On this occasion, I have received a special grant of 500 million (萬) won from His Excellency.

**Township Head (面長)**: I would like to say a few words to all of you. Our village is a model village that strives to live well. As the village head mentioned, the honor of receiving a grant of 500 million (萬) won and our leader receiving a medal is all thanks to your efforts. I suggest we use this grant for a business that can increase our income.

**Choi Gi-hwan (崔寄煥)**: Everyone knows that our village increases income through vinyl greenhouses. However, we face inconveniences each year due to the use of bamboo and acacia. This time, we will install a communal seedling farm to improve our income through communal seedling cultivation.

**Choi Hak-bong**: Regarding the communal seedling farm and the purchase of iron materials (鐵材), it would be best to go to Daejeon (大田) and buy the items directly (直接).

**Leader (指導者)**: You mentioned that the business we urgently need is the communal seedling farm. Let's ask for your agreement. Those in favor, please raise your hands. Unanimous agreement (滿場一致). Then, please explain the procedure for purchasing the land and iron materials needed for the seedling farm.

**Choi Gi-hwan (崔寄煥)**: First, let's select a sunny field near the village for the seedling farm land, and let's go to Daejeon (大田) to purchase the iron materials.

**Leader (指導者)**: It seems best to purchase the land for the seedling farm in front of the village, which is owned by Im Hak-cheol (林學喆).

**Im Hak-cheol (林學喆)**: That's a good idea. As you all know, I am in poor health and unable to farm directly, so I am trying to sell my land. Please buy my 1,290 pyeong (坪) field.

**Leader (指導者)**: Thank you very much. Then, what do you all think? (Everyone welcomes with loud applause.) Then, please state the price per pyeong (坪當).

**Im Hak-cheol (林學喆)**: There was a recent case of Im Dong-soo (林東洙) selling his field (田), so it's obvious.

**Village Head (里長)**: Then, since it's better than Im Hyung's (林兄) field as it is a home garden, I will give you 3,500 won.

**Im Hak-cheol (林學喆)**: If the villagers (洞民) wish, I will do so.

**Leader (指導者)**: Please state the real estate (不動産) description (表示).

## 4. Future Development Plan (發展構想)

Through the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動), we have gained the confidence that "we can do it," learned the value of sweat, and strived to create a developing, advancing, and prosperous village. For these purposes, all residents of Jatmi Village will join forces and move towards the 1980s (80年代) to achieve:

1. A village with improved housing (住宅) and settlements (聚落)
2. A village where farming (營農) is mechanized (機械化) and scientified (科學化)
3. A village where income (所得) is 3 million won (萬원) or more (以上)
4. In 1978 (78年度), we will purchase 20 head (頭) of fattening cattle (肥育牛) and 5 head (頭) of dairy cows
5. We will purchase a small (小型) truck (貨物車) to directly (直接) ship (出荷) various agricultural products (各種農產物) to Seoraksan (俗離山), Cheongju (淸州), and Seoul

Thus, our village will practice thrift (勤儉) and frugality (節約) as a way of life (生活化), elevate the Saemaul spirit (새마을精神) as our village's faith, and steadily (着實) realize (實現) our ideals (理想) for the 1980s (80年代).


--- (p. 306) ---

# 1. Village Overview

## a. History

* During the Joseon Dynasty, this area belonged to what is now Yongdong County, Boeun County, and Sangju County, and was incorporated into Buk-myeon, Okcheon County in 1914. It was integrated into Cheongsan-myeon in 1947 and became Sangnyegok-ri, Cheongsan-myeon in 1951.
* This village was established when Uam Song Si-yeol, a former Prime Minister, and Kim Gwang-ro, a descendant of the Gwangju Kim clan, settled here due to the Hu Gyeon Rebellion during the reign of King Sukjong. The village still preserves several cultural assets, including Song Si-yeol's personal writings, which are considered village treasures.

## b. Location and Conditions

* Located in the far eastern part of Okcheon County, this mountain village is surrounded by natural barriers. It is 8 km east to Sangju County in Gyeongbuk, 5 km west to the Cheongsan-myeon office, 10 km south to Yongsan-myeon in Yongdong County, and 4 km north to Maro-myeon in Boeun County.
* As a remote mountain village consisting of three natural hamlets, it has the Yeokcheon Stream flowing in front and the rugged Yesan Mountain behind, resulting in relatively less arable land compared to other villages.

## 2. Village Development Process (發展過程)

### A. Situation Before 1970 (70年 以前의 情況)

#### 1) Basic Environment (基礎環境)

- The Yeokgokcheon (禮谷川) flowing through the center of O Village had its embankment (堤防) completed in 1963, but it was left abandoned, allowing weeds to grow densely around the Yeokgokcheon (禮谷川). The approximately 50 thatched houses (草家) divided by the Yeokgokcheon (禮谷川) as a boundary (境界) were in such a state that it was difficult to even distinguish between houses (家屋) and barns (畜舍).
- The only access road (進入路) to the village was a gravel path that could barely accommodate a bicycle, and the ditches (도랑) between the thatched houses (草家) were filled with weeds (雜草) emitting a foul odor (惡臭) year-round. This made O Village the dirtiest in terms of cleanliness (淸掃狀態) within the region (面內).

#### 2) Income Level (所得水準)

- At that time, the area of rice paddies (논) was less than 20 hectares, with a per-household (戶當) cultivated area (耕地面積) of about 0.5 hectares.
- Due to a lack of farming skills (營農技術), there were rarely any years with a proper harvest (收穫).
- The area for cultivating tobacco (煙草栽培), now the main source of income (主所得源), was only about 1 hectare.
- While some households made and sold dried persimmons (곶감), it was difficult to sell them at a fair price (제값).


--- (p. 308) ---

The average household income in this area was barely exceeding 210,000 won, making it the poorest and most marginal village within the jurisdiction.

### 3) Living Conditions

#### a) Mental State

* This village was composed of a clan, with 51 out of 59 households belonging to the Gwang-san Kim clan, accounting for 90% of the population. The elders in this village were stubborn, adhering strictly to traditional customs without any knowledge of reform. They took great pride in being descendants of the yangban class, considering work beneath them and accepting their ancestral poverty as fate. This led to a stagnant mindset and a lethargic, unmotivated way of life.
* Additionally, there was a mining village 8 km away, and the rough nature of the miners seeped into this village. Men would seize any opportunity to drink and gamble, wasting their time. There was little sense of cooperation or mutual support, and the village was in such a dire state that development was unimaginable.
* As the saying goes, "If someone goes to the market wearing a manggeon, I'll wear one too," the villagers would go to the market just to drink excessively and cause fights, leading to constant chaos in the village.

#### b) Culture and Daily Life (Clothing, Food, Shelter)

* The residents of this village, who had lived for generations without electricity, were too busy surviving to even think about living a human life. Their only source of news was from the school.
* Fortunately, there were two radios in the village, which served as their only source of entertainment and news.
* Almost every household had to rely on porridge for at least one meal a day. During the spring famine, which is now a thing of the past, they often had to skip meals. Thatched roofs went years without proper repair, emitting a foul odor. Houses and pigsties were almost indistinguishable in some cases. Makeshift outhouses were overflowing with waste, attracting flies and maggots. In the dark kitchens, various insects buzzed around without any cats to keep them at bay.

### b. The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

#### 1) Motivation and Results of the Pilot Project

* In 1970, news spread that the Saemaul Undong, initiated by President Park Chung-hee, was reaching various villages. In 1971, the county provided support for a pilot project, supplying 335 bags of cement. The village began work on expanding the main village road and repairing the communal well.
* However, due to a lack of cooperation from the residents and insufficient technical skills, the construction was shoddy and substandard. Later, the entire project had to be redone.


--- (p. 309) ---

After that, without undertaking any significant projects, the years 1971-1972 were wasted in the residents' apathy and the elders' stubbornness.
In 1973, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) spread like wildfire across the country, and neighboring villages began to change day by day.
Stimulated by this, the residents began to feel ashamed of their own laziness and apathy.
After that, led by Kim (金) the leader, the village residents eagerly took the lead in the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) to avoid falling behind their neighbors.

## 2) Leader's (指導者) Activities (活動)

Kim Se-hyun, the leader, who had been taking care of household and village affairs after graduating from middle school (中學校), was elected as a formal Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) leader in 1972 following a village assembly (마을總會) resolution.
Determined to approach his new role with renewed resolve, he promoted village infrastructure projects in 1973 with government (政府) support materials, but achieved little success.
Realizing this was not enough, Kim (金) the leader began to personally persuade residents who were not participating, visiting each household (戶別).
Meanwhile, Kim Wan-su (金完洙), who had graduated from university (大學) in Seoul and was working as an employee (社員), returned to his hometown (故鄕).
After becoming the village head (里長) in December 1975, he spared no effort to overcome the village's backwardness (落後性), working together with Kim (金) the leader to create a prosperous village without a moment's pause.
Their tireless efforts and dedicated service greatly contributed to making this village the best in the district (管內).

## 3) Overcoming Difficulties (隘路 克服)

During the expansion of the back alley behind Kim Young-hak's house in Sangnyegok (上禮谷):
After repeatedly failing to persuade the landowner (地主) to donate the field (垡地) to be incorporated into the expansion, the villagers took advantage of the landowner's absence and demolished the wall to widen the alley.
That night at 11 PM, upon returning from an outing, the landowner stormed into Kim (金) the leader's house with a spinning top, threatening to kill him by smashing the door.
Kim (金) the leader barely escaped through the back door and had to hide elsewhere for four days.
After that, when the villagers neatly repaired the demolished wall and beautifully renovated and painted the roofs, the landowner finally regretted his previous stubbornness and actively participated in the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement).
When preparing to open a communal farm (共同 農場), which became the source of wealth (富) for this village in 1976:
Since the village's soil (土壤) was originally sandy with poor water absorption (吸收力) and the water source (水源) was insufficient, and since the land to be reclaimed, Yeokgokcheon (禮谷川), was also sandy, making it unclear how to secure water (水源), the residents strongly opposed, claiming that the project would only waste money and manpower (人力).


--- (p. 310) ---

Even worse, some people would not hesitate to blame leaders like Kim, the village chief (金里長), for suffering caused by colluding with businessmen (業者), to the extent that Kim had to leave the village for a few days. However, by persuading them day and night, we were able to complete difficult construction projects such as installing a water pumping station (揚水場).

### 4) Developmental Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (新村運動)
O Until the year 1974, this village could not shake off the stigma of being a "basic village" (基礎마을), so
O In January 1975, taking the resolution of the village general assembly (住民總會) as an opportunity, the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) began to reignite.
O That year, as the first project, the village's long-awaited community center (會舘) was started with a village fund of 130,000 won (萬圓), and
O With all residents (住民) united as one, they completed the project without any external support, doing everything from making bricks to constructing the framework with their own village strength (自力).
O After erecting a modern-style (現代式) community center (會舘) and installing various equipment (機材) donated by well-wishers (喜捨), the residents (住민) gained confidence (自信感) and determination, saying, "If we do it, we can do it."
O The enthusiasm (熱誠) of the residents (住民) to surpass neighboring hamlets (隣近部落) led to the achievement of many projects, including income-generating businesses (所得事業).
In this way, as a result of the cooperative efforts (協同) of all residents (住民), by the end of 1976, the village shed the stigma of being a "basic village" (基礎마을) and, without going through the stage of a self-help village (自助마을), was immediately promoted to a self-reliant village (自立마을), earning the honor of being the "Best Saemaul Village" in the province (道內).

### 5) Land and Cash Donation Status (土地 및 現金喜捨狀況)
For this village, which transformed from a basic (基礎) to a self-reliant village (自立마을) in just one year through blood, sweat, and tears, encouragement (激勵) and monetary/donations (誠金品) came one after another from village dignitaries (在京) in Seoul and various sectors (各界), and the residents (住民) also did not hesitate to donate (喜捨) for the sake of the village.

### 6) Heartwarming Stories (美談) Anecdotes (佳話)
#### a) First Story (第一話)
*   Hearing the news that the Saemaul Undong (運動) for a better life was gradually taking place in his hometown, Kim Deok-jung, a Cheongsan Unit Association President (靑山單位組合長) from this village, decided to actively support the village's development in both material and spiritual aspects.
*   On February 10, 1977, when the village farm (農場) development project was facing difficulties due to insufficient funds, he pledged his personal assets as collateral and lent 3,000,000 won to help the villagers regain their courage and successfully complete the farm development project.
*   After visiting the village several times to comfort and encourage the residents and guide the Saemaul Undong (事業), the village was selected as the best village in the province in 1977 and received a commendation and 2,000,000 won prize money from the Minister of the Interior (內務部長官).

#### b) Second Story (第二話)
*   Since 1972, Jeong Heon-ae (鄭憲愛), a female leader in this village, organized the village women's association (婦女會) and aimed to practice thrift in daily life. She established and operated a village purchasing and selling center (購販場) and encouraged all members of the women's association to participate in the "Buy Korean Goods" campaign.
*   As a result, the women's association was able to raise 2,800,000 won in funds that year. With this, the members continued to operate the purchasing and selling business while also promoting a rice-saving campaign to support the Saemaul Undong (事業). From 1972 to 1976, they raised a total of 11,300,000 won in common funds for the women's association. In 1976, they donated 6,000,000 won to complete the internal wiring work for the village electrification project.
*   Additionally, they donated 5,300,000 won to promote the construction of a simple water supply facility that year, which greatly contributed to the project's progress.
*   Jeong Heon-ae (鄭憲愛), the president of the women's association (婦女會長), donated her own land of 200 pyeong (坪) to the village, ensuring the successful completion of the project.
*   In 1977, during the village farm (農場) development, she took turns with the men to promote the project, earning the nickname "Diligent Women's Association" for her dedication.

8) Special notes (特記 事項)
a) Joyful events
O On May 15, 1975, when the village community center (會舘) was completed, even the usually indifferent elderly neighbors came out wearing hats and suits, and we enjoyed the lively atmosphere together.
O In February 1977, when our village was selected as the nation's best Saemaul Undong (新村運動) village (部落), we received a commendation (表彰) from the Minister of the Interior (內務部長官) and a prize of 20,000,000 won (원).
O In 1977, we received an outstanding administrative achievement award (行政 實績 優秀) of 1,000,000 won (원) in business expenses (事業費) and a governor's prize (道知事 賞金) of 1,000,000 won (원).
O When the water supply (上水道) project, overcome with great difficulty (難關 克服), was completed, the residents (住民) were overjoyed.
O On March 18, 1977, when Assembly member (議員) Yuk In-su (陸寅修) and Governor (知事) Jeong Jong-taek (鄭宗澤) visited our village farm (農場) to encourage (激勵) and donate (誠金).
O On August 7, 1977, when the county magistrate (郡守), leaders (指導者), and village head (里長) appeared on KBS TV's "New Saemaul, New Life" (新村 新 生活) program to introduce (紹介) the village (마을) development (發展).
O On March 18, 1976, when Vice County Magistrate (副郡守) Kim Jae-hyeong (金在衡) visited to encourage (激勵) the unfinished business (未盡 事業) and promised (約束) to support (支援) with 450 bags of cement.
O On June 29, 1976, when the village (마을) development (發展) situation (狀況) was introduced (紹介) in the Chungcheong Ilbo (忠淸日報).

b) Difficult events
O When creating the village farm (農場 造成), there were conflicts (衝突) of opinion (意見) between residents (住民) and contractors (業者), and when leaders (指導者) tried to mediate (解決), they were only met with criticism (非難) and complaints (怨聲).
O Due to excessive enthusiasm (過度 意慾) in business (事業) that exceeded the available manpower (人員), during the sewer (下水溝), water supply (上水道), and village farm (農場) construction (工事), even women (婦女子) and children had to work at night (夜間).
O It was most heartbreaking when the farm (農場) that we had worked so hard to create was damaged by the drought (旱害) of 1977.

### Ba. Achievements through Saemaul Undong

#### 1) Spiritual and Daily Life Aspects

* Through Saemaul Undong, the residents have become the most diligent in the area and have learned to do everything themselves.
* On May 15, 1975, the village meeting decided to:
  1. Lead by example (솔선수범)
  2. Unite and cooperate (협동단결)
  The villagers are practicing these village agreements (향약) and working vigorously for the modernization of the country (조국).

#### 2) Production and Income Aspects

* Income has expanded through the cultivation of 98% unpolished rice (통일벼).
* There has been a dramatic expansion in the area cultivated with tobacco (연초), and the cultivation of high-quality vegetables (고등소채), leading to an expected income exceeding 200 million won in 1977, up from just 210 million won in 1970. The village is enjoying prosperity as a welfare village.
