# 3. Residents' Assembly (住民總會)

Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (1)

**Agenda (議題):** Promoting the 72 Saemaul Undong (事業)
**Date (日時):** December 20, 1971 (19:00~21:30)
**Venue (場所):** Kim Tae-jung's living room
**Attendees (參席):** Kim Nan-su and 51 others (6 absent (不參))
**Chairperson (司會者):** Village Head (Kim Yong-dal (金容達))

**Chairperson (司會者):** I apologize for calling this meeting in such cold weather. However, there are urgent matters to discuss with you all, and I have called you here to talk about several pressing projects. Please understand this and cooperate to make this a serious meeting. As you all know, starting next year, the government (政府) plans to support the Saemaul Undong (事業) on a large scale by providing cement and steel reinforcement. However, our village (部落) has not received any support, perhaps due to my lack of ability (能力). The truth is, our village (部落) has always been known for drinking too much, enjoying ourselves too much, and being lazy. The county (面) officials said they cannot support such a village (部落). Please blame me for everything. And they said they cannot support a lazy village (部落) like ours in the future. However, we have promised to learn from the past and work hard to build a diligent village (部落).

**Kim Bong-su:** Hey, who cares if they support us or not! I'll handle it myself tomorrow, won't I? If you're going to say stuff like that, just cancel today's meeting!

**Chairperson (司會者):** I'm sorry. Our village (部落) is one where our ancestors (先祖) have lived for generations. It is also the village (部落) of the Gwang-san Kim clan (光山金氏) where our descendants (後孫) must live forever. Can we continue to live without escaping the old dilapidated walls, thatched roofs, and narrow alleys? We must cultivate and improve them with our own hands.

**Kim Bong-su:** Hey, are you giving a sermon (說敎)? What trick do you have to touch what has been passed down through generations? Are you trying to invite a lightning strike from our ancestors (祖上)?

**Kim Jae-su:** Brother, why do you say such things? Let's just listen to the story.

**Chairperson (司會者):** Our neighborhood is too dirty. Let's try to live well by making it clean and beautiful with our own hands. Look at our village (部落). Can you even tell the difference between the roads, sewers, pigsties, and houses? How can we be indifferent (無關心)? We need a lot of land (垈地) to straighten the alleys. Residents (住民), you must leave a valuable inheritance (遺産) for our descendants (後孫) rather than our remaining lifespan (餘生). Without your wholehearted cooperation (協助), we cannot expand the alleys (擴張).

**Kim Yong-yeon:** The village head (里長) is right. It's a shameful thing. Let's all work together. My field...


--- (p. 316) ---

### Let's Expand the Roads First

Host: Thank you. Please approve the road expansion and fence improvement projects for this year by unanimous consent. What are the residents' opinions?
Kim Yong-yeon: Since it's something we have to do, let's just do it (All residents agree)
Kim Yong-cheol: The village head (里長) and the development committee members should first establish a comprehensive business plan and disclose how much each household will contribute. After obtaining approval letters, we can start the project.
Village Head (里長): That is a good opinion. For expanding the roads, we mainly need the approval of Kim Jaeik's fields and Lee Seongchun's fields, among a few others. We will establish the business plan within a few days, visit each household to obtain approvals, and explain the details. We ask for your active cooperation and will strive to secure support for our village by 1973. With that, I will conclude today's meeting.

Date (日時): January 10, 1972 (19:30~21:30)
Location (場所): Kim Tae-jung's living room

Host: Please recommend candidates.

Host: Are there any other candidates?

Host: I will announce the voting results. Kim Se-hyun received 37 votes, Kim In-su received 13 votes, and Kim Yong-bok received 3 votes. Kim Se-hyun, who received the most votes, has been elected. Let's give a round of applause to encourage Kim Se-hyun, who has been elected as our village's Saemaul Leader (指導者). (All residents applaud) Then, as the elected Saemaul Leader (指導者) for this village,

### Minutes of the Meeting (3)
*   **Date**: November 10, 1972
*   **Location**: Yeok National Elementary School (禮谷國民學校)
*   **Agenda**: Formulation of the 1973 Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) Business Plan
*   **Attendees**: 58 (All villagers)

**Host**: Thanks to your cooperation, it has been decided that the 1973 Saemaul Undong business will be carried out with the support of 400 bags of cement and 1 ton of steel reinforcement. We must express our gratitude to the county and district offices. Now, please share your thoughts on how we can best utilize the 400 bags of cement and 1 ton of steel reinforcement that we have received.
**Leader**: Last year, we expanded the village road and improved some of the fences, but the work was not completed properly. I propose that the materials we receive next year be first used to complete the road expansion project, and the remaining materials be used for constructing underground drains, small bridges, and sewer facilities. Please share your opinions on this.
**Kim Jae-ik**: In my opinion, we should build a bridge because students cannot commute to school during the flood season due to the lack of a bridge in front of the village.
**Kim Myeong-su**: I think we should distribute a few bags of cement to each household to build fences.

Please raise your hand if you agree with the business I proposed. (53 out of 58 agree) With 53 votes in favor, I will adopt the agenda item I proposed. Therefore, the 1973 Saemaul Undong business plan will be decided as follows: one road expansion site, four underground drain sites, and one small bridge site. Now, please share your opinions on the implementation methods.

**Chairperson:** Thank you all for coming today despite your busy schedules. Thanks to your relentless cooperation, our village has seen many changes. However, there is still much to be done. Therefore, we have gathered here today to decide on our 1977 Saemaul Undong projects with everyone's participation. Please share your ideas on what projects we should undertake.

**Kim Yong-dal:** We have undertaken many projects so far, but there is still a 50-meter stretch of the alleyway near Jeong Heon-ae's and Park Cha-ha's houses that remains unfinished. I propose that we include this in this year's projects.

I have been contemplating this idea for a few years. If we utilize our cooperative spirit that we have demonstrated so far, we can complete this project within 60 days. The required funds can be obtained through loans from the county or the agricultural cooperative, and the remaining amount can be covered by small contributions from all villagers. The provided cement and steel reinforcement can be used for the waterway and water pump station. What do you think of my proposal? (All villagers agree)

**Chairperson**: Thanks to your active cooperation, we have overcome the difficulties and challenges of this year and successfully completed the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) business. I would like to express my gratitude at this opportunity.
At the beginning, there were moments of hesitation about whether we could really do it. However, with the special support of 1 million won from the governor after his visit to our county, we were able to create a large farm.
Now, the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) leader will report on the business settlement.

**Saemaul Undong (新村運動) Leader**: I would like to express my gratitude to all the residents and promotion committee members who have worked hard for this business. First, the area of the village farm has been developed to 6,705 pyeong (坪) according to the county's measurement results. A total of 820 million won has been invested, including 200 million won in support funds, 300 million won in agricultural cooperative loans, and 320 million won borne by our residents.
We have completed the auxiliary facilities of the farm, such as a water lifting station and waterway facilities. As you all know, we planted unified rice and harvested 199 seok, earning 2.5 million won in revenue. This money will first be used to repay the loan from the agricultural cooperative, and the rest will be used to repay next year's farming.

The audit committee and business committee members have reviewed all the accounts. Please share the results.

**Business Committee Member**: Yes, I would like to express my gratitude for the successful completion of the business through the cooperation and unity of the village head, the leader, and all the residents. After carefully reviewing and confirming the payment of wages, the use of equipment, and the purchase of materials, it is believed that the funds have been appropriately executed. Thank you.

**Chairperson**: All documents are always available at the village community center. If you have any questions, please review them. If there are any objections to this settlement, please let us know. (No objections from residents)

**Chairperson**: Finally, I would like to express my gratitude to all the residents. If we all work together next year, abundant fruits will be before us.
Let's end the meeting by singing the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) song in unison.

## 4. Future Development Plan (發展構想)

- After being promoted to a self-sufficient village in February 1977, Yeokgok (禮谷) village, which achieved an income of over 2 million won in 1977 and became a welfare village, will focus on the expansion of village culture and welfare facilities. It plans to organize a scholarship association with farm profits to help disadvantaged but diligent students, build a children's playground in 1979, operate a library and expand the village community center in 1978, and operate a village school bus in 1980.
- On the other hand, it will continue to strive for increased income. In 1978, it will operate a fish farm and complete a rice polishing factory. It will gradually attract Saemaul factories, aiming to exceed 3 million won per household income by 1980.

# Chungbuk (Chungcheongbuk-do) Goesan County (Goesan-gun) Mun'gwang-myeon (Mun'gwang-myeon) Bangseong-ri (Bangseong-ri)

## 1. Overview of the Village

### Ga. History

*   During the late Joseon Dynasty (李朝), this village was called Yeosaang (如思仰) in Namyeon-myeon (南隱面). It was renamed Bangseong-ri (方城里) in Mun'gwang-myeon (文光面) following the 1914 administrative district (行政區域) reorganization during the Japanese colonial period (日帝). It is said that during the Imjin War (壬辰倭亂) in 1592 (宣祖 25年, April 13), the 14th-generation ancestor of the Jeonju Yi clan (全州李氏) residing in this village at that time considered this area, which forms the central part of the three villages (三室) (Baesil, Jwasil, Jipsil), as a suitable refuge (避難處) and settled here, leading to the establishment of the village.
*   Surrounded by steep mountains (險峻한 산) on three sides, with "Baemisan" mountain to the north forming a natural barrier like a screen, the remains of a fortress (城廓) can still be seen today. This is why the area has been called Bangseong (方城), meaning a walled city.

### Na. Location and Conditions

*   Located 16 km south of the Goesan County Office (槐山郡廳), across Darae Pass, this village is situated 5 km further northwest along a mountain valley, passing through Deokpyeong (德平), famous for its uranium (鑛) drilling site (試錐地區).
*   Nestled in a narrow valley (狹谷) surrounded by steep mountains (險峻한 산) at a 60-70 degree incline, the village is surrounded by rice paddies (田沓) clinging to the valley sides like water striders.
*   The three natural hamlets (自然部落) are connected by narrow, invisible grass roads (草路) around a large mountain circumference of 6 km.
*   About 10 km to the south, along the upper reaches of the Geocheon (槐江) River, lies Hwayangdong (花陽洞), a famous scenic spot (名勝地) that attracts many tourists (觀光客) throughout the year.
*   The upper reaches of the Geocheon River, where the Goesan Hydroelectric Power Plant (槐山水力發電所) is located, are always bustling with anglers.

### Da. Basic Situation

## 2. Village Development Process (發展過程)

### 가. Situation Before 1970 (70年 以前 的 狀況)

#### 1) Basic Environment (基礎環境)
The village is located in the most remote area within Mun'gwang-myeon (文光面) and was the most backward hamlet. There were no access roads to the village, only rough mountain paths that required traversing hills. Even trips to the market would leave clothes damp with morning dew. The thatched roofs of the houses were worn and the mud walls were stained with bird droppings, resembling abstract art. The traditional outhouses were indistinguishable from compost pits, breeding grounds for flies and mosquitoes. On rainy days, the lack of drainage caused waste to overflow into the village lanes, filling the air with unsanitary odors. The winding village paths, unlit by electricity, were hazardous, and accidents were common. Due to poor transportation, the villagers lived in isolation, lacking communication and cultural facilities, which contributed to their ignorance and poverty. Their way of life showed no signs of progress.

#### 2) Income Level (所得水準)


--- (p. 324) ---

It was a small village with the lowest income level in the district, relying on a limited amount of farmland inherited from ancestors, traditional farming methods, and the cultivation of regional specialty crops such as tobacco, chili peppers, garlic, potatoes, and some sericulture to make up for the shortage of staple crops.

**Income Level in 1970**

| Wheat Production | 11.3ha        | 24,500kg      | 2,620         |                             |
| Documents      | 92.           | 146           | 1,320         |                             |
| Chili Cultivation | 7.4ha         | 14,680kg      | 1,026         |                             |

| Hanwoo Breeding | 16 heads      |               | 800,000       |                             |
| Others        |               |               | 50,000        | Average income per household: 430,000 |

3) Living Conditions

Dependent on the meager income from traditional farming methods on limited farmland, the villagers' living conditions bred ignorance and poverty. The educational level of the young people was low, and even those who graduated from middle or high school were buried in small farms, helping with farm work. The villagers' outdated thinking, laziness, mutual jealousy, and restraint made them indifferent and expressionless, with no hope for the future or desire to live better.

**B. Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)**

1) Motivation and Results of the Pilot Project

On April 22, 1970, President Park Chung-hee proposed the "Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)," which echoed throughout the country. The village head and the secretary of the face came to the village to educate the residents on the implementation methods. However, the uncooperative and indifferent residents made it like reading scriptures to a cow, and the communication between the leaders and the residents was like answering questions from the east when asked from the west. Amidst this indifference, the year 1970 had to pass.

2) Election of Leaders and Activity Status

Amidst the villagers' indifference, the village head and the responsible secretary persistently explained and persuaded Ju Kwang-u, who had graduated from high school and was helping with farm work at home, to the true meaning of the Saemaul business. Ju Kwang-u became convinced that this was the right opportunity for the village to "wake up from a long winter sleep, welcome a new spring, and make a vigorous new start" and that it was the right condition to "live better." He visited other high school and middle school graduates in the village to persuade them, and those who had studied new learning agreed and visited each household whenever they had time, explaining the principles (理)


--- (p. 325) ---

They tried to explain and persuade, but

- The residents, entrenched in their old ways, resisted with stubbornness, and even when meetings were held to explain the true meaning of the Saemaul Undong and to foster a spirit of cooperation and participation, they merely sat and complained, gaining nothing.
- In this ignorant village environment, recent high school graduates who formed the 4-H Club took on the role of volunteer leaders, aiming to increase income through new farming techniques,
- Establishing village and neighborhood collective farms, cultivating special crops to increase profits, and participating in 4-H competitions to win prizes, etc., began to change the residents' perceptions,
- And gradually, they started to adopt new farming methods. In response to this movement among the residents, leaders volunteered with the firm resolve to make this village into an "ideal new community."

### 3) Overcoming Difficulties

- After volunteering as Saemaul leaders, they purchased books and magazines about new farming methods from county or township guidance centers,
- Visiting homes or gathering rooms where residents frequently gathered to update their knowledge with new farming techniques and news,
- And tried to persuade them by citing the drawbacks of traditional farming methods and the post-war revival of Japanese rural life as examples, but
- The residents remained indifferent, and some even said ignorantly, "If you're so smart, why don't you become a township head or a member of the National Assembly?" Meanwhile, a Mr. Ji, a member of the middle class in this village, visited with a gloomy expression.
- Upon receiving a message from the leader of a neighboring village in Cheongcheon-myeon, Daejeon-ri, asking to "come discuss something," he went to find that they wanted his village's land for constructing a Saemaul farm road, leading to a whole day of argument: "Donate the land!" "No way!" Unable to contain his anger, Mr. Ji said, "Tomorrow, I'll bring the whole family and have a brawl if I must," and came to ask the youths in this village to cooperate.
- In this situation, the whole village buzzed with talk, and the next day, dozens of residents whose farmland was adjacent gathered in Daejeon-ri hamlet to support and observe.
- Here, the arguments between the two parties were entirely self-serving.
After repeated debates, a new road was built from Deokpyeong to Bangseong-ri village, a 5km stretch where no road had existed before,
- Allowing ox carts and taxis to pass smoothly, and considering that many residents of Daejeon-ri owned farmland in the direction of Bangseong-ri village, the issue of donating farmland became a major concern for both sides.


--- (p. 326) ---

The two village leaders reached a consensus that their villages were largely similar and decided to construct a 2km access road leading to Bangseong-ri village. After raising awareness among the villagers and returning, they convened a village assembly to discuss the expansion of the access road. Once the business plan was explained and the land to be incorporated into the access road was revealed, the meeting hall turned into chaos with some residents strongly opposing the plan. However, after some persuasion and appeasement, the residents regained their composure and voluntarily took on the burden of effort. The access road project began, but as usual, there were obstacles in the field, such as accurately marking lines according to the design. After overcoming numerous difficulties, the access road expansion project was completed by the residents' own efforts on February 8, 1972. The completed access road made the villagers' footsteps lighter, and even those who had previously opposed the project smiled, saying, "We should try the Saemaul Undong," experiencing infinite possibilities and emotions.

## 4) Developmental Promotion of Saemaul Undong (새마을事業)

Taking the village access road expansion project as a model, in February 1972, they were able to easily expand four 600m-long village inner roads. Along with the village inner road expansion project, wall improvement projects were carried out, and in areas with many stones, neat stone walls were constructed. 62 sites totaling 2,850m of stone walls were topped with tiles, resulting in an exquisite finish. The same year, with government support, they received 335 bags of cement to repair six 850m-long sewers and construct some prefabricated walls. In October 1972, with government-supported materials such as cement and steel reinforcement, they began constructing a 30-pyeong warehouse in I-dong village and completed it in 1973 by injecting the I-dong village common fund. In 1973, roof improvement projects began, and after eight months of persistent effort and hard work by the villagers, 82 houses were completely transformed. The same year, 12 houses were improved, and projects to straighten 500m of two sites in Secheon in front of the village and 550m of three small streams were accomplished. In 1974, with government support, four 24m small bridge projects were carried out, and in May, the long-awaited telephone project was realized, bringing light to 50 households. In 1975, temporary water supply facilities were installed in 38 households, and wall painting and kitchen improvement projects were completed as part of the environmental beautification project. In 1976, as part of the environmental improvement and hygiene projects, roof painting was carried out in 36 houses, wall painting in 28 houses, toilet improvement in 33 houses, and kitchen improvement in 42 houses.


--- (p. 327) ---

In 1977, as part of the livestock barn improvement (畜舍改良) project, 30 buildings (棟) of traditional (在來式) livestock barns (畜舍) were completely renovated (一新) and reconstructed (改築). In May, 2,500 meters of farm roads (農路) were established (開設) in 2 locations (個所), and 16 houses (住宅) were improved (改良). According to the village's site conditions (立地條件), 500 trees (株) of persimmon (밤 나무), 3,000 trees (株) of jujube (대추나무), and 2,000 trees (株) of persimmon (감나무) were planted. The villagers truly contributed to income increase (所得增大) and did not neglect it. Today, the villagers, holding onto the dreams of tomorrow, look back on the days when they suffered from hunger and are firmly united.

## 6) Heartwarming Stories (美談佳話)

### a) First Story (第1話)
With the opening (開通) of the village access road (進入路) in the narrow valley (山間狹谷), the villagers, who had been like frogs in a well (우물안 개구리) in a dark (暗黑) world (世界), were injected with vitality (活氣) into their lives (生活), which had been plagued by ignorance (無知) and selfishness (我執). This was made possible by the generous land donation (土地 喜捨) of the village development committee chairperson (開發委員會長), leading to a wave of donations (喜捨) from everyone. Now, not only is transportation (交通) facilitated (疎通), but the burden (수고로움) of carrying goods (物品運搬) has been reduced.

### b) Second Story (第2話)
The villagers had been using (使用) water from a natural well (天然우물) in the rice paddy dike (논두렁) as their sole (唯一) water source (食水). Due to the inconvenience (번거로움) of carrying water (물) over long distances (원거리) using old water containers (물동이) or water jugs (물통), a simple water supply (簡易給水) facility project (施設工事) was carried out (施行). Despite their poverty (가난), the women's association (婦女會) launched a rice-saving (節米) campaign (運動) and donated (喜捨) the 380,000 won (參拾八萬圓) they had saved (貯蓄) to the project (本工事). Now, each household (各家庭) can easily draw (기르) water by simply turning on the tap (수도꼭지). They have found new meaning (보람) in life (生活) through this facility (施設).

### Achievements of the Saemaul Movement (事業)

### 1) Spiritual Aspect (精神面)
*   Through the Saemaul Movement (事業), people were transformed into diligent, self-reliant, and cooperative individuals. They learned that "if you try, you can do it" and that "the results of effort come with a price."
*   Through village assemblies (住民總會), they understood the true meaning of democracy in the public square (廣場) of dialogue (對話).
*   They developed a sense of gratitude towards their country (祖國), learned to love their nation, appreciate the government's efforts, and understood the truth that they should help those in need (不遇).

### 2) Livelihood Aspect (生活面)
*   With the reform of agricultural technology (營農技術), seed renewal (種子更新), and livestock breeding (家畜增殖) business (事業), income (所得) increased, leading to a stable life (生活). People became more dedicated to their duties (職務), conducted research, and adopted a progressive attitude (進取的姿勢).
*   Through thrift (勤儉節約), they saved money (貯蓄), helped their less fortunate neighbors (不遇), and practiced the belief that "everyone living well means I live well."

### 3) Production Aspect (生產面)
*   Traditional farming methods (在來式營農方法) were abandoned in favor of new agricultural technologies (營農技術), with a focus on increasing income (所得增大).
*   Encouraged by the introduction of superior seed varieties (品種), they aimed for progressive income growth (所得增大), maximizing the use of cultivated land (耕作地) to increase income (所得).

3. Residents' General Assembly (住民總會)
♦ Minutes of the Meeting (會議錄) (1)

**Date (日時)**: December 13, 1972
**Location (場所)**: Living room of Mr. Lee Se-jung's house
**Agenda (議制)**: Construction of access roads (進入路)
**Attendees (參席佛)**: Mr. Lee Jae-woo and 45 others
**Absentees (不參者)**: Mr. Lee Eung-sik and 23 others
**Chairperson (司會)**: Lee Se-jung

**Chairperson (司會)**: Despite the cold weather, I have gathered all of you here today for a Residents' General Assembly to discuss the access roads for our village as part of the 1973 Saemaul Undong (事業). I would like to hear your opinions on where and how long these roads should be. Please share your thoughts.

**Lee Jae-woo**: I apologize for speaking first. I believe we should construct an access road from the lower part of Yeosaeng to the upper part. I estimate it would be around 2 kilometers if we take a straight line. Currently, we carry all our goods on our backs along a 4-kilometer path that has been used since our ancestors' time. I think it's time we make a change.

**Ji Jang-hoon**: That's an excellent suggestion. I fully support Mr. Lee Jae-woo's opinion.

**Kim Hwa-kyung**: We should not only focus on Yeosaeng but also construct a road from Galgol to Bangseonggol.

**Lee Jae-woo**: Let's start with Yeosaeng first and then consider Bangseonggol later.

**Kim Hwa-kyung**: Since the villages are similar, it would be better to start together.

**Chairperson (司會)**: Please be patient. Let's first decide on the number of locations. What do you think?

**Son Seong-gi**: For 1973, I suggest constructing access roads of 2 kilometers in Yeosaeng, 1 kilometer in Bangseonggol, and 3 kilometers in another location, totaling 6 kilometers.

**Lee Jung-il**: That's a good idea. I agree.

**Chairperson (司會)**: Are there any other opinions? If not, please show your support with applause.

*(Applause)*

**Chairperson (司會)**: Since the majority has agreed, we will proceed with constructing access roads at two locations, totaling 3 kilometers. Now, how should we proceed with this plan? Please share your thoughts.

**Lee Young-joong**: When constructing roads, it's better to consider the shade and sunlight. I think it would be best to build roads on the sunny side, even if it requires more land.

**Oh Jin-bok**: In that case, we will need to purchase that land, won't we?


--- (p. 331) ---

**Jijanghun**: What if the landowners each donate a few pyeong of land?
**Ogije**: Are you crazy? Do you expect people to give away their land for free?
**Ojinbon**: Some people will need to contribute more land than others. Let's set a price for each.
**Lee Jae-u**: I don't think that's possible. The village fund won't have money to buy the land.
**Yoon Seok-chae**: If 15 people need to contribute land for the access road, there will be others who don't. Those who need to contribute land should donate it, and those who don't should each give 5,000 won to the village. What do you think?
**Lee Jung-ok**: That's a great idea. I feel bad as someone who doesn't need to contribute land, so I agree.
**Jijanghun**: Some people will need to contribute more land than others.
**Chairperson**: It seems we have some good suggestions. Does anyone have other opinions? If you oppose, please clap. (Silence) Since no one is clapping, I assume everyone agrees. When pursuing a communal project, individuals may sometimes incur personal losses. Please keep in mind that this is for the good of the village and cooperate actively with an open mind. That concludes today's meeting.

### 4. Future Development Plans (發展 計劃)

#### 1) Environmental Improvement Projects (環境 改善 事業)

*   Secure a communal village site (共同 敷地) and build a village community center (會舘) of about 30 pyeong (坪) to 40 pyeong (坪). Inside the center, we will create a meeting room (會議室), a neighborhood safe (里洞 金庫), a children's study room (工夫房), and a village library (文庫) to efficiently operate village development (發展).
*   Purchase 1 hectare of forest land (林野) to create a children's playground and nurture the emotions of growing children.
*   Purchase a site of about 5 pyeong (坪) to build a Senior Citizens' Hall (敬老堂) for the elderly, providing recreational facilities (娛樂 施設) and a place of rest (安息處) for them.

#### 2) Production Base Establishment Projects (生産 基盤 造成 事業)

*   Build a communal village kitchen (共同 炊事場) to reduce labor during the busy farming season (農繁期). Additionally, open 3 more farm roads (農路) totaling 680 meters and install 2 more water collection tunnels (集水 暗渠) to prepare for droughts (旱害).

#### 3) Income Increase Projects (所得 增大 事業)

*   Expand the persimmon orchard (團地) by 6 hectares, the jujube orchard (團地) by 4 hectares, and the chestnut orchard (團地) by 3 hectares. Additionally, introduce 25 more fattening cattle (肥育牛).
*   Expand the neighborhood purchasing and selling market (里洞 購販場) and build a market building (建物). Select sales personnel (要員) from the village, expand the sales range (範圍), and entrust the sales of local specialties (特產物) to outside regions (外地). Also, delegate the purchase of vinyl and agricultural chemicals (農藥).
*   Create a communal workshop (共同 作業場) in the village and utilize the off-farming season (農閑期) to produce silk cocoons (새끼꼬기), pottery (가마기치기), and dried persimmons (잠박).
*   Build a communal drying facility (共同 乾操場) to dry chili peppers (고추치기), persimmons (꼬감찌기), and traditional Chinese medicinal materials (漢藥材).
*   Establish a communal compost shed (共同 堆肥舍) in the village, implement communal grass cutting, increase compost production (堆肥 增產), and renew the soil fertility (地力) of aged farmland (農耕地) to contribute to income increase (所得 增大).
*   As part of the national policy (國家 施策), we will cultivate the village as a self-sufficient New Community village in 1978 and further promote an ideal New Community project (事業) to leap forward as a model village (示範 部落) by the year 1980. We will build an ideal village (理想村) in this deep mountain valley, creating a paradise on earth (地上 樂園).

# Chungnam (Chungcheongnam-do) Daedeok-gun (Daedeok County) Giseong-myeon (Giseong Township) Bongok-ri (Bongok Village)

## 1. Overview of the Village

### a. History

Bongok-ri 1-ga (Bongok Village 1-ga) in Giseong-myeon, Daedeok-gun is a mountainous village formed about 500 years ago when the Deoksu Lee (李) clan first settled here. During the Joseon Dynasty, it belonged to Hanam-myeon (下南面) in Jinjam-hyeon (Jinjam County), and later became part of Daejeon-gun (Daejeon County) due to administrative district name changes at the end of the Joseon Dynasty. In 1931, when Daejeon-eup (Daejeon Township) was promoted to a city (府), the administrative districts were reorganized, and the village became part of Giseong-myeon, Daedeok-gun, where it remains today. Currently, there are 71 households divided into 5 natural hamlets (자연부락).

### b. Location and Conditions

Located about 16 km southwest of Daejeon along the Honam Expressway, the village can be seen near the Hakha Reservoir. From there, it is about 2 km further into the mountains.

As mentioned earlier, this village is composed of 5 natural hamlets due to its location in the mountains with limited farmland. The farmland is mostly unreliable for irrigation, resulting in poor harvests. The village is situated by the upper reaches of the Gapcheon (甲川) River, which has a width of 70-80 meters, and is cut off from transportation to places like Heukseok-ri (黑石里) along the Honam Line railway, which connects to the Daejeon metropolitan area. As a result, the village has been isolated in terms of development, administrative penetration, agricultural advancement, and educational improvement, among other aspects. The villagers have lived believing that their fate depends on the heavens, as they guard their ancestors' graves and farm the land passed down through generations.

## 2. Village Development Process (發展過程)

### A. Situation Before 1970 (70年以前的狀況)

#### 1) Basic Environment (基礎環境)

- Everyone in the village, whether inside or outside, suffered from poverty. The entire village had no tiled-roof houses, only thatched huts with reed fences. The village roads and farmland connecting roads were as narrow as primitive paths where people could barely pass each other. Life was as primitive as it gets, with no one even knowing how to use a handcart.

#### 2) Income Level (所得水準)

- Without a doubt, the meager farmland, mostly fields, yielded harvests that could only sustain a life of boiling porridge twice a day for survival. Over 90% of the villagers lived in this harsh cycle.

#### 3) Mental State (精神狀態)

- Living in ignorance and poverty, the villagers never thought about improving their lives. They spent their days drinking and gambling. On market days in the town, they would go without any purpose, get drunk, and either collapse under someone's eaves or get into fights. The concept of unity was just a word in the dictionary. They lived without hope for the future or a pioneering spirit, indifferent and expressionless.

#### 4) Culture and Daily Life (文化及衣食住生活)

- The residents here lived under lantern light without electricity. Struggling to make ends meet, they could not afford a huma


--- (p. 340) ---

People had never enjoyed life, had no idea what cultural life was, thought television was a magical story from a fairy tale, and had only three radios, which served as the sole medium for news. In winter, they wore patched cotton pants made of broadcloth, ate porridge made from weeds growing in the fields, or survived on sweet potatoes and chestnuts. Only when they sold firewood could they afford to buy food. They lived in squalor, with doors made from fertilizer sacks, floors covered with straw mats or stone slabs, and dark kitchens with mud stoves that were only whitewashed during the harvest season. The outhouse was indistinguishable from a manure pit or ash shed, and waste flowed into the courtyard, tormenting residents like cattle plagued by flies and mosquitoes.

## A. Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

### 1) Achievements in the First Year of the Saemaul Undong (事業)

Our country has four seasons, and after summer and autumn pass, and the three winters (三冬) go by, spring arrives. However, for this village, after 500 years, spring finally came with sprouting seedlings and budding hope. This was made possible by the ignition of the Saemaul Undong.

From autumn 1971 to spring 1972, the Saemaul Undong experienced dark and painful early stages while beginning to open a new chapter in history. With persistent persuasion and guidance from the government, the first task undertaken in the village was the construction of farm roads (農路) connecting scattered natural hamlets and farmlands. However, they faced numerous obstacles. Go Chang-jae was elected as the first Saemaul Undong leader to spearhead the Saemaul Undong.

However, the Saemaul Undong was not something that could be abandoned, and it was impossible to return the cement (洋灰) that had been provided to our village for the first time in history. Some people strongly advocated and insisted on solving this issue, holding a village assembly five times before finally establishing the 1971 Saemaul Undong business plan (事業計劃).

With such persistent persuasion, the villagers united under the slogan "Drive out the old village, the rotten spirit, all at once!" They constructed 2,000 meters of farm roads, 500 meters of village roads, and installed 200 meters of sewers. The total investment was 1,901,000 won, with the villagers bearing 1,775,000 won after deducting the 126,000 won worth of materials supported by the government. They completed the first year's work on May 28, 1972.

However, the difficulty in uniting the villagers' consensus to complete the first year's work is evident from the fact that the Saemaul Undong leader resigned three times, necessitating the election of new leaders.

The following year, from winter 1972 to spring 1973, with 422,000 won in government support, the villagers completed two public wells, two public laundries, 100 meters of sewers, and the renovation of 10 roofs, all with a total budget of 1,170,000 won.

### 2) Activities of the Leaders (指導者)


--- (p. 341) ---

Song Mu-ho (宋武鎬), the only college graduate (大學卒業者) in the village, had left his hometown (故鄕) and spent several years working in Daejeon (大田). In January 1974, during a holiday, he visited his hometown for the first time in a long while. Feeling guilty for having neglected his hometown, he seriously listened to the village head (里長) and a local leader (指導者) discuss the progress of the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) projects that had been undertaken.

On the night of January 6th, a village assembly (村總會) was held. During the assembly, Mr. Song shared his feelings and declared his determination to work for the betterment of his hometown. He resigned from his job and immediately became a Saemaul leader (指導者). He worked diligently with the villagers, extending and constructing 500 additional feet of village farm roads (農路), personally designing and helping to build a village community center (會館), constructing underground drainage systems, building 120 feet of stone fences, improving the roofs of 20 houses, and setting up a laundry area, among other projects.

The following year, he focused on developing the mountainous areas that made up most of the village. He planted 800 Chinese hackberry trees on the hill behind the village, as well as various other fruit trees. He also improved the roofs of 40 additional thatched houses and carried out other environmental improvement projects (環境整備事業).

Leader Song (宋) first persuaded the village head (里長) and other leading figures (指導層) in the village development committee (開發委員) to discuss the matter at a village assembly (村總會). On February 20, 1976, the assembly was held. At this meeting, Leader Song proposed a five-year plan (個年計劃) to build a bridge, the Bonggokdaegyo (鳳谷大橋), which had long been a dream of the village. Some residents (住民) opposed the plan, saying it was impossible, while most were stunned into silence. The planned bridge was a massive project (大工事), measuring 80 meters in length and 5.4 meters in width. However, undeterred by the opposition, Leader Song convinced the village leaders (指導層) to proceed with the project, and construction began on February 25, 1976.

Leader Song divided the residents (住民) into technical teams (技術者班), women's teams, 4-H clubs, boys' teams, and three construction teams (作業班). The women and 4-H club members gathered sand and gravel daily, while the other members dug the foundation and mixed concrete. The entire village participated in the construction of the bridge.

Starting in May, the work teams were divided into two shifts, working on alternate days. From June 10th, during the busy farming season (農繁期), the work teams were divided into three shifts, working two days on farming and one day on the bridge construction. Leader Song contributed 900,000 won, and Lee Gi-cheol, the village head (里長), contributed 300,000 won. The villagers also donated generously to purchase materials, and 400 bags of cement (洋灰) provided by the Dadeok County magistrate (大德郡守) were a great help.

By the end of October 1976, two piers (個) and seven bridge spans (個) were nearing completion. However, connecting the eight spans (個) seemed daunting. Although much had been accomplished that year, obtaining the massive amount of steel reinforcement (鐵筋) required seemed like a task that would take not five years, but ten.

On November 6, 1976, Congressman Kim Jae-won (金濟源) visited the construction site and praised the villagers for their hard work (勞苦). Congressman Kim said, "I came suddenly and didn't have time to prepare a big gift (膳物) for you all," and left 50,000 won. After hearing about the villagers' struggles, Congressman Kim reported the situation in detail to the governor (道知事), who provided 4 million won in special support funds (特別支援金). The county magistrate (郡守) also provided support worth 4,380,000 won.


--- (p. 342) ---

On the night of November 20th, when news of this kind spread throughout the village, the entire village gathered with torches at the worksite (作業場), playing traditional music and holding a festival (祝祭). The villagers felt as if they had completed the construction of a bridge (橋梁) since the 5-year plan (5年計劃) was achieved in less than 2 years (2年). From that moment, the villagers, filled with excitement, went to the worksite (作業場) every morning without a single complaint (不平). Women dug the frozen ground, sweating profusely, and even the elderly (老人) from the neighborhood came out to carry stones and help with the work.

One day, when reporters from the media came to cover the site, the elderly (老人) said:
"I have believed since I was young that it would be a miracle (奇蹟) if I ever saw a bridge built across this river in my lifetime. But truly, a miracle (奇蹟) has come. Once this bridge is completed, I will cross it and then I will have no regrets (餘恨) even if I die. I am truly proud to see this construction (作業) scene."

The construction (工事) progressed smoothly and finally, on May 5, 1977 (年), an 80-meter-long large bridge (大橋) was completed (完工).

With the completion (竣工) of such a bridge (橋梁), the following effects were achieved:
- Transportation (交通) became more convenient, with about 230 people and 16 vehicles passing daily, making it easier to transport agricultural products (農作物).
- Students who could not attend school (登校) due to heavy rain no longer had to worry.
- Mechanization (機械化) of farming (營農) was promoted, with the distribution of cultivators (耕耘機) and threshers (脫穀機), and the cultivation (栽培) of special crops (特殊作物) expanded (擴大).

The completion (竣工) of the bridge (橋梁) and the promotion of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) thus far have been supported by encouragement and comfort from various sectors, and the residents have also donated their front yards (門前沃畓) and cash (現金) without hesitation for the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement).

## 6) Heartwarming Stories (美談佳話)

Every harvest season (秋收期), a village without a threshing machine (脫穀機) would have its crops (農事) threshed (脫穀) by a neighboring village (他部落) using a tractor (耕耘機), and the village would receive a high threshing fee (脫穀料) of 10%. Feeling sorry about this, Mr. Lee Jong-rook donated 1 million won (100만원) from his personal funds (私財) in July 1997 to purchase a tractor (耕耘機) and a threshing machine (脫穀機), which he donated (喜捨) to the village. The villagers, moved by this gesture, celebrated (自祝) the unexpected joyous event (慶事) and were filled with enthusiasm (意欲) to do something for the village. During the threshing season (脫穀時), they would happily and gratefully thresh (脫穀) the crops with a low threshing fee (脫穀料) of 3%, which was added to the village fund (마을基金), making everyone even happier.

### 8) Special Items (特記事項)

#### a) Pleasant Events
On February 20, 1976, when I proposed building an 80-meter-long bridge across the Gamcheon Stream, some residents (住民) said it was impossible and others were stunned into silence. Persuaded by the argument that we could not leave our descendants the same conditions we had endured for 500 years, and with support from the authorities (官), we began the massive construction on February 25, 1976, with the determination to complete it successfully. On May 5, 1977, we held a grand completion ceremony for the historic 80-meter-long, 5.4-meter-wide bridge, attended by all the villagers and many dignitaries who had supported our Saemaul Undong and bridge project. Amid the envious glances of people from other villages, I felt deeply moved alongside the entire village.

### 1) Spiritual Aspect (精神面)

*   Through Saemaul projects (事業), a new human image (人間像) was established, characterized by diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), cooperation (協同), and unity (團結);
*   It was realized that when residents (住民) engage in dialogue (對話) and understand (理解) reality (現實), they can be persuaded (說得) to join the glorious ranks (榮光) of the Saemaul Movement (事業) voluntarily (自發的);
*   A sense of gratitude (感謝) towards the nation (祖國) and neighbors (이웃) was fostered;
*   It was understood that with effort (努力) and patience (忍耐), anything can be achieved, instilling a sense of confidence (自信感).

### 2) Livelihood Aspect (生活面)

*   Bridge construction (橋梁架設) and the development of farm roads (農路) and village paths facilitated the transportation (出荷) of agricultural products (農作物), promoting the expansion (擴大) of specialized farming (特殊栽培);
*   Improvements in farming techniques (營農技術) and the purchase of farming machinery (營農機械) enhanced productivity (能率), transforming farmers (農民) into proactive (進取的) individuals who study (工夫) and research (硏究);
*   A culture of thrift (勤儉) and savings (節約) was cultivated;
*   A spirit of mutual aid (互助) emerged, where helping those in need (不遇) was seen as a way to improve one's own well-being (氣風).

### ◆ Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (1)

*   Date (日時): 72.1.31.
*   Location (場所): Below the house of Mr. Gosugil
*   Agenda (議提): Farm Road Development (農路開設)
*   Attendees (參席人員): Lee Seong-ju and 52 others (名)
*   Chairperson (社會者): Leader (指導者)


--- (p. 346) ---

Host: I am terribly sorry, everyone. Today's meeting (會議) is because the path from the outer village to the inner village, which is about 2 km long, is too narrow to pass through. We have gathered you here to discuss widening the path and establishing a farm road (農路). I hope you will understand.

Lee Jong-jin: To widen the farm road (農路), won't we need to take up a lot of the farmland (田畓) on both sides of the path?

Host: We must be prepared for that.

Yoon Cheol-joong: What? You say "that's all"? How can we farm if we give up our ancestral farmland (田畓) to widen the path?

Lee Seong-ju (Ri-jang): Yoon, think about this: if we widen the path, we can pull carts and drive cars. And you can take sheaves of rice directly from your field to your home. Isn't that convenient?

Hwang Bong-jo: That's right. Other villages are all making farm roads (農路) and widening paths, so we can't just sit here and watch.

Host: Yes, I passed by the neighboring village of Yasil yesterday, and even the distant mountain roads were being turned into farm roads (農路). Moreover, it's the off-season for farming (農閑期) now, and there isn't much to do. Not much farmland (田畓) will be taken up. As much as possible, we will use the mountains, and only where necessary will we slightly widen the areas that must include farmland (田畓). Please understand and agree.

Park Chan-gap: Well, everyone has good ideas, but I think we shouldn't debate (曰可曰否) here and now. The Ri-jang (里長) and leaders (指導者) should consult and find a way to avoid taking up farmland (田畓) as much as possible. Today, let's just discuss whether or not to make the farm road (農路).

Villagers: That's right. It's already late at night, and arguing won't solve anything. Let's just discuss whether to make the farm road (農路) or not.

Host: Then, everyone, what do you think? I suggest we proceed with making the farm road (農路). Tomorrow, the Ri-jang (里長) and I will survey the site (現地) and personally ask for understanding (諒解) from those whose farmland (田畓) will be affected. Please grant your permission (許諾).

Villagers: Alright.

Host: Then, we will make the farm road (農路). Now, when should we start the work (作業)?

Yoon Cheol-joong: I absolutely cannot compromise! I'm sorry, but I must go and get some sleep now. (Exits (退場))

Host: Those who wish to leave may do so. Please discuss among those who remain and decide when to start the work (作業).

Hwang Bong-jo: Let's start the work (作業) on February 5th after the site survey (踏査) is completed tomorrow.

Host: What do the others think?

Villagers: Let's do that.

Host: Then, how should we divide the work teams (作業班)?

Park Chan-yong: It would be best to alternate between the outer village and the inner village every other day (隔日制) for duty (出役).


--- (p. 347) ---

Host: I agree with that. What do others think?
Village Head: First, on the first day, please come out to the outer work site. Children under 18 cannot participate, so please have as many young adults come out as possible.
Villagers: Let's do that. (Agreement)
Host: Then, those who come to the work site, please bring hoes, shovels, carrying poles, and rakes.
Villagers: Understood.
Village Head: I will prepare the list of participants for each work team and post it on the bulletin board.
Leader: Then, we will conclude today's meeting. Sorry for keeping you late. Good night.

## Meeting Minutes (會議錄)(2)
Date: November 16, 1972
Venue: Mill House
Agenda: Formulation of 1973 Saemaul Undong Business Plan
Attendees: 62 people
Host: Saemaul Leader

Host: I called this late meeting because I wanted to hear the opinions of the elders in the neighborhood regarding the preparation of the 1973 Saemaul beautification business plan. I apologize for the late hour.
Song Jin-ok: If that's the case, why don't you just consult with the village head and get things done? Why call us out late at night?
Village Head: It's not that. We have received 500 bags of cement and 1 ton of rebar for next year's Saemaul Undong, but although there are countless things to do in our neighborhood, we should prioritize the most urgent tasks, shouldn't we? If the leader and I prepare the business plan, people might start complaining right in front of my house and refuse to work. That's why I thought if we prepare the business plan here with everyone present, no one would object. I apologize for the inconvenience.
Host: As the village head just said, since we have the materials for the Saemaul beautification project, shouldn't we first prepare a business plan and report it to the town mayor to be able to carry out the Saemaul Undong? Please share your thoughts in order of priority. First, mention the projects that require cement, and then share the projects that can be done without support.
Ju Young-no: In my opinion, it would be best to first build the sewer system in the outer area.
Ko Chang-jae: Rather than that, it would be better to first cement the well to prevent dirty water from entering. We should prioritize two things: one in the outer area and one in the inner area.
Lee Jong-jin: In my opinion, it would also be good to build two laundries so that women can do their laundry without inconvenience. Let's leave the unsupported business plan to the village head and the leader.


--- (p. 348) ---

Host: That is a wonderful idea. I agree with you. What do you all think?
Villagers: I agree. It's good.
Host: Then, I will summarize what you have just said and report it to the village office as part of the 1973 Saemaul Undong project plan. To summarize, we need one sewer, two wells, two laundry areas, etc. We will conduct a field survey with the village head tomorrow to determine the detailed items and project locations, and then decide on the project scope. Does anyone object?
Villager: No objections.
Village Head: Then, let's tentatively set next year's project plan. Before the weather gets too cold, we need to transport materials such as sand and gravel for the 500 bags of cement we plan to use. Once the project plan is finalized, we will form a work team to excavate the materials, so please understand.
Host: Then, we will conclude today's meeting. Please go home safely.

# Minutes of Meeting (會議錄) (3)

*   **Date** : February 4, 1973
*   **Location** : Kim Yong-ju's living room
*   **Agenda** : Paving the village road and promoting concurrent projects
*   **Attendees** : 38 people
*   **Host** : Saemaul Undong Leader

Host: Today's meeting will first discuss bringing stones to the widened village road and piling them up. If we leave them as is, the road keeps getting narrower. Additionally, we need to complete the concurrent projects before the farming season. That's why I asked everyone to come today. I would like to hear your opinions and proceed with the work.
Yuk Geun-seok: Where are we going to bring all those stones from?
Host: For now, we will gather the large stones discarded around the village and collect them from the hill behind. That's all we can do.
Lee Jong-sung: Stones are one thing, but when will we start the concurrent projects?
Host: On the days when everyone doesn't come, please work on repairing your courtyards, walls, etc., at home and finish everything before the farming season. The village head and our village guidance officer also instructed us to promote the concurrent projects quickly as they were leaving today.
Lee Jae-sung: How much of the village road needs to be paved with stones?

### 4. Future Development Plans (發展構想)

*   In 1978, we plan to utilize 200 hectares of extensive forests to mass-plant fruit trees such as persimmons, chestnuts, and peaches, creating a demonstration complex, while also raising at least 3 head of Hanwoo per household to develop and promote the village as a demonstration livestock village.
*   By utilizing reservoirs to attract agritourism, we aim for an average of 3 million won per household in the 1980s, with all residents cooperating to promote this plan.
*   In 1979, we will improve the village structure to cultivate a cultural and welfare-oriented rural community.

# Chungcheongnam-do (충남) Yeongi County (연기군) Jeondong-myeon (전동면) Yanggok-ri (양곡리) (Yangchon (양촌))

### 1. Village Overview

#### a. History

During the Three Kingdoms period, this area was part of Baekje's territory. In the reign of King Gyeongdeok of Silla, the administrative division (府) was abolished, and the area became part of the present-day Cheonwon County (천원군), belonging to the Yeongi region. Later, it was separated into Soseo-myeon (소서면) of Jeonui County (전의군). In 1914, during the county merger, the then 10 villages of Nam-myeon (남면) and 6 villages of Soseo-myeon (소서면) were combined to form the present-day Jeondong-myeon (전동면) Yanggok-ri (양곡리) village. About 600 years ago, Jeon Seogong (전서공), the sixth-generation ancestor of the Andong Kim clan (안동 김씨), settled at the sunny slope of Geumseong Mountain (금성산), part of the Jaryeong Mountain Range (차령산맥), and the village was called Yangchon (양촌). After the village settled in the valley of Geumseong Mountain (금성산), it was renamed Yanggok-ri (양곡리). Currently, the Andong Kim clan (안동 김씨) forms the largest clan in the village.

#### b. Conditions

- The village is composed of 5 natural hamlets (자연부락) in a mountainous area, with Yangji Village (양지촌) as the central village.
- The village is traversed by Jocheoncheon (조천천), a stream that flows through the center of the hamlet. The stream, 40 meters wide, runs parallel to the farmland and is 1.5 kilometers long.
- The village is surrounded by high mountains with slopes of 40~65 degrees. Agriculture is relatively developed, and the village earns high income from cultivating red peppers.

## 2. Village Development Process (發展過程)

### 가. Development Situation Before the 1970s (70년대(年代) 이전(以前)의 개발상황(開發狀況))

#### 1) Basic Environment (基礎環境)
Since the village was located at the foot of a mountain, winding paths stretched for 1km with about 60 thatched-roof houses on one side. Most of these houses had no walls or gates, and many were dilapidated with roofs almost touching the ground. The tilted thatched roofs were overgrown with weeds and mushrooms, and when rain or snow melted, red water would flow down, staining hair and clothing. There were no farm roads, not even a path leading into the village. At the village entrance stood a 300-year-old oak tree (a zelkova tree), beneath which the village's discarded waste and items deemed "useless" by households were piled up on tangled ropes, startling children who passed by late at night. This unremarkable village was once called "Dongtu" Pass.

#### 2) Income Level (所得水準)
For generations, the village had inherited only 66ha of farmland, consisting of 42ha of dry fields and 24ha of paddy fields. Rice farming in the paddy fields yielded about one bushel (石) per 200 pyeong (坪) of land, while dry field farming was challenging due to the scarcity of seeds. With a per household cultivated land area of 0.7ha, the annual income per household was around 250,000 won (萬圓). This village had the lowest income level in the region, struggling with debt that it could not repay to other villages.


--- (p. 358) ---

3) Culture and Living Standards

- Income Levels in the 1970s

| District | Category | Project Scale | Production Volume | Income | Remarks |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| | Vegetables (蔬菜) | 5 | 60 | 6,000 | |

- Residents of this area lived without electricity, relying on oil lamps. Struggling to make ends meet, they could not afford a humane life. In this village, where even a single newspaper or magazine was a luxury, radios were scarce, and the few clocks they had were broken, covered in dust, and hanging on the mud walls. The village women, unaware of the time, would call out to their children playing outside in the evenings, asking, "How much of the sun is left?" before starting to prepare dinner. In winter, wearing cotton-padded clothes dyed black with military blankets wrapped around them was considered high-class.

- In summer, they wore patched work clothes indistinguishable from railroad ties. Men carried wooden loads to the town to sell for food, and women gathered wild greens in the spring to supplement their diet. Upon entering their homes, one would find straw mats or rush mats laid out, with children rolling around on the floor covered in filth, like moles. In the dark kitchen, like a burrow, earthworms would wriggle under the water pails, and the outhouse made of thatch or old sacks, along with the livestock shed, tormented the villagers with flies and mosquitoes. They lived without shame or sorrow, as if this were their destiny.

4) Consciousness Structure

- Living in ignorance and poverty, they had never even considered the idea of living better. Without unity, they spent their days drinking and gambling, indifferent to the world. On market days in the town, they would be found drunk, collapsed anywhere, or fighting, earning the village the reputation of "Yangjichon (陽地村)" or "Manosil." These residents, who frequented the town's outreach office due to fights, lawsuits, and gambling, showed no hope or pioneering spirit for the future. They lived with apathy, expressionless, and lazy consciousness.

The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) Promotion

1) Development Motivation and Experimental Project Achievements

- On December 10, 1969, men gathered in Kim Jae-won's (金在員) living room, spreading out elaborately illustrated playing cards.


--- (p. 359) ---

When looking at the quilts of housewives (主婦), as clean and fluffy as a dowry (婚需) blanket, one feels like lying down on them once. On top of these quilts, there are about 40 sheets of paper money (紙錢), and eyes are focused on the cards being shuffled. "Head of the village (里長)! We're doing dry wood," they say, offering a share and inviting me to play together. Holding the five cards I was dealt, I was bewildered, but with a shout of "Here it comes," money changes hands as the cards are thrown down. I thought that this had a gambling nature (賭博性), but Kim Jae-min realized that "Head of the village (里長), if you're good, you can do several loads of wood." I now understood that the earlier mention of dry wood referred to this. "Then what about the person who loses? They can't do it," I said. No one knows who will win or lose, but it's a strange trick where you have to cry if you don't laugh. Kim Jae-won, who lost money, provided the room and withdrew with an annoyed expression as his money ran out. Watching this, I realized that gambling is about abandoning people and squandering property (財產) with playing cards (化圖). After that, I advised those who enjoyed playing cards (化圖) to not waste our precious time (時間) in dissipation (放湯) but to engage in constructive (建設的) and fulfilling activities that would bring light (光明) to our descendants (後孫) and let us live well for once. However, it seems that no one responded or reflected on this.

○ From that time on, I visited rooms where neighbors (洞里) gathered and engaged in conversations (對話) about improving our village. Whenever I visited the elders, I would light a cigarette for them and say, "Have a smoke." The elderly would say, "How can you give such expensive cigarettes (卷煙)? Thank you," and for a moment, their wrinkled faces would break into a smile. "Grandfather, what do you think about the rest of your life (餘生)?" "What can I think? When I consider that in my youth I spent each day in anxiety (不安) under the domination (支配) of the Japanese," tears would flow. I took out a handkerchief from my pocket to wipe away the flowing tears and said, "Grandfather, you must live a long and healthy life (健康)." "Yes, yes, thank you. But I, an old man, don't know if what the country is doing now is good. You young people must do well so that you don't lose to the Japanese," he said, holding my hand. "I'm asking for your opinion on how to live well. Grandfather, please cooperate (協助) with the young people." "Young Head of the village (里長) Seung-hoe comes late at night to complain to us old people, but if it's something we all need to do, I will cooperate in spirit. Don't worry and give it a try," he said.

○ The first project we started was the construction (開設) of a farm road (農路), which was too large in scale (規模) and caused much deliberation (골몰) due to land donations (土地 喜捨). Every time we reduced the fields, there were fights, and the work (作業) was interrupted. At times like this, if I went back to the landowner (土地 主人) and spoke again, the response "I don't know" was painful to hear.

◦ After overcoming such adversity (逆境), a planned 1km farm road (農路) was completed in 47 days, and the residents (住民) were filled with satisfaction. However, the construction (架設) of a bridge (橋梁) remained. On January 6, 1971, we visited Yu Ung-yeol (柳雄烈), the magistrate (郡守) of Eongi County (燕岐郡), to request that if the residents' (住民) self-reliance (自力) was insufficient for the long-desired project (宿願 事業) of building a 40m bridge (橋梁) in front of the village, the county (郡) would complete it.

O The effect (効果) is that 66 households (世代) with 132 students (學生) can commute (往來) even in rainy weather (雨天時). The planned self-funded amount (自體 資金) is 540,000 won, with 240,000 won already deposited in the Head of the village's (里長) account as the main project fund (本事業 資金), and the remaining 300,000 won is to be raised (造成) within 10 days. However, I was worried if it would be completed (完工). The magistrate (郡守) said, "If it's a 40m bridge (橋梁), the construction cost (工事費) is


--- (p. 360) ---

With over one million won needed, Chairman Kim (金里長) is indeed a great person. "I understand the ideology of this young village head. I will help as much as I can," he said, patting my shoulder in encouragement. His words gave me even more strength.

Having gained courage, I posted the contents resolved at the Yangjichon Village Development Committee (開發委員會) on the bulletin board (揭示板) so that the fund-raising promotion committee (資金造成推進委員) could collect the money. However, the amount required was so enormous that it was like throwing stones into the Han River (漢江). The residents continued to sit around the tavern (酒幕), spending their days complaining and criticizing.

On April 22, 1971, when I heard the news that the "Saemaul Undong (運動)" initiated by President Park Chung-hee (朴正熙大統領) was spreading across the country like a spark in the darkness, I was deep in thought, wondering if it would reach our village as well. Just then, the government provided 336 bags of cement as a trial project (試驗事業), solving the material problem for bridge construction (橋梁架設). The residents, now united, were eager to proceed with the bridge construction (橋梁作業), even lighting torches and rushing to complete the work. Men, women, and children alike were of one mind.

However, they believed that as long as they cooperated and united, their desired bridge (橋梁) would be realized, without considering technical guidance (技術指導面). Even those who had opposed the project gathered in the square (廣場), sharing large cups of wine under the setting sun (夕陽).

On August 9, 1972, the residents gathered at the site for the completion ceremony (竣工式). From the elderly Mr. Kim Haemuk (長壯老人) to the youngest, they stood in line, looking at the straight path leading into the village. The residents' shouts of joy echoed through the mountains. Our village of Yangjichon (陽地村) firmly resolved to take the lead over neighboring villages with a sense of accomplishment and to continue advancing. In 1972, after being promoted from a basic village (基礎村) to a self-help village (自助村), we opened a new chapter in history as an independent village (自立村), with the leader (指導者) at the center, achieving democratic totality (民主總和).

2) Leader Election (指導者選出) and Activity Status (活動狀況)

Current leader Kim Seung-hui (金承會), after graduating from Cheonan Agricultural High School (天安農高), followed his parents' will (遺志) and engaged in agriculture (農業). In March 1966, he was appointed village head (里長) and has been striving for village development (開發) ever since. With the start of the Saemaul Undong (運動) in 1971, he volunteered to become a Saemaul leader (指導者職) and has continued his efforts for village development (開發).

It cannot be denied that the transformation of a backward village, plagued by poverty, ignorance, gambling, and drunkenness, into the best village in Yeongi County (燕岐郡) is the crystallization of Kim Seung-hui's (金指導者) determination (執念).

Before the start of the Saemaul project (事業), he opened a 1km agricultural road (農路), laying the foundation for development (發展基盤). He also completed a 40m-long bridge (延長40m의橋梁), a long-cherished project (宿願事業), through self-help efforts (自力事業). This united the residents (住民) and utilized their unity (團結力) to promote environmental improvement (環境改善事業) and income-increasing projects (所得增大事業). This was the result of his unwavering belief (信念) and continuous, planned efforts (計劃性있게實踐한). Behind this were the leader's (指導者) relentless efforts, sacrificing his youth (靑春) and even his private funds (私財), to embody and perpetuate (永續化) the Saemaul spirit (精神) in daily life (生活化).

His activities, dedicating 12 years—5 years as village head (里長) and 7 years as leader (指導者)—to the ideal of rural development (理想農村育成), are evident in today's Yanggok-ri (陽谷里).

3) Overcoming Difficulties (隘路克服狀況)

After volunteering to become a Saemaul leader (指導者), I thought that to foster the residents' (住民) cooperative spirit (協同心) and participation awareness (參與意識), we should first start with communal work (共同作業) such as farm roads (農路) and village paths (村內길). Breathing together with the residents (住民), I surveyed the village conditions (部落與件) and found that the village was burdened with agricultural cooperative (農協) debts (債務), and in the evenings, they played Hwatu (화투)


--- (p. 361) ---

Of course, the leader tried to develop the spirit of the people through understanding and persuasion, but they remained indifferent. The leader visited each household to persuade them, but no one responded, and he alone worked tirelessly.

Mr. Kim, the leader, eventually went to the elders of the village, explained the situation, and pleaded for their help in improving their lives. A village meeting was held, and unusually, many residents attended. They discussed and decided on the village development plan, but a few days later, when the road expansion project began, they encountered obstacles.

An 80-year-old man lay down in front of the workers, refusing to let them take his land, saying, "Is this new community movement about taking other people's land?" Despite several incidents where they had to restrain him to continue the work, they eventually completed the 1km access road after 47 days of hard work. This is an unforgettable achievement.

The village planned to build a bridge across the Jocheon Stream in front of the village, a long-cherished project with a width of 5m and a length of 40m. They started the construction with 6 million won of their own funds out of the total construction cost of 30 million won and tried to persuade the residents to contribute funds, but they were ignored. Unable to give up on the bridge, they sought help from outsiders, collected donations, and even pledged village property, but it was all in vain. Upon learning that the large-scale bridge project had been initiated solely through the cooperation and enthusiasm of the residents, Yun Ung-yeol, the county magistrate, visited the site, encouraged and promised to support them. This gave them the courage to proceed. The 335 bags of cement provided as a trial project for the Saemaul Undong played a crucial role in the successful construction of the bridge and ignited the Saemaul Undong in Yanggok-ri.

### 5) Heartwarming Stories (美談) Anecdotes (佳話)

#### a) First Story (第1話)

In a remote mountain village, the Saemaul Undong (運動) was ignited to create a foundation for development. However, the road expansion project faced difficulties due to land issues. The Saemaul leader Kim Seung-hoe (金承會) donated his own farmland of 400 pyeong to the village for road and warehouse construction, inspiring all residents to willingly donate their land. This turned the project into a success.

#### b) Second Story (第2話)

Efforts to bring the light of progress through rural telephone services were hampered by the residents' inability to bear the financial burden. The Saemaul leader met with Mrs. B.M. Zaret, the chairperson of the American veterans' organization CARE. Moved by the leader's account of the village's development and future plans, Mrs. Zaret provided 14 million won to electrify five remote villages, centering around Yanggok-ri. On the day of the inauguration, when the previously unimaginable electric lights came on, all the residents rejoiced and expressed their gratitude to Mrs. Zaret.


--- (p. 363) ---

## 7) Special Notes (特記 事項)

### a) Joyful Events (즐거웠던 일)

* Before the Saemaul Undong began, the day the village access road construction was completed after negotiating for 67 plots of land totaling 2,100 pyeong of farmland, and the 1km agricultural road was opened.
* After the electric lighting ceremony sponsored by Mrs. B.M. Jarett, Chairperson of the American Legion Auxiliary, when we saw villagers watching TV by electric light, having previously lived like frogs in a well in darkness.
* The overwhelming emotion when, instead of carrying sacks of rice far away to the collective market, we first stored 3,000 sacks in the newly established 50 pyeong communal warehouse as part of the cooperative business.

### b) Sad Events (슬펐던 일)

* During the promotion of the bridge construction project, which was a long-cherished goal, when heavy rain caused many materials to be washed away, I felt resentment towards heaven.
* It was sad when, after going to the site at midnight to rescue the bridge construction materials feared to be washed away by heavy rain, I survived a dramatic fall of about 50m but ended up in a hospital bed with injuries.

## La. Achievements (成果) Due to Saemaul Undong (新村運動)

### 1) Spiritual Aspect (精神面)

Through the Saemaul Undong (新村運動), people were transformed into new human beings characterized by diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperation (協同). The guiding ideology of "If you do it, it can be done" helped people gain self-confidence (自身感). Through village assemblies (住民總會), people experienced Korean-style democracy (韓國的民主主義) firsthand and developed a sense of gratitude (感謝) toward the nation (祖國) and awareness of their neighbors. The Saemaul Undong (新村運動) became a creed (信條) that people truly experienced and internalized.

### 2) Livelihood Aspect (生活面)

○ With the reform (改革) of agricultural (營農) techniques (技術), seed (種子) renewal (更新), and the expansion (擴大) of Hanwoo (韓牛) breeding (增殖) projects (事業), farmers' income (所得) increased. Farmers became more proactive (進取的) in studying (工夫) and researching (硏究). Through thrift (勤儉節約), they saved (貯蓄) and helped their less fortunate (不偶) neighbors, understanding that the well-being (다 잘 사는) of everyone around them was essential to their own well-being (내가 잘 사는). They put this understanding into practice (實踐).


--- (p. 366) ---

## 3) Production Aspect (生産面)

*   Income (所得) improved through the expanded cultivation (擴大栽培) of unified (統一) rice varieties (系統 벼의 확대(擴大) 재배(栽培)), and residents' income (住民의 소득(所得)) doubled with the introduction (事業) of Hanwoo (韓牛) cattle breeding (增殖) funded by government subsidies (下賜金(下賜金)).
