## 3. Residents' Assembly (住民總會)

◆ Meeting Minutes (會議錄)(1)

*   Date (日) and Time (時): July 3, 1968
*   Venue (場所): Kim Seung-hee's house living room
*   Agenda (議題): Construction (建立) of government (政府) grain (糧穀) storage warehouse (保管倉庫)
*   Attendees (參席人員): Kim Jae-woo and 37 others
*   Absentees (不參者): Kim Shin-jang and 41 others
*   Chairperson (司會者): Village head (里長) Kim Seung-hoe

Chairperson (司會者): I apologize for convening this meeting at night during the busy farming season (農繁期). First, I would like to discuss the government's (政府) grain (糧穀) public market (共販場).

Every year (每年), around autumn, you all have to carry your grain (糧穀) on your backs for 6 km to the purchasing station (收買場所) in Jeonui (全義) to have it inspected (檢査), which is quite strenuous (苦生).

Therefore, we plan to build a grain (糧穀) storage warehouse (保管倉庫) in Yanggok-ri (糧穀里), the central village (中心地). Of course (勿論), constructing it requires funds (資金) and labor (勞力), so we have convened this meeting to discuss fund-raising (造成) and labor mobilization (動員).

What do you all think about establishing a public market (共販場) by first building a government (政府) grain (糧穀) storage warehouse (保管倉庫)?

Kim Myeong-gi (金命基): Should I alone do what the whole village (洞네) is supposed to do together? Am I the only one who should agree (贊成)?

Chairperson (議長): Brother Myeong-gi (命基), please do not think (生覺) so simply (簡單). We should discuss (議論) this matter together (다 같이). You should not speak (말씀) like that.


--- (p. 367) ---

Kim Jae-woo: If we borrow money to build it, how will we pay it back?
Host: If we build a 30-pyeong warehouse, we can store 2,500 kama. I don't know the exact storage fee, but it seems like it will be settled in about three years with the storage fees. That means the storage fee would be around 300,000 won.
Lee Soon-bae: What if we can't pay it back in three years? It would take four years, right? So let's build it.
Host: Yes, that's sufficient.
Kim In-muk: Let those who want to do it, do it. I don't like doing things with many people.
Kim Yoon-muk: No, the village head's idea is correct. We're not borrowing money now; we're taking a loan from the agricultural cooperative. The villagers just need to contribute labor for a few days. It's the most idle season right now, so let's do it.
Kim Jae-gu: Enough talking. Since the village head is suggesting it, let's try it. We'll make sure the villagers don't have to pay anything.
Lee Sang-mun: I don't need it. I'm out! If I starve, will the village head feed me?
Host: It seems you all are not thinking about this properly. If we hold a public auction in our village, the transportation cost won't be high because it's close by, which will increase our income. After paying off the debt, it will become the village's property. So, please decide today evening whether we should do it or not.
Kim Myeong-gi: I can't answer here today because not all villagers are present.
Kim In-muk: I feel the same way.
Host: It seems we won't be able to conclude today. Please go home and think about it well. This is a project that must be accomplished in our village. Although we couldn't reach an agreement, the goal is for all residents to live well.
Kim Yoon-muk: There's a lot to say, but if even a few people can do it, let's discuss it with the village head among those present here.
Kim Jae-gu: Yoon-muk is right. There's a saying, "You might as well try," so let's do it.
Kim Yoon-muk: I agree with that.
Host: Some of you who understand my intention are worried and can't even leave. I'm worried too. Then, apart from the village head, seven of us will write a petition to the county magistrate. If the project goes through, the seven of us will take full responsibility. After three years, when the debt is paid off, we can hand it over to the village to create village property.
Kim Yoon-muk and five others: That's fine.
Host: Then, the village head will handle this issue starting tomorrow. With that, I conclude the meeting.

1968. 7. 3.
Representatives: Kim Seung-hee, Kim Yoon-muk, Lee Soon-bae, Gil Jae-gu, Gil Gwan-hoe, Gil Jae-min, Gil Jae-dong.


--- (p. 368) ---

# Minutes (會議錄) (2)

**Agenda(議案):** New Road Construction (農路開設) - 1km Addition
**Date(日時):** January 28, 1970
**Location(場所):** Kim Seung-hee's Living Room
**Attendees(參席者):** Kim Jae-gil and 27 others
**Absentees(不參者):** Im Wan-bok and 37 others
**Chairperson(司會者):** Village Head Kim Seung-hoe

**Chairperson:** I apologize for convening this meeting on such a cold and dark night. The purpose of today's meeting is to discuss the construction of new roads, specifically the road leading to the farmlands and the road beneath the hill. First, I must inform all landowners that their cooperation is essential for this project. No collective development can be achieved without individual sacrifices. In the future, we will continue to improve our village roads during the farming off-season, year by year.

**Kim Gwan-mok:** So, you're saying we're supposed to clear the roads without any compensation for the land?

**Chairperson:** Yes, where would we get the money for land compensation? Besides, if we build roads in various places, almost every villager will be affected. Therefore, if we all understand and cooperate, we can create straight roads that will make it easier to transport goods by oxcart or wheelbarrow, which will in turn contribute to the continuous development of our village.

**Kim Gwan-mok:** How wide are you planning to make these roads?

**Chairperson:** We plan to make them approximately 4 meters wide.

**Kim Gwan-mok:** You're insane! What do we need roads that wide for? If it's just two shovel lengths, I could understand, but four is just too wide and will take up too much land.

**Kim Seong-hui's Mother:** Whoever dares to touch my land will suffer from resentment and die from it. No one is allowed to even approach my land.

**Kim Yoon-mok:** Instead of just saying it can't be done, let's listen to what the village head has to say. In the future, we will need to build access roads to our village and roads within it, as well as farm roads. If we build all of them, there will be no one whose farmland is not affected. Of course, some will be affected more than others. But my farmland will also be affected just as much as anyone else's. I publicly declare this in front of everyone. Village Head, when it comes time to build these roads, I won't complain about how much land I'm losing, no matter how many magoji (approx. 0.1 acre) it is. So, go ahead and get the consent of the other villagers.

**Kim Bong-deul:** Of course, Yoon-mok may have a lot of farmland, but I can't spare that much of my land.

**Kim Jae-u:** Uncle, do you plan to spend your entire life farming with just a carrying pole? Even your son, "Jae-il," has said that if he can't farm properly, he won't farm at all, and certainly not with just a carrying pole. Besides, you can't guarantee that you'll own that land for the rest of your life and continue to farm it. So, please stop complaining and let the village head widen the village roads.


--- (p. 369) ---

Let us not say that we cannot farm in this way and that vehicles cannot enter our village. Let us not just say it cannot be done.

Moderator: Please be quiet for a moment!

Currently, Kim Jae-u and three others have agreed to have their land included. I expect about 200 pyeong of my own field to be included as well, and I consent to this. I would like to inform my fellow villagers that I will mark the center line so that both sides of the field can be included equally. Please do not request that the land donation be on one side for easier work. I will plant two shovel lengths of stakes on either side of the line I have marked.

I earnestly request that the landowners please donate their land.

Kim Jae-gil: If we widen the road equally on both sides, it will be winding, and somewhere it will have to be narrowed to one side to be manageable. Kim Cheon-hee, what do you think about that corner over there?

Kim Cheon-hee: Uncle, if only my field around here is included, that's fine. Please allow your field instead, Uncle.

Kim Jae-gil: If you say so, I will allow my field as well.

Kim Gwan-muk: In any case, most have agreed, so the village head should just mark the line as he sees fit. If the marked line is unfair, we cannot proceed.

Village Head: Yes! Thank you.

I would like to speak to the landowners once more. Please truly understand and support the ongoing road construction. This is not a road that only Village Head Seung-hui uses or a road that someone else provides. It is a road to be passed down to our descendants and a source of pride for our village. If the villagers actively cooperate with the village head's work, I will undertake various tasks. Do you have any objections regarding the land for the two farm road construction sites this time? If there are any objections, I will apologize a hundred times, but please cooperate so that the planned projects can be carried out continuously.

Thanks to your cooperation until late at night, the development committee and I will plant stakes at the site, so please be aware of this.

Village Attendees Representatives: Kim Seung-hee, Kim Jae-pil, Kim Gwan-muk, Kim Seong-hee, Kim Yun-muk, Kim Bong-deul, Kim Jae-u.

## Minutes of the Meeting (會議錄) (3)

*   Agenda (議題): Purchase of Saemaul Plaza (購入)
*   Date (日時): February 9, 1972
*   Location (場所): Ijang Kim Seung-hee's Residence
*   Attendees: Kim Yun-muk and 47 others
*   Absentees (不參者): Kim Jae-gu and 19 others
*   Moderator: Village Head Kim Seung-hee

Moderator: Today, it will be difficult to do other work as it is snowing heavily, and we also have urgent administrative directives for the village to address.


--- (p. 370) ---

Let's secure a Saemaul Plaza of at least 100 pyeong (330 m²) in our village as well, as it has been mandated. This is an urgent matter as the government and Congressman Kim Jae-won are likely to provide children's play facilities in the future. Let's discuss this.

**Kim Yoon-muk**: If it's a Saemaul Plaza, it would be best to secure it within the village. Are there any suitable locations?
**Kim Shin-hee**: Will the residents bear the purchase costs, or will the government provide support?
**Moderator**: The land purchase costs will be borne by the residents. The neighborhood will secure funds through a fundraising campaign.
**Kim Yoon-muk**: Kim Shin-hee, why don't you purchase it alone and donate it to the village?
**Kim Shin-hee**: I can't even afford to donate if I have to fundraise.
**Lee Sun-bae**: Giving or not giving is decided by the neighborhood association's resolution. Are you, Shin-hee, the only one who won't cooperate with the resolution? Don't even joke like that.
**Lee Sang-moon**: First, let's plan the budget.
**Moderator**: We need to secure the land first, as the budget depends on the value of the property.
**Kim Min-muk**: You're all crazy. How can we, who are struggling to make a living, buy a new village plaza and beg for money?
**Moderator**: That's not the case. If our Saemaul Undong succeeds, it will contribute to national economic development. If things continue as they are, we might as well give up on the world. The government will provide each village with a Saemaul Plaza and install play equipment for children to grow up healthily.
**Kim Jae-soo**: The government is also doing crazy things! What is this?
**Moderator**: Everyone, please don't say anything. It's our duty to study and cooperate in the right direction. Now, please suggest a good location.
**Kim Jae-woo**: How much land does Kim Jae-jung's paddy field next to Kim Jae-soo's house have? Why don't we buy that?
**Moderator**: Please, another suggestion.
**Lee Sang-moon**: That paddy field seems fine, but I don't know if it's for sale.
**Moderator**: As Kim Jae-woo and Lee Sang-moon mentioned, the only paddy field along the village road gets very muddy when it rains, which is not ideal. If we purchase and tidy up that location, it will be good for the village, clean, and suitable as a Saemaul Plaza.
**All villagers (同民一同)**: Please handle it, village chief.
**Moderator**: Alright. How much will the land cost?
**Kim Pan-muk**: I sold that land. It was 94 pyeong and 12 hop (312 m²) at the time, but the price may have changed now.


--- (p. 371) ---

Host: Then, we will proceed with the land price and rice payment of 12 sacks of rice per unit area.
We kindly ask for your cooperation in providing an average of 2 do of rice per household.
With this, we conclude the meeting. Moving forward, this work will be carried out under the leadership of the vice-captain.
February 9, 1972
Signed by the resident representatives

### Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (4)
Agenda: Expansion of Yangjichon Access Road
Date: January 18, 1972
Location: Kim Seung-hui's Ijang's Sarangbang
Attendees: Kim Jin-hee and 37 others
Absentees: Kim Jae-cheol and 4 others
Host: Ijang Kim Seung-hui

Host: Thank you for your efforts in coming here on this dark night.
The agenda for today's evening meeting is to plan the expansion work from the bridge area to the front of Kim Gwan-hee's house.
There should be no issues with the area we will be working on this time, except for Kim Myeong-gi's compost pit.
Kim Jae-jun: There are ditches on both sides of our upper field. It would be better to cut off the upper ditch and place a water hole to merge it with the lower ditch.
Host: That is a good suggestion.
It would be best to proceed as Kim Jae-jun suggested at that point.
Kim Jae-do: Will our rice fields be included?
Host: Yes, Kim Jae-do's rice fields will be partially included at the end. We ask for your understanding.
Kim Jae-do: It's not that much, so it can't be helped if it's just a little.
Kim Jin-hui: What about the front of the field?
Host: For areas with fields, we will only remove the curved part with Kim Jin-hee's lower field and straighten it into a direct path.
Kim Shin-hui: Regarding the busy street, will we pave it downward as the Ijang suggested, or upward?
Host: For the busy street, we have reached a compromise with Kim Seon-hee that if we pave it downward, about 50 pyeong of the rice field will be included.
Let's decide whether to pave it upward or downward.
Kim Yoon-muk: In my opinion, I agree that paving upward would be better.
Kim Jae-hong: It's fine to pave it downward, but I'm afraid of the work, so let's pave it upward.
Host: Three people have spoken in favor of paving upward. Are there any objections?
Kim Heon-muk: It's settled then.


--- (p. 372) ---

Host: How should we clean the area in front of Kim Myeong-gi's house where the manure pit is located?
Lee Suk-bae: Have you consulted with the village head Kim Myeong-gi?
Host: We cannot create a path from Kim Myeong-gi's house, where we will prune the fruit tree branches, to the current manure pit location and then to the end of the village head's small ridge, because of the fruit tree.
Lee Sang-mok: There's no other way. We must extend the drainage cover downward and reduce the village head's small ridge.
Host: From my house to Kim Seong-hui's house, we will clear a straight path, and from Kim Seong-hui's house to the three-way intersection, we will also clear a straight path.
Kim Jae-gu: How much will our farmland be reduced, and what should we do?
Host: If we fold and raise half of the upper ridge, it will become one ridge.
Kim Jae-gu: Won't the hill be too high then? And there is a water gate behind the farmland.
Host: Yes, I am planning to build a three-tiered stone embankment in the lower part.
Kim Gwan-muk: Next, it's my turn.
Host: We need to remove the small ridge in the middle of Grandfather's farmland. We will use the soil from that ridge to expand the farmland.
Kim Gwan-muk: It seems like we are just taking up a lot of land.
Kim Gwan-hui: Our watercress field will be halved. Can we use the remaining part as a watercress field?
Kim Jae-u: No, Gwan-hui. If we leave a path as wide as a palm, everyone will say something.
Kim Gwan-hui: Alright. I understand that we will use it all.
Host: Lastly, as we work on the house site, there may be places that we did not expect to be absorbed. Please understand that.
Village Members: In any case, the village head is thinking about it, but if we say it cannot be done, the work cannot be done. Please proceed well.
Host: Yes, thank you very much. Today's evening meeting was meaningful and was achieved through mutual compromise. With the hearts of the villagers like this, our village is sure to continue developing.
January 18, 1972
Representatives of the Residents: Kim Jae-jun, Kim Heon-muk, Kim Jae-do, Lee Sun-bae, Kim Jin-hee, Kim Yun-muk, Kim Shin-hee, Kim Jae-gu.

## ♦ Minutes of the Meeting (會議錄) (5)

Agenda: Road opening for agriculture.
Date: January 26, 1973
Location: Kim Seung-hui's living room
Attendees: 29 people
Absentees: Im Ho-seong and 15 others
Host: Village head Kim Seung-hui


--- (p. 373) ---

Host: Today, we have gathered for a village general assembly (總會) to discuss the farm road construction (農路開設) project designated as part of the 1973 Saemaul beautification campaign (事業). We would like to gather your opinions (意見) and make a resolution (決議) regarding this matter.

First, please share your thoughts on which locations (個所), specific points (地點), and extension distances (延長距離) would be most suitable.

Kim Jae-hong: For the farm road construction (農路開設), it would be best to prioritize areas with extensive farmland (農耕地). I suggest constructing roads from the upper village to Sojungjae (800m), from Marudeul to Gunneunggol (700m), and from the upper village to Hwangso Pass (500m). These three locations (個所) would be ideal for development (開設).

Kim Yun-muk: That is a very good suggestion. However, we have about two months to work on this project (作業) until the rice paddy weeding (논두렁 가래질) season begins. I wonder if we can complete all these tasks (事業) in that time.

Lee Soon-bae: Last year, we completed the village entrance road expansion project (進入路擴張事業) in just over 20 days with the participation (參與) of all residents (住民). If everyone works hard, I believe we can complete this project (完成) without any problems (問題). Let's all work hard with the hope (希望) of reducing our burdens (지게 덜 짊어진다는).

Host: Are there any objections (異議)?

Kim Jae-eok: In my opinion, it would be better to start with Jungteogol rather than Hwangso Pass.

All residents (住民一同): No, that is not appropriate. That statement is merely self-interest (慾心), aiming to benefit your own farmland (田畓). Let's follow Kim Jae-hong's suggestion and finalize (確定) the project (事業) accordingly.

Kim Gyeong-hoe: For the Gunneunggol route, we need to cross a small stream (小河川). How should we handle the construction of a small bridge (小橋樑)?

Host: Yes, constructing a small bridge (小橋樑) is too difficult for this year (今年度), so we plan to repair the existing path (現方채) for use.

Now, when should we start the project (事業)?

Kim Jae-gu: Since we need to prepare for farming (農事準備) when the weather warms up, it would be best to start as early as possible and finish before the farming season (農事철) begins. I suggest starting around mid-February, about 10 days after the Lunar New Year (음력設), with the village leader (里長) determining the exact date based on the village's situation (狀況).

Kim Myeong-gi: That sounds good to me.

Host: Alright, I will go and set the date for mobilization (動員) at that time. Please send as many able-bodied workers (可及的一할 수 있는 사람) as possible from each household (한집도 빠짐없이).

Kim Jae-jun: Last year, I noticed that some households sent only small children or women to work, even when there were able-bodied men (壯丁) at home. I suggest that from now on, if such people are sent, they should be sent back and considered as non-participants (不參者).

Kim Jae-seon: What penalty (罰則) will be imposed on households that do not send workers?

Host: As last year, non-participants (不參者) should be required to pay one day's wage (日當金額). Are there any objections (異議)?

All residents (住民一同): No objections (異議).

Host: Are there any other suggestions (意見)?

Someone suggests purchasing about two more hoes (황새 곡괭이).

# Chungnam (Chungcheongnam-do) Nonsan-gun (Nonsan County) Yeonmu-eup (Yeonmu Township) Dongsan 1-dong (Dongsan 1 Neighborhood) Haengjung Village (Haengjung Village)

## 1. Overview of the Village

### a. History

* According to legend, during the late Joseon Dynasty, Dongsan-ri (Dongsan Village) was one of the yangban (aristocrat) villages nestled in the forest. In the courtyard of a yangban house, there was a large persimmon tree resembling a pavilion, which led nearby villages to call it Haengjung (Persimmon Pavilion). At that time, Haengjung had only about 30 households, roughly half the number today. Excluding a few households, most lived in poverty, making and selling charcoal for a living.
* In the 1950s, with the establishment of a military base nearby, the administrative district name changed from 'Guja-gamyeon' to Yeonmu-eup, and the Haengjung hamlet came to be called Dongsan-ri.
* Simultaneously with the establishment of the military base, many refugees from across the country settled in the area, bringing the number of households to about 70, as it is today.
* To produce and sell charcoal, many trees were cut down, leading to the development of numerous hillsides. In the early 1960s, peach farming from neighboring Eunjin, introduced by Park No-won, spread to this village and continues to this day.
* In 1972, the village was initially designated as a self-sufficient village and has since developed further. On December 10, 1976, it became a village of honor when its Saemaul leader, Hwang Jong-cheol, received the Saemaul Medal (Self-Help Medal) at the National Saemaul Leaders Conference.

### b. Location and Conditions

#### **<Location>**

The village is located around the Yeonmu entrance of the Honam Expressway. It is 2 km east of Yeonmu-eup, 1.7 km west of the Yeonmu entrance road, and about 20 km south of the county office. There is one military unit stationed near the village.

#### **<Conditions>**

* Most of the area where the village is located consists of hilly terrain suitable for cultivation. The village benefits from convenient transportation, making it easy to transport and sell agricultural products. However, it has relatively few wooded areas compared to farmland.
* Nearby (within 4 km) are elementary, middle, and high schools, making education convenient and the villagers' enthusiasm for education high.


--- (p. 378) ---

## 2. Village Development Process (發展過程)

### a. Situation Before 1970 (70年以前的狀況)

Although there are no accurate records (正確的記錄) of the village's development in the 1970s (70年代的開發狀況), the village's slogans from 1970 (1970年的口號) provide some insight. The village envisioned its future (未來象) as:
1. A village without shoulder poles (地게 없는 마을),
2. A village without lanterns (호롱불 없는 마을),
3. A village without idle people or land (노는 사람, 노는 땅 없는 마을),
4. A village without superstition or gambling (迷信, 賭博 없는 마을),
5. A village without thatched roofs (초가(草家) 없는 마을).

1) Basic Environment (基礎環境)

The village was surrounded by brushwood fences and earthen walls, with low eaves that required one to bow their head to enter. Thatched-roof houses (草家집) covered all 70 households (戶) in Dongsan-ri (東山里).


--- (p. 380) ---

The filth (汚物) seeping from pigsties and cattle sheds occupied half (切半) of the narrow alleyways, and the waste from sweet potatoes and potatoes, which had been a major food source (食糧) for the influx of residents (流入住民), was carelessly discarded in the courtyards. The term "unclean (不潔)" became synonymous with the village, leading to the vision of fostering a village without thatched houses as a future goal (未來像).

## 2) Living Habits (生活習性)

After the visitation system (面會制度) of the OO unit (部隊) was discontinued, some local residents (土着住民) and influx residents (流入住民) who had been living off the visitors from all over the country (全國) engaged in superstitious (迷信的) taboos for quick profits, and the village was never at peace due to the rampant gambling (賭博) and fighting. The village slogan (口號) was set as "a village without superstition (迷信), gambling (賭博), and lanterns (호롱불)."

## 3) Income Level (所得水準)

After the discontinuation of the visitation system (面會制度) of the military unit (軍部隊), the influx residents (流入民) who had lost their means of livelihood (生活的 수단) mostly eked out a living as mobile taverns (移動酒保) or peddlers (行商) following the training soldiers (訓練兵) during their education time (敎育時間), while more diligent residents (住民) would cut wood from distant mountains and sell it in the commercial district (商街) of Yeonmu-eup (鍊武邑) to get through the barren season. The estimated average household income (戶當平均所得) at that time was a mere 306,000 won (千). Given the circumstances (事情) of the time, the adoption of the village slogan (口號) advocating "cultivating (開墾) idle land and putting idle people to work in their vocations (生業)" provides insight into the income level (所得水準) of the village.

## 4) Cultural Level (文化水準)

Since electricity (電氣) had not been introduced, residents (住民) could not even dream of electric record players (電蓄) or TVs. The most advanced cultural tool (文化利器) they enjoyed was a phonograph (스피카), and a household with a bicycle (自轉車) was as rare as two households, making it a more valuable inheritance (遺產) than a motorcycle today.

### B. Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (運動의 추진)

#### 1) Motives (動機) and Results of Pilot Projects (試驗事業의 성과)

##### <Development Motives (開發動機)>

In 1958 (年), leader Hwang Jong-cheol (黃鍾哲) was discharged (除隊) from the military (軍). At that time, the Hwang (黃氏) family was in a dire situation. With an elderly mother and being an anti-communist family (反共家族), Hwang was left alone to take care of his sister-in-law (兄嫂), nephew, and six other family members (食口) who were struggling with debt. Determined to live like the earth itself, Hwang began to study farming techniques (農事技術) at agricultural guidance centers (農村指導所) to reorganize farmland (農地), pay off debts (清算), and gain the trust (信望) of residents (住民) as an advanced farm household (先進農家). Based on this trust, Hwang initiated joint work (共同作業) to raise funds (資金), which eventually led to the rural self-powered electrification project (自力電氣事業). The rural telephone project (農村電話事業) in 1968 (年度) demonstrated the possibility (可能性) of self-development (自力開發), and the leader's (指導者) obsession (執念) with rural revitalization (農村復興) and the trust (信望) of residents (住民) became the driving force (動機) behind village development (開發).

##### <Results of Early Pilot Projects (初年도試驗事業의 성과)>

From 1968 (年度) to 1971 (年), joint benefit projects (共同利益事業) were continuously carried out, and the accumulated joint fund (共同基金) was used to improve 3 wells (우물보수), construct 4 laundry areas (빨래터), build 300 meters of sewer facilities (下水溝施設), and install 7 soil pipes (토관) with 335 bags of government-supported (政府支援) cement. These projects were the foundation of the Saemaul basic environmental improvement (基礎環境改善) initiatives driven by resident cooperation (住民協同).


--- (p. 381) ---

During the initial year of the movement, it would be inaccurate to say that the project yielded significant results or outputs. Instead, the success should be measured by the community's enhanced spirit of cooperation and unity, as well as the sense of mission it instilled in residents to improve their own villages with their own hands. Additionally, the movement provided residents with an experiential understanding of the need to distribute support materials more effectively and systematically.

## 2) Overcoming Challenges

In 1974, the village head changed from Park Beom-gyu to Kim In-hui, and in 1976, the women's association president changed from Kim Gi-sun to Lee Young-ae, marking a gradual generational shift. However, the Saemaul leaders remained steadfast in their roles, continuing their activities for seven consecutive years without replacement.

### <Three Months of Morning Greetings>

Dongsan-ri has two access roads. One is an expanded version of an old path leading to Yeonmu-eup, and the other is a newly constructed farm road connecting the central part of the village to the Yeonmu entrance of the expressway, currently in use. In 1972, a general meeting of residents was held to request the donation of land for the new farm road. While local landowners eventually agreed to donate the land, the 140-plus pyeong of forested land owned by non-resident Kim OO presented a challenge. This forest contains the ancestral grave of Kim OO's ancestors, and his descendants are said to be numerous. Despite several attempts to discuss the matter with the landowner, progress was impossible.

The village leader and head began visiting the home of Kim OO's descendant living in a neighboring village, kneeling at the doorstep with a sack cloth for nearly three months, paying morning respects and pleading for the land donation. Their persistence eventually led to the creation of the current farm road. However, the access road remains unsatisfactory. Once a direct access road to the community center is completed, Dongsan-ri will have resolved one of its longstanding issues. Currently, the bend in the road near the ancestral grave site, still not fully straightened, reminds the leader and head of their own bent backs as they knelt before the landowner.

### <Heavy Equipment Stuck in a Manure Pit>

This incident occurred during the construction of a simple water supply system in 1973. We express our gratitude to the manager of the Nonsan Office of the Korea Expressway Corporation, whose assistance we will never forget, and share a poignant story.

After completing the installation of a water intake facility at the lower well site and a water purification facility on the rear hill, and connecting water taps to each household, we attempted to operate the water intake facility's motor. However, due to low voltage, the motor would not start. There was no choice but to install a transformer, requiring the erection of a power pole for voltage increase.

Residents' united efforts to install a concrete power pole proved futile. Left with no alternative, we visited the manager of the road construction office, who kindly allowed us to use a dump truck. As the dump truck began to pull the power pole into place, it started to sink into the ground. The heavy dump truck, along with its cargo, gradually disappeared beneath the surface, leaving residents and the driver bewildered. As the elders recounted, that spot was once used for outdoor training by the OO unit.


--- (p. 382) ---

Upon hearing that it was a human waste treatment facility (人糞處理場) at the training ground (練場), it was a situation where one could neither laugh nor cry. With great effort, an 8-ton tow truck managed to pull out the dump truck and the utility poles (電柱) were put back in place, allowing the provision of high-quality tap water to 72 households (家口). Whenever I see the water pumping station (揚水場) now, I recall the image of residents (住民) clinging to ropes like ants all through the night to pull out the truck that had fallen into the human waste (人糞) pit.

## 5) Sisterhood Bond (姉妹結緣)

On around March 20, 1972, during the busy farming season, residents who needed to complete the farm road before the season began were anxious. They decided to carry out nighttime torchlight work.

In the darkness, with snowflakes falling on the fields, the procession of torches creating a city that never sleeps was a magnificent sight. At that time, the manager of the Nonsan Management Office of the Honam Expressway, who happened to pass by the work site, saw the vigorous procession of the New Village movement burning in the middle of the night.

He couldn't help but be drawn to the fervor of the New Village movement, inspecting the work site and promising to provide equipment support. To repay the kindness of the equipment support, the residents prepared autumn rice cakes that year and visited the management office 1.7 km away.

Coming courtesy begets going courtesy, forming a sisterhood bond that continues to this day without waning.

The 1973 business shifted from the Saemaul beautification projects of 1972 to income-increasing projects. Notably, the technical workforce cultivated through Saemaul beautification projects was utilized to undertake landscaping projects along highways on a contract basis, yielding two benefits: village funds and wage income.

### <First Contract Project>
Starting in February 1972, residents of Dongsan-ri (東山里) established a connection with the Nonsan Management Office (論山管理事務所) of the Road Corporation (道路公社) and undertook the beautification of highway areas on a contract basis.
*   Construction Period: March 22, 1973 ~ September 8, 1973
*   Number of Contracts: 3
*   Contract Amount: 7,030,000 won

Saemaul leaders worked tirelessly in three roles—ensuring the successful completion of the project, securing funds, and overseeing the work—to generate wage income for the residents. As a result, a net profit of 1,804,505 won was deposited into the village fund, and 2,350,090 won in wage income was returned to the residents. For residents who had never known prosperity and struggled to survive, this sum was immense and overwhelming.

This influx of external funds created an opportunity for productive investment, breaking the cycle of poverty. The Saemaul spirit of diligence, self-help, and cooperation brought wealth to the residents, helping them understand the true meaning of the Saemaul Movement. They proudly became the creators of a new history for Dongsan-ri (東山里). The village's common fund was reinvested in Saemaul projects, such as simple water supply systems, to improve residents' welfare through self-reliant initiatives.

The residents learned that Saemaul involves not only environmental improvement but also acquiring various skills. These skills could enhance individual lives, serving as a strong foundation for prosperity.

The Saemaul Undong (Movement) in 1974 (Annual) is characterized by its self-reliance (純自力事業). Additionally, the residents' income increase (所得增加) in 1974 (Annual), particularly in the wage income sector (勞賃所得分野), was driven by the residents themselves, showcasing a unique feature where government support (政府支援) was not the primary driving force.

#### <Second Phase (第2次) Landscaping Construction (造景工事) Subcontracting (都給)>

Following the 1973 (Year) project, landscaping construction (造景工事) subcontracting (都給工事) along the Honam Expressway (湖南高速道) was carried out. The subcontracting included rock cutting (岩 切取工事) at the 27.2km mark from Daejeon (大田) and earth cutting (切土部) and tidying up (整理) at the 23km mark, totaling two projects (件).
*   Subcontracting Period (都給工事 기간): 74.11.10~74.12.30
*   Subcontracting Amount (都給金額): 3,610 Thousand Won (千원)
*   Net Profit (純利益金): 500 Thousand Won (千원)
*   Wage Payment (勞賃支給額): 2,184 Thousand Won (千원)

Continuing from 1973 (Year), the 2,184 Thousand Won (千원) in wage income (勞賃所得) and the 500 Thousand Won (千원) in village community fund (共同基金) formation became agricultural investment funds (農事基金) for expanding high-yield crops (高所得作物) cultivation (栽培), playing a significant role in the 1973 (Year) income increase (所得增加). Furthermore, the village community fund (共同基金) saved in 1974 (Year) and 1976 (Year) became the financial resources (財源) for constructing a 68-pyeong (坪) Saemaul warehouse (倉庫) self-reliantly (自力) in 1975 (Year).

In the harsh cold of below freezing temperatures, the residents of Dongsan-ri (東山里) worked on a landscaping subcontracting site (造景都給工事場) where they hung from ropes on 30-meter-high rocks along the expressway (高速道), chiseling away at the rocks with pickaxes. Amidst the dust and sweat, they melted rice balls with their breath to stave off hunger in their tents (天幕). Through this experience, the residents learned that increasing Saemaul income (所得增大) is not something that can be achieved by merely sitting around, chanting slogans (口號). The fruits of their lessons (敎訓) and efforts (努力) are what built the prosperous Dongsan-ri (東山里) of today.

# <Highway (高速道邊) Landscaping (造景事業) and Connected (連棟式) Steel (鐵製) Greenhouse>

From March 1, 1975, to April 26, 1975, a total of five projects, including the 23km uphill (上行線) attachment work (工事) on the Honam Expressway (湖南高速道路), and landscaping (造景工事) were contracted for 11,650,000 won (千원), with labor income (勞賃所得) of 5,598,000 won (千원) returned to the residents (住民). The labor income (勞賃所得) of 10,132,000 won (千원) achieved over three years (年) became the fund (基金) for cooperative farming (協業營農). In November 1975, with a loan (融資) of 7,500,000 won (千원) from the county fund (郡費) and a self-funded (自負擔) amount of 7,500,000 won (千원), a total of 40 connected (連棟式) steel (鐵製) greenhouses covering 4,180 pyeong (坪) were installed (設置).

The installation (設置) of semi-permanent (半永久) connected (連棟式) steel (鐵製) greenhouses changed the agricultural method (農業方式) from traditional (固式的) rice farming (農事) to high-income (高所得) economic crops (經濟作物). This utilized the advantages (利點) of the highway (高速道路邊) and allowed for direct shipment (直接出荷) to major city consumption areas (大都市消費地).

The village's future vision (未來像) from 1970, "a village without idle land" and "a village without idle people," is being realized (實現) with the installation (設置) of 4,180 pyeong (坪) of connected (連棟式) steel (鐵製) greenhouses. A resident (住民) who spent an entire winter (冬) working (作業場) for wages (勞賃) and sold a single jar of rice (쌀 한 가마) to fulfill a lifetime (平生) of regret (恨) is now earning a net profit (純利益) of 1,700,000 won (萬원) from strawberry (딸기) farming in a 500 pyeong (坪) connected (連棟式) steel (鐵製) greenhouse. This resident's joyful (웃음짓는) demeanor, unseen by others, reminds us once again of the miracle (奇蹟) achieved by Saemaul Undong (新村運動).

In addition to strawberries (딸기), pineapples (파인애플), chives (얼갈이), and cucumbers (오이) are also being cultivated (栽培) as year-round crops (年中作物). With the installation (設置) of telephones (電話), residents (住民) are sensitive (敏感性) to market information (市場情報) and are increasing their circulating (回轉) capital (資金) derived from wealth (富). They are aiming for a household (戶當) income (所得) of 2,500,000 won (萬원) and experiencing a significant change (金石之感) in their farming methods (營農方式).

# 9) Achievements of the Saemaul Movement (事業)

The achievements of the Saemaul Movement (事業) can be seen by comparing the village slogans of 1970 and 1977.

a) 1970 Village Slogans (未來像)
- A village without shoulder poles
- A village without lanterns
- A village without idle people or idle land
- A village without superstition (迷信) or gambling (賭博)
- A village without thatched houses

b) 1977 Village Slogans
- A leading village
- A village without idle people or idle land
- A village where every word spoken is beneficial
- A village that thinks of others when thinking of oneself

c) Renewal of Spiritual Attitude (精神姿勢)
In 1970, the dominant mindset of the villagers was to live well and peacefully by relying on superstition (迷信) or gambling (賭博). However, after being guided by leaders for 7 years, the residents of Dongsan-ri (東山里) have cultivated a higher spiritual attitude (精神姿勢), thinking not only of themselves but also of their neighborhood and the development of the country. When the morning bugle call sounds at 6 AM and the Saemaul song echoes, people of all ages gather in the Saemaul plaza for morning assembly, creating a scene that might be mistaken for a foreign collective village training institute (集團村訓練院). As the sun sets, the national anthem (愛國歌) plays from the Saemaul loudspeaker, and farmers pause their work to stand respectfully (敬虔) for the lowering of the flag (下旗式), their sun-tanned faces turned towards the national flag (國旗). Even children playing in the playground stand still to salute the Taegeukgi (太極旗), evoking a sense of reverence (敬虔) similar to that depicted in "Millet's Angelus." The villagers have rid themselves of the harmful mentalities of laziness (懶怠), dependence (依他), jealousy (猜忌), and chance (遇然), embracing diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperation (協同) in their daily lives, and striving towards higher patriotic ideals (愛國理想).

d) Reform of Living Standards (生活面)
In 1970, the village aimed to be free of lanterns and shoulder poles. Now, out of 72 households, 46 have televisions (安房劇場)(TV) bringing the world into their homes, and every kitchen has running water (水道). Plows have been largely replaced by cultivators (耕耘機), and shoulder poles by handcarts (리어카). The village has long since banished both shoulder poles and lanterns.


--- (p. 389) ---

Initially, the residents' utmost desire was to eliminate thatched roofs and create a village without them, but now, more than 20 units of rural cultural houses have been built, and the residents are more enthusiastic about constructing rural cultural houses than improving roofs! Amidst neatly adorned standard rural houses, residents live vibrant lives, seemingly having forgotten their humble thatched-roof homes from seven years ago.

## Production Aspect: Structural Improvement

"Earning two bushels of rice per dong (unit of land) is considered prime land" was, just a few years ago, the value measure among residents for assessing land. Now, the saying has transformed into "Earning only two bushels of rice per dong is not prime land," proving how drastically rice production has increased. Residents of Dongsan-ri, who once farmed for self-sufficiency, have now changed their perspective on agriculture. They focus on how to continuously cultivate high-yield crops, increase production, and time it right, showing keen interest in market information. Fields that once grew sweet potatoes, potatoes, and beans are now turning into golden fields of high-yield crops. Moreover, since the installation of 4,180 pyeong of semi-permanent, connected, iron-framed vinyl greenhouses at the end of 1975, the variety of crops being cultivated has significantly increased. However, there is one key characteristic: farming is no longer for self-sufficiency but to meet the desires of urban consumers. Additionally, previously overlooked collective cooperative farming and collective shipping have gained prominence, and farming is now approached from a managerial perspective. Crop types have shifted from self-sufficiency products like sweet potatoes, potatoes, corn, and millet to market products like pineapples, strawberries, off-season cucumbers, and winter cabbage, enabling year-round farming. With the residents of Dongsan-ri leveraging the nearby expressway, even a small village's products can now compete in the national market.

## Income Aspect: Innovation

Located near OO Unit, residents in the 1970s eked out a living by selling sweet potatoes, potatoes, and bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes) to trainees, with an average household income of only 306,000 won. Like any rural village, residents here sustained themselves through intercropping sweet potatoes and potatoes between fruit trees. However, through the Saemaul beautification project in 1971-72, they learned various skills and, based on these skills, secured 10,000,000 won in wage income by undertaking seven expressway landscaping projects from 1973 to 1975. This not only freed them from the rural off-season idleness but also provided them with leisure funds for reinvestment in agriculture, leading to increased income. The increased income was not a coincidence but a result of applying the basic economic principle of breaking the poverty cycle. Funds injected through the Saemaul Undong and the frugal living habits it fostered enabled expansion and reinvestment, becoming the driving force behind today's wealth. Now, achieving an average household income of 2,500,000 won by the 1980s is no longer an unrealistic goal.


--- (p. 390) ---

# 3. Future Development Plans

1) Production and Income Aspect
We are expediting fund-raising to establish small-scale, multi-purpose agricultural processing plants, improve the livelihood of village women, and install feed production machinery to promote livestock farming. We plan to build a 35-pyeong (118.8 square meters) shared workspace to enable women to process agricultural products during the winter and generate off-farm income.

2) Distribution Structure Aspect
We plan to purchase one agricultural product transport truck (2.5% of the total) to directly ship village specialty products to major consumption areas, thereby reducing distribution margins and achieving timely product delivery to increase village income.

3) Youth Guidance
To guide and educate youth, we will establish a scholarship fund and build a house for Dongsan-ri residents in Daejeon and Seoul to support the education of village children studying there. We plan to provide scholarships to cultivate future leaders for our village.

4) Improvement of Village Structure
Starting in 1978, we plan to begin improving our village structure to match advanced countries by building standard rural houses for 30 dilapidated houses (in addition to the already built 8 standard and 12 self-improved houses) and implementing land readjustment projects.

# Chungcheongnam-do (충남) Seocheon County (서천군) Pangeo-myeon (판교면) Bokdae-ri (복대리) 2-gu (2구)

## 1. Overview of the Village

### a. History

*   As Jichang County during the Baekje (百濟) era, it became Piin (庇仁) under the Unified Silla (統一新羅) dynasty and was part of Seorim County. In the 9th year of King Hyojong (顯宗) of Goryeo, it was renamed Garim County (嘉林縣) and became a Gammu (監務). In the 13th year of King Taejong (太宗) of Joseon (李朝), it was renamed Piin County (庇仁縣) and was under the supervision of Hongju Jin (洪州鎭管). It was changed to Piin County (庇仁郡) and, as a result of the county merger (郡廢合) by Governor-General of Chosen Order No. 111 on December 29, 1933, it became part of Dong-myeon (東面) of Seocheon County (舒川郡). On September 30, 1942, as part of the administrative district (行政區域) reorganization of Chungcheongnam-do (忠淸南道), it became Bokdae-ri (卜大里) 2-gu (區) of Pangeo-myeon (板橋面).
*   In particular, Gu-eokmal (九億洞) was originally a village where nine households, each with nine able-bodied men, took the initiative to handle all village affairs. Moreover, they influenced neighboring villages as well. Thus, the village was called Gu-eokmal (九億洞), meaning a village where the nine Gu-eok (九億) merchants lived. Over time, the name evolved into the current Gu-eokmal.

### b. Location and Conditions

#### <Location>

*   Located approximately 12 km north of the Seocheon County Office (舒川郡廳), the village is bordered by mountains and hills to the east, west, and north, forming the boundaries with Buyeo County (扶餘郡) and Boryeong County (保寧郡).
*   The village consists of five natural hamlets: Bundoong, Gu-eokmal (九億洞), Gasil (價實), Jindeul (眞得), and Yudeokgol (有得洞).

#### <Conditions>

*   Surrounded by mountains and hills, the village has vast rice paddies stretching from north to south in the center.
*   The national Route No. 2 between Daejeon (大田) and Janghang (長項) runs alongside the rice paddies.
*   The hills are cultivated with orchards and fields.

## 2. Village Development Process (發展過程)

### 가. Situation Before 1970 (70年以前의 상황(狀況))

#### 1) Basic Environment (基礎環境)

*   All farming households (全農家) were formed with thatched roofs (草家집) and mud fences,
*   The winding village paths were inconvenient (不便) even for carrying a shoulder pole (地게), and
*   The village access road (進入路) followed ditches and curved paddy fields, making it necessary to push bicycles (自轉車) rather than ride them.
*   The roofs were rotten with weeds (雜草) growing, and during rain, basins (함지박) were placed in the rooms (房) to catch leaks,
*   The narrow alleys had no sewers (下水溝), and waste water flowed onto the streets, making it impossible to tell the difference between the road and a sewer (下水溝).


--- (p. 405) ---

The stream flowing in front of O village had no embankment, so whenever a heavy rain (暴雨) fell, the dike would collapse, causing the villagers to abandon their crops (農事) every year.

2) Income Level (所得水準)
- Each household (戶當) had 0.7ha of farmland (耕地面積), where they practiced traditional farming methods (傳來農事法), growing grains (米穀), cereals (麥類), root crops (薯類), and legumes (豆類). The harvests barely provided each household (戶當所得) with 322,000 won (千), making self-sufficiency in food (食糧) impossible. To make ends meet, villagers had to either work as day laborers in neighboring villages or as live-in farmhands.
- The village's livestock (畜産) consisted of only 2 cows (頭), 10 pigs (頭), and around 30 chickens (餘首). Pigs took a year (年) to raise and only yielded about 100 won (斥) each, making the village one of the poorest in the region (管內) in terms of income level (所得水準).

3) Living Conditions in 1970 (70年도(年度)의 생활狀態)
a) Mental State (精神狀態)
- Due to the villagers' poverty (貧困), they could not even afford to properly educate their children (子息) or maintain regular meals without relying on others for work. Caught in a cycle of poverty, the villagers were more likely to resign themselves to their fate (諦念) and indulge in dissipation (放湯) than to aspire to a better life.
- During the day, the villagers worked half-heartedly, as if the work belonged to others, not themselves (自己). At night, they passed the time (消日) with drinking and gambling (賭博).
- Ignorance (無知), laziness, and poverty led the residents (住民) to focus on gossiping and slandering (中傷謀略) others, and fights were common.
- Once known for its hardworking residents (九億洞), the village had become infamous for fighting, drinking, and revelry (九雜洞), earning it the reputation of a decaying village (廢村) within a decaying village.
- On market days in Pangeo (板橋), villagers would spend the little money they earned as intermediaries (居間) at taverns, worsening their already difficult lives (生活) and often ending up drunk (滿醉) and collapsing anywhere.
- In such a lifestyle (生活), there was no pioneering spirit (開拓精神), and the idea of working diligently (熱心히) to achieve self-reliance (自立) was a distant dream.

b) Culture and Daily Life (文化 및衣食住生活)
- The villagers, preoccupied with maintaining their livelihoods (生計維持), could not afford newspapers (新聞) or magazines (雜誌) and relied on only three radios for news. However, they mostly listened to popular songs (流行歌) and serial dramas (連續劇) rather than news or farming updates (農事消息).
- The villagers' houses were in disrepair, and they wore patched clothes.
- Adults considered a single pair of knee-length pants (베잠뱅이) sufficient until the chilly autumn, while children could not even afford to see sneakers (運動靴) and wore black rubber shoes (고무신) made of cheap nylon, which barely lasted a season. The villagers' faded clothing and the sight of children carrying a few notebooks wrapped in tattered cloth for their compulsory education (義務敎育) were pitiful, reflecting the parents' laziness and lack of consideration for future generations (後代).
- In the summer, the villagers were content with barley rice (꽁보리밥) and either fermented shrimp (새우젓) or chili paste (고추장). Even this meager meal was often not enough to fill their stomachs.


--- (p. 406) ---

It would have been fortunate if there was any, but during the spring famine, it was common to prolong life with vegetable porridge, and those who didn't even have that would go a day with just one or two meals, surviving on acorn porridge.
O In winter, too, men would substitute meals with a few sweet potatoes, yet they would still rush to taverns for gambling as soon as they had a few coins. Women, sent to such places by their parents, would resent them but still prepare barley porridge waiting for their husbands, but even past midnight, they wouldn't know when they would return.

Na. Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

1) Development Motive (開發動機)

O The news that the "Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)" proclaimed by President Park on April 22, 1970, was rising like a flame across the country could not have failed to reach this village.
O However, for three years, from 1971 to 1973, there was no sign of any movement in this hamlet.
O In April 1972, Kim Byung-yeol (aged 31) was elected as the village head, and the young head, with his aspirations, ran day and night throughout the village, but the residents, once tamed wrongly, only looked at him with eyes of derision.
O Even if a few elderly people responded, the young people would rebel, and if the young people responded, the elderly's derisive glances made it impossible to unite the residents.

2) Election of Leaders (指導者) and Activity Status (活動狀況)

O In February 1974, a few people who were concerned about the development of other hamlets and worried about their own gathered the residents for a general meeting, emphasizing that something must be done in their hamlet too, and elected a leader whom the entire village could trust and follow.
O The person elected at the village general meeting on February 17 of the same year is none other than today's village head, Seo Seong.

3) Achievements of the First-Year Trial Business (初年度試驗事業)

O As the first project, it was decided to widen and straighten the winding village access road from the national road to the hamlet, and to resolve the land issues related to it, Village Head Seo voluntarily donated 100 pyeong of farmland, leading others to follow suit.
O In February 1974, the village head and leaders mobilized men, and the women's association president mobilized women, and despite the harsh cold and snow, the residents came out without exception, bringing carts, tractors, shoulder poles, shovels, and reels.
O Village Head Seo Seong could not hide his joyous cheers. The work of demolishing embankments, digging soil from the mountains, and filling the fields continued until April, and in just two months, they successfully completed a 200m access road.
O The joy of having the artery of our village, the access road, opened was immense, but even more so was the fact that everyone, young and old, had continuously come out to work without exception. It was as if they had gained an army of a thousand and ten thousand, making them feel moved, happy, and proud.
O Now, they had the confidence that they could accomplish anything, and the residents of the hamlet also felt the power of cooperation and unity.


--- (p. 407) ---

I realized.
O The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) in Hadae 2-ri, which started late, proceeded day and night without distinction, including torchlight work at night.

## 4) Overcoming Difficulties (隘路克服) Situation (狀況)
O After being elected as a leader (指導者), Orijang (吳里長) completed his first project smoothly and, with newfound confidence, proposed a 500m farm road construction (農路開設) at the general meeting (總會). However,
O Unlike the smooth land donation (土地喜捨) of the first project, he encountered a major obstacle (難關). When he tried to tie a rope and start digging,
O An 80-year-old man (老人) participating in the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) lay down on the ground, saying, "You're going to take away all the land I have," and rolled around, even saying they might as well kill him,
O Some women (婦人) pulled and tore his clothes, and such incidents happened more than once or twice. Each time, instead of getting angry, he had to sweat profusely to persuade them, and
O His lips turned pitch black, and his body, unable to eat on time, became as weak as it could be, but his unyielding determination (執念) allowed him to complete the 500m farm road construction (農路開設) solely through his own efforts (純自力).
O In March 1974, they decided to build a multipurpose (多目的) community center (會舘), but without any support (支援) or even a penny from communal fundraising (共同募金), starting the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) with empty hands made building the center seem impossible.
O After much deliberation with the village (部落) leaders (指導者), they agreed to sell a 300-year-old (年) zelkova tree (느티나무) in the center of the village (部落) to create a communal fund (共同基金).
O Upon hearing this news (消息), the local district (面) officials said the tree was a protected tree (保護樹) and could not be cut down. Until then, Hadae 2-ri (下大 2里) had been considered a troublesome village and ignored by the district (面), but this incident sparked their interest (關心). The news even reached the county (郡), and although all financial support (資金支援) had ended, the villagers were overjoyed to hear that Kim Chang-hee (金昌熙), the vice-mayor (副郡守) of Seocheon County (舒川郡), had decided to support them with 300 bags (袋) of cement (洋灰).
O The joy of knowing that the administrative authorities (行政當局) were no longer ignoring but helping them was indescribable. It felt as if the saying "Heaven helps those who help themselves" was meant for us.
O Sand excavation (採取) today, gravel excavation (採取) tomorrow—the work proceeded as planned without a single day's delay. However, the 50-pyeong (坪) site for the community center (會舘敷地) was a problem. They planned to build it next to the zelkova tree (느티나무) at the village entrance (入口), but the entire area was owned by Lee Jong-cheol alone, making it difficult to ask for a land donation (喜捨) without feeling guilty.
O At the meeting (會議), Lee Jong-cheol remained silent (默默不答) for several hours (數時間). The air in the room was heavy. Past midnight, Lee Jong-cheol raised his head and said, "Can we not build the community center (會舘) because of me? Go ahead without any worries!" At this, all the residents (住民) cheered with joy (歎呼).
O After that, Lee Jong-cheol actively led the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) in silence, and following the villagers' enthusiastic requests (性化), he was elected as the unique "Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) Chairman (會長)" found nowhere else in the country, becoming an advisor (顧問格) for all matters related to the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement).
O As the saying goes, "The beginning is half the battle." With the firmly united strength of our village residents (部落住民), we completed the village community center (會舘) without much difficulty.


--- (p. 408) ---

During the day, the tireless leaders of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) worked on the Saemaul business (새마을事業), and at night, they planned the day's work results (作業成果) and future plans (計劃). They were simply overjoyed.

In early 1975, Mr. Oh, the village head (里長), along with the leaders (指導者), the village association chairperson (會長), and the development committee members (開發委員), decided to first improve their own houses with the 29-house roof improvement funds (改良資金) they had received. Then, they began to improve the roofs of some residents' houses who had refused to do so.

The thatched roofs (草家) gradually transformed into roofs made of slate and corrugated iron. The county officials, including the county magistrate (郡守), frequently visited to encourage and comfort the residents.

On April 23, 1975, Mr. Oh and the promotion committee members (推進委員) silently began to remove the roof of Jeon Gi-bok's house, who had been the most resistant. The house owner also climbed onto the roof. While Mr. Oh was busily removing the roof, the house owner suddenly pushed him off in a fit of emotion. That evening, as he lay on his sickbed (病席) with a hurt waist, he shed endless tears, lamenting, "Why did this have to happen to me?" It is said that he even felt sorrow and pain.

The next day, Jeon Gi-bok visited him, apologizing that he had acted impulsively out of temporary (一時的) emotion and asking for forgiveness. At that moment, all sorrow and pain were forgotten.

### 5) Developmental Promotion of Saemaul Undong (새마을事業)

With the lessons learned from the village entrance road (進入路), farm roads (農路), and the construction of community centers (會舘), they were able to easily complete the construction of a 1,100m village road, the expansion of 300m of farm roads, the installation of one 8m bridge (橋梁), one 2-pyeong (坪) public restroom (共同便所), and the installation of 30 signs (標識) by April 10. The construction had started on February 21, 1974.

Moreover, with the government's (政府) continuous support (支援) and the united strength of the residents (住民), all projects (事業) proceeded without difficulty.

### 6) Land (土地) and Cash Donations (現金 희사)

Comforting and warm hands (溫情의 손길) from all walks of life (各界) reached the villagers who worked hard with their sweat. The residents also generously donated their front yard fields (門前沃畓) for the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) without hesitation.

## 7) Heartwarming Stories (美談佳話)

### a) Story 1 (第1話)
* Lim Sam-gil, a resident of this village, is a hunchback with a disabled body, making his livelihood difficult and his situation dire. Yet,
* Without a word, he took the lead in the Saemaul Undong (事業), touching everyone's hearts. Despite his meager circumstances, he devoted himself to the movement, struggling even to have meals.
* In December 1974, the residents donated 8 sacks of white rice and 4 sacks of barley to Lim Sam-gil.
* Once united, the villagers eagerly helped their less fortunate neighbors, their passion for the Neighborly Mutual Aid Movement (隣保相助運動) overflowing.

### b) Story 2 (第2話)
* On April 5, 1975, a fire broke out at the home of resident Chae Sang-byeong. Although all residents mobilized for firefighting efforts, the late-night blaze destroyed the house and left Chae's mother with severe burns.
* Already struggling financially, Chae now faced homelessness and his mother's hospitalization. The villagers, familiar with Chae's situation,
* Donated 20 sacks of white rice and 17 sacks of barley, and
* Officials Jang Young-su and village headman Oh Se-jong contributed 10,000 won each, with the women's association adding 50,000 won, ensuring Chae's mother was admitted to the hospital.
* Chae wept with gratitude. In the past, such help would have been unthinkable. But with the Saemaul Undong (事業) uniting the residents, they now selflessly aided those in need and comforted the unfortunate.

### c) Story 3 (第3話)
* On April 12, 1975, our village was praised for its Neighborly Mutual Aid (隣保相助) and successful Saemaul Undong (事業) despite hardships. Congressman Kim Jong-ik visited, listened to a briefing, inspected the village, and donated 20,000 won as encouragement, urging continued efforts.
* All residents were proud to receive a congressman's visit just one year into the Saemaul Undong (事業), and their determination to keep working


--- (p. 410) ---

"That's amazing!" The joy of that moment is still unforgettable.

### 라) 제4화

O In September of that year, we decided to eliminate idle land and implement double cropping (2모작), investing our united strength into fertilizer production (퇴비(堆肥) 증산(增產)).
O With the goal of becoming the top village in the province (도내(道內) 1위(位)), we worked day and night. Men pulled carts and carried loads, while women and the elderly cut grass.
O Determined to innovate our village (마을(部落) 혁신(革新)), we spared no effort. On September 19, 1975, at around 11 AM, 77-year-old (77세(才)) Mr. Na Se-du (나세두(斗) 노인(老人)) collapsed while vigorously working on grass-cutting in the mountainside and passed away (별세(別世)).
O On September 21 of the same year, during Mr. Na's funeral (장(葬)) in Jeottae-ri 2-gu (텃대리2구), the village head (이장(里長)) said, "Let us follow Mr. Na's (나노인(羅老人)) aspirations (취지(旨)) and work hard to achieve self-sufficiency (자립(自立))." That day, the entire village (마을(部落) 사람(民)) embraced and wept together.
O Although our fertilizer production (퇴비(堆肥) 증산(增產)) did not achieve the top spot in the province (도내(道內) 1위(位)), we secured the first place in the county (군내(郡內) 1위(位)) and received a prize of 300,000 won (30만원). Moreover, County Magistrate Jeong Yeon-dal (정연달 군수(郡守)) encouraged us to work even harder and provided additional business funds (사업자금(事業資金)) of 500,000 won (50만원). All residents (주민(住民)) firmly united, recalling our painful past (쓰라렸던 과거(過去)).

### 마) 제5화

O The Saemaul Undong (새마을 사업(事業)) initiated in early 1974 (74년도(年度) 초(初)) transformed our village from a basic (기초마을) to a self-sufficient community (자립마을) in less than a year.
O On November 28, 1975, at the National Saemaul Undong Leaders Conference (전국(全國) 새마을 지도자(指導者) 대회(大會)) held in Daegu (大邱), we received a presidential gift (대통령(大統領) 각하(閣下) 하사금(下賜金)) of 1,000,000 won (100만원). The villagers (마을(部落) 사람(民)) forgot all the hardships (고초(苦楚)) and obstacles (난관(難關)) and rejoiced.
O Leader Choi Seong-hee (최성희 지도자(指導者)), who received the presidential gift (하사금(下賜金)), attributed that day's glory (영광(榮光)) to Mr. O Se-jong and urged everyone to work vigorously.

### 9) 특기사항(特記事項)

#### 가) 즐거웠던 일


--- (p. 411) ---

* When the first project, the completion of a 500m village road, was finished, all residents rejoiced more than if a highway had been built, and they were overflowing with confidence that they could accomplish any project
* After deciding to establish a community center, when landowner Mr. Lee Jong-cheol, whose land at the village entrance under a hackberry tree was difficult to donate, finally agreed to donate after a long time
* When the villagers, concerned about the livelihood of the hunchbacked Mr. Im Sam-gil, donated and delivered white rice and barley
* When Mr. Chae Sang-byeong's house caught fire, and white rice and barley were delivered, and leaders, responsible officials, and the women's association contributed a large sum of money to treat Mr. Chae's mother, it still warms my heart today.
* When Mr. Kim Jong-ik, a member of the National Assembly, first visited in April 1975
* When, during the summer fertilizer production increase, we ranked first in the county and received a prize of 300,000 won and 500,000 won in business funds from the county magistrate
* When, during the Saemaul Leaders Conference in Daegu on November 28, 1975, we received a grant of 1,000,000 won from His Excellency

### 나. Sad Events

* When, during the second project of road construction, an 80-year-old man with a few magaji of land rolled on the ground saying that the Saemaul Undong would take away all his land, and women had their clothes torn while resisting, it was pitch dark before my eyes.
* When, while forcibly carrying out the opposition to roof improvement, I was pushed by the owner, injured my waist, and had to lie in bed, the regret is still unforgettable.
* When, on September 21, 1975, 77-year-old Ms. Na Se-hwa passed away in the mountains while working day and night to increase fertilizer production, there were unforgettable sad events.

### Ba. Achievements of Saemaul Undong (새마을事業)

*   With the leader (指導者) at the center, the spirit of unity (融和 團結) and mutual assistance (相扶相助) has been established, and all matters are handled democratically (民主的) at the general meeting (總會席上),
*   Through the development of wasteland (野山開發), reform of agricultural techniques (農事技術), and successful cultivation of special crops (特用作物栽培) with renewed seeds (種子更新), income (所得) has increased,
*   By expanding the cultivation of unified rice varieties (統一系統벼), developing wasteland (野山), and cultivating special crops (特用作物) such as corn, and from high-quality vegetables (高等蔬菜) and horticultural crops (園藝作物) to silvopasture (穀樹林栽培), efforts have been made to double residents' income (住民所得),
*   The cultivation of unified rice varieties (統一系統벼) has achieved 126% of the planned area (計劃面積) with 20.3ha, aiming for a yield of 700kg per 10a (反當), and
*   Wheat (麥類) has achieved 108% of the planned area (計劃面積) with 22.3ha, with a yield of 350kg per 10a (反當), and special crops (特用作物) with 17.2ha, and wasteland (野山) with 10ha of greenhouses (中  비닐하우스) for cultivating corn, etc.,
*   Every household (農家) raises at least one livestock (家畜), with no household without a cow or a pig,
*   600 persimmon trees (穀樹林) have been planted, expecting an income of 10,000 won per tree (株當) in the 1980s (80年代), with a total expected income (總收益) of 60 million won (千萬).


--- (p. 413) ---

In the 1980s, a household income of 2.5 million won appears to be a bright prospect.

### 3. Future Development Plans

* Expansion of the Onggi (Korean traditional pottery) Factory
  - Transform the existing small-scale (50 pyeong) traditional Onggi factory into a modern large-scale factory, aiming to enterprise it, and invest the idle labor force of the village to increase income.
* Simple Water Supply Facilities
  - Install an automatic pump and develop underground water. In 1978, it is planned to provide simple water supply facilities to all 54 farming households. The village fund of 250,000 won will be invested, and the design for free installation has been completed.
* Now, with the installation of a telephone, we are dreaming that we will not lag behind the cultural life level of the city.

### 4. Village Assembly

#### ♦ Meeting Minutes (1)

* Date: February 17, 1974
* Venue: Lee Jong-cheol's House
* Agenda: Election of Leader
* Attendees: Oh Se-jong and 36 others
* Absentees: Yu Byeong-seon and 11 others
* Chairperson: Lee Jong-cheol

Chairperson: I have called you all here late at night because, as you can see, other villages have been transforming remarkably since they started the Saemaul Undong in 1971. However, our village has not done anything yet and has been consistent with drinking and playing. Not only within the face but also within the county, our village is the most backward. If we continue like this, we will have no face to show our children in the future. Currently, Byeong-ri is working hard as the village head, but as far as I know, no one is properly responding. So, after consulting with a few people, we decided to elect a leader whom everyone can trust and follow, and try to do something developmental.

Choi Seong-hee: Stop talking nonsense! You called busy people here and are making empty talk. What kind of Saemaul Undong is that? We don't even have money.

Chairperson: Saemaul Undong is not about money. I'm sorry, but please listen to my story until the end.


--- (p. 414) ---

I hope you will.
If you recommend people of good will, we will pass it by vote.
Na Se-hwa: Wait a minute! I can't understand what you're suddenly talking about. Please speak slowly so I can think about it! (Temporary silence)
Kim Ui-hwan: That's a good point.
We also go around and see, but other villages are changing beyond recognition. We thought we should do something too, but we need someone reliable. In my opinion, how about Mr. Oh Se-jong?
Chairperson: Good. There is someone who recommends Mr. Oh Se-jong. Are there any objections?
Na Hak-seok: I agree. We can trust him!
Lee Soon-ham: I second the motion. Mr. Oh Se-jong is not only meticulous but also has tremendous drive, so I think he can do it!
Chairperson: Good. If there are any other candidates, please speak up! Anyone you have in mind is fine. (Everyone is silent)
Chairperson: No one? I also think highly of Mr. Oh Se-jong. As you all know, he is a man of integrity and can be trusted with any task. I will distribute paper, so please indicate your approval with an O and your disapproval with an X.
(He distributes the paper. Mr. Oh Se-jong remains silent, only bowing his head)
Chairperson: I was hoping someone would recommend me, but no one did!
Na Se-hwa: Ha! Do you think you can do it? (Everyone bursts into laughter)
Chairperson: (Laughing) That was a joke. Now that the vote is over, I will announce the results.
34 in favor, 3 against. I declare the election.
You haven't said anything yet, but Mr. Oh Se-jong, please come forward and say a few words.
(Mr. Oh Se-jong steps forward with a flushed face)
Oh Se-jong: Thank you. However, three people opposed me. Therefore, I will decline this position until those who opposed me support me. (He seems to have had some thoughts)
Let me ask you. If there is anyone who still opposes me, please raise your hand. (No one does. Only Choi Seong-hee leaves with a displeased expression)
Oh Se-jong: Then, assuming there is no one who opposes me, I will take on the role of village chief and say a few words. I understand that you all unanimously decided to believe in and follow me as your village chief.
From now on, I will handle everything through actions rather than words. As I have always felt, to turn this backward village into a new community, there may be some personal loss for each of you, but I ask that you continue to believe in and follow me as you do now. If there is even a little opposition or criticism of what I do, I will resign from this position that day... (He looks around at the residents)
After that, leave everything to me!

Date: December 12, 1975
Venue: Village Community Center
Agenda: Selection of Businesses for Presidential Grant and Fund Usage

Secretary: Yang Young-soo, Local Agricultural and Forestry Office
Chair: Village Head Oh Se-jong

Chair: Out of the 49 attendees, 47 are present, making a quorum. Now, let us discuss how to use the 1 million won granted by President Park at the National Saemaul Leadership Conference on November 28, 1975. Please share your opinions on what businesses we should undertake and how we should manage them.

Kim Young-seon: In my opinion, there are many tasks such as stream improvement, wall reinforcement, and sewer maintenance, but we can handle those with our own efforts. I think it would be better to focus on income-generating businesses.

Myung No-heon: That is a valid point, but starting an income-generating business carries the risk of failure due to lack of experience. Perhaps we could start by purchasing communal farmland and gradually explore other business opportunities after gaining some insight.

Choi Seong-hui: That's a good idea. Incidentally, there is a piece of land for sale in Pangyo-ri owned by Lee Geun-chang: 450.1 pyeong of rice fields and 479 pyeong of dry fields. What do you think about purchasing that?

Choi Jong-jin: That's perfect timing. I agree with that.
All: That seems like a safe business. I agree.

Chair: Then, we need to determine the price and address post-management issues.
Choi Seong-hui: Please do not worry about that.
Last time, I negotiated a deal where Lee Geun-chang asked for 1.5 million won, and the buyer offered up to 1.49 million won. Lee held out for 1,496,000 won, but the deal fell through over a trivial 6,000 won. If our village adds 496,000 won to the presidential grant, we can afford it.

Chair: That sounds good. Our village's communal fund is around 6 million won, so setting the land price at 1,496,000 won seems reasonable.
All: Agreed.

Chair: Then, management is an issue. If anyone has good suggestions, please share them.
Lee Jong-cheol: Since it is communal farmland, we should share the effort and reinvest the profits into the village's communal fund for future business opportunities.
Kim In-seok: I fully support that.
All: Agreed. I agree.

**Absentees:** 13

**Chairperson:** We have gathered you all here today to discuss how to utilize the proceeds from the barley harvest, which amounted to 8 units, cultivated from the field purchased through the President's donation project last December 1975. I would like to hear your opinions on how to use these proceeds.

**Myung No-heon:** Please provide a detailed breakdown of the net profit after deducting farming expenses.

**Chairperson:** I was just about to explain. As you all know, the total revenue of 8 units of barley is equivalent to 72,000 won at the current market price. After deducting the farming expenses, which include the cost of fertilizers (urea at 2,400 won per bag and compound at 4,400 won for two bags), totaling 6,800 won, the net profit amounts to 65,000 won. That concludes my report. If anyone has any good suggestions on how to use this money, please share your thoughts.

**Kim Mu-hong:** I understand. In my opinion, we could accumulate this money and, when we have enough, invest it in public projects for our village.

**Lee Young-seop:** In my opinion, since our village has not yet completed the roof improvement project by 100%, I think it would be better to use this money to support those in our village who are struggling to improve their roofs due to financial difficulties.

**Choi Jong-jin:** That's a good point. I also encourage those in need to improve their roofs, but I feel hesitant because I know their financial situations well. It would be best to select a few of the most financially struggling individuals and support them with this money.

**Na Hak-seok:** Agreed. I support this idea.

**Chairperson:** There is a motion of support. Are there any objections?
