# Minutes (會議錄) (6)

*   **Date(日時)**: December 20, 1976
*   **Location(場所)**: Village Community Center
*   **Agenda(議提)**: Irrigation Facilities for Communal Rice Fields (共同畓)
*   **Attendees(參席人員)**: Lee Jong-cheol and 40 others
*   **Absentees(不參人員)**: 17
*   **Chair(司會)**: Village Head Oh Se-jong (吳世鍾)

**Chair(司會)**: I am truly sorry to have called you all here so late. The reason is that we have completed the settlement for the past two months in November, but as you all know, the communal rice fields that we are cultivating with the President (大統領) His Excellency's (閣下) grant are rain-fed (天水畓), and without rain, farming is almost impossible. Fortunately, this year was not too dry, but we cannot predict what will happen in the future. Therefore, I thought that if we could make it possible to receive the nearby stream flowing next to the rice fields this winter, what do you think? I have called you all here to hear your opinions.

**Kim Mu-hong (金武洪)**: I oppose this. The rice fields are all terraced, and there is at least a 2-cheok (尺) difference between the lowest and highest fields. To make them all level, we would have to dig the lower fields by 2-cheok to create a uniform terrace. In reality, it would take at least ten days to two weeks to mobilize the entire village (全住民) for this task. Moreover, there would be many problems with handling the soil. I think it would be much easier to undertake a different project rather than this difficult construction with little effect.

**Chair(司會)**: Kim Mu-hong's (金武洪) point is valid, but I have also considered these problems. However, I do not think it would take as much time as you might think. If we dig the upper fields to fill the lower ones, we would only need to dig about half a cheok (尺), which would be sufficient to receive the stream. Furthermore, if we create irrigation-safe rice fields (水利安全畓), not only would farming become more convenient, but we would also be able to manage the water on time, increasing our income. Moreover, the value of the rice fields would rise by more than twice the current market price (時價). Therefore, we would be able to increase our profits without doing anything. Additionally, I calculate that the work period would take about three days.

**Choi Seong-hee (崔成熙)**: I agree with the village head's opinion. I have also had this idea. If we mobilize tractors and carts, it would take at most two days.

**Myung No-heon (明魯憲)**: Agreed. I second the motion.

**All (一同)**: Agreed.

**Na Hu-seok (羅厚碩)**: Then when will we start?

**Chair(司會)**: Since it will be busy around the New Year, what about starting from the 6th to the 7th? That sounds good.

**Chair(司會)**: Then, it is unanimously decided, and we will adjourn the meeting for today.


--- (p. 423) ---

# Chungcheongnam-do (충남) Yesan County (예산군) Yesan-eup (예산읍) Changso 1-ri (창소1리)

## 1. Overview of the Village

### a. History

* During the Joseon (李朝) era, large warehouses were built along the upper reaches of the West Sea (西海) Asan Bay (牙山灣), specifically at the mouth of the Muhancheon (무한천) River. Agricultural (農產物) and marine products (海產物) were shipped to Hanseong (漢陽) (present-day Seoul) via Incheon Port (仁川港), which led to the village being named Changso-ri (倉所里).
* This village has a small hill at its center, which resembles the shape of a mouse's head, hence the alternative name Seodu-mul (鼠頭物).
* The village originally consisted of two natural hamlets: Naeseodu-mul and Oeseodu-mul. On March 20, 1972, as part of an administrative district (行政區域) reorganization, Oeseodu-mul became Changso 1-ri (창소1리) and Naeseodu-mul became Changso 2-ri (창소2리).

### b. Location and Conditions

**Location**

* Located approximately 6 km from the Yesan County Office (禮山郡廳) in all directions.
* Situated along National Route 21 (國道 21호).

**Conditions**

* The village is located along a road, making it a convenient (便利) plain village with excellent transportation (交通).
* It is an ideal location for high-quality vegetable (高等蔬菜) cultivation using greenhouses (비닐하우스).

### c. Basic Situation

## 2. Village Development Process

### Ga. Situation Before 1970

#### 1) Basic Environment
- At that time, before the area was divided into District 1 and District 2, a river flowing through the middle of the village meandered freely. Even with 80mm of rain, the river would flood, causing farmland to be lost and submerged, resulting in severe damage. Additionally, 25 households along the riverbank had to endure the floodwaters.
- The only means of transportation were paths along the ridges of rice paddies and fields, carried on one's back.
- Excluding about 10 wealthy farming households, the roofs of other homes were thatched with straw, rotting and sunken, with weeds growing abundantly.
- The structure of the houses: about 50% of the total households in the village, around 60 households, lived in earthen houses made of mud. The ancillary buildings were also made of mud or thatch, open to the sky, in a primitive state. Many houses had no heated floor (ondol) or veranda, and the kitchens had earthen stoves, which were very unsanitary. There were no cabinets for displaying dishes.
- There were no farm roads, not even access roads, only winding paths like snakes.

#### 2) Income Level
- The village had inherited about 50 hectares of farmland from ancestors, where they only grew rice in the paddies and barley, wheat, and beans in the fields. The average farmland per household was about 0.5 hectares, with an annual average income per household of around 242 won, which was quite low.
- Adjacent to Asan Bay in the West Sea, along the Muhancheon River, summer and autumn saw shrimp paste boats arriving, which the villagers would buy and resell, serving as the sole source of non-agricultural income.


--- (p. 425) ---

O The only livestock were a few head of Korean cattle and pigs, and among all the villages in the district, this one had the lowest income level and was the most backward.

### 3) Mental State (精神狀態)
O With an average annual household income of only 242,000 won, residents lived in abject poverty and ignorance, yet no one had the will to improve their lives. Instead, they idled away their time during the farming off-season, gathering in groups of 20 or more to drink and gamble, leading a degenerate lifestyle.

### 4) Culture (文化) and Daily Life (衣食住生活)
O Life was lived by the dim light of kerosene lamps, with even bamboo paper fans being a rarity.
O News was scarce, with only a few newspapers or magazines circulating, leaving residents far removed from current events.
O Summer attire consisted solely of hemp ramie shirts, while winter clothing was limited to indigo-dyed cotton pants and jackets.
O With food scarce, residents would squander what little they had on alcohol and gambling, forcing them to rely on high-interest loans for rice in the spring and survive on barley porridge before the harvest, enduring the hardships of the spring famine.
O Walls were covered with old books or torn fertilizer sacks, and floors were laid with straw mats made from rice straw, creating an unpleasant environment filled with the smells of infant waste and filth.
O Kitchens had blackened, doorless cabinets filled with dishes, while pigsties overflowed with waste that attracted countless flies and insects, creating a squalid environment in which residents lived as if bound by an ancestral fate.

## B. Implementation of the Saemaul Undong (運動)
### 1) Motivation (動機) and Trial Project Results (試驗事業)
O Five residents, including Kim Gi-yeol, Jeon Bong-seon, Kim Gi-bok, Park Tae-gyu, and Kim Il-hwan, who had graduated from Yeosan Agricultural High School, formed the Nonguhoe (農友會) with a firm resolve to break free from the village's chronic laziness and generations of poverty. Their first venture was to cultivate high-value vegetables, starting with Chinese cabbage and cucumbers.
O The five members of Nonguhoe pooled their skills and knowledge to cultivate 250 pyeong of Chinese cabbage and 250 pyeong of cucumbers. While other residents indulged in drinking and gambling during the cold month of December, they erected bamboo frames and covered them with plastic sheeting to create a greenhouse.


--- (p. 426) ---

When they saw five young people making a pit inside the house and putting straw in it to decompose in order to raise the temperature inside the house and use the resulting heat for seedling cultivation, the attitude of the residents was one of skepticism or even slander and malicious criticism.

*   Despite this, these individuals devoted all their passion to growing cucumbers and Chinese cabbage inside the greenhouse.
As the saying goes, "Where there is a will, there is a way," and they succeeded. In 1965, they achieved remarkable income of 250,000 won from cucumbers, 300,000 won from Chinese cabbage, totaling 550,000 won (in the currency of that time). Based on this one-year experience, they decided to further expand vinyl greenhouse farming and began actively recommending it to other residents. Residents, who had lived as if poverty was their destiny, started to realize that they too could live well by working hard and making consistent efforts. In this way, the number of participating farms gradually increased, and today, every farm in the village practices vinyl greenhouse farming. Describing the current situation, the area of the greenhouses is 12 hectares, and they cultivate high-quality vegetables with more than four crops per year, resulting in a net profit of 86 million won. This has become the village's largest source of income.

*   Along with the efforts of five members of the Nonguhoe (農友會) to increase income, Park Sam-shin, a graduate of Yesan Agricultural High School, dedicated himself to leading the village's development by transforming idle spirits into diligence and teaching cooperation. Park Sam-shin, who had nurtured dreams of local development since his high school days, devoted all his passion to local development instead of seeking employment after graduation. To remove the dark veil of poverty and create a healthy, prosperous, and wealthy village, he persuaded the residents with firm resolve and passion. In the process, in 1967, they decided to make the land improvement project a communal endeavor to change the residents' mental state, which had been wasted on alcohol and gambling, and to create a diligent atmosphere. The residents, who had initially been fond of playing, were not inclined to comply with Park Sam-shin's words from the beginning. However, by continuously persuading them that implementing land improvement could enhance soil fertility and increase yields from the limited farmland, he declared that it was our generation's duty to break free from the shackles of poverty, which they had considered their destiny, and leave a glorious inheritance for future generations.

*   Through such appeals, from autumn 1967 to spring 1968, approximately 3,500 people in total participated in the land improvement project over a period of about three months, covering 10 hectares of the village's aging farmland. Through the land improvement project, the residents learned cooperation and transformed their lazy habits into diligent attitudes. News of this spread, and they received words of encouragement and a monetary reward from the then-mayor of Yesan County. Furthermore, they received words of encouragement and a monetary reward from the governor of Chungcheongnam-do. Among the governor's words of encouragement, the village was praised as a village where "evergreen trees of humanity" reside, an evaluation beyond their station. Additionally, this fact was introduced nationwide in the Daejeon Ilbo and Jungdo Ilbo newspapers. After this, everything in the village was undergoing a transformation. The past laziness, poverty, and alcohol


--- (p. 427) ---

Gambling gradually disappeared, and the villagers began to unite under the leadership of Mr. Park Sam-shin.
- Here, Mr. Park Sam-shin boosted the villagers' morale and sought to increase their income by borrowing 1.5 million won in agricultural special funds from Yeosan County Office and distributing one Hanwoo cow each to 30 farming households to raise. The construction of cattle sheds for raising cows led to natural environmental improvements. Based on this, the shabby attached sheds that had been passed down for thousands of years began to be transformed into connected structures, and nearby residents even whispered that they were better than human dwellings.
- This can be considered the beginning of the Saemaul Undong in this village, and it turns out that the Saemaul Undong was actually taking place in this village three years before it was nationwide.
With environmental improvements, increased income, and diligent residents, the village also indirectly generated income by using manure from cow sheds for vinyl house farming.
- In 1969, the village continued to expand the improvement of attached sheds for environmental improvement, while also implementing roof and housing improvement projects in parallel.
- To instill a sense of dignity and patriotism in the residents, the village invented and installed national flag raising platforms in every household.
- A watchtower was set up on the hill behind the village to guard against 10 nearby villages and achieve perfect self-defense. Two guard posts were even set up at the village entrance.
The national flag raising platforms invented and installed in this village can be said to be a good example of a project expanded throughout the province.
The national flag raising platforms installed in the village were set up in every household with a donation of 60,000 won from Mr. Lee Hyo-yeon, a villager who was working in West Germany and had temporarily returned home on leave.
- The development process of the village clearly shows how crucial the role of a dedicated and capable leader is.
From poverty and laziness, and from the mire of alcohol and gambling, this village became a model village with increased income, improved environment, and a strong anti-communist spirit, even receiving a plaque of appreciation from the chairman of the Korean Anti-Communist League on February 14, 1969.
- Countless criticisms and mockery turned into cooperation and diligence, and the village was gradually changing. However, since the village had been so deteriorated for so long, there was still much to do in 1970. Now, Changso Village was no longer the past Changso Village, but an image of a prosperous and harmonious village was emerging.
The village became one where there were no days off and no idle people throughout the four seasons. To achieve high income from a small piece of land, the village continued to expand the cultivation of high-quality vegetables using vinyl houses, and actively promoted special crops suitable for the village's soil. A good example of special crop cultivation is the collective cultivation of burdock on 2 hectares of sandy soil.


--- (p. 428) ---

Thus, the village was able to increase its annual income by 2 million won, and this effect also spread to the neighboring Shinam-myeon, greatly contributing to regional income growth.

O Mr. Park Sam-shin, who was dedicated solely to the development of the village, had countless tasks on his mind. However, the most urgent matter was the improvement project of the small stream (Sohacheon) flowing through the center of the village.

Even with just 80mm of rain, the stream would flood, submerging farmland and inundating 25 houses nearby. He proposed to the villagers to improve the small stream. The elderly dismissed it as madness, asking how they could possibly develop such a large stream. However, Mr. Park joined forces with the young adults and, with the participation of 2,800 villagers, successfully improved a 400m section of the Changsocheon.

Mr. Park Sam-shin, a volunteer leader, reaffirmed his commitment to his guiding principle of selfless dedication solely for the village's development: "A single grain of wheat rots to leave countless seeds."

O To promote environmental improvement for the poor village residents, Mr. Park secured a dump truck from the Yesan County Office, mobilized the villagers, and piled up sand and gravel in the village square. He also used his personal funds to purchase cement, accelerating the block production and environmental improvement projects. Moreover, Mr. Park provided the village's 'community square' using his own funds. He purchased 520 pyeong of land belonging to Kim Hyeon-gap, a villager, for 300,000 won, where block production and community work for environmental improvement took place. Thus, Mr. Park Sam-shin, the volunteer leader, invested 1.8 million won. As mentioned earlier, Mr. Park Sam-shin could undertake such tasks because he had long pledged to dedicate himself to this poor and arid village.

No villager could help but be moved. Such events had never occurred since the village's establishment, making the impact even greater. These facts will remain as a legacy for future generations as long as the village exists.

O When news spread that an unnamed farmer's son was working in obscurity, on November 11, 1970, he received the direct honor of being awarded the Industrial Merit Medal from President (大統領) himself, a tearful moment of glory.

Mr. Park Sam-shin, the leader, dedicated himself not to gain recognition or awards but solely for the village's development. The villagers, awakened from their ignorance, worked diligently. The past days of this village, when it was steeped in poverty and indulged in the decadent waste of time with alcohol and gambling, have now become a stained page in the village's history.

## 2) First-Year Trial Project Results

In 1970, when President Park Chung-hee launched the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), it began to spread across the nation. This village also had the opportunity to receive 335 bags of cement for the Saemaul Undong from the government for the first time.

However, to use the cement efficiently, the entire village's consensus was needed for implementation. With this in mind, a village general meeting was planned in consultation with Kim Gi-jong, who was the village chief at the time.


--- (p. 429) ---

On September 29, 1970, the term "Saemaul beautification project (事業)" was still unfamiliar to the residents, and they were informed about it. Additionally, a plan was conceived for a project involving 335 bags of Saemaul cement (洋灰) to be supported by the government. The situation at that time, when a plan for the Saemaul beautification support project (事業) was being drafted, was as follows.

◆ Minutes of the Meeting (會議錄)

**Venue**: Village Community Center
**Date**: September 29, 1970
**Attendees**: 98 people
**Attending Officials**: Kim Gi-dae
**Chairperson**: Village Head
**Agenda**:
1. Introduction to the Saemaul beautification movement
2. Decision on the Saemaul beautification project (事業)

**Chairperson**: Residents, thank you very much for gathering here in such large numbers. Today, we have convened this village general assembly (總會) to discuss the Saemaul beautification project (事業) initiated by President Park Chung-hee. First, our village's assigned officer will provide detailed information about the Saemaul beautification movement (運動), so please listen carefully.

**Assigned Officer**: Thank you. I am the assigned officer Kim Gi-dae. As mentioned by the village head, I will now explain the Saemaul beautification movement (運動) initiated by President Park Chung-hee. Please listen carefully and use this as a reference when formulating your plans (explanation omitted).

**Chairperson**: I believe you have all listened carefully to the assigned officer's explanation of the Saemaul beautification movement (運動). Now, please share your thoughts on the plans that our village should undertake.

**Park Sam-shin**: You have all worked very hard to develop our village. However, it seems there is still much to be done. Based on the Saemaul beautification movement plan (運動計劃), I have conceived the following plan. First, to improve our living conditions, we should widen the village roads to accommodate rickshaws and horse-drawn carts. Second, when constructing these roads, we should install underground drainage facilities (暗渠施設) where they connect to rivers or ditches. Third, we should create laundry facilities near the rivers we have developed, so that housewives can easily do their laundry. Fourth, we should repair the 3-hectare rain-fed fields (天水畓) to make them safe fields (安全畓) by installing repair facilities (修理施設物). Lastly, we should renovate the shared wells (共同井戶) to ensure that we have access to hygienic well water. Among the many tasks at hand, I propose that we prioritize these projects as our first phase.

**Chairperson**: I believe you have all listened carefully to Park Sam-shin's explanation of our village's Saemaul beautification project plan (事業計劃). What are your thoughts on this?

**Residents**: We agree (majority).

**Chairperson**: If there are any other opinions, please share them.


--- (p. 430) ---

Resident: There is none. Let's proceed with Mr. Park Sam-shin's plan.
Society (社會): Then, we will proceed with Mr. Park Sam-shin's plan for our village's Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) business. We hope for your active cooperation (協助), residents. Today's general meeting (總會) will conclude here. Thank you very much.

Thus, after the residents' general meeting (住民總會議), the villagers, with volunteer leaders (自願指導者) as the core, began the village road expansion project (擴張事業) and the formal Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) business commenced. In fact, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) had been unfolding in this village since three years prior, in 1968, so the villagers' cooperation (協同) and unity (團結) were well established.

The first year of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) beautification project (事業) progressed without any issues. In particular, the villagers' trust (信望度) in volunteer leader (自願指導者) Park Sam-shin (朴三信) was very high, so everything proceeded smoothly and in an orderly fashion.

Here, let us briefly introduce the guiding principles (指導指針) that Park Sam-shin (朴三信) has personally held in his heart since his school days (學窓時節) for the development (發展) of the local community (地域社會): "Know yourself," "Reflect on yourself," and "Realize yourself." Additionally, his practical guidelines (實踐要綱) were "When you open your mouth, speak words that help" and "When you move, do things that help." He even invested his own private funds (私財) and dedicated himself (獻身努力) to the village, so the residents all recognized him as a genuine village leader (指導者).

Therefore, all the villagers, in a combined atmosphere (總和), were able to complete many projects (事業) beyond the planned (計劃) amount in approximately six months, from September 28, 1970, to the end of March 1971. It was truly an enormous effect (効果) that was achieved.

Thus, on April 2, 1971, the village received an award in the social welfare (社會福祉) category of the Hyangto Culture Award (鄕土文化賞), given to those selected by the Ministry of Culture and Information (文化公報部) as evergreen trees (常綠樹) among humanity (人間).

In the first year of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) beautification campaign (運動) initiated by President (大統領) Park Chung-hee (朴正熙), this village achieved remarkable results, hundreds of percent (數百) above the planned (計劃) business (事業).

### 3. Leader (指導者) Activities (活動) and Replacement Situation (交替狀況)

Due to the administrative district (行政區域) reorganization (改編) on March 20, 1972, this hamlet (部落) was divided into two natural hamlets (自然部落) and became Changso-ri (倉所里) 1-gu (區) and 2-gu (區). Park Sam-shin (朴三信), who had been working until now, was in the 2-gu (區) village, so he became the 2-gu (區) leader (指導者). The newly divided Changso-ri (倉所里) 1-gu (區) needed to elect a new leader (指導者).

Although the village had developed to some extent (程度), it felt empty after being halved. However, with new resolve, the villagers elected a new Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) leader (指導者) and took new steps forward (出發).

### Saemaul Undong Achievements and Exemplary Leader Cases

With the newly elected Saemaul leaders (指導者) at the center, we began to accomplish one village project (事業) after another. These included paving 300 meters of village roads, installing 400 meters of sewers (下水溝), expanding 700 meters of farm roads (農路擴張), installing 30 meters of clay pipes (土管), creating two communal laundries (共同 빨래터), repairing one village hall (會舘), and installing a 5-pyeong (坪) communal bathhouse (共同沐浴湯), among many other projects. We also promoted roof improvements (地붕 개량) and attached house (附屬舍) improvements.

In October 1974, Jeon Young-woo (全永愚), a leader (指導者) from a neighboring village, Gwanjak-ri, who had been dedicated (獻身) to improving the lazy (懶怠) and impoverished (貧困) living environment (生活環境), was an college graduate (學士出身) who had a strong will (意思) to develop rural areas (農村地域). He moved to this area, which had been a refuge (避亂處) during the war (戰亂), leaving his life in Seoul behind (淸算), and had been living in Gwanjak village. With his capable leadership (有能指導力) and dedicated efforts (獻身的努力), he guided (指導) Gwanjak village to be promoted (昇級) to a self-reliant village (自立村) in 1973, making him an elite leader (指導者).


--- (p. 432) ---

At that time, there was a peculiar project: they drilled holes in bamboo to create water pipes, making hundreds of meters of waterways to transform rain-fed fields into irrigated ones. This fact truly showed that there was a capable and diligent leader who researched and strove for improvement.

Such a leader, Kim Jeon-hwan, moved to Changso 1-gu village and decided to pass the baton to Jeon Young-woo. The goal was to further develop the village.

At the Residents' Assembly, Mr. Jeon Young-woo was appointed as the new Saemaul leader of the village.

Jeon Young-woo dedicated himself to guiding the village. By the end of 1975, he was able to upgrade the village to a self-reliant one at the Saemaul Movement General Review. In 1976, he presented the success story of the Saemaul Undong in Changso 1-gu at the National Saemaul Leaders Conference, elevating the village to a nationally representative Saemaul. He also had the honor of receiving the Saemaul Medal of Cooperation from the President (大統領).

As mentioned earlier, the role of capable leaders like Jeon Young-woo in the village's development process was so influential that there is no room for debate. With such a capable leader, the village became flawless in all aspects, including production base, public facilities, and welfare and environmental projects. The income level was also at a high standard comparable to advanced countries. Through improvement projects for the village structure, it became an urbanized rural area, not just a countryside.

This rapidly developed village also became a field education village for the Suwon Saemaul Leaders Training Institute, educating leaders on multiple occasions and continuing to serve as an education site.

Jeon Young-woo has now become a nationally recognized Saemaul leader, enlightening others through Saemaul Undong case studies in various Saemaul education programs.

## 4) Overcoming Challenges

Numerous challenges and hardships were faced to reach the current state of the village. The most significant challenge was obtaining land for village roads and farm roads through donations. In reality, cutting into farmland is like cutting one's own flesh, as it is essential for agriculture. However, creating a legacy for future generations is not something that can be easily achieved.

During the process of opening a 500-meter farm road, approximately 300 pyeong of land was needed for incorporation. Despite persistent persuasion day and night, consent was not obtained, so part of it was left and later pushed forward semi-forcibly. Those who had strongly refused at that time now feel sorry for their actions and appreciate the convenience of the farm road.

## 7) Special (特記) Matters (事項)
### a) Joyful Events
Overcoming all hardships (苦難) and adversities (逆境), this village presented a successful (成功) case (事例) at the National (全國) Saemaul Undong (新村運動) Leader (指導者) Conference (大會) held in Daejeon (大田) in 1976. President (大統領) Park (朴) personally awarded the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) Medal (勲章) to Jeon Young-woo (全永愚), the village leader (指導者).

All residents (住民) of the village, forgetting the various pains (苦痛) and sorrows of the past, celebrated with traditional (農樂) music and festivities, which will remain in the history (歷史) of this Saemaul Undong (新村運動) village.

Furthermore, on December 21 of the same year, Chungcheongnam-do (忠淸南道) Governor (知事) Jeong Seok-mo (鄭石模) visited (視察) the village and promised (約束) to support (支援) the development (育成) of this village as a comprehensive (綜合) model (示範) Saemaul Undong (新村運動) village, which was a significant (慶事) event for the village.

Additionally, the selection (策定) of this village for the 1977 Cluster (聚落) Structure (構造) Improvement (改善) Project (事業) was another joyful (事例) for our village.


--- (p. 434) ---

### n) Sad Events

When we couldn't receive land donations (喜捨) for the construction of village roads and farm roads (農路), we couldn't push forward the work smoothly. The leaders had to break up the completed roads from the parts where land had been donated and plow the donated land again to plant crops. The path for the leaders at that time was more rugged than a thorny path.

## Ba. Achievements (成果) from the New Village (事業)

### 1) Spiritual Aspect (精神面)

*   The residents, who were once lazy (懶怠) and impoverished (貧困), learned the new image (人間像) of diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperation (協同) through the Saemaul Undong (事業);
*   Through the process (過程) of promoting (推進) the Saemaul Undong (事業), they gained a firm (確固) sense of confidence (自信感) that they can achieve (做到) anything;
*   The residents learned Korean-style (韓國的) democracy (民主主義) where the entire community (全體) can gather (集合) and comprehensively (綜合) integrate (整合) each other's opinions (意思) through dialogue (對話).
*   They deepened their gratitude (感謝) towards the nation (祖國) and broadened their magnanimity (雅量) to live in harmony (和睦) with their neighbors (鄰居).


--- (p. 436) ---

## 2) Living Aspect
With the improvement of agricultural techniques and the expansion of vinyl house farming, life became more affluent, and farmers, as scholars and researchers, adopted a proactive attitude. Rather than a selfish attitude of wanting to live well alone, they embraced a cooperative approach where the well-being of all villagers meant their own prosperity.

## 3) Production Aspect
Through the cultivation of high-value vegetables using vinyl houses, income saw a dramatic increase. Additionally, by expanding the cultivation of unified system new rice varieties, the village rose as a rural city that was not inferior to advanced countries, not a city but a thriving rural urban area.

## 4. Future Development Vision
### a. Income Increase
22 hectares of farmland have been reorganized, and recently, automatic misting systems (sprinkler coolers) have been installed, along with electric seedling raising machines. By maximizing the use of these facilities, scientific farming methods are being researched and developed. The current system of four crops per year will be expanded to six or more crops per year, maximizing the productivity per unit of limited land to its highest level. Every effort will be made to achieve the goal of an average household income of 5 million won by 1980.

### b. Construction of a Comprehensive Welfare Center
A comprehensive welfare center of about 200 pyeong will be constructed, including a library, office, purchasing and sales area, senior citizen center, emergency treatment room, and meeting room.

### c. Establishment of a Scholarship System
A scholarship fund of over 50 million won will be established to provide full tuition coverage for high school education for students in this village, striving for the best in improving educational levels.


--- (p. 437) ---

# Chungcheongnam-do (충남) Dangjin-gun (당진군) Seokmun-myeon (석문면) Samhwa-2-ri (삼화2리)

1. Overview of the Village (마을의 개황)

a. History (연혁)

This village was known as "Oechang (외창)" during the Goryeo (高麗) Hyunjong (顯宗) era. The name "Oechang (外倉)" originated from the fact that there was a port (浦口) connected to the sea, and this port had a warehouse (倉庫) for storing military grain (軍糧米). In 1914, during the administrative district (行政區域) reorganization (改編), the three villages of "Songdang (松堂)," "Oechang (外倉)," and "Damosseok (담꼿)" were merged to form Samhwa-ri (三花里). Later, in 1958, it was further divided into Samhwa (三花) 1, 2, and 3 districts (區), leading to the current (現在) configuration.

b. Location and Conditions (위치 및 여건)

The village is located 12 km north (北) of the county office (郡廳) and 2.5 km northeast (東北向) of the town hall (面 所在地). The northern end (北端) of the village is adjacent to a 2 km coastline (海岸線) and is surrounded by gentle hills (順坦한 야산), offering scenic (秀麗) and abundant (豊盛) surroundings. A local road (地方道路) runs through the center of the village, with regular buses (定期 버스) operating 4-5 times a day (回).

c. Basic Situation (기본현황)

## 2. Village Development Process (發展過程)

### A. Situation Before 1970 (70年以前的狀況)

1) **Basic Environment (基礎環境)**
The total number of houses in the village was 179, but only 8 had undergone roof improvements. The densely packed substandard housing, such as "thatched fences," spoke volumes about the village's poverty. The village community center was using a privately owned wooden building, and the farm roads were winding footpaths where agricultural products were still carried in "back baskets," indicating a primitive agricultural village that could not escape its backwardness.

2) **Income Level (所得水準)**
The average income of farming households, which primarily relied on agricultural income (耕種所得), was a mere 670,000 won. Among this, non-agricultural income did not exceed 20%, and the monoculture farming focused on rice and wheat resulted in a meager living standard that the villagers could not escape.

3) **Mental State (精神狀態)**
The central area of the village, known as "Saeter-mal," was infamous for its decadence. The tavern there was always bustling with gambling and drinking. The villagers' conversations were filled with distrust and gossip about each other, and their mindset was extremely calculating, selfish, skeptical, and indifferent to the village's affairs. This general attitude of the villagers was a significant obstacle to the village's development.

### B. Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動의推進)

1) **Motivation and Trial Project Results (動機及試驗事業的成果)**
Until 1972, this village remained a backward and stagnant community. While neighboring villages were actively engaged in the Saemaul Undong, this village merely watched from afar with cold indifference. Faced with this disheartening reality, Han Daegun, then 46 years old, silently struggled with his frustration and determination.

- He had returned to Korea in October 1945 after attending middle school in Japan. Without a single pyeong of land to his name, he carried a "backpack" and traveled as a peddler.


--- (p. 439) ---

With the filial piety (孝心) of wanting to warmly welcome his parents (父母님), he settled in Samhwa (三花) 2-gu (區) village, borrowed and reclaimed abandoned mountains, and sustained his parents' livelihood from the harvest of the approximately 1,000 pyeong (坪) of land. While others mocked him, saying, "Didn't you study at a high school (學校) abroad? Are you now working as a mole?", he possessed an unparalleled belief (信念) and will (意志).

O He made filial piety (孝道) to his parents (父母) and faith and love to his neighbors his life creed (生活信條), and he, who only waited for retribution (應報) through diligent (健實) efforts (努力), received an appointment (任命) as an elder (長老) from the superintendent (監理師) in 1956 (年), the year he turned 30 (才).

O Even in difficult circumstances, his filial piety (孝心) was extreme (至極), taking his parents (父母님) to Seoul once a year (年) and always ensuring they had clean clothes (衣服). His wife, Song Bunsun (宋分順) female historian (女史), who assisted (內助) him with feminine virtue (婦德), serving his parents (父母님) wholeheartedly (極盡) regardless of cold or heat, was also a model household (模範家庭) head (家長) who received the Filial Wife Award (孝婦賞) from the Governor (道知事) of Chungcheongnam-do (忠淸南道) in 1974 (年) March (月). Han Daegun (韓大根), who always took the lead in resolving unpleasant tasks that others hesitated to undertake, is known to the world (世上) as a person of character (人格).

Unable to bear seeing his village fall into desolation (荒廢), he yearned for the "Saetmal" liquor district to be swept into the furnace of the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) fervor (熱風) as soon as possible. Feeling the pain of this reality (現實), he spent several days and nights deep in thought before reaching a firm resolution (決心). He vowed to dedicate his entire being and all his passion (情熱) to the glory (榮光) of his village's future (來日).

O On October 1, 1971 (年月日), he held a village general assembly (總會), declared his intention (意思) to voluntarily become a Saemaul Undong (新村運動) leader (指導者), and gained the absolute (絶對的) support (支持) of the residents (住民), becoming a historic (歷史的) Saemaul Undong (新村運動) leader (指導者).

Knowing well that the 335 bags (袋) of cement (洋灰) received as a trial project (試驗事業) for the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) had not been effectively (効果的) used (使用) in this village due to the lack of a solid spiritual foundation (精神), Han Daegun (韓大근), the successor (後位) leader (指導者), first established a step-by-step (段階的) promotion plan (推進計劃) for the Saemaul Undong (新村運動).

## 2) Leader's (指導者) Activity Status (活動狀況)
O He pursued (推進) the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) with the goal (目標) of ideal (理想) rural construction (農村健設) in the 1980s (年代), placing primary (第一義的) emphasis (力點) on spiritual reform (精神改革) of the residents (住民). He established a step-by-step (段階的) development plan (發展計劃) and vowed to pursue (推進) it steadily (着實) until the target year (目標年度).

He designated 1972 (年) as the year of spiritual reform (精神改革) and reorganized (改編) the village organization (組織).

O He created 5 teams (個班) based on natural hamlets (自然部落) and appointed 2 development committee members (開發委員) from each team (各班). Simultaneously, he reorganized (改編) the youth association (靑年會), women's association (女會), 4-H club (會), and senior citizens' association (老人會) into a new system (體制), established a comprehensive promotion system (總和推進體制), and published a village newsletter (會報) to distribute (配付) to all residents (住民), thereby fostering (啓發) their spirit (精神), raising awareness (認識) of current tasks (當面事業), and promoting self-awareness (自覺).

O Although this village became the number one (1位) village in Chungnam (忠南) and gained the honor (榮譽) of being a national standard village (標準마을) as a result of the 1973 (年度) Saemaul Undong (新村運動) general review (總閱), the leader's (指導者) persistent (執念) determination (執念) continued unabated (續). Every day (每日), he would wake up at five in the morning (時), greet his parents (父母님), inspect the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) site (事業場), and begin his daily routine (日課) with new ideas (構想). He would return home at midnight (時), eat cold rice (飯) to satisfy his hungry stomach (腹), and stay awake designing (設計) the next day's (來日) plans (設計). This arduous process (過程) continued daily (每日), making the household (家) situation difficult (難).

O Whenever this happened, he would renew (新) his initial resolve (初志一貫) and determination (覺悟) and had to overcome (受難) the second and third trials (受難).


--- (p. 440) ---

At times, he received baseless slander from the residents while also receiving warm encouragement and thanks. This cycle of lamentation continued.
○ The residents called him "crazy." The Saemaul Movement and a crazy person? Even if his face was struck, he would not retaliate. Even if he was insulted, he would laugh and interfere with others' livelihoods. Some said that in this world, a person who does not know how to live and cannot make ends meet is a "fool." His daily routine of service and sacrifice, not lasting just 1-2 years, made some feel pointless doubt while also leaving an immense impression.
○ The Saemaul Movement is a "practical dojo for cultivating patriotism." This was the philosophy and faith he deeply held in his heart. Gentle and overflowing with human emotion, he was honest, bright with righteousness, and had a strong sense of responsibility. The spirit of sacrificing oneself and serving others! The mind of a leader, always busy, was filled with the design of an ideal rural construction (until the year 81) with clear goals and timelines.
○ The Saemaul Movement is a movement to live well. He always thought about and researched how to connect the Saemaul Movement with income-generating activities and develop them. From this, he came to think in two concepts: one was individual income-generating activities at the household level, and the other was communal income-generating activities at the village level.
○ Communal income-generating activities at the village level could become a breeding ground for the residents' cooperative spirit and played a good role in providing opportunities for interest and participation in the Saemaul Movement. This was because the relationship was directly related to the residents.
○ As a communal income-generating business, they built a factory with 30 pyeong for making sacks and an additional warehouse building. Thanks to the Korean residents in Japan, they purchased and installed one automatic loom and one sewing machine each for 1,950,000 won, enabling the production of 35,000 sacks per year and generating an annual profit of 2,100,000 won. In addition, the village's rice polishing factory, which was initially operated as a joint venture with individual businesses, became a fully village-run business within four years, generating an annual income of 3,000,000 won. The village's communal purchasing and selling market, which started with an investment of 50,000 won in 1973, now generates an annual net income of 600,000 won. A small processing factory, started in 1976 with a construction area of 20 pyeong and a resident's investment of 1,200,000 won, equipped with various flour milling and processing facilities, generates an annual income of 300,000 won. A 10-hectare snail farming site, with a total project cost of 5,000,000 won (3,000,000 won of which was supported by the 1974 economic trend report project funds), started generating an effect from 1976, producing an annual resident income of 8,000,000 won and a village income of 2,000,000 won. Additionally, the rental, usage, or storage income from two village warehouses and a cultivator amounted to an annual income of 400,000 won. Thus, the total village management income reached 7,800,000 won annually, establishing a solid Saemaul management system. In 1977, the village purchased a 2.5-ton communal vehicle for 5,000,000 won, further brightening the prospect of increased income.
○ Particularly, such communal businesses always carried the risk of failure. A Korean leader, well aware that even the slightest flaw in the management subject's sincerity, the manager's sense of responsibility, management methods, or system could easily lead to collapse, took upon himself the fate of success or failure and worked tirelessly day and night.
○ On the other hand, individual income-generating activities actively promoted self-reliant land reclamation to expand farmland, considering the special characteristics of the mountainous region. They developed a 10-hectare reclaimed land into an apple orchard and expanded the cultivation of high-yielding tobacco.


--- (p. 441) ---

In 10 hectares, they are earning an annual income of 20,000,000 won. With autumn vegetable cultivation (菜蔬栽培) and its systematic distribution (系統出荷), the annual income reaches 32,000,000 won. Not only does this account for a significant portion of the village's income, but they are also changing the planting system (作付體係) of vegetables (菜蔬類) to prepare for the forced cultivation (促成栽培) of high-quality vegetables.

A Korean (韓) leader who upholds diligence (勤勉), sincerity (誠實), and frugality (儉素) as his life creed (生活信條) is a treasure of the village (人間), a model for society (社會), and a pioneer (先驅者) of the Saemaul Undong (新村運動). Leading all residents (住民), he is a flag bearer (旗手) striving for a paradise (樂園) beyond an excellent village (優秀新村).

Having established a foundation for self-reliance (自立基盤), he stands at the threshold of cultural rural construction (文化農村建設). Out of a total of 101 households (世帶), 78 have installed telephones (體信電話) through the Kyongyang main line (京鄕要路) over the past two years (76 and 77), enabling them to enjoy the convenience of making clothes and hosting morning birthday celebrations (生日) from the comfort of their homes. Additionally, despite the village work being overwhelming, since 1977, he has voluntarily taken on the role of honorary mayor (名譽面長) of Seokmun-myeon (石門面), dedicating himself to local (面政) and county (郡政) affairs with sincerity (精誠).

Moreover, he is a dedicated leader (指導者) who, at his own expense (自費), helps neighboring small farmers (零細農家) build new homes, replacing their shacks (오두막집).

The Saemaul leader (指導者) from Suwon (水原), Gyeonggi-do (京畿道), has been to the Saemaul leadership training institute (指導者硏修院) and large factories (大規模工場), and has been tirelessly traveling to every corner of the county (道內) to share successful cases (成功事例). Since 1974, he has established a Saemaul leadership on-site living education center (生活敎育場) at the IHwa-2ri (二花2里) Saemaul community center (會舘), inviting 4-5 leaders (指導者) from backward villages (落後新村) across the nation (全國) every term (每期) for a 3-day, 4-night education (敎育) program. The 12 batches of leaders who have passed through this village have almost all turned their own villages into excellent villages (優秀新村), a fact that speaks volumes about the immense satisfaction (보람) and dedication (獻身) of this leader.

In the evenings, he gathers the residents (住民) at the community center (會舘) to conduct wholesome (健全) education programs, including folk song education (歌謠敎育), loyalty and filial piety education (忠孝敎育), farming education (營農敎育), long-term development education for Saemaul projects (事業長期發展敎育), and anti-communist education (反共敎育). He spares no effort (精誠) in undertaking any beneficial (有益) task for the village, regardless of time or place.

His countless tears, joys, and sorrows (哀歡), and his silent (默默) sacrifices (犧牲) and services (奉仕) overcome unknown hardships (苦楚). These invaluable (值錢) contributions are irreplaceable (報償) creations (創造) that will serve as eternal (連綿) examples (龜鑑) of precious national spirit (民族正氣) for future generations.

### 3) Overcoming Difficulties (隘路克服狀況)

Through seven years of the Saemaul Undong (新村運動), he has proven that only an unyielding spirit (百折不屈) and bold advance (果敢突進) can bring about new changes (變革) and construction (建設). Whether it was dealing with poor fences (不良담장), auxiliary buildings (附屬建物), or livestock sheds (畜舍), every transformation (變革) required him to endure all kinds of humiliation (數莫), from being grabbed by the collar (멱살을 잡힘) to being kicked (발길질을 당함). Who would have known that this was the fate (運命) of a leader (指導者) driving innovation (革新)?

For six years, he led the residents (住民) to press forward with their goals (目標事業), overcoming every fall (넘어짐) by standing up again. Those six years were both rewarding (보람) and challenging (苦難).

### 4) Heartwarming Stories (美談佳話)

Han Daegun (韓大根), the leader (指導者), finally had some quiet time with his family (家族). With their livelihood (生計) depending on 2,000 pyeong (坪) of farmland, they had never been able to enjoy the good life (好衣好食) like others. His family's hands were so calloused that they bled,


--- (p. 442) ---

Witnessing his wife tirelessly managing household chores (家事) and personally tending to special crops (特殊作物) to sustain their livelihood (生計)! Even as he returned home late at night, his wife would warmly welcome and comfort (慰勞) her husband (男便), causing him to feel a pang in his heart and a lump in his throat as he caressed his children.

When the O County (郡) Saemaul leaders (指導者) including the cooperative association chairman (議協會長) Kim Jong-in (金鍾仁) and other cooperative association (協議會) residents gathered with sincere efforts (誠意) to prepare 2 seok (石) of white rice (白米) to support his difficult life (生活), not only the leader (韓指導者) but also his family could not help but shed tears. Unable to refuse the heartfelt gift (精誠), he accepted it, consulted with his wife that evening, and contributed it to the women's association (婦女會) fund (基金) to revitalize (活氣) its spirit.

Thanks to the grace of God (하나님의 보살핌), his wife's specialty horticultural cultivation (特用園藝栽培) yields good harvests (收獲) every year, easing the burdens (苦衷) of child education (子女敎育) and household expenses. The home is always (恒常) filled with laughter, a bright (明朗) and exemplary (模範) family that loves its neighbors and respects elders, constantly (恒時) brimming with vitality (活氣).

On April 3, 1973, the Tangjin Education Office (唐津敎育廳) formed a sisterhood alliance (姉妹結緣) with this village, supporting the construction of a village hall (會舘建立) by providing 50 bags (包) of cement (洋灰). Then, on July 18 of the same year, a delegation (一行) of overseas Koreans (僑胞) from the Gifu Prefecture (琦玉縣) local headquarters (地方本部) of the Japanese Residents Association (日本居留民團) visited Samhwa 2-ri (三花 2里) as part of a visit to their homeland (母國訪問). Along with warm encouragement (激勵), they formed a sisterhood alliance (姉妹結緣) and donated 3,060,000 won in contributions (誠金), boosting the morale (士氣) of the residents. The sincere contributions (誠金) from these distant compatriots (同胞) who crossed the East China Sea (玄海灘) were meaningfully used to promote the prosperity (繁榮) of a sack factory (工場) and its ancillary warehouse facilities (附屬倉庫施設), turning them into seeds of growth (昇華).

### 6) Other Notable Matters (其他特記事項)

- In 1973, at the National Saemaul Leaders Conference held in Gwangju, South Jeolla Province (全南光州市), I was awarded the "Diligent Medal" of the Saemaul Medal (新村勳章勤勉章) and received a presidential gift (大統領下賜金) of 1 million won, the greatest honor of my lifetime (一生一代最上榮光). With this, I established the capital (資產) for the village's business of operating a rice polishing factory (搗精工場).
- After completing the basic environmental business (基礎環境事業), the residents' will (住民意志) to increase income (所得增大) realized the truth (眞理) of "If you do it, you can do it" and on February 5, 1974, we had the honor (榮光) of reporting the economic situation (經濟動向報吿) to President (大統領) Park Chung-hee. Another Saemaul Medal, the "Cooperation Medal" (勲章協同章), was awarded in the name of Rev. Lee In-chwi (李仁萃牧師), the religious leader (宗敎人指導者) of this village at that time. A reward business fund (賞事業費) of 3 million won was simultaneously granted by President (大統領) Park Chung-hee, and the residents bore a burden (住民負擔) of 2 million won to create a 10-hectare stone-throwing and raft-cultivating farm (投石式굴養殖場), which has grown into an annual income business (所得事業) of 10 million won.

### 3. Village Assembly (住民總會)

♦ Meeting Minutes (會議錄)(1)

*   **Date**: April 1, 1977
*   **Venue**: Village Community Center (會館)
*   **Attendees**: 95
*   **Chairperson**: Village Head (里長)
*   **Agenda**:
    1. Village Shared Warehouse (共同倉庫)
    2. Village Tree Planting (植樹) and Greening (綠化)

**Discussion Items (討議事項)**: 1. Village Shared Warehouse (共同倉庫) Painting (塗色)
    The leader (指導者) proposed to paint the village shared warehouse (共同倉庫) and discussed that residents (住民) would directly manage (直營) the labor (人夫)

**Resolution Items (決議事項)**: It was resolved that the leader (指導者) would oversee the painting of the village shared warehouse (共同倉庫) and that residents (住民) would participate (參與) in the process.
*   Approve (贊) (90)
*   Disapprove (否) (5)
Representatives of Attendees (參席人員): Kim Gi-yeol (金基烈) • Kim Yong-hwa (金容和) • Yu Jae-ko (劉載高) • Min Byeong-dae (閔炳臺) • Park Eun-dae (朴殷臺)


--- (p. 455) ---

♦ Minutes (會議錄)(2)
Date: May 30, 1976
Location: Village Community Center
Attendees: 87 (including village leaders and agency secretaries)
Chairperson: Village Leader, Government Official (指導者) as co-chair
Agenda Items: Establishment of Saemaul Flour Mill (製粉工場), Important Material Education

- Resolved to establish the Saemaul Flour Mill (製粉工場), a long-desired project for the villagers, to save food and eliminate the waste of time traveling long distances for milling and making noodles. The mill will be operated directly in our village, providing convenience for the residents and strengthening the proactive Saemaul Movement.
- Resolved that out of the total construction cost of 3,500,000 won, 1,000,000 won will be borrowed and 2,500,000 won will be borne by the village, with support for materials to be received.
Representatives of Attendees: Village Leader An Il-su, Leader (指導者) Han Dae-geun, Committee Members Baek Eun-tae, An Gab-su, Kim Yong-seop

♦ Minutes (會議錄)(3)
Date: April 27, 1976
Location: Samhwa 2-ri, Seokmun-myeon, Dangjin-gun
Attendees: 8 (including government officials from the Development Committee)
Chairperson: Village Leader Han Dae-geun, Leader (指導者)
Agenda Items: 1976 Regional Community Development Project Plan, Issues with Joint Warehouse Construction (建築) and Operation, Discussion on Flour Mill (製粉工場) Installation

Construction (建築) of the Third Joint Toilet
Strategies (對策) for Purchasing a Village Shared Vehicle
Resolutions: Resolved unanimously to proceed with cooperation
Votes: In favor (贊成) 8, Against (反對) 0
Representatives of Attendees: Development Committee Chair An Gil-su, Leader (指導者) Han Dae-geun, Committee Members Kim Yeon-gon, Kim Yong-hwa, Choi Jong-wan

## Agenda for Discussion

3.  Improvement of necessary personnel for the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

## Resolutions

1.  Our village, with an 80-year history as a Christian village, shall unite in Christian spirit to build a paradise on earth.
    *   Agreed to make the 1973 Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) a Grade A project
    *   The key points in the regulations are that all projects shall be completed 100%
    *   All land required for the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) shall be donated unconditionally
    *   All work shall be done collectively
    *   All projects shall be self-reliant

## 4. Future Development Vision

*   We will concentrate our will (意志) for the great aspiration (大望) of the 1980s (年代) into the Saemaul income business (所得事業) and strive to establish a foundation (基盤) by developing technology (技術開發) and creating a mass production system (量產體制).
*   To expand the foundation (基盤) for developing personal income sources (個人所得源), we will promote the development of wasteland (野山開發) to produce specialized products (特化產品). We will establish a breeding farm (種豚場) for the communal income business (共同所得事業) to connect with and promote the development of personal income businesses (所得事業). Simultaneously, we will implement a systematic purchasing and distribution system (系統購人搬出體制) to ensure a smooth supply (圓滑) and convenience (便益) of feed (飼料供給), protect the rights (權益保護) of producers (生產者), and establish a planned production system (計劃生產體制) to enhance farm income (農家所得向上).
*   Furthermore, we will expand social welfare (社會福祉) and cultural facilities (文化施設), including senior citizen centers (老人會舘), medical facilities (醫療施設), and children's welfare facilities (福祉施設). By completing these facilities by 1980 (年), we plan to strive for the genuine construction (名實相符) of an ideal rural community (理想農村建設).

## 1. Village Overview

### a. History

- A village where descendants of the 14th generation of Kimhae Kim (金海 金氏) and Gurye Jang (求禮 張氏), two scholars who settled here to avoid political turmoil 400 years ago during the 11th year of King Seonjo's reign (1573), have lived relying solely on farming.
- According to the theory of geomancy, before August 15, 1945, the village used only two communal wells. After liberation, each household dug its own well, resulting in a high mortality rate among young villagers, with few living past the age of 50. This led to a high number of widows, earning the village the nickname "Widow Village." However, after filling in all household wells 60 years ago, the village no longer has young people dying prematurely, a rather amusing fact.

### b. Location and Conditions

#### <Location>
- A village located northeast of Muju County's administrative center, on the way to Gucheon-dong (九千洞). It is 99 km from Jeonju (全州) and 12 km from the Muju-eup (茂朱邑) area, situated along a road. The village borders Yonghwa-myeon (龍化面), Yonggwang Village, of Chungcheongbuk-do (忠清北道), Yongdong County (永同郡), to the north, with the clear and refreshing upstream of the Geumgang River (錦江) serving as the boundary.

#### <Conditions>
- The village, surrounded by farmland at an altitude of 300 meters, has relatively fertile soil suitable for cultivation and good drainage, making it ideal for double cropping. It is also a central hub for barley production.
- The upstream of the Geumgang River (錦江) flowing around the village is rich in freshwater fish such as eel and catfish, providing a delightful culinary experience throughout the year.

## 2. Village Development (發展) Process (過程)

### A. Situation (狀況) Before 1970 (70年 以前)

#### 1) Basic (基本) Status (現況)

*   Number of Households (家口數): 36 households (180 people (名))
*   Roof Improvement (改良): 10 buildings (棟) (27%)
*   Cultivated Land (耕地) Area (面積): 25.0ha (0.7ha per household (戶當))
*   ※ Income (所得) per Household (戶當): 287,000 won (千원)

*   From the road (道路), taking a narrow path around the rice fields to reach the village, even a cart could not pass through the narrow village alleys filled with trash and weeds;
*   Entering the house, the warped thatched roofs were overgrown with weeds, resembling the ruins (廢墟) of a war (戰爭), the walls (壁體) were worn away by rain and wind, revealing the bare framework, and there were no improved kitchens (改良), verandas (마루), or raised floors (토방), only warped houses (家屋).

#### 2) Cultural Aspect (文化面)

*   Cultural Facilities (文化施設)

| Newspaper (新聞) |        | Radio (라디오) | TV  | Telephone (電化) Business (事業) | Simple (簡易) Water Supply (給水) | Village Library (文庫) |
| :--------- | :----- | :----- | :-- | :-------------------- | :-------------------- | :-------------- |
| Central (中央) | Local (地方) |        |     |                       |                       |                 |
| -          | -      | 4 sets (臺) | -   | -                     | -                     | -               |

*   The only cultural facility (文化施設) was a radio (라디오) that used batteries (4 sets (臺)). During the drama time (時間), all the villagers (住民) would gather in front of the radio;
*   There were no lamps (램프), only oil lamps (호롱불) with wicks (심지) lit, no newspapers (新聞) or magazines (雜誌) to speak of (생각), only a few old novels (小說冊) like Chunhyangjeon (春香傳).

#### 3) Spiritual Aspect (精神面)

*   There was no cooperation (協同), and clan (氏族) factions (間) led to slander and curses (因), causing the entire village to be in discord (不和), and in laziness (怠) and idleness (安逸), drinking (飮酒) and gambling (賭博) increased daily, and all the residents (住民) suffered from poverty (貧困).
*   Regardless of how the neighbors were, they only lived for themselves (自己), slandering and scheming against each other (中傷), with no trust (不信), no hope (希望) or development plans (發展 計劃) for the future (未來), just living listlessly (無氣力).


--- (p. 463) ---

## 4) Income

O The farming was extremely small-scale, with only 0.7ha per household inherited from ancestors, totaling 25ha of farmland.
O In 1970, the income per household was 287,000 won, ranking below the county average, and farming was heavily focused on rice and wheat, with no consideration for non-agricultural income.
O The income composition in 1970 was as follows:

| Item                               | Percentage |
| :--------------------------------- | :--- |
| Income from food crops(食糧作物)   | 78%  |
| Income from special crops(特用作物) | 8%   |
| Sericulture income(養蠶所得)        | 6%   |
| Livestock income(畜産所得)          | 5%   |
| Non-agricultural and other income(農外及其他收入) | 3%   |

## 4) Daily Life (Clothing, Food, and Shelter)

O Due to the low income from farming focused on rice and wheat, residents were too busy making ends meet to think about their neighbors.
O Without electricity, residents used oil lamps, severely limiting nighttime activities.
O The annual "barley hump" (a period of food shortage) tightened already empty stomachs and made the village vulnerable to petty thieves.
O Clothing was patched together, with women's skirts and jackets hand-dyed and stained.
O Windows were layered with paper to insulate the crumbling walls, and broken window frames were tied together with bark and willow branches to maintain their condition.
O The walls inside the rooms were covered with newspapers used for silkworm breeding or school textbooks, resembling an exhibition hall.
O The kitchen was not improved, and there was no distinction between the toilet and the livestock shed. The village endured the spring famine and summer diseases as if it were their destiny.

### The Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

#### 1) Motivation and Experimental Project Results

O Seven years ago, the fierce wave of the "Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)" was sweeping across the country. However, the villagers were like spectators watching from across the river, spending their time drinking and gambling, wasting their days away.
O In October 1971, the village chief at the time, Mr. Jang In-yeol (張寅烈), thought that he could not abandon the village that had been passed down through generations and where our descendants should live. He decided to promote the project he had been feeling and planning.
O In October 1971, he convened a general meeting of the residents, reorganized the promotion committee, and explained the concept of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) and the project plan.
First: Expand the narrow alleys and improve the walls to improve the environment.
Second: Expand the access road connecting the village and the national highway.


--- (p. 464) ---

### Third: To build dikes around the village, which had been suffering from annual flood damage, to ease the residents' minds

Fourth: To improve the small streams flowing through the center of the farmland, straighten the ridges, and improve the low-lying fields to aim for increased income.

* However, the residents did not agree and instead expressed opposition.
* "We've lived like this without any problems, so why do we need to improve the walls?" they asked. "Building dikes would be good, but how can we possibly build them?"
* As the late autumn sun set, no conclusion was reached, and the meeting dispersed in disarray.

## 2) Election of Leaders and Promotion of Projects

* At the time, the village head, Jang In-yeol (張寅烈), could not bear to see the village fall behind. He decided to elect male and female leaders and promotion committee members to start the project. On September 10, 1972, a general meeting of the residents was held, and the following were elected.
* Male leader (男子指導者): Jang In-yeol (張寅烈)
* Female leader (婦女指導者): Kim Hyo-cheol (金孝喆)
* Promotion committee chairperson (推進委員長): Jang In-nok (張寅祿)
* Jang In-yeol (張寅烈), who was elected as the Saemaul leader (指導者), appealed to the elected officials and the residents to unite and strive to create a better village, despite any difficulties or obstacles.
* To foster a spirit of cooperation among the residents and set an example, he emphasized the need to prioritize the improvement of walls and the expansion of the village's inner roads. He declared that work would begin the next day.
* After the general meeting (總會), the promotion committee (推進委員) convened separately to draw up a plan for the expansion of the inner roads and resolved to proceed despite any obstacles (隘路).

## 3) Overcoming Obstacles

* On September 11, 1972, the residents gathered for the first time since the village was established, armed with shovels and reels, ready to start the Saemaul project.
* Leader Jang (張指導者) began to explain the work plan (作業計劃) based on the rough map (略圖) he had prepared for the expansion of the inner roads, but the residents' protests grew louder.
* "Why does my house have to be demolished?" some shouted, while others bellowed, "Is widening the roads by removing courtyards what Saemaul is about?" Some even threatened, "I'd rather die than give up my land," and "Anyone who touches my land will die, and so will I." The work promotion (作業推進) hit a wall.
* Undeterred, Leader Jang (張指導者) and the promotion committee (推進委員) started demolishing the house of Jang's aunt, Mrs. Kim Jeong-suk (金貞淑女史). As they began to systematically demolish the committee members' houses and walls, the village residents started to understand.
* For one month (1個餘月), they fought at the work site during the day and persuaded the residents at night! Persuading the stubborn residents was the first cause for celebration since the village was established.
* On March 10, 1977, after five months (5個月) of work, 1,080 meters of walls and 820 meters of inner village roads were neatly improved. Twelve buildings (棟) were demolished, and 800 pyeong (坪) of land was incorporated, resulting in ten or more injured (負傷者).


--- (p. 465) ---

In particular, the cooperation and hard work shown by the women of this village, which was particularly lacking in labor force compared to other villages, during the process of promoting the business, was truly heartbreaking.

### 4) Leader Change and Activity Status

#### Leader Change Situation

| Last Name | First Name | Age | Education | Activity Period | Promoted Business | Remarks |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Zhang | In-yeol | 45 | High School Graduate | 2 years | O Village inner road expansion 1080m<br>O Entrance road construction 420m<br>O Embankment 220m | Moved to Daejeon (大田市) |
| Zhang | In-ryuk | 45 | " | 5 years | O Embankment 610m<br>O Land reclamation 2ha | Current leader |

O With the successful completion of the village inner road, it was possible to proceed with new businesses.
O The construction of the entrance road, which was not even passable by a cart, and the embankment project, which had been left unattended while hoping for the government to solve the problem of losing precious farmland to flood damage every rainy season and losing crops cultivated with effort to turbid waters, was started with a resolute determination to complete this project no matter what, with the support of the Construction Bureau's technical support and 700,000 won of labor business funds.
O Although the project was started, it was a difficult business with only 34 people mobilized, one person per household, and no equipment.
O The foundation was laid with crude technology, and stone masonry was built with stones carried by women.
O As the farming season approached, there were not enough hands, and as the number of injured people increased due to the leader's forced promotion, the morale of the residents began to decline.
O To make matters worse, two stonemasons in charge of stone stacking became bedridden, and the construction was temporarily suspended.
O Leader Zhang went to neighboring Sincheon Village to explain the difficult situation and received support for stonemasonry technology.
O Despite such difficulties, on September 10, 1973, 8 months after the start of construction, 13,000 people in total were mobilized to complete a 220m long and 3m high embankment.
O Without even a moment to rest, Leader Zhang began to promote the construction of the entrance road.
O First, the problem was the 720 pyeong of farmland to be incorporated, but obtaining the consent of the landlords for the 240 pyeong of land owned by residents of Chungcheongbuk-do across the river was difficult.
O On September 10, 1977, 15 days after Leader Zhang personally visited 18 landlords in Chungcheongbuk-do to explain the situation, he received a donation of 240 pyeong of land.
O Starting construction on September 16, 1977, a straight and wide 420m entrance road was completed in 60 days, and today large trucks are coming and going.
O In mid-November 1973, when the business was completed, Zhang In-yeol, the leader who had lit the torch in this village, left Jijeon Village


--- (p. 466) ---

The year 1973 was a year of glory and fulfillment that will forever shine in the history of Jijyeon (芝田) Village.

- On November 25, 1973, the village assembly elected the second-generation (代) leader (指導者), and the current (現在) leader (指導者), Jang In-rok (張寅祿), was elected. Kim Jung-tae (金重泰) was elected as the promotion committee chairperson (推進委員長).
- On March 10, 1974, using the techniques learned from the embankment (堤防) construction (工事), they built stone embankments (石築) along the small streams (小河川) flowing between farmlands (農耕地), straightened the water flow, and established irrigation channels (導水路), solving both farmland (農耕地) protection (保護) and agricultural water (農業用水) issues.
- The pioneering (先進) Saemaul Undong (新村運動) residents' sweat never ceased, and family (家庭圏) businesses (事業) were voluntarily (自進) initiated (着手).
- The roof improvement (改良) of 36 households (陳) was completed (完了), transforming the environment (環境). Kitchens and restrooms (便所) were refined to urban standards (都市), and a 20 pyeong (坪) community center (會舘) was constructed (建立) and beautifully decorated (單掛) in the village center.
- In 1976, with the help of county funds (郡費), a public bathhouse (共同 沐浴湯) and restrooms (便所) were built, greatly benefiting the residents' health (健康).
- A 30 pyeong (坪) public livestock barn (共同 畜舍) houses 30 pigs, and a 40 pyeong (坪) public compost shed (共同 堆肥舍) built with an investment (投資) of 800,000 won was completed (完工), becoming a means (첩경) to increase income (所得).
- A 900 pyeong (坪) nursery (養苗場) grows lush persimmon trees (柿), and encouragement (激勵) and comfort (慰勞) were received from various sectors (各界) for the revitalizing (新羅) village residents (住民).

The reporting meeting (報告會(報告會)) was attended (參席(參席)) by Kim Yeong-bae (金永培), County Magistrate (郡守(郡守)) of Muju-gun (茂朱郡), Park Dong-yong (朴棟用), Village Head (面長(面長)), Jang In-nok (張寅祿), Leader (指導者(指導者)), and Kim Hyo-cheol (金孝喆), Chairperson (會長(會長)) of the Women's Association (婦女(婦女)).

O Leader (指導者(指導者)) Jang In-nok (張寅祿) received a medal (授與(授與)) from President (大統領(大統領)) Park Chung-hee (朴正熙), along with an award (表彰(表彰)) and a gift (下賜金(下賜金)) from Jijeon (芝田) Saemaul (새마을) organization (團體(團體)).


--- (p. 468) ---

500 million won was received.

The residents of Ji Jeon Village (芝田마을) united as one, based on the lesson "If you do it, it can be done," and embarked on another long-cherished project. With the President's (大統領) grant of 500 million won and the residents' contribution of 1,285 thousand won, they built a 390m long dike and reclaimed 2 hectares of land, thereby increasing grain production by 10% annually and creating communal property.
