**Date**: September 7, 1974
**Venue**: Community Center
**Agenda**: Discussion on the Installation of Simple Water Supply Systems
**Attendees**: Seo Yong-su and 54 others
**Absentees**: Kim Ae-gi and 4 others
**Chairperson**: Kim Jong-o, the village leader

**Chairperson**: Today, we have received 1,200,000 won from His Excellency the President (大統領) for the water supply facility, which has been deposited at the Agricultural Cooperative (農協). The design has also been completed. According to the design, the total cost, including materials, technical fees, labor costs, and other expenses, amounts to 2,378,000 won. After calculating with the Promotion Committee members, it appears that, in addition to the support funds, we will need an additional 830,000 won for purchasing materials and other miscellaneous expenses. Please discuss this issue.
**Yang Jong-hyun**: Let's have the villagers contribute labor and cover the shortfall through equal personal contributions per household.
**Chairperson**: Are there any objections?
**Villagers**: None.
**Chairperson**: It is declared unanimously adopted. Even if the cost per household is considerable, we must remember that this amount was personally granted by His Excellency the President (閣下). We should also adhere to the principle of self-responsibility and actively promote the project.
**All Villagers**: Agreed. (All in favor)
**Chairperson**: Are there any other agenda items?
**Byun Sang-gi**: Let's delegate the business plan and promotion methods to the village committee members.
**Chairperson**: Please explain the proposal.
**Byun Sang-gi**: Since it is the busy farming season, it would be more convenient and effective if the committee members meet regularly to discuss and promote the business rather than having all villagers participate.
**Yeom Seong-gu**: In my opinion, we should elect a Water Supply Promotion Committee to promote this water supply project. This project is particularly special as it is funded by a special grant from His Excellency the President (閣下), so we should form an organization to promote the project more effectively.
**Chairperson**: Are there any other opinions?
**Lee Pan-jeong**: Let's reconstitute the Water Supply Promotion Committee by adding current village committee members and young adults.
**Chairperson**: Are there any other opinions?
**All Villagers**: None.
**Chairperson**: Then, we will proceed to a vote.
1. Byun Sang-gi's proposal: 12 votes in favor,
2. Yeom Seong-gu's proposal: 14 votes in favor,
3. Lee Pan-jeong's proposal: 31 votes in favor.


--- (p. 502) ---

I inform you that Mr. Lee Pan-seong's opinion was passed with 31 votes in favor. For the formation of the Promotion Committee, let's elect by show of hands after receiving oral recommendations.

**Dongmin (同民)**: I agree.
**Seo Gab-deung**: I recommend Mr. Byung-sang-gi as the chairman of the Water Supply Business Promotion Committee.
**Dongmin (同民)**: Good. (Unanimously passed)
**Chair**: Election of committee members by oral recommendation, Chairman of the Promotion Committee: Byung-sang-gi, Finance Officer: Yang Gil-su, Secretary: Kim Jong-su, Guidance Committee Member: Kim Jong-o, Development Chairman: Yeom Seong-gu, Committee Members: Lee Pan-seong, Seo Byung-sik, Lee In-seon, Kim Gwi-gwon, Seo Han-jong, totaling 10 people, are elected as the Water Supply Business Promotion Committee by unanimous vote.
**Chair**: If there are any special matters afterward, we will hold a meeting. I will delegate the promotion of the water supply business to the Promotion Committee and conclude the meeting. Thank you. Please go home safely.

Date: March 18, 1975
Venue: Community Center
Agenda: Promotion of Won Myeong-deok Bridge Construction
Attendees: Kim Gui-gwon and 52 others
Absentees: Lee Gi-ok and 6 others
Chairperson: Leader Yeom Seong-gu

Chairperson: Thank you all for attending despite your busy schedules and fatigue. We will now begin our meeting on the promotion of bridge construction. Please feel free to discuss openly, and I hope we can have fruitful discussions for the development of our village.
Mr. Kang Jeong-sang: I propose that the 872,000 won that our residents need to bear should be covered through effort.
Chairperson: That is a good suggestion. Are there any other opinions?
Mr. Dong-min: None.
Chairperson: Then we will consider it as none and decide to cover it through effort. The width of the bridge, as designed, should be 5m, and the length should be 12m. When would be a good start date for construction?
Mr. Byeon Sang-gi: To complete it as soon as possible before the busy farming season, let's start tomorrow, April 19.
Chairperson: That sounds good. Please share your next opinion.
Mr. Seo Han-jong: Tomorrow seems too early, so let's make it the 20th.
Chairperson: Please share your next opinion.
Mr. Jeon Dong-min: None.
Chairperson: Then we will consider it as none and decide by vote. First, please raise your hand if you agree with Mr. Seo Han-jong's opinion.
Agreed: 30 people
Next, please raise your hand if you agree with Mr. Byeon Sang-gi's opinion.
Agreed: 15 people


--- (p. 505) ---

**Chair**: According to the vote, 30 people agreed with Mr. Seo Han-jong's opinion, 15 with Mr. Byeon Sang-gi's, and 8 abstained. It has been decided to start construction on April 20th as per Mr. Seo Han-jong's suggestion. Now, how should we manage manpower during the project period?

**Seo Byung-seok**: In my opinion, it would be best if one able-bodied man from each first-generation family participated.

**Lee In-sun**: We should have one able-bodied man from each first-generation family, but we should also consider those who live alone, shouldn't we?

**Jeon Dong-min**: Agreed. Unanimous.

**Chair**: Let's decide on the issue of able-bodied men from single-person households at the next meeting. Please share your thoughts on how to handle those who did not attend.

**Choi Man-gwon**: I think we should set the penalty for non-attendance at 1,000 won per day and make them responsible for their own expenses.

**Lee Young-sook**: I propose that the penalty be set at 1,000 won without the expense responsibility.

**Han Seung-ok**: To complete the bridge construction project faster, I suggest setting the daily wage at 700 won and having all participants receive their penalty in person on the day of their participation.

**Chair**: Let's vote.

**Choi Man-gwon's opinion**: 30 votes
**Lee Young-sook's opinion**: 17 votes
**Han Seung-ok's opinion**: 5 votes

The vote resulted in Choi Man-gwon's opinion being passed.

**Chair**: Now, let's set working hours, lunch breaks, and rest times to ensure a regular work schedule.

**Jeon Dong-min**: Agreed.

**Chair**: Despite the inconvenience, thank you to all the residents for cooperating in the development of our village. Please be careful on your way back.

### Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (9)

| Item       | Details            |

| Date       | 76. 4. 20           |

**Chair**: Hello, I'm sorry to have taken up your time today. The reason we've gathered is that the Women's Association has been running a market business in our village so far, and now we need to...


--- (p. 506) ---

We have been taking turns visiting each household, but this has led to times when mothers are too busy or cannot pay attention as they should. Therefore, we are considering setting up a fixed sales booth. If any of you have good ideas, please share them.

**Kim Sun-bok:** As the chairperson mentioned, our mothers are often too busy. Sometimes, even if we just want to buy a single bar of soap, we find the door locked and they have gone out to work, which is very inconvenient. I have been wanting to compromise on this issue for some time.

**Lee Ok-ja:** That's a good idea. We should move the current women's association sales booth to the village community center and establish it there to promote it.

**All members:** Agree.

**Secretary:** If we move the sales booth to the village community center, we will need someone to take responsibility for fixed sales. Who would you like to appoint?

**Kim Sun-i:** If that's the case, I recommend Kim Ok-soon, who has been running the store from before and currently lives next to the community center.

**All members:** Agree.

**Secretary:** Since all members support Kim Ok-soon, Kim Ok-soon, we ask you to take on the task. Of course, we will bring more items to the sales booth by going to the wholesale market tomorrow.

**Kim Sun-ok:** If that's the general opinion, I will give it a try. However, if I take care of the sales booth, I won't be able to attend to my original work, so I hope you will consider that as well.

**Secretary:** Well said. In my opinion, rather than daily odd jobs which earn about 700 won, running the sales booth requires working day and night, so although it is busy, if we save a little from the total profit, what do you think about 15,000 won per month?

**All members:** That's a great idea.

**Kim Ok-soon:** 15,000 won seems a bit low, so could you raise it to 20,000 won? Please cooperate a little more.

**Park Ok-ja:** Let's do that. Originally, Kim Ok-soon is a marginalized citizen without even one pyeong of land, so let's help her out of sympathy. What do you think?

**All members:** Agree.

**Secretary:** Then, let's decide on 20,000 won. Kim Ok-soon, in return, please take good care of the women's association sales booth in our village as if it were your own and make the maximum effort to achieve significant income. If there are any other opinions, please share them.

**All members:** None.

**Secretary:** Then, we will conclude today's meeting. Tomorrow, please come early to move all the items to the community center and prepare any missing items. A few of you, please come and cooperate. Thank you.

**Location**: Community Center

**Chairperson**: Village Leader Kim Jong-su

**Chairperson**: Good day everyone. Today, we are gathered to discuss the agenda of constructing a joint worksite of 50 pyeong (坪) this year using the President's (大統領) grant. According to the design documents, the total construction cost is 4,000,000 won, with 1,500,000 won to be supported and 2,500,000 won to be borne by the residents. We must aim for completion. To promote this project, there will be many obstacles ahead, so I kindly ask for your valuable opinions.

**Leader Lee Young-suk**: Enough with the joint worksite and all that. Every year, because of the Saemaul Undong (新村運動), who has the time to farm and make a living?

**Jeon Gab-dong**: Indeed. We are so exhausted from the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) that we are about to die.

**Yeom Seong-gu**: Hey, you guys are causing trouble again. Among all the projects you've done so far, has there been any bad outcome? Even if it's a bit tough while working, once you finish, everything becomes ours and is effectively used. Let's just endure a bit more and keep working.

**Chairperson**: Chairman Yeom's words are right. Aren't all things like that? Isn't the sweat of today promising the fruits of tomorrow? Shouldn't we just do it?

**Leader Yu Sang-geon**: But then, isn't the land for the worksite a problem? And it will require a lot of self-funding. How are we going to manage that? I don't think I can do it! How much debt do we already have in our village?

**Kim Jong-su**: I understand the concerns of all the elders, but can we refuse the President's (大統領) special grant to our village? Let's try once and if we really can't, let's go to the town mayor or county governor for cooperation.

**Yang Jong-hyun**: The village leader's words seem right. Let's try hard. There will be an end if we keep going, right? What do you all think?

**Villagers**: Let's try.

**Chairperson**: Thank you very much. I am truly grateful for your cooperation. Then, let's decide to build the worksite (50 pyeong) next to the vacant land beside the cattle shed.

**Villagers**: That sounds good.

**Chairperson**: And we will need technicians. In my opinion, instead of bringing in technicians from outside, our village has acquired many skills through the Saemaul Undong (新村運動). So, if we all residents put in effort under Yeom Seong-gu's overall responsibility, we can definitely do it.


--- (p. 508) ---

Yom Seong-gu: Hey, you! Are you doing things your way now? I'm exhausted and can't take it anymore. Go ahead and do as you please.
Yu Sang-geon: But this is something that my father-in-law should do, not someone else. I must ask you to endure (受苦) one more time. What do you all think?
Villager (洞民): That's fine with us.
Community (社會): Since all the residents (住民) are supporting this, we kindly ask you to endure (受苦) one more time.
Yom Seong-gu: Oh dear, this is so frustrating. It seems like nothing can be done if I don't agree. If the residents (住民) want it, I'll do it one more time!

Lee Jun-ok: Then let's start the work immediately from tomorrow. We need to finish early and get back to farming.
Villager (洞民): I agree (贊成).

Villager (洞民): None.
Community (社會): Then we will conclude today's meeting (會議) here. Thank you very much. Please go home safely.

### 4. Future Development Plan (發展構想)

- Install the long-awaited Myeongdeok Dike (明德堤) to convert 15ha of paddy fields (天水沓) into safe irrigation (水利) fields (安全畓)
- Reclaim 3.4ha of wasteland (野山) and establish an orchard (團地) with persimmon and apple trees (有實樹)
- Introduce a feed grinder to utilize the natural resource (草資源) of grass and expand the livestock industry (畜產業) to achieve the long-awaited goal of a 2,000,000 won income in the 1980s (年代) earlier than expected.


--- (p. 509) ---

# Jeonbuk (Jeollabuk-do) Imseol-gun (Imseol County) Imseol-myeon (Imseol Township) Hyeongok-ri (Hyeongok Village) Yeonhwa Village

## 1. Overview of the Village

### Ga. History

- During the Joseon Dynasty (李朝), this village belonged to Sinan County (新安縣), but it was integrated into Imseol-myeon (任實面) during the administrative district reorganization (行政區域改編) by the Japanese government in April 1914. The village was established after Kim Daejang (金大壯), a descendant of Kim Gu-son (金驅孫) from the Kimhae Kim clan (金海 金氏) Pandosan-seongongpa (版圖判書公派) Samhyeonpa (三賢派), settled here to avoid political turmoil (사화) in 1578, during the 11th year of King Seonjo's reign (宣祖). Later, families from Jinju Gang clan (晋州 姜氏) and Gyeongju Yi clan (慶州 李氏) also settled in this area.
- The village is said to be located near Yeonhwa Hamro (蓮花含壚), one of the eight scenic views of Sinan (新安 八景), and attracts visitors from all over the country. The exact location of this auspicious site remains unknown. A legend about Yeonhwa Hamro (蓮花含壚) has been passed down through generations.
- About 700 years ago, a man with the Kim surname (金氏) was hunting in the deep mountains when he found a single lotus flower blooming in a valley. Upon closer inspection, he realized that this place was an unparalleled auspicious site (明堂). He told his children that he wanted to be buried there after his death.
- After his death, his descendants tried to find the lotus flower site to bury him, but they couldn't locate it. The village's terrain resembles the shape of a lotus fruit (蓮實), so the village was named Yeonhwa-sil (蓮花實).

### Na. Location and Conditions

#### <Location>

- Yeonhwa Village is located about 8 km (twenty ri) southwest of Imseol County Office (任實郡廳), beyond a mountain pass called Oshipryeong (五十嶺, also known as Swiheunjae). The village is situated near the large village of Hyeongok-ri (玄谷里).
- Long ago, this mountain pass was home to dozens of large pythons that would harm passersby. People could only cross the pass safely when fifty travelers gathered together, which is how the pass got its name, Oshipryeong (五十嶺). Consequently, this area suffered from frequent encounters with bandits, tigers, and other wild animals, and transportation was inconvenient.

#### <Conditions>

- Surrounded by steep mountains (70~80 degrees) and nestled in a narrow valley, the center of this village features a stream flowing between rocks. The village is encircled by steep mountains on all sides.


--- (p. 510) ---

## 2. Village Development Process (發展過程)

### 가. Development Situation Before 1970 (70年以前)의 개발상황)

#### 1) Basic Environment (基礎環境)
The stream flowing through the center of the village is composed of rocks and bedrock (岩盤), and following the stream...


--- (p. 511) ---

Carrying bundles of firewood, the villagers could barely make their way through the winding village paths. The 50 or so thatched houses lining both sides were mostly crumpled huts with no heated floors or verandas, their mud walls crumbling in places.

There were no farm roads (農路), let alone village access roads (進入路), and the pavilion (亭閣) built under a 700-year-old (餘年) zelkova tree at the village entrance (入口) had deteriorated beyond recognition.

## 2) Income Level (所得水準)

O For generations, the villagers had farmed rice (米麥) and other crops on 30 hectares of inherited farmland (農地). With an average cultivated area (耕地面積) of 0.6 hectares per household (戶當), the villagers' average annual income (年間平均 所得) in the 1970s (年代) was 241,000 won (千원).
O While cattle breeding (韓牛增殖事業) and dry field farming (火田) of chili peppers and tobacco (煙草栽培) were the main sources of income (主所得源), this village was one of the poorest (零細) in the region (管內) in terms of income level (所得水準).

## 3) Living Conditions (生活狀態)

### a) Consciousness Structure (意識構造)

O Living in ignorance (無知) and poverty (貧困), the villagers had never even considered trying to live better. They knew nothing of unity (團結), and their days were filled with idleness (懶怠), envy (嫉視), drinking (飮酒), and gambling (賭博).
O On market days in the town (읍내), villagers would often be found drunk (醉하여) under the eaves of houses along the street, sleeping or fighting over a piece of rice cake (떡). The people of Yeonghwaseol (蓮花實) or Hansil (한실) were often the subject of gossip and ridicule. The villagers were so accustomed to their old habits (因習) and stubborn (頑固) in their ways that they had no pioneering spirit (開拓精神) or hope (希望) for the future. They were indifferent (無關心) and expressionless (無表情) in all matters.

### b) Culture (文化) and Clothing, Food, and Shelter (衣食住) Living (生活)

O Without electricity (電氣), the villagers lived by the light of oil lamps (호롱불). Struggling to make ends meet, they had never experienced a decent life (人間生活).
O In this village where not a single newspaper (新聞) or magazine (雜誌) could be found, an old radio (古物 라디오) was the only source of news (뉴우스 매개체).
O In winter, a padded cotton pants (무명 솜바지) and a dyed military blanket (軍用 담요) were considered high-class attire (高級), and in summer, they wore patched hemp clothing (삼베 잠뱀이) several times over.


--- (p. 512) ---

*   After benefiting from the three phases of the Five-Year Economic Development Plans (經濟開發五個年計劃), the people in neighboring villages had long since escaped the shackles of poverty. However, this village remained unchanged, with residents still wearing straw sandals and living as they always had.
*   Now forgotten, during the spring famine (春窮期), they had to rely on long-grain rice (長利쌀) to survive, and most people had to carry bundles of firewood to the town market to sell in order to obtain food and prolong their lives.
*   Opening the window, which was patched with fertilizer sacks (肥料包袋) used as paper, one would enter to find children defecating on straw mats or rush mats, the floor filthy with excrement. Their lives were like a dark kitchen from a story, where flies buzzed incessantly.
*   It was unclear whether the traditional outhouse (在來式便所) was a toilet or a manure pit (堆肥場), with filth flowing into the middle of the courtyard. Like cattle tormented by flies and mosquitoes in the barn (畜舍), the villagers lived without shame or sorrow, as if this were their destiny (宿命).

## 나. The Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

### 1) Motivation (動機) and Achievements of the Pilot Project (試驗事業)

*   News reached this village that the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動), initiated by President (大統領) Park Chung-hee on April 22, 1970, was spreading across the country.
*   However, throughout the year 1971, no signs of reform appeared in this village. The government had supported a pilot project (試驗事業) by providing 80 bags of cement (洋灰) to the larger village of Hyangok-ri (玄谷里), where they attempted to build a small bridge (小橋梁). Due to a lack of technical skills (技術) and resident cooperation (協助), the construction turned out to be a shoddy job (粗雜不實工事).
*   As the year passed with the villagers stuck in their old ways (惰性), their stubbornness (我執), and indifference (無關心), the result was a shameful exclusion from the 1972 Saemaul Undong support. The residents, unmoved, continued to gather at the local tavern (酒幕), gossiping and complaining, wasting their time (虛送歲月).

### 2) Election of Leaders (指導者) and Their Activities (活動狀況)

*   After graduating from high school (高等學校), Gang Daeyong (姜大容), who had been reporting village affairs as the neighborhood head (里長) while tending to the family farm (農土), reflected on his own and his neighbors' desperate poverty (凄絕).
*   He sometimes resented his ancestors (祖上) for bequeathing poverty like an inheritance (遺產) and was tempted (誘惑) by the allure of city life (都市生活), but he also firmly resolved to improve his hometown (故鄕), where his ancestors' bones lay and where his own would one day rest.
*   However, he was uncertain about how to improve their lives or how to properly implement the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動). Feeling disheartened (失意), he spent 1971 without accomplishment or fulfillment. After being excluded from the Saemaul Undong support, he decided to take action.
*   Gang Daeyong (姜指導者) declared 1972 as the year of the <Voluntary (自進) Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)> and vowed to surpass other supported villages by demonstrating self-help (自助的) capabilities (能力) and achieving the ultimate goal (至上命題) of rural modernization (農村近代化).
*   To establish a more robust leadership system (指導體制), he volunteered to become a Saemaul leader (指導者) and sought out younger individuals with strong leadership (指導力) and creativity (創意力) to join him.


--- (p. 513) ---

The head of the village (반장) was reorganized, with Gang Dae-chan (姜大賛) appointed as the first head (1반장), Gang Gil-jun (姜吉俊) as the second head (2반장), and Lee Man-won (李萬雨) as the third head (3반장) to take charge of guidance.

### 3) Overcoming the Road (노) Situation (狀況)

*   Gang, a volunteer village leader (지도자), thought that to inspire cooperation (협동심) and participation (참여의식) among the residents (주민), they should first start with communal work (공동작업) such as farm roads (농로) or village paths. However, despite several village meetings (주민총회), the residents' response remained cold (냉담) and indifferent (무관심).
*   As time passed, Gang continued to persuade residents through house visits (호별방문), but no one readily responded. Eventually, Gang turned his attention to the village children.
*   In this village, 10 ri (餘里) away, there were about 70 children (70여명) who commuted to school (통학). Gang took care of these children, who were neglected by their parents (부모) due to farm work (농사), teaching them hygiene (위생관념) and providing them with picture books (동화책) purchased with his own money (사비). He also helped them with their schoolwork (숙제), stamped their homework notebooks (숙제장) to confirm completion (확인검사), and began instilling the Saemaul spirit (새마을 정신).
*   Having become familiar (친숙) with the children, Gang started cleaning the village (청소) with them every morning.
*   As the adults' (마을 어른) awareness (인식) gradually changed, they began to join in the cleaning, showing signs of participating (참여) in the Saemaul movement (새마을운동).
*   Seeing this as a turning point (전기), Gang announced 1972 (72년) as the year of "Voluntary (자진) Saemaul Undong (운동)" to all residents (주민) and convened a village meeting (주민총회) on December 23, 1971 (71.12.23) to discuss the first project: widening the village paths (마을 안길 확장).
*   After explaining the project plan (사업계획), the meeting room (회의장) turned into chaos (수라장) as it was revealed which lands (토지) would be included in the path and which houses (가옥) would need to be demolished (철거).
*   The villagers protested, asking why they alone should suffer (피해) for a road (길) that everyone would use (사용).
*   Fortunately, the residents (주민) regained their reason (이성) and volunteered (자원) to share the labor burden (노력부담), agreeing to provide some compensation (피해보상) for the affected parties. Thus, the meeting (회의) ended safely (무사).
*   However, when it came to their own land (자기 토지), a 70-year-old relative (친척 70 노인) shouted that they would never give up their land, and drunk teenage boys (술에 취한 10대 소년) threatened to kill anyone who touched their land with a hoe (곡괭이), causing the work (작업) to halt several times.
*   Seeing this, Gang thought that the first step should be to eliminate the three taverns (주점) in the small village. The village women (마을 부녀자), who had long suffered from their husbands' (남편) drunkenness (술주정), were the first to enthusiastically (쌍수) welcome the idea.
*   Gang put the women's association members (부녀회원) at the forefront to persuade their husbands, who were addicted to gambling (도박) and alcohol (술), and through the village meeting (주민총회), he established a village regulation (마을 규약) prohibiting drinking (음주행위). Additionally, he persuaded the tavern owners (주점 주인) to voluntarily close (자진 폐점) two of the three taverns (2개소), succeeding in his endeavor (성공).


--- (p. 514) ---

- However, the only exception was the tavern owner who was a relative of the Kang village leader (姜指導者). Despite the efforts of the women in the village, led by the village leader, to shut down the tavern using every possible method, the tavern owner continued to operate, accusing the village leader's large household of illegally harvesting timber and reporting them to the county forestry office (郡山林課).
- At that time, the household was fined 110,000 won by the prosecution (檢察廳) for having a few logs of pine trees.
- The village leader (姜指導者) paid 60,000 won, and his large household paid 50,000 won to settle the fine. However, this incident strained their relationship to the point of estrangement, and they lived in this difficult situation for about three months.
- On another occasion, a young man in the village reported the tavern for operating without a license, resulting in a fine of 5,000 won. The village leader (指導者) paid this fine on behalf of the tavern owner, which led to the tavern's closure.
- However, this incident had repercussions. Later, the tavern owner wrote an anonymous letter claiming that the village leader (指導者) had sold 20 bags of government-supported cement (政府支援 洋灰), leading to an investigation by a team dispatched from the National Cooperation Prime Minister's Office (國協總理室). However, the investigation proved the claims to be groundless, and everyone, including the investigators, ended up laughing about it.
- The parents of the Kang village leader (姜指導者) constantly scolded him, urging him to resign from his position and focus solely on farming.
- They even threatened to cut off their parental ties if he refused to step down from his role as a village leader (指導者職).
- Despite these numerous challenges, the Kang village leader (姜指導者) continued to lead the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) by rallying the community. Whenever work was interrupted, he would convene the village assembly (住民總會) or visit households to appeal and urge them not to be stingy in creating a prosperous village for their descendants, as the village was no longer just for those who had lived there for half a century.
- Expanding the village roads required the daunting task of removing over 100 ryō of rocks and boulders.
- The sheer volume of work was immense, and the village elders, superstitious about the protective rocks of the village, vehemently opposed the project, believing that touching these rocks would bring ruin to the village or even death to those who dared.
- From ancient times, the village had a tradition of writing and displaying the talisman "Gang Taegong's minor work (姜太公小作也)" in every household to ward off disasters. Capitalizing on this tradition,
- The village leader (姜指導者) convened a village assembly (住民總會) and declared that no minor gods could dare interfere with the Saemaul Undong (新村運動), which was being carried out under the special orders of President (大統領) Park. He distributed papers with the inscription "President (朴大統領) Park's Special Order for Saemaul Undong (新村運動)" to be used as talismans in place of the old ones. With this, the village leader (姜指導者) began to vigorously push forward the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) by first removing the protective rocks and other obstacles.
- Through these efforts, the village was able to straighten and solidify its internal roads and streams to an impressive length of 1,420 meters, a feat that was once considered impossible.
- News of the first self-initiated Saemaul Undong (自進 新村運動) in the region spread, catching the attention of Choi Wan-sang (崔完相), the then-governor of Imreal County (任實郡守), who visited the village to inspect the progress of the Saemaul Undong (新村運動).


--- (p. 515) ---

O It was said that the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) in this village was impossible unless the entire village was moved to another place, so one can infer the extent of the village's conditions.

O However, the relentless determination of one leader and the residents' strenuous efforts turned the impossible into the possible. The successful completion of the village's main road was an opportunity for the residents, who had only been able to look enviously at their well-off neighbors, to see their grudges and wishes fulfilled one by one. It was also a solemn and celebratory moment where a new tomorrow filled with hope opened up, and a new chapter of history unfolded.

### 4) Developmental Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

O Taking the successful opening of the main road as an opportunity, the residents further united and devoted themselves to the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), carrying out home improvement projects such as wall construction, earthen wall building, Jangdokdae (Korean traditional storage space), kitchen renovation, and toilet improvement.

O Leader Kang led 49 villagers at his own expense to visit Galma Village in Imsil-myeon (任實面), a model village of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), to renew their direction and sensitivity towards the movement, thereby promoting the project efficiently.

O As news of the village's proactive Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) spread, visits and words of encouragement began to arrive from various sectors and levels of society.

O The administrative authorities, who had hesitated to support the village's Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) deeming it impossible, presented a significant gift in the form of support for the 1973 Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement).

O With renewed courage, the villagers embarked on the task of constructing an access farm road to the village, aiming to leap from a basic village to a self-sufficient village in 1973.

O At that time, they received a donation of 453 pyeong (坪) of land worth over 1.3 million won (萬圓) at the current market price and, through the residents' labor, successfully built a 490m access farm road on March 2, 1973, and renovated a 980m small stream.

O Additionally, a village hall, which they had never even dreamed of, was completed through the residents' own efforts, and a grand completion ceremony was held.

O Furthermore, with the support of cement, 16 small bridges totaling 80m were constructed in 1973, and as the village was selected as an advanced Saemaul village, rural telephone services were expedited and initiated.

O The day the telephone service was initiated was a day of celebration for the entire neighborhood. Each household made sirutteok (Korean rice cake steamed in a traditional steamer) and held a ritual under the electric light, expressing their joy.

O In 1974, the village continued to promote wall improvement, roof improvement, and roof painting projects. They also completed community facilities such as a children's playground, a red pepper drying field, and a public toilet, achieving the great honor of being promoted to a self-sufficient village in 1973.

O Moreover, with the special support of 1 million won (萬圓) from President (大統領) for the project, 8 head of Hanwoo (韓牛) were purchased and distributed to 8 farming households that actively cooperated with the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), thereby increasing their income and encouraging all residents to actively participate in the movement.

O In 1975, the village simultaneously promoted wall repair and whitewashing projects, as well as the renovation and repair of substandard housing, transforming the village's appearance.

O While completing cultural and welfare facilities such as a public bathhouse and a community warehouse, and production base construction projects, they also managed a budget of 1.32 million won (萬圓).


--- (p. 516) ---

With government support (政府支援), the simple water supply facility (簡易給水施設) was completed (完工), and women danced as the water flowing from the water pipe (給水管) was called the villagers' (住民) mountain lifeblood. Their celebration knew no end even as the night deepened.

○ Furthermore, following the active encouragement (積極勸獎) of the administrative authorities (行政當局), a village nursery (養苗) of 300 pyeong (坪) suitable for the conditions (與件) of a mountain village (山間마을) was established (造成) as a productive income business (生產所得事業), and 162,000 trees (株) were planted over 35 days (日間) in 68 hectares (Ha) of timber forest (用材林) and fuel forest (燃料林).

○ The total number of people (延入員) involved in this endeavor (所要) was over 3,500, with each household (家口) contributing 2 or more people (名) aged 16 to 60 (才), resulting in the mobilization (總動員) of all villagers (全住民).

○ Additionally, a major project (大事業) of planting 4,500 zelkova trees (株), which are economically valuable (經濟性), was successfully completed (無事) in an area of 8 hectares (ha).

○ In the fiscal year (年度) of 1976, with 2 million won (萬) in subsidies (支援) from the county (郡) and 400,000 won (萬) contributed by the residents (住民), a 200-meter small stream (小河川) was improved (整備) using stone baskets (돌망태).

○ In the fiscal year (年度) of 1977, a new communal work site (共同作業場) was constructed (新築) with a special support fund (特別支援金) of 2 million won (萬) donated (下賜) by His Excellency the President (大統領 閣下), providing convenience (便宜) and a foundation for cooperation (協同) among the residents (住民). Additionally, a communal purchasing and selling site (共同購販場) was established (開設) to supply daily necessities (生必品) at low prices (低廉 價格).

○ In particular, the continuous efforts (繼續事業) in environmental improvement (環境改善事業) and residential area beautification (住居圏 가꾸기 사업) were completed (마무리), with most households (大部分) now equipped with tiled kitchens and toilets (변소) and using hygienic toilets (衛生便器), leading to a more hygienic lifestyle (衛生的 生活).

○ Through the successful promotion (成功的 推進) of the Saemaul income-increasing business (所得增大事業), this village achieved an astonishing miracle (驚異的 奇蹟) in the mountains (山中) in the fiscal year (年度) of 1977, with an average annual household income (戶當所得) of 1,705,000 won (千).

### 5) Land (土地) and Cash Donation (現金喜捨) Status (狀況)

○ Encouragement (激勵) and comfort (慰勞) were swiftly (速至) extended to the hardworking residents (住民) from various sectors (各界), and the residents also generously donated (內出した) their land (門前沃沓) and cash (現金) without hesitation for the Saemaul Undong (事業).

## 6) Heartwarming Stories

### a) Story 1

*   In April 1967, General Song Ho-rim (宋虎林), then Commander (司令官) of the Gwangju (光州) CAC, visited this village while directing an anti-spy (對間諜) operation (作戰) at Mount Unsubong (雲水峰). He was deeply moved by the impoverished yet dedicated cooperation of the villagers in this remote and vulnerable area.
*   He promised that if they lived well, they would not have to worry about spies or guerrillas, and he would always support them if they showed their efforts to improve their lives.
*   Leader Kang had received much advice and guidance from General Song through letters and had received considerable support for the village.
*   When the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) began in this village and the Saemaul spirit (熱氣) grew stronger, Leader Kang sent a letter with photographs of the developing village, requesting support.
*   To his surprise, General Song visited the village on March 18, 1973, and was deeply moved again by the villagers' hard work on projects like road construction. He promised active support.
*   Through Colonel Lee Mu-ji (李武治) of the Gwangju (光州) CAC Headquarters (司令部) Civil Affairs (民事) Staff (參謀), 700,000 won was donated for the construction of the village hall (里會舘) or elderly care center (養老堂) on April 22, 1973. The villagers were deeply touched and celebrated this unexpected joy.

### b) Story 2

*   Kang Jaesoo (姜才秀), a native of this village, heard about the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) taking place in his hometown. He donated the use of his 42-pyeong (坪) field for road construction on December 5, 1973.
*   When he visited the village on August 6, 1974, he was amazed and moved by the transformed village. He immediately donated 100,000 won to purchase a television for the village.
*   Leader Kang persuaded the villagers to use the money for compost production, the foundation of increased food production, instead of buying a television. They easily collected the abundant compost piled on the mountain.


--- (p. 518) ---

To descend within the given time, they purchased and set up 420 meters of cable. While camping, they cut grass and transported it down the mountain, which significantly reduced the manpower needed for composting. This allowed them to focus entirely on collecting compost, achieving a remarkable 1,948% of their target (512%), burying the entire village in compost piles. This outstanding achievement earned them first place in the nation for compost production, leading to an award and a television set from the Minister of the Interior.

## 8) Special Matters (特記事項)

### a) Joyful Events

* When the villagers, not to mention the administrative authorities, thought it was impossible to open a village road, but it was opened through the Saemaul Undong, and when the villagers voluntarily responded enthusiastically to the idea of breaking through the farm roads with their own strength
* When Choi Wan-sang (崔完相), the governor of Imreal County (任實郡守), visited the village for the first time in history (72.2.10)
* On April 22, 1973, when the villagers shed tears of joy and cheered upon receiving a donation of 200,000 won from General Song Ho-rim (宋虎林), the commander of the CAC in Gwangju (光州)
* When the villagers were deeply moved after purchasing 8 head of fattened cattle with the special support fund of 1,000,000 won, a gift from the President (大統領閣下)
* When the village was promoted from a basic village (基礎마을) to a self-sufficient village (自立마을) in 1974
* When the simple water supply system was completed and clear water gushed out
* When the village won first place nationwide in the manure production (堆肥增產) unit competition in 1974
* When news was received that the leader Kang (姜) would meet with the President (大統領閣下) during Park Chung-hee's (朴正熙) New Year inspection of Jeollanam-do (全羅南道) in 1975
* When news was received that the leader Kang (姜) would present a successful case at the National Saemaul Leaders Conference in 1975
* When the village was selected as an excellent Saemaul Undong village in 1974, and an interview with Sa Pil-seo (社弼緖), the governor of Imreal County (任實郡守), and the leader Kang (姜) was broadcast on TV by MBC Jeonju Broadcasting Station (全州放送局)
* When news was received that the leader Kang (姜) would be awarded a medal at the National Saemaul Leaders Conference to be held in Daejeon (大田) on December 10, 1976
* When the leader Kang (姜) received a prize of 1,000,000 won from Lee Sang-chil (李相七), the governor of Imreal County (任實郡守), and was promised the construction of a small reservoir (小溜池), a long-cherished project of the villagers, on October 16, 1977
* When the village completed a joint work site with a special support project fund of 1,500,000 won from the President (大統領閣下) in 1977

### b) Sad Events

* When the villagers ignored the persistent objections and enthusiasm of the elderly, who said that removing the rocks in the village would bring ruin to the neighborhood and cause deaths, and continued the work, but a cow tied to a nearby mountain died of strangulation after misstepping, and the villagers blamed the leader (指導者) for touching the protective rock of the village
* When a few disgruntled young men beat up the leader Kang (姜), and while he was lying at home, his second child broke an arm while playing, and the villagers gossiped that the father and son were receiving punishment for touching the protective rock of the village, which was the most painful and sad time.

## Ba. Achievements through Saemaul Undong (事業)

### 1) Spiritual Aspect (精神面)

* Through the Saemaul Undong (運動), people became new humans (人間像) embodying diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperation (協同), achieving human transformation (人間改造);
* Residents gained the confidence (自信感) that no task is impossible when they unite (總和 團結) and push forward (推進) together, regardless of the difficulty;
* Through village assemblies (住民總會), residents experienced and practiced Korean-style democracy (韓國的民主主義) in the public square (廣場) of dialogue (對話); and
* Residents developed a sense of gratitude (感謝함) towards their country (祖國) and neighbors (이웃).

### 2) Livelihood Aspect (生活面)

* With the reform (改革) of agricultural technology (學農技術), seed renewal (種子更新), and the expansion (擴大) of Hanwoo cattle breeding (韓牛增殖事業), incomes (所得) increased, leading to;
* Farmers adopting a proactive (進取的) attitude (姿勢) through study (工夫) and research (硏究); and
* Residents practicing thrift (勤儉節約), saving (貯蓄), helping neighbors, and understanding that the well-being of all is key to individual prosperity (我が).

### 3) Production Aspect (生產面)

* Income (所得) increased through the expanded cultivation (擴大栽培) of unified rice varieties (統一系統 米), cooperative farming (協業化), and the expanded cultivation (擴大栽培) and seed renewal (種子更新) of tobacco (煙草) and chili peppers (고추); and
* Residents' lives became more affluent (潤澤) through Hanwoo cattle businesses (韓牛事業) (increased by 1,800%) purchased and bred (增殖) with grants (下賜金).

### 4) Income Aspect (所得面)

* In Suwon, the per-household (戶當) annual income (年間 所得) for 1977 was 1,705,000 won (千원), a significant increase from 1970; and
* A comfortable outlook (展望) for a per-household (戶當) income (所得) of 2,500,000 won (千원) in the 1980s (年代) is expected.

### 3. Village Assembly (住民總會)

♦ Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (1)

*   **Agenda (議題):** Expansion of Village Inner Road (村內道路擴張)
*   **Date (日時):** December 23, 1971
*   **Location (場所):** Kang Pan-nam's (姜判男) downstairs room
*   **Attendees (參席人員):** Kang Sung-jun (姜聲俊) and 46 others
*   **Absentees (不參席人員):** Lee Sun-deok (李順德) and 3 others
*   **Chairperson (司會者):** Leader Kang Dae-yong (姜大容)

**Chairperson (司會者):** I am truly sorry to have called this late-night meeting. Before we begin, I would like to apologize to all of you. Elders, as you know, neighboring villages like Hyeon-gok Village (玄谷部落) and Shin-an Village (新安部落) have received government support, including cement and rebar, for their Saemaul Undong projects. It is not that I lack the ability to secure such support, but the truth is that our village has long been known for gambling, drinking, laziness, and overall unfavorable conditions. The last time County Magistrate Choi Wan-sang (崔完相) visited, he left disappointed. His words as the village's responsible leader were truly disheartening. He said that our village could only participate in the Saemaul Undong by moving all our houses elsewhere. I will never forget those words in my lifetime.
Please, elders, do not blame me for everything.
However, learning from the past, I will do my utmost, even if it costs me my life, for the sake of you and our descendants.

**Lee Sang-ho (李相鎬):** Leader (指導者), are you giving a lecture (講演) or what? Why did you call this meeting?

**Leader (指導者):** I apologize. As I mentioned earlier, cement and rebar are not the only requirements for Saemaul Undong. This year, we have decided to proactively pursue the Saemaul Undong by ourselves and propose to build an inner village road. I kindly ask for your cooperation in this matter.

**Kang Jun-su (姜俊壽):** Hey, Leader (指導者), even the county magistrate (郡守) can't build an inner village road for the Saemaul Undong? As the saying goes, you need rice cakes to perform a good (굿), what are you talking about? If even the county magistrate can't do it, how can you? Stop making foolish remarks.

**Kang Dae-chan (姜大贊):** Uncle, why do you speak like that? You should listen to the discussion first before commenting.


--- (p. 523) ---

The county magistrate says we can't do it, but after making us suffer, he's just trying to save face by suggesting we build a road. Don't say useless, impossible things.
**Leader**: Is the neighborhood we're living in now a neighborhood?
As I mentioned earlier, we should live in a way that distinguishes between what's a ditch and what's a road, as others have thought it through.
**Lee Man-Geum**: I've lived to be 70 without distinguishing between ditches and roads.
**Kang Dae-Chan**: What's inappropriate is that the elders came this evening to oppose (反對) it. You're really overdoing it. That's why we've been living poorly, gambling well, fighting well, accusing each other well, and living like commoners (市井) fighting all the time.
**Lee Man-Geum**: That's right. Are you saying I did that? You heaven-damned bad guy. Just because you're the vice-leader...
**Kang Dae-Chan**: It's not because I'm the vice-leader.
At this precious moment, we shouldn't be concerned about positions (職位).
I was wrong to the elders.
Please forgive me.
**Lee Man-Geum**: Whether we build the road or not, no one from my house will go out.
(Exits.)
**Lee Beong-Woo**: Village head (里長), don't be indignant (憤慨) at the elders' words, and please proceed with the meeting (會議) quickly.
**Leader**: Yes, I had a rough idea that today's evening would turn out this way. I'm sorry (罪悚) about everything. Then, I will ask for your understanding regarding building a road inside the village.
If we do it well, the damage (被害) to the houses (家屋) will be less, but if we make a mistake and you misunderstand (誤解), the damage will be great. So, we should reduce our greed (慾心) and make concessions (讓步) to each other.
Our village (部落) happens to have a stream (河川) flowing through the middle, and the road goes back and forth this way. Whichever side we choose, it will be the stream, and we have to make one side.
In my opinion, if we make the stream (河川) on the sunny side (陽地), only Lee Sang-Gwon's (李相權) annex (行廊) will have to be removed. If we make it on the shady side (陰地), Kang Seong-Jun's (姜聲俊) annex, main house, Kang Jang-Su's (姜長秀) annex, main house, Kang Dae-Mun's (姜大汶) annex, main house, Lee Jong-Jin's (李鍾鎭) annex, and Lee Man-U's (李萬雨) annex will have to be removed.
If the stream (河川) is on the sunny side (陽地), Kim Pan-Yong's (金判用) land (垈地) will be significantly affected. What do you all think? Please let me know your thoughts.
**Kang Pan-Yong**: It's a road we all use and a stream (河川) we all share, so the damage (被害) should be equal. Why should I and Sang-Gwon (相權) bear the damage? No way.
**Kang Pan-Suk**: We need to reconsider.
I'm also significantly affected (被害).
**Lee Beong-Woo**: I'm also slightly affected (被害), but we should do things in a way that minimizes damage (被害) to the house.
**Kang Seong-Hwan**: As our uncle Pan-Sul (判述) just said, in fact, our uncle is making a concession (讓步)...


--- (p. 524) ---

You must do it. If the village promotion committee chairman says he won't do it, who will?
Lee Si-woo: Judgeon (判述) sir, you should compromise.
Villager: That's correct.
Kang Pan-suk: If you force the promotion committee chairman, it will be a loss.
Let him do it voluntarily.
Kang Seong-hwan: Kim Pan-yong sir, please think again. Of course, farmers are all greedy for land, but-
If a sensible person opposes and doesn't do it, who will? Please think carefully.
Kim Pan-yong: Please resolve the issue with Lee Sang-gwon's house first. I will think about it.
Leader: Lee Sang-gwon, if you remove your shed, will you not oppose?
Kim Pan-yong: Sang-gwon should think carefully. If you remove your shed and it affects the stream, our house will be directly affected.
Lee Sang-gwon: I understand. However, I am a poor man and live on government welfare rice, so what can I say? Please find a way that minimizes my loss.
Kang Dae-mun: Thank you very much. I will contribute three bags of rice as compensation.
Kang Jang-su: I will also contribute two bags.
Lee Jong-jin: I will also give three bags to Lee Sang-gwon.
Lee Man-woo: I should also contribute something.
Kang Seong-jun: I will also give three bags to the village head.
Leader: Thank you very much.
Villager: We fought at the beginning today, but things are going well now. I'm laughing.
Leader: Kim Pan-yong sir, what will you do?
Kim Pan-yong: I'm not doing it just because others are, but I have three conditions.
First: Our house is very old, so if you demolish and dig the wall, valuable artifacts might appear. If so, you must return them to me.
Second: You must completely rebuild our wall with stones to about 180 meters.
Third: If the stream side is ever demolished, the villagers must restore it.
If the villagers sign and seal a pledge like this, I will agree.
Leader: Will you accept Kim Pan-yong's three conditions as mentioned just now?
Kang Seong-jun: Even if the stream side is demolished, does that include our descendants?
Kim Pan-yong: Yes.
Leader: We think Kim Pan-yong's three conditions are not a problem. Because if we do it firmly and solidly from the beginning, the Saemaul Undong is for our descendants, so there is no problem.
Villager: Laughing in agreement.
Leader: Do you have anything else to say?
Villager: No.
Leader: Earlier, regarding the compensation for Lee Sang-gwon's house damage. Lee Man-woo said he would contribute, but how much?


--- (p. 525) ---

Leader: Please share your thoughts.
Lee Man-woo: I should also make my three points.
Leader: Then, it's one for each person.
This amount of money or rice should be given to me by the 26th. And when will we start construction?
Kang Pan-sul: We would like to start from tomorrow, but it would be better to start from the 28th after the market on the 26th.
All: Agree.
Leader: What should be the age limit for participation?
Kang Seong-eun: Let's set it at 18 years old and above, and 60 years old and below.
All: Good.
Leader: Any more comments?
All: None.
Leader: Thank you very much.
I'm sorry for the late hour. Today's meeting is concluded with all matters settled. As this is a pilot project for the government's 1973 support for our village, I urge you to take this seriously. The meeting is adjourned.

## Minutes (2)

*   **Agenda**: Selection of 74 Saemaul President (大統領) Grant (下賜金) Projects and Fund Usage
*   **Date**: November 25, 1973, 19:00-21:00
*   **Location**: Village Meeting Hall
*   **Attendees**: Kang Pan-sul (姜判述) and 42 others
*   **Absentees**: Lee Bong-yeol (李奉烈) and 9 others
*   **Chairperson**: Kang Dae-yong (姜大容)
*   **Standing Observer**: Im-sil Myeonlong (任實面長) Park Jin-sik (朴珍植), General Affairs Section Chief (總務係長) Han Jang.

Chairperson: Now, thanks to the special consideration of President Park (朴大統領), our village has also received one million won (壹百萬원) each as income (所得) business funds for outstanding Saemaul villages in 1974. Please share your opinions on what kind of business we should undertake in our village so that we can live well in a few years.

Kang Pan-sul: In my opinion, there are many public works (公共事業) in the village such as small streams (小河川), but they do not require special funds. If we work together, we can do it with our own strength. I think it would be good to select farms without cattle and provide them with cattle. If they are well raised (飼育) and fattened, the profits (利得金) can be distributed in a 6:4 ratio to the raisers (飼育者) and the village. This way, the raisers (飼育者) will do their best to raise (飼育) the cattle, and the village can solve any business issues with the profits (利得金). I think the cattle business (한우사업) is good. Let's also use the village fund of 108,000 won together this time.

Lee Bong-yeol: I agree completely. (Unanimously agreed with no objections (滿場一致))

Chairperson: Next, please share how many raisers (飼育者) we should have for raising (飼育).


--- (p. 526) ---

Kim Pan-yong (金判用): In my opinion, eight people would be the most suitable number. This is because the cattle at the market are expensive, and we cannot afford to buy them with our limited funds.

Lee Gong-u (李共雨): I agree. (Unanimously passed)

Chairperson: Please proceed to select the breeders (飼育者).

Kang Sung-jun (姜聲俊): I nominate Lee Sang-mun (李相文), Lee Si-u (李時雨), Kang Dae-chan (姜大賛), and Kang Dae-sa (姜大沙).

Kim Pan-yong (金判用): I nominate Kang Sung-ban (姜聲般), Jeong Do-sun (鄭道順), Kang Sung-hwan (姜聲煥), and Kang Sung-jun (姜聲俊).

Chairperson: What do you all think of the eight people just selected?

Kang Cheol-su (姜喆秀): I think they have been well selected. (Unanimously passed)

Chairperson: Next, regarding the improvement (改良) of the barns (畜舍), who should bear the cost (費用)?

Lee Bong-u (李奉雨): In my opinion, since the barns (畜舍) are the breeders' (飼育者) own property, it would be best for the breeders (飼育者) to handle the improvements (改良). (No objections, unanimously passed)

Chairperson: Next, please decide on the method and responsible party for purchasing (購入) the cattle (畜牛).

Kang Sung-jun (姜聲俊): It shouldn't be just one or two people; let all the development committee members (開發委員) purchase (購入) and also handle the sales (販賣). (Unanimously passed)

Chairperson: Lastly, please decide on the breeding period (飼育期間) in years.

Lee Man-u (李萬雨): I suggest two years. This is because, while there are separate issues with fattening cattle (肥育牛), the main concern with Hanwoo (韓牛) is the calves.

Kang Dae-mun (姜大汶): I agree.

Chairperson: With that, we will conclude the village assembly (部落總會).

Attendee (參席者) Representatives' Signatures (署名捺印): Lee Gi-hyeon (李基賢), Kang Sung-hwan (姜星煥), Kang Dae-woong (姜大雄), Kang Dae-geun (姜大根), Lee Sang-rae (李象來), Kang Pan-sul (姜判述), Jeon Jeong-eum (全正今), Kang Chang-won (姜昌原), Lee Si-u (李時雨), Kim Gil-seong (金吉成), Kang Dae-sang (姜大相), Kang Sung-jun (姜星俊), Kang Dae-chang (姜大昌), Kang Dae-gyu (姜大圭), Lee Man-u (李萬雨), Kang Jae-won (姜在元), Lee Jong-jin (李鍾振), Kang Dae-chan (姜大燦), Lee Sang-eun (李象殷), Jeong Do-sun (鄭道順), Lee Bong-u (李奉雨), Lee Sang-chan (李相燦), Lee Seong-chan, Kang Seong-eun (姜星殷), Kim Young-sik (金榮植), Kang Sung-chun (姜星春), Kang Cheol-su (姜哲秀), Lee Sang-ho (李相浩), Kang Dae-mun (姜大文), Kang Dae-u (姜大友), Kang Pil-gu (姜弼求), Kang Dae-seop (姜大燮), Kang Dae-il (姜大一), Kim Yang-i (金良二), Kang Pan-seong (姜判成), Lee Jang-seon (李章善), Choi Sang-sun (崔相淳), Lee Sang-sin (李相信).

### Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (3)

**Agenda (議提):** Settlement of the purchase of Hanwoo (韓牛) with the President (大統領) His Excellency's (閣下) special grant (特別下賜金)

**Date (日時):** February 17, 1974, 20:30~22:39

**Location (場所):** Below Kang Pan-nam's (姜判南) room

**Attendees (參席人員):** Kang Dae-chan (姜大賛) and 39 others

**Absentees (不參人員):** Kang Il-su (姜日秀) and 12 others

**Chairperson:** Saemaul Leader (새마을指導者)

Chairperson: We have convened this meeting to discuss the settlement report (決算報告) of the purchase (購入) of Hanwoo (韓牛) with His Excellency's (閣下) grant (下賜金) and other subsequent issues (諸般問題). First, let us hear the report from the Promotion Committee Chairperson (推進委員長).


--- (p. 527) ---

We will now hear the closing remarks.

**Kang Pansul**: Then, I will now report on the settlement (purchase). Mr. Lee Siu (李時雨) purchased 127,000 won, Mr. Lee Sangmun (李相汶) 111,000 won on the 6th (日) market day. On the 6th (日) market, Mr. Kang Daechan (姜大賛) purchased 128,000 won, on the 26th (日) market day Mr. Kang Seonghwan (姜聲煥) 110,000 won, on February (月) 1st (日) Mr. Kang Seongjun (姜聲俊) 132,000 won, on the 16th (日) market day Mr. Jeong Josun (鄭道順) 190,000 won, Mr. Kang Seongban (姜聲般) 150,000 won, Mr. Kang Daesa (姜大沙) 160,000 won, totaling 1,108,000 won, all purchases have been completed.

**Host**: Kang Pansul (姜判述) has just reported on the settlement (決算) regarding the purchases. If you have any comments, please share them.

**Kang Pansul**: Yes, we did try to purchase on the same market day, but it didn't work out because the cattle assigned to the livestock were not available.

**Host**: Any comments regarding the purchases?

**Lee Sangho**: Of course, it was troublesome to attend the purchases, but how was the lunch (點心) at lunchtime?

**Kang Pansul**: Rather, we should have provided the lunch (點心), but we ate at the village (部落) (everyone laughs).

**Host**: Any more comments? (None)

**Host**: Then, we will conclude the settlement (決算) here and for the next purchases, instead of only the development committee (開發委員) going, let's have those who go to the market day go together.

**Kim Panyong**: That is definitely how it should be. This time, since only we went, we didn't know much about the cattle and went here and there, so the sellers charged high prices. It would be better to have people who know about cattle.

**Host**: Any more comments? (None) (Unanimous decision (滿場一致))

**Host**: Then, we will conclude the settlement report (決算報告) here.

: Kang Pansul (姜判述), Lee Giwoo (李奇雨), Kang Seongchun (姜聲春), Kang Daeyong (姜大容), Kang Seongjun (姜聲俊), Lee Manwoo (李萬雨), Kim Panyong (金判用), Kang Seongban (姜聲般), Kang Daechan (姜大賛), Lee Sangun (李相銀), Kang Daegun (姜大根), Lee Gihyeon (李起鉉)

## Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (4)

| Agenda (議提)    | Afforestation of Oak and Timber (用材林)    |
| :---------- | :--------------------------- |
| Date (日時)    | 75. 2.22                     |
| Venue (場所)    | Kim Youngshik's small room              |
| Attendees (參席)    | Lee Sangshin (李相信) and 42 others     |
| Absentees (不參)    | Kang Ilsoo (姜日秀) 8             |
| Host (社會者) | Leader (指導者) Kang Daeyong (姜大容) |

**Leader**: I apologize for being a bit late. The reason I asked everyone to come tonight is simply that we need to plant the seedlings (苗木) we cultivated last spring of 1972 and the county office (郡廳) is supporting us with 100,000 (萬株) oak seedlings, 4,500 of which are subsidized (補助). We need to plant them this spring, but who should plant what on which mountain (山) and what should be planted?


--- (p. 528) ---

We have gathered today to discuss this matter. The saplings (苗木) we have cultivated amount to approximately 62,000, and including the persimmon trees 4,500 and Japanese cedar (扁柏) 100,000 provided to us, we have a total of 166,500 saplings to plant this spring. This covers an area of about 70 hectares.

**Lee Sang-sil (李相實)**: Leader (指導者), please, we must also focus on farming (農事). If we plant trees, it will be troublesome. Our village (洞네) is surrounded by mountains (山中), and if the trees grow densely, wild animals will be a menace and cause significant damage to our crops (農作物). Let's not plant them and instead distribute the free saplings (苗木) to those in need.

**Leader (指導者)**: Everyone, as President (大統領) Park Chung-hee declared the Saemaul Undong (運動), he also announced a 10-year plan for mountain treatment and greening (治山綠化). I believe that the sooner we plant the trees, the sooner our income (所得) will increase. After several negotiations (折衝) with the Forestry Office (조산림과), we have set a plan. Last year, in 1972, when we built the village road, the authorities (行政當局) and all of you said it was impossible (不可能). However, through your relentless efforts (努力), we completed it. If we unite our strength, there is nothing we cannot achieve. For planting trees, we just need to follow the guidance (指導) of the county office's (郡廳) technical (技術) officials (公務員). If we mobilize (總動員) both men and women (男女) and work as if it were our own task, we can finish quickly.

**Lee Man-u (萬雨)**: Since it's already decided (決定), we have to plant the trees. If each household (戶當) sends out 2 people, we can mobilize (動員) about 100 people a day. Could you please tell us how many days it will take for 100 people to complete the task?

**Leader (指導者)**: Well, to plant on approximately 70 hectares, we first need to dig the holes (植穴) for planting, which will take about 35 days. The specifics (具體的) will become clearer once we start the work (作業).

**Kang Daemun (大汶)**: This damn Saemaul (新村). Planting trees is driving me crazy. But if I don't farm (農事) this year, I can still make a living.

**Kang Daesang (大床)**: Brother, don't say that. Last time, when we built the village road, the county magistrate (郡守) said it was impossible (不可能). But we all united (合心) and completed it. Now, cars, taxis, and trucks come right up to our houses, and the county magistrate (郡守) was surprised. Isn't that right?

**Leader (指導者)**: Yes, that's correct. Whatever we do, unity (團結) is key. With unity, we can even move mountains, right? Last November 1973, at the National Saemaul Leader (指導者) Conference (大會) in Gwangju (光州), I heard President (大統領) Park Chung-hee say that the government (政府) will continue (繼續) to support (支援) those who make efforts (努力), but will not help villages that remain idle. I heard this directly (直接) as I attended (參席) the conference. So, let's once again unite (團合) our strength and achieve (發揮) our goals.

**Kang Pansul (判述)**: Alright, let's do it. Everything we've done so far was necessary (必須). If we keep arguing ( 옥신각신), the leader (指導者) will spend a considerable amount (相當) of personal funds (私財) on activities (活動), and no one even covers his travel expenses (旅費). For the sake of his dedication (心情), let's support him.

**Lee Siu (時雨)**: We have to plant them since it's decided (決定).

**Kang Daerim (大林)**: We must plant the trees. Trees (木) are treasures (寶) in the mountains (山中), and water (水) is treasure in the sea (海). Earlier, someone said that dense trees (樹) would attract wild animals (獸), but people in the mountains (山中) would rather die without encountering a tiger (虎) than people by the sea (海) who would drown (溺死) in water (水). Our village (洞네) lacks farmland (農土), so our income (所得) comes from the trees (樹).


--- (p. 529) ---

A few years ago, we used to make a living by selling firewood in Imseong-eup!
**Participant:** Let's do that and laughs.
**Lee Sang-eun (李相銀):** I wonder where we should plant trees and what kind of trees we should plant.
**Leader (指導者):** That's exactly the point. If I choose a place to plant trees by myself, it will be considered as planting privately, which is a problem.
**Kang Daejun (姜大俊):** In my opinion, we cannot make a decision here. Because it is a matter for the county forestry (郡山林) and the technical team (技術陣). Even if we select, it is not suitable (適地) to plant trees like oak trees.
**Kang Seongchan (聲賛):** Let's have the technical team (技術陣) and the leader (指導者) select the suitable (適地) site. For example, if we cut down trees in Naesan this year, we will plant them next year.
**Participant:** That's good. Let's do it that way.
**Leader (指導者):** Any more?
**Participant:** None.
**Lee Jongjin (鍾鎭):** There is one. It is said that we should plant trees with two people per household, but if children come out, the work efficiency (作業能率) will be delayed because of the labor force (勞動力). So, we need to set an age limit (年齡制限). We will do it for those aged 18 and above up to 60.
**Leader (指導者):** That's a very good opinion.
What do you think about what Mr. Lee Jongjin (鍾鎭) just said?
**Kang Daehwang (大旺):** Just leave it to them, why bother with that.
**Lee Jongjin (鍾鎭):** Hey, you must be the one who will definitely send your young son out.
**Kang Daehwang (大旺):** Who knows, how do you know? It's too much to say that I will go out or send my child out.
**Leader (指導者):** Alright, let's stop here. Everyone, do you think Mr. Lee Jongjin's (鍾鎭) opinion is good?
**Participant:** Of course, let's set the age limit (年齡制限) from 18 to 60.
**Leader (指導者):** No more.
**Participant:** None.
**Leader (指導者):** Then, we have decided to plant trees today, and we will entrust the selection of the suitable (適地) site to the technical team (技術陣) and Seohan. The age of the labor force (出力人夫) is decided to be from 18 to 60.
**Leader (指導者):** Thank you. We will conclude today's meeting.

### ♦ Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (5)

*   **Agenda (議事):** Selection of beneficiary households (對象) for the 73rd subsidy (下賜金) project and management of surplus funds (利得金) after the purchase of Hanwoo (韓牛)
*   **Date (日時):** August 17, 1975, 20:00~23:00
*   **Location (場所):** Home of Saemaul Leader (指導者) Kang Daeyong
*   **Attendees (人員):** 51 beneficiaries (對象)
*   **Chairperson (司會者):** Saemaul Leader (指導者) Kang Daeyong


--- (p. 530) ---

**Chairperson**: We have convened this meeting to discuss the selection of target households for the 73th Livestock Purchase Replacement Project and the post-management of the profit (利益金). The meeting has been established with the attendance of more than half of the members.
**Chairperson**: I apologize for calling this meeting despite your busy schedules. Please share your thoughts on how we should select the target households for replacement.
**Lee Bong-woo**: It has already been two years.
**Chairperson**: It has not yet been two years, but we need to select the target households in advance so that they can prepare for barn improvements and other pre-work. Also, yesterday, I decided to purchase a cow from Lee Si-woo after a meeting of the Development Committee (開發委員), as the cow was not eating and was drying up. However, after purchasing the cow, we realized that the selection of target households for the post-management of the village profit (部落利益金) is a preliminary issue that needs to be addressed. Therefore, I called this meeting to report and decide on the matter.
**Chairperson**: First, I will report on the settlement of the purchase of Lee Si-woo's cow yesterday. Initially, we purchased the cow for 127,000 won and sold it after 20 months for 214,500 won, resulting in a profit (利益金) of 87,500 won. Out of this, 52,500 won was given to Lee Si-woo as the usage profit (使用農家利益金), and 35,000 won was deposited in the agricultural cooperative (農協) to be used according to the resolution of the villagers. However, as the price of cows has risen and it was not possible to purchase a suitable cow at the initial purchase price, we met with the temporary Development Committee (開發委員) members at the market and agreed to use the village profit (部落利益金) again for purchasing a cow. Therefore, we purchased the cow from Lee Si-woo for 162,000 won.
**Kim Pan-yong**: Well done.
**Chairperson**: Some of you may have doubts that Lee Si-woo will benefit alone if he raises the cow initially and continues to raise it. However, when we purchased the cow at the market, we received a promise from Lee Si-woo that if a target person is selected at tonight's meeting, the cow will be given to the selected person. If no target person is selected, it will be returned. So, there is no need to worry about that.
**Chairperson**: Please share your thoughts, Mr. Lee Si-woo.
**Lee Si-woo**: Mr. Kang Dae-yong's words are true. If a target person is selected, the cow will be given to the village.
**Chairperson**: Let's decide on this matter first. Currently, when the raising household's (飼育農家) contract period expires and they sell the cow, the amount is distributed in a 4:6 ratio, excluding the initial purchase price. The raising household keeps 60%, and 40% becomes the village profit (部落利益金). Please share your opinions on how to use the village profit (部落利益金).
**Kang Dae-woo**: Currently, the community center (會館) has not been painted, but in other villages, the community centers are well-painted. I think we should paint our community center (會館) and the walls.
**Lee Man-woo**: That is an excellent opinion.
**Villagers**: That is an excellent opinion. (All agree)
**Chairperson**: Are there any other opinions? Please share your good opinions.
**Kang Seong-chun**: There are no other opinions. We cannot do a big project with the profit (利益金), so let's paint the community center (會館) as Mr. Kang Dae-woo suggested and use the remaining amount to purchase a cow.


--- (p. 531) ---

I agree.
Lee Sang-ho: Yes, that's also a good opinion. I agree.
Gang Daemun: I also agree with Gang Seong-yun's opinion.
All residents: All agree.
Chairperson: Then, it has been decided to use the village's profit (利得金) to paint the community center (會館) and use the remaining money to purchase Hanwoo (Korean cattle). We will proceed with the event (行事) in this manner, and the development committee (開發委員) will handle the painting of the community center (會館).
Chairperson: Next, we will select the target households (對象農家) for rotation. When selecting the target households (對象農家), we will prioritize small-scale farmers (零細農).
Lee Sang-chan: We will decide on that.
Resident: All agree.
Chairperson: Then, let's first select the target households (對象農家). You can express your hope (希望) yourself or be recommended by others.
Gang Seong-yun: I will raise (飼育) them.
Lee Sang-chan: I also hope (希望).
Lee Sang-hoon: I will also raise (飼育) them.
Gang Daeyong: I will also raise (飼育) them this time.
Chairperson: Anyone else?
Residents: No one speaks.
Chairperson: Anyone else? (Asking again)
Residents: No one.
Kim Pan-yong: In my opinion, I think Lee Sang-hoon is planning to sell his house and move (移住) elsewhere, so he should not be allowed to raise (飼育).
Chairperson: Kim Pan-yong has raised an objection (異議) to Lee Sang-hoon's hope (希望) to raise (飼育). What do you all think?
Resident: I think it's not allowed.
Chairperson: Then, I declare that Lee Sang-hoon cannot become a hopeful household (希望農家) due to his moving (移住) situation.
Chairperson: Then, the hopeful households (希望農家) are confirmed to be Gang Seong-yun, Lee Sang-chan, and Gang Daeyong, totaling 3 households.
Chairperson: Now, we will select volunteers (希望者) from the current raising households (飼育農家). First, please speak if you do not want to raise (飼育) this time.
Jeong Doo-soon: I will not raise (飼育) this time.
Gang Daeseong: I will also give up (抛棄) this time.
Chairperson: Anyone else?
Lee Sang-mun: I will also give up (抛棄).
Chairperson: So far, 3 people have given up (抛棄). Do the other 5 of you hope (希望) to raise (飼育)?
Gang Seong-yun and 4 others: We hope (希望).


--- (p. 532) ---

Chairperson: That concludes this matter. Fortunately, there are 3 hopeful farm households, but 3 of the previous livestock raisers have given up, so we won't discuss this further.
Chairperson: Now, I will announce the selected farm households. They are Kang Seong-eun, Kang Seong-yun, Lee Sang-chan, Kang Seong-hwan, Kang Dae-yong, Lee Si-u, Kang Dae-chan, and Kang Seong-jun, totaling 8 individuals. Are there any objections?
Villager: No objections (agreeing).
Chairperson: Then, I will summarize. The village's profit will be used to paint the irrigation facility, and the remaining money will be used to purchase cattle. The selection of target farm households resulted in 3 hopefuls and 3 withdrawals from previous raisers, leaving 5 households to continue. Are there any objections?
Villagers: No objections.
Chairperson: Then, I will conclude the meeting. The target farm households are requested to improve their livestock facilities. The meeting is hereby adjourned. After confirming that the above proceedings are accurate, the village representative will sign and seal.

## Development of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) and Required Business Names

**Gang Pan-sul:** Continuously receiving government support, I would like to express my gratitude to the concerned authorities. I would also like to request an explanation of the support amount for 1977.

**Host:** While the official support amount has not been announced, it has been mentioned that cement and reinforcement will be allocated after reviewing each village's business plan. Please propose the specific business names that your village urgently needs.

**Lee Man-woo:** While we have been promoting the Saemaul Undong, there are still unfinished businesses. For instance, bridges need to be built in front of Im Mok-gwi's house, Kim Gil-seong's house, the most cave, Gang Chang-won's house, and in front of Gang Dae-yong and Gang Dae-il's houses. Only then will the path be completely connected. I propose that we proceed with this.

**Host:** Lee Man-woo has just suggested the installation of seven small bridges. Does anyone have other opinions?

**Gang Seong-eun:** While promoting the Saemaul Undong, I have noticed that block walls look better than stone walls. Next year, what if we collectively improve the walls with cement?

**Host:** That's a good suggestion. However, the support association cannot be used for personal purposes but only for public works. Those who want to build block walls should purchase and use them individually.

**All residents:** Agree.

**Host:** Are there any other opinions?

**Lee Bong-woo:** I would like to make a second request.

**Host:** If there are no other agenda items, we will proceed to a vote. Please raise your hand if you agree with the proposal made by Lee Man-woo and the second request made by Lee Bong-woo.

**All members:** Agree.

**Host:** Then, the Saemaul Undong for 1977 will be decided as the installation of seven bridges. However, we also need to promote other businesses. I would like to point out that Gang Dae-rim and Gang Dae-rim must improve their housing. Although it may be personally difficult, the village will volunteer to help. We will designate and plan this as an essential business for our village.

Furthermore, we plan to plant 500 trees within the village. Please be aware of this, and we also need to repair the already installed 14 bridges slightly. Does anyone object?

**All residents:** Agree.

**Host:** Then, we will report the beautification plan to the face (administrative unit) as it is. Please make sure that all households and home improvements are completed. This concludes the meeting. Thank you.

**Resolution by the Residents' General Meeting (住民總會決議)**
Signed and sealed by the representative of the Development Committee (開發委員代表署名捺印).

## Agenda (議案): Fundraising (基金募金) for the 77 Saemaul Beautification Project (事業)
Date (日時): December 5, 1976, 1:00 PM
Location (場所): Rihee Hall
Attendance (參席人員): Total (總員) 52, Present (參席) 52
Chairperson (司會者): Village Head (里長)(지도자(指導者)) Kang Daeyong (姜大容)

**Chairperson (司會者)**: Thank you.
Thanks to everyone's active cooperation, our village, although it is a remote area (奧地), has been diligently carrying out the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) since 1971. Although the work was arduous at the time, it has now become a village filled with smiles.
However, to organize and carry out the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) this year, we must dedicate part of the abundant harvest (豊作) we achieved through hard work this year to support next year's Saemaul Undong (新村運動).
After our general meeting (總會) on October 15, the promotion committee (推進委員) and I estimated that we would need around 700,000 won for next year's projects to run smoothly.
You have all diligently prepared the funds (基金) every year, enabling us to carry out the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) smoothly. If anyone has good ideas for next year's projects, please share them.

**Kang Pansul (姜判述)**: We residents all know about the sacrifices and services our leader (指導者) has been making. It would be good to collect voluntary donations (喜捨金) orally here. I myself will contribute 5 sacks (斗) of rice (白米).

# Minutes (會議錄)

*   **Agenda (議題)**: Purchase of Shared Materials (共同資材)
*   **Date (日時)**: March 10, 1977, 19:20
*   **Location (場所)**: Village Community Center
*   **Attendees (參席人員)**: Total target population (總對象) 52 people, Attendance (參席人員) 49 people, Absentees (不參) 3 people
*   **Present Government Officials (臨席公務員)**: Local Administration Clerk (地方行政 書記補) Park Hong-seop

**Opening Declaration (開會宣言)**: It is declared that 49 out of 52 total households (總世帶數) are present, making the meeting well-attended.

**Chairperson (司會者)**: To complete our Saemaul Undong (새마을事業) this year, we urgently need to purchase materials. As far as I know, we will need 1 ton of steel reinforcement at 12,500 won (including freight (運賃)), 94 sheets of steel at 102,460 won, 15 ridge beams at 3,300 won, and 2,800 won for stone, totaling 233,560 won.

**Kang Pansul**: When securing the village fund (마을基金) for our village (部落), we have secured funds to complete the Saemaul Undong (새마을事業). Please do not worry, Village Head (里長) and Saemaul Leader. Let us work as one (渾然一體) for Yeonhwa Village and purchase the materials to complete the work.

**Chairperson (司會者)**: Are there any other opinions (意見)?

**Kang Daemun**: When securing the village fund (마을基금) for our village (部落), as far as I know, we secured funds to install facilities (施設) for Angon Farm. What about Angil Farm Road?

**Chairperson (司會者)**: The Angil Farm Road is our village's long-cherished project (宿願事業). We have proposed this twice to the upper authorities (上部) and to our guests visiting our village. We plan to secure more village funds (마을基金) and complete the work with full funding (完金). Please understand this, residents (住民). The Angil Farm Road seems to have government support (政府支援), so it can be done during the first half (上半期) of the budget (豫算) execution (執行). If not this year (今年), we will do it next year (來年).

**Lee Gongu**: As the Village Head (里長) said, the Angil Farm Road requires a large budget (豫算), so it is better to first complete the Saemaul Undong (새마을事業) with our own village funds (部落 자체(自體) 마을基金(基金)).

**Chairperson (司會者)**: Are there any other opinions (意見)?

**All Residents (住民一同)**: None.

**Chairperson (司會者)**: Then, with the questions from Kang Pansul and Lee Gongu, the residents unanimously (滿場一致) agreed to purchase the materials (資材購入). With this, we will conclude the Residents' General Meeting (住民總會). Thank you.
