# ♦ Minutes of the Meeting (13)

**Agenda:** Final Report on the Construction of the Shared Workspace
**Date:** June 28, 1977
**Location:** Village Community Center
**Chairperson:** Saemaul Leader (Gang Daeyong)
**Attendees:** Gang Daeyong and 45 others
**Absentees:** Gang Judong and 7 others

**Chairperson:** We will now begin the final report meeting for the construction of the shared workspace. I would like to express my sincere gratitude to all the residents, committee chairpersons, committee members, and auditors who have worked hard for this project.

First, on December 31, 1976, 300,000 won was withdrawn for gravel, sand, cement, formwork usage fees, nails, and lumber totaling 300,000 won. On April 9, 500,000 won was withdrawn for bricks, lumber, and cement totaling 500,000 won. On April 27, 220,000 won was withdrawn for the annex (120,000 won) and lumber (100,000 won). On May 13, 150,000 won was spent on lumber, rebar, thread, ridgepole, and sludge. On May 17, 87,000 won was spent on labor, 88,000 won on doors, 22,000 won on gas masks, 900 won on nails, and 2,100 won on tractor fares. On May 31, 50,000 won was spent on water-based paint (interior and exterior), rollers, and brushes. On June 8, 50,000 won was spent on roof painting (pigments, varnish, and paint). On June 27, 6,000 won was spent on decoration and locks, and 45,000 won on labor. In total, 1,521,000 won was spent, and today we have completed the construction.

Please review and confirm all documents, and share the results.

**Auditor:** Yes, throughout this time, with the Saemaul Leader at the center, all residents have united and completed the project without any issues. After carefully reviewing the procurement of materials and payment of wages, we have determined that only necessary materials were purchased and the construction was completed with economy. Additionally, we would like to report that there are no irregularities in the disbursement of business funds.

---

**Chairperson:** Thank you for your hard work. Although the busy farming season is approaching, I believe the transplanting will be finished soon. (Laughter)

**Chairperson:** Thank you. We will conclude the final report here. Please do not neglect the Saemaul beautification project while focusing on farming. Ensure proper management, and no matter how busy you are, please make cleaning a part of your daily life. Thank you. June 1977.

Based on the resolution of this development committee, the expenditure details are disclosed, and the attendees sign and seal in representation of the resolution of the general assembly of residents.

**Leader:** Gang Daeyong
**Promotion Committee Member:** Gang Pansul
**Women's Association President:** Jeong Dosun

Chairperson: Please share your thoughts, citizens.
Citizens: We have no objections.
Chairperson: No objections?
Citizens: We have no objections.
Chairperson: Lastly, I would like to express my gratitude to all of you once again. Please treat the communal work site (共同作業場) as if it were your own home, taking care of it to ensure it leads to increased income (所得增大). If any repairs are needed, please take the initiative to fix them. I would like to express my thanks to the government (政府) once more and wish for the continuous (繼續) development (發展) of our village. With that, we will conclude the final settlement (總決算) of the communal work site (共同作業場) construction (新築) project funded by the special support fund (特別支援金).
Thank you very much.

## 4. Future Development Plan (發展構想)

*   In 1978, as part of the demonstration village (示範마을) development strategy (育成策) for business income (經營所得事業), we will expand the purchasing and selling business (購販事業) to not only provide affordable daily necessities but also improve the circulation of agricultural products (農產物) and link it with the purchasing and selling business (購販事業).
*   We will introduce 30 more head of beef cattle (肥肉牛) and test the raising of dairy cows (乳牛).
*   In 1979, we plan to introduce and raise 10 head of dairy cows (乳牛) to increase dairy farming (落農) and supply milk (牛乳) to the Imseal Cheese Factory (任實 치즈 공장). We will also build one new small reservoir (小溜池) to improve water safety (水利安全沓化).
*   In 1980, we will increase the number of dairy cows (乳牛) to 50 head, purchase a small truck (小型 트럭), and fully mechanize (機械化) farm equipment (農機具) to modernize (科學化) operations (營業). Through this, we will definitely achieve the modernization (近代化) of rural areas (農村) and the construction of a welfare-oriented rural community (福祉農村建設) to leave as a legacy (遺產) for future generations (後孫).

# Jeonbuk (Jeollabuk-do) Jeongeup-gun (Jeongeup County) Soseong-myeon (Soseong Township) Bohwa-ri (Bohwa Village) Waseok Village (Waseok Village)

## 1. Overview of the Village

### a. History

*   During the Joseon (Joseon) Dynasty, it belonged to Sogo-myeon (Sogo Township), but after the Japan-Korea Annexion Treaty in 1914, it was integrated into Soseong-myeon (Soseong Township) as part of an administrative district reorganization.
*   From the late Three Kingdoms (Three Kingdoms) period to the later Baekje (Baekje) period to the present, this village has been known as Waseok Village (Waseok Village) because a black stone measuring 2m wide, 1m long, and 1.5m high has been lying diagonally in the village.
*   Even today, this stone is located in the courtyard of Kim Yong-ha's (Kim Yong-ha) house in this village.

### b. Location and Conditions

#### <Location>

*   Located about 30 ri (approximately 13 km) southwest of Jeongeup-eup (Jeongeup Township), the location of Jeongeup County Office (Jeongeup County Office).
*   Along the way, the Soseong (Soseong) Reservoir is situated. This reservoir, developed as a long-standing project for the benefit of the people due to the severe drought in 1968, has become the only agricultural water facility that allows for all-weather farming.

#### <Conditions>

*   This village, located in the mid-mountainous area, has a national road connecting Jeongeup (Jeongeup) and Go-eup (Go Township) running through its center.
*   To the southeast of the village, well-cultivated farmland is organized.
*   The village's back mountain and the southwest side are connected by the boundary line between Gocheon (Gocheon) and Jeongeup (Jeongeup) County.

## 2. Village Development Process (發展過程)

### Before 1970 (70年 以前)의 상황(狀況)

#### 1) Basic Environment (基礎環境)

*   The village paths were so narrow that even shoulder poles could barely pass through, with crumbling and dilapidated stone walls or fences nowhere to be seen. The village had been desolate since the 1950s, with small houses moving to neighboring villages.
*   Thatched houses made of mud walls were covered with straw or barley stalks, their sunken roofs overgrown with mushrooms and weeds, appearing abandoned. Most houses lacked proper rooms or verandas, consisting mainly of mud walls.
*   Moreover, the village had been a stronghold for communist forces during the Korean War (6.25 戰亂), leaving behind ideological destruction and delusions that lingered on.

#### 2) Income Level (所得水準)

*   Even during the Japanese colonial period (日帝時代) 35 years ago, income was derived mainly from cultivating cotton and ramie. The village relied on forest products from the surrounding areas for subsistence.
*   Before the expansion of irrigation facilities (水利施設), each household could farm an average of 0.9 hectares of fields (畓), but most were tenant farmers (小作農).


--- (p. 545) ---

# In the 1970s

O As land consolidation (耕地整理) was carried out and agricultural water facilities (農業用水施設) expanded, the average farm size per household (戶當平均) grew rapidly to 1.3ha.

O The main source of income (所得源), cotton (木花) and ramie cultivation (栽培), also failed to thrive due to the emergence of chemical fibers (化學纖維製品) and synthetic products (人造製品), losing economic viability (經濟性). As a result, the average annual income (平均所得) of residents was a mere 410,000 won (千圓).

O Residents relied on slash-and-burn agriculture (火田) on the hills behind the village to cultivate chili peppers, sweet potatoes, and tobacco (葉煙草) for income (所得).

O Livestock farming, such as Hanwoo (韓牛) cattle, pig (養豚), and poultry (養鷄), faced challenges with feed (飼料) and disease prevention (疾病豫防) due to a lack of basic knowledge (基礎常識), leaving the village in extreme poverty.

## 3) Living Conditions in 1970

### a) Consciousness Structure (意識構造)

O Since the 1930s, residents' living conditions (生活形便) had gradually worsened, making day labor (日品拍) their primary occupation (主業) during the spring famine (春窮期).

O People's minds (人心) were harsh, yet they were trapped by feudal ideology (封建思想) and conservative ideas (保守主義), unable to find a path to self-reliance (自立), making them powerless (無氣力) residents.

O Swept up in a decadent atmosphere (頹廢風潮), they were extremely lazy (懶怠), indulging in drinking (飲酒), gambling (賭博), and other wasteful habits (浪費弊習), accumulating high-interest debt (高利債) yearly (每年). Even young people, who should have been working and studying daily (每日), spent their days drinking or gambling, and teenagers often abandoned their hometowns (故鄕) for distant lands (客地).

O Consequently, most farming households (農家) struggled to survive on borrowed grain (貸與糧穀), and there was no hope (希望) or pioneering spirit (開拓精神) for the future (來日).

O The only hope (希望) or pride (自豪) was the children (子女) who had left the hometown (故鄕).

O As more farming households (農家) went bankrupt (破産) and abandoned their beloved hometowns (故鄕), village residents (住民) became even less cooperative (協同) and lacked self-help spirit (自助精神).

### b) Cultural Life (文化生活)

O In such a corrupt (腐敗) and ruined (廢墟) village, there was no cultural life (文化生活) to be found.

O The only sources of information (消息) were two radios (收音機) sent by children (子女) struggling in distant lands (客地).

O The education level (敎育水準) was so low that there were only three high school graduates (高等學校卒業者), and even they had to leave for distant lands (客地) to find opportunities.


--- (p. 546) ---

## B. The Launch of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

### 1) Motivation (動機) and Trial Project (試驗事業) Results

#### 〈Motivation (動機)〉
O In 1971, a person with the firm resolve to work for this village was Jeong Hak-yi, who stands as the current leader. He had, since as early as 1968, organized a village core group (求心體) capable of developing the village to awaken the residents who had regarded poverty as their fate.
O This is also the current village youth association (靑年會), which gathered members and attempted to eradicate illiteracy (文盲) to quickly acquire the benefits of civilization (文明) in this village.
O Despite the village being in ruins due to extreme poverty and ignorance (無知), the residents fought endless hardships using sweat (利用하여) to increase income. They built greenhouses for strawberry farming and succeeded in special crop (特用作物) cultivation.
O Thinking about how to create a prosperous and blessed village where everyone could live well and overcome persistent poverty, he took the initiative.
O Coincidentally, in 1970, the President (大統領) initiated the Saemaul Undong, which echoed in this village as well.
O The first Saemaul project in 1971 was a success when the government (政府) supported the village by providing free Saemaul cement (用  양회) and the 150-meter village entrance road was completed through community unity.
O At this pivotal moment when the Saemaul wave was resonating, the leader precisely recognized that the Saemaul Undong could drive poverty out of the village and pave the way for a better life. He made a personal resolution to persuade each resident by first convening a general village meeting (住民總會).
O On January 20, 1971, a general village meeting (住民總會) was called, but only 6-7 people out of 52 households attended.
O The meeting was postponed to the next day, and he even visited each household (戶別) to plead with tears, but only about 10 people attended again.
O Therefore, on the third attempt, he mobilized the well-organized village youth association members and devoted his full effort (全力) to persuading the residents (住民) from early morning.


--- (p. 547) ---

At this time, the villagers, unable to bear it any longer, saw three-quarters of the households (38 households) participate in the post-war efforts.

Saemaul leader Jeong Hak-i began to passionately argue at the Village Assembly (住民總會) as follows:

- We must drive out laziness and decadence from our village and unite with all our might under the resolve to live well together.
- Why must we suffer and starve? What fault of ours forces us to cling to makeshift solutions and live miserably all our lives?
- The villagers' understanding, cooperation, and dedicated participation, especially among the youth, were repeatedly encouraged to ignite their enthusiasm.
- Where there is a will, there is a way. With the firm resolve that "we can do it," we can build a prosperous village together.
- With such heartfelt appeals, a few young people took the lead, following the leader's vision, and eagerly promised to cooperate in village affairs.

Thus, a revitalized Youth Association (靑年會) was reconstituted at the meeting.

- **President (會長)**: Han Jong-young (韓鍾永)
- **Vice President (副會長)**: Han Ju-seok (韓周錫)
- **Members (會員)**: 14

- Subsequently, a Women's Association (婦女會) was organized.

- **President (會長)**: Park Geum-soon (朴今順)
- **Vice President (副會長)**: Kim Seung-hee (金承姬)
- **Members (會員)**: 23

- A Development Committee (開發委員會), crucial for village improvement and advancement, was established, with each member providing their signature and seal.

- **Development Committee Chair (開發委員長)**: Han Gyu-pal (韓圭八)

1. **Date (日時)**: January 23, 1971, 20:00
2. **Location (場所)**: Leader's residence (指導者自宅)
3. **Attendees (參席人員)**: 38 (34 male, 4 female)
4. **Master of Ceremonies (司會者)**: Jeong Hak-i (鄭鶴二)

The villagers, who had long accepted poverty as their fate, and the ruined village of Wa-seok (臥石) were filled with the enthusiasm to live well together. They resolved to dedicate themselves to leaving a meaningful and valuable legacy for future generations.


--- (p. 548) ---

At the meeting, the first decision made was to draft a simple plan for the Saemaul project. It was agreed that the narrow village access road, which was barely passable even with a shoulder pole, would be expanded to 5 meters in width. At the same time, it was resolved to commence basic environmental improvement projects. The meeting concluded with these decisions.

<Pilot Project>
On the morning of January 29, 1971, after persuading each household to bring out hoes and shovels, all the villagers were gathered in one place. From that day, a 150-meter village access road was expanded. Although the initial plan with the village youths made the work progress smoothly, there were significant difficulties with the land company. Thus, this marked the first step of the grand history of Saemaul. Through this project, the scattered hearts of the villagers were united, becoming a crucial moment of solidarity. The first attempted project was completed successfully amidst hardships and trials, showcasing the villagers' cooperation that was truly commendable. However, resolving the farm road integration land for the access road was a significant barrier. Consequently, the villagers showed evident hesitation. Therefore, the village leader, Mr. Jeong, compared his position with the current situation of the villagers. He made a firm decision and initially offered 6 sacks of white rice to purchase the land, but it was insufficient. However, the villagers, with their conscience, started with some offering their fields and others donating, leading to the completion of the access road project in just 13 days. This instilled greater courage and confidence in the villagers, reinforcing their belief that "we can do it."

In the impoverished and ignorant village of Waseok, leader Jeong Hak-i (鄭鶴二) served while concurrently holding the position of sub-village head.


--- (p. 549) ---

3) Overcoming the Narrow Path (隙路) Situation (狀況)

O Mr. Jeong (鄭氏) took charge of the village affairs, working with a sense of pride (矜持) and conviction (信念) that he would live his life to the fullest despite the overwhelming challenges. Unfortunately, his father suffered from stomach cancer (胃癌), a condition that left the family in dire circumstances.
O In such an environment, Mr. Jeong managed to complete his third year of high school in Jeonju, but due to his father's illness, he spent his days merely tending to the remaining farmland, living in vague and uncertain times.
O However, on March 16, 1970, he represented his village and district (所屬面) as the chairman of the 4-H Club and received a week of agricultural education, life improvement, and spiritual revolution (精神革命) education at the Jeonju County (井邑郡) Rural Guidance Center (農村指導所).
O Before he could reflect on what constituted a wise (賢明) life, his family situation was dire. After his father's passing from stomach cancer (胃癌), having squandered the family fortune, Mr. Jeong struggled with despair.
O Yet, the sight of vibrant young people in the village kept his resolve to lead and improve the village alive in his mind.
O Determined to lift his family out of poverty (貧困) and hunger and to develop his village, he vowed to overcome any hardship.
O Fortunately, his first business venture in January 1971 was successful, giving him hope.
O By August 29, 1973, having completed extensive local education, Mr. Jeong attended the Central Training Institute (中央硏修院) of the Saemaul Undong, a turning point towards self-reliance (自立) for his village.
O Through approximately ten days of disciplined and systematic education, he learned the essence of the Saemaul spirit (精神), which, coupled with his unwavering determination and perseverance (執念), greatly aided in the gradual development of his village.
O Driven by a spirit of self-sacrificing service (犧牲的 奉仕 精神), Mr. Jeong led the residents, taking pride in his efforts. By March 1974, his dedication resulted in the village receiving a special livestock resources project.
O In November 1976, the village was granted another 1,500,000 won (千元) from the President's (大統領) special support project (特別支援事業). Mr. Jeong tirelessly worked to resolve land (敷地) issues and secured 1,850,000 won (千元) for the village fund.
O The Wa-seok (臥石) village, determined to create a new history (歷史), has reached its present state through Mr. Jeong's relentless efforts, despite having no time to tend to his own family (家庭). His achievements (業績) came with numerous bittersweet stories (喜悲劇).
3) Overcoming the Narrow Path (隙路) Situation (狀況)
O After volunteering (自願) as a Saemaul Undong (新村運動) leader, Mr. Jeong aimed to foster a sense of cooperation (協同), unity (團合心), and participation (參與) among the residents (住民). He initiated the project to open a new village access road (進入路).
O Several village general assemblies (住民 總會) were held, but the residents' response was underwhelming.
O With residents struggling to meet even their basic food needs (食生活), Mr. Jeong grappled with how to engage them in collective work (共同作業).


--- (p. 550) ---

He could not help but feel disheartened about how to pursue the Saemaul Undong (運動) so that people could live well.

So, in early spring of 1971, he decided to cultivate strawberries in a 500-pyeong vinyl greenhouse in his own field for early growth, aiming to develop a market relative to Jeongeup (井邑). He planned to promote strawberry seedling cultivation targeting farmhouses with land.

However, the residents had no experience in strawberry cultivation and were primarily concerned with basic sustenance, making it difficult for them to understand easily.

Eventually, he invited a guidance teacher from the Jeongeup Rural Guidance Center (井邑農村指導所) to conduct strawberry cultivation education (敎育). He also set the condition that if there were losses in the market, he would take responsibility for compensation. As a result, vinyl greenhouses, clearly visible, were installed on 6.9ha of land.

With the firm belief and will of "It can be done," he was able to showcase high-quality strawberries in the market for the first time, bringing a sense of accomplishment with a total income of 360,000 won that year.

Through this, the residents' awareness began to change gradually, and they started to trust the leader. They followed whatever the leader said.

Taking this as an opportunity, Leader Jeong (鄭) encouraged the residents to participate directly in the Saemaul business and exerted his full efforts to establish the village fund, which serves as the foundation for all businesses.

On September 5, 1972, he convened a general meeting of the residents to create a turning point for the new village.

Nearby villages pooled their money, collected bit by bit, into a village safe to discover the secrets of living better in Waseok (臥石) village. They held a general meeting to elect a village safe director and to invest the village's jointly obtained income into the village safe.

First, they reached a consensus to elect Han Gyu-pal (韓圭八), the most understanding and influential person in the village, as the village safe director by unanimous vote. As a result, the first Guppan business was implemented, leading to the establishment of the current large safe.

However, the efforts of Vice President Park Geum-sun (朴今順) were truly remarkable in further solidifying these achievements.

The residents' resolve to live well, expressed in words alone, collapsed overnight on March 6, 1973. The accountant in charge of the village safe's accounting (會計) had embezzled the entire 375,000 won, which had been contributed with blood, sweat, and tears, and disappeared.

Residents filled with despair and resentment began to gather and make noise at Leader Jeong's (鄭) house.

However, Leader Jeong, gathered with the director and vice president, pleaded with them.

Here, Vice President Park Geum-sun (朴今順) made a firm resolution. How powerful a woman's strength could be for the village.

The vice president first urged the women's club members to absorb various subordinate organizations into the village safe and invest in it, repeatedly appealing to them to make a new start, in order to reassure the residents.


--- (p. 551) ---

O They succeeded in reorganizing the village treasury just before it went bankrupt.
O To facilitate household contributions, the women's association president personally purchased piggy banks for each home, and to generate even a small profit, they operated a rotating joint purchasing and sales center, which gradually reduced the number of women going out to shop.
O It was only when the village treasury cultivation and self-reliance village advancement rally achieved the glory of surpassing 2 million won that the leader truly felt the satisfaction of their hard work.
O Furthermore, Saemaul leader Mr. Jeong saw success in strawberry farming in 1972 and wanted to consistently increase income over three years by cultivating specialty crops alongside previous crops to boost farm income.
O It was March 10, 1974.
O Until then, it was believed that tobacco farming was extremely difficult in Wa-seok Village, but through Saemaul income-increasing education, he realized that tobacco farming was possible even in Wa-seok (臥石) Village.
O To this end, he installed a vinyl greenhouse on his 400-pyeong field to cultivate tobacco and decided to distribute seedlings to farms.
O Initially, the success and effort from strawberry farming moved the villagers, and the residents were filled with the belief that "if this is the path to a better life, we will achieve it no matter what."
O Thus, on August 20, 1974, they produced 12% from a total area of 8.5ha and received 1.65 million won from the tobacco cooperative, marking the third achievement that led to the village's promotion to self-reliance.
O However, leader Mr. Jeong, who was not satisfied with this alone, started cultivating high-quality vegetables in vinyl greenhouses.
O The convenience of market channels in Jeonju, Jeonju, and Gwangju, connected by highways, made it even easier to cultivate high-quality vegetables.
O They began installing vinyl greenhouses to cultivate high-quality vegetables, specifically Chinese chives, on half of the field area, totaling 13ha, through crop rotation.
O The income from high-quality vegetables, started in the early spring of 1974, was remarkably bountiful, raising the farm household income per capita to 1.37 million won for the year.

## 4) Developmental Promotion of the Saemaul Movement (事業)
O Following the successful implementation of village entrance road construction and internal village road improvements,
O On April 2, 1973, they easily promoted the installation of 450m of village sewers,
O Around the same time, they constructed a 15m small bridge on the farm road,
O For this, government-supported cement was insufficient, so they secured 1.65 million won from village funds, achieving results through strenuous effort and burden,
O When rural telephone services were expedited and ignited, all villagers in Ondong rejoiced and celebrated.
O This renewed their awareness of the Saemaul Movement.
O Additionally, they established a communal daycare center, temporary water supply facilities, agricultural product drying facilities, communal storage, communal workspaces, village community centers, and communal


--- (p. 552) ---

The kitchen (炊事場), nutrition improvement center, and other cultural (文化) welfare (福祉) facilities, as well as production (生産) infrastructure (基盤) development projects, have been completed by the villagers. They:
* Carried out wall (담장) improvement and painting, roof improvement and painting, wall (壁體) repair, and substandard housing (住宅) improvement and demolition repair work in parallel, and completed the installation of methane gas facilities and telephone lines aimed at rural (農村) modernization (近代化), transforming the village into a new historical (歷史) community.
* Through the residential area (住居圏) improvement project, they attached tiles to kitchens and toilets (便所), enabling a hygienic (衛生的) lifestyle (生活).
* In the mid-mountain (中山間) village, they raise 43 head of Hanwoo (韓牛) cattle suitable for the local conditions (與件), and are currently focusing on tobacco leaf (煙草) production, high-quality vegetable (菜蔬) farming, and strawberry cultivation as their main income-generating (所得) activities (事業).
* In 1976, the President (大統領) graciously provided special (特別) support funds, which were used to build a 60-pyeong (坪) community (共同) warehouse (倉庫). This allowed the village to store government (政府) grain (糧穀), earning storage fees (保管料) that doubled their income (所得). Additionally, they operated a nutrition (營養) improvement (改善) center, not only improving (改善) their diet (食生活) but also processing and producing (生産) canned food and cheese for sale (販賣).

### 5) Land (土地) and Cash (現金) Donation Status (狀況)
* Encouragement (激勵) and comfort (慰勞) poured in from all sectors (各界) to this village where residents toiled (努力) with sweat and blood (피땀).
* The residents also donated their ancestral land (문전옥토) and generously contributed cash (現金) for the Saemaul Undong (事業), embodying a spirit (精神) filled with nobility (高貴).

## 6) Heartwarming Stories

### a) Story 1

O On May 20, 1975, National Assembly Member (國會議員) Jang Dong-sun (張垌淳), who hails from this area, visited to see the self-reliant development of the village savings bank (마을금고).
O He was deeply moved by the village's steadfast efforts to improve the savings bank and the remarkable progress made through the Saemaul Undong, despite living in a rigid and decaying old way of life.
O He encouraged everyone to endure and live well, no matter what difficulties or dangers might come, and promised to always help if they showed their efforts to live well.
O At that time, Representative Jang donated 100,000 won to support the Saemaul Undong projects being carried out in the village.
O Later, on November 5, 1976, he donated funds for the construction of a community grain storage facility, enabling the village to store grain independently. The entire village was overjoyed.

### b) Story 2

O During the peak of the Saemaul Undong, the Ministry of Health and Social Affairs provided special support funds for the installation of simple water supply facilities (간이급수시설).
O To secure land for a communal water collection well (공동집수정), village development committee chairperson Han Gyu-pal (韓圭八) agreed to use 43 pyeong (坪) of his own land and donated it on March 16, 1977.
O This made it possible for all households in the village to use hygienic water through the simple water supply facilities.

# 8) Special Notes (特記事項)

### a) Joyful Events

* When the village entrance road, which residents thought they couldn't build, was successfully opened through the Saemaul Undong, and when residents responded enthusiastically to building it with sun-dried bricks
* On April 20, 1973, when the provincial interior affairs bureau chief first visited the village
* When National Assembly member (國會議員) Mr. Jang Dong-sun (張垌淳) donated 100,000 won and residents cheered with joy
* When the village was promoted from a self-help (自助) village to a self-reliant (自立) village in 1974
* When the village was designated as the best village in Jeonju County (井邑郡) in 1975
* When the village received a visit from FAO (세계식량기구(世界食糧機構)), British, and Filipino members to inspect the nutrition improvement (營養改善) center operations
* When the village received special support funds (特別支援) from the President (大統領) in 1974, 1976, and 1977
* When a simple water supply facility (簡易給水施設) was installed and residents' faces lit up with joy as water flowed abundantly into each home
* When the 60-pyeong (坪) village communal warehouse (共同倉庫) was completed and residents participated in the completion ceremony (竣工式)

### b) Sad Events

* When elders criticized the village for moving a large rock at the village entrance, saying it would bring misfortune
* When stubborn residents insisted on not touching the annex buildings while expanding the village interior road
* When the village treasurer (金庫 會計員) disappeared with all the investment funds (出資金), and the leader was blamed and punished

## Ba. Achievements through the Saemaul Undong (事業)

1) Spiritual Aspect (精神面)
* Through the Saemaul Undong (事業), a new human image of diligence, self-help, and cooperation was established,
* People gained confidence that they could overcome any obstacle,
* Through village assemblies or neighborhood meetings, a forum for dialogue was created, and Korean democracy (民主主義) was embodied,
* A sense of gratitude towards the government (政府) and a spirit of neighborly love was cultivated.

2) Livelihood Aspect (生活面)
* With the reform of farming techniques, seed renewal, and the expansion of off-farm income businesses, incomes increased,
* Farmers adopted a progressive attitude and practiced thrift and frugality,
* The spirit of reform discarded empty rituals, and the philosophy of helping the underprivileged and ensuring that every village could prosper became a practical philosophy for the nation's long-term future.

3) Production Aspect (生産面)
* The expansion of high-yield varieties under the Tongil system (統一系統) increased unit production (生産量),
* The cattle breeding business (事業) and warehouse storage fees from the subsidy business (事業) doubled residents' incomes.

3. Village Assembly (住民總會)

♦ Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (1)
Date: December 23, 1970, 20:00
Location (場所): Jeong Hak-yi's (氏) house
Agenda (議提): Opening of village entrance road
Attendees (參席人員): Han Gyu-pal (氏) and 37 others
Chairperson (司會者): Jeong Hak-yi


--- (p. 557) ---

Host: I am truly sorry to have called this meeting so late at night. The reason is that the neighboring village is brimming with enthusiasm for the Saemaul Undong, actively promoting it. However, promoting the Saemaul Undong is not just about using government-supported materials like cement and rebar. First, we need to utilize the farm paths to carry out shoulder pole work and expand this path into a farm road, creating a safe path for everyone to use. That is why I have called this meeting.

Leader: What are you rambling on about? Just get to the point.

Han Jae-seok: We are proposing to expand this path, which has already been prepared by our young members, to a width of 5 meters. Through this path, we aim to rid ourselves of poverty and create a prosperous village.

Han Gyu-pal: Your suggestion is indeed good, but who will solve the issue of the land required for road access, and who will take responsibility for it?

Leader: I will take full responsibility for this, but it is impossible without the cooperation of all the residents. Therefore, if Mr. Han Gyu-pal, Han Nae-su, Kim Yong-ho, and Kim Yong-ha could donate their land for this path, it would be possible.

Han Gyu-pal: Alright, I will donate 45 pyeong first. Let the others express their opinions.

Han Nae-su: I will also concede 3 pyeong.

Kim Yong-ho: Kim Yong-ha and I will agree as well.

Leader: Thank you very much for your cooperation. However, we must carry out the work ourselves. I would like to start the joint work from tomorrow, but what do the elders think?

Han Gyu-pal: There's no choice. We must solve our own problems. It would be good if one person from each household comes out to work from tomorrow.

Participants: All in favor.

Leader: Then, I will believe that everyone will work from tomorrow and will thoroughly prepare by organizing a work team.

Han Gyu-pal: Alright, let's adjourn the meeting.

Leader: Thank you. I'm sorry for the late hour. This concludes the meeting.

## ◆ Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (2)

| Item         | Content                 |
| :----------- | :------------------- |
| **Date(日時)** | January 18, 1971           |
| **Location(場所)** | Han Gyu-pal's House (宅)     |
| **Agenda(議案)** | Village Path Expansion (擴張)  |
| **Attendees(參席人員)** | Han Nae-su and 44 others |

Leader: I am truly sorry to have called this meeting so late. Before this meeting, the sub-county magistrate and the general affairs section chief visited our village. They highly commended us for the access road we had promoted and completed last time. They promised that next year, our village would receive government support to obtain Saemaul Undong materials. Our village must also, with our own strength,


--- (p. 558) ---

Expansion (擴張), let's try that.

**Han Gyeong-su**: Are you really trying to ruin the neighborhood (洞里) by calling meetings (會議) just because you have nothing to do during the winter for the New Community Movement (事業)?

**Leader**: Absolutely not. We should use the off-season (農閑期) to expand (擴張) the paths within the village that we can freely use during the busy farming season, and create a comfortable village to live in.

**Han Gyeong-su**: I've lived to be 60 years old, and I still don't understand what all the fuss is about.

**Han Jae-su**: Instead of just talking, let's all work together to widen the paths like the neighboring village so we can comfortably use our shoulder poles.

**Han Chang-nam**: I don't know how wide the paths in the village should be. Please tell us about this.

**Leader**: Yes. Since we're talking about a long-term plan (百年大計), it would be best to expand (擴張) it to a width (幅) of 4 meters.

**Han Jae-su**: Then we'll have to demolish (撤去) all the existing fences (全體).

**Han Young-ho**: The land value (所要) required to widen the paths is a big problem (問題). Let's come up with a solution (解決策).

**Leader**: Originally (原來), the village fund (마을基金) is a fund (基金), but we will need the generous donation (喜捨) of the landowners (地主) and I ask that you all not spare your sincere cooperation (協助).

**Han Young-ho**: If we do that, we'll have to tear down several houses. What support measures (支援對策) should be in place? Let's all gather opinions (意見).

**Han Jae-su**: No, I believe it would be wiser (賢明) for the residents (住民) to make sacrifices (勘當) themselves by each making concessions (讓步) for the land (用地) issue (問題) being promoted (推進) by the New Community Movement (事業).

**Leader**: I think that would be a good idea.

**All residents (住民一同)**: All in favor (贊成).

**Leader**: Next, what should we do about the mobilization (出役) issue (關係) that we residents (住民) should do ourselves?

**Han Jae-su**: Let's form a joint work team (共同作業班) and have all residents (住民) under the age of 60 (歲) participate (參與) fully (全員).

**All residents (住民一同)**: Let's elect (選出) the work team leaders (作業班長) here. Let's have the 1st team leader be the youth leader (青年會長), the 2nd team leader be Han Gyu-pal, and the 3rd team leader be the women's leader (婦女會長).

**All residents (住民一同)**: All in favor (全員 贊成).

**Leader**: Tomorrow (來日) morning, please gather at the work site (場所) using a bell (鈴) as a signal (信號). That's all for the meeting (會議). It's dark, so please go home safely (安寧).

## Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (3)

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Date (日時) | 74. 3.10. |
| Location (場所) | Han Gyu-pal's house |
| Agenda (議題) | Expansion (擴大) of high-quality vegetable (高等蔬菜) (上菜) cultivation (栽培) area (面積) |
| Attendees (參席人員) | Jeong Hak-i and 37 others |
| Chairperson (司會者) | Jeong Hak-i |


--- (p. 559) ---

**Host**: Tonight, we have gathered all of you, the villagers, for a meeting with one purpose: to increase rural income (農村所得增進). I believe that we should not focus solely on traditional agriculture but should expand the cultivation (栽培) of economic crops (經濟作物) to boost farm income (農家所得). The main reason I emphasize this is that, as you all know, we had some success with this last year, which has given us confidence. Therefore, this year, our goal is to greatly expand cultivation (擴大栽培) in our village to achieve increased income (所得增進).

**Villager (김용호)**: The guidance (指導) we just heard was excellent. However, to push forward with this endeavor (事業), we need to explore our approach (推進方針) and management methods (經營方式). I propose we discuss this.

**Villager (한규팔)**: In my opinion, we should manage (經營) everything from purchasing materials (資材購入) to cultivation (栽培) through collective work (共同作業). Since our technical skills (技術) are currently lacking (未洽), working together (共同) will provide an opportunity (契機) for all of us to acquire (習得) the necessary techniques (技術).

**Host**: Han Gyu-pal suggested we proceed with collective cultivation (共同栽培). What do you think?

**All Villagers (住民一同)**: No objections.

**Jeong Hak-i**: I conducted a trial cultivation (試驗栽培) in a 200-pyeong greenhouse (平). Including the cost of materials (資材代), the total management cost (經營費) was 80,000 won, but the total revenue (總收益) was 165,000 won. Even after deducting the management cost (經營費), we could easily earn 100,000 won per pyeong (反當). Given this, I am optimistic that the future development (發展) of our village looks bright. We have good transportation (交通), good water, abundant farmland (耕地), and with effort, we will surely succeed (成功).

**Guide (한재수)**: I heard the practical experiences (經驗談) shared by Village Head (里長) Jeong Hak-i. We farmers always have to fight and win against the land. If we use this as an opportunity (契機) to introduce (導入) technology (技術), conduct our own research (硏究), and develop (開發) our existing resources (賦存資源), I believe our village will become a modernized (近代化) ideal rural village (理想農村) by the 1980s. Let us all unite (合心), learn, and move forward together (前進), with the guide (指導者) and village head (里長) leading the way.

**Host**: Then, we will adopt the plan (方案) to proceed with collective cultivation (共同栽培) and collective sales (共同出荷) through work teams (作業班).

**Villager (한영호)**: I have an opinion (意見).

**Host**: Please share it.

**Villager (한영호)**: Regarding the management (管理) of greenhouses (비닐하우스) and high-quality vegetables (高等蔬菜), we currently lack technical expertise (技術的). Therefore, I suggest we receive technical guidance (技術指導) from the crop division (作物係) at the Rural Guidance Center (農村指導所).

**Host**: That's an excellent idea. Let's choose an appropriate time (時間) to invite them for education (敎育).

**All Villagers (住民一同)**: We strongly agree (大贊成).

**Host (Village Head, 里長)**: What should be the scale (規模) of our cultivation area (栽培面積)? If anyone has good opinions (意見) on this, please share them. As discussed above, we will make a resolution (決議) and have the attendees (參席者) sign and stamp (署名捺印) it.

**Attendees (參席者)**: Lee Sang-gi, Choi Dong-sun, Han Gwan-ho, Han Nae-su, Im Sun-taek, Han Tae-su, Kim Jeong-dae, Kim Yong-hwan, Hwang Gyu-ik, Han Jae-seok, Mun Yong-nim, Han Jin-seok, Kang Geum-rye, Han Gyeong-su, Lee Bok-rye, Kim Yong-ha, Han Jae-su, Han Il-seok, Kim Yong-o, Jeong Hak-i, Baek Nak-seon, Hwang Jong-du, Seo Man-seop, Jo Il-chul, Han Gyeong-ho, Hwang Jong-du, Han Geum-dong, Han Myeong-ho, Na Nam-sik, Han Chang-ho, Han Gyu-pal, Lee Geum-jin, Nam Jeong-gyeon, Kim Seol-ja, Han Gyeon-ho, Im Chae-il, Hwang Taek-gu, Han Eul-seok, Park Yeon-rye.


--- (p. 560) ---

### Minutes (會議錄) (4)
*   **Date(日時)**: December 10, 1976
*   **Location(場所)**: Wa-seok Saemaul Community Center
*   **Attendees(參席人員)**: 43 people
*   **Agenda(案件)**: Selection and Promotion of 1976 Special Support Project
*   **Chairperson(司會者)**: Saemaul Leader Han Jae-soo, Ri-jang Jeong Hak-i
*   **Guests(臨席者)**: Myeon-jang Lee Sang-mun of So-seong Myeon, Chief of General Affairs Han Gap-jeon

**Ri-jang(分離長)**: Today, we will discuss the methods for selecting and promoting the special support project bestowed by His Excellency the President (大統領).
**Kim Yong-o(金龍五)**: The special support project must be well managed in the future and should serve as the foundation for increasing our village's income. Let us carefully consider the projects we select.
**Leader(指導者)**: In my opinion, since our village's main industry is rice cultivation using the unified system, it would be beneficial to establish a village community warehouse (共同倉庫) as a production facility. This would not only facilitate the storage of grain but also reduce transportation costs for long-distance deliveries and increase storage fees, contributing to income growth.
**Ri-jang(分離長)**: The leader has suggested establishing a village community warehouse. Please feel free to share your opinions.
**All Residents(住民一同)**: We have no objections and agree.
**Ri-jang(分離長)**: What do you think would be the most appropriate scale for the warehouse?
**Han Chang-nam(韓昌男)**: Since our village already has a 400-pyeong plaza, I think we should locate the warehouse there and build it to a scale of 60 pyeong, which should meet the government's grain storage requirements.
**All Residents(住民一同)**: We all agree.
**Ri-jang(分離長)**: Based on our discussion, we have decided to build a 60-pyeong village community warehouse. Regarding the residents' share of the cost, which amounts to 1,850,000 won, please share your thoughts.
**Kim Yong-o(金龍五)**: The residents' share should be used from the village fund, and the three of us—the leader, ri-jang, and development committee chair—should jointly manage the expenditure.
**All Residents(住民一同)**: That would be good.
**Ri-jang(分離長)**: Finally, I would like to once again ask for your continued cooperation and hereby declare this meeting adjourned.

### Minutes (會議錄) (5)

*   **Location(場所)**: Saemaul Community Center
*   **Attendees(參席人員)**: 49 people
*   **Agenda(案件)**: Election of Project Promotion Committee Members
*   **Chairperson(司會者)**: Ri-jang (分離長)

**Host (社會者):** We will now hold a meeting to elect the promotion committee (推進委員) for the Special Support Fund (特別支援金) project (事業). Please select capable individuals to promote the project (事業) as decided at the last village assembly (部落總會) on December 10th for the construction (新築) of a new communal warehouse (共同倉庫). The project funds amounting to 1,500,000 won have been deposited into the unit association (單位組合) account by the face of the village head, Saemaul leader, and Ri-jang (里長), and the passbook (預金通帳) is also here.

**Cho Il-chul:** You have worked hard indeed. Please select someone with the ability (力量) to successfully promote (推進) the project (事業).

**Han Jae-su:** I will recommend. Let Han Gyu-pal be the promotion committee chair (推進委員長), and let Jeong Hak-i and Han Jae-su be the auditors (監査).

**Han Gyu-pal:** Let Han Yong-su, Mun Yong-rim, and Han Jae-seok be the promotion committee members (推進委員).

**All Residents (住民一同):** That sounds good. I believe we have selected individuals with strong promotional abilities (推進力).

**Host (社會者):** Are there any other recommendations?

**All Residents (住民一同):** None.

**Host (社會者):** Therefore, it is announced that Han Gyu-pal is elected as the promotion committee chair (推進委員長), Jeong Hak-i and Han Jae-su as auditors (監査), and Han Yong-su, Mun Yong-rim, and Han Jae-seok as promotion committee members (推進委員). I sincerely request that the elected project committee members (事業委員) redouble their efforts (奮發) and dedicate themselves (獻身) to volunteer (奉仕) for an excellent project (事業). This concludes the meeting.

## Minutes of the Meeting (會議論) (6)

*   **Date:** June 1, 1977
*   **Venue:** Waseok Village Hall
*   **Agenda:** Settlement (決算) of the completion (竣工) of the communal warehouse (共同倉庫) (Special Support Project (特別支援事業))
*   **Attendees:** Jeong Hak-i and 40 others
*   **Host (社會者):** Ri-jang (里長) Jeong Hak-i

**Host (社會者):** Thank you very much for your attendance today. Due to your active cooperation (協助) during the warehouse construction (新築) period (期間), we were able to complete (完工) the project and reach the settlement (決算) stage. I will now report on the progress (經過) of the construction (工事). The scale (規模) is 60 pyeong of cement bricks and steel frames, and the construction period (工事期間) took approximately 3 months from February 27, 1977, to May 30, 1977. The total construction cost (工事費) was 3,229,000 won, which includes the Special Support Fund (特別支援金) of 1,500,000 won, interest (利子) of 13,980 won from the deposit period (預置期間), and the residents' burden (住民負擔金) consisting of village funds (마을기금) of 59,440 won and village savings bank loan (마을금고 대부금) of 1,120,580 won, totaling 1,715,020 won.

The number of workers (動員人員) mobilized for this project (工事) was 341, including 152 special laborers (特殊人夫) and 189 ordinary laborers (普通人夫).

○ The main materials (資材) used for this project (工事) were 40,000 cement bricks, 600 cement bags, 1,300 kg of rebar (鐵筋), 250 steel frames (스레트), 90 plywood (合板) sheets, 31 rubbe of sand, 21.5 rubbe of gravel, 24 m³ of rubble (雜石), 80 piles (말뚝), 310ℓ of waterproofing agent (방수제), 2,620 units of lumber (木材), 50 rolls of binding wire (結束線), and other miscellaneous items. The detailed list (明細) of items (物品) and expenditure records (支出內譯) are attached separately.


--- (p. 562) ---

As reported above, we have presented the settlement (決算) report. If there are any doubts or objections, please speak up.

**Han Gyeong-su**: You have worked hard throughout the project (事業) promotion (推進) process. Among various questions (質問), regarding the settlement (決算) report details, the use of bricks appears to be less on paper. Could you please explain?

**Host**: 300 sheets were naturally damaged (破損) during the construction (工事). Are there any other questions (質問)?

**Han Gyu-pal**: The report mentions that the borrowed funds (借用金) exceeded 100 million won. Could you please explain the repayment (償還) strategy (對策)? Should we collect (徵收) from the residents (住民) to cover this, or are there other methods?

**Host**: As initially agreed (決議), we plan to replace 40 million won from the village funds (部落資金) this autumn, and use the income (收入) from storing grain (糧穀) in the warehouse (倉庫) to repay (償還) the remaining balance (殘額). Currently, we have no plans (計劃) to impose (賦課) any additional charges.

**Choi Dong-sun**: I would also like to sincerely commend (致賀) the village leader (里長) for his efforts (勞苦) in promoting (推進) this project. In the future, all village residents (部落民) should cooperate (協助) in repaying (償還) the borrowed funds (借用金), and the promotion (推進) committee chairperson (委員長) should make every effort (最善的努力) to manage (運營) the warehouse (倉庫) without any flaws (瑕疵).

**Host**: I deeply appreciate (敬意) your remarks. If there are no further comments, please vote for approval (可決).

**Hwang Dae-ik**: I propose to accept the settlement (決算) report as is.

**All Village Residents (部落民一同)**: We agree (贊成).

**Host**: As you have heard, the settlement (決算) report for the construction (建立) of the warehouse (倉庫) using the grant (下賜金) is concluded here. This will conclude the meeting (會議).

**Han Gyu-pal**: We are grateful to the authorities (當局) for their consideration (配慮) in continuing government (政府) support (支援). Please have the Sub-village Head (分里長) directly (直接) explain the plan (案).

**<Business Overview(槪要)>**: Village entrance road (進入路) stone wall (石築) 150m, inner village road (안길) paving (鋪裝) 350m, sewer (下水溝) covering (覆蓋) 480m, temporary water supply facility (簡易給水施設) 37 units (號), wall (擔墻) plastering (泥匠) and painting (塗色) 1,200m, housing improvement (住宅改良) 13 units (棟), home improvement business (事業) 47 households (號)

**Chairperson(司會者)**: Are there any other opinions (意見)?
**All Residents(住民一同)**: None.

## 4. Future Development Plan

○ In 1978, as a model village for income-generating businesses, we will promote collective marketing of agricultural products and explore market channels in conjunction with the cooperative's joint sales.
○ We will introduce 50 more Hanwoo cattle and cultivate large-scale high-quality vegetables to manage triple cropping.
○ We will expand the nutrition processing center to utilize idle labor and aim to expand the machinery sector.
○ In 1980, we will purchase 5 small tractors and fully mechanize farm equipment to achieve scientific farming, passing this legacy on to future generations.


--- (p. 566) ---

# Jeonbuk (Jeollabuk-do) Buan County (Buan-gun) Baeksan-myeon (Baeksan-myeon) Geumsan-ri (Geumsan-ri) Shin-geum Village

## 1. Overview of the Village

### A. History

*   At the end of the Joseon Dynasty (李朝), this area was tidal flat land belonging to Geoma-myeon (巨麻面) in Gobu County (古阜郡), a stronghold of the Donghak Peasant Revolution (東學).
*   In March 1914, during the administrative reorganization of provinces, counties, and districts, it was transferred from Geoma-myeon in Gobu County to Baeksan-myeon in Buan County.
*   In 1921, during the Japanese colonial period, the Oriental Development Company (東洋拓殖會社) constructed a seawall along the west coast and a dike along the Dongjin River (東津江), and established a large-scale farm (東拓農場) in this area. Additionally,
    *   In April 1922, 10 hectares of farmland were reclaimed and distributed to 10 households: 3 households of the Lee family (李氏), 2 households of the Park family (朴氏), 1 household of the Hong family (洪氏), 1 household of the Jeong family (鄭氏), and 1 household of the Kim family (金氏), with each household receiving 1 hectare.
*   For the next 23 years, the village suffered from the exploitation of the Oriental Development Company's farm, becoming known as a symbol of poverty, often referred to as an "immigrant village" or a "slum." However,
*   After liberation in 1949, the implementation of the Land Reform Act (農地改革法) led to the privatization of the land, boosting the farming enthusiasm of the owners and significantly improving farming techniques and yields. As a result, the cultivated area per household doubled, and the village came to be known as the "new gold field (新金)" by nearby residents, a name that endures to this day.

### B. Location and Conditions

#### <Location>

*   Located 25 km southwest of the famous Bansan Peninsula (邊山半島) and Bansan Beach (邊山海水浴場), one of the eight major tourist attractions in the country, and 6 km east of the county office.
*   Adjacent to Gimje (金堤), it is situated 16 km away, a 20-minute drive along the unique Bonggol Dike (碧骨堤) that cuts across the heart of the Honam Plain (湖南平野).
*   The village is located along the lower reaches of the Dongjin River (東津江), which originates from the western foothills of Moak Mountain (母岳山) in the Noryeong Mountain Range (蘆嶺山脈) and flows into the Yellow Sea (黃海). The village has a history of battling annual floods and tidal waves, making flood control a constant challenge.

#### <Conditions>

*   Composed of tenant farmers who suffered under the exploitation of the Oriental Development Company (東洋拓殖會社) during the Japanese colonial period, the village's residents harbored a sense of victimization and despair.
*   Lacking proper irrigation facilities, the village was at the mercy of annual droughts and flood damage, relying on the heavens for its fate.
*   With a clay soil composition, the village's narrow access roads would often be submerged in mud whenever it rained.


--- (p. 567) ---

## 2. Village Development Process (發展過程)

### 가. Situation Before 1970 (70年 以前 的 情 境)

#### 1) Basic Environment (基礎環境)

O The 800-meter access road from the provincial road between Jeonju (全州) and Buan (扶安) to the village was a narrow, winding path following the edge of rice fields, too narrow for even a cart to pass, with a width of about 1 meter.
O The road's base was low, so when it rained, it would flood the fields, making passage impossible without rain boots. In front of the village,


--- (p. 568) ---

The stream flowing through the village was littered with torn old clothes and discarded shoes, and the village paths and courtyards were unclear with about 30 thatched-roof houses (草家) without toban (토방) or verandas, with mud walls crumbling in places, giving a desolate atmosphere.

## 2) Income Level (所得水準)
O Focusing on rice and wheat (米麥) farming methods, the village utilized 65ha of farmland (耕地面積) inherited from ancestors to build an income base (所得基盤).
O The farmland per household (戶當) was 1.6ha, and the average annual income (平均所得) of the villagers in the 1970s (70年代) was 750,000 won (千원).
O Early attempts to introduce double cropping (二毛作) farming methods and cultivate rapeseed (油菜栽培) in most fields, excluding lowland paddies (低濕畓), failed repeatedly.
O Some villagers participated in high-value product production (高供品生產) such as sack weaving during the winter farming off-season (農閑期), but did not progress beyond the initial stages.

## 3) Lifestyle Before 1970 (70年(年) 이전(以前)의 생활상태(生活狀態))
### a) Consciousness Structure (意識構造)
O Living in ignorance (無知) and poverty (貧困), the villagers had no hope or plans for the future (來日) and were indifferent (無關心) and expressionless (無表情) in everything, knowing neither diligence (勤勉) nor laziness (懶怠), envying (嫉視) others, and spending their days (消日) drinking (飮酒) and gambling.

### b) Culture (文化) and Clothing, Food, and Shelter (衣食住) Lifestyle (生活)
O Without electricity (電氣施設) at the time, the villagers were too busy just trying to survive, unable to afford a newspaper (新聞) or a magazine (雜誌). The entire village had only three radios, which were the sole source (唯一) of news (新聞) about the country and the world (國內外).
O Despite focusing on rice and wheat (米麥) as staple crops (主穀) in agriculture (農業), the villagers often had to borrow long-grain rice (長利쌀) from neighboring villages during the spring famine (春窮期).
O In years when even one harvest passed, the villagers would go to nearby tidal flats to gather "namuchae" (나무채) or collect seeds from wild plants growing in the fields to make porridge.

## b. Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (運動)
### 1) Motivation (動機) and Results of Pilot Projects (試驗事業)
O In 1970, when the Saemaul Undong (運動) was spreading across the country, this village also sought to break free from old habits (舊態依然) and


--- (p. 569) ---

A small reform and new spirit began to emerge.
With the support of the government for the experimental project, 200 bags of cement were provided, allowing for the construction of a temporary water supply system for 40 households, a community center, and a communal warehouse. However, due to the lack of community consciousness and cooperation among the residents, the construction deadline was significantly extended beyond the original plan. Additionally, the lack of technical skills and rough construction led to substandard work.

Some residents, still unaware of the situation, would gather at the local tavern and complain that the New Community Movement was forcing them to participate daily, even when they had no food to eat, openly expressing their grievances and dissatisfaction.

## 2) Selection and Activities of Leaders

A leader named Jeong Young-mo, who had completed his studies in the Law Department at Chungang University in Seoul, began his activities to revitalize the rural village, fulfilling a dream he had since his student days. Along with a few influential villagers who shared his vision, he initiated a project to improve the village's basic environment. However, securing funds for the project was extremely difficult due to resistance from the residents.

After much effort, they managed to secure a fund of 300,000 won, including the income from a communal field. Leader Jeong Young-mo was overjoyed, like a general who had won a battle. Thus, the first phase of the New Community Movement began in 1970.

## 3) Overcoming Challenges

To foster a sense of cooperation and participation among the residents, Leader Jeong Young-mo believed that community work, such as improving the village's internal roads, should be initiated. Noticing that an old stream running through the village's southwest side was hindering the expansion of the internal roads, he decided to block the stream with the residents' efforts to widen the roads. However, even before the project could begin, he faced strong opposition from the residents.

The residents argued that they had never faced any significant threats to their livelihoods despite the lack of internal roads and that even if they invested considerable effort and manpower to build them, what material benefits would they gain?

Although the expansion of the internal roads was a matter decided by the village assembly, the leader realized that he had not presented the residents with substantial effects that they could agree upon. Along with the promotion committee members Gang Su-won and Han Du-shik, the leader visited each household daily to persuade and seek their understanding.

Eventually, even the residents who had been vocal in their complaints began to participate in the New Community Movement, which was flowing like a great river. Sensing a turning point in the residents' mindset, Leader Jeong felt the need for a symbolic and central figure for the village.

A decision was made at the village assembly to prioritize the construction of a community center over other projects, and a vacant lot in the center of the village was chosen for the purpose. On September 20, 1970, the day Shin-geum Village was reborn, the strong will of the residents gathered in front of the Taegeukgi flag gave Leader Jeong immense courage.


--- (p. 570) ---

*   Leader Jeong (鄭) leveraged the residents' fervent enthusiasm to simultaneously push forward with simple water supply facilities for all 40 households and the construction of a communal warehouse.
*   In early 1971, after achieving considerable success in the 1970 Saemaul Undong (運動) pilot project, Leader Jeong, along with his promotion committee, identified road improvement as the top priority among various environmental improvement projects desired by the residents.
*   The 850-meter farm road and village access road connecting the village to the provincial road between Jeonju (全州) and Buan (扶安) was so winding that it was nicknamed "the crooked road." It followed the edge of rice paddies, crossed numerous ditches, and during rainy seasons, would flood, making it impassable.
*   When the road expansion project was presented to the village assembly, all residents agreed, but when it came to their own land being included, they would suddenly change their tune.
*   The desperate resistance of a 70-year-old man, who had endured 36 years of Japanese colonial exploitation and hardship, refusing to part with the land he had barely managed to acquire, was heartbreaking. Meanwhile, a drunk resident would charge in, threatening to stab Leader Jeong with a sickle if he dared touch his land, causing work to halt several times.
*   Landowners whose farmland was included in the road expansion would chase Leader Jeong to his home at night and early morning, demanding compensation and hurling insults. Leader Jeong's wife, Mrs. Jo (趙), eventually fainted from the outrage. However, undeterred, Leader Jeong persisted with unwavering determination and conviction.
*   After pushing forward with the project for about 20 days, with 1,360 people mobilized from the neighboring village, the final day of the road expansion construction arrived, and the village was filled with a festive atmosphere.
*   The road, previously only 1 meter wide, was now expanded to 7 meters, straight and wide enough for large trucks to pass freely. The elderly villagers, in particular, marveled and praised the transformation, saying they had no regrets left in life.
*   On this joyous day, another remarkable change occurred: the landowners, who had previously harbored jealousy and caused trouble, suddenly visited Leader Jeong to apologize for their past behavior and express their gratitude for his efforts. Leader Jeong felt the first genuine sense of accomplishment in his life.
*   Furthermore, after enduring immense hardship, the village constructed a communal fertilizer site covering 800 pyeong (坪) to relocate the unsanitary fertilizer previously stored within the village walls, and completed the improvement of 16 roofs through self-help efforts.

## 4) Developmental Promotion of Saemaul Undong (事業)

*   The successful completion of the village community center and road expansion projects strengthened the bond among residents, fostering cooperation and unity.
*   In 1972, the village completed the expansion of 2,490 meters of farm roads, improved the roofs of 30 houses, and installed telephone facilities in 27 households.


--- (p. 571) ---

In 1974, the year when the initial ambitious project of penetrating the village's east-west roads by filling the discontinued water channel was undertaken, the residents' new determination converged. However, some residents began to express opposition, questioning how much benefit the residents would truly gain from the effort and manpower invested in penetrating the east-west roads within the village. To understand and persuade the opposing residents, the village leader and the promotion committee visited each household every morning, resulting in the residents once again participating in the Saemaul Undong. They filled the old water channel, which was 2 meters deep, 4 meters wide, and 980 meters long. With a total of 3,023 participants, 4 tractors, and 24 carts mobilized, the project was successfully completed in 35 days of intense effort. Additionally, with 700 bags of government-supplied cement and the residents' share, they completed 980 meters of sewer facilities. On October 14, 1973, the women's association of Singeum Village was organized with 28 members, and Song Bo-sun was elected as the president. However, substantial activities began in February 1974. The women's association members, who shared the government's initiative to promote the family planning campaign as a national movement, actively participated and persuaded their neighbors, making the village a model for family planning in the county. Centered around the women's association members, the village savings bank, which started with thrift rice savings, was composed of 32 members. Despite the fierce commands of their in-laws, they persevered and secured 215,300 won in capital in just six months. Additionally, despite persistent interference from the two existing shop owners, the Singeum Saemaul purchasing and selling market operated solidly, and the women's association members combined their joint work income to secure 2,150,000 won in village savings bank capital within a year of establishment. As the thatched fences were replaced with reinforced concrete walls, 28 households had sturdy door frames and urban-style iron gates. The village residents, who were diligently developing new sources of income outside of farming, discovered that most of their cultivated fields were suitable for growing Chinese cabbage and rapeseed due to the soil quality. They cultivated Chinese cabbage on 10 hectares targeting government supply, earning an annual income of 10,000,000 won from 2,000 bundles, and cultivated rapeseed on 30,000 pyeong, earning 16,000,000 won from 2,000 bundles. Furthermore, actively recommending the high-yield unified rice variety resulted in 82% of all farming households significantly expanding their unified rice cultivation area, achieving a record of 450 kg per 0.1 hectare, which was undoubtedly the result of the Rural Guidance Office's active agricultural guidance. The village designated 1975 as the year to complete roof improvement, excluding two substandard houses, and improved the roofs of all main buildings. The residents completed the roof painting of 19 buildings on their own, and installed 8 meters of clay pipes in 8 sewer locations.


--- (p. 572) ---

It was a project from 76.

- The two 150-pyeong (坪) community warehouses started on March 17, 1977, were completed with the blood and sweat of the residents, establishing a new foundation for income.
- Five dilapidated houses (不良住宅) that were impossible to renovate were improved to standard rural housing through persistent persuasion and effort.
- A 200-meter sewer cover project was completed, allowing 4-ton trucks to pass freely, resolving the inconvenience caused by the sewer located in the center of the village path.
- A modern communal restroom was newly constructed near the village community center, and a children's playground was installed in the plaza in front of the community center, creating a paradise for children.
- Through the campaign to plant five trees per household, 180 trees were planted for the village water supply, and a 30-pyeong (坪) communal livestock barn was completed with a donation of 1 million won, laying the groundwork for future livestock production growth.
- Roof painting was carried out for 36 households, focusing on color coordination to create a pleasant environment. Wall repairs totaling 1,210 meters were completed, making the entire village bright and clean. Additionally, the irrationality of traditional kitchens was corrected, restrooms were improved, and ancillary facilities were renovated, completing the home improvement project for 40 households.

- Fertile land was donated to the village to contribute to the New Community Movement, a shortcut to the modernization of the fatherland. The following is a list of donations received from various sectors to comfort and encourage the residents.

## 6) Heartwarming Stories (美談逸話)

*   With the expansion of new double-cropping (二毛作) farming methods (營農方法), the phenomenon of soil degradation (地力墜落現象) began to occur, and the rice panicles (稔實度) from the milky stage (乳熟期) to the ripening stage (結實期) began to decrease, and the occurrence of pests and diseases (病蟲害發生) increased as the damage (害) increased. Residents (住民) who felt the necessity of compost (堆肥必要性) worked hard on summer compost (夏季堆肥) in the summer.
*   Women members (婦女會員) also decided to participate in wild grass cutting (野營 풀베기) and gathered opinions (意見) to establish a 5-day (日間) schedule (日程別計劃). Women leaders (婦女指導者) Song Bo-sun (宋輔順) contributed 30,000 won (萬圓) from her own funds (私費) to prepare meals (食事準備) and participated in wild grass cutting (野營 풀베기) at Naebyeon-san (內邊山), 16 km away from Sin-geum Village (新金).
*   By achieving 640 holes (穴) of compost (堆肥), exceeding 200% of the target (目標) of 312 holes (穴), the village was selected as the best village (最優村) in the county's (郡內) compost (堆肥施賞) and received a prize (施賞金) of 100,000 won (萬圓).


--- (p. 574) ---

## 8) Special Matters (特記事項)
### a) Joyful Events
*   O When the 730-meter village entrance road was expanded to a width of 7 meters, despite the residents' outer appearances
*   O When the 980-meter village road was filled in, allowing trucks to freely pass through the village
*   O When the backward base village suddenly became a self-sufficient village in 1974
*   O When the temporary water supply facility was completed, ending the need to transport water from 3 km away
*   O When the village received a donation of 1.5 million won from President (大統領) during the National Saemaul Undong Leaders Conference in 1976
*   O When members of the National Unification Democratic National Convention visited the village in 1977
*   O When the male and female Saemaul Undong leaders, as the top income village, met with President (大統領)

### b) Sad Events
*   O When some residents verbally assaulted Leader Jeong during the construction of the village entrance road
*   O When Mrs. Jo, the wife of Leader Jeong, fainted due to the residents' verbal abuse
*   O When residents refused to follow the leaders and promotion committee members during the village road filling

## 12) Achievements of the Saemaul Movement

### A) Spiritual Aspect

O Through the Saemaul Movement, a new human image of diligence, self-help, and cooperation was established
O With the consciousness of "we," a comprehensive system of residents was constructed, and it was realized that any difficult task can be easily accomplished with confidence
O Through the general assembly of residents, it was learned that productive and rational thoughts can be created only from the will of the majority
O As the trend developed from "me" to "we," the spirit of benevolence began to sprout

### B) Living Aspect

O Through the village savings and loans, a frugal and thrifty lifestyle was boldly introduced
O In order to improve farming technology and increase rational productivity, efforts were made to mechanize farming
O A proactive attitude towards life, full of research and development aspirations, was maintained

### C) Production Aspect

O The expansion of rice cultivation increased farm income dramatically
O A new trend began to seek off-farm income sources from livestock farming

### D) Income Aspect

O The average annual household income jumped from 750,000 won in 1975 to 3,481,000 won in 1977, and it is expected that the average annual household income of 5,000,000 won in the 1980s will be easily achieved
