## 3. Residents' Assembly (住民總會)

### ♦ Minutes (會議錄) (1)

*   **Date (日時)** : Jan. 4, 1971, 16:00
*   **Location (場所)**: Village Community Center
*   **Agenda (案件)** : Regarding the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)
*   **Attendees (參席人員)** : 32 people
*   **Absentees (不參人員)** : 3 people
*   **Chairperson (司會者)**: Jeong Young-bo
*   **Attending Officials (臨席公務員)** : Han Woo-sik

**Chairperson (司會者)**: Thank you all for attending. Compared to other villages, we seem to lag behind in every aspect.
This year, let's strive to improve our village's environment (環境) just like other villages do, so we can receive government support (政府支援).
**Han Young-guk**: The access road (進入路) to our village is inconvenient even for carts. I suggest we expand the access road (進入路).
**Chairperson (司會者)**: Please share any good ideas you have.
**Kang Su-won**: I suggest we improve the fences made of straw by replacing them with brick or mud walls.
**Chairperson (司會者)**: Please share any better ideas you have.
**Han Young-guk**: I suggest we establish a communal composting site (共同堆肥場) to gather summer compost (夏季 堆肥) in one place instead of scattered around.
**Chairperson (司會者)**: Then, let's vote on the following matters to select the projects (事業).
For the communal project (共同事業), 30 people will work on expanding the access road (進入路), and 25 people will work on the communal composting site (共同堆肥場). We will prioritize the access road (進入路) expansion, and if we have extra funds (餘力), we will purchase the composting site (堆肥場).
Additionally, we should renovate at least two-thirds of the fences to brick or mud walls, and improve at least one-third of the roofs.
Then, I declare this meeting adjourned.
(All 32 attendees have stamped their approval)


--- (p. 578) ---

♦ Minutes (會議錄) (2)

Date and Time: December 29, 1971, 18:00
Venue: Village Community Center (村會館)
Agenda: 1971 Business Settlement (事業決算) Report
Attendees: 26
Absentees: 9
Chairperson: Jeong Yeong-mo (鄭永模)

Chairperson: Although our village's business, which started with great ambitions, is not lagging behind other villages, the achievements of each individual resident can only be seen as about half of what was planned. However, we have completed the small path we initially planned into a 7m wide and 730m long road, and purchased a 800-pyeong (坪) communal composting site (堆肥場) with our funds and efforts, which has given us a sense of pride that "we can do it too." Especially, breaking down the fences and building floating force dams (浮力) and earthen walls is a significant step forward in our 5,000-year history, and the improvement of roofs is also a great progress. Looking at the business by category, 670,000 won was spent on the expansion of farm roads (農路), 400,000 won on the composting site, 90,000 won was supported for the individual business of roof improvement for 16 houses, and a total of 1,540,000 won was spent, including 1,450,000 won by self-effort. Additionally, 1,245m of earthen walls and floating force dams were installed for fence improvement.

I Sang-keun (李相根): Please explain about the purchase of the access road site (進入路敷地).

Chairperson: We received donations from Han Du-seok (韓斗植), Seo Bok-nam (徐福男), An Sun-ye (安順禮), Gang Pan-seon (姜判善), and Han Gab-seong (韓甲成). For the 17 people who do not live in this village, 1,500 won per pyeong (坪) was paid. If there are any questions, please ask.

All: None.

Chairperson: This concludes the settlement meeting.

(Signed by all 26 attendees)

♦ Minutes (會議錄) (3)

Date and Time: January 23, 1972, 19:00
Venue: Village Community Center (村會館)
Agenda: Regarding the Saemaul Business Plan (事業計劃)
Attendees: 31
Absentees: 4
Chairperson: Jeong Yeong-mo (鄭永模)

Chairperson: This meeting is convened to establish the Saemaul Business (新村事業) plan. I was going to mention this during last year's Saemaul settlement, but since it was not yet finalized, I only discussed it with the development committee (開發委員). The matter is about the telephone business (電話事業). If the subscription fee (請約金) of approximately 20,000 won per household (戶當) is paid by January 25,


--- (p. 579) ---

We can start the construction now. Please raise your hand if you are willing to set up the telephone.
(23 people)

Then, I will conclude the telephone setup and ask you to share this year's Saemaul Undong plan.
**경월금**: This year, we plan to establish a cooperative store as a means to increase income through non-agricultural businesses and indirectly motivate unity.
**All**: We agree.
**Chairperson**: This fair profit, not unjust gain, will be a path to lead our village to prosperity.
Then, please discuss ways to collect village funds.
**이길봉**: I propose collecting 5 sacks of rice per household.
**All**: We strongly agree.
**Chairperson**: We will collect 5 sacks of rice per household. How about the operation of the cooperative store?
**강수원**: Let's decide on the operation of the cooperative store at the settlement meeting after its completion. It's getting late, so let's adjourn now.
**All**: We agree.
**Chairperson**: Then, I will adjourn the meeting now.
(31 attendees' signatures)

## Minutes (4)
*   Date: June 30, 1972, 20:00
*   Venue: Community Center
*   Agenda: Saemaul Undong settlement report
*   Attendees: 23
*   Absentees: 12
*   Chairperson: 정영모
*   Attending Public Official: 한우식

**Chairperson**: You have all worked hard with the Saemaul Undong and the current income-increasing project of transplanting rice seedlings. We planned to hold the Saemaul settlement meeting by the end of May, but due to the busy farming season, we couldn't have a proper meeting. I'm sorry that we could only hold it now.
In February, the telephone business was set up by four additional people: 정동호, 정귀모, 한영식, and 서복남, totaling 27 lines.
The establishment of the Saemaul cooperative store was funded by 18 sacks of village funds and 7 sacks of profits from the joint rice milling facility, totaling 25 sacks, which amounted to 280,000 won. Due to everyone's daily contributions, a 38-pyeong cooperative store was built. The cost of materials was explained by development committee member 이상근 to all of you.
Now, please discuss the operation of the cooperative store.


--- (p. 580) ---

Lee Chang-hee: I propose that the women's association take charge of managing the old market, but we should entrust the operation to a special individual.
Han Yeon-sik: The management of the old market should be entirely handled by the women's association.
Kang Pan-seon: I agree with Lee Chang-hee's opinion. This is because none of the women in our neighborhood are idle; everyone is busy.

Chairperson: Then, let's put Lee Chang-hee's and Han Yeon-sik's opinions to a vote.
* Lee Chang-hee's opinion: 16 votes in favor.
* Han Yeon-sik's opinion: 6 votes in favor.
Lee Chang-hee's opinion has been confirmed. The women's association will take charge, but they should entrust the operation to someone who can investigate market conditions and operate it to procure good items at low prices.
This concludes the meeting.
(Seal of 23 attendees)

♦ Minutes of the Meeting (會議錄) (5)

Date: January 17, 1974, 18:00
Venue: Saemaul Community Center
Attendees: 33
Absentees: 5
Agenda: Regarding the 1974 Saemaul Undong Business Plan
Chairperson: Jeong Young-mo

Chairperson: This seems to be our first village assembly this year. Among the basic environmental improvement projects that have been ignited like a spark, our village still has many issues such as road expansion and sewer construction.
In particular, if we gather our strength, we can completely bury the abandoned irrigation canals flowing through our village and turn them into our farmland.
I will listen to your wise opinions in detail and proceed with the burial.
Kyeong Gil-su: How long is the abandoned irrigation canal in total?
Chairperson: It is approximately 1,000 meters.
Kang Su-won: Our development committee has already selected a site where we can dig and bury the soil. However, all villagers must be mobilized, and everything, including tractors and wheelbarrows, must be mobilized to complete the task as soon as possible.
Kang Pan-seon: If we bury the irrigation canal, a 5-meter-wide village road will be opened. Let's mobilize everyone and bury it.
All: We strongly agree.
Chairperson: Before I speak, I heard you all getting excited and saying that you will lead the project. This proves how crucial this project is to us. Not everything can be done with emotion. Each of you must work tirelessly on land improvement for at least 15 days without a single day off.


--- (p. 581) ---

For 15 days, all tractors and carts must be fully mobilized (總動員) as if there were no distinction between mine and yours.
**Gang Su-won**: Are there any objections to the leader's (指導者) words?
**All**: No.
**Gang Su-won**: Then, let the Development Committee (開發委員會) handle all detailed operational plans (運營計劃), and let's push forward with the leader's (指導者) meticulous personnel mobilization (人員動員) plan (計劃).
**Host**: Then, I will conclude the meeting here.
(33 attendees (參席者) have stamped their attendance (捺印畢))

### ♦ Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (6)

|       | Content                                 |
| :---- | :----------------------------------- |
| Date (日時)   | 74. 6.30 20:30                       |
| Venue (場所)   | Village Community Center (마을會館)                       |
| Attendees (參席人員) | 37                                  |
| Absentees (不參人員) | 1                                   |
| Agenda (案件)   | Spring Season Saemaul Beautification Project (事業) Settlement (決算) Report |
| Host (司會者) | Jeong Young-mo                               |

**Host**: You have all worked very hard with landfill (埋立), sewerage, and farming (農事日). It is because of our belief that "we can do it" that we have been able to achieve this.
Then, we will have a progress report (經過報告) from Lee Sang-geun.
**Lee Sang-geun**: We mobilized (總動員) 4 tractors (耕耘機) and 24 carts to fill in a 2m deep, 4m wide, and 980m long irrigation canal (用水路). A total of 3,023 people worked for 15 days. Although a few people could not participate due to household matters, I felt that our village is a tightly-knit community where everyone takes the lead in the Saemaul movement (隊列) without leaving anyone behind.
Thank you.
**Host**: Are there any objections or shortcomings in Lee Sang-geun's (開發委員) remarks?
**Lee Gil-bong**: We initially planned only for the An-gil expansion (安吉擴張), but we ended up including sewerage facilities (施設) as well. Could you please explain the sewerage facility (施設) issue (問題)?
**Host**: Well said. Whenever you have questions or feel something is unfair (不當), you should speak up to resolve any misunderstandings (誤解).
Please provide a settlement report (決算報告) on the sewerage project (事業), Mr. Park Jong-sun.
**Park Jong-sun**: Due to the complexity (複雜) of Development Committee member (開發委員) Lee Sang-geun's tasks (業務), I took charge of the sewerage project (事業).
With government support (政府支援) of 500 bags of cement (洋灰), additional support (追加支援) of 200 bags, totaling 700 bags of cement (洋灰) worth 315,000 won, and a fund (基金) of 740,000 won, totaling 1,055,000 won, we completed a 980m sewerage system. The total of 1,150 participants (延人員) is thanks to your voluntary service (出役).
**Host**: Mr. Park Jong-sun, who took on this task for the first time, and Mr. Lee Sang-geun, who manages our village affairs, have truly worked very hard. In this regard, please show your appreciation with applause (拍手).


--- (p. 582) ---

Everyone: Applause
Gang Su-won: The person who has worked the hardest is our leader, Jeong Young-mo.
Everyone: Applause
Chairperson: The people who deserve our applause and God's blessings are our Shin-geum residents. The fact that we have completed our work so diligently is clear proof that we are united.
If villages like ours across the country can find such fulfillment in this project, then our future will be filled with hope.
Since roof improvements are currently at 60%, let's prepare the funds and aim to complete them in the second half of the year.
This concludes our meeting.
(Attendance: 37 people sealed)

## Meeting Minutes (8)

Chairperson: We have convened this meeting tonight to establish the Saemaul Beautification Business Plan for 1977. This Saemaul project will be an excellent opportunity to showcase every small effort we have made so far to outsiders. Please feel free to share any good ideas you may have.
Kang Su-won: First, I propose covering the sewer from Lee Gil-bong's house to Han Ok-sik's house. This area always gets flooded and becomes the dirtiest place whenever it rains.

Chairperson: That is indeed an excellent proposal. If there are any other good ideas, please share them.
Gyeong-wol Kim: We hold meetings here at this hall 2 to 3 times a month. However, there is no communal restroom next to the hall, so we have to use Yu Gui-sang's and Kang Pan-seon's restrooms. ## Minutes (9)

Date: January 25, 1977, 18:00
Location: Community Center
Agenda: Selection and Promotion of President's Gift Fund Business
Number of Attendees: 37
Number of Absentees: 4
Host: Jeong Young-mo
Attending Official: Kim Tae-hyun, Assistant Provincial Administrator

Host: This time, His Excellency the President has specially granted us 1.5 million won. We have discussed this with the development committee members, and although there were some good opinions, we have brought this to the village meeting to convey His Excellency's intentions and to find a better opinion that can lead us to a prosperous and united path.
I would like to hear your frank opinions on the business selection.
Park Jong-sun: I would like to hear the thoughts of the development committee members first.
Host: The development committee thought of cultivating high-grade vegetables in vinyl houses. However, we could not reach a final conclusion in the final discussion. This is because there is not a single person in our village who possesses the cultivation technology for vinyl houses.
Yu Gui-sang: I hope that the President's gift fund will be used for a business that is clear and has a high chance of success, so that we can respond to His Excellency's intentions with a constructive business.


--- (p. 585) ---

Host: Please select successful business ventures (事業) if there are any, as suggested by Yu Gui-sang (劉貴相).

Park Jong-sun: Every year, a public auction market (共販場) for autumn grain procurement (秋穀收買) is being established in our village. Recently, due to the high yield of Tongil (統一) rice varieties, significant individual and village losses are occurring even when the grain is piled up in the fields and transported to the Baeksan Agricultural Cooperative (白山農協) auction market. Therefore, I would like to establish a joint warehouse (共同倉庫).

Host: If there are any other opinions (意見), please share them.

Lee Gil-bong: I would like to purchase a drying machine (乾燥機) to improve the quality of autumn grain procurement (秋穀收買) and contribute to increasing farmers' income (所得向上).

Host: Are there any better opinions (意見) above?

All: No.

Lee Chang-hee: As this is an important business (事業) initiative, could we please have about 30 minutes for discussion (討論)?

Host: Then, we will proceed to a vote (票決).

Please raise your hand (擧手) if you agree with Lee Gil-bong's opinion (意見).

4 people.

Please raise your hand (擧手) if you agree with Park Jong-sun's opinion (意見).

29 people.

Out of the total attendees (總參席人員) of 37, 29 votes (票) were cast for Park Jong-sun's opinion (意見) to establish a joint warehouse (共同倉庫), 4 votes (票) for Lee Gil-bong's opinion (意見) to purchase a joint drying machine (共同乾燥機), and 4 abstentions (棄權). It is announced that the establishment of a joint warehouse (共同倉庫) has been selected. Please devise (講究) a plan for the warehouse site (敷地) and the contribution (醵出) of joint funds (基金).

**Kang Su-won:** Let us construct a 100-pyeong (坪) community grain storage (共同倉庫) facility to store government grain (政府良穀) shipped from Geumpan-ri and use the storage fees (保管料) to create a village fund (마을기금) for future development (發展).

**Chairperson (社會者):** Are there any objections to Kang Su-won's proposal?

**All (一同):** None.

**Gyeong Gil-su:** The government (政府) is currently offering loans (融資) for the construction of grain storage facilities (保管倉庫). Can we also apply for a loan (融資)?

**Chairperson (社會者):** I have already looked into this matter. According to the military government's food administration officer (糧政係長), if we construct a community grain storage facility (共同倉庫) of 100 pyeong (坪) or more, we can first establish it using village funds (마을 기금) and then receive a loan (融資) of 8,600,000 won from the agricultural cooperative (農協).

Let us first contribute by August 10 and use the common property (共同財産) as collateral (擔保) with the bank (銀行) or unit association (單位組合) to secure a loan (融資) of approximately 7,000,000 won for construction. **Chairperson (社會者):** Then, let the development committee (開發委員) members and I explore the possibility of securing a loan (融資) and complete the construction as soon as possible.

### 4. Future Development Plans (發展 計劃)

* In 1978, as part of the plan to foster a model village for foreign promotion (弘報), we plan to expand farm income (所得) beyond agriculture (農外) by collectively (共同) raising 40 pigs (養豚) to develop additional income sources (所得源).
* We will cultivate high-quality horticultural crops (高等 園藝 作物) in 30 greenhouses (비닐하우스) for double-cropping (二毛作沓) and further expand the purchasing and selling business (購販 事業) to supply daily necessities (生必品) at low prices (低廉), while also promoting collective (集團) sales of agricultural products (農產物) in conjunction with the agricultural cooperative's (農協) purchasing and selling business (購販 事業).
* We will actively promote the housing savings system (賦金制) to transform 15 substandard houses (不良 住宅) into standard rural housing (農村 標準 住宅), and by establishing senior citizen centers (敬老堂) and libraries (圖書館), we will enhance residents' respect for the elderly (敬老) ideology (思想) and research motivation (硏究 意欲).
* We will fully mechanize farm equipment (農機具) and modernize farming (營農) through science (科學), aiming for a farm household income (農家 所得) of 5,000,000 won in the 1980s to achieve the modernization (近代化) and welfare (福祉) of rural areas (農村), which we must inevitably accomplish and pass on to future generations (後孫) as a valuable legacy (遺産).

# 1. Village Overview

## 가. History

In 1636 (the 28th year of King Seonjo's reign in the Joseon Dynasty), Giryong Village in Yongsan-ri, Geumsan-myeon, Gimje-gun, Jeollabuk-do was a large village with over 100 households. However, it was completely burned down during the Imjin War and became an abandoned village. Later, Yun Dongto, a magistrate of Gimje, praised the land below Geumsan Mountain as the greatest land under heaven and held poetry gatherings there.

In 1654 (the 5th year of King Hyojong's reign), local Confucian scholars established Geumseong Seowon (a Confucian academy) to study literature. However, in 1865 (the 3rd year of King Gojong's reign), the academy was closed down by the Daewongun's order. The stone tablets of Yun Myeongjae and Yun Dongto were erected, and the spirit tablets were enshrined. In 1918, Kim Young-gwan, a surveyor, built a thatched house and settled a Chinese family named Wang there, but they eventually left. In 1924, Choi Dam, a geographer from Gangwon-do, and his brother-in-law Jang Byeong-ok moved to the area and built six houses, cultivating the wasteland that had been abandoned for over 400 years. The village gradually formed and was initially called Giryong-ri, but it was renamed Giryong (after Choi Damryong). Seven years later, father and son Park Yoon-bo and Park Gil-min moved in from Gayachon Village. In 1936, the administrative district was changed from Hari-myeon, Gimje-gun to Suryu-myeon (now Geumsan-myeon). In 1949, 18 households from the Dongdo Church (Samdeok Church) settled there, and by 1955, the total number of households reached 31, elevating the village to the status of a natural hamlet.

## 나. Location and Conditions

### <Location>

The village is located at the foot of Geumsan Mountain (478m above sea level), a famous mountain in Gimje, connected to Mobusan Mountain. It is 18km from Jeonju, 11km from Gimje, and 28km from Jeongeup.

### <Conditions>

At that time, the village was established on barren land covered with rocks and thorny bushes, making cultivation extremely difficult. The surrounding mountains were bare, and whenever it rained, the village suffered from floods and sandstorms, causing houses and fields to be buried. It was said that even goblins appeared in the village.

## 2. Village Development Process (發展過程)

### A. Situation Before 1970 (70年 以前 的 情 境)

#### 1) Basic Environment (基礎環境)
After carefully walking up the dusty, bus-filled road and the hillside, you would find thatched-roof houses (草屋) huddled together, their walls made of piled-up earth. Looking around the village, enclosed by haphazardly stacked stone walls, you would see large boulders scattered everywhere. The winding paths, like seaside mudflats crawling with clams, would confuse first-time visitors, making it difficult to find their way. Rags, torn pieces of cloth, and piles of straw here and there would wrinkle your nose. Livestock manure would overflow onto the streets, forcing you to cover your nose against the foul stench. Inside the houses, behind the main gate (大門), open-air toilets (便所) would emit a putrid smell amidst the buzzing of flies. The earthen walls, with holes where the mud had fallen away, were unpresentable. Blackened ceilings would have cobwebs swinging like swings, and collapsed stoves would have blackened iron pots hanging from broken holes.

#### Village Environment Before the 1970s (70年代 以前 的 村 落 環 境)

#### 2) Income Level (所得水準)
The village was situated on barren land (不毛地), surrounded by rocks and thorny bushes, making it infertile and useless. The villagers lived in poverty with few sources of income (所得源). They mainly made candy from taro harvested from their fields and sold it outside the village to earn money (收入) to make ends meet. Even then, when it rained, landslides (沙汰) would occur, and floods (洪水) would submerge the fields (田沓), destroying houses (家屋) and making life extremely difficult.


--- (p. 594) ---

## Living conditions

Residents who had struggled with poverty for years had extremely selfish living habits, were steeped in routine, and spent lazy, unproductive days. As the residents had originally migrated from other areas, there was little expectation of cooperation or unity among them, and they acted according to their own lifestyles and thoughts.

The dirty state of the houses darkened the residents' minds, fostering an atmosphere of mutual envy and hostility.

When the seasons changed, they would go to neighboring villages to work for wages to obtain food, or they would go up into the mountains to cut firewood and sell it at the market to buy food and clothing. As a result, they often skipped meals and had never properly worn a set of clothes.

In winter, they would crouch in the corner of the wall to make jokes, or gather at taverns to drink and sing, or fight among themselves. Young people born into impoverished families, unable to attend school or receive an education, would roam around playing pranks and harass passersby. In each household, marital disputes never ceased, and everyone sighed and sighed.

At one time, due to a flood causing a bad harvest, everyone was on the verge of starvation, but the government implemented public works programs to rescue the local residents.

How could these people have the will to live or hope for the future? They were poor residents who were only concerned with the present and looked forward to a bleak tomorrow.

## The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

### Motivation and results of the pilot project

#### <Motivation for development>—Establishment of the Giryong Village Improvement and Development Association

On April 7, 1966, a few young people in this village came together and named their group the Giryong Village Improvement and Development Association to promote mutual friendship and


--- (p. 595) ---

## Article on the Establishment of Giryeong Village Improvement and Development Association

A group was formed with a contractual format to plan (圖謀) for improvement. This group, with 5 initiators (發起人), established its member (會員) organization through a set of bylaws.

<Bylaws of Giryeong Village (起龍部落) Improvement and Development Association (向上發展會)>

## Chapter 1: General Provisions (總則)

### Article 1: The name of this association shall be Giryeong Village (起龍部落) Improvement and Development Association (向上發展會).

### Article 2: This association, with all members (會員) adhering to the principles of self-help (自助), self-reliance (自立), and service (奉仕), shall work together to carry out projects related to regional (地域) development. Through these efforts, the association aims to improve the overall economic (經濟), social (社會), and cultural (文化) lives of the villagers (部落民), contributing to the prosperity (富強) of the nation (國家) and the ethnic (民族的) development (發展).

### Article 3: Members (會員) of this association shall be residents of Giryeong Village (起龍部落).

## Chapter 2: Members (會員) and Organization (組織)

### Article 4: This association shall have regular members (正會員) and associate members (準會員).

Regular members (正會員) shall be granted membership upon receiving approval from a majority of more than two-thirds of the attending members (會員) at the general assembly (總會). Associate members (準會員) shall be residents of this village (本部落) other than regular members (正會員) who cooperate (協力) with village (部落) development (發展).

### Article 5: Regular members (正會員) shall have the right to vote (表決權), elect and be elected (選擧) for executive positions (任員), and actively (積極) participate (參與) in the operation (運營) of the association's projects (事業) and organizational structure (組織體).

### Article 6: Associate members (準會員) of this association shall have the same rights (權利) as regular members (正會員) except those specified in Article 5.

### Article 7: This association shall establish an advisory committee (諮問委員會) consisting of 5 or more advisory committee members (諮問委員) recommended by the chairperson (會長). The advisory committee members (諮問委員) shall act as the proxy agency (代行機關) for associate members (準會員).

### Article 8: This association shall have the following executives (任員):

1. Chairperson (會長) 1
2. General Affairs Director (總務) 1
3. Treasurer (財務) 1
4. Secretary (書記) 1
5. Business Manager (事業幹事) 1
6. Public Relations Officers (公報) 2

※ Advisory Committee (諮問委員會)
a. The chairperson (會長) shall represent the association (本會), manage its affairs (會務), and issue commands (命令) related to its operation (運營).
b. The General Affairs Director (總務) shall handle all internal affairs (內務) of the association (本會) as directed by the chairperson (會長) and shall be responsible for the custody (保管) of all documents (書類).
c. The Treasurer (財務) shall handle all financial (財政) matters (事務).
d. The Business Manager (事業幹事) shall research (硏究), plan (計劃), and establish (樹立) the operation (運營) of projects (事業).
e. The Secretary (書記) shall record (記錄) the minutes (會議錄) and be responsible for the custody (保管) of all other documents (書類).
f. The Public Relations Officers (公報) shall maintain close ties (紐帶) with the villagers (部落民), handle communication (通信) and contact (連絡) matters (事務), and engage in internal and external public relations activities (公報活動).

### Article 9: The chairperson (會長), General Affairs Director (總務), and Treasurer (財務) of this association shall be elected through a secret ballot (秘密投票) by plurality (得點者), while other executives (任員) shall be appointed by the chairperson (會長).

### Article 10: The term of office (任期) for the chairperson (會長) of this association shall be one year (一年). In case of a vacancy (闕位), a by-election (補選) shall be held at the regular meeting (定例會) with a majority of attending members (會員) to fill the remaining term (殘任期間).

### Article 11: In case of a vacancy (闕位) among the executives (任員) of this association, the chairperson (會長) shall appoint a successor (任命) with the consent (同意) of the executive board (任員會) to fill the remaining term (殘任期間).

### Article 12: All members (會員) of this association shall have the duty (義務) to sincerely (誠心誠意) cooperate (協力) for the betterment of the village (本部落).


--- (p. 596) ---

## Chapter 3 (第3章) Meetings (會議)

### Article 13 (第13條)
The Association shall have a Regular General Assembly (定期總會), Regular Meetings (定例會), and Executive Meetings (任員會).
① The Regular General Assembly (定期總會) shall be held annually on a specified date and shall amend the bylaws (會則), elect officers (任員), prepare budgets (豫算編成), decide on rewards and punishments (賞罰), and establish business plans (事業計劃).
② A Special General Assembly (臨時總會) shall be convened by the President (會長) or upon the request of 7 or more members (會員) when there are urgent matters concerning the Association (本會).
③ Regular Meetings (定例會) shall be held on the 15th and the last day of each month to plan and advance business operations (事業進行), education (敎育), and plans (計劃).

### Article 14 (第14條)
The chairperson (議長) of meetings (會議) of the Association (本會) shall be the President (會長), or a member (會員) designated by the President (會長) may act as the chairperson (議長).

## Chapter 4 (第4章) Finance (財政)

### Article 15 (第15條)
The finances (財政) of the Association (本會) shall be funded as follows:
① Membership fees (會費) ② Government subsidies (國家補助金) ③ Donations from villagers (部落民 喜捨金) ④ Business profits (事業收益) ⑤ Prize money (賞與金) ⑥ Others (其他)

### Article 16 (第16條)
The finances (財政) of the Association (本會) shall be divided into Village Common Fund (部落共同資金) and Operational Funds (運營費) of the Association (本會). The Village Common Fund (部落共同資金) and the Operational Funds (運營費) of the Association (本會) shall be used in accordance with the Regulations on the Management of Common Funds (共同資金管理細則).

### Article 17 (第17條)
The finances (財政) of the Association (本會) shall be managed by the Finance Department (財務), but shall be managed in accordance with the Regulations on the Management of Common Funds (共同資金管理細則) of the Association (本會).

### Article 18 (第18條)
All members (部落會員 全體) of the Association (本會) shall actively cooperate (積極 協助) in the management (管理), utilization (活用), and contribution (各出) of the Common Fund (共同資金) as their obligation (義務) as members (會員), as decided by the Regular Members (正會員) and the Advisory Committee (諮問委員會).

### Article 19 (第19條)
The financial principles (財政原則) of the Association (本會) shall be used for the benefit of the entire village (部落全體), but special privileges (特惠) shall be given to one member (會員) per contributing household (出資 戶口).

## Chapter 5 (第5章) Business (事業)

### Article 20 (第20條)
Decisions on business operations (事業運營) of the Association (本會) shall be made by a majority vote (過半數) of the Regular Members (正會員) present and a majority vote (過半數) of those present (出席會員).

### Article 21 (第21條)
The selection of business organization members (事業組織員) shall be made at the Executive Meeting (任員會) with a majority vote (過半數) of those present (出席) and a two-thirds majority vote (3分の 2) of those present (出席會員).

### Article 22 (第22條)
The organization members (組織員) of the Association (本會) shall be Regular Members (正會員), and business employees (事業雇傭人) shall be selected by the Association (本會).

### Article 23 (第23條)
The business funds (事業資金) from the Common Fund (共同資金) of the Association (本會) shall be used in accordance with the Regulations on the Management of Common Funds (共同資金管理細則) of the Association (本會).

### Article 24 (第24條)
The business operation guidance (事業運營指導) and auditing (監査) of the Association (本會) shall be conducted by the Association (本會), and detailed technical requirements (技術要件) shall be decided within the organization (組織體).

## Chapter 6 (第6章) Rewards and Punishments (賞罰)

### Article 25 (第25條)
Those who have made outstanding contributions (顯著 貢獻) to the operation (運營) of the Association (本會) and the development (事業發展) of the hometown (本故鄕) shall be decided before the Regular General Assembly (定期總會) and awarded at the Regular General Assembly (定期總會).

### Article 26 (第26條)
Those who have defamed (名譽毀損), disrupted public order (風紀紊亂), or engaged in destructive acts (破壞行爲) against the Association (本會) and the village (本部落) shall be expelled (除名) by a two-thirds majority vote (3分の 2) of the members (出席員) present.

### Article 27 (第27條)
Those who have lost their qualifications (資格喪失) under the penalty provisions (罰則 規定) of the Association (本會) or have moved out of the hometown (本故鄕 移住) shall bear the punishment (處罰) under these regulations (規定).

### Article 28 (第28條)
Those who have resigned (脫會) or been expelled (除名) from the Association (本會) shall not make any financial demands (財政的 要求) on the Association (本會).


--- (p. 597) ---

However, considering the person's activities, it is possible to pay the prescribed amount of money as decided by the meeting resolution.
Article 29 New members of this association shall pay the prescribed amount of membership fees at the regular general meeting, sign this constitution, swear to abide by the constitution as a member of this association, and pledge to exert their utmost efforts for the development of this village.

## Chapter 7 Supplementary Provisions
### Article 30 This association shall establish detailed regulations on finance, business, rewards and punishments, etc., within the scope of this constitution.
### Article 31 Amendments to this constitution shall be made by a resolution of two-thirds or more of the members present and voting at the regular general meeting, and shall come into effect three days after the announcement.
### Article 32 All matters not provided for in this constitution shall be governed by general norms.
### Article 33 This constitution shall come into effect from January 1, 1966.

The young people of the village, despite their poverty, were concerned about the improvement of village development and strove to prepare village funds. Even before such gatherings, they had been conducting a rice-saving movement, and at the time of the establishment of the association, they had accumulated 18 dou of fine rice. Not satisfied with this, the young people handed over the rice-saving movement to the women's association and devoted their total efforts to preparing village funds, collecting white rice from every household and lending it to villagers at low interest rates, thus increasing the funds. Through such lives, a sense of unity began to sprout among them. They used the funds to purchase farming tools to develop agriculture, and also directed the funds to improve cultural houses.

For the young people, 4-H clubs were formed to foster a sense of cooperation and savings. Gradually, men, women, and children of all ages contributed to the development of the village. On January 20, 1972, a historic event took place in Giryong Village. The neighboring Yongjeon-ri Yongban Village was carrying out a farm road construction project of 1,200 meters as part of the New Community Movement. However, the enthusiasm for the New Community Movement in Yongban Village waned, leading to the suspension of the project. At this time, the residents of Giryong Village, without anyone knowing who started it, suggested helping Yongban Village.

However, it was not the voice of one person. It was the united cry of the entire Giryong Village. On January 19, 1972, the residents of Giryong Village held a general meeting of all residents and unanimously decided to help Yongban Village.
On the morning of the 20th, the dark night air turned into the sound of a bell and pierced through the morning air. Soon, all the residents, as if they had been waiting, gathered in the dark square with shovels, hoes, stretchers, and carts. There were 27 stretchers, 12 carts, and a total of about 80 people. More residents than the total number of households (60) attended. This grand procession, carrying lunch boxes and shouldering shovels and hoes, set off for the farm road construction project in Yongban Village. They worked late into the night and achieved remarkable results. The residents of Yongban Village were surprised and ashamed. The next day, the residents of Yongban Village rose again and eventually completed the project.
However, the residents of Giryong used this as an opportunity to prove that the entire village had united with one mind and one heart at the same time as


--- (p. 598) ---

We also gained the confidence (自信感) that we can do anything if we try. With the support of the residents (住民), the five initiators (發起人) of the Uplift and Development Association (向上發展會) took the lead.

## <Pilot Project in the First Year>
- On April 22, 1970, the New Community Movement was initiated by President (大統領) Park Chung-hee, and at the same time, the New Community Project began in every corner of the country.
- The village of Kiryong received 400 bags of cement from the government in 1972 and started the New Community Project on December 10 of the same year.
- All residents, without exception, were mobilized using wheelbarrows, shoulder poles, and horse-drawn carts. They collected sand from a field 700 meters away, with the owner's permission, and piled it up like a mountain in the village square. They built a greenhouse in one corner of the square and produced blocks inside it.
- After completing all preparations, the residents first discussed and decided to secure a place to store materials.
- Village community center, village communal warehouse, communal toilet, access road, widening of the village inner road, improvement of fences, and rural electrification


--- (p. 600) ---

carried out various projects.
O By December 30, 1973, all initial projects were successfully completed.
<Achievements>
O Villages that completed such projects in a short time initially started as basic villages, skipped the self-help village stage, and suddenly advanced to self-sufficient villages.
O A 700-meter-wide open village entrance road was constructed to allow large trucks to enter freely, a 30-pyeong community center became a living room for all residents to relax after their hard work, and the village's communal warehouse allowed agricultural materials previously stored in cramped houses to be neatly organized.
O In particular, when the electrification project was completed, illuminating their previously dark lives, all residents cheered with joy.

2) Leader Selection and Obstacle Overcoming

a) Selection

O Every year at the beginning of the year, a regular general meeting was held, adopting the familiar democratic method, and from the nominated executives, a leader was chosen by a majority vote with more than two-thirds of the attending members present.

b) Leader Activity Situation

<Activities of Leader 오석일(吳錫一)>

He was a model farmer with 5,000 pyeong of rice fields and 6,000 pyeong of mulberry fields, supporting a family of 16. Having experienced poverty in 1965, he gathered several young men in the neighborhood to promote thrift through the rice-saving movement and, on April 1, 1966, organized the Kiryong Village Improvement Promotion Association, the predecessor of the Kiryong Village Credit Union. He devoted himself wholeheartedly to any matter related to the village's development.
O When he was appointed as the Saemaul leader in 1971, he felt the weight of responsibility on his shoulders. The Kiryong Improvement Promotion Association changed its name to the Village Credit Union, and the rice-saving movement was turned over to women's activities, giving birth to the Housing Construction Association.
O To boost the morale of the villagers, he spent two weeks compiling a systematic history of Kiryong Village, tracing its origins and development.


--- (p. 601) ---

During the implementation of the Saemaul Undong (事業), he, who was trusted by all residents (全住民) and held their respect (信望), exerted his utmost efforts (全力) to lead (指導) and advance (進行) the movement in response (報答) to their trust. Forgetting about his own family (家庭), he dedicated himself (熱中) solely to the Saemaul Undong and village affairs, which led to significant obstacles (支障) in silkworm farming (養蠶) and even caused him to ruin (那來) a year's worth of farming (農事).

### <Leader (指導者) Jang Gab-nak (張甲洛) and His Activities (活動)>
When Mr. O Seok-il (吳錫一) handed over his leadership due to poor health (虛弱), he vowed (盟誓) to dedicate himself (獻身) to village affairs (部落事) even more than his predecessor (前指導者). Working from early morning till late at night, there were times when he fell ill, and once, he suffered from continuous (連日) nosebleeds and groans, prompting the county magistrate (郡守) to visit with ginseng (人蔘) for his wife (婦人) to prepare as a remedy. His activities (活動) later became a model (鏡) for all residents (全住民), and he even received presidential (大統領) gifts (下賜金) three times, contributing greatly (至大) to the village's development (部落發展).

### 3) Overcoming Challenges (隘路克服) Situations (狀況)
- The stubbornness (固執) of landowners (土地所有者) who refused to donate (喜捨) their inherited (先親) land (土地) for widening (寬) the village entrance (進人路) and inner roads (安路), leading to the Saemaul Undong being halted (中斷) and the Saemaul promotion committee (推進委員) persuading (說得) and appealing (呼訴) them morning and evening.
- During the Saemaul Undong promotion (推進), the lack of funds (基金不足) led to committee members (推進委員) visiting (訪問) each household (家家戶戶) with frozen hands (꽁꽁 언 손) to collect (醵出) donations.
- When the opinions (意見) of residents (住民) divided (分分) along their 27 different surnames (姓氏), leaders (指導者) stayed up all night (夜眠不成) to mediate (調停) and guide (引導) them towards a common goal (總和).

### 4) Developmental Promotion (發展的推進) of the Saemaul Undong (事業)
- With the initial (初期) success of the Saemaul Undong (事業), the morale (意慾) of all villagers (全體住民) seemed boundless (無際).
- That year, a national flagpole (國旗揭揚臺) was erected (揭揚) for every household (全戶數).
- With Mrs. Jeon Yeon-ok (田蓮玉) as the leader (中心), a large-scale (大大的) roof improvement (改良) project (事業) was carried out (實施) for all households (全體家口), making the village a pioneer (先進) in roof improvement (改良) compared to neighboring villages (比村).
- A simple water supply facility (簡易上水道施設) was completed (完成) for all 55 households (戶), and home improvement (家庭改良) projects (事業) were implemented (實施) to promote hygienic living (衛生生活) and advanced cultural life (文化生活), including kitchen (廚房), toilet (便所), and livestock shed (畜舍) improvements (改良).
- Once the environmental infrastructure project (環境基盤事業) was nearly completed (完), an income-increasing project (所得增大事業) was initiated (實施). In 1973, with a presidential gift (下賜金) of 2 million won (萬), a communal farm (共同農場) was purchased (購入), sericulture (養蠶) was practiced, and a nursery (養苗場) was established (設置) and maintained (養).
- In 1976, with a presidential gift (下賜金) of 1.5 million won (萬), a communal livestock barn (共同畜舍) was built (建立), and poultry (養鷄), pig farming (養豚), Hanwoo (韓牛) cattle, and fattening cattle (肥育牛) were introduced (入殖) to further boost (拍車) income (所得).

## 6) Heartwarming Stories
### a) First Story

In the winter of 1973, during the initial phase of constructing the village community center, about 60 residents gathered at night, holding torches, and started digging the ground for earthwork. During the process, the current village head, Kim Jin-sul, and resident Park Jong-hui, who were working together, were injured on their waists and legs when a hillside collapsed, causing great confusion. All the residents were in tears, carrying the injured on their backs towards the hospital. At that moment, the county magistrate at the time, Moon Pil-byeong, who had heard the news of the night work, came to the village to encourage the residents. He immediately turned his car around and admitted the injured to the hospital, and the medical expenses were paid by the county magistrate. Heaven (天)


--- (p. 604) ---

It must have been the work of divine assistance.

## B) The Second Story

In 1977, the leader, who had endured countless hardships and trials, neglected household chores to serve the village, even to the point of nosebleeds and several instances of falling ill. In gratitude, the county magistrate visited with a gift of ginseng to console him. All the residents, in high spirits, withdrew 140,000 won from the village fund to purchase a calf as a token of their thanks. Amidst the residents' joy, hot tears of pride flowed as they received the gift, each reminiscing about the fruits of their labor with heartfelt emotions.

## 7) Visits by Dignitaries

On August 8, 1975, the Prime Minister, accompanied by the Minister of Home Affairs, the provincial governor, and the chief of police, inspected the village's remarkable transformation through the Saemaul Undong. He listened to reports on the current situation and praised the residents' efforts, offering words of encouragement. Along the way, he also donated 200,000 won for the Saemaul Undong fund and 700 bags of cement to the village.

## 8) Special Incidents

### A) Joyful Events

As part of the rural electrification project, the village celebrated the completion of the installed lights and the simple water supply system. Through the village's amplifier, everyone turned on the lights and water faucets together. The residents cheered and danced throughout the night.

### B) Sad Events

As part of the Forestry Agency's experimental project, 20 hectares of Orchard Grass (牧草) was established on the hill behind the village, achieving successful results. However, due to a lack of funds at the time, the village was unable to purchase Hanwoo (韓牛) cattle, resulting in the grass being used as firewood and fertilizer, ultimately leading to its natural death the following year.


--- (p. 605) ---

### Ba. Achievements (成果) from the Saemaul Undong (事業)

In 1975, this village was designated as a promotional village (弘報마을) for the county (郡) and has been transforming its appearance (面貌) every year. In 1977, 54 households (世帶) utilized tile roofs (타이루) to renovate their kitchens (部엌 개량), among other (等) housing environment improvement (住宅 環境 개선事業) projects.

#### O Housing (住宅) Improvement (가꾸기) Projects (事業)

| Project (事業) Name (名) | Plan (計劃) | Performance (實績) | Remarks (備考)                  |
| :--------------- | :--------- | :--------- | :-------------------------- |
| Roof (地붕) Improvement (改良)  | 57 units       | 104 units      | Includes (包含) ancillary (附屬) buildings (建物) and livestock (畜舍) sheds |
| Wall (담장) Improvement (改良)  | 3,600m     | 3,600m     | Built (이조式) style (式) stone walls (돌담) with tiles (기와) |
| Temporary (簡易) Water Supply (給水) | 57 units       | 57 units       |                             |
| Kitchen (部엌) Improvement (改良)  | 57〃       | 54〃       |                             |
| Toilet (便所)       | 57〃       | 27〃       |                             |
| Livestock (畜舍) Shed       | 10〃       | 10〃       |                             |

Since the inception (始作) of the Saemaul Undong (事業), the residents of Giryong (起龍) village have risen from a low-income (低所得) community of 20-30万원 to a high-income (高所得) village of 150万원. They vow to create a terrestrial (地上) paradise (樂園) by equipping themselves with various (各種) cultural (文化) facilities (施設). With confidence (自信), they declare that by the 1980s (年代), each household (戶當) will achieve an income (所得) of 300万원. Additionally, they have organized (組織) village-level (單位) self-defense (自衛) Saemaul Undong (事業) units to prepare for potential (有事時) defense (防護) systems (體制).

#### 1) Spiritual (精神) Aspect (面)
*   The spirit (精神) of mutual aid (隣保相助) is embodied, where residents eagerly volunteer (發 벗고 나서는) to help the village (마을을 위하고) and care for their neighbors (이웃을 보살필 일이면).
*   There is an overwhelming (꽉 차 있다) sense of confidence (自信感) that anything can be accomplished (무엇이든지 하면 된다는).
*   A strong (깊어지다) sense of cooperation (協同) and unity (團結) has taken root (깊어지다), fostering the belief that no task is insurmountable (힘을 합하면 안 되는 일이 없다는).

#### 2) Lifestyle (生活) Aspect (面)
*   Residents have transitioned from a life of rags (누더기) and hunger (굶기) to a more prosperous (潤澤) existence (生活), where they support (도우며) one another (이웃을).
*   Houses (住宅), once indistinguishable (분간할 수 없었다) between livestock (畜舍) sheds and kitchens (部엌), have been modernized (現代式) with tile roofs (타이루) and renovated (단장), enabling a more cultured (文化) rural (農村) lifestyle (生活).


--- (p. 607) ---

O They are living a hygienic life (生活) through simple water supply and toilet improvement.
O With increasing income (所得), cultural facilities (文化施設) such as TVs and refrigerators are continuously growing.
3) Income Aspect (所得面)
O The per-household income, which used to be around 100,000 to 200,000 won (萬원), now exceeds 2,000,000 won (萬원).
O With the increase in livestock (家畜), nursery business (養苗事業), and tobacco cultivation (葉煙草栽培), the initial cultivated area (耕地面積) of 39ha has increased to 51ha. The profit (利益金) from the operation (經營) of the village's collective farm (共同農場) and the purchasing and selling business (購販場事業) by women has significantly increased, now reaching 12,000,000 won (千원).
O Through the rice-saving movement (節米運動) and scrap collection (廢品蒐集), the women's association (婦女會) is utilizing 40 sacks (石) of white rice (白米) as a fund (基金).

## 3. Residents' General Assembly (住民總會)

### ◆ Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (1)

*   Date (日時) : June 15, 1973, 9 AM
*   Location (場所) : Village Community Center Meeting Room
*   Agenda (議題) : Promotion of Income-Generating Businesses
*   Attendees (參席人員) : 31 people

Park Gui-Geum, Jeong Nam-Suk, Oh Seok-Gu, Jo Seok-Il, Park Jong-Seop, Kim Jin-Sul, Oh Seok-Young, Lee Song-Jae, Jeong Gyu-Sam, Heung Won-Seon, Park Jong-Seok
Lee Jab-Dol, Lee Jong-Jeol, Jo Man-Jae, Choi Hyun-Gyeon, Park Hong-Gi, Ju Chang-Hyeon, Oh Young-Taek, Yu Beon-Deok, Park Yeon-Jang, Hong Oe-Bok, Jang Jeung-Won
Jo Dong-Uk, Kim Un-Young, Kwon Sang-Bong, Lee Sang-Do, Bong Dong-Chan, Yoon Si-Jung, Choi Chul-Gil, Seo Gil-Yeon, Oh Yun-Taek,
Chairperson (議長) (Village Head (里長)) : With the government's support of 1,100,000 won (萬원), we will proceed with the business according to the resolution (決議) of our residents.


--- (p. 608) ---

Please decide on this matter tonight.
**Jeong Nam-sook (Agreeing):** As this is a livelihood-improvement project, the project content must be thorough and solid, and it should benefit all residents. Therefore, I propose that we improve the central stream, which is the lifeline of our village.

**Choi Hyeon-gyeon (Supporting Statement):** I would like to further explain Jeong Nam-sook's statement. The upper part of the central stream is a communal laundry area, and there is also a well. Residents use the stream water frequently, and it is also used for irrigation. Therefore, this project will have multiple benefits for livelihood improvement, and I support it.

**Chairperson:** Do you agree?
**Residents:** We agree.
**Chairperson:** Are there any objections?
**Kim Jin-sook (Objecting):** I propose that, as our village has been called the "top of the mung bean field" since ancient times, we use the project funds to build an irrigation channel. I suggest that the irrigation channel should follow the path leading up to Giryeong Village.

**Chairperson:** Do you agree?
**Residents:** We agree.
**Chairperson:** Are there any more statements?
**Residents:** None.
**Chairperson:** We will now proceed to a vote. (Show of hands)
*   Agree: 21 households
*   Object: 10 households
**Chairperson:** The agreement has been passed with the support of the majority of the 31 attendees.
**Residents:** May we have the floor?
**Chairperson:** Proceed.
**Choi Hyeon-gyeon:** This is not a small project, and under the mission of being a livelihood-improvement project, not all residents can participate in its execution. Therefore, let us form a committee of several members to carry out this project.

**Chairperson:** Do you agree with Choi Hyeon-gyeon's proposal?
**Residents:** We strongly agree.
**Chairperson:** Please recommend members for the committee.
**Committee Recommendation (Village Head: Jang Gap-rak):** Oh Seok-il, Jeong Nam-sook, Lee Song-jae, Yu Byeong-deok, Park Gwi-nam, Kim Jin-sul, Choi Hyeon-gyeon

**Residents:** May we have the floor?
**Chairperson:** Proceed.
**Jeon Gyu-deok:** Now that the committee has been appointed, let us not discuss this matter further and entrust it to the committee members.


--- (p. 609) ---

### Minutes (會議錄) (2)

Date(日時): September 25, 1973
Location(場所): Giryong Hall (起龍會館)
Agenda(議題): Ceremony for the President (大統領) Donation and Approval of Business Plan (事業計劃)
Attendees(參席人員): 51 people
Guests(臨席官): Kim Je County Magistrate (金堤郡守), Saemaul Chief (係長), Geumsan Myeon Chief (金山面長)

Chairperson (鄭圭得): We will now begin the ceremony for the President (大統領) Donation and the meeting for the establishment and approval of the business plan, with the honorable County Magistrate in attendance.

Village Chief (里長): It is an immense honor to have the County Magistrate, Myeon Chief, and all residents gathered here today for the ceremony to receive the President (大統領) Donation of 2,000,000 won. To our residents who have long suffered from poverty, I say that under the banner of Yusin (維新), let us unite as one and dedicate ourselves to the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) to build a prosperous future. This is our opportunity to create a great legacy for future generations. I urge everyone to work together diligently and frugally, leaving no one behind, and give your all to the upcoming projects.

Chairperson: Next, we will have the County Magistrate deliver the President (大統領) Donation and a message of encouragement.

County Magistrate (郡守): It is with great humility that I stand before you all as the County Magistrate. I believe that the President (大統領) has taken notice of your hard work and has bestowed this great honor upon you to help you achieve even greater results. However, the President (大統領) always emphasizes that the path to prosperity lies in national unity and the Saemaul Undong (新村運動). This substantial donation is given to those who strive to build up our humble hometowns. I hope that you will use this noble gift to achieve even greater and more valuable endeavors.

(County Magistrate (郡守) presents the donation to Village Chief (里長) 장갑락. Loud applause and cheers erupt from the attendees.)

Chairperson: With that, we conclude the President (大統領) Donation ceremony and will now begin the meeting for the establishment and approval of the business plan.

Village Chief (里長): The business funds will consist of the President (大統領) Donation of 2,000,000 won, 238,000 won from the reinvestment fund of the small stream improvement project (小河川整備事業) implemented in August 1973, and 1,262,000 won from the village self-fund, totaling 3,500,000 won. Please propose business plans that can generate high income through collective work. We will then vote on the combined proposals.

鄭圭三: I propose a poultry farming business (養鷄事業).

李松宰: I propose a grain processing business (糧穀加工事業).

權明基: I propose a feed mill (飼料工場).

吳錫一: I propose purchasing a communal farm "High-Income Mulberry Field Development (桑田造成)."


--- (p. 610) ---

Lee Sun-gyu (李舜圭): I would like to propose a project to develop a reservoir (貯水池) and transform rain-fed fields (天水沓) into irrigated fields (水利安全沓).
Oh Seong-taek (吳盛澤): I would like to propose a project to establish a livestock (肥育牛) complex (團地).
Village Head (里長): Besides the proposal by Jeong Gyeong-sam (鄭圭三) and five others, are there any other good projects you would like to suggest?
Village Residents: None.
Village Head (里長): Then, we will vote on the six proposals. The proposal with more than half of the votes from the attendees will be adopted.
(The chairperson (司會者) writes the six proposals on the blackboard (黑板) and decides by a majority vote (擧手 다수).)
Please raise your hand if you agree with the sixth proposal by Oh Seong-taek (吳盛澤). 6 votes.
Please raise your hand if you agree with the fifth proposal by Lee Sun-gyu (李舜圭). 3 votes.
Please raise your hand if you agree with the fourth proposal by Oh Hak-il (吳學一). 28 votes.
Please raise your hand if you agree with the third proposal by Gwon Myeong-gi (權明基). 2 votes.
Please raise your hand if you agree with the second proposal by Lee Song-jae (李松宰) for grain (糧穀) processing. 3 votes.
Please raise your hand if you agree with the first proposal by Jeong Gyeong-sam (鄭圭三) for poultry farming (養鷄). 9 votes.
Village Head (里長): Then, the proposal by Oh Hak-il (吳學一) for the joint purchase of a farm (共同農場購入) has received more than half of the votes with 28 votes and has been adopted. Farmers are the foundation of the world (農者天下大本), so the joint purchase of a farm has great significance. Now, let's hear the specific plan (具體計劃) for the farm purchase from Oh Seok-il (吳錫一).
Oh Hak-il (吳學一): I proposed the joint purchase of a farm (共同農場購入) with the village community center (會館) as the starting point, aiming to completely purchase farms within a 1km radius in 10 to 20 years. Using scientific farming methods (科學營農方法), we will increase income and use the funds to support students' tuition (學費支援), build a nursing home (養老堂) for seniors over 70, operate a kindergarten, achieve self-sufficiency in residents' food (食生活自給自足), and save the surplus funds to build "Saemaul-style (新村型) apartments (아파트建立)." Residents, let's unite and strive towards this goal. First, I think we should elect a farm purchase committee (農場購入委員會).
Village Head (里長): I have heard Oh Seok-il's (吳錫一) vision for the farm purchase. If there are no objections or other proposals regarding the election of the farm purchase committee (農場購入委員會選任), please speak up.
Village Residents: There are no objections to Oh Seok-il's (吳錫一) proposal.
Chairperson (議長): Oh Seok-il's (吳錫一) proposal has been adopted. How should we elect the committee chairperson (委員長) and members (委員)?
Jeong Nam-suk (丁南叔): It would be best to nominate someone with internal and external prestige (德望) and put it to a vote (表決).
Kim Jin-sul (金鎭述): I will nominate someone.
Village Head (里長) suggests appointing Jang Gap-rak (張甲洛), Jeong Nam-suk (丁南叔), Park Gwi-nam (朴貴男), Oh Seok-il (吳錫一), Lee Song-je (李松帝), Oh Seok-yeong (吳錫永), and Seo Byeong-gu (徐丙玖) as committee members (委員選任).
Village Head (里長): Are there any other committee members or proposals? Please speak up.
Village Residents: None. The nominees by Kim Jin-sul (金鎭述) are the best, and there are no objections.
Jeong Gyeong-deuk (鄭圭得): Among the nominated committee members (委員互薦), we need one committee chairperson (委員長). I nominate Seo Byeong-gu (徐丙玖) as the committee chairperson (委員長互薦).
Chairperson (議長): The committee members (委員) nominated by Kim Jin-sul (金鎭述) have been appointed with absolute support (絕對支持) from all residents (住民一同).


--- (p. 611) ---

Mr. Jeong Guk-deok (鄭圭得) nominated Mr. Seo Nae-gu (徐乃玖) as the chairman. Are there any objections?
All residents (一同): We agree.

Chairman (議長): The newly appointed chairman, Mr. Seo Byeong-gu (徐丙玖), will give his remarks.
Chairman (委員長) (Seo Byeong-gu (徐丙玖)): I am at a loss for words that you have entrusted this important task to someone as incapable as me. With the 2 million won granted by Your Excellency and the blood, sweat, and tears we have poured into our village self-funding (部落自體資金) (funded by the rice-saving movement (節米運動), 120 dou (斗) of white rice (白米), and 238,000 won from the small stream improvement project (小河川整備事業), totaling 3.5 million won), I pledge, together with all the committee members (委員), to devote all our efforts to purchase the farmland around the designated community center (會館) as fairly as possible. This is my remark. (All residents (全住民) applaud.)
Host (司會者): Thank you very much. This concludes the ceremony for the delivery of the President (大統領) His Excellency's (閣下) grant (下賜金) and the business plan (事業計劃).
Seo Byeong-gu, Cho Man-jae, Jang Gab-rap, Yu Byeong-deok, Jeong Guk-deok, Jeon Jae-hak, Kim Jin-sul, Oh Seok-jung, Jeong Guk-sam, Lee Gap-dol, Park Gwi-nam, Jang Dong-woo, Jeong Nam-suk, Bong Dong-chan, Oh Seok-gu, Seo Jeong-dong, Oh Seok-young, Yoon Si-jung, Oh Seok-il, Heo Jae-seop, Oh Seong-taek, Cho Dong-wook, Kim Young-dae, Lee Sang-do, Hong Won-seon, Ju Chang-hyeon, Heung Oe-bok, Cho Chang-su, Park Gil-min, Choi Yu-gil, Lee Jong-geol, Im Hyeong-jae, Lee Gyu-hee, Jang Dong-woo, Choi Cheol-gil, Go Hang-gon, Kwon Sang-bong,

### Minutes of the Meeting (會議錄) (3)

Date (日時): September 25, 1973, 8 PM
Location (場所): Giryong Village Community Center
Meeting Contents (會議內容): Settlement of government-supported 1.1 million won small stream income business and small stream business
Attendees (參席人員): 40 people
Host (司會者): Village head

Chairman (議長) (Village head (里長)): I will report on the settlement of the 1.1 million won small stream income business.

| | Item | Quantity/Unit | Amount (won) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. | Crushed stone | 5,752 pieces | 396,438 won |
| 2. | Gravel | 152.4 m³ | 153,398 won |
| 3. | Limestone quarrying fee | 120 m³ | 73,080 won |
| 4. | Wages | 723 | 239,084 won |
| 5. | Small stream fund | | 238,000 won |
| Total | | | 1,100,000 won |

Currently, as shown above, the 1.1 million won has been fully expended and the project has been completed.
Moreover, I would like to clearly state that the seven appointed committee members (委員) faced many difficulties and worked day and night to complete the project. I, the village head, would like to commend their efforts. Next, regarding the wages, we have set aside 50% for the small stream fund. I would like to hear your opinions on this.
Resident Oh Yoon-taek: I agree to buy and raise cattle with the small stream fund.
Chairman (議長): Are there any objections?
Residents (住民): There are objections.


--- (p. 612) ---

Chairperson: Shall we begin the meeting?
Lee Jong-geol: With this fund, I would like to purchase a farm (農場)(land (土地)). Raising cattle (農牛) is inconvenient in many ways and as they are movable property (動産), they cannot be guaranteed (保障) for future generations (後代). However, purchasing land (土地) does not easily become liquid (流動) and it is possible to generate income (所得) from the land (土地) to carry out (再復車) business (事業). I submit this proposal (案件).

Chairperson: Is there any agreement (同意)?
Resident: I agree (贊成).
Chairperson: We will proceed to a vote (表決). The voting (表決) method (方法) will be by show of hands (擧手) as per precedent (前例).
Oh Yun-taek: 11 people
Lee Jong-geol: 21 people
The motion (開議) is passed (可決) with more than a majority (過半數) in favor (贊同).
Chairperson: Then, we will conclude today's settlement (決算) general meeting (總會) for the business (事業) of restoring (復車). If there are any objections (異議), please speak up.
Resident: None.
Chairperson: Adjournment (閉會).

**Attendees**

♦ Minutes (會議錄) (4)

*   **Date (日時)**: November 1, 1973 (年月日)
*   **Location (場所)**: Village (部落) Hall (會館)
*   **Agenda (會議案件)**: Purchase of land (土地) for a joint farm (共同農場)
*   **Scope of attendance (參席範圍)**: Committee (委員) for land (農地) purchase (7명)

Chairperson (議長) Personnel (人事): I will now explain the matters (事項) regarding the promotion (推進) of farm (農場) land (土地) purchase (買入).
After repeated negotiations (累次 節衝) with the committee (委員) members and land (土地) owners (所有者), we have agreed (合議) on a price (時價) of 1,000 won (圓) per pyeong (坪當) for the land (土地) with ownership rights (所有權), and 600 won (圓) per pyeong (坪當) for the riverbed land (河川敷地) due to ownership rights (所有權) issues (關係). Please express (發意) your opinions (意見), committee (委員) members.

Jang Gap-rak (張甲洛): I think (可) it is reasonable (可) to set the price (當) at 1,000 won (圓) per pyeong (坪當) for land (土地) with ownership rights (所有權), and 600 won (圓) per pyeong (坪當) for riverbed land (河川敷地).

Chairperson (議長): Are there any objections (異議) to the proposal (發意) by committee (委員) member Jang Gap-rak (張甲洛)?
Committee (委員) member: All 6 other attending (參席) committee (委員) members agree (贊同) without objection (異議).

Chairperson (議長): It has been agreed (合議) that the above-ground objects (地上物), specifically mulberry trees (桑木), should be valued (可當) at 200 won (圓) per tree (株). Please express (表) your opinions (意思), committee (委員) members.


--- (p. 613) ---

Committee Member (Jeong Nam-sook): If we calculate the annual income per mulberry tree, I believe it is possible to achieve 200 won per tree.
Chairperson: Committee Member Jeong Nam-sook mentioned that 200 won per mulberry tree is possible. What are your opinions on this?
Committee Member: Committee Members Park Gui-nam and 6 others fully agree with the opinion of Committee Member Jeong Nam-sook.
Chairperson: The total area of the collective farmland is 3,500 pyeong, and the total purchase price is 3,500,000 won. Among this amount, 371,600 won is included for the purchase of 1,858 mulberry trees. Please take note of this. Furthermore, the details of the land purchase are as stated in the separate deed of sale. I would like to express my gratitude for the efforts of the committee members. I hope you will exert your best efforts to achieve the expected results in the future. With that, I will conclude this meeting. Thank you very much.
November 1, 1973

Chairperson: Seo Byeong-gu
Committee Members: Jang Gab-rak, Oh Seok-il, Oh Seok-young, Park Gui-nam, Lee Song-jae, Jeong Nam-sook

## Minutes of the Meeting (5)

Location: Community Center of This Tribe
Date: November 10, 1973
Attendees: All Residents of This Tribe

Host (Kim Jin-sul): We will now hold a meeting to report on the progress of purchasing collective farmland using the President's donation of 2,000,000 won and the residents' contribution of 150,000 won.
Village Head: Respected residents, how much have you all struggled for the Saemaul Undong? Thank you for attending this meeting for all residents. I will now report on the process of purchasing the collective farmland.
Before I begin, I would like to express my gratitude for your tireless efforts for the Saemaul Undong. Thanks to your hard work, our esteemed President Park has donated a large sum of 2,000,000 won, which has become a resource for our tribe that could not escape poverty. When I think about the purchase of 3,500 pyeong of land with this money, I join the residents present here in expressing my sincere gratitude to the President. (Applause like thunder) I ask that we repay this kindness by cooperating with the national policy. (Applause again) Thank you.
Now, I will mention the details of the collective farmland purchase. Initially, the President's donation of 2,000,000 won and the residents' contribution of 150,000 won were combined to form a total fund of 350,000 won. With this, we have completed the purchase of 2,571 pyeong of rice fields (current market value: 2,511,100 won), 929 pyeong of riverbed land (current market value: 557,400 won), and 1,818 mulberry trees (current market value: 371,800 won). At this moment, I would like to make a promise to the residents that we will exert several times more cooperative spirit and devote ourselves to increasing income, making it a glorious business for our descendants for generations to come. I would also like to express my gratitude to the land purchase committee members elected by you all.
With that, I will conclude this meeting.


--- (p. 614) ---

## Minutes of the Meeting (6)

*   **Date**: November 10, 1973
*   **Location**: Main Office Village Community Center
*   **Agenda**: Telecommunication (電化) Business in the Village
*   **Attendance Scope**: All residents of the Main Office Village

**Chairperson (金鎭述)**: We will now begin the meeting to discuss the promotion of the telecommunication business in the Main Office Village.

**Village Head Inspection**: Thank you all for attending despite your busy schedules. We are very grateful. One of our long-cherished projects, the telecommunication business, is now being promoted with the support of the current government and Korea Electric Power Corporation. We consider this an infinite honor for the residents. Now, we would like to hear your opinions on promoting this business and selecting the executives at the same time.

**Lee Song-jae (李松宰)**: To promote such a large business, I think it would be good to organize a promotion committee to carry out the business.

**Village Head**: As Lee Song-jae just mentioned, it is a good idea to organize a promotion committee for the telecommunication business. What do the residents think? Those who agree, please speak up.

**Park Gwi-nam (朴貴男)**: I agree. To hear everyone's opinions, I think it would be good to decide by a show of hands.

**Village Head**: To decide on the pros and cons of the above, we will decide by a show of hands whether it is good to organize a committee. Those who think it is good to organize a committee, please raise your hands.

**Chairperson**: Counting the number of people who raised their hands, everyone raised their hands. (Number of people who raised their hands: 51)

**Village Head**: Then, we will now begin the selection of executives. We will select 1 chairperson, 5 committee members, 1 treasurer, and 2 auditors. Please let us know the selection method.

**Oh Seok-gu (吳錫九)**: I think it would be good to select suitable candidates by oral nomination. (All attendees agree)

**Village Head**: We will first select the promotion committee chairperson. Please nominate someone suitable.

**Lee Jong-geol (李鍾杰)**: I think Jeong Nam-suk (丁南淑) is suitable for the chairperson. (Everyone agrees unanimously)

**Village Head**: Jeong Nam-suk (丁南淑) has been selected as the chairperson, and we will now select 1 treasurer.

**Yun Si-jung (尹時中)**: Yu Gyeong-deok (柳京德) has been selected as the treasurer. (Selected in the same manner as above)


--- (p. 615) ---

# Head of Village (里長)

The following committee members were elected by majority vote: Park Gui-nam (朴貴男), Oh Seok-gu (吳錫九), Lee Song-jae (李松宰), Lee Jong-geol (李鍾杰), and Kim Jin-sul (金鎭述). Additionally, Choi Hyun-gyun (崔鉉均) and Park Gil-min (朴吉汶) were elected as auditors according to your wishes. Thank you for your time. Now, the chairperson of the promotion committee will present the business promotion plan and budget.

# Chairperson (委員長)

Although I am not confident in my abilities as the chairperson, I will do my best to promote this enormous project with your absolute cooperation. Please help decide on the business promotion plan and budget by negotiating and compromising on any issues. After negotiating with the electric company, even at the lowest possible level, we will need 6,000 won per household for internal wiring costs and provide meals for 5 electricians. Therefore, we will need a budget of 7,000 won per household for this project. Additionally, one laborer per household will need to be dispatched for the installation of utility poles. Please decide on this matter under the agreement of the residents.

# Oh Seok-il (吳錫一)

As the chairperson mentioned, I believe that the construction budget and labor dispatch will be necessary. However, please express your opinions. All residents agreed with Oh Seok-il's opinion and made the decision. We hope for your active cooperation. Today's meeting regarding the electrification project is now adjourned.

We express our heartfelt gratitude.

## Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (7)—Giryeong Village 1st Executive Meeting Resolution
Date (日時): October 25, 1974
Attendees (參席對象): All Executives (全任員)
Number of Attendees (參席人員): 10 (8 male, 2 female)
Agenda (會議案件): Discussion on the Promotion Plan for the Special Support Project (閣下特別支援事業推進方案會議)

### Speaker (發言者) (Oh Seok-il)
We plan to start this project on November 1st. First, we need funds for this project, so we will secure 500,000 won from the National Agricultural Cooperative Federation (農協) for material purchase costs. We will cover 200,000 won through resident contributions, which will be supported through efforts. Additionally, 20% of the wages will be used to purchase sheep for the village improvement project, which we will raise annually.

### Speaker (發言者) (Lee Song-jae)
I agree with Mr. Oh Seok-il's proposal.
Unanimous approval (滿場一致贊成)

# Jeonnam (Jeollanam-do) Seungju-gun (Seungju County) Seomyeon (Seomyeon) Geumpyeong (Geumpyeong) Village

## 1. Overview of the Village

### Ga. History

*   During the Imjin War (1592-1598), this area was temporarily used as a training ground. The village courtyard was trampled by troops, making it difficult for crops to grow, so it was left as wasteland. Over time, a settlement formed, and 12 households established the village. During the Joseon Dynasty, under King Seonjo's reign, the village was named Heukseok (Black Stone) because of the black stone in front of the village.
*   In 1935, the village was renamed Geumpyeong (Geumpyeong) because the mountain behind the village resembled a zither. In 1940, it was renamed again to Geumpyeong (Geumpyeong), which it is called today.

### Na. Location and Conditions

**<Location>**
The village is located 80 km southeast of Gwangju and 7 km northeast of Suncheon. It is adjacent to the Suncheon Interchange on the Namhae Expressway.

**<Conditions>**
This mid-mountain village is situated along the Suncheon East River. It is surrounded by mountains on both sides and has extensive riverbanks. In the past, it was a small agricultural village with sandy soil, but now it is gaining recognition as a suitable area for advanced horticulture.

## 2. Village Development Process

### 가. Situation Before 1970

#### 1) Basic Environment

* The village access road was so narrow that it was impossible to avoid the side paths, and it was always muddy due to overflowing water in the rice fields.
* The inner village roads were so narrow that carrying a load on a pole would get caught on the fences, making it difficult to pass.
* Houses were extremely dilapidated, with thatched roofs sunken in and overgrown with weeds, and most were earthen houses without verandas.
* Moreover, the river embankments were not properly constructed, so whenever heavy rain fell, they would overflow and sweep away the farmland.

#### 2) Income Level

* The village had been cultivating rice and wheat on about 40 hectares of farmland inherited from ancestors,
* With an average of 0.4 hectares of farmland per household, the village could not escape poverty, with an average annual income of 190,000 won.


--- (p. 622) ---

The main source of income was rice farming and selling baskets to neighboring villages to barely make ends meet.
