## 3) Living Conditions Before the 1970s

### a) Consciousness Structure
The villagers were lazy and lacked understanding and cooperation. They would gather to drink and gamble, squandering their meager assets, making it a degenerate and backward village.

### b) Cultural Life and Daily Living
The village barely made a living through day labor and selling large baskets. Neighboring villages even hesitated to arrange marriages with this impoverished village. During the Japanese colonial period, about one-third of the village women had to beg for food. During the Korean War, the village relied on government relief rice. Without electricity, villagers read under the dim light of oil lamps, with only worn-out radios as their news source. Their homes were papered with fertilizer sacks or newspapers, with no ceilings, living like moles. The outhouses were exposed, infested with maggots, and indistinguishable from manure pits, reflecting their unsanitary living conditions.

## b. Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

### 1) Motivation and Results of Pilot Projects
In a village notorious for its extreme poverty and lack of cooperation among its ignorant residents, a few determined individuals gathered to discuss either breaking free from this poverty or moving elsewhere.


--- (p. 623) ---

Worried about the two-sided argument,

O On April 22, 1970, coinciding with President (大統領) Mr. Park Chung-hee's proclamation of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동), we decided to join forces, foster a spirit of cooperation, and nurture the dream of building a welfare-oriented rural community. To this end, we held a residents' general assembly (住民總會).
O On October 20, 1970, as a result of the residents' general assembly (住民總會), we resolved to undertake the first project (第1次 事業) of opening a 520-meter access road to the village.
O On November 15, 1970, we held another residents' general assembly (住民總會) regarding the opening of farm roads (農路) and resolved to create regulations for resident cooperation (住民協同), including donations of land for road inclusion, joint work, and other resident regulations (住民規約), and to start the project.
O However, although we had resolved to do so, we faced difficulties in pushing forward with the project (事業) as there was no village fund (마을基金) and the issue was directly tied to the residents' (住民) interests (利害).
O By January 10, 1971, we completed the extension of 520 meters (width 5m) from the county road (地方道) to the village entrance (入口).
O Now that the previously muddy path had become a road wide enough for cars to enter, the village residents (住民) gained new motivation, and the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) based on resident cooperation (住民協同) began to take off. In this sense, the opened village access road served as a catalyst for changing the residents' minds.

## 2) Leader (指導者) Election (選出) and Activity (活動) Situation (狀況)

### <Leader (指導者) Election (選出)>

O On October 20, 1970, at 20:00, following the resolution (決議) of the residents' general assembly (住民總會), Mr. Lee Jong-gil (李鍾吉) was elected as the leader (指導者).
O However, due to family matters (家事關係), Mr. Lee Jong-gil (李鍾吉) could not devote himself to village affairs, leading to a stagnation in the Saemaul Undong (事業).

### <Leader (指導者) Replacement (交替)>

O Kim Yong-hwan (金用煥), who served as the chairman of the Saemaul Undong (事業) promotion committee (推進 委員長), effectively became the leader (指導者) and took the lead in all Saemaul Undong (事業) activities. Consequently, on March 20, 1971, by the consensus of the residents (住民總意), Mr. Kim Yong-hwan (金用煥) took on the additional role of village leader (指導者).

### <Leader (指導者) Activity (活動)>

O Leader (指導者) Kim Yong-hwan (金用煥) barely finished elementary school (國民學校) and, due to poverty and debt, led a transient life (客地生活) while learning bamboo craftsmanship (竹細工). For about five years, he made and sold fishing gear (漁具) along the coast (海邊) and in fishing villages (漁村). After saving some money, he returned home (歸鄕), paid off all his debts, bought one acre of farmland and a cow, and decided to solidify his path to self-sufficiency (自立) with the dream of a prosperous farmer (農夫). It was around this time that the Yeosu-Suncheon Rebellion (麗順叛亂) occurred.
Unable to stay at home at a young age, he voluntarily joined the riot police (戰警隊) and participated in operations (作戰) such as Jirisan (智異山) and Baegunsan (白雲山) guerrilla suppression (共匪討伐), leaving behind meritorious deeds. During the Korean War (6.25動亂), he participated in operations (作戰) such as Jinju (晋州) and Haman (咸安) Jindong (晋東) and earned three Hwarang (花郎) Military Merit Medals (武功勲章). He was a military (軍人) veteran (出身).
After serving in the police (警察) for seven years (年間), he resigned (辭職) in 1957 and returned home (故鄕) to find it devastated (焦土化) by the Korean War (6.25戰禍).
O Mr. Kim Yong-hwan (金用煥), who vowed to start anew from scratch (原點) a decade (10餘年) earlier, became engrossed (狂奔) in high-grade horticulture (高等園藝) cultivation (栽培) as a means to increase unit yield (單位當 所得) after pondering how to escape the poverty of the past (過去) that relied on wheat-based farming (米麥爲主) and how to create a prosperous rural community (農村) that others would envy, so that future generations (後代) would not inherit such poverty (遺產).


--- (p. 624) ---

However, due to insufficient technology, they started recklessly and faced repeated failures, leading to increasing debts and eventually family disputes. There were many times when tears were shed secretly inside the plastic greenhouse.

*   Even in this desperate situation, they never gave up. They consistently reclaimed 1,200 pyeong of abandoned riverbank land and used it for farming. At the same time, they visited advanced horticulture regions like Gimhae and Jinhae in Gyeongnam to learn techniques and purchase high-quality seeds. They also studied technical books at night, gaining confidence in advanced horticulture, which eventually led to significant profits.

*   However, finding markets was a major challenge. They would wake up at 3 AM and pull a cart to Suncheon, 7 km away, every day. Neighbors would mock them, saying they were acting crazy when they didn't need to struggle to live. They even covered their faces with towels and lived like criminals, but gradually, as their livelihood improved, they found joy and dreams, ignoring both hardships and mockery.

*   Heaven helps those who help themselves, and the earth rewards those who cultivate it with sincerity and effort. Soon, neighbors also started learning techniques and participating in greenhouse farming. As the entire village became enthusiastic about advanced horticulture, they organized work teams and led large-scale technical farming development.

They utilized every inch of land to its highest degree, improving soil fertility with imported soil and compost, and practicing scientific farming with multiple cropping up to 4-5 times a year.

*   Meanwhile, by using seed renewal and growth promoters, they could produce high-quality products early and increase income. They even cultivated turnip greens in tunnel farming before transplanting rice, ensuring no land was left idle. After harvesting unified rice in early October, they planted spinach and green onions, harvesting them by late February, maximizing land use and unit income.

Additionally, by planting potatoes and sweet potatoes earlier with tunnel farming, they could harvest and sell them earlier, increasing income. They also sold the tender stems of early sweet potatoes, which were in high demand, earning significant profits.

Even production materials for advanced horticulture were reused. Old plastic sheets were buried in the ground for storage and reused, reducing production costs.

Through this intensive farming with no idle land and no off-season, practicing scientific farming with 4-5 cropping cycles a year, they achieved high agricultural income.

*   As residential areas formed and large quantities of agricultural products were produced, transportation and market channels became issues. At a time when great effort and expense were required to overcome these challenges, on June 5, 1975, during an economic trends report meeting, they received a car as a gift from President (大統領) Park Chung-hee. This led to a major revolution in market channel development and distribution structure improvement.

Residents could package their products according to standards near their fields, and the car would collect and transport them quickly, maintaining the freshness of vegetables and ensuring fair prices.

Moreover, the rational operation of the car contributed to the overall well-being of residents, providing various benefits such as urgent patient transportation and cargo delivery.

*   They shipped products to major cities like Seoul, Busan, and Gwangju and, on the return trips, transported empty boxes at low cost to producers.


--- (p. 625) ---

By providing supply, we were able to achieve dual effects such as benefits to producers and the operational efficiency of automobiles. On January 25, 1977, we were able to purchase an additional Titan truck due to operational income, and currently, the annual revenue from automobile operations alone reaches 2 million won. Meanwhile, a pig farming boom occurred, with some enterprises raising up to 800 heads of pigs. Even small-scale farmers raise more than 2 heads per household, significantly contributing to farmers' secondary income. In the process of selling the grown pigs, direct collective sales to the market excluded intermediate margins, allowing us to receive fair prices. Through collective procurement and purchase of feed, we reduced production costs and expanded pure profits.

With the active support of the government, 25 households were able to have telephone lines installed, further opening up opportunities for market access, information, and circulation.

As described above, through continuous development and relentless effort, we achieved the scientific management of farming and high utilization of farmland, leading to high income. By 1977, we were able to achieve the goal of 2.5 million won per household three years ahead of schedule for the 1980s. We are now dreaming of higher-dimensional regional development and the construction of a welfare-oriented rural community.

### 3) Overcoming Challenges

When the Saemaul Undong began to spread like wildfire in 1970, we initiated our first project to improve our village by opening farm roads. However, as our village consisted of over 40 households, cooperation was poor. Although resolutions were easily passed at village meetings, the next day, only about 10 people would gather to drink alcohol, and often, the achievements were not even worth the cost of the alcohol. Additionally, during the construction of farm roads, we often faced difficulties in obtaining land donations, leaving gaps in the roads. In areas where land donations were not forthcoming, forcing the project forward sometimes led to conflicts with landowners, causing significant confusion. Despite these challenges, we persisted, emphasizing that the Saemaul Undong was not just for individual prosperity but for the collective well-being of the village. However, some residents, driven by selfishness and ignorance, embezzled village funds and even made false accusations against our gold-level (金) leaders, making their tasks extremely difficult. Through persistent persuasion day and night, we eventually succeeded in opening 520 meters of farm roads.

To guide the residents, who were often lazy and prone to drunkenness, we held a village meeting on November 15, 1970, at 20:00, and established the following village regulations to strictly adhere to:

1. No fighting among residents
2. No drunkenness
3. Enforcement of moral discipline and formation of an enforcement team
4. Eradication of gambling
5. Observance of etiquette
6. Creation of a theft-free village
7. Regulations for punishing those who fail to comply with resolutions, etc.


--- (p. 626) ---

As a result, it was not possible to completely eradicate bad habits in a short period of time, but the number of people who drank excessively and fought gradually decreased. By introducing horticultural cultivation, the agricultural off-season was eliminated, and naturally, the bad habits of gambling and drinking during the winter were corrected. Everyone became eager to improve their livelihoods, and the village gradually became diligent.

6) Heartwarming Stories
a) Episode 1
O Partnering with five nearby villages engaged in advanced horticulture, the community provided agricultural technical guidance, facilitated the purchase and supply of production materials, and helped open up sales channels. This created a wave of increased income that spread to neighboring villages. By organizing these efforts, they formed a cooperative circle for increased income, leading the way in building a prosperous rural community where people cooperate and help each other.

b) Episode 2
O On December 5, 1974, during the Saemaul Undong Promotion General Assembly, initiator Jeong Jin-young and 19 others donated 600,000 won to set an example for future generations of the Saemaul spirit of diligence, self-help, and cooperation. To commemorate the achievements of Saemaul leader Kim Yong-hwan, who had long championed these values, they erected a memorial in front of the village.

8) Special Items
a) Joyful Events
O In the past, frequent water shortages made farming difficult, even during minor droughts. However, after completing the construction of three reservoirs totaling 135 meters in 1971, they could transplant rice seedlings on time and create all-weather farmland. During bountiful harvests, they could feel the satisfaction of their hard work.


--- (p. 630) ---

O During the peak harvest season for advanced horticulture (高等園藝), when products flooded out like a river and we were at a loss for how to handle them, joyous shouts would erupt.
O Just 10 years ago, a village where only one or two middle and high school students could be found now has over 50 students wearing uniforms filling the streets on their way to school, a sight that brings immense satisfaction.

**Sad Moments**
O In the early 1970s, when we were pioneering agricultural roads (農路), those who took the lead in the work faced physical abuse and injuries due to land disputes, and were even falsely accused and investigated, with no one to comfort them as they bore their crosses alone.
O In the early days of developing advanced horticulture (高等園藝) technology, repeated failures led to increasing debts and family discord, causing us to shed bitter tears in despair. However, after overcoming all these adversities and achieving success, we found ourselves shedding tears of emotion, forgetting all the hardships we had endured.

**Various Organizations and Activities**

| Name | Members | Activities and Achievements |
| :--------- | :--------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 4-H | 30 | O Each member is assigned a research topic for focused research and development<br>O Under the guidance of the resident instructor, emphasis is placed on the dissemination of farming techniques<br>O Notably, raising over 500 rabbits led to winning first place in the 4-H competition in the Jeollanam-do region<br>O Using the communal kitchen to improve residents' diets as a demonstration activity. |
| Women's Association | 80 | O Implementing communal work during the farming season<br>O Communal cooking to save time and expenses<br>O Producing canned food 'Bongjorim' for use as meals during the farming season<br>O Saving through the 'Jomdori' savings scheme to create a women's association fund of 250,000 won<br>O Installing village loudspeakers and broadcasting equipment. |
| Diligent Farming Association | 45 | O Promoting farming techniques, early detection of market information, and improving the distribution system to carry out joint sales and cooperative work for mutual benefit and village fund creation, contributing to the Saemaul (새마을) movement funds<br>O Currently, a fund of 1,300,000 won has been created, also contributing to the development of the village savings bank. |

**Achievements Due to the Saemaul (새마을) Movement**

1) Spiritual Aspect
O A village that once squandered its wealth on alcohol and gambling and was prone to daily fights has, through the Saemaul (새마을) movement, become a diligent village without an off-season, with residents actively cooperating and possessing a dynamic and motivated personality, nurturing new mindsets and dreams each day.

2) Livelihood Aspect
O A poor village that could barely avoid begging has, in just 6-7 years, become a prosperous village where nearly every household owns a television.


--- (p. 631) ---

3) Production Aspect
By installing three sets of facilities in paddy fields (天水沓) and shifting from rice and wheat (米麥) centered farming to the Saemaul Undong (新村運動), we created all-weather farmland (全天候). Through improvements in the cropping system (作付體系), such as increasing the number of harvests per year to 4-5, we achieved production levels five times higher than traditional farming (在來式).

4) Income Aspect
A village with a mere 190,000 won per household (戶當) income in 1960 saw its agricultural household (農家) income rise to 2.5 million won by the end of 1977 through the cultivation of high-value vegetables (高等蔬菜), improvements in the cropping system (作付體系), livestock farming (畜產), and fruit-bearing trees (有實樹).

3. Village Assembly (住民總會)
♦ Minutes (會議錄) (1)

Agenda (議題): Establishment of Saemaul Undong (新村運動) Promotion Plan (推進計劃) and Election of Leaders (指導者)
Date (日時): October 20, 1970, 20:00
Location (場所): Kim Gye-hwan's (金桂煥) House (宅)
Attendees (參席人員): 35 people (名)
Absentees (不參人員): 37 people (名)
Chairperson (司會者): Kim Gye-hwan (金桂煥)

Chairperson (司會): Now, we must leave behind poverty and laziness (懶怠) to build a prosperous new village (新村) that is not inferior to others. What is the first business (事業) we should undertake for our village?
Kim Yong-hwan (金用煥): First, the entrance road (入口進入路) to the village is too narrow, making it difficult to enter. Let's open a farm road (農路).
Choi Jeong-keun (崔正根): That's a good idea, but isn't the land (敷地) for the farm road (農路) incorporation (編入) an issue (問題)?
Kim Yong-hwan (金用煥): Although it may be difficult for the corresponding farm households (該當農家), we should donate (喜捨) the land (敷地) for the sake of our village's distant future (將來).


--- (p. 632) ---

Let's do it. I will donate about 80 pyeong (餘坪) of my field.
Lee Byung-gwon (李炳權): I will also contribute about 15 pyeong (餘坪) of my field.
Kim Dong-ryeol (金東烈): I will also donate as much as I can.
Chairperson (司會): These are commendable acts. For the remaining land to be incorporated (編入), a few participants did not attend, so please persuade them to donate (喜捨) and let's start the farm road (農路) project.
Im San-u (林山友): For the construction (開設) of the farm road (農路), the principle (原則) is to start within the year (年中) from the provincial road (地方道) to the village entrance (入口) for 520m. I propose to hold another meeting regarding the concrete (具體的) land donation (土地 喜捨) and promotion (促進) of the project (事業).
All (全體): We agree (贊同) (unanimous decision (滿場一致)).

## 4. Future Development Plans

○ While further developing our main source of income, advanced horticulture, we plan to push forward with road paving and repair, irrigation facilities, and other agricultural water supply projects. We also plan to develop our sources of income by introducing new varieties and expanding the cultivation of bamboo (孟宗竹).

○ Through focused development of the residential area, we plan to improve housing, enhance food life, and promote projects to improve the environment, ultimately creating a model rural community that truly embodies the welfare standards of a prosperous Seoul (京化).

○ We sincerely hope that our future generations will inherit the precious and sacred spirit that our grandparents, parents, and mothers have worked hard to cultivate in creating a good village, and that they will never neglect their love for their hometown and country.


--- (p. 637) ---

# 1. Village Overview

## a. History

* Around 500 years ago (around 1400 AD), nomadic tribes led by the Yu and Kim clans settled in the area after discovering golden sand, naming the village Sachon.
* In April 14, 1592, during the Imjin War, Japanese forces landed at Busan on April 14 and by October, the village was ravaged, with dozens losing their lives.
* On January 3, 1894 (Gabo Year), during the Donghak Peasant Revolution, Park Gi-jo from this village played an active role and died in battle against Japanese forces at Seokdaejeon, near the southern gate of Jangheung, in mid-October of the same year.

## b. Location and Conditions

* Geographically, the village is located in the shadow of Mount Handeok, connected to Mount Sajasan (545m) and Mount Eokbulsan (525m), part of the Jirisan mountain range extending southwestward from the largest mountain range in South Korea. It is a fishing village connected to the small port of Jangjaedo, situated on the Geumgangman Sea.
* From 1955 to 1957, the Jangjaedo land reclamation project transformed the shallow sea into tidal flats suitable for aquaculture, creating a golden tidal flat.
* From 1959 to 1962, as part of a regional development project (supervised by the Ministry of Reconstruction), a 73-hectare agricultural reclamation project was completed, creating excellent conditions for both agriculture and fishing.

## O Village Characteristics

- Located on the coast, the village forms a coastal settlement. The sea has shallow waters, connecting the village to Jangjae Island (長財島), which is surrounded by golden tidal flats, providing a natural fishing ground that has brought prosperity to the village.
- Land reclamation projects have expanded farmland, allowing for year-round production alongside fishing, fostering industrious residents.
- The development of the surrounding hills and the creation of a residential complex with trees are expected to increase income.

## 2. Village Development Process

### 가. Situation Before the 1970s

#### 1) Basic Environment
- Only three houses had improved roofs, and most residents lived in thatched houses passed down through generations. The outbuildings served as both toilets and animal sheds, creating unsanitary conditions. The narrow alleys, enclosed by stone walls, were difficult to navigate with carts and horses, and during the rainy season, they would flood, requiring residents to wear boots.
- As a coastal and mountainous region with a dense population, the village lacked space for development.
- Inside the houses, the walls were black with soot, doors were patched with fertilizer sacks, and the floors were either covered with thick layers of dust or lined with newspaper, creating a typical scene of a decaying village.
- During the Jangjae Island (長財島) land reclamation project, the village's front road was filled in with a width of 5 meters, serving as a playground, courtyard, and meeting place for the children.

#### 2) Income Level
- The main agricultural products were coarse grains harvested from fields cultivated on sloped forest land. The average farmland per household was less than 0.2 hectares, and the reclaimed land, due to high salt content, yielded only three bags of rice per segment (段步當) in total.
- Naturally, the villagers turned to the sea, transitioning from collecting shellfish in scattered natural fishing grounds to artificial aquaculture. Fishing gear mechanization occurred in the late 1960s.
- In the 1960s, daily wage labor was the norm, with annual household income around 500,000 won, barely sufficient for subsistence.

#### 3) Mental State
- Impoverished residents had no leisure to pursue constructive income-generating activities. Adults were often gamblers and alcoholics, neglecting their farms and not utilizing improved fishing gear.
- Youths strayed onto the wrong path, engaging in fights, and parental disputes escalated into neighborhood conflicts, leaving the village without unity.
- To convene a meeting to discuss village affairs, it was necessary to prepare food and drinks.


--- (p. 640) ---

### 4) Cultural Life
O Two radios were the extent of cultural life. There was no electricity, and people couldn't imagine living a dignified life by the dim light of an oil lamp. A few newspapers brought from the village head or the district office were the only reading material, and there was no children's study room for emotional and intellectual development. Parents' enthusiasm for education was pure ignorance, and children carried tattered textbooks wrapped in cloth to school for their lessons.

### 5) Daily Life (Clothing, Food, Shelter)
O Most people wore quilted cotton jackets to block the winter sea winds, and occasionally obtained military surplus jackets became first-class clothing.
O Debts grew with the rice harvest, and people sold fish and shellfish caught by rowboat to afford daily necessities. Sweet potatoes were the main food staple to get through the winter.
O The difficult days of the "barley hump" (a period of food shortage) were a bitter memory that repeated several years.

## II. The Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

### 1) Motives and Achievements of Pilot Projects
O Although poverty was increasing and the residents' spirits were low, awareness of development began to sprout due to reclamation projects and bridge construction. However, there was no driving force for self-reliance. Realizing that marine income was greater than agriculture, members of the youth association initiated artificial aquaculture using tidal flats through their own efforts, shifting from natural aquaculture (shellfish) to artificial methods. As harvests increased, some residents began investing in the sea.
O Motorizing fishing boats to catch fish far out at sea and selling them transformed lives within a year. Seeking a path for all residents to participate, village leaders Kim Sung-keun, Son Seong-myeong, Jeong Min-sik, and the current Saemaul leader (then youth association president) compromised and in 1968 received 2 million won in special income-increasing funds for fishermen and farmers. They sowed seed oysters on 10 hectares of tidal flats, but amid residents' criticism of pursuing personal gain, they anxiously waited two tedious years. When oysters as large as the pit of a persimmon finally appeared, both participants and opponents shared a festive atmosphere.
O That year's oyster harvest totaled 150 tons, generating 8 million won in income. This directly demonstrated that the path to residents' prosperity lay in the sea, and that diligence and cooperation were key.

### 2) Leaders' Activities
O In January 1972, Kim Sung-keun (46 years old) was appointed as the Saemaul leader at the general assembly, and all residents established their own Saemaul regulations.
"We will uphold the Saemaul spirit of self-reliance, cooperation, diligence, creativity, and pioneering with sincerity and responsibility to


--- (p. 641) ---

We vow to carry out the Saemaul Undong to create villages of trust and development in the following ways:
1. We will take the lead in the Saemaul Undong, protecting and building our village with our own strength.
2. We will eliminate idleness and increase income through side businesses.
3. We will cultivate fallow land (遊休地) and develop reclaimed land to enrich our livelihoods.
4. We will research and develop the fisheries sector (水産部門) (fish and shellfish) to enrich our livelihoods.
5. We will uphold etiquette and handle village affairs with unity and solidarity.
6. We will cultivate a savings mentality, with each household having a savings account, to build a prosperous life.
7. We will plant and cultivate trees to green the forests and increase income.
8. We will always maintain environmental cleanliness and contribute to the health and well-being of the residents.
9. We will designate the 1st of each month as Saemaul Day, fostering a thorough anti-communist and counterintelligence spirit to build a democratic society (民主社會).

Starting from 1972, when income increased with the implementation of the Saemaul Undong regulations, the movement began to gain momentum. When 335 bags of cement (洋灰) arrived from the government (政府) in 1971, the then village head (里長), Kim Sun-geun (46 years old), proposed to construct a sewer (下水溝) for the village, but due to the recently established regulations, many residents opposed the idea, fearing that their own land might be affected. As a result, the village-wide project (部落共同事業) could not be pushed forward and was handed over to the youth group (靑年會), who completed about 500m in the most flooded area. However, even after completion, the opposition continued, with people criticizing and refusing to cooperate.

After establishing the Saemaul Undong regulations in 1972, we promoted environmental improvement projects such as roof improvement (改良), achieving 60% of the total progress in 1972 and 1973. We completed 72 out of 74 total houses (2%) in two years, and now the villagers truly understood what the Saemaul Undong was about. Although there were many obstacles, such as opposition to road expansion due to the cost of acquiring land, and the roads ended up winding and uneven, the momentum gradually increased. By 1972, the enthusiasm for the Saemaul Undong was at its peak, and in 1973, the village was promoted to a self-sufficient village (自立마을).

Taking the promotion to a self-sufficient village as an opportunity, we held a face-level Saemaul Undong leadership conference in a well-maintained cousin village in 1973 to build a genuine Saemaul Undong. The conference aimed to sustain the enthusiasm for cooperation and unity. Preparing for the face-level event (行事) was no easy task. We practiced traditional music (農樂) to create a festival atmosphere, formed and practiced a children's choir as the Saemaul Undong choir for over a month, and promoted the event by dividing tasks by sector (分野別). With active cooperation from the face level, the event was successfully concluded, albeit not grandly.

To ensure that village affairs are promoted as a trinity (三位一體), we established a system with the village head (里長) responsible for external affairs (事務), the leader (指導者) focusing on village projects (事業), and the management committee chairperson (運營委員長) managing the village's livelihood. When cooperation and unity were lacking, it was difficult to gather the opinions of these three individuals, but now, if these three people decide to do something, all residents fully cooperate. In 1973, Kim Sun-geun served as the Saemaul Undong leader, Son Seong-myeong as the village head, Jung Min-sik as the management committee chairperson, and Park Sun-tae as the youth group president. From then on, Kim Ra-sun took on the role of the leader (指導者).


--- (p. 642) ---

With active cooperation, the village essentially became a united body of five (오위일체(五位一體)), laying the foundation for Saechon Village to become the best-off village in Jangheung County. Starting in 1973, annual village general assemblies (총회) were held in September and October to discuss the success and sales of shellfish farming, but until 1971, only about half of the residents attended the meetings (회의(會議)). However, from 1972 onwards, 80-90% of residents attended before the meetings even began, causing the meeting hall to become too small and leading to frequent discussions about expanding it. Kim, the village leader, and the residents, who had completely reformed the spiritual aspect (정신면(精神面)) of the village, appointed Park Sun-tae, who had served as the chairman (회장(會長)) of the youth association (청년회(靑年會)), to take on the role of village chief (이장(里長)) to cultivate the next generation of Saemaul leaders.

Starting in 1975, Park energetically managed village affairs, gaining the trust of even the elderly (老人), and encouraged participation from all villagers, regardless of age or gender (남녀노소(男女老少)). In 1974, when the shellfish farming business was going well, the youth association (청년회(靑年會)) and women's association (부녀회(婦女會)) took the lead in establishing a village fund (마을금고) in the form of a village contract (부락계(部落契)), initiating the "One Household, One Account" campaign.

At that time, neighboring villages valued money so highly that they would borrow from Saechon Village to buy even a small piece of land, making it difficult to build up the village fund's assets (자산(資産)). The National Agricultural Cooperative Federation (농협) dispatched staff to promote cooperative savings and time deposits with favorable conditions, making it impossible for the village fund to compete in terms of credit (신용면(信用面)). However, in October 1975, when the village was in the midst of a roof renovation boom, the village fund's executives actively pushed for loans for roof improvements. They persistently pursued understanding and persuasion during monthly neighborhood meetings (반상회(班常會)), women's association (부녀회(婦女會)), senior citizens' association (경로회(敬老會)), youth association (청년회(靑年會)), and 4-H meetings, encouraging even small contributions of one won (壹圓) to the village fund through reward cloth contracts (상포계(賞布契)) and other means.

Gradually, the assets (자산(資産)) grew to 5 million won by the end of 1977, and in 1978, they hurried to establish a legal entity (법인(法人)). Within less than a year of starting, the village fund had amassed a large sum of money (거금(巨金)), becoming the village bank and the village agricultural cooperative. The women's association (부녀회(婦女會)) played the most significant role in this achievement. With the determination (집념(執念)) of the women leaders, they collected and sold 1kg of shellfish, such as oyster shells and cockles, from the shellfish farms, depositing the sales proceeds into their own accounts. This "1kg collection campaign (작전(作戰))" was the result of the persistent determination of the women's association members, building upon the foundation of the frugal rice movement (절미운동(節米運動)).

In January 1977, Park Sun-tae (32) was selected as the Saemaul leader (지도자(指導者)). This selection was made unanimously by all residents (만장일치(滿場一致)) in recognition of his dedication and effort as the village chief (이장(里長)) and youth association chairman (청년회(靑年會) 회장(會長)) in 1975. In his first project after being appointed, he successfully completed an 18-pyeong Saemaul community center within two months, allowing all residents to utilize it. The village fund, with assets (자산(資産)) of 5 million won, contributed to the prosperity of Saechon Village. Additionally, Park is devoted to constructing a warehouse as a long-cherished project (숙원사업(宿願事業)) through the 1977 special support project, and a simple water supply system (간이(簡易) 상수도(上水道)) is expected to be completed this year, contributing to the cultural and welfare environment (문화복지(文化福祉) 환경(環境)) of the new Saechon Village.

### 3) Path Overcoming (경로극복(経路克服)) Situation (상황(狀況))

To boost participation awareness (참여의식(參與意識)), the village fund integrated and operated the women's association (부녀회(婦女會)), senior citizens' association (경로회(敬老會)), youth association (청년회(靑年會)), 4-H, and reward cloth contracts (상포계(賞布契)) through persuasive campaigns (설득작전(說得作戰)). During house-to-house visits, when residents would remark, "Isn't there something else to do?" it seemed better to refuse and say that the village fund was not involved. The spiritual pain (정신적(精神的)) of this was even more agonizing than being hit with a fist.

When calling for meetings (회의(會議)) and spending money they didn't have on alcohol, what results (결과(結果)) could they possibly achieve? It was so unpleasant that they wanted to quit immediately, but they endured by whipping themselves.


--- (p. 643) ---

This is also a fragment of joyful memories.

* When alcohol and gambling were rampant, creating many addicts, I would open doors and shout at the top of my lungs, "They're gambling in there!" only to be threatened, "I'll kill you." I would try to persuade them, "We have no personal grudges. Do you think you can live well by taking other people's money?" and "You must have a good heart to live well," but some would protest by brandishing kitchen knives. Kim Sun-geun recalled such incidents.
* To actively promote roof improvements, I would climb onto roofs without knowing that the rafters were rotten, and two young members fell and were injured when the house collapsed. Fortunately, their injuries were not severe, but the mother of one injured member chased me, the leader (then the youth group president), with a hoe, saying, "You made my son a cripple. You should become a cripple too," forcing me to hide in a neighboring village for two nights. During that time, some members kept asking themselves, "Do we really have to go through this to build a new village?" while others encouraged them.
* However, the residents persuaded the mothers of the two injured members to calm down, and the injured members also recovered. Only then could I visit their homes to comfort them and say, "If we complete the roof improvements, our environmental project will be finished. Please bear with us a little longer. We will install a simple water supply system in 2-3 years and help you, madam." Despite this, the residents just wanted to leave things as they were, and my motivation waned. However, I believed that the collapsed house should be replaced with a new one, so I secretly sold one maggi of rice paddies and, through the village head Ha Jong-gwan, provided the materials for reconstruction.
* This news spread among the villagers, changing their perception of the leader. However, my father was furious, saying, "He is the ruin of our family," and ordered me to either leave the house or stop being a leader. My mother took to her bed, unable to rise due to the disappointment and mental strain caused by my actions. I felt so guilty towards my parents that I did not know what to do. The homeowner whose house had collapsed felt sorry for my family situation, returned the money to my father, and the residents collected donations to help rebuild the house. Everyone praised and encouraged the leader, and even my father understood my position, forgave me, and donated the money (except for my mother's medical expenses) to the village's common fund. When he said that he supported my opinion, I felt a surge of energy knowing that even my father was cooperating. Although my mother recovered, the chest pain she suffered then still continues.

### 4) Developmental Promotion of Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

* Aquaculture has been established with support and self-help efforts, currently covering 42 hectares and yielding an annual harvest of 40 million won. The aquaculture farms using tidal flats are expanding annually, becoming the main source of income and strengthening the foundation.
* Wall improvement has been fully implemented, prioritizing environmental improvement and completing the appearance of a small port.
* The residential improvement project has been expanded, including toilet, kitchen, and annex improvements, playing a decisive role in changing the residents' lifestyle.
* As a special support project, a communal warehouse has been constructed to store and sell the village's products, ensuring price stability and


--- (p. 644) ---

and directly connected to their livelihoods.
- With the simple water supply project, the residential area (住居圏) environment improved in tandem, making housework lighter for women and greatly helping to secure manpower for productive income.

## 6) Heartwarming Stories (美談佳話)

- When the village savings bank chairman was struggling to find an accountant (會計員), Jung Min-sik, a village operating committee member (運營委員), offered his 22-year-old daughter for the position. With the cooperation of all residents, she is now working as an unpaid female accountant (會計員) diligently. She is praised by the residents as a hidden hero behind the village savings bank's achievements.
- On holidays, village representatives visit the frontline outpost of Jeongjaedo to express their gratitude. The proposal was made by Son Seong-myeong, and with the consensus of the residents, they visit the soldiers who work day and night for the defense of the homeland. This strengthens the bond between the military and civilians, fostering a unified system. The villagers humbly express their gratitude to those who have protected their golden opportunity for income growth.

## 8) Special Notes (特記 事項)

### a) Joyful Events

- The senior citizen gathering held every year brings together those aged 70 and above to enjoy a day of festivities. As our income gradually increases, our hospitality becomes more generous. The elderly, witnessing this prosperity, reflect on what they have left for their descendants. They feel a sense of guilt towards the nation and are proud of the achievements of the youth. When they praise the efforts of the leaders, it fills them with more energy and determination to dedicate themselves to the Saemaul Undong. What could be more joyful than receiving recognition?
- In 1968, the joy of overcoming the hardships faced at the Gomak aquaculture farm was shared by everyone, whether they were opponents or supporters. The village was filled with a festive atmosphere, and those who waited and endured realized the power of unity. The happiness felt during that time seems unforgettable, and it made the residents understand the path of cooperation and solidarity.

### b) Sad Events

- When gambling and drunkenness were rampant, we regret not being more bold in eradicating laziness and injustice.


--- (p. 645) ---

Poverty became an even greater enemy (敵). When thinking about living in poverty forever, residents (住民) with aspirations would rather leave their hometowns (故鄕), and when the conviction (信念) of leaders (指導者) who rose in such an environment (環境) was about to waver, sorrow was greater than anger (憤怒). Thinking that this was the obstacle (難關) that the Saemaul Undong had to overcome, it now brings joy.

## Ba. Achievements of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

### 1) Spiritual Aspect (精神面)

*   Taking the era (時節) of laziness (懶怠) and poverty (貧困) as a mirror, established the image (像) of Saemaul for total unity (總和團結), aroused self-confidence (自信感) and pioneering spirit (進取性), and
*   Expressed gratitude (感謝) to the government (政府) and related agencies (關係機關) that supported (支援) various (各種) projects (事業), and as a citizen (國民) of the Republic of Korea (大韓民國), felt pride (自負心) and gratitude (感謝) towards the motherland (祖國),
*   Abandoned dependence (依他心) and took care of (處理) their own affairs (自身의 일), leading a constructive (建設的) and productive (生産的) life (生活), recognizing (認識) neighbors (이웃), and participating (參與) in Saemaul as a leader (旗手) of self-help (自助) and cooperation (協同).

### 2) Lifestyle Aspect (生活面)

*   Supplemented (補完) income increase (所得增大) and development process (開發過程) issues (問題點) by fostering (造成) a frugal (勤儉) and thrifty (節約) atmosphere (氣風)
*   Actively (積極) participated (參與) in bold (果敢) investment (投資) for cultural life (文化生活) to create (造成) an environment (環境) to bequeath (物려주다) to future generations (後孫)
*   Cultivated (涵養) emotions (情緖) and wisdom (智慧) of life (生活) from a wealthy (富裕) and leisurely (餘裕) lifestyle (生活習性)

### 3) Production Aspect (生産面)

*   Increased (增大) fishing (漁業) catches (漁獲高) through mechanization (機械化) and reduced (節減) manpower (人力), time (時間), and expenses (經費) through the powerization (動力化) of fishing boats (漁船), aiming for improved (能率化) production (生産) efficiency (能率).

This is not the property of a few individuals. Everyone who participates becomes an owner. **Park Seong-jae**: Village Chief (漁村契長)! How can we afford 1,000,000 won when we're struggling to make ends meet? If it were that easy, we would have done it by now. As Kim Young-joo said, joint ventures won't work. I don't need this, so I'm going home. (2 people leave)

## 4. Future Development Plans (發展構想)

- The temporary water supply facility, scheduled for completion in December 1977, is a long-standing project for all residents. With 1.7 million won in support, a project worth 5 million won will be completed, finishing the environmental project. This will allow all 138 households to maximize the benefits of cultural citizenship, reducing the workload for women.
- Through the 1977 special support project, a warehouse will be built once the temporary water supply facility is completed. With an area of 50 pyeong, it is expected to generate an annual fixed income of 300,000 won, establishing the village as one centered around shared facilities.
- By repairing the fishing storage facility on Jangjae Island and opening 300 meters of farm roads, we can expect to increase the catch and combine fisheries with agriculture. This will lead to a household income of 3 million won in the 1980s, making our village the most prosperous in Jangheung County.

# Jeollanam-do (全南) Yeongam County (靈岩郡) Haksan-myeon (鶴山面) Yongso-ri (龍沼里) Saemhae Village

## 1. Village Overview (槪況)

### a. History (沿革)

O Saemhae Village in Yongso-ri (龍沼里), Haksan-myeon (鶴山面), Yeongam County (靈岩郡) traces its origins to approximately 360 years ago during the Joseon (李朝) Dynasty under King Sukjong (肅宗). A person with the surname Park (咸陽朴氏) from Hamyang settled in what was then a barren wasteland covered with sand and gravel. Despite numerous hardships and adversities, this individual began to cultivate the land, marking the village's beginning. Later, impoverished farmers from the surrounding areas joined, forming a hamlet that eventually became the village's current site.

O Originally, the village was called "Galgol (葛洞)." Due to the dense wild bamboo growing around the village and the clear, clean stream, it was renamed "Jukgye-ri (竹溪里)." Later, because of the many springs and the vast, sea-like fields, the village was called "Saembadae" in pure Korean dialect. After the Korea-Japan Annexation Treaty, the administrative district was reorganized, and the village was renamed "Saemhae" following the meaning of the Chinese character for "Saembadae," leading to today's name.

O The village started as a basic village in 1972, became a self-help village in 1975, and by the end of 1976, with a household income of 1,560,000 won, it was promoted to a self-reliant village in 1977.
