As shown above, the village owns a relatively large amount of common property, which can be seen as proof of the strong cooperative spirit of the usually diligent and honest villagers. Such common property has been managed and operated under the name "Cheonhaem Village Contract." At the annual general meeting held on December 31, the incumbent manager reports the year's management situation, and the newly elected advisory committee examines and approves it, then transfers the management to the new manager.

Therefore, the main manager is 1 person, the auditor is 5 people, and the advisory committee is composed of 5 people, ensuring that the village common property is managed and increased without any gaps.

## 2. Village Development Process

### Before the Saemaul Undong

#### Self-Reliance Movement Under Japanese Rule

Due to the Japan-Korea Annexation Treaty concluded amidst the anger of the Korean people, the farmland of this village became the property of a Japanese landlord named "Chungdo," and the misfortune of the Baedal people inevitably befell Cheonhaem Village.


--- (p. 656) ---

Therefore, the 24 households that had transformed into tenant farmers lived a life below human dignity. They were so poor that when beggars on the street were asked which village they lived in, they would consistently reply, "I live in Saembadae." The village of Saembadae had become a collective of beggars.

However, the residents, who were kind-hearted, self-reliant, and had a pioneering spirit inherited from their ancestors who had reclaimed wastelands, began to escape the shackles of poverty. This was due to the arrival of a capable leader, Park Woosang, whose presence seemed to move the heavens. Park Woosang emphasized that the entire village must unite to rebuild the lost nation and create a prosperous country and a thriving village. He organized a cooperative body called "Jaryeokgaengsaehoe" (Self-Reliance Revival Association), and the villagers, young and old, actively responded and pledged to work together.

To achieve independence from the Japanese rule, Park Woosang believed that self-owned farmland was essential. Along with the villagers' aspirations, he persistently negotiated with the Japanese landlord "Jungdo" and the credit union. As a result, the credit union provided long-term low-interest funds, enabling the purchase of 260 durak of land from Jungdo. This land was evenly distributed among the 24 farming households. To repay the credit union's debt, the villagers prepared spinning wheels in every household, spinning yarn day and night, and collectively selling the yarn to generate profit. With this profit and their savings, they eventually repaid all debts. Thus, the beggar village of Saembadae was revitalized into a self-owned farming village through diligence and cooperation, marking the beginning of Cheonhae's son's spirit.

The revival of this village under the oppressive Japanese rule, marked by exploitation and tyranny, was not only due to the villagers' enthusiasm but also to the patriotic and people-loving spirit of its leader, Park Woosang. In 1939, at the age of 42, Park passed away without witnessing the liberation of the country. However, his noble spirit continues to flow among the villagers to this day. In his honor, the villagers erected a memorial stone at Donggu to commemorate him and to serve as a model for village development, embodying the residents' sincere dedication to the village.

## 2) Post-Liberation Village Development Movement

With the liberation of the country achieved through the persistent and fierce independence movement, the entire village gained new vitality. The village's Jaryeokgaengsaehoe changed its name to "Cheonhaechonkye" and created a village charter with 45 articles and 4 supplementary articles as a guide for village development. This charter is still read aloud at every village general assembly.

In the chaotic post-liberation era, the leading role in village development was taken by Cheonhae Church, established in 1952 as part of the Presbyterian Church of Korea. This church awakened the villagers' faith, sparking a spiritual revolution and raising their consciousness. It faithfully fulfilled its pioneering role in regional community development, laying the foundation for village development in the 1960s.

### 3) Village Development Movement in the 1960s

The village development in the 1960s began with Cho Jae-yeol, who returned home after three years of public service. In 1961, Cho Jae-yeol gathered like-minded comrades and initiated improvements to toilets, expansion of farm roads, and widening of paths and walls.


--- (p. 657) ---

Good (良), improved stove (아궁이 개량) and other business plans (사업계획) were established and unanimously approved (만장일치 가결) at the village assembly (부락총회), resulting in the village becoming the top model (최고 모범 마을) in Yeongam County (영암군). This growing Cheonhae (천해) village became the foundation (모체) for Yeongam County's development (발전), attracting visits (견학) from related government officials (관계공무원) and village leaders (부락 이장), and even receiving an award (표창) from Yu Dal-young (유달영), then the head of the National Movement Headquarters (국민운동 본부장).

- In 1962, the village initiated the "Eliminate the Carrier Movement" (지게 없애기 운동), collectively purchasing 60 handcarts (손수레, 리어카) and distributing them to all farming households (전 농가), thereby starting to develop efficient farming methods (능률적 농사방법).

Additionally, leader Cho Jae-yeol (조재열) persuaded the residents (주민) with three main points: ① not paying agricultural tax (농지세) and water tax (수세), ② minimal farming costs (농사비용), and ③ reduced labor costs (인건비), leading to the spread of double cropping (논보리 이모작). In response, the residents unanimously decided (만장일치 의결) to participate in the summer fertilization (하계퇴비) and increased production movement (증산운동) for double cropping (이모작 맥파종). As a result of full resident participation (전 주민 참여), the village won an award (입상) in the Jeollanam-do (전남) fertilization (퇴비) increased production (증산) competition (심사), receiving the Excellent Village Award (우수마을 표창) for fertilization increased production (퇴비 증산).

- In 1963, the village established two leading organizations (주도체) for development (발전): the "Jinhung Club" (진흥 구락부) and the "Green Club" (녹색 구락부), thereby constructing a system (체제) for village development (마을 발전).

- In 1964, the village began to focus on increasing non-agricultural income (농외소득), using village funds (마을 기금) to build a 60-pyeong (坪) communal warehouse (공동창고) and starting government (정부) grain (양곡) management (관리) agency work (대행업무), earning 100,000 won in non-agricultural income (농외소득).

- In 1966, the village completed electricity (전기) installation (가설) for all 62 households (62호 전 농가) and held an inauguration ceremony (점화식) on May 16, laying the cultural (문화적) foundation (기초) for daily life (생활). Additionally, the village expanded the communal warehouse (공동창고) by 40 pyeong (坪) and focused on income improvement (소득증진).

- In 1967, the village opened 1,200 meters of farm roads (농로), and in 1968, it expanded farm roads (농로) by 2,300 meters, including Cheonhae (천해) to Sadeung (사등간) 1km, Cheonhae (천해) to Bugok (부곡간) 600m, and Cheonhae (천해) to Sangwol (상월간) 700m. As the village's environment (환경) improved and income levels (소득수준) rose, attention turned to education (교육) for the future (후세) due to the presence of underprivileged children (불우아동) who could not advance to middle school (중학교). With the cooperation (협조) of Reverend Jeong Young-chae (정영채) of Cheonhae Church (천해교회), established in 1952, the village founded Seongseo Middle School (성서중학교) attached to the church (교회 부설). The first principal (초대 교장) was Park Mun-sang (박문상), the village development committee chair (마을 개발위원장).

Seongseo Middle School (성서중학교), true to its original purpose (취지) at the time of its establishment (설립), has been providing middle school (중학교) courses (과정) to underprivileged rural students (부진한 농촌학생) who could not advance to middle school (중학교). This school (학교) has made significant contributions (지대한 공헌) to the development (발전) of the local community (지역사회).

## B. Development Process (발전과정)
### 1) The emergence of a university graduate leader (학사 지도자 출현) as motivation (동기)

Cho Jae-yeol (조재열), who serves as the Saemaul (새마을) leader (지도자) in Cheonhae (천해) village, first became involved in the village's business (사업) in 1962. After Park Woo-sang (박우상), who had devotedly (헌신적) worked for the village's development (발전) during the Japanese colonial period (일제치하), the village lacked a distinct leader (뚜렷한 지도자), and its atmosphere (분위기) was gradually fading (시들어 가다). After graduating (졸업) from the College of Liberal Arts and Sciences (문리대) at Jeonnam National University (전남대학교) in 1958 and working (근무) at the Seoul City Hall (서울 시청) for three years (3년간), Cho faced (직면) the stark contrast (현격한 차이) between urban (도시) and rural (농촌) areas. He realized (인식) that his mission (임무) was to enlighten (계몽) the ignorant (우매) and poor farmers (가난한 농민) and develop (개발) the countryside (농촌) to build (건설) a prosperous (부강) rural (농촌) community (농촌).


--- (p. 658) ---

Recognizing that this was the way to go and that this was also the prerequisite for the radical balanced development of the motherland (祖國), he resolutely gave up the glamorous life in Seoul despite opposition from his family and surroundings. Having returned to his hometown unfamiliar with rural life or farming, he often stayed up all night worrying about the future of the village. Eventually, his first initiative was the establishment of a village club (俱樂部).

At that time, 15 young adults who shared his vision formed the club members, and they fully accepted Cho Jae-yeol's (曹在烈) ideas. Gathering every night in the living room, they deliberated on how the entire village could escape poverty and stagnation. They concluded that organizing the power of the residents (住民) through understanding, persuasion, and a spirit of cooperation, and increasing food production (食糧) through scientific farming (營農) would lead to early self-sufficiency (自立).

The first phase of the project included expanding the farm roads (農路) and village lanes (안길) as prerequisites for village development (發展). This was the initial step to replace the uneconomical and backward use of shoulder poles (지게) for transporting crops with handcarts (리어카). Using handcarts instead of shoulder poles allowed for more work to be done in a shorter period, and more importantly, it helped to modernize and make the residents' thinking more progressive.

Thus, at the general village meeting (部落總會) held on April 25, 1961, with the persistent persuasion of the leader, all residents agreed to the decision. However, when it came to the implementation phase, the residents, whose lives still revolved around short-sighted thinking, were reluctant to offer their fields and refused to donate land for the lane expansion. It might have been natural for them to hesitate to give up land inherited from their ancestors and acquired through hard work just to make way for roads.

However, Cho Jae-yeol (曹在烈), the leader, paid no heed to the villagers' temporary hesitation and, by mobilizing club members through persuasion and semi-compulsory means, managed to complete the expansion of 600 meters of farm roads and 200 meters of village lanes by June 1961, successfully concluding the first project. Thanks to this, in 1962, all farming households jointly purchased handcarts, and the village began to stir with the waves of development as they focused on increasing the production of fertilizer (推肥).

## 2) The Village General Assembly (總會) is the Birthplace of Village Development (發展)

In this village, all important matters, including the New Community Movement (事業), were discussed and decided at the village general assembly (總會) composed of all residents (住民).

Even before the 1960s, this village held an annual regular general assembly (定期總會) in December to report on the management of communal property (共同財產) and handle pending issues for the following year. At this regular assembly, the village head (里長), five development committee members (開發委員), and New Community leaders (指導者) were elected by direct vote of all residents. Urgent matters were discussed at an extraordinary general assembly (臨時總會) when ① each officer deemed it necessary, ② there was a request from the residents, or ③ there was an instruction from the administrative agency. Additionally, a monthly meeting (月例會) was held once a month.

## 3) Activities of the New Community Leader (指導者)

Cho Jae-yeol (曹在烈), the New Community leader of this village, was born on January 15, 1933. After graduating from Chonnam National University (全南大學校) in 1958, he worked at the Seoul City Hall (서울市廳) for three years before returning to his hometown with a purpose to work for the village's development.


--- (p. 659) ---

He has diverse career experiences, including serving as the president of the Hak-san National School (鶴山國民學校) Development Association (育成會長) for 5 years, acting as the Livestock Cooperative (畜協) president (畜協長) for 1 year, and being a national movement member (國民運動要員) for 5 years.

*   Since 1972, he has been at the forefront of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動), faithfully performing his duties as a leader. During his tenure as a leader in 1972, he reorganized the club (俱樂部), which was the center of village development in the 1960s, into the "Green Association (綠色會)" and began laying the foundation for the Saemaul Undong by training village workers. He also organized the Women's Association (婦女會) with female leaders such as Kim Chae-ryeon. Jo Jae-yeol organized the Women's Association and, based on his own experience, realized that the stagnation of rural development was due to the lack of vision among village residents, who were satisfied with their lives as "frogs in a well." To change this, he used some village funds and his own money to take the village women on national tours and visits to advanced villages. Although some villagers criticized him for distracting the women and ruining their homes, Leader Jo did not waver from his resolve, and the results were excellent. The women, seeing the well-maintained streets, improved roofs, and other advanced features of the developed villages, were inspired and began to play a central role in the Saemaul Undong.

*   His organizational skills and outstanding leadership were evident in the village development plan. He divided all residents into departments such as the General Affairs Department (總務部), Work Department (作業部), Materials Department (資材部), Wall Improvement Department (改良部), Toilet Improvement Department (便所改良部), Kitchen Improvement Department (改良部), Roof Improvement Department (改良部), and Annex Improvement Department (附屬舍改良部), and supervised their work while also planning comprehensively.

*   His excellent negotiating skills, both domestically and internationally, led him to frequently travel between counties and districts. In 1971, he secured 335 bags of cement (洋灰), and in 1972, he obtained 500 bags of cement and 1 ton of steel reinforcement for projects such as dike repairs, stone walls, well facilities, laundry areas, public toilet improvements, community center repairs, and public bathhouse construction. In 1976, he received 530 bags of cement and 1 ton of steel reinforcement for warehouse repairs, underground drainage, and sewer installation.

*   In 1977, he was designated as a standard rural village (標準農村) development fund recipient for the Youngsan River (榮山江) with 10 million won (萬원) and was selected as one of two villages in the county for the cluster structure improvement (聚落構造改善) project, receiving 24.75 million won (萬원) in support. His activities were remarkable.

However, his determination for regional development did not stop there.

His passion for education, evident in his 5-year tenure as the president of the Hak-san National School (鶴山國民學校) Development Association (育成會長職), eventually led him to pursue the establishment of a high school. Noticing the lack of a high school in Hak-san-myeon (鶴山面), which had a population of over 15,000, he worked with Hyeon Yeong-bok to secure the necessary conditions for establishing a public high school, including a 5,000-pyeong (坪) school site, annex, and school forest. Through negotiations with the provincial education committee (道敎委) and the Ministry of Education (文敎部), he secured 40 million won (萬원) in donations from residents and government support, leading to the groundbreaking of "Nangju" High School (高等學校) on April 1, 1974, and its completion on March 15, 1977.

*   His will and determination for the Saemaul Undong did not stop there, as he continued to prioritize the village's development over his own family and health. His health deteriorated due to the excessive workload day and night.


--- (p. 660) ---

However, his wife's complaints about his actions, which left her with no time to take care of the household and no savings to spare, dealt a significant blow to his spirit.

Yet, despite this, he remained composed and patient, earning him the title of an evergreen (常綠樹) Saemaul leader.

### 4) Overcoming Challenges

Like all villages involved in the Saemaul Undong, including rural communities such as Cheonhae Village, the path to its current state was not without obstacles. Moreover, with 62 out of 62 households fully engaged in agriculture, the lack of business promotion skills resulted in significant setbacks, and initially, the villagers' lack of unity led to low work efficiency.

* First, there were issues related to religion.

Cheonhae Village is home to Cheonhae Church, a Presbyterian (長老會) church established in 1952. Out of 62 households, 30 are church members. The unity among these members is strong, and their opposition to village projects could halt progress. Additionally, most members avoided work on Sundays, causing significant disruptions to the busy schedule. Saemaul leader Cho Jae-yeol and a few other leaders visited the church to persuade the pastor and, through their righteous actions, won over the members, eventually uniting their strength towards the Saemaul Undong's goals.

* Second, there were disputes among the villagers.

To address this, village assemblies were frequently held to unite the villagers. Through warm conversations and persuasion, along with meals prepared using women's association funds, a sense of unity was achieved.

* Third, the villagers' lack of skills hindered progress.

The village lacked essential workers such as earthworkers, carpenters, and plasterers, requiring the village to hire skilled workers from outside. To prevent the outflow of villagers and to ensure the smooth progress of all projects according to the initial plans, promotion committee members from each department visited other villages to learn and then implement what they had learned. Now, most villagers possess the necessary skills.

* Fourth, construction materials and other supplies often arrived during the busy farming season, making it difficult to mobilize daily workers for communal work.

To resolve this, a village consensus was reached to start work at 6:30 AM every morning, involving all villagers, thus solving the problem.

### 5) Land and Material Donations

* The current self-sufficient Cheonhae Village is a result of not only the leader's dedicated efforts but also the villagers' willing sacrifices and donations.
* For instance, in 1967, when a 1,200m farm road with a width of 2m was opened, 15 people including Park Mun-sang donated about 600 pyeong of fertile land for the village's development.
* In 1968, when the farm road was expanded from 2m to 6m in width over a length of 2,300m, 17 people including Park Mun-sang donated about 2,500 pyeong of farmland.


--- (p. 661) ---

In 1973, when expanding the village road to 320 meters in width and 4 meters in length, almost all residents, including Lee Jun-ho, Park Bong-gyu, and Park Jae-pyeong, cooperated wholeheartedly by either reducing their farmland or building walls.

In 1977, when the village improvement project was underway, 397 residents aged 62, armed with the Saemaul spirit of diligence, self-help, and cooperation, began to contribute their private funds without distinction of age or gender. Specifically:

1. Park Young-dae donated 70 pyeong of land required for the creation of a children's park.
2. Park Bong-gyu and two others donated 60 pyeong of land needed for the expansion of the village entrance road.
3. Fifteen individuals, including Cheonhae Church, donated 227 pyeong of land for the integration of main and branch roads, thereby promoting village development.

Witnessing their hometown transform through the village improvement project, natives of this region, including Choi Byung-hwan from Gwangju, Choi Young-sik from Seoul, and Kim Young-gu from Seoul, donated a total of 170,000 won to the Saemaul leaders and encouraged the residents. Additionally, individuals from various locations delivered cabinets, TVs, and complete reception sets to be placed in the community center, demonstrating their commendable patriotism.

6) The Wisdom and Tenacity of Women: The Driving Force Behind Cheonhae Village's Development

Cheonhae Village's current appearance is a testament to the significant role played by the support of women. The women of this village, led by Mrs. Cho Jae-yeol and Mrs. Park Chae-ryeon, participated in a nationwide industrial inspection tour and visited advanced villages in the spring of 1972. Upon their return, they recognized the necessity of village development and the important responsibilities of women. They warmly encouraged their disheartened husbands, enabling the men to devote their entire passion to village development, temporarily forgetting their families.

However, the women's dedication did not stop there. In the scorching heat of July 1977, over 40 women from the village, undeterred by the intense summer heat, collected sand required for communal village work from Mangwolcheon, a border area between Haksan-myeon and Miam-myeon, 3 km away from the village. Although they had obtained prior permission from the county to collect the sand, several nearby unscrupulous businessmen, enraged at the loss of their vested interests, threatened the workers with sickles and tops to halt the work. Frightened, the men fled, but the women, undaunted and soaked in sweat, continued their work in the water up to their knees. This work continued throughout July, and the men, initially frightened, eventually found courage and continued working, moved by the women's tenacious fighting spirit and gratitude. Thus, it can be said that the development of this village was truly achieved by the women.

D. Annual Progress and Achievements

The village entrance road and internal roads, commenced on October 11, 1961, were completed by November 30 of the same year, earning the village the distinction of being a model village in the county. The village received an award from Yu Dal-young, the director of the National Movement Headquarters, laying the foundation for village development.

Through local improvement projects, the village achieved increased production of fertilizer, earning recognition in the Jeonnam Fertilizer Production Competition. Additionally, the village constructed a handcart using its own resources.


--- (p. 662) ---

The purchase of 60 units (臺) and their distribution to all farming households (全農家) led to the elimination of shoulder poles and the beginning of scientific farming (科學營農). The consciousness structure (意識構造) of the residents (住民) became scientified (科學化).

- In 1964, a 60-pyeong (坪) village warehouse (倉庫) was established, generating an income (所得) of 100,000 won (萬) from storage fees (保管料).
- On January 15, 1966, electrical installation (電氣架設) began, and ignition (點火) occurred on May 16. This was achieved independently by the village (自體), allowing all residents (全住民) to start a minimum level (最小限) of cultural life (文化生活) while also expanding the communal warehouse (共同倉庫) by 40 pyeong (坪).
- In 1967, a 1,200-meter agricultural road (農路) was constructed independently, starting on May 12 and completing on August 10.
- In 1968, a 2,300-meter agricultural road (農路) was constructed independently, starting on June 11 and completing on July 28.
- In 1971, the village received 335 bags (袋) of cement (洋灰) from the county (郡) to build a bathhouse (沐浴湯) (May 19–June 19) and a communal toilet (共同便所) (July 10–July 29), raising the cultural level (文化水準) and fundamentally changing the residents' consciousness structure (意識構造).
- In 1972, four communal laundries (共同 빨래터) were installed, and 800 pyeong (坪) of "Rigida" pine (松) and "Italian" poplar saplings were cultivated, generating an income (所得) of 1.5 million won (萬).
- In 1973, the village expanded the inner road (마을안길) by 320 meters, completed roof improvements (지붕 개량) on 42 buildings (棟), and introduced 80 head (頭) of beef cattle (肥肉牛), beginning to diversify income (所得) beyond agriculture (農事).
- In 1974, the village purchased 3,000 pyeong (坪) of communal land (共同 재산) and, through communal labor (共同作業), cultivated unified rice (統一) to harvest 75 sacks (石).
- In 1975, a 40-pyeong (坪) fish farm (養漁場) was installed through a presidential (大統領) gift project (事業), beginning to focus on non-agricultural income (農外所得) and creating a new momentum for increased income (所得增大).
- In 1976, with 530 bags (袋) of cement (洋灰) and 1 ton of rebar (鐵筋) support (支援), the village completed 416 meters of sewer (下水溝), 4 dark drains (暗渠), an 18-pyeong (坪) warehouse (倉庫), 800 meters of fence improvement (담장 개량), and telephone line installation (通信電話架設) by the year's end (年末).
- In 1977:
  - **Saemaul Community Center (會館)**: Through a presidential (大統領) special support project (特別支援事業), 1.5 million won (萬) was supported (支援) to build a two-story (層), 40-pyeong (坪) building (建物), starting construction (着工) on February 20 and completing (完工) on April 15.
  - **Standard Rural Development Project (標準農村 育成事業)**: Village inner road improvement (整備) of 880 meters, fence improvement (改良) of 1,300 meters, sewer improvement (下水溝整備) of 510 meters, 24 meters of dark drains (暗渠), village tree planting (植樹) of 200 trees (本), roof painting (塗色) of 39 buildings (棟), and a 50-pyeong (坪) children's playground were started (起工) on February 28 and completed (完了) on April 30, with a support fund (支援金) of 10 million won (萬).
  - **Hamlet Structure Improvement Project (聚落構造 改善事業)**: With 24.75 million won (萬) of government support (政府支援) and 24.17 million won (萬) of self-funding (自負擔), a groundbreaking ceremony (起工式) was held on July 5. The detailed projects (細部事業) included relocating 17 houses (住宅移築), repairing 30 houses (住宅補修), repairing 36 annexes (附屬舍補修), improving 45 toilets (便所改良), improving 45 kitchens (部엌 개량), improving 1,440 meters of fences (담장 개良), expanding and improving 120 meters of access roads (進入路), 260 meters of main inner roads (幹線 안길), 260 meters of branch inner roads (地線 안길), installing 510 meters of sewers (下水溝設置), and planting 3,100 trees (植樹) in the village. The project was completed (完工) on December 13, making Cheonhae Village (泉海마을) a true cultural rural community (名實相付한 文化農村).

### La. Various (各種) Organizations (組織) and Activities (活動) Situation (狀況)

- This village has two important (重要한) organizations (組織): the "Green Association (綠色會)" and the "New Life Improvement Association (改善會)."
- The Green Association (綠色會), as the successor (後身) to the club (俱樂部), consists of 15 members (名) ranging from youth (靑年) to the elderly (老人).


--- (p. 663) ---

The core of improving farming methods (營農方法改善).

In 1972, the Green (綠色) members who were reorganized (再編成) prioritized improving the backward farming methods (營農方法) by visiting advanced (先進) villages to learn and practice advanced farming knowledge (營農知識) and techniques (技術). They then conducted daily village tours (巡廻) to provide dedicated farming guidance (營農指導), fostering cooperation (協同心) and increasing income (所得增大) among residents (住民). To promote a diligent (勤勉) atmosphere (氣風), they launched campaigns such as "Smoke Two Fewer Cigarettes a Day Movement (運動)" and "Drink One Less Glass of Alcohol a Day Movement (運動)," deeply ingraining these ideas into the residents' consciousness (意識). Additionally, they established a village savings fund (金庫) following the initiative of Cho Jae-yeol (曹在烈), the chairman (理事長) of the Haksan-myeon (鶴山面) village savings fund (金庫) and a Saemaul leader (指導者), by creating a rice fund (基金) of 62 seok (섬).

* The New Life Improvement Association (새生活改善會) was reorganized (再編成) at the end of 1975 from the women's group (婦女會) established in 1972. Park Chae-ryeon (朴採蓮), the leader (指導者) of the women's group (婦女會), gathered 15 like-minded women (婦女子) to form a small-scale association (契) aimed at living frugally and practicing thrift. This marked the beginning of their efforts. After returning from national tours (全國觀光) and visits to advanced (先進) villages, they took the lead in Saemaul projects (新村事業) such as kitchen improvement (部屋改良) and toilet improvement (便所改良). Despite initial strong resistance (抵抗) from residents (住民), the 15 tenacious women (婦人) persisted with patience (忍耐) and solidarity (結束), achieving good results (成果) and significantly contributing to fostering a frugal ( 검소한) lifestyle (生活) with a monthly savings (貯蓄) of approximately 1,000 won per person (人當). However, the tenacious spirit (억척) of the women (婦人), once ignited, knew no bounds. They organized work teams (作業班) for collective farming (共同作業) such as rice transplanting (모내기) and barley harvesting (보리베기), and engaged in collective purchasing and sales (購販) to eliminate intermediaries' profits (中間利益) and increase their own income (所得). They prospered with a rice fund (基金) of 125 seok (섬), which was distributed (配付) to individuals (個人) in 1975. The New Life Improvement Association (새生活改善會), which focuses on kitchen improvement (改良) and dietary improvement (食生活改善), consists of 22 members (名) and holds a fund (基金) of 300,000 won (萬원).

Ma. Self-reliance achieved through sweat and toil (自立)

1. Spiritual aspect (精神面)
* Through their hard work, villagers replaced roofs and straightened narrow village paths, coming to understand the true value of sweat (眞債). Witnessing their cleanly organized village and increasing income (所得), they deeply ingrained the belief (信念) that "it can be done" and the resolve (意志) that "it must be done" into their consciousness (意識構造). They also learned to respond to the nation's modernization (近代化) policies (政策).
* Starting their days at 6:30 AM and working late into the evening, they developed an industrious (勤勉) lifestyle habit (生活習性) that couldn't tolerate inactivity. Through activities (團體活動) of organizations like the Green Association (綠色會) and the New Life Improvement Association (새生活改善會), as well as daily village general assemblies (總會), they learned to understand each other and developed cooperative efficiency (協同的能率) through collective work (共同作業). After these arduous efforts (刻苦), as their income (所得) increased and the village environment (環境) was renewed (一新), they abandoned their dependency on authorities (官依賴) and solidified their self-awareness as the main characters (主人公意識) of their own lives. This self-reliant (自力) atmosphere (風土) will greatly contribute to the healthy development (健全한發展) of democracy (民主主義) in this country.

2. Environmental aspect (環境面)
* After completing the main project (事業) of 1977, the village improvement project (聚落構造改善事業), the village was organized (整備) so thoroughly that it gave the impression of being a part of a city (都市), rather than a rural (農村) village.


--- (p. 664) ---

The main roads in the village were widened to 8 meters, and the branch roads to 4 meters. A 4-meter-wide farm road, 510 meters of covered sewers, and 3,100 trees planted around the entrance roads to beautify the surroundings were completed. Additionally, collective facilities such as a community warehouse, a multipurpose hall (會舘), a purchasing and selling place (購販場), a children's playground, and a public bathhouse (共同沐浴湯) were constructed. Every household improved their roofs, painted their houses, renovated their walls, and upgraded their kitchens, thereby significantly improving the village environment. Notably, the "Steam" heating system and the "Tayru" modern kitchen counters demonstrated advanced hygiene management. The 200-pyeong (坪) village park in the center of the village also caught the eye.

*   Cultural facilities include electricity installed in 1966, 11 telephones, 23 TVs, 8 record players, and more than 64 radios (one per household). Additionally, 30 households subscribed to various newspapers, making this village a model rural community with urban-level cultural life.

### 3) Production and Income

*   Originally, the village's farmland consisted of sandy soil with poor water retention. To address this, under the guidance of leader Cho Jae-yeol (曹在烈), the villagers worked tirelessly during the winter off-season for over 60 days, transporting 2,100 truckloads of soil to transform it into fertile land. They also devoted considerable effort to compost production, creating over 1,600 tons annually. By 1975, the soil had become suitable for rice farming with a pH of 6, and by 1977, land consolidation was completed, resulting in excellent farmland unmatched by other villages.
*   Recognizing that increasing per-unit production was key to rice production, leader Cho Jae-yeol educated residents on new rice farming methods. He diligently implemented the 7-step agricultural guidance for food self-sufficiency by the Agricultural Guidance Center, promoting timely transplanting, timely collective pest control, and the dissemination of scientific rice farming techniques. By 1977, all farming households were cultivating unified rice varieties, achieving an average yield of 660 kg per 10 a (反), a remarkable feat. Additionally, the village promoted double cropping of barley, renewed seed varieties with new strains such as "Buhung Olbarley" and "Milyang 64," and achieved a 52% increase in barley production.
*   Not content with these achievements, leader Cho Jae-yeol realized that rice and wheat farming alone would not sufficiently increase income. After considering the efficient use of the 9.4-hectare field, he decided to expand chili pepper cultivation. Starting in 1975, he invited agricultural guidance officers, acquired new cultivation techniques, and with the Green Members (綠色會員), implemented "cover planting." This method yielded a 40% increase in production compared to traditional direct seeding, inspiring the entire village. Focusing on the color and quality of the mass-produced chili peppers, and improving the drying methods, the village harvested 9.4 tons from 5 hectares in 1977, generating an income of 4 million won. Additionally, melon and tomato cultivation brought in an income of 1.4 million won.

# 3. Residents' Assembly (住民總會)

♦ Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (1)

*   **Date of Meeting (開催日時)**: December 13, 1965, 11:00 AM
*   **Venue (開催場所)**: Resident Im Chunchae's (任春彩) House
*   **Attendance (出席數)**: 42 people
*   **Chairperson (議長)**: Vice Chairman of the Advisory Committee (諮問委員會副委員長), Park Hwandae (朴奐大)
*   **Minutes Secretary (會議錄書記)**: Park Jaepyeong (朴在平)

O Proceedings and Resolutions
O Chairman Park Hwandae (朴奐大) declared the meeting open.
O Im Chunchae (任春彩) read out the village (村) financial (禊) management (管理) report for the year 1965. The newly elected Advisory Committee (諮問委員會) was tasked with examining and approving the documents on the same day.
O Cho Jaeyeol (曹在烈) read out the village (部落) regulations (洞案).
O The following temporary (臨時) agenda was approved:

Agenda (會順)
1. Opening remarks (開會辭) and declaration of the meeting open (開會宣言)
2. Village (村) financial (禊) report (財政報告)
3. Reading of the village (部落) regulations (洞案)
4. Reading of the previous meeting minutes (會議錄)
5. Village (洞長) personnel affairs (人事)
6. Evaluation of village (洞長) rewards and punishments (賞罰審査)
7. Determination of the village (里長) leader's (班長) monthly salary (月俸) and rations (客糧)
8. Determination of the village (村) financial (禊) compensation (手苦料) for the village head (有司)
9. Determination of various (各種) wages (勞賃) for the year
10. Protection of village (洞) forests (有林)
11. Reorganization of various (各級) village (部落) committee members (役任委員)
    (a) Advisory (諮問) committee members (委員)
    (b) Village (里長) leaders
    (c) Agricultural cooperative (農協) executives (任員)
    (d) Development fund (開發禊) executives (任員)
12. Selection of the village head (有司)
13. New construction and repair of farm roads (農路)
14. Other (其他) discussion items (討議事項)
15. Reading of the meeting minutes (會議錄)
16. Declaration of the meeting closed (閉會宣言)

O The monthly salary (月俸) for the village (里長) leader was set at 1 do (斗) of regular rice (正租) or naked barley (裸麥) per month, and the annual salary (年俸) for the sub-leader (班長) was set at 1 do (斗) of regular rice (正租). The village (里長) cooperative leader's (組合長) rations (客糧) were set at 1 do (斗) of regular rice (正租) per month, as they hold a concurrent position (兼任). The collection committee (收合委員) will consist of the sub-leader (班長) and the old and new village heads (新舊有司), and will collect on the 14th of each month.
O Various (各種) wages (勞賃) were determined as follows: plowing (爭氣質) - 1 do (斗) of regular rice (正租) per magi (斗落), weeding (除草) - 1 do (斗) of regular rice (正租) per magi (斗落), transplanting (모내기) - 8 shi (升) of regular rice (正租) per magi (斗落), general (一般) wages (勞賃) - 1 shi (升) of white rice (白米) for men and 1 shi (升) of plain rice (平) for women per day.
O The boundary survey (測量) of the village (洞) forests (有林) was entrusted to the Advisory Committee (諮問委員), with the cost (費用) to be borne by the village (里) finances (財政). The survey must be completed by the last day of the 12th lunar month (陰曆). If privately owned land (個人所有土地) is found to be part of the village (洞) forests (有林), it will be temporarily purchased (差入) and handled according to the resolution of a temporary village (部落) assembly (臨時總會) to be held later.
O Regarding the protection (保護) of the village (洞) forests (有林), all village residents (部落民) were asked to pay attention (關心) and prevent theft and logging (盜伐). The forest (山林) account manager (禊長), village (里長) leader, and village head (村有司) were given special responsibility (特히責任) and authority (管轄權) over forest protection (山林保護).
O The village head (有司) for 1966 was selected as Park Mansok (朴萬束).

*   For each (各) executive (任員) election (選擧), advisory committee members (諮問委員) were elected by secret (秘密) ballot (投票) without naming (無指名), and the ballot (開票委員) committee members Cho Jae-yeol (曹在烈) and Park Jae-pyeong (朴在平) oversaw the counting (開票) and announced the election (當選) of 5 advisory committee members (諮問委員): Park Mun-sang (朴文相), Park Hwan-dae (朴焕大), Choi Ik-don (崔益敦), Ryu Nan-chul (劉蘭出), and Cho Gi-hwan (曹奇煥).

    ② Park Mun-sang (朴文相) requested (諫請) that the neighborhood heads (洞長) discipline (訓戒) those who have caused problems (問題) in community (共同) life (生活) or acted improperly (不順), without favoritism (私情).
    ③ Park Mun-sang (朴文相) requested (懇請) that the neighborhood heads (洞長會) advise (勸勉) Kim Yong-dae (金龍台) as his family (家庭) has been disorderly (家規가 어지러우며) and his family life (家庭生活) has received poor public opinion (輿論), asking them to improve (여론이 없도록) in the future (앞으로).
    ④ The neighborhood head meeting (洞長會) pointed out (指摘) that Lee Gi-beom (李基範) and Lee Gi-bok (李基福) brothers have had an unhappy (不睦) family life (家庭生活), lack (不足) of respect for the elderly (敬老心), and disobeyed (不順從) their parents (父母님). The meeting (會) urged (勸勉) all villagers (部落民) to advise (勸勉) each other (서로 서로가) with kind words (좋은 말로) to prevent (없도록) such issues (일) in the future (앞으로) and to make their village (마을) a model (模範) worthy of praise (贊辭) even from outsiders (外處). They asked (當付) the villagers (部落민) to take this admonition (훈계) seriously (명심) and to guide (善導) those who were admonished (훈계받은 자) today (오늘에).
    ⑤ Kim Yeon-tae (金燕泰) and Cho Yeong-dae (曹永大) were commended (致賀) for their great (至大) dedication (獻身) to public (公共) village affairs (部落事) and for being models (模範) of diligence (勤勉) in their personal (私生活) lives (生活). Park Yeong-dae (朴瑛大) was also commended (致賀) for his many (多) contributions (功勞) to public welfare (公益事業) in the village (部落). It was decided (可決) to award (褒賞) them with a budget (豫算) of 600 won (一金 육백원) from the village development (材禊) funds (財政).
*   For farm road (農路) repairs (補修), all villagers (部落民全員) and carts (리어카) were mobilized (總動員) to transport (運搬) stones (돌) from Yulgisan (栗崎山). It was decided (可決) to complete (完了) the repairs (補修) by the end of December (陰 12月末日) and that the village head (里長) would be responsible (責任) for the mobilization (動員) and implementation (實踐).
*   For the construction (新設) of a new farm road (農路), it was decided (可決) to push forward (推進) the construction (新設) from Doryeongjeong (桃林亭) to Hanteulbangdae Bridge (한뜰방아 다리까지). A promotion committee (推進委員) consisting of Park Mun-sang (朴文相), Ryu Nan-chul (劉蘭出), Im Ok-am (任玉岩), Kim Cheon-su (金千壽), Choi Ik-don (崔益敦), Im Ryang-mo (任良模), Park Mo-dae (朴模大), Park Jae-pyeong (朴在平), and Lee Jun-ho (李俊浩), totaling 9 people (名), was selected (選定) to oversee the project (推進).
*   It was decided (可決) that the election (選擧) of the advisory committee chairperson (諮問委員長) and the development (開發) contract manager (禊長) would be held (舉行) separately (別途) at a later committee meeting (委員會) and the results (選出) would be announced (公布).
*   The congratulatory fee (致賀費) for the official (有司) Im Chun-chae (任春彩) was decided (決定) to be 500 won (一金 오백원정) and it was agreed (可決) to pay (支拂) it.
*   The chairman (議長) declared the closure (閉會) of the meeting at 17:25 (時 17時 25分) on the same day (同日).

## Minutes(會議錄)(2)

Date and Time of Meeting: December 16, 1966, 11:55 AM
Venue: Park Man-song's (朴萬松) Residence
Attendees: 46
Chairperson: Tribal Advisor Committee Chairman Park Hwan-dae (朴焕大)
Minutes Secretary: Park Bong-gyu (朴奉圭)

- The Chairperson, Park Hwan-dae (朴焕大), declared the opening of the meeting and the following agenda items were resolved.
- The village chief, Park Man-song (朴萬松), reported the financial settlement for the year 1966 as recorded in the separate volume of the village treasury ledger. Although there was a deficit, it was resolved to cover it with the income from the warehouse storage business.
- The Chairperson announced and reported the interim financial settlement of the warehouse storage business up to the summer harvest of 1966.
- Cho Jae-yeol (曹在烈) presented a reading of the village records, and Park Bong-gyu (朴奉圭) read the minutes of the previous year's meeting.
- The village head, Park Han-nyeon (朴漢年), made remarks regarding personnel matters, discipline within the village, and requested cooperation. These remarks were noted.
- The following agenda items were adopted for discussion and resolution:
    1. Survey of the village forest boundary (Carried Over)
    2. Determination of various allowances: Village chief's monthly ration, sub-chief's annual salary, clerk's gratuity, and processing of incoming residents
    3. Amendment of the village regulations
    4. Preparation of an inventory of supplies and disposal of discarded items
    5. Reward and punishment review at the village head meeting
    6. Selection of advisory committee members
    7. Selection of clerks
    8. Other matters for discussion
- It was resolved that the survey of the village forest boundary, a carried-over agenda item, must be completed this year.
- It was resolved that the sub-chief's annual salary would be paid in standard measure of rice.
- It was resolved to amend the village regulations by adding the following provisions (Article 6 of the Supplementary Provisions):
    1. All matters related to the tribe shall be subject to the audit of the Advisory Committee as follows:
        1. The matters subject to audit shall be village administration and village treasury documents.
        2. The first audit shall be conducted three days before the village's day of honesty each year.
        3. The second audit shall be conducted two days before the village's day of honesty at the end of the year.
    2. Village administration and village treasury documents must obtain the approval of the Advisory Committee. Documents must be submitted for review and approval within three months of their issuance or implementation. If this period is exceeded, the documents will not be recognized, and the person in charge may be dismissed from their position.
    Article 39, Paragraph 1: The village chief's monthly stipend for the summer harvest shall be six bushels of barley (120 kg in net weight) from May to October, and six bushels of rough rice (100 kg in net weight) from November to April of the following year.
- A farewell banquet shall be held for those who have completely sold their property and moved out.
- It was resolved that the village chief would be reappointed. (Reappointed village chief: Park Jae-pyeong (朴在平))
- It was resolved that the election of tribal officials under the village chief would be held annually on March 1.
- The meeting was adjourned for lunch and resumed at 3:15 PM the same day.


--- (p. 668) ---

Handling meeting affairs.

*   Inventory (備品臺帳) and disposal of discarded items (廢品處理), the disposal of discarded items (廢品處理) was delegated (委任) to the advisory committee (諮問委員) and passed (可決).
*   Selection of advisory committee members (諮問委員 選定): A motion was made to nominate members by oral recommendation (口頭呼薦), and an amendment was proposed to elect 5 members by secret ballot (秘密投票) and select the top 5 vote-getters (多點者順). The amendment passed, and the voting results were as follows:
    Park Yeong-dae (朴瑛大) 24 votes (票), Cho Jae-yeol (曹在烈) 20 votes (票), Im Ok-am (任玉岩) 11 votes (票), Park Bong-gyu (朴奉圭) 20 votes (票), Im Chun-chae (任春彩) 18 votes (票), Cho Gi-hwan (曹奇煥) 15 votes (票), Choi Young-jak (崔瑛作) 13 votes (票), Park Mun-sang (朴文相) 15 votes (票), Cho Eun-sik (曹殷植) 21 votes (票), Kim Yong-dae (金溶大) 11 votes (票). The top 5 vote-getters (多點者順) were elected: Park Yeong-dae (朴瑛大), Cho Eun-sik (曹殷植), Park Bong-gyu (朴奉圭), Cho Jae-yeol (曹在烈), and Im Chun-chae (任春彩).
*   For the selection of new officers (新有司選定), a 10-minute recess (分間) was taken to consult with the neighborhood association (洞丈會), and Kim Jae-si (金在氏) was elected as an officer (有司).
*   The neighborhood association (洞丈會) announced that villagers should self-reflect (自覺 自省) and actively contribute (積極 獻身) to the development of the village (部落 發展).
*   Due to the resignation (辭免) of a team leader (班長), re-election (再選) was held. The village head (里長), Park Jae-pyeong (朴在平), nominated Lee Sang-keun (李尙根) as the second team leader (第二班長) and Jeong Yong-gi (鄭龍基) as the third team leader (第三班長), which was approved (認准).
*   Fundraising for the expansion of Haksan Elementary School (鶴山國民校) and the self-raised funds (自己 自己) of the agricultural cooperative (農協) will be conducted simultaneously with the collection of the village head's monthly fee (里長 月料). The allocation method for the village head's monthly fee (里長 月料) will follow the summer grain monthly fee (夏穀月料) grading (等級), and the collection schedule (據出 日期) was set for December 17.
*   Regarding the re-organization of the village's agricultural improvement club (農事改良俱樂部), Park Bong-gyu (朴奉圭) provided a detailed explanation (仔細 說明). Those wishing to join (入會) should register (登錄) with the village head (里長) by December 17 with their seal (印章).

--- (p. 669) ---

This year's (1967) residents of this village are Im Yun-bong (任允奉), Kim Un-ho (金云鎬), and Park So-il (朴昭日). The new residents are Im Yun-bong (任允奉) and Kim Jun-chae (金俊彩).

Regarding pending matters, it was decided to overcome any difficulties and conduct the survey of Dongyu Rim (洞有林) in 1968.

The decision on the standard wages for the village in 1968 will be discussed and determined at the next general meeting.

Park Chun-woong (朴春雄) was elected as the village head (촌계 유사, 村契有司) for 1968.

The method for collecting the village head's allowance will be divided into three grades as before. The village head will receive 600 geun (斤) of regular rice for the village affairs, and the team leader will be paid per person in the daedu style (臺斗式).

The electricity bill for the streetlights in the village will be budgeted at three du (斗) of regular rice. If the bill is less than 1,000 won, the village head will pay it on behalf of the village. If the bill exceeds 1,000 won, the village head will sell one du (斗) of rice to cover the cost. The final settlement will be made at the regular general meeting.

Regarding the paddy field owned by Jeong Yong-gi (鄭龍基), it was decided to sell it this year, considering the purchasing power of individuals. The selling price was set at seven seok (石) of regular rice, to be paid in two installments of three seok and five du (石五斗) of autumn crops in 1968.

A report was made by Cho Gi-hwan regarding the forest in Geumsaenggol, Sangwol-ri (上月里), which is jointly managed by six villages (육개리, 六個里). A profit of nine seok and three du (九石三斗) and six shik (升) was distributed to the village, which will be absorbed into the village finances but managed separately.

Regarding the land that was cultivated and used without permission within Dongyu Rim (洞有林), it was decided that all villagers will participate in reforestation.

Other matters discussed included Park Bong-gyu's suggestion for each household to guide children's education, and Choi Ik-don's proposal to draw water due to the drying up of the daily water path. It was decided to carry out the water drawing on December 17 with joint participation.

The congratulatory gift for the village head Kim Jae-tae (金在泰) was set at 500 won.

As there were no further matters, the meeting was adjourned at 3:30 PM on the same day.

December 16, 1967
Chairman: Park Young-dae (朴鍈大)
Minutes Secretary: Park Tae-gyu (朴泰圭)
Witnesses: Choi Ik-don (崔益敦), Cho Gi-hwan (曹奇煥), Yu Nan-chul (劉蘭出)

Date and Time: December 17, 1968, 10 AM
Location: Residence of the village head Park Chun-woong (朴春雄)

Chairman: Advisory Committee Chairman Park Young-dae (朴鍈大)
Minutes Secretary:

Im Chun-chae (任春彩) called the roll, and upon confirmation of the quorum, Chairman Park Young-dae (朴鍈大) declared the meeting open.

*   The Chairperson (議長), Park Hwang-dae (朴瘓大), read out the minutes (會議錄) from the previous year (前年度).
*   Cho Jae-yeol (曹在烈) read out the village affairs (洞案).

The report was recorded in the separate volume (別册) of the village account book (村禊金錢出納簿). It was decided unanimously to cover the deficit (赤字金) with cash (現金) earned from the warehouse management business (倉庫保管業).
*   The following items were adopted for the agenda (會順):
    1.  Handling of pending matters (留案件) (Boundary measurement (境界測量) of Dong-yu-rim (洞有林), afforestation (植木) of Dong-yu-rim (洞有林) cultivated land (起耕地))
    2.  Amendment of village affairs (洞案)
    3.  The matter of village funds (里經費) and tax collection (稅收納)
    4.  The matter of village head (里長) election (選擧)
    5.  The matter of selecting the village administrator (有司)
    6.  Remarks from the village head (洞長)
    7.  Other discussion items (討議事項)
    8.  Declaration of adjournment (閉會)
*   In handling the pending matter (留案件) of boundary measurement (境界測量) of Dong-yu-rim (洞有林), it was decided unanimously to postpone it to the next year (明年渡) due to financial (財政) reasons.
*   In handling the pending matter (留案件) of Dong-yu-rim (洞有林) cultivated land (起耕地), it was decided, based on Park Yoon-seop's (朴允燮) suggestion, to proceed with afforestation (植木) in the following spring (明年春) and to have the villagers (部落民) participate (出役) on April 5th.
*   The amendment of village affairs (洞案) changed Article 17 of Chapter 4 from "The village head (里長) shall be elected every year (每年) in October (拾月)" to "The village head (里長) shall be elected on the day of village assembly (講信日)" (including officers (任員)). This was passed without objection.
*   The term of the village head (里長) was set from February 1st to January 31st of the following year (翌年), and the handover (引繼) between the new and old village heads (新舊里長) was set for February 1st. This was passed unanimously.
*   The election (選擧) schedule for the village head (里長) was passed, and it was decided to proceed with the election (選擧) based on the suggestion (勸議). The staff members (從事員) were decided to be Cho Jae-yeol (曹在烈), Lee Sang-keun (李尙根), and Jeong Yong-gi (鄭龍基), and this was passed unanimously. The election (選擧) method (方法) was decided to follow the village affairs (洞案) based on the chairperson's (委員長) suggestion, and this was passed without objection.
*   As lunchtime (中食) had arrived, it was decided unanimously to hold the village farmer (里農) election (選擧) after lunch (中食後). The adjournment (停會) was at 1:40 PM (午後1時40分).
*   After lunch (中食), the chairperson (委員長) declared the resumption (續會) at 2:30 PM (午後2時30分). The number of voters (投票人員) for the village head (里長) election (選擧) was 45. In the first round (一次投票), Lee Jun-ho (李俊浩) received 9 votes and Cho Jae-yeol (曹在烈) received 8 votes. In the second round (二次投票), Cho Jae-yeol (曹在烈) received 14 votes and Lee Jun-ho (李俊浩) received 29 votes. Lee Jun-ho (李俊浩) was declared the winner (當選) by the chairperson (委員長).
*   The advisory committee members (諮問委員) were decided through a list voting (連記名投票) system, and this was passed without objection. Park Jae-pyeong (朴在平) received 19 votes, Cho Jae-yeol (曹在烈) received 21 votes, Im Chun-chae (任春彩) received 16 votes, Park Yeong-dae (朴瑛大) received 14 votes, and Park Mun-sang (朴文相) received 11 votes. The five individuals (人) with the most votes (多點者) were declared the elected advisory committee members (委員) by the chairperson (委員長).
*   The selection (選定) of the village administrator (有司) was suggested by the village head (洞長) to be Jeong Yong-gi (鄭龍基), and this was passed unanimously.
*   It was decided to entrust (一任) the advisory committee members (諮問委員) with determining the village funds (里經費) for the year (年中) by referring to the village funds (里經費).
*   The monthly salary (月料) of the village head (里長) was decided to be collected (收集) on the 20th of this month (今月), with the ranking (等級) to be referred to from the past (從前). It was decided to entrust (一任) the collection (收集) to the new and old village administrators (新舊有司).
*   With all matters (案件) concluded, the adjournment (閉會) was declared at 4:20 PM (午後4時20分) on the same day (同日).

### Agenda

*   Election of the Ijang (里長) and Executive Members
*   Park Hyun-yong (朴鉉用) proposed that the Ijang (里長) should be elected by a committee system, where 3 candidates would be selected by the committee members and then voted on by all members. This was agreed unanimously.
*   The list of committee members is as follows:
    Jo Jae-yeol (曹在烈), Park Hyun-yong (朴鉉用), Jo Gi-hwan (曹奇煥), Kim Hong-su (金弘洙), Im Ok-am (任玉岩), Im Chun-chae (任春彩) - a total of 6 members.
*   For the election officials, the chairperson nominated 3 members as follows:
    Park Mun-sang (朴文相), Jo Jae-yeol (曹在烈), Choi Seong-rae (崔成來)
*   The committee members selected 3 candidates for the Ijang (里長) as follows:
    Park Jae-nyeon (朴在年), Im Chun-chae (任春彩), Jo Eun-sik
*   All 46 members voted, and the results were as follows:
    Park Jae-pyeong (朴在平) 26 votes, Jo Eun-sik 11 votes, Im Chun-chae (任春彩) 6 votes, invalid votes 3. Park Jae-pyeong (朴在平) was declared the elected Ijang (里長).
*   Regarding the selection of advisory committee members, Jo Jae-yeol (曹在烈) proposed that there should be 2 members over the age of 50, 3 members over the age of 30, and 2 members over the age of 20. This was agreed unanimously.
    The method for selecting advisory committee members was agreed to be by oral nomination, with unanimous approval.

The additional 2 members were Kim Byeong-ju (金炳柱) and Lee Dong-geun (李東根).
*   The date of the field survey was to be decided by consensus among the 9 members.

### Regarding the Rijang (里長) Election
1. In the Rijang (里長) election, there was a proposal from Jogi Hwan to reappoint the former Rijang (里長), and an objection from Bak Chunung (朴春雄) to proceed with a secret ballot (無記名) vote. The vote resulted in 12 votes for the proposal and 21 votes for the objection, with the objection carrying the majority and being passed without objection.
2. The ballot counters were Cho Eunsik, Yu Youngjin, and Lee Daegin. The results (41 voters) were: Cho Eunsik 14, Im Chunjae 15, Cho Jaeyeol 5, Baek Chunung 2, Jeong Jeongchae 1, Kim Youngchun 1, abstentions 3, total 41. As no candidate received more than half of the votes, a runoff was held between the top two candidates, Cho Eunsik and Im Chunchae, resulting in Cho Eunsik receiving 26 votes and Im Chunchae receiving 19 votes. Cho Eunsik was thus elected with a majority.

### Regarding the Selection of the Dongyurim Manager
The meeting resulted in the unanimous approval of Lee Donggeun (李東根) for the position. The matter of his remuneration was delegated to the Advisory Committee (諮問委員會).
*   The cultivation fee (耕作料) and land tax (里田稅) for Dongyurim will be collected on December 23.
There being no further business, the Chair declared the meeting adjourned at 4:45 PM.

This meeting was convened at 11:55 AM on December 21, 1973, at the residence of Village Head Lee Yunsu, with Park Gigu, the chairman of the advisory committee, presiding. Tasked with recording the minutes, Im Gwi-bae called out the names of the household heads. With 44 out of 65 household heads in attendance, the chairman declared the meeting open.

* New agenda discussion

The matter of selling the warehouse was decided by a subcommittee of three members, who agreed with the advisory committee to sell it. The decision was unanimously approved.

### O Amendment of Dongan

Article 20 of the Dongan was amended to extend the term of the Dongjang from 1 year to 2 years. However, re-election is allowed, and an additional term is possible, but no more than 3 years in total.

- **Warehouse (倉庫) Disposal Negotiation Committee (交涉委員)**: The following were selected: Park Yeong-dae, Lee Jun-ho, and Cho Jae-yeol.

# Jeollanam-do (全南) Muan County (務安郡) Cheonggye-myeon (淸溪面) Taebong (台峰) Village

## 1. Overview of the Village

### a. History (沿革)

- During the Joseon (李朝) Dynasty, the ancestor of the Pyo (表) clan, Pyo Hoe (表繪), established the village. Later, during the reign of King Sejo (世祖), royal family members took refuge here and buried the fetus of the Crown Prince (太子) on the mountain behind the village, which is why it was called Taebong (胎峰). Later, fearing misfortune, the character '胎' (fetus) was changed to '台' (platform), and the name Taebong (台峰) has been passed down to the present day.
- To defend against external enemies and prevent diseases, 50 paulownia trees were planted and maintained around the village, forming a scenic forest (風致林) today.

### b. Location (位置) and Conditions (與件)

**Location (位置)**

- Located 6 km from Muan County Office (務安郡廳) towards Mokpo (木浦) on the national road (國道) along the roadside (沿邊) at Guangmok Interval (光木間).
- Situated beneath Yudalsan (儒達山), famous for its auspicious location (明堂吉地), the village attracts spring appreciators (賞春客) and geomancers (地官) seeking good fortune (明堂) in spring.

**Conditions (與件)**

- The village is surrounded by rocky mountains (巖山) in the rear and expansive dark green fields in the front. A national road (國道) runs in front of the village, making it convenient for transportation (交通).
- The valley behind the village is lush with wild grasses (山野草), making it suitable for livestock farming (畜產). The village is also famous for its beautiful scenery (山水), attracting many visitors who come to bathe in the medicinal waters (藥水).

### c. Basic Status (基本現況)

## 2. Village Development Process (發展過程)

### a. Situation Before the 1970s (年代) (以前) (狀況)

#### 1) Basic Environment (基礎環境)

*   The small stream (小河川) flowing through both sides of the village meandered, causing flooding even with 50mm of rainfall (降雨).
*   The narrow paths along the stream had been used for 500 years (年) for passage, and the village's internal roads were so narrow that women carrying loads on their backs and men with shoulder poles could barely pass each other.
*   Except for the main family house (宗家집), all households (全戶) had thatched roofs (草家). After the harvest (秋收), the entire village would be bustling with thatching activities. However, non-farming households (非農家) had to re-thatch their roofs every three years (年), leading to roofs with sunken areas overgrown with weeds (雜草).
*   The farm roads (農路) were only wide enough for a cart to pass, with one path leading to the center of the fields.
*   The village entrance (入口) was occupied by a dilapidated community building (洞閣) that had deteriorated over 300 years (餘年) of wind and snow (風雪).

#### 2) Income Level (所得水準)

*   The village had inherited only 49.5 hectares of farmland (農地) from ancestors (祖上), and the primitive agriculture (原始營農) focused on rice and wheat (米麥) had not advanced.
*   The cultivated area (耕地面積) per household (戶當) was 0.5 hectares, and the annual income (年間) per household (戶當) was around 180,000 won (萬원).


--- (p. 686) ---

*   Apart from rice and wheat, livestock farming included raising 10 cattle and about 30 goats.
*   As cash crops, about 10 households grew tobacco to this extent, making it a poor village.

### Income Level in the 1970s
<Unit: Thousand Won>

| Business Name | Business Volume | Production Volume | Income | Remarks |
| :------------- | :-------------- | :--------------- | :------------- | :----------- |
| Grains | 37ha | 740 bushels | 11,430 | |

| Chili Peppers | 7 | 14,000 | 2,130 | |

| Income per Household | | | 380 | |

### 3) Living Conditions in the 1970s
#### a) Consciousness Structure
*   This village was poor but strongly influenced by Confucianism and conservatism, making it very reluctant to adopt new culture, with over 70% illiteracy.
*   Only 4-5 people attended school during the late Japanese colonial period, but only 2-3 graduated, indicating a low level of civilization.
*   However, this region was known as the yangban (two-class system) and had a tendency to look down on other clans.
*   Like other villages, alcohol and gambling were prevalent, often leading to the loss of land and causing family distress, especially in spring.
*   The village was also known for its weak administration due to its self-contained nature.
*   The dream of unity and development was non-existent.
*   Examples of conservatism include:
  1. Continuing the annual ritual of Dangsanje (堂山祭) for the Dangsan tree (poplar tree) even after the 1970s.
  2. Among non-farming households, 3 families made a living as shamans or similar professions.
#### b) Cultural Life and Daily Life
*   The residents, who lived by the light of oil lamps instead of electricity,
*   Had to endure the so-called "spring famine" (춘궁기), surviving on grass roots and tree bark in spring,
*   And could only afford to buy "Ssaet-gori" (샛거리), a type of long-grain rice, to feed their hungry families.
*   Especially on rainy days, they used gunny sacks or fertilizer bags instead of umbrellas to go to school.
*   About 20% of the village's non-farming households, who were extremely poor, relied on a few large farmers for their livelihood.
*   This village, where even seeing a newspaper or magazine was a luxury, had a youth reconstruction association established in 1962 that collected funds to purchase


--- (p. 687) ---

Radio was the sole medium for news.
* Most households' kitchens were as dark as cave interiors, and narrow rooms surrounded by earthen walls were always filled with foul odors.
* The straw mat doors and outhouses were so precarious that one wrong step could send you tumbling into the cesspit.
* The courtyard, piled high with straw ash, was a breeding ground for flies, mosquitoes, and filth, as fertilizer juices seeped out.
* Residents, unaware of how to manage sewage, dug ponds by the courtyard, leading to accidents where children would fall in, reflecting an extremely primitive living environment.
* Even as women returning from the fields ate cold barley rice with unwashed hands and faces, they lived as if in a terrestrial paradise.

## B. The Launch of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

### 1) Motivation and Achievements of the Pilot Project

* Before the curtain rose on the "Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)" proclaimed by President Park Chung-hee on April 22, 1970, a group of young people led by Kim Seong-hwan established the Rebuilding Youth Association (also known as the Harmony Pact) in 1962 to develop the village. However, they failed due to the residents' stubborn conservatism. When the Saemaul Undong began, this youth association became the driving force, easily embracing the movement.
* The Saemaul Undong pilot project implemented in 1971 yielded unexpectedly significant results. The residents' long-standing wish for a 1,500-meter farm road and an 890-meter village road expansion was successfully achieved.
* Of course, at that time, the Rebuilding Youth Association's funds and the village association's funds were used to partially compensate for the land, and the residents' excited emotions suppressed any opposition, allowing the project to proceed relatively smoothly.

### 2) Selection and Activities of Leaders

* After completing the first year's projects, the Rebuilding Youth Association recognized that more work lay ahead and resolved to elect new leaders through a general village meeting. They elected Hyob Sun-ryong, who was then the village head, as the leader and disbanded the Rebuilding Youth Association. The reasons for disbandment were financial exhaustion and conflicting opinions.
* At the time of the leader election, it was decided to change leaders annually. As shown in the following table, five leaders have guided the village over the years, fostering a competitive spirit to leave a lasting mark during their terms, driving continuous village development.
* In 1972, Leader Hyob Sun-ryong, who received support of 500 bags of cement and 1 ton of steel reinforcement, first convened the Development Committee to finalize the business plan. He then held a general village meeting to explain the plan but faced his first trial when residents refused to volunteer unless compensated for land, similar to the previous year.
* However, recognizing that if the Development Committee, organized by the village's central figures, could not proactively push forward planned projects—projects previously driven by the youth association—he felt he lacked the qualifications to be a leader and to live in the village.


--- (p. 688) ---

One by one, they began to engage in persuasion campaigns. Although the leader was able to secure agreement within 20 days by launching a begging campaign due to the lack of village funds and methods to raise a common fund, there were many residents who opposed the work during the initial stages, leading to several work stoppages. However, realizing that giving up would mean the village's dream would disappear forever, the leader visited opponents, offering them alcohol and cigarettes, and even issued promissory notes promising to pay them compensation. Through these trials, they were able to open 2,500 meters of farm roads, complete 620 meters of sewers, and 1,100 meters of immediate road improvements, which were then handed over to the next leader.

As the village changed its leader annually, each leader had their own stories of joy and sorrow, but all shared a great sense of pride and dignity. Each leader left behind historical artifacts for the village. The following table shows the turnover of Saemaul leaders and the main projects during their terms.

### ＜Saemaul Leader Turnover Status＞

| Period       | Name     | Activities                                                                                             |
| :----------- | :------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 71. 4〜72.12 | Bae Sun-yong | Creating a boom, farm roads, sewers, widening lanes                                                   |
| 73. 1〜73.12 | Bae Geum-nam | Community center, small streams, methane gas, sewer facilities                                        |
| 74. 1〜75.12 | Bae Cheol-woong | Roof improvements, small bridges, small streams, house improvements                                   |
| 76. 1〜77. 7 | Bae Seok-jun     | Saemaul factory, small bridges, simple water supply, warehouses, house improvements                 |
| 77. 8       | Bae Ung-gi     | Family circle projects                                                                              |

As seen in the table above, the village gradually developed with each passing year. However, it was from 1976 that the village developed dramatically and became known as the best village in the region. In 1976, Pyo Seok-jun, who was elected as the Saemaul leader, had been working as the general affairs section chief of Cheonggye-myeon but left his job due to family business circumstances and contributed greatly to the village's development as a Ri development committee member, assisting previous leaders.

In particular, Pyo Seok-jun was highly trusted as the head of the Pyo clan and had been a figure of respect among the youth. Although he tried to change the village's structure into a modern one by presenting his village development plan to the residents, it was not easy to gain their support as it was a distant plan. To gather the scattered minds of the residents, he started with easy tasks such as village cleaning and farm road maintenance, leading the 4H club members.

Before his election as the leader, during the previous four years of Saemaul, the village had completed basic environmental facilities such as internal roads, sewers, community centers, and small stream improvements. Major farm roads were almost opened, and in 1975, the village received a loan of 30 million won from the Saemaul Income Savings Bank for income-generating businesses, installing facilities such as 900 pyeong of peonies, small processing factories like milking machines, red pepper powder crushers, and rice cake making machines. In 1974, land consolidation and water facilities were also completed.


--- (p. 689) ---

### 3) Overcoming Challenges (隘路克服) Situation (狀況)

At that time, despite completing the construction of 22 new houses (棟) and the renovation of 12 old ones (棟), as well as the renovation of 63 auxiliary buildings (棟), and fully equipping the village with basic water supply facilities (簡易給水施設), the vision of building a standard rural community (標準農村) was realized, and income (所得) and production methods improved. However, there were still many challenges to overcome.

Additionally, two houses (棟) located along the village entrance road (進入路邊) had to be demolished to widen the road to 7 meters, and the village tavern (酒幕) had to be removed. There were countless tasks to be done.

To address these numerous challenges, the women's association (婦女會) was strengthened to support thrift and savings (節米貯蓄) and the operation of the women's purchasing and selling market (婦女購販場). Visits were made to households (家庭) selected for house renovations (家屋改補修) to assess their economic situation (經濟的) and offer hope (希望). Efforts were also made to secure land agreements (土地承諾) for the construction of new farm roads (農路新設), and despite neglecting household chores (家事), the villagers dedicated themselves day and night to village development (開發), even exploring loan options (融資) from the agricultural cooperative (農協), though with little success.

Just then, the second phase of the Yeongsan River Basin (榮山江流域) project, the Hagu Dam (河口堰) construction, began, and fortunately, the village was selected under the Yeongsan River Basin Standard Rural Village Development Plan (榮山江流域標準農村造成計劃) to receive 10 million won (千萬) in support. The villagers held a general meeting (住民總會) with a sense of relief and presented their blueprint (靑寫眞) again.

However, even with 10 million won (千萬), it was difficult to overcome all challenges. After allocating funds for joint projects (共同事業) such as the communal warehouse (共同倉庫), drying facility (乾燥場), small stream covering (小河川覆蓋), and simple water supply system (簡易上水道), only 200 million won (百餘萬) remained, leaving insufficient funds for house relocation and reconstruction (移改築) and demolition (家屋撤去).

Thus, it was decided that the villagers would directly manage all projects (直營) and use the earnings (賃金) to start house renovations (家屋改補修). It was promised that those lacking financial means (經濟的) would be provided with funds, and all planned projects were completed by June 30, 1977. Relocation and reconstruction (移改築分) were supported with 5 million won (萬), roof improvements (改良) with 2 million won (萬), and more funds were available for house demolitions (撤去家屋).

However, among the houses to be demolished, the tavern (酒店) stubbornly resisted, questioning whether depriving others of their right to live was part of the Saemaul Undong (新村運動). This led to a situation where, after enjoying the benefits, they refused to cooperate, like someone who has eaten their fill and then loses their nose.

To expand the women's association purchasing and selling market (婦女會購販場) and foster the village savings bank (金庫), a chairperson (理事長職) was appointed to increase membership. When all villagers resolved not to patronize the tavern (酒店), it naturally closed, allowing for its demolition and ending the days of drinking and idle chatter (雜談) there.

A leading figure (指導者) stated that if one always acts without personal bias (私心), is honest (正直), fair (公平), and transparent (隱弊), all villagers will naturally follow, feeling a sense of purpose in their work.

However, the leader's anguish (苦惱) stemmed from the unfulfilled promise of constructing 18 new houses (家屋新築棟分), leading to constant pressure from indebted villagers (住民) to fulfill the promise (約束履行). Despite repeated requests for support (支援) from the agricultural cooperative (農協) and the county (郡), no solution was found, and the leader had to borrow money on personal credit (自己信用) to partially fulfill the promise (約束).

Just then, the then Cheonggye Myeonlong (淸溪面長) resigned, and the local leaders (有志) unanimously agreed that Pyoseokjun (表錫俊), a capable leader (指導者), should be the successor (後任) for the village.


--- (p. 690) ---

Recommended as a qualified leader (長의 적격자), he was appointed as the Cheonggye-myeon (淸溪面) leader on August 1, 1978, and has remained in the position to this day.

### 4) Developmental Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (事業)

*   After Pyoseok-jun (表錫俊) took office as the leader, this village elected Pyoung-gi (表雄基) as the next leader.
*   Leader Pyoung-gi (表雄基) is following in the footsteps of Leader Pyoseok-jun (表錫俊) and is working diligently on home improvement projects, such as renovating toilets, kitchens, and livestock sheds.
*   Walls and roofs have been repainted, with the main building completed at 100%. Efforts are being made to increase residents' income through income-generating projects.
*   To expand the assets of the Saemaul Undong savings bank, which serves as the core of the Saemaul Undong, each household contributed 180 dou (斗) of rice per year, securing a fund of 42 million won (萬圓).
*   The scenic beautification of a small stream in front of the village and the planting of trees along the national road have further enhanced the village's appearance. Benches have been installed along the stream, providing a resting place to cool off from the hard work.
*   Along with the telephone (電化) project of that year, 40 TV sets have been introduced, elevating the cultural image of the village. Meanwhile, agricultural structures are being improved with the introduction of farming machinery such as plows, threshers, and power sprayers.
*   Now, alongside improvements in living environments and agricultural structures, the movement to cultivate a new spirit is in full swing. Events like filial piety banquets are being held to promote the spirit of loyalty and filial piety, transforming the village into a complete standard model. The past way of life has become like a myth.

## 6) Heartwarming Stories (美談佳話)

### a) Story 1 (第一話)

*   In 1972, along with the high spirit of the Saemaul Undong, the villagers' only gathering place and rest area, a 300-year-old dilapidated pavilion, began its repair work.
*   Pyobyeong-eon (表光彥), residing in Mokpo (木浦), donated 40,000 won in cash to greatly aid the pavilion's repair, and
*   In 1977, he donated 600 pyeong of fertile land as a gift, transferring it as communal property, and
*   During holidays, he would visit his hometown, hosting senior citizen banquets, among others, contributing greatly to the village's development and earning high praise from the residents.

### b) Story 2 (第二話)

*   In 1976, Pyoseok-jun (表錫俊), the Saemaul Undong leader, contributed 30,000 won in cash, uniting the residents' efforts, and
*   In 1977, he lent 120,000 won at simple interest to cover the shortfall in construction costs for 18 newly built houses, boosting morale.

### c) Story 3 (第三話)

*   In 1976, to promote the respect-for-the-elderly ideology, the village established the Nosung-dang (老成堂), and
*   In April 1977, centering around the Nosung-dang, they held a respect-for-the-elderly banquet, discovering and commending filial children, filial spouses, and virtuous individuals as follows.

## 7) Visits by Dignitaries (要人訪問) Situation (狀況)

* Starting from the first year of the Saemaul Undong, as the enthusiasm and motivation of the Saemaul movement were superior (優越) and various projects were proceeding smoothly, Park Jung-dong (朴重東) (current (現) Dong-gu Office (東區廳) Chief (廳長) of Gwangju (光州)), who was then the Internal Affairs Section Chief (內務課長) of the county, led the Saemaul leaders (指導者) in the jurisdiction (管內) for a study tour (見學).
* Many dignitaries (要人) visited, and in particular, the visit by Park Gyeong-won (朴璟遠), then Minister of Home Affairs (內務部長官), provided a significant opportunity (契機) for the Saemaul Undong.
* The village residents took pride (矜持) and developed a sense of self-esteem (自負心) as the village became a study tour site (見學場) not only for the county (郡內) but also for Saemaul leaders (指導者) from other cities and counties (他市郡).
