## 8) Special Items (特記事項)

a) Joyful Events

* When the Saemaul project (새마을事業) ended in 1972 and was evaluated as outstanding (優秀) in the county inspection (審査), and was promoted to one of the 9 self-reliant villages (自立마을) selected in the jurisdiction (管內)
* When Park Gyeong-won (朴璟遠), Minister of Home Affairs (內務部長官), visited and encouraged, promising the installation (設置) of a simple water supply (簡易上水道), and in 1973, when the simple water supply (簡易上水道) was installed (施設) and water came out from the water tap (水道꼭지)
* When Kim Hyeon-ok (金玄玉), Minister of Home Affairs (內務部長官), visited and encouraged, donating (寄贈) 5 rickshaws (臺) in 1973


--- (p. 694) ---

In the same year, Kim Bo-hyeon (金甫鉉), the governor, awarded the village with a commendation (村表彰).
When the Saemaul leaders (새마을指導者) from Mokpo City (木浦市) visited the village for a study tour and praised it, saying it was no less impressive than a city,
On the day in April 1977 when a senior citizen's festival was held and everyone, young and old, enjoyed the day happily, commending filial children, dutiful spouses, and virtuous individuals,
During the peak of the Saemaul Undong in 1977, when Park Geon-hong (朴建弘), the Mu'an County magistrate (務安郡守), visited to encourage the village and inspired them, saying that Daebong Village (台峰) would become one of the best villages in the country, and consoled the residents with a monetary gift (金一封),
And many other joyful moments during those seven years are too numerous to count.

## b) Sad Moments
When tearing down buildings on the village road, someone fiercely opposed and charged at the leader (指導者) with a spinning top,
When someone agreed to donate land for farm road construction but then opposed it at the site,
When a small bridge (小橋梁) built in front of the village collapsed due to technical insufficiency, causing a farm machine (耕耘機) to break and a person to be injured, leading to hospitalization, and the Saemaul leader (새마을指導者) was demanded to cover the hospital expenses (病院費),
When the constructors of 18 houses (棟) visited the leader (指導者) demanding the fulfillment of the promised loan (融資金) support, asking how they could live with only a house and debts,
And there were many other sad stories.

--- (p. 696) ---

## NoSeongDang (老成堂) Operation Rules

### Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of establishing NoSeongDang (老成堂) is to provide a place of rest for the elderly and to promote the spirit of respecting the elderly, thereby fostering a culture of reverence and affection, and constructing a cheerful and orderly welfare society.

### Article 2 (Members)
Members shall be men aged 50 or older residing in Taebong-ri (泰鳳里) (or those with connections). A few honorary members may be appointed.

### Article 3 (Officers)
The following officers shall be appointed to operate the association:
* Chairman (委員長) 1
* Vice Chairman (副委員長) 2
* General Affairs (總務) 1
* Advisors (顧問) A few
* Committee Members (委員) 3

### Article 4 (Election of Officers)
The Chairman (委員長) and Vice Chairman (副委員長) shall be elected from among the members, and the General Affairs (總務) and Advisors (顧問) shall be elected from among the members and honorary members. Election shall require the attendance of more than half of the members and the approval of two-thirds of those present.

### Article 5 (Term of Office)
The term of office for each officer shall be one year, with the possibility of re-election.

### Article 6 (Duties)
① The Chairman (委員長) shall represent the association (NoSeongDang) and be responsible for its operation.
② The Vice Chairman (副委員長) shall assist the Chairman (委員長) and, in the event of the Chairman's absence, the eldest member shall perform the duties of the Chairman (職務代理) for the remaining term.
③ The General Affairs (總務) shall assist the Chairman (委員長) and handle the affairs of the association.

### Article 7 (General Assembly)
The General Assembly shall consist of members and shall be divided into regular and extraordinary assemblies.
① Regular assemblies shall be held annually on a specified date.
② Extraordinary assemblies may be convened at any time by the Chairman (委員長) as deemed necessary.
③ Regular assemblies shall report on the settlement of accounts and progress reports.
④ The General Assembly may coincide with events (various events).
⑤ Minor matters in business shall be handled by the Board of Directors, with only progress reports to the General Assembly. Various business settlements shall be decided once a month at the Board of Directors meeting.
⑥ Decisions on the execution of various businesses shall be made with the attendance of a majority and the approval of a majority.

### Article 8 (Business)
The association may engage in the following businesses, in mutual agreement with the Development Committee (委員會):
① Social welfare (福祉) business
② Matters related to good customs (美風良俗)
③ Respect for the elderly (敬老) meetings
④ Youth guidance (善導) business
⑤ Introduction business (introduction of tangible and intangible property)


--- (p. 697) ---

### ⑥ Resident's Day Event
**Article 9** Articles 1, 2, 3, and 4 of Article 8 shall be carried out in accordance with the resolutions of the Executive Board and the General Assembly at that time.
**Article 10** Introduction business shall be carried out in accordance with the following regulations.
1. Income from real estate introduction fees
2. Income from movable property introduction fees
**Article 11** The Resident's Day event shall be carried out as follows.
1. The chairman shall consult with the village head and carry it out.
2. Resident's Day shall be held once a year.
3. Resident's Day shall award the following individuals:
   - Longevity Award: 1 person
   - Merit Award: 1 person
   - Respect Award: 1 person
   - Diligence Award: 1 person
   - Pioneer Award: 1 person
   - Filial Son Award: 1 person
   - Filial Daughter-in-Law Award: 1 person
4. Resident's Day may be combined with other events.
5. The selection of awardees shall be conducted by an evaluation committee elected at the General Assembly through secret ballot, and the majority vote shall decide the awardees.
**Article 12 (Finance)** The funds for operating expenses and business expenses shall be secured from the income of the business specified in Article 10, other income-generating businesses, and sponsorship funds, and may also be used for Saemaul Undong business expenses.
**Article 13 (Books and Documents)** The following documents shall be kept.
1. Bylaws
2. Minutes and resolution records
3. Financial statements and progress records
4. Accounting books
5. Membership roster
**Article 14** This bylaws shall be enacted after being approved by the General Assembly of the residents of Taebong-ri and affixed with signatures and seals, and shall come into effect simultaneously.
**Article 15** Any person who abuses or causes unreasonable situations with this bylaws shall be dealt with in accordance with a resolution.

**Supplementary Provisions**
**Article 1** The business specified in Article 10 shall not be conducted by anyone, regardless of their status. In unavoidable cases where an individual conducts introduction business, they shall remit the fees to the association, and the association may pay a collection fee of 30%.
**Article 2 (Remuneration)** Each executive member shall serve without remuneration. However, gratuities may be paid in accordance with a resolution.
**Article 3** To smoothly carry out the business specified in Article 10, a responsible person may be appointed for each region to handle reports and submissions.
**Article 4** All residents shall obligatorily report to smoothly carry out the business specified in Article 10 and shall comply with this bylaws, separately affixing their signatures and seals to a list.
*Note: Signature and seal may be omitted.*


--- (p. 698) ---

## Ba. Achievements from the Saemaul Undong (事業)

1) Spiritual Aspect (精神面)
- Through the Saemaul Undong (運動), a new consciousness structure (意識構造) was transformed with diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperation (協同).
- A new courage (勇氣) and self-confidence (自信感) were obtained with the saying "If you do it, it can be done."
- Democratic (民主的) capacity (力量) grew along with the dialogue (對話) square (廣場) through the residents' assembly (住民總會) and the neighborhood association (班常會).
- Savings spirit (貯蓄精神) was cultivated through the operation (運營) of the village safe (金庫), etc. (等).
- The basic (基本) ethical order (倫理秩序) was established by reviving the respect-for-the-aged ideology (敬老思想) along with the loyalty-and-filial-piety ideology (忠孝思想).

2) Living Aspect (生活面)
- A clean environment (環境) was created, allowing for a cultural (文化的) lifestyle (生活).
- Residents (住民) in modern villages (近代農村) are living with life information (生活情報) from various (各種) mass media (매스콤) such as TV, etc. (等).
- The structure (構造) of farming (營農) is being improved (改善) through the introduction (導入) of mechanized farming (機械營農) and modern (現代的) farming methods (農法).

3) Production Aspect (生産面)
- With the completion (完備) of land consolidation (耕地整理) and irrigation facilities (水利施設), agricultural production (農業生產) saw a groundbreaking (劃期的) development (發展) through the reform (改革) of farming techniques (營農技術) and seed renewal (種子更新), etc. (等).
- The cropping system (作付體係) was improved (改善), changing from single-cropping (一毛作) to double-cropping (二毛作) and improving (改善) the cultivation method (耕種法).
- Income (所得) has been improved (向上) through the breeding (增殖) of Korean cattle (韓牛), the expanded cultivation (擴大栽培) of high-quality vegetables (高等蔬菜栽培), and the cultivation of leaf tobacco (葉煙草), etc. (等).

4) Income Aspect (所得面)

# 3. Residents' Assembly (住民總會)

## ♦ Minutes of the Meeting (會議錄)(1)

*   **Date (日時)**: November 13, 1971
*   **Location (場所)**: Home of the village head, Bae Sun-yong
*   **Agenda (案件)**:
    1. Election of Saemaul Leader (새마을指導者)
    2. Election of Development Committee Members (開發委員)
    3. Business Plan for the Year 1972 (年度事業計劃)
*   **Attendees (參席人員)**: 72 out of 101 residents
*   **Officials in Attendance (任席官)**: Village officer in charge, Bae Seok-jun

**Village Head (里長)**: Declaration of Opening (開會宣言)
So far, we have done a lot for the development of our village, but to have more lively and proactive activities, we will first elect a Saemaul Leader (指導者).

**Bae Seok-keun**: Our village has many Bae family members, so the eldest in the Bae clan should naturally become the leader.

**Kim Seong-yeol**: Mr. Seok-keun's statement is a misunderstanding of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動). Rather than considering surnames (姓氏), it would be better to have a younger person who can work for the residents (住民) and the development of the village.

---Most agree with this statement---

**Village Head (里長)**: Then, we will seek recommendations from the relatively younger generation.

**Bae Yoon-soo**: Instead of recommending a new person, it would be better for the village head (里長), who has been doing a good job so far without any issues, to take on the role as well.

**Village Head (里長)**: That's a good idea. Then, let's seek another recommendation.

**Bae Jin-hyeong**: Currently, no one knows the village affairs better and can handle them as well as the village head (里長).

---Most agree with this---

**Village Head (里長)**: Is there any opposition?
If that's the case, I will do my best despite my lack of ability. However, from today onwards, we must abandon our previous lazy mindset and approach this with new determination.
Now, we will elect 8 Development Committee Members (開發委員) to work with the Saemaul Leader (새마을指導者).

**Bae Sun-seon**: Currently, we have 7 members from the Hwamokgye group. Let's just elect one more.

**Kim Seong-yeol**: That won't do.
Since the Saemaul Leader (새마을指導者) is also the village head (里長), we should elect new Development Committee Members (開發委員) as well.


--- (p. 700) ---

The Go Hwamokgye is dissolved as of today. Do not connect with this place.
Bae Seok-Geun: I recommend Bae Hak-Ryeong.
Bae Sun-Seon: I recommend Kim Seong-Yeol.
---Other majority recommendations---
Kim Seong-Yeol: Instead of doing this, let's delegate the election to the village head (里長) and have them select.
Bae Jeon-Yong: Since the Saemaul leader (指導者) and the village head must work together, it would be better to do it that way.
Village Head (里長): Then, I will report the matter of electing the development committee (開發委員) at the next meeting (會議). Also, the agenda includes establishing the 1972 business plan (事業計劃), which we will pass on to the next meeting (會議) after the development committee (開發委員) is elected.
---Saemaul leader (指導者) personnel remarks, closing declaration (閉會宣言).---

## Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (2)

Date (日時): December 25, 1972
Location (場所): Village Community Center
Agenda (議案):
1. Saemaul business settlement (事業決算)
2. Saemaul leader (指導者) replacement (交替)
Attendance (參席人員): 82 out of 97 total members

Bae Sun-Yong: We will hold a general village meeting (總會) to discuss the settlement (決算) of this year's Saemaul beautification business (事業) and the election (選出) of the next leader (指導者).

---Reading of the settlement report (決算報告書)---

This year, due to your active participation (參與), we were able to smoothly carry out the planned work. To complete the environmental improvement business (環境改善事業) in our village, we will need to work even harder. While we will strive to receive government (政府) support (支援) for the year 1973, it would be better to create a business plan (事業計劃) on our own and build a village that never rests. As stipulated in our regulations (規定), the Saemaul leader (指導者) should be elected annually, so please elect my successor (後任).
Bae Cheol-Yong: The leader (指導者) has worked hard this year for the Saemaul business (事業). Therefore, it would be better to rotate the leader (指導者) so that the burden is not on one person alone.
Bae Ung-Gi: Since the Saemaul business (事業) has just begun, it would be better for the incumbent (前任者) to work an additional year to create a model village (模範部落) within the county (郡內).
Kim Tae-Rang: Let's decide whether to continue (繼續) the current term. ---Former leader (前任者) Bae Sun-Yong exits.
Bae Seok-Jun: In that case, since there is opposition (反對), it would be better to replace (交替) the leader (指導者).
Kim Tae-Rang: Then, please let Bae Seok-Jun act as the temporary chair (司會).
Bae Seok-Jun: I will act as the chair (司會) according to your opinions (意見). Then, how should we elect (選出) the new leader (指導者)?
Bae Poong-Tae-Rang: Bae Geum-Nam would be good. ---All members (全員) agree (贊成).
Bae Geum-Nam: Let's discuss the personnel (人事) and the 1973 business plan (事業計劃) together.


--- (p. 701) ---

**Bae Seok-jun:** Next year, we should extend the village entrance road to 5m and widen the bridge as well. Completing the expansion of the inner road should be our top priority. All in favor.
**Bae Seok-jun:** We should compensate the former leader for his efforts. What do you think?
**Bae Yong-o:** Let's have the village head take responsibility and push forward within the range of 3,000 won. All in favor.
**Bae Seok-jun:** Declare the meeting closed.

### Meeting Minutes (3)

*   **Date:** December 15, 1976
*   **Location:** Leader's House
*   **Agenda:** Selection of Demonstration Village in the Yeongsan River Basin
*   **Attendees:** 70 people
*   **Chairperson:** Kim Tae-rang (Local Official)

**Chairperson:** First, please explain the reasons for selecting our village as the demonstration village in the Yeongsan River Basin and suggest directions for business selection. With a support of 10 million won, please share your opinions on village environment renewal.

**Leader Kwun Seok-jun:** We are grateful to the authorities for selecting our village as the demonstration village in the Yeongsan River Basin. We have 106 households, with 25 main buildings and 34 auxiliary buildings that have not undergone roof improvement. We should prioritize improving these structures. Additionally, demolishing the two houses located at the edge of the entrance road, covering the small stream in front of the community center, and installing a temporary water supply system are important tasks.

**Bae Geum-nam:** While the leader's suggestion is good, our village is large but lacks a village warehouse. I suggest using this opportunity to build a 50-pyeong warehouse for grain storage to generate income.

**Bae Deok-gu:** What about government support for roof improvement?

**Chairperson:** For main buildings, there is a loan of 20,000 won and a subsidy of 10,000 won per building.

**Bae Dong-il:** What about auxiliary buildings?

**Chairperson:** Those are self-funded. (Attendees: Then it will be difficult to improve them.)

**Leader:** I would like to ask the chairperson. If we add our self-funded portion to the 10 million won, can we decide on our village's long-awaited projects along with environmental improvement and submit them to the authorities for review and decision? What do you think?

**Chairperson:** That's a good idea. We should certainly carry out the residents' long-awaited projects while aligning the business plan with the government's sensibilities.


--- (p. 702) ---

**Minutes of the Meeting (4)**

| Item               | Details                              |
| :----------------- | :----------------------------------- |
| Date               | October 2, 1975                     |
| Venue              | Village Community Center (會舘)      |
| Agenda             | Saemaul Savings and Credit Union (所得金庫) Business (事業) |
| Attendees          | 31 people (11 absent)               |
| Chairperson        | Bae Cheol-yong (裵哲容)             |

**Chairperson (司會):** I apologize for calling this late-night meeting after a long day of harvesting. I know you must all be tired.

Tonight, we need to discuss the matter I raised with the town mayor during my visit to the town office. I asked if there was any way our village could receive support for starting an income-generating business (所得事業). The mayor said he would discuss it with the county Saemaul Undong (新村運動) office and get back to me.

**Village Head (里長):** Bae Chung-tae, let's decide on each project one by one. (All participants agree)

**Bae Cheol-yong:** Earlier, the leader mentioned that we need to demolish two houses along the access road. Do you think those residents will agree?

**Leader:** Those residents didn't attend today's meeting, but we should persuade them for the sake of our village's future and offer appropriate compensation. Now, let me share my thoughts on this.

- Demolition of houses: 400,000 won (萬원) per house
- Roof improvement: 20,000 won (萬원) subsidy per house
- Demolition of ancillary buildings: 10,000 won (萬원) subsidy per building

Let's draw up a business plan based on these points. (All agree)

**Leader:** We will decide on the business expenses (事業費) through consultation with the authorities and finalize the scope of work today. Then, we will adjourn the meeting.

- Road widening: 120m
- Wall improvement: 250m
- Sewer repair: 290m
- Roof painting: 69 houses
- House improvement: 22 houses
- House repair: 13 houses
- Ancillary building repair: 34 buildings
- Temporary water supply facilities: 65 units (40 units already installed)
- Small stream improvement: 1,000m
- Small stream covering: 30m
- Community warehouse: 50 pyeong (1 unit)
- Community drying facility: 200 pyeong

We plan to decide on these matters, so please share your opinions. (All agree)

Then, tomorrow (來日), I will go to the town (面) to decide on the business expenses (事業費) and other matters, and we will hold another meeting upon my return. With that, I will conclude today's meeting.

**Minutes of the Meeting (會議錄) (4)**


--- (p. 703) ---

We have received a notice stating that we will be provided with a loan (融資金) from the Saemaul Undong Fund. We are to select and apply for a community-based income-generating business that suits our village conditions. Today, we need to decide on a business to undertake with approximately 3 million won in loan funds. The interest rate is 3% per annum, with repayment options of 2 years deferred and 3 years equal installments, or 1 year deferred and 2 years equal installments. Please suggest a good business idea that can receive support, keeping in mind that it must be a community-based business.

**Baek Geumnam**: The Baek clan has 1,000 pyeong of land for sale. What do you think about purchasing it for our village?

**Chairperson**: That method could be good, but I heard that existing land (旣成沓) is not allowed. The policy is to find new sources of income. Reclamation is good, but is there any suitable land for reclamation in the Baek clan's mountainous area?

**Baek Geumnam**: There are mountains, but no land suitable for reclamation.

**Kim Taerang**: What about purchasing or building a storage facility for the village's agricultural cooperative?

**Baek Seokjo**: The agricultural cooperative will not sell its storage facility. Currently, there is a shortage of storage facilities, isn't there? Even if we build one, there won't be any grain left to store after depositing it in the cooperative's facility. If we receive the loan, we will have to repay the principal and interest, but without generating income, I think it's not a good idea.

*(Majority agrees)*

**Baek Unggi**: Our village is a plain, suitable for medicinal herb cultivation. What about growing medicinal herbs? I heard that cultivating Coptis chinensis is profitable.

**Chairperson**: Well, I have also considered medicinal herbs, but since we don't have communal land, it's difficult to run a community-based business. I'm hesitant.

**Baek Unggi**: What if we have each individual cultivate Coptis chinensis and contribute a percentage of the profits to the village? In other words, we can make it a community effort by having individuals cultivate it on behalf of the village, increasing residents' income and creating a village fund at the same time. Wouldn't that be good?

**Chairperson**: What do you all think?

**Baek Geumnam**: I think that would be a good idea.

**Kim Taerang**: I think it would be better to establish a small Saemaul factory in our village. For example, oil pressing, rice pounding, and red pepper powder are all needed in households at any time. If we establish such facilities in our village, women won't have to go to the town, and people from other villages will also come, increasing our village's income. Wouldn't that be good?

**Chairperson**: Both medicinal herbs and oil pressing factories are good ideas. (Residents' opinions are unanimous)

**Chairperson**: Then, what if we split the support amount in half and try both the medicinal herb cultivation and the Saemaul factory?

**Kim Taerang**: It would be good to have two types of income-generating businesses. First, let's assess the required funds for the oil pressing factory facilities, and then use the remaining funds for the Coptis chinensis business. I checked, and it will cost approximately 2.5 million won to establish a Saemaul factory (as previously mentioned).

**Chairperson**: Then, let's start by accepting applications from farming households hoping to cultivate Coptis chinensis here, within a budget of approximately 1 million won.


--- (p. 704) ---

Let's discuss this. A few days ago, someone bought some from Seoho Village, and they say it costs 150 won per copy. Please speak up if you have any hopes regarding this. (Baek Geumnam (裵錦男) and 16 others: 8,000 copies = 1,200,000 won (萬圓))

O For the mulberry business (事業), if 1,200,000 won (萬圓) is needed, we have an additional 1,800,000 won (萬圓) left. If we use 700,000 won (萬圓) from the village fund (基金) to cover the shortfall (不足金), what do you think? (All in favor (全員贊成))

Baek Geumnam (裵錦男): If we entrust the cultivation (委託栽培), what percentage of the profit (利益金) should we give to the village? Please make a decision.

Chairperson (司會): In my opinion, would 30% be appropriate? What do you all think?

Kim Taerang (金泰浪): We need to repay the principal and interest (元利金) for the mulberry cultivation (栽培), but 30% is too much. 20% would be better.

Baek Geumnam (裵錦男): I also plan to cultivate mulberries (栽培), but 30% of the profit (利益金) is too much. I think 20% would be sufficient.

Baek Dongil (裵東一): Then, it would be best to decide on 20%.

Kim Taerang (金泰浪): Let's have the Development Committee (開發委員會) make a detailed decision (決議) on this tomorrow. It's getting late, so let's adjourn the meeting.

Residents (住民): Alright.

Chairperson (司會): It's late, so let's end the meeting today. The detailed plans for the Saemaul factory (工場) construction (建立), the contractual relationship (契約關係) with herbal (藥草) farming households (農家), and the supply of seedlings (苗木供給) will be discussed and promoted by our village Development Committee (開發委員會). Please be careful not to make any mistakes.

Residents (住民): We will follow the decision (決議) of the Development Committee (開發委員).

Chairperson (司會): Then, let's conclude the meeting. Thank you.

Now, I will report on the matters decided with the local authorities (面當局) regarding the Yeongsangang (榮山江) Demonstration Village (示範마을) business (事業) at the general meeting (總會) on the 15th.

### Village Improvement Projects

- Roof painting: 30 households (楝)
- Subsidiary building renovation: 34 households (楝)
- Farm road construction: 2,000 meters
- Purchase and sale facility: 10 pyeong (坪)
- Village tree planting: 500 trees (本)
- Access road expansion: 150 meters

We have decided on these projects. What are your opinions?

**Gon Cheol-yong (袞哲容):** The matters passed in the previous meeting have no objections, but I am concerned about the economic burden on those who will improve their houses.

**Gon Gwang-woong (袞光雄):** This time, my house (hotel (酒店)) should be excluded from the demolition (撤去) target. In fact, I have nowhere to go, and if my livelihood (生計) is blocked, I will have no choice but to die. Please consider this.

**Gon Ung-gi (袞雄基):** I understand Gwang-woong's (光雄) position, but this is a matter for the entire village, so a minority (小數) must sacrifice (犧牲).

(At this point, a dispute between Gwang-woong (光雄) and Ung-gi (雄基))

**Leader (指導者):** Be quiet. It's not that we are depriving Gwang-woong (光雄) of his livelihood (生計). How about leasing the new purchase and sale facility (購販場) we are building to run a business? We are considering this idea. What do you think?

**Bae Jeon-yong:** Then, shouldn't a contract (契約) with the village be established?

**Leader (指導者):** Of course (勿論), it should be. That must be done after the house is completed. Let's discuss it at that time. For now, please gather your opinions. (Participants (參席者) agree (同意))

**Bae Gwang-woong:** I cannot answer, so I will say "Do as you please" and leave.

**Leader (指導者):** Then, are there any objections to the decision on the main project (本事業)?

**Bae Poong-taerang (배豊太郎) (Village head (里長)):** Please answer clearly. You cannot say anything different later.

**Geum Taerang (金太郎):** In my opinion (生覺), the problem is house reconstruction (改築). It would be good to support (支援) those who reconstruct (改築) their houses from the support fund (支援金). What do you think?

**Leader (指導者):** For those who reconstruct (改築) their houses, 50,000 won (萬) per household (楝) will be provided, and for those who demolish (撤去), 400,000 won (萬) will be provided.

**Kim Young-tae:** In fact, I am the most troubled person, but I will reconstruct (改築) for the sake of the entire village (全體).

(At this point, it was agreed (合意) by all)

**Leader (指導者):** Since there are no further objections (以上), the business plan (事業計劃) is passed. (Everyone (全員) applauds (拍手))

**Leader (指導者):** Next, we need to organize (組織) and improve (整備) the management of the Saemaul savings bank (金庫) for its operation (運營). First, please elect the board of directors (理事陣). The board of directors (理事陣) will consist of 1 chairman (理事長), 1 vice chairman (副理事長), 2 credit committee members (與信委員), 2 management committee members (運營委員), 2 guidance committee members (敎導委員), 2 auditors (監査), and 1 accountant (會計員).

**Bae Soon-yong:** No matter who does it, the chairman (理事長) should be the leader (指導者). (Everyone (全員) applauds (拍手))

**Bae Jin-young:** Rather than that, the leader (指導者), village head (里長), and development committee members (開發委員) should form a camp (陣營) and announce it. We will follow as it is announced. (Everyone (全員) agrees (贊成) At this time, a meeting of the elders (鳩首會談))

**Leader (指導者):** Then, I will announce the board of directors (理事陣). Chairman (理事長) Gon Seok-jun (袞錫俊), Vice Chairman (副理事長) Gon Soon-yong (袞順龍), Credit Committee Chairman (與信委員長) Gon Geum-nam (袞錦南), Management Committee Chairman (運營委員長) Bae Poong-taerang (배豊太郎), Guidance Committee Chairman (敎導委員長) Gon Ung-gi (袞雄基), Auditors (監査) Gon Yoong-tae (袞융태), Gon Cheol-yong (袞哲容), Accountant (會計員) Gon Seok-chae (袞錫彩) are appointed (定).

**Minutes of the Meeting (6)**

**Date:** March 5, 1977
**Location:** Village Leader's House
**Agenda:** Expansion of the Village Road
**Attendees:** 53
**Chairperson:** Leader

Leader: We have 890,000 won in support funds and need to raise another 890,000 won through self-reliance for the village road expansion project. How should we proceed?

Village Leader: I suggest we cover the self-reliance portion through labor contributions and allocate 50% of the support funds for wages once the work is recognized as progress. (All attendees agree)

Leader: How many days per household should we allocate for labor contributions?

Bae Geumnam: Considering the current practice of bringing lunch, we should allocate 5 days per household, implemented by class. This will ensure efficiency and prevent overcrowding. (All attendees agree and the proposal passes)

Leader: We need some form of penalty for those who do not participate in labor contributions.

Bae Unggi: Rather than penalties, let's encourage voluntary participation. For those who oppose, let's have the development committee, leader, village leader, and all attendees persuade them to participate.

Leader: To efficiently cover the self-reliance portion and address the support fund project, the actual distance is about 1,500 meters, which presents many challenges.

Village Leader: Rather than just doing 1,500 meters, let's push forward as much as we can. This is our village's long-standing wish, so let's start off on the right foot.

Leader: Any further comments or references?

Attendees: No objections.

Leader: This concludes today's meeting. Thank you.

# Minutes (會議錄) (7)

Date(日時): 77. 8. 16.
Location(場所): Village Hall (會舘)
Agenda(會議案件): Selection of Leader (指導者)
Attendees(參席者): Bae Jin-young and 5 others (名)
Chairperson(司會): Pyo Gwang-woong (表光雄)

Village Head(里長): Let us elect a Saemaul Leader (指導者) who can contribute to the development of our village.
Chairperson(司會): Then, how should we elect the leader (指導者)?
Village Head(里長): It would be best to elect by oral nomination (口頭呼薦) if the majority (多數) agree that someone is suitable. Of course (勿論), it is a burdensome task. But everyone should be willing to serve the village at least once, and there should be no opposition (反對) even if nominated.
(Unanimous (全員) applause in agreement (贊成))
Chairperson(司會): Then, let's proceed with oral nomination (口頭呼薦). Please make your nominations.
Gon Jeong-seok (衮正錫): Since there is not much time left in the term (任期), let's elect the former leader (舊指導者), Pyo Cheol-yong (表哲容), as the leader (指導者).
(At this time, the nominee (本人) objects (反對))
Gon Ung-gi (袞雄基): There are about 7 months (個月) left in the term (任期), and administrative matters (行政事項) need to be consolidated (綜合), so I suggest the Village Head (里長) should take on the role concurrently (兼任).
Village Head(里長): According to the village rules (里規則), the Saemaul Leader (指導者) should be a different person each term (任期), so a new leader (指導者) must be elected, and the Village Head (里長) cannot take on the role concurrently (兼).
Gon Tae-u (衮太佑): Three opinions (意見) have been presented. Let's decide by secret ballot (秘密投票).
Chairperson(司會): Since everyone is hesitant and modest, we will decide by secret ballot (秘密投票).
(At this time, a secret ballot (秘密投票) was conducted, and the Village Head's (里長) opinion (意見) was passed (可決))
Chairperson(司會): According to the Village Head's (里長) opinion (意見), please nominate (呼薦) someone who is not the Village Head (里長) and has not been a leader (指導者) before.
Gon Tae-u (衮太佑): I nominate Pyo Ung-gi (表雄基).
Gon Geum-nam (衮錦南): I agree (同意).
Bae Woong-tae: I second (三請) the nomination.
Chairperson(司會): There is a second (三請) for Pyo Ung-gi (表雄基), so he is nominated (呼薦者).
Gon Jeong-seok (衮正錫): I nominate Pyo Gwang-woong (表光雄).
Chairperson(司會): Then, those who agree with Pyo Ung-gi (表雄基) please raise your hands (擧手).
(More than 2/3 (3分の 2) of the attendees (參席人員) raised their hands (擧手), and it was passed (通過))
Chairperson(司會): According to the majority (多數) opinion (意見), we hereby declare Pyo Ung-gi (表雄基) as the elected Saemaul Leader (指導者).

# 4. Future Development Vision (發展構想)

## 1) Income Increase (所得增大)
First, in rice production (米穀生產), we will expand the cultivation of high-yield unified strain (統一系) rice to 100% and aim for the perfection of mechanized farming (機械營農).
Second, through Korean beef cattle breeding (韓牛育成), we will raise at least two heads (頭) per household (戶當) and establish Korean beef cattle farms (韓牛團地).
Third, we will expand the cultivation of special crops (特用作物) such as onions, tobacco leaves (葉煙草), and spinach to increase income (所得) from economic crops (經濟作物).
Fourth, we plan to expand medicinal herb (藥草) harvests in 1979 and small-scale factories (小規模工場) to build Saemaul factories (工場) by 1980. Meanwhile, non-agricultural income (農外所得) is expected to exceed 3 million won (萬圓) per household (戶當所得) by 1980.

## 2) Welfare Facilities (福祉施設)
First, we will expand the current village hall (會舘) into a two-story building (二層) and develop it into a comprehensive welfare center (綜合施設) equipped with various facilities (諸般).
Second, we plan to promote telephone installation (電話架設) in 1979 to ensure smooth communication (通信手段).
Third, with the successful operation of a 1,200-pyeong (坪) communal farm (共同畓), income from Saemaul warehouses (倉庫收入), small-scale factories (小規模工場收入), and purchasing and selling markets (購販場收入), we plan to establish a village scholarship fund (獎學會) to contribute to the education of future generations (後世養成). We will strive to keep the flame of today's prosperity (繁榮) burning forever (永遠).

## 3) Environmental Improvement (環境改善)
First, we will modernize household facilities (家庭圈事業) such as toilets (便所), kitchens, and livestock sheds (畜舍), and each household (家庭) will maintain flower beds (花壇). We will promote a culture of cleanliness (淸掃) to create a constantly clean environment (環境).
Second, we will focus on the protection and management (保護管理) of Saemaul facilities (施設物). The village-wide projects (圈事業) will be nearly completed.

## 4) Spiritual Development (精神啓發)
With the established senior citizens' association (老成堂) as the center, we will foster loyalty and filial piety (忠孝思想) and promote participation in various educations (敎育) and the operation of neighborhood associations (班常會). We will elevate ethical (倫理的) foundations to modern (近代的) thinking (思考) and strive to build a proud Taebong (台峰) with cultural pride (文化人).
Next, we will further develop the village savings bank (金庫) to create self-reliance (自立) on the Taebong (台峰) land and establish self-owned assets (自體資產) to eliminate the need for external funding (資金). We will make every effort to achieve this.


--- (p. 709) ---

# Ga-dong Village, Ga-un 2-ri, Dasi-myeon, Naju-gun, Jeollanam-do

## 1. Overview of the Village

### a. History

The village is located on the site of a former temple, part of the 200 or so hermitages of Bogwangsa Temple, which was founded in the first year of King Mu-yeol of Silla (AD 156). During the Joseon Dynasty, when anti-Buddhist sentiment was at its height, all the hermitages were burned down and only one remained, hidden by thickets and forests. This hermitage has been passed down to the present day and is now Bokamsa Temple. It is said that during the mid-Joseon period, when political factionalism was at its peak, a scholar from the Naju Lim clan took refuge here and the village was formed.

In September 1973, a resettlement complex for families whose homes were demolished along the national highway was formed in the southern part of the village. 20 households moved there collectively, and the village experienced a period of great turmoil.

### b. Location and Conditions

#### ＜Location＞

The village is located along the national highway and railway between Gwangju and Mokpo, 8km from Naju-eup, the county seat, towards Mokpo. As you pass along the Gwangju-Mokpo national highway, you will see a village with a straight, open entrance surrounded by mountains, a towering village community center, and beautifully maintained roofs and walls, giving a very impressive impression.

#### ＜Conditions＞

As a mountainous village, the arable land per household is small. Moreover, the farmland is mostly gravelly loam with steep slopes and poor irrigation facilities, so the village has long relied on rain-fed farming and has not been able to escape poverty.

## 2. Village Development Process (發展過程)
### a. Situation Before 1970 (70年 以前 的 狀況)
#### 1) Basic Environment (基礎環境)
The village was not densely clustered in one location but was scattered across five different areas, with the farthest distance being 1.5km apart, making it geographically difficult to consider it as a single village. Most of the 38 households lived in thatched houses that seemed ready to collapse at any moment. There were no proper farm roads, nor was there any maintained access road to the village; one had to traverse 1.5km of winding paths along the edges of rice paddies from the national road. The only water source, the village well, was a place where water bugs thrived during the summer.


--- (p. 711) ---

## 2) Income Level (所得水準)
The land, even if called farmland (田沓), was neither fertile nor equipped with sufficient irrigation facilities (水利施設), resulting in significant damage even from slight rainfall. The average yield per unit (單位當) across the nation (全國) was far from being met. Residents (住民) did not even consider cultivating crops (作物) other than barley (麥), relying solely on selling firewood from the mountains to the market in Yeongsanpo (榮山浦), 8km away, as their only sideline (副業). The average annual income (平均所得) per household (戶當) was 325,000 won (千원), making it one of the poorest villages in Naju County (羅州郡).

## 3) Living Conditions in 1970 (70년도(年度)의生活狀態)
### a) Consciousness Structure (意識構造)
Even within the small village, class consciousness (階級意識) was extremely pronounced, differentiating the banjang (班常). Residents (住民) would rush to any opportunity for food or drink, often getting drunk and causing a spectacle from broad daylight. Women (婦女者), having little to do, would spend their days gossiping about others, which was almost a daily routine. From the village elders to the youth (靑年), gambling (노름) was rampant, making it difficult to distinguish between farming (農事) as the main occupation (本業) or gambling. Moreover, disputes (是非) arising from gambling often led to physical altercations between the elderly (老人) and the youth (靑年), with reason (道理) being scarce.

Thus, despite living in ignorance (無知) and poverty (貧困), there was no ambition (慾望) to improve their lives. Young people who thought about the future (將來) would leave the village in droves, seeking employment (雇傭) in urban areas (都會地) or even moving to the capital (上京). Those who had not yet left dreamed of escaping to the city (都會地) as their greatest wish (所望).

### b) Culture (文化) and Clothing, Food, and Shelter (衣食住) Life (生活)
The village's cultural facilities (文化施設) were limited to a single gramophone (蓄音器) and three radios (收音機), with no access to newspapers (新聞) or books (册). There wasn't even a single traditional Korean house (東角) to be found. Electricity (電氣) was unthinkable, and living by the light of an oil lamp (호롱불) was considered fate (宿命). Amidst the struggle to make ends meet, no one could afford to wear clean and tidy clothes (衣).

During the hungry spring (春窮期), often referred to as "borigoe" (보리고개), residents would scramble to obtain long-grain rice (長利쌀) just to survive. Even selling firewood (나무짐) on time was crucial for daily sustenance (延命). Life was that harsh.


--- (p. 712) ---

Until then, people could barely maintain even the minimum standards of human life. Creating a clean and hygienic living environment seemed like a distant dream for the villagers.

## II. The Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

### 1) Motivation and Achievements of the Pilot Project

Since President Park Chung-hee first proposed the Saemaul Undong in April 1970, advocating for ideal and prosperous villages, the movement's fervor began to spread across the nation. The government supported this village with 335 bags of cement as a pilot project. However, the village head and other leaders at the time were more concerned with personal gain than the community's collective interests. The 335 bags of cement disappeared without a trace, with no clear record of how they were used. The villagers remained self-centered, with no sense of cooperation, and the village was filled with selfishness.

As late as 1973, the ignorant and backward villagers showed no signs of awakening. While the Saemaul Undong burned like wildfire across the country, this village remained an exception. In September 1973, as part of the government's project to improve independent houses and substandard housing along national roads, 20 households were relocated to the southern part of the village. Most of these newcomers were urban day laborers struggling to make a living, bringing even more poverty to the already impoverished village. The existing villagers treated the newcomers as subhuman, ignoring them completely. The newcomers, in turn, were consumed by extreme individualism and blind dependence on others.

The village's only bar was packed from early morning, with people drunk in broad daylight. Gambling soon escalated into large-scale betting, attracting gamblers from as far as Gwangju in the evenings.

### 2) Election of Leaders and Their Activities

Im Jeong-sun, a university graduate who had moved to the city after marriage but felt disillusioned with urban life, decided to move to her hometown with the relocated residents, hoping to build a modest home. She and her husband, Park Young-seon, another leader, arrived in the village, only to find their new homes standing alone, without toilets, wells, or fences. Treated with contempt by the existing villagers, they spent several days in self-deprecation and sighs, wondering if this was truly a place for human habitation. Determined to change the situation, they recalled the warm and friendly village of their childhood and decided to bring the light of the Saemaul Undong to this village, making it a true community. First, the couple decided to ban alcohol and gambling from the village and began to unite the women.


--- (p. 713) ---

As fellow immigrants (移住民), they had to endure the same hardships (苦痛) and faced the same struggles as their husbands (男便) squandered their spirits (精神) on alcohol and gambling, threatening their very livelihoods (生計). This shared empathy (以心傳心) made it easy for them to unite. However, the established village women (旣存婦女), who had suffered greatly at the hands of these immigrants (移住民) and regarded them as beneath human dignity (人以下), were impossible to approach with such ideas.

Leader Im (林) was convinced that if they could fully unite these immigrants (移住民) and raise their living standards (生活水準) to match those of the established residents (旣存住民), the latter would naturally join in. On November 19, 1973, she organized a women's association (婦女會) and became its leader (指導者) herself.

The women (婦女會員) vowed that even if their husbands (男便) remained as they were, they would strive to live differently, seeking a path to a better tomorrow (來日). After achieving this, they would redouble their efforts to alleviate the pain of their village, which resembled a miniature (縮少版) of their divided homeland (分斷祖國), and break the cycle of mutual contempt (相互輕視) between established residents (旣存住民) and immigrants (移住民), becoming a strong and complete bridge (橋梁) uniting the entire community (住民總和).

Leader Im (林) first gathered a women's association fund (婦女會基金) of 6,000 won, with each member contributing 300 won personally (個人出資), and started a mobile market (移動購販場). In an attempt to draw their husbands (男便) away from the bars, they set up alcohol at the market (購販場), which indeed increased the market's profits (利益金). However, this merely resulted in two bars operating in the village, creating a situation where the entire community was drunken.

Leader Park Young-seon (朴英仙) seized every opportunity to gather the immigrants (移住民) and persuade them that even if they accepted poverty (貧困) as their fate (宿命), they should at least live their lives (生活姿勢) with dignity (悧悧), not envying others (南部慾). However, their extreme (極度) despair and lazy attitudes (生活態度) showed no signs of changing easily.

### 3) Overcoming Difficulties (隘路克服狀況)

* As the women's association fund (婦女會基金) grew and the husbands' (男便) continuous persuasion (說得) began to show some effect on their mental state (精神狀態), Leader Im (林) thought it was time to instill the Saemaul spirit (精神) in the village children (兒童) first. The children of these immigrants (移住民), like colts freed from their harnesses (韁), were left to their own devices (任意) all day due to their parents' (父母) neglect (無關心) and extreme poverty (極貧生活). They would eat sweet potatoes (고구마) from any field they pleased and pick persimmons (柿子) from trees, becoming seeds of discord (不和의 씨앗) between established residents (旣存住民) and immigrants (移住民). From the mouths of these children, who should be using polite language (禮貌語), came unmentionable vulgarities (上所語).

* A couple (夫婦) who had set up a children's study room (兒童學習房) in their own home (自己家) began to gather the village children (村兒童) one by one. In the evenings, they helped the children with their homework (宿題), read them interesting fairy tales (童話), and sang beautiful nursery rhymes (童謠) together, gradually teaching them about the Saemaul spirit (精神) of diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperation (協同), and what it means to be a good child (善兒童). From then on, the sound of children's bright and pure choir (合唱) echoed through the night sky in Gadong village (佳洞), seeping into the windows (窓) of the established village residents (旣存住民) and drawing their children (兒童) to join in as well. Around the same time, incidents of people losing things in the mountains (山) or fields (田) disappeared, and emboldened (勇氣), the couple (夫婦) launched a campaign (運動) to "save money by not eating snacks and having a single bankbook (通帳)." The children learned to save even a single 10-won bill (十圓), and discarded snack wrappers (飴包裝紙) could no longer be found lying around on the streets (街).

* To hold a general village meeting (住民總會), whenever the children's study room (兒童學習房) was off, the children would pester (請求) their parents (父母) all day to attend (參加) the meeting (會).


--- (p. 714) ---

The meetings were always full.
The O couple leaders, after hearing about successful Saemaul cases from Saemaul Magazine and the radio, finally established their path as leaders. They realized that without transforming the residents' unlimited dependence on authorities, their laziness, and their acceptance of poverty as fate, and without designing a future, it would take 100 years for the village to become prosperous. At every meeting, they conducted spiritual education, emphasizing the possibility of overcoming poverty and living well, and urged everyone to return to square one, be reborn, and live with diligence and cooperation towards a proud tomorrow.

Gradually, the residents' awareness and thoughts began to change. They cooperated to install a shared well and laundry area, and helped each other build additional buildings. The residents felt the joy of cooperation for the first time, and especially the women, who now had a laundry area nearby, seemed to gather more often centered around the women's association.

As the living environment improved with the addition of toilets and additional buildings, the residents developed a sense of attachment to their homes, and the frequency of drinking decreased. Their spiritual attitudes also improved with continuous education, but they couldn't become new people overnight.

- Even when the couple leaders tried to build a wall around their own house first, most of the residents protested, saying, "If we just leave it, the government will take care of everything. Why should we build a wall with our own strength and prevent others from receiving government support?"

However, the couple leaders did not yield. They gathered like-minded young people and, together with the women's association, organized a youth association to lead the Saemaul movement. They improved a 150m stream and a 200m farm road, achieving good results in time-limited farming such as planting and harvesting barley. When the youth members united to create 40 tons of shared fertilizer, they embraced each other and shed tears of gratitude.

The residents realized that there was nothing they couldn't do together. After that, they gathered whenever they could to discuss plans for everyone and gradually planned village affairs one by one.

As the once dirty village became cleaner, they even managed to install telephone facilities, a long-standing wish for the village. Along with the telephone project, they installed a village amplifier for 100,000 won. At 6 am, the Saemaul song echoed in every window, and a flagpole was erected in the village's open space. Children gathered to sing the national anthem and raise the flag, breathing in the fresh morning air and doing morning runs, awakening the children to the dignity of the nation. The village residents became diligent and proud residents, each devoted to their own field.

In November 1975, the existing village residents, amazed at the transformation of the new residents, proposed working together and held a general assembly to elect Park Young-seon as the village leader.

Feeling a sense of unity and accomplishment, like a divided nation being reunified, the couple leaders resolved to make this village the best in the country with even greater effort. Together with the village residents, they studied and researched advanced farming techniques, opening irrigation channels in the fields and planting unified rice in 1975.


--- (p. 715) ---

The success of the Saemaul Undong in this village led to a bountiful harvest of rice with a yield of 6 seok (石) per dan (段當), and fields were planted with vegetables like perilla leaves, garlic, and beans, resulting in a harvest double that of the previous year. In 1976, the village continuously cultivated garlic, onions, perilla leaves, and radish greens without letting the land rest, achieving a household income nearly doubling the previous year's. The paddy fields, which had previously been single-cropped, were transformed into double-cropped fields.

In November 1975, recognizing the need for a storage facility to keep government-supported gravel and communal materials, Leader Park proposed the construction of a village warehouse at the village assembly. However, the residents, who had only known poverty, were reluctant to support the idea, questioning the necessity of such a warehouse.

Despite the initial resistance, Leader Park's persistent advocacy for the warehouse's necessity and the evident signs of the village's improving conditions eventually convinced the villagers to resolve to build a Saemaul warehouse. After several visits to the administrative authorities, Leader Park's sincere pleas and unwavering determination to create a prosperous village led to the village being designated to receive 500,000 won for the construction of the Saemaul warehouse as part of a roadside beautification project.

However, disagreements arose between the original residents and the transplanted residents over the location of the warehouse. While the original residents insisted on building it near their homes, no one was willing to donate land. After a month of deliberation, the warehouse was finally agreed to be built on a vacant lot in the transplanted residents' village. Yet, when the construction began, the original residents did not participate, and the transplanted residents, who earned their living through day labor, could not dedicate themselves to the task daily. Ultimately, Leader Park and two supportive residents, with the help of the women's association, completed a 20-pyeong warehouse through tearful efforts.

To keep the villagers occupied during the farming off-season, the village purchased 8 spinning wheels and 6 reelers with village funds, boosting the income of landless small-scale farmers and significantly contributing to increasing farm income by maximizing the use of straw.

The village's continuous development instilled more courage in the leader and residents. The married leader couple relentlessly researched and discussed ways to increase individual residents' income, considering each resident's circumstances and characteristics. They arranged for those engaged in small-scale farming to raise beef cattle as a side income and supported specialized crop contract farming.

However, a few uneducated individuals who owned some farmland but relied on others for farming and had been acting as local leaders, joined forces to spread false accusations that the leader had embezzled support cement. They filed complaints with the prosecution and police, causing turmoil. Many people pressured the leader to unconditionally submit, and public criticism that the leader had amassed wealth dealt a significant blow and trial to the married leader couple. This brought a year-long stagnation period to the once thriving village.

In the midst of this frustrating and painful life, the married leader couple thought they could neither give up nor be defeated.


--- (p. 716) ---

The leader, President Park (朴指導者), decided to visit the Saemaul Training Institute (硏修院), where he had learned the true meaning of the New Community Movement, to seek advice and counsel from the instructors (敎官) there.

O There, the leader (指導者) realized anew that one is never alone, that the path of justice (正義) is fraught with difficulties (險難), but that perseverance brings commensurate rewards. He resolved to consider the feelings of every resident (住民) and ensure that no one felt left out. With this determination, he returned to the village.

The village was tense, and rumors were rife that the leader (指導者) had fled after taking all he could. The walls of the community center (會舘) and warehouse (倉庫) that had been built with such effort were covered in footprints.

O The residents (住民) were completely divided into two groups: those who had often complained about their work and those who had diligently worked all along.

However, the children's genuine greeting of "I like it" to the two leaders (指導者) gave them courage. The leader (指導者) earnestly urged the residents (住民) who came to him for help to work together as true friends, even in the worst of circumstances, trusting that the law (法) would judge fairly (審判).

O The next day, amidst the sweltering heat, the couple leaders (夫婦指導者) began to drain the overgrown village farm (農場). If they received a summons (通知) from the police (警察), they would wash their hands in the pond, change into their work clothes (作業服), and go to the police station (警察署). These trials continued.

Even in such difficult circumstances, the couple leaders (夫婦指導者) remained steadfast in their pride (矜持) as Saemaul leaders (指導者) and approached their tasks with composure. The residents (住民), in turn, worked even more diligently, which gave the leaders (指導者) strength.

With newfound enthusiasm, the residents (住民) began water supply (上水道) facility work (施設作業) with the leader (指導者) at the center. Many residents (住民) who had turned their backs on the leader (指導者) also joined the work one by one. Through three months of effort, they were able to complete the village's long-cherished project (宿願事業).

O As the water supply (上水道) project (事業) neared completion on November 27, 1975, the police (警察) issued a notice of no suspicion (通知), and the investigation (捜査) was concluded (一段落). Although many people around them urged them to file charges for false accusation (罪) and defamation (罪), they decided to let the matter drop, believing that true unity (總和) of the village would be impossible otherwise.

Now, the village has overcome the shame of its divided past (過去) and, with the two leaders (指導者) at its center, is firmly united, striving wholeheartedly towards a cultural and welfare-oriented (文化福祉) rural (農村) society in the 1980s (代).

#### 4) Developmental Promotion of the Saemaul Movement (事業)

Emboldened by the successful improvement (整備) of the small stream (小河川) and farm roads (農路), this village began, in 1975, to improve its environment, which had been like a beggar's den. Using 300 bags (袋) of cement supported by the government (政府) and sand purchased with Women's Association (婦女會) funds (基金), they installed a 350-meter sewer (下水溝) on both sides of the 5-meter village road, solving the long-standing problem (宿願) of the village becoming a sea of water whenever it rained. They also improved 10 roofs (棟), built 6 personal bathhouses (沐浴湯), improved 23 kitchens (戶), improved 10 toilets (便所), and installed 20 jar stands (個所), achieving remarkable results in just two months during the farming off-season (農閑期).

On the other hand, they neatly constructed a 640-meter wall around 20 migrant houses (移住民住宅) and, through the cooperation (協同) of the residents (住民), repaired a 200-meter village road in just ten days, making it straight and clean. In October of that year, using 300,000 won (萬원) from the Women's Association (婦女會) funds (基金) as a foundation and 1.8 million won (萬원) from the residents' self-financing (自力負擔), they were able to bring electricity (電氣) to the village, a long-cherished dream (宿願) that had eluded them until November 1975.


--- (p. 717) ---

The day electricity came to the village, it seemed as if the entire community embraced and danced, turning the village into a festive celebration. Particularly during the electrification project, poorer households received support from more affluent families, showcasing the virtue of cooperation. The Women's Association's fund of 300,000 won greatly supported the residents, teaching them the importance of savings and reinforcing their belief that "if you try, you can achieve." In January 1976, the village formed a sisterhood relationship with Samyang Tire, securing support for lumber and thread, which enabled the residents to build a 40-pyeong multipurpose community center through their own efforts. In June 1976, the village received the honor of a 1,000,000 won donation from the President (大統領), which, combined with their own savings of 1,280,000 won, allowed them to purchase a 2,000-pyeong farm. The income from this farm alone was expected to reach 7,000,000 won annually. Additionally, the village planted over 1,000 fruit and economic trees along the riverside and hillsides, enhancing the village's scenery and increasing residents' income, ultimately securing village assets worth nearly 80,000,000 won. In September 1976, the village completed a simple water supply facility for 2,500,000 won, ensuring a hygienic and cultured rural environment. Recently, the village organized group visits to the National Cemetery to experience patriotism and loyalty to the nation. They also toured sister companies like the Samyang Tire factory, witnessing the diligent work of laborers and the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) within the factory. Furthermore, they visited the provincial livestock farm and private ranches to learn about livestock farming firsthand.

### 6) Heartwarming Stories (美談佳話)

#### a) Story 1 (第1話)

A 67-year-old grandmother who lives alone in this village is always the first to arrive at meetings, attentively listening to discussions about village affairs. She is always the first to help with village cleaning and all Saemaul work sites. If there are disagreements or someone is slacking off, she passionately encourages everyone to work hard, saying that the success of the Saemaul Undong will lead to a prosperous nation. Despite having no descendants to carry on her legacy, she insists on participating, saying she will live long enough to see her village thrive before she dies. What an admirable grandmother!

#### b) Story 2 (第2話)

A 65-year-old carpenter dedicated 40 days to building the village community center, from doors to roofing, and refused to accept any compensation, saying, "Why would I take payment for working on our village's affairs?" A 47-year-old man named Tosu, originally from Daegu in Gyeongsang Province, devoted nearly 100 days to the Saemaul Undong before leaving. Thanks to such dedicated individuals, our village has been able to develop as much as it has today.

### 8) Notable Matters (特記 事項)

#### a) Joyful Events

* Before the Saemaul Undong began, it was difficult to find young people in this village. However, the movement brought innovation to the village and diversified income sources, enabling self-sufficient families. Young people who had previously left for urban areas began to return home and participate in the Saemaul Undong.
* Even those who had not yet returned home continued to save money and contribute it to the Saemaul Undong in their hometowns.


--- (p. 719) ---

### Joyful Events

*   The immigrants (移住民) who were previously treated as subhuman (人間以下) by the existing residents (旣存住民) spontaneously elected Park (朴) as the village leader (指導者) and proposed to work together.
*   When the President (大統領) granted financial support in 1976 (年).
*   When Governor (知事) Ko Geon (高建) visited unexpectedly on February 27, 1976 (76.2.27).
*   When the multipurpose hall (多目的 會舘) of 40 pyeong (坪) was completed with the support of Samyang (三陽) Tire.
*   When the residents (住民) were able to light electric (電氣) lights on their own on November 15, 1975 (75.11.15).

### Sad Events

*   During the period of rapid village development and family progress (上昇期) through the simultaneous movement of environmental improvement (環境改善) and income source development (所得源開發), some people's schemes (謀略) caused legal (法的) problems (問題), leading to a stagnant period (沉滞期) lasting nearly a year (年).
*   Residents (住民) who had actively participated in the work fell into apathy (平), doubted the leader (指導者), and turned their backs.
*   When the construction (工事) of the Saemaul warehouse (倉庫) could not start quickly due to the issue of its location (位置), and eventually, none of the existing village residents (旣存마을 住民) came out to help.

## 바. Achievements (成果) from Saemaul (新村) Projects (事業)

1) Spiritual (精神) Aspect
◦ The villagers, who were lazy, listless, and overly dependent (依他心), transformed into the driving force (役軍) of a new village (新村) through the Saemaul Undong (運動), embodying diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperation (協同);
◦ Villagers, who were once engrossed in selfishness (利己主義) and surprised by the greatness (偉大) of cooperation (協同) through joint work (共同作業), have now established a sound national perspective (國家觀), understanding that the village is more important than the individual (個人) and the nation (國家) is more important than the village.

2) Lifestyle (生活) Aspect
◦ The sight of women walking 1km to the laundry area and the squabbles at the bug-infested well are now distant tales of the past.
◦ Villages that once had houses standing alone without fences now boast clean, well-maintained roofs and walls.


--- (p. 721) ---

Enjoying the bright electric lights and clean drinking water from the simple water supply, they are living a cultural life in a hygienic, improved kitchen, and enjoying laughter-blooming family life.

### 3) Production Aspect
- By establishing unified (統一) systems for rice cultivation and Yu Shin rice (維新─) clusters, the yield per unit increased by 2.5 times,
- In 1977, cultivating the Milyang 23 variety further increased the harvest.
- Residents who previously only sowed barley are now enthusiastically engaging in contract farming of various high-income crops such as tobacco, onions, garlic, and medicinal herbs.
- Although not yet in the harvest season, crops like peaches, persimmons, and jujubes will significantly boost residents' income in three years.

### 3. Residents' Assembly (住民總會)

♦ Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (1)

|               |                                       |
|:--------------|:--------------------------------------|
| Agenda (議 題)   | Organization of Women's Association (婦女會組織) |
| Date (日 時)   | November 9, 1973                      |
| Venue (場 所)   | Im Jeong-sun's (林貞順) downstairs room |
| Attendees (參席人員) | Hong Ui-sun (洪義順) and 19 others     |
| Absentees (不參人員) | 36 people                             |
| Chairperson (司會者) | Im Jeong-sun (林貞順)                 |

Chairperson (司會者): I apologize for convening this late-night meeting. Our village was formed by people who moved here together, and it seems we've been living in an awkward atmosphere. We are all poor, and the men usually spend their time drinking and living recklessly, which has been a shameful situation for all of us. Although I am also an outsider here, this place is also my hometown. We are like this because...


--- (p. 722) ---

The more we struggle, the more we must understand each other and overcome adversity (逆境) together. I believe that is what we must do. The reason I have gathered all of you here today is to create an organization (組織) for women, to change the atmosphere (雰圍氣) and do something meaningful.

Currently, administrative agencies (行政機關) are promoting the establishment of women's associations (婦女會), and that is today's task (課題). Through sufficient exchange of opinions (意思交換), we will organize the women's association (婦女會) and form its members (會員) tonight. I will proceed according to your will (意思). First, let us elect the president (會長) of the women's association (婦女會), form the members (會員), and discuss future tasks (課題).

**Lee Deok-soon**: First, let us decide the number of candidates (候補者) for the president (會長). I think two candidates would be appropriate.

**Host**: That is a good opinion (意見). Please, another person speak. ―No one speaks― After a while―

**Host**: If there is no will (意思) from you, we will consider it as deciding two candidates (候補者). Please state the candidates.

**Kim Young-rye**: I nominate Im Jeong-soon (氏).

**Host**: Yes, please speak again.

―Everyone remains in a quiet atmosphere (雰圍氣)― After a while―

**Host**: If there are no more candidates (候補者), I have received a nomination, but I will ask for your will (意思). Please raise your hand (擧手) if you agree (贊成).

―Result (結果)― 18 people (名) agree (贊成), no one disagrees (反對), and 1 person (名) abstains (棄權). Everyone applauds (拍手) to congratulate (祝賀) Im Jeong-soon.

**President of the Women's Association (婦女會長)**: I am very happy that you have elected me as the president (會長) of the women's association (婦女會), but at the same time, I feel a heavy sense of responsibility (責任感). I look forward to your guidance (指導) and cooperation (協助). Now, let us discuss the next issue (問題). First, the matter of our members (會員). Our women's association members (婦女會員) should be one person (名) per household (家口), but currently, we have 51 members (名). However, many are absent today, so what should we do?

**Madame Ma Sun**: In my opinion, all women (婦女子) should participate (參與), and we should try to make them understand (理解) each other.

**Park Bok-soon**: That is a good opinion (意見).

**President of the Women's Association (婦女會長)**: Are there any other opinions (意見)?

―No one speaks―

**President of the Women's Association (婦女會長)**: Then, I will decide by a vote (可否). Please raise your hand (擧手) if you agree (贊成).

―Everyone agrees (贊成)―

**President of the Women's Association (婦女會長)**: Then, according to your will (意思), all women (婦女子) will become members (會員). We will create the list (名簿) later, and at the next meeting (會議), please persuade (說得) everyone (全員) to attend (參席).

**President of the Women's Association (婦女會長)**: Now, since our members (會員) are organized (組織), I would like to do something for the village (村落). If you have any good opinions (意見), please speak.

**Lee Deok-soon**: My village has no notable shops (店鋪) and inconvenient transportation (交通), making it difficult (困難) to go to the market (市場). I would like to create a small village shopping center (購販場). And I would like it to be operated (運營) by moving (移動) from house to house (家口).


--- (p. 723) ---

**Woman's Association President**: That is an excellent suggestion. If anyone has any other good ideas, please share them.
—Silence—
**Woman's Association President**: It seems there are no other opinions. Let's discuss this idea further at the next meeting and decide if it's good. Who thinks this project is a good idea? Please raise your hand.
—Result— 15 in favor, 4 opposed
**Woman's Association President**: For those who opposed, if you have any good opinions, please share them.
**Kim Young-rye**: I think that if we have a mobile market stall, it might cause inconvenience to everyone. Therefore, I think it would be better to build a community center and set up the market stall there,
**Woman's Association President**: That is a good opinion. However, my opinion is similar in that we cannot immediately build a community center, and our village fund is also quite necessary. I think it would be meaningful to try operating it for a while, even if it is a bit inconvenient. What do you think?
**Woman's Association President**: If anyone has any other good opinions, please share them.
—Silence—
**Woman's Association President**: Then, I will take it that everyone agrees and proceed with a vote. However, to push forward with this project, we need capital. How should we do this?
**Ma Sun-nim**: My opinion is that first, the members present today should take the lead and contribute, with each household contributing 300 won, totaling 6,000 won. I think we should start with this amount, even if it is small. What do you all think?
**Woman's Association President**: That is a good opinion. Does anyone have any other good methods to suggest?
—Members remain silent—
**Woman's Association President**: If no one has any better ideas, shall we discuss this method?
**Park Bok-sun**: Then, let's do it that way.
**Woman's Association President**: Then, I will ask for your approval. Please raise your hand if you are in favor.
—Unanimous approval—
**Woman's Association President**: Then, based on your approval, the members present today should each contribute 300 won by the day after tomorrow to me. Once the funds are collected, I will consult with everyone to purchase the market stall items. As it is getting late, we will end the meeting here today.
Thank you.


--- (p. 724) ---

# Agenda(議題): Construction of Community Center (會舘) (建立)
Date(日時): Jan. 10, 1976
Location(場所): Home of Saemaul Leader Park Young-seon
Attendees(參席人員): Jeong Young-gyu and 30 others
Absentees(不參人員): Im Jong-cheol and 25 others
Chairperson(司會者): Saemaul Leader Park Young-seon (朴英仙)

Chairperson: I am very sorry to have called this meeting so late at night. Today's agenda is the construction of a community center. So far, our village has completed various projects such as stream improvement, sewer installation, roof and wall reinforcement, and even the difficult electrification project, transforming our village into a very clean environment. However, our women's association members who jointly operate the mobile market stall lack a proper meeting place, which has caused considerable inconvenience.

As part of the '76 Saemaul Beautification Project (事業), we have already decided to build a community center. This meeting has been called to efficiently promote this project, so please share your good opinions. By the way, to build a 40-pyeong community center, we estimate that we will need 400 bags of government (政府) support (支援) cement, 4 million won (萬圓) for materials, and an additional 1 million won (萬圓) in cash from our own efforts. First and foremost, we need to discuss funding (資金). If anyone has good opinions, please speak up.

Choe Il-bok: We have a total of 57 households (家口). I propose that we initially collect 300 won per household and make up any shortfall later through additional per-household contributions.

Chairperson: That is a good opinion. Let's hear from another attendee.

Im Jong-yeol: I propose that we collect 400 won per household and use the remaining funds from the village's reserve (基金).

Chairperson: That is also a good opinion. Does anyone else have something to say?

—Silence—

Chairperson: If there are no further opinions, we will now vote on the two proposals.

(Result(結果)) Proposal 1 (第1案) received 23 votes in favor (贊成)
Proposal 2 (第2案) received 8 votes in favor (贊成)

Chairperson: Based on your opinions, we will initially collect 300 won per household and make additional collections later if more funds are needed. Now, let's move on to selecting the project period (事業時期). The administrative agency (行政機關) has requested that we complete the project by the end of April, but when should we aim to finish?

Im Myeong-gyu: Since it is the farming off-season (農閑期), I think we should start construction as soon as possible. Let's begin on January 10th and aim to complete the project before the busy farming season (農繁期).

Chairperson: Does anyone else have an opinion?

—Silence—

Chairperson: Then, I will ask for a show of hands from those who agree (贊成).

— 724 —


--- (p. 725) ---

(Result) It was decided with 28 votes in favor.
Chairperson: Then, according to your will, we will start construction on January 10th, and when the labor of the village residents is needed, we will have all residents participate without complaint.
Then, today's meeting will conclude here. Thank you.

## 3. Future Development Plan

- O After the completion of the Daecheodam Dam in 1976 as part of the comprehensive development project of the Yeongsan River basin, this village, which is one of the few remaining in Naju County with half-day irrigation, plans to install a permanent water lifting facility using the waters of the Yeongsan River in 1978 to secure irrigation facilities without water worries.
- O Once the irrigation facilities are fully equipped, plans include preparing facilities for the cultivation of specialty crops and greenhouse crops, aiming to achieve revolutionary all-weather agriculture and high utilization of land starting in the year 1978.
- O To develop the village into a livestock farming enterprise village alongside the expansion of livestock farms, plans include expanding the number of beef cattle farms in 1978.
- O Plans include creating orchards suitable for the village's land composition, such as persimmon, jujube, apricot, and apple trees, and expanding home-based sideline businesses according to their aptitude. At the same time, leveraging the village's conditions, plans include creating a high-income welfare village through mechanized diversified farming.

# Jeonnam (全南) Jangseong County (長城郡) Jangseong-eup (長城邑) Sang-o (上蜈) Village

## 1. Overview of the Village

### a. History

- Over 1,300 years ago, a settlement was established here. In the 9th year of King Gyeongjong (顯宗), the 8th king of Goryeo (高麗) (1018 AD), the village belonged to Buksam-myeon (北三面) of Jangseong County (長城縣). During the Japanese colonial period (日帝) in 1936, the village was reorganized as Sang-o-ri (上蜈里) of Jangseong-eup (長城邑) during an administrative district (行政區域) reform (改編), leading to the present day.
- The village's name, Sang-o (上蜈), comes from the fact that the mountain behind the village resembles a centipede ("지네"). Meanwhile, a neighboring village visible across the way is named Baekgae-ri (白鷄里) because the mountain behind it resembles a white rooster ("흰닭"). The two villages, like the centipede and the rooster, have always had a mutual antagonism (相克), with residents of Sang-o (上蜈) Village being sensitive to the stimulus of their neighboring village. This competitive spirit (競爭意識) has not been without its role in promoting community cooperation (住民協同) since the inception of the Saemaul Undong (新村運動).

### b. Location and Conditions

**Location**

- The village is located 30 km northwest of Gwangju (光州), the provincial capital (道廳), along the Honam Expressway (湖南高速道路). It is adjacent to the Jangseong Dam (長城댐), which was completed on October 14, 1976.

**Conditions**

- The village's mountain, Jinsan (鎭山), is formed by the extension of Noryeong (蘆領), the northern border of Jeonnam (全南), embracing Jangseong Lake (長城湖). The village is scenic (風致) and conveniently located (便利) along the expressway (高速道邊), with the Jangseong Plain (長城平野) spreading out in front of it.
- Thanks to the irrigation water (灌漑水) from the Jangseong Dam, the village is free from drought and flood damage (旱水害), enabling year-round agriculture (全天候農業). It is a beneficiary village of the Yeongsan River (榮山江) comprehensive development project (綜合開發事業).
