# 2. The Development Process of the Village

### Before the 1970s

1) Basic Environment
- The rivers were not properly maintained, and even a little rain would cause houses to flood, creating an extremely unsanitary environment.
- There were no proper farm roads, not even a proper access road to the village. The village had been stuck with its thatched roofs for hundreds of years, presenting a pitifully poor appearance.

2) Income Level
- With only 0.5ha of farmland per household and primitive farming methods, it was difficult to make ends meet. The income level was so low that it was hard to even calculate.
- However, since 30 years ago, the village had been surviving on wages from a traditional Korean paper (hanji) factory that used wild paper mulberry trees growing around the village. It was an extremely poor village.
- The great flood of 1963 swept away all the farmland of this poor village, presenting a very harsh trial.

3) Living Conditions in 1970
a) Consciousness Structure
- Drinking and gambling were rampant, and everyone acted selfishly with no sense of cooperation. The conflict between clans like Kim (金氏) and Cha (車氏) caused frequent disputes among the villagers, making it impossible to even think about unity among residents.
- b) Culture and Daily Life
- Since daily life largely depended on manual labor, cultural activities were out of the question. Most houses were dilapidated thatched-roof huts, and many people survived on wild vegetables.

### The Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

1) Motivation and Results of the Pilot Project
- As previously mentioned, the environment, income, spirit, and culture of the village were in a state of despair and resignation. Time passed, and the lack of a bridge over the small river in front of the village caused problems: even a little rain would block the children's school commute, and there was even a drowning accident of a woman crossing the river. This saddened the conscious residents.
- The village head at the time, Kim Ik-su (金益洙), used the grain he usually received as compensation to secure 50 sacks of rice. On February 16, 1962, he built an 18m long and 2.5m wide bridge, touching the hearts of the residents.
- In 1963, an unexpected flood caused significant damage, including the flooding of houses and the loss of farmland along the Hwangryonggang River in front of the village. The financial and psychological impact on the residents was severe, making their situation even worse.


--- (p. 729) ---

In the midst of despair and sorrow, President Park Chung-hee (朴正熙) (大統領) (閣下) encouraged the villagers while inspecting the Jangseong (長城) region. During his visit, he had a conversation with Kim Myeong-su (金明洙), a young man from Sang'o (上蜈) village, and encouraged the villagers, saying, "This disaster has befallen us because we were not sufficiently prepared. From now on, all villagers should cooperate and unite to overcome all disasters together and strive to live even better with the will and courage to do so." He also gave them warm comfort and guidance on how to overcome all hardships.

Inspired by this, young leader Kim Myeong-su (金明洙) began to explore ways for all villagers to live well together.

## 2) Activities of the Saemaul Leader (指導者)
Saemaul leader Kim Myeong-su (金明洙) graduated from Jangseong Middle School (長城中學校) and joined the police during the Korean War (6.25), participating in operations to suppress the communist guerrillas in Jirisan (地理山). Afterward, he moved around Seoul, Jeonju (全州), and other places in search of a livelihood but failed to achieve his goals. In 1962, he returned to his hometown and established a hanji (韓紙) paper factory, working diligently while taking care of village affairs.

The construction of today's Sang'o (上蜈) village was based on Kim Myeong-su's (金明洙) dedicated efforts as a leader (指導者), who served as the chairman of the youth association (靑年會長) and village chief (里長) among other roles, and devoted himself selflessly to the village.

In 1971, with Kim Myeong-su (金明洙) as the center, the village development committee (開發委員) was formed to develop farm roads (農路) in the farmland (農耕地) behind the village and between the village. While constructing a 1,000-meter farm road (農路), they faced opposition from landowners (地主) and were beaten, but this did not deter their resolve. The villagers trusted and supported the young leader (指導者) for his outstanding leadership (指導力) and ambitious spirit (霸氣), and thus the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) began.

The construction of the Honam (湖南) Expressway (高速道路), which began in 1971, brought new vitality to the villagers.

To effectively utilize the Honam (湖南) Expressway (高速道路) construction site (現場) for the development of the village (部落), Kim Myeong-su (金明洙) convened a village general assembly (總會) and decided that men would work at the construction site (現場), while women (婦女子) and the elderly (老人) would promote the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) in the village.

From the Honam (湖南) Expressway (高速道路) construction site (現場) in 1971 alone, they earned 38 million won in wages (勞賃), and by the time the expressway (高速道路) was completed in 1973, their total earnings (所得) from wages (勞賃) reached 150 million won.

In 1972, the fervor of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動), which swept the nation like a strong wind, also reached Sang'o (上蜈) village. With the unity of the leader (指導者) and the development committee (開發委員), they widened the main roads (安길), improved the walls (담장), and installed sewers (下水溝), beginning a history of renovating the village's appearance (革新).

In 1973, they expanded the main roads (安길) and installed sewers (下水溝), followed by the construction of one laundry area (빨래터) and four small bridges (小橋梁).

By July 1973, as the Honam (湖南) Expressway (高速道路) construction was nearing completion, the construction of the Jangseong Lake (長城湖) dam on the upper reaches of the Hwangsangang (黃山江) River began, further increasing the villagers' income.

With the skills (技術) learned and acquired from the expressway (高速道路) construction site (現場), wages (勞賃) increased, and even women (婦女子) began to work at the construction site (現場).


--- (p. 730) ---

They cooked meals and did laundry for the villagers, and did whatever work they could. The wages earned by the residents at the Jangseong Dam construction site amounted to approximately 46 million won, which provided this village with the opportunity to prosper. The residents completed various construction projects in the village with skilled techniques, and by saving on project funds, they ensured that no resident had to contribute operational funds, all thanks to Kim Myeong-su's outstanding leadership and planned approach, which greatly contributed to the village's development.

* By spring of 1973, they had completely upgraded the thatched roofs of 138 houses, including the annex, using slate and tiles. Additionally, they contributed 700,000 won from the village's communal fund to upgrade the homes of two impoverished households, reinforcing the spirit of cooperation among neighbors.
* Through diligent completion of each assigned project, the village was promoted to a self-sufficient village in 1974. They invested 500,000 won in self-sufficient village support funds to complete a multipurpose market building (including a barbershop and warehouse). Due to the construction of the Jangseong Dam, the water level of the Hwangryonggang River in front of the village decreased, creating riverfront land. The leader and villagers took the initiative, obtained permission to use the riverfront land, and successfully created a communal farm of 1,100 pyeong.
Additionally, through the New Community Movement, they constructed and set up a small bridge, and with construction support funds, they established a new bridge.
* With a special support fund of 1 million won from the President, they excellently improved a 200-meter small stream in the village that often flooded during the rainy season, submerging many homes. From the wages earned, they created a second-round fund of 235,000 won and, combined with 40,000 won from the village fund, purchased two engines and two threshing machines for communal use.
* In 1975, they connected and constructed a 340-meter small stream for the second-round small stream project to the small stream improved in 1974 with the President's special support.
On August 8, 1975, former Prime Minister Kim Jong-pil visited the village and, with the 700 bags of cement provided, expanded the bridge connected to the village's access road.
This bridge, initially repaired by former village head Kim Ik-su in 1962 using 50 bushels of rice converted into village funds, had a width of 2.5 meters, which was inconvenient for the current traffic volume. By expanding it to a length of 18 meters and a width of 5 meters, it became possible for large vehicles to pass through comfortably.
Additionally, in October, they installed water supply systems for all households by combining 650,000 won from the women's association fund and 1 million won from government support, providing hygienic drinking water to residents who previously used stream water from in front of the village.
* Kim Ok-ja, a women's leader with teaching experience, established and operated a village library, holding monthly reading clubs. This allowed all members to learn new farming techniques and general knowledge through books.
* Members with experience as nannies in Seoul took the lead in operating daycare centers during the busy farming season, allowing parents busy with construction work and farming to work with peace of mind, knowing their children were being taken care of.
* Notably, the women's association and the youth association resolved to improve soil quality to increase crop yields per unit area. Starting in the summer, they formed a joint work team of 54 men and women, camped in the mountains behind Wolseong-ri, Bukha-myeon, 10 km away from the village, and produced 300% compost by cutting grass. They also applied purchased soil to 25 hectares of rice fields.


--- (p. 731) ---

They improved the soil fertility.
- In this way, after the residents cooperated to improve the soil quality of the rice fields, they installed a common seedbed for high-yield varieties such as the "Yushin" rice and collectively carried out farming tasks such as transplanting, pest control, etc. As a result, the fields, which previously only produced an average of 300kg per segment, achieved a harvest of 560kg in 1976, allowing the residents to celebrate an unprecedented bumper crop. This motivated the residents to strive even harder to live better.
- In 1976, with the support of the New Community Movement beautification project, an 18-pyeong village community center was established. Part of the community center was designated as a "Home for Improving Dietary Life," which is used as an educational facility for improving the dietary life of housewives on a regular basis and as a communal kitchen during communal work.
- Meanwhile, in April 1976, the residents cooperated to develop a 2,200-pyeong mountain behind the village into a nursery and began raising 25,000 village seedlings, including Italian Poplar and Silverberry, to develop new sources of income.
- Kim Myeong-su, the leader, had achieved village life stability through public projects such as the Honam Expressway and the Jangseong Dam. However, he realized that temporary wages and meager agricultural income were not enough and began to seek new permanent sources of income.
- Kim Myeong-su, the New Community Movement leader, hurried to plan the development of his primitively managed hanji (Korean paper) manufacturing plant into a large-scale, labor-intensive factory where many residents could participate.
- In 1973, he invested 300 million won of his own capital and 400 million won of loans from a small and medium-sized enterprise bank to construct a 63-pyeong New Community Movement factory and improved the existing facilities. On February 16, 1974, it was designated as a New Village Factory by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, providing jobs for 36 villagers and contributing to the increase of residents' income.
- The process of producing hanji (Korean paper) at this factory is as follows:
  1. Using the bark of "Dak" trees, which grow abundantly in Jangseong, and straw as raw materials,
  2. Mixing waste paper and pulp purchased from cities with a bleaching agent and boiling them,
  3. Finely pulverizing them with a pulverizer, putting them into a paper vat, and making a slurry,
  4. Draining and drying them with a bamboo net, and
  5. Finally, selecting them by grade and packaging them.
  This factory can self-supply its raw materials from the village, and most of its processes are labor-intensive, maximizing the employment effects for the village residents and fulfilling the original role of a New Community Movement factory.
- The produced paper is classified into three types: Taiji, Hwaseonji, and Jangjaji, and is mainly used as calligraphy paper. All products are exported to Japan, achieving export performances of $30,000 in 1974, $38,000 in 1975, $84,000 in 1976, and $87,000 as of the end of November 1977. With new purchase demands from Hong Kong, Italy, and Saudi Arabia, the prospects for foreign currency earnings are bright.
- In particular, on November 9, 1976, when Kim, the leader, reported the monthly economic trends to His Excellency the President, he received the honor of being awarded a medal (Medal of Industry No. 77). With the grant money, it was decided by the consensus of the residents to expand and operate the Sangam New Community Movement Hanji Factory as communal property. The articles of association were established and notarized on June 14, 1977. A total of 919 million won, including 500 million won of grant money, 300 million won of loans from the New Community Movement Income Savings Bank, and 119 million won of resident burdens, was invested to expand the facilities.


--- (p. 732) ---

and expansion of the facilities and the articles of association are as follows.

### Articles of Association (Summary)
The purpose of this association is to manage and operate the hanji (Korean paper) factory efficiently through stockholding, fostering a spirit of cooperation and a comprehensive system among residents, increasing assets, and improving village income. The assets of this factory, as of March 21, 1977, are owned by the current leader Kim Myeong-su (金明洙), as evaluated by the Korean Appraisal Institute (韓國鑑定院) Gwangju Branch (光州支店).

| Item | Area/Quantity | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| Land | 213 pyeong (坪) | 639,000 won |
| Buildings | 138 pyeong (坪) | 6,042,000 won |
| Machinery and Equipment | 79 items (點) | 2,559,000 won |
| **Total** | | **9,240,000 won** |

With a total of 9,240,000 won, the residents' equivalent contribution is combined to make 18,480,000 won. Additionally, 5,000,000 won is jointly contributed by Kim Myeong-su (金明洙) and the village residents as operating funds for the factory. The total assets and operating funds of the factory, amounting to 23,480,000 won, are equally divided, with Kim Myeong-su (金明洙) contributing 50% (11,740,000 won) and the village residents contributing 50% (11,740,000 won). The operating funds can be adjusted by the residents' general meeting as circumstances dictate. The current leader cannot contribute more than 50% under any circumstances.

### Facility Expansion through Donation Projects
The expansion of the hanji (Korean paper) factory, carried out as a donation project, began on April 19, 1977, and was completed on July 1, 1977. The expansion included the installation of a 15-horsepower (馬力) power line, the addition of 7 paper barrels, the installation of 1 dewatering machine (脫水機), a drying facility (乾燥施設) covering 23 pyeong (坪), and the construction of raw material storage, all aimed at improving the efficiency of hanji (Korean paper) production.

### Land Donation and Road Construction Challenges
In 1971, leader Kim Myeong-su (金明洙) persuaded the development committee and village residents to open a 1,000-meter agricultural road connecting the village and farmland. Despite strong opposition from landowners in the neighboring village (上蜈 2區), the project was forcibly carried out, leading to an incident where the leader was beaten. However, the leader's persistent persuasion, emphasizing the benefits for both villages and future generations, eventually moved the landowners to donate their land, ensuring the successful completion of the road.

In 1974, with special support of 1,000,000 won from the authorities, the village straightened a winding stream and built a new path along it. Facing strong opposition from landowners, the project was temporarily halted. However, Kim Jong-in (金鍾仁), a village resident and member of the development committee, negotiated with the landowners and donated his own land in exchange for the opposing landowners' 90 pyeong (坪) of land, which was then donated to the village. This act of generosity left a lasting impression on the village residents and is remembered as a beautiful and wise example of overcoming adversity.

### Heartwarming Stories
In 1972, amidst the strong momentum of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), the village of Sangnok (上蜈) also widened paths and improved fences.


--- (p. 733) ---

A great transformation was taking place in the village, but without village funds, it was almost impossible to continue the projects. Even in such a difficult situation, the leader came up with a solution after discussing with the development committee. As the saying goes, "Many hands make light work," if every villager contributed a little, a considerable amount of funds could be raised.

A general meeting of O village was held, and the leader himself took the lead by donating 100,000 won to the village. Not only the development committee but also various village organizations such as the Uichin Society and influential villagers voluntarily showed their sincerity, resulting in the collection of 600,000 won. This was beyond expectation, and both the leader and the development committee were astonished. The fact that such a large amount of funds was collected from the poor villagers was the result of the villagers uniting as one, and it seemed that a ray of hope had dawned on the future of Sang-eup village.

Furthermore, in 1976, two dilapidated houses of extremely poor small-scale farmers were improved by investing 700,000 won from the village funds, creating a precedent of mutual help and loving one's neighbor as one's own brother.

## 8) Village Various (各種) Organizations (組織) and Activities (活動) Situation (狀況)

### a) Development (開發) Committee (委員會)

O Discuss and deliberate on all aspects of village management (村落 經營) for the development (發展) of O village, and deliberate on, approve, and address issues in the implementation (實施) of new community (新村) projects and overall village finances (財政). (11 members (名))

### b) Youth Association (靑年會)

O Actively participate in various new community (新村) projects and research and promote aspects of increasing communal (共同) income (所得). (35 members (名))

### c) Women's Association (婦女會) (43 members (名))

O Since 1973, have conducted purchasing (購販) business (事業), depositing the profits (利益金) in individual (個人) accounts (通帳) under the names (名義) of the beneficiaries (需要者). When a certain limit (一定 限度額) is reached, loans (貸付) are provided for income-generating (所得 事業費) activities according to the beneficiaries' (需要者) wishes (希望). In 1976, part of the community center (會舘) was designated as a nutrition (營養) improvement (改善) house to study and improve dietary (食生活) habits, and the communal (共同) kitchen (炊事場) is utilized (活用) during communal (共同) work (作業).

### d) Reserve Forces (豫備軍) (16 members (名))

Construct (構築) and train (訓練) defensive (防禦) positions (陣地) for village self-defense (自體 防禦).

## 9) New Community (新村) Project (事業) Achievements (成果)

### a) Production (生産) and Income (所得) Aspects

O With all village residents (住民) united (固) under the leadership (中心) of new community (新村) leaders (指導者), working diligently (勤勞) and earning wage (勞賃) income (所得) from the construction (工事場) of the Honam (湖南) Expressway (高速道路) and Jangseong Dam (長城댐), while establishing (建立) a new community (新村) Korean paper (韓紙) factory (工場) suited to local (地域) conditions (實情), income (所得) has increased (增加) from an average (平均) of 193,000 won (萬 千원) per household (戶當) in 1970 to 1,343,000 won (千원) in 1975, and to 1,649,000 won (千원) by the end of 1976, an 8.5-fold (8.5倍) increase (伸張) compared to 1970. This has transformed (脫바꿈) the village into a proud and prosperous (豊盛) new community (新村) that neighboring (隣近) villages (村落) envy (嫉妒).

O Analyzing (分析) the income (所得) structure (構造) of the village residents (住民), in 1970, agricultural (食糧) income (所得) accounted (占) for 82% of total (全部) income (所得), but by the end of 1976, agricultural (食糧 作物) income (所得) had decreased (減) to 68%, while non-agricultural (農外) income (所得) had increased (增加) to 32%, leading to a more balanced (均衡) agricultural (農) and industrial (工) income (所得) structure (構造).


--- (p. 736) ---

O In this way, this village overcame the difficult natural conditions where farmland per household was only 0.64ha and opened up new sources of non-agricultural income through self-reliance, demonstrating once again that residents could certainly live well if they cooperated and worked hard.

### b) Spirit and Living Conditions

O Just like all poor villages, the residents of this village had resigned themselves to poverty as an inevitable consequence of their limited farmland. They lived in a state of stagnation and helplessness, with men spending any small income on alcohol and gambling, and women indulging in shameful leisure activities. The village was never peaceful due to clan consciousness among families like the Cars and the Kims.

O The environment was also poor, with narrow paths that were difficult to navigate and frequent flooding that would inundate homes and wash away farmland like an annual ritual. Despite these challenges, the Saemaul leader's strong belief and willpower convinced the villagers to improve various facilities according to the village's actual conditions. They also showed particular interest in home improvement projects like roof and housing upgrades, which not only enhanced the village's scenery but also made it more convenient to use, transforming it into an exemplary village.

This will also create an atmosphere where villagers are more enthusiastic about participating in village affairs.

◆ Minutes (會議錄) (7)
Date (日時): December 19, 1976
Location (場所): Village Community Center (會舘)
Attendance (參席人員): Total (總員) 53 members (名), Attendance (參席) 45 members (名)
Agenda (討議案件): Economic (經濟) Trends (動向) Report (報吿) as of November 9, 1976, Adjustment (再調整) of Business (事業) Plan (計劃) for Special (特別) Support (支援) Fund (下賜金) (5,000,000 won) from President (大統領) Park Chung-hee (朴正熙)
Chairperson (司會者): Kim Myeong-su (金明洙)

<Resolution (決意內容)>
The residents (住民) of Sang-eo Village (上어마을) unanimously (一同) resolve to change the initial (當初) plan for the establishment (設置) of a bleaching agent (漂白液) manufacturing (製造) plant (工場) to a Korean paper (韓紙) factory (工場) expansion (擴張) project (事業) for the following reasons (利點) and grounds (事由), and decide (決意) on the following specific (具體的) implementation (推進) measures (方案) through the collective (總意) will (意) of the village residents (民):

a) Advantages (利點) of Korean Paper (韓紙) Factory (工場) Expansion (擴張)
1. The residents (住民) possess the necessary (可能) technical (技術) skills (技術) for manufacturing (製造), and there is an unmet (未備) foreign (外國) demand (注文量) due to insufficient (未備) facilities (施設).
2. Expanding (擴張) the facilities (施設) will increase (增大) employment (雇傭) opportunities (効果), boost (高) production (生產量), and contribute (寄與) to foreign currency (外貨) earnings (獲得) and stable (安全) income (所得) growth (增大) for residents (住民).
3. The current (現在) Korean paper (韓紙) factory (工場) facilities (施設), owned (所有) by Kim Myeong-su (金明洙), will be appraised (鑑定) at market value (時價) and distributed (配當) to residents (住民) based on investment (投資) ratios (比率), fostering (誘發) a sense (愛着心) of attachment (愛着心) to "our factory (工場)."

b) Reasons (事由) for Business (事業) Change (變更)
1. Limited (稀薄) employment (雇傭) effects (効果) and weak (稀薄) Saemaul (新村) factory (工場) characteristics (性格).
2. Handling (取扱) of corrosive (腐蝕) and highly toxic (猛毒性) chlorine (氯) poses (危險) risks (危險).
3. Raw materials (原料) such as chlorine (氯), quicklime (石灰), and caustic soda (苛性蘇打) must be purchased (購入) from distant (遠距離) locations like Seoul (서울) and Busan (釜山).
4. Competition (競合) concerns (憂慮) due to existing (存在) bleaching agent (漂白液) manufacturing (製造) plants (工場) in Jeonbuk (全北) Jeonju (全州) and other areas (等地).
5. Potential (憂慮) pollution (公害) emissions (排出).
6. Insufficient (不足) funds (資金): Only 7,000,000 won (中) is currently (現在) available (保有), including the 5,000,000 won (下賜金) grant (下賜金) and 2,000,000 won (負擔) from the village (村) fund (基金), leaving a shortfall (不足額) of 7,700,000 won (萬) to be secured (確保).

c) Initial (當初) Business (事業) Plan (計劃)
1. Project Name (事業名): Turbid Bleaching Agent (濁白液) Manufacturing (製造) Plant (工場) Establishment (設置).
2. Scale (規模): 50 pyeong (坪) (including (包含) machine (機臺) installation (設置) and auxiliary (附帶) facilities (施設)).
3. Project Cost (事業費): 8,390,000 won (千) (including (包含) 5,000,000 won (千) in support (支援)), with an additional (所要) 6,310,000 won (千) required (所要) for operation (運營) funds (資金) (total (合計) 14,700,000 won (千)).

d) Revised (變更) Business (事業) Plan (計劃)
1. Project Name (事業名): Korean Paper (韓紙) Manufacturing (製造) Plant (工場) Expansion (擴張).

## 4. Future Plans (計劃)

Utilizing the abundant natural (自然) pastures (草地) on the village's rear mountain (山), we plan to expand Hanwoo (韓牛) breeding (育成) (40 head (頭)) and focus on pig farming (養豚) (400 head (頭)). While fully utilizing the natural (自然) conditions (條件) of the Hwangryong River (黃龍江) in front of the village, we will devote all our efforts to duck farming (飼育) (4,000 head (首)). Additionally, taking advantage of the convenient (便利) transportation (交通) and aiming to increase unit production (生產高), we will implement advanced (高等) horticulture (園藝) (2,000 pyeong (坪)) with the goal of achieving an average (平均) of 2.5 million (萬) won per household (戶當) by 1980. We are immersed in the dream of a prosperous future.

# 1. Village Overview

## a. History

*   During the Goryeo Dynasty, it was part of Gulha County (屈下郡), and in the early Goryeo period, it was Imha County (臨河縣). By the end of the Joseon Dynasty, it belonged to Imha County and has remained so until the present day.
*   In the 6th year of King Yeonsan's reign (February 3, 1500), Cheonggyeongong (淸溪公) was born at the current location in Cheonjeon (川前) Daejongga (大宗家) and settled there. During the Joseon Dynasty, Hakseong (鶴峯) Kim Seong-il (金誠一), a famous politician and Confucian scholar, and his four brothers passed the national examination (登科及第). Among their descendants, 24 people passed the higher civil service examination (大科) and 64 people passed the lower civil service examination (小科). The village is also the hometown of Ilsong (逸松) Kim Dong-sam, an independence activist (獨立運動家), making it a place of great cultural heritage (鄒魯之鄕).
*   The surrounding area is scenic with mountains and water, and dense forests cover all four sides. Tourist attractions such as Baegunjeong (白雲亭), Gaehosong (開湖松), and Gyeongpodae (鏡浦臺) attract many visitors. The village is located along the national road between Andong (安東) and Yeongdeok (盈德), making it easily accessible.

## b. Location and Conditions

### <Location>

*   The village is located on the left bank, 12 km east of Andong (安東) along the national road to Yeongdeok (盈德).

### <Conditions>

*   Behind the village, there are mountains covered with dense forests, and the fields in front are well-organized for farming.
*   The village has convenient transportation and good water resources, making it an ideal standard rural area (標準農村) for agriculture.
*   The Banbyeoncheon (半邊川) river flows in front of the village, and forests along the riverbank make it a potential tourist destination (觀光地) for development.

2. Village Development Process (發展 過程)

a. Situation Before 1970 (70年 以前)

1) Basic Environment (基礎 環境)
- The Cheonjeoncheon (泉田川) flowing through the village often caused severe soil erosion during the rainy season, submerging farmland and flooding houses, making it a habitual flood-prone area.
- The alleys were very narrow, requiring people to carry goods on their backs and walk sideways.
- Over 70% of the houses were thatched, with fences either non-existent or dilapidated.
- The village entrance road was a narrow path, allowing only one-way traffic for horse-drawn carts.

2) Income Level (所得 水準)
- The village relied on traditional farming methods passed down through generations and cultivated crops such as watermelons and other vegetables.
- The average farmland per household was 0.7 hectares, consisting mostly of marginal farms, with significant income disparities, typical of a standard Yangban (兩班) village.
- There were many tenant farmers, with some engaging in medicinal herb cultivation. Apart from farming, the only other income source was the salaries of civil servants.
- The average household income was around 268,000 won, but the village's Yangban pretensions led to increasing poverty.

## 3) Living Conditions Before 1970
### a) Mental Aspect
* Most farming households were tenant farmers working on landlords' property, struggling to make ends meet, with no thought for the future.
* Landlords enjoyed themselves in the living room while tenant farmers toiled, leading to natural conflicts and a lack of unity.
* The residents were narrow-minded, resistant to change, and content with their current situation, spending money sent by children living elsewhere on games and alcohol.

### b) Living Conditions
* While the wealthy had radios, most residents relied on news from elders.
* Houses were generally in disrepair, mostly with thatched roofs, and looked even more dilapidated in winter.
* Clothes were not shabby thanks to money sent by children living elsewhere, but financial situations were tough, with half the households needing to borrow rice in spring.
* Most outhouses and manure pits were unclean, and especially during the rainy season, it was difficult to step around.

## b. Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

### 1) Motivation and Trial Project Results
* News spread to this village that the "Saemaul Undong" initiated by President Park on April 22, 1970, was taking place across the country.
* In 1971, the village received support for 335 bags of cement and decided at a village meeting to distribute 3 bags per household to start the project, repairing walls and partially renovating outhouses.
* Due to lack of effort, some households did not use the cement at all, while others did not maintain the proper mixing ratio of cement, sand, and gravel, leading to waste of cement.


--- (p. 747) ---

O I hesitated to speak up about the Saemaul Undong first, fearing I might be seen as rash, so no one dared to take the lead in the movement.
O However, through the 1971 Saemaul Undong, residents learned how to hold serious discussions and came to believe that they could achieve their goals if they tried.

## 2) Activities of Saemaul Leaders (指導者)

O At this time, Saemaul leader Kim In-ho took the initiative, visiting each household and strongly persuading the elders of the necessity of the Saemaul Undong.
O However, the stubborn elders barely listened. Like a madman, he ran here and there, frequented taverns, discouraged gambling, and prevented the sale of alcohol.
O Despite being called a madman and ostracized, he did not yield and continued his persuasion. As a result, the residents gradually began to respond.
O However, whenever there was a slight conflict of interest, they would oppose the movement.
O He thought, "If I don't do this, I can't live," and considered quitting several times. But with the thought, "Once I've made up my mind, I must do it," he continued to persuade and encourage the residents to work.
O However, he had to withdraw due to health issues.
O Kim Si-eok took over as the Saemaul leader. Kim, the leader, quit his job at the Seoul Railroad Bureau, where he had worked for 10 years, and returned to his hometown. He had always been thinking about how to transform his hometown into a prosperous place. Seizing the opportunity, he boldly resigned from his job and returned to his hometown's soil.
O Upon returning home, he worked as diligently as an ox. The residents were all civil servants (公務員) living in Seoul and were inwardly amazed at how he could work so hard.
O He devoted his body and mind to building a model hometown and firmly resolved to make it a prosperous village.

## 3) Overcoming Difficulties (隘路克服狀況)

O Upon returning home, he planned to construct the village access road as the first project. However, the residents found it difficult to resolve the land issue and left the construction site after coming out once and then did not return.
O He did not give up and visited households in the evening to persuade the landowners, but they barely listened.
O He held a village assembly, but only 20-30 out of 130 residents attended. Those who attended were mostly keeping an eye on the influential figures, so the meeting (會議) became meaningless.
O He gathered a few young people to start the work, but strong opposition from the landowners forced them to stop again. He felt as if the sky was falling but did not give up. After reading and explaining newspapers and weekly magazines introducing the Saemaul Undong (새마을事業) progress in other villages ten times, he barely obtained their consent.


--- (p. 748) ---

After obtaining consent, time flew by, and before he knew it, it was May, the busy farming season. As a result, his farming fell into disarray, and at home, his family opposed him, saying, "If you become a Saemaul leader, our family will starve to death." He began to miss his job in Seoul. However, he thought that for the sake of his hometown's future, he would endure even if his body broke down, and he was determined to accomplish his mission.

He would secretly go to the worksite at night, cutting down miscellaneous trees and digging the ground alone. Residents who had been watching him from afar began to appear at the worksite one by one.

As a result, although it was late, by the end of August, they completed a 400m village road and a 150m access road.

Residents, who had learned the will of "If you try, you can do it," were enthusiastic. They attended village general assemblies well, and everyone began to show great interest as if it were their own business. Thus, in 1977, the village was selected as a target for improving village structure, and through the total participation of the villagers, they completed the construction of 10 houses, the repair of 5 houses, the improvement of 34 ancillary facilities, the painting of 60 roofs, the installation of 110 simple water supply facilities, the construction of 400m embankments, the installation of 256m sewers, and the removal of 8 substandard houses. The villagers voluntarily took the initiative, and now a model village has been formed that is not inferior to any other hamlet. From now on, they are determined, led by the Saemaul leader and all villagers, to continue their efforts to achieve even greater income.

### 4) Developmental Promotion of Saemaul Projects

Taking the successful opening of the village road and access road as an opportunity, in 1973, they completed the improvement of a 200m small stream and the improvement of a 600m wall by their own efforts in the first half of the year, and completed a 50m agricultural water facility in the second half of the year.

With the second round of income-generating projects in 1973, they improved a 200m small stream and created 900 pyeong of communal fields.

They completed the improvement of walls, roofs, kitchens, toilets, and basic projects, and in 1974, they were selected as an excellent village and used 1 million won from the Prime Minister's donation to thoroughly improve a 200m small stream.

In 1976, through the fourth special support project, they demolished the old community center and completed a new one.

In 1977, they were selected as a village for improving village structure, and completed the construction of 10 houses, the repair of 5 houses, the improvement of 34 ancillary facilities, the painting of 60 roofs, the installation of 110 simple water supply facilities, the construction of 400m embankments, the installation of 256m sewers, and the removal of 8 substandard houses, thus building a model rural village.

## Saemaul Movement Achievements

### 1) Spiritual Aspect

* Through the Saemaul Movement, people were transformed into new human beings characterized by diligence, self-help, and cooperation, fostering self-confidence and the beautiful custom of mutual assistance;
* Through the Residents' Assembly, class distinctions were abolished, and the meaning of democracy was understood;
* Patriotism was cultivated, and an environment was created where people could share each other's joys and sorrows.

### 2) Livelihood Aspect

* Agricultural techniques were reformed, seeds were improved, beef cattle were introduced, and tobacco intercropping was implemented, leading to increased income;
* Farmers became research-oriented, developing a progressive spirit;
* The family ritual guidelines were practiced, promoting thrift, savings, and wealth accumulation;
* The idea of helping the underprivileged and working together for a better life was embraced as a means to build a paradise.

### 3) Production Aspect

* Income doubled through the full-scale cultivation of unified rice;
* Income increased through tobacco intercropping business profits, business loan funds for beef cattle introduction, and fruit tree and medicinal herb cultivation, achieving diversification of income sources.

# 3. Residents' General Assembly (住民總會)

## Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (1)

Date (日時) : April 8, 1971
Location (場所) : Kim Ik-ro's House, Sarang
Agenda (議題) : Saemaul Village Cement Usage
Attendees (參席人員) : 40 people
Chairperson (司會) : Dongjang (洞長) Kim Ik-ro (金翼魯)

Chairperson (司會) : Has everyone had dinner? I have called you all here because you must be tired, but it is to discuss how to handle the Saemaul cement that the government has provided for free. Please feel free to discuss this openly.
Lee Chun-bo (李春寶) : Is this free now but we will have to pay later?
Chairperson (司會) : No, that will not happen. I will take responsibility for that. Please discuss what to use it for, regardless of whether it is paid or free.
Kim Hong-ro (金洪路) : How much cement is there?
Chairperson (司會) : There are 335 bags. This is the same for every village.
Kim Hong-byeong (金洪炳) : I saw in Andongjang that the people of Songhyeon are building walls. Let's divide the cement individually and build walls.
Kim Byeong-seon (金炳善) : That's a good idea.
Hong Su-won (洪水源) : I agree.
All (一同) : Silence.
Chairperson (司會) : Are there any other opinions?
All (一同) : Silence.
Chairperson (司會) : Then let's decide to build walls. How should we distribute the cement? Please speak.
Kim Dong-seon (金東善) : Some houses have more walls than others, so it would be better to distribute the cement according to the amount of wall each house has.
Kim Maeng-ho (金孟鎬) : Kim Dong-seon's opinion is good, but in my opinion, if we divide the 335 bags a little bit, it won't be of much use. It would be better to give it first to the houses along the road, just like other villages, and build the road first.


--- (p. 754) ---

Lee Do-hak: I agree with Mr. Kim Dong-seon's suggestion. I think it would be best if the cement is distributed equally to every household. This way, there will be no complaints.

Bae Won-jik: I think that would be a good idea. Even if we have to pay money later, it would be better to do it this way.

Chairperson: Why keep talking about money when it's supposed to be free! (Shouting loudly)

Kim Si-wan: Please don't get angry, Dongjang (洞長) sir. We're saying this because we've been deceived a few times before.

Chairperson: I'm sorry.

Participants: Silence.

Chairperson: Are there any other opinions? Then, we will distribute the cement equally to each household. Please come to the warehouse tomorrow to take your share, and make sure to build your walls by the end of this month. With that, today's meeting is adjourned.

### Attendees (參席者)
Kim Ik-ro, Kim Jae-hyuk, Kim Sang-sul, Kim Si-dong, Kwon Oh-bong, Kim Hak-byeong, Lee Chun-bo, Kim Hong-ro, Kim Geun-dae, Kim Seong-tae, Kim Dong-hwan, Kim Nam-ho, Kim Si-woong, Kim Si-seong, Kim Si-wan, Kim No-jin, Park Jae-seon, Kim No-chun, Lee Jae-won, Kim Hui-dae, Lee Chun-hwa, Kim Wi-seok, Kim Hyung-sik, Kim Seong-gu, Kim Hyung-bak, Kim Dong-sik, Kim Woo-bong, Kim Ye-hwan, Lee Won-mok, Jo Gyu-hwan, Lee Won-hak, Kim No-sik, Kim Young-dal, Hong Geun-pyo, Kim Ji-won, Kim Si-chang, Kim Gyeong-ro, Kim Heung-byeong, Kim Si-gap, Kim Gi-su.

### Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (2)
*   **Date (日時)**: 1972. 10. 25.
*   **Location (場所)**: Cheonjeon National School
*   **Agenda (議提)**: Election of Dong (洞) Development Committee (開發委員會) Members (選出)
*   **Chairperson (社會)**: Dongjang (洞長) Kim Ik-ro

Chairperson: Good day, everyone. I have called you all here, despite your hardships, to elect Dong (洞) Development Committee (開發委員) members for the development (發展) of our Dong (洞). The duties of the Development Committee (開發委員) include establishing and implementing business plans (事業計劃), confirming results (結果), and other important tasks (業務). Please keep this in mind and recommend capable individuals (有能). The committee chairperson (委員長) will be myself, the Dongjang (洞長), and we need to elect two auditors (監査委員), two business committee members (事業委員), and 5-6 general committee members (一般委員). Please suggest a method for the election.

Kim Ye-hwan: I understand, Dongjang (洞長) sir. For the recommendation process, I suggest we elect a selection committee (銓衡委員) who will then recommend and decide on the Development Committee (開發委員) members. We can then obtain approval from the Dong (洞) General Assembly (總會).

Kim Seok-dae: I agree with Mr. Kim Ye-hwan's opinion.

Participants: Silence.

Chairperson: Are there any other opinions?


--- (p. 755) ---

# Meeting Minutes

**Chair:** Silence.

**Chair:** We will have the selection committee decide on the development committee member list. Please suggest who should be on the selection committee.

**Kim Si-seong:** The selection committee should consist of Mr. Kim Heung-no, Mr. Kim Ye-hwan, Mr. Kim Maeng-ho, and Mr. Kim Hee-dae. Although it will be troublesome for these respected individuals, it would be best if they recommend qualified individuals for the development committee.

**Kim Maeng-ho:** Since the development committee members will work with the village chief, it would be good to include the village chief in the selection committee to consider their opinions.

**Kim Hak-byeong:** I agree with both opinions.

**Kim Seong-won:** I support this.

**Chair:** Silence.

**Chair:** Are there any other opinions? We will adjourn the meeting for 20 minutes while the selection committee makes their recommendations.

**Kim Hong-ro:** (whispering) It should be at least 30 minutes...

**Chair:** We will adjourn for 30 minutes and please reconvene when the time is up.

**Chair:** The selection committee has recommended the following 14 individuals for the development committee: Kim Heung-ro, Kim Si-tak, Kim Gi-ro, Kim Maeng-ho, Kim Si-seong, Kim Seok-dae, Kim Byeong-seon, Kim Ye-hwan, Kim Young-dal, Kim In-ho, Kim Si-u, Kim Seong-won, Kim Hee-dae, and Lee Do-hak. Please share your opinions.

**Kim Heung-byeong:** I think capable individuals have been selected.

**Kim Hang-dae:** That's good.

**Kim Dong-han:** I support this.

**Chair:** If there are no other opinions, the development committee will consist of the aforementioned 14 individuals plus myself, making a total of 15 people.

**Kim No-jin:** What are the duties of the business committee and the audit committee?

**Chair:** The business committee will be the main body responsible for promoting village self-businesses, managing business funds, and promoting business activities. The audit committee will be responsible for reviewing the legitimacy of business fund expenditures and auditing the authenticity of business results.

**Kim Si-hwan:** I understand. The audit committee should consist of individuals with administrative experience and social awareness. Therefore, I recommend Mr. Kim Heung-ro (Mr. Stay) and Mr. Kim Seong-won (Mr. Park).

**Chair:** The audit committee will consist of Mr. Kim Heung-ro and Mr. Kim Seong-won. Please also recommend members for the business committee.

**Lee Dong-cheol:** I think the business committee should consist of Mr. Kim Maeng-ho and Mr. Kim Seok-dae.

**Kim Maeng-ho:** This person lacks ability and is too busy to handle such an important responsibility. Please exclude me.


--- (p. 756) ---

Kim Hong-ro: Everyone is busy. Who isn't busy?
Chairperson: That's right. We all need to participate for the sake of our village.
Kim Won-ho: The two business committee members have been well selected.
All: We acknowledge that they have been well selected.
Chairperson: Then, we will conclude the village general assembly for selecting the development committee. Committee members, please actively participate in village projects. Fellow villagers, I'm very sorry for keeping you so late. We will conclude today's meeting here. Please go home safely.

### Minutes (會議錄) (3)

Date: December 18, 1972
Location: Cheonjeon National School (國民學校)
Agenda: Promoting the Saemaul Undong (事業)
Chairperson: Dongjang (洞長) Kim Ik-ro

Chairperson: I have called you all here because other villages are actively engaging in the Saemaul Undong (事業). However, our village cannot remain as it is. Therefore, we must strongly promote the Saemaul Undong (事業). I ask for your cooperation and guidance. Please take care of your own household affairs and also engage in community projects. Please share your candid opinions without hesitation.
Hong Dae-won: The Saemaul Undong (事業) is good, but how can we have a new village when we don't even have food to eat? (Excited) Alright, let's each take care of our own household affairs. Who will handle the group projects? Who will farm? We have lived this long without the Saemaul Undong (事業), so I can't do it.
Chairperson: It is currently the off-season for farming. And shouldn't each household take care of itself? Meanwhile, other villages are engaging in the Saemaul Undong (事業) and becoming cleaner and more livable, while our hamlet is still living under thatched roofs, carrying poles on our backs. (Excited)
Kim Hong-ro: Let's all calm down. There's no need to get upset. I also observed carefully on my way back from Seoul, and everywhere I saw people of all ages clearing paths and demolishing houses. Our village must quickly start the Saemaul Undong (事業), improve our roofs, build walls, and widen the roads.
Chairperson: That's right. If we idle while other villages work, we will fall that much behind.
Kim Chi-dae: Who will provide the cement and who will provide the wire?
Chairperson: Taking care of one's own house is the spirit of the Saemaul Undong (事業).
Kim Chi-dae: I have lived without the Saemaul Undong (事業), and our village has lived for 400 years without doing such things and has been fine.
Kim Maeng-ho: Those who are well-off may not have problems, but those who are not well-off actually lack the ability, which is a problem. But that doesn't mean they can't do it. Those who cannot afford cement should build rammed earth walls instead.


--- (p. 757) ---

Let's improve our roofs (改良) as the county office says they will provide loans (融資金) for this purpose. Let's not just say we can't do it; let's give it a try. Villages worse off than ours are doing it, and I've even seen places where people are contributing their small plots of land (門前沃沓) in front of their houses to widen roads. It's also being introduced on the radio and in newspapers (新聞). Why can't our village do it? Let's give it a shot.

**Chairperson**: Let's discuss our communal projects (共同事業) aside from individual houses. First, our village access road (進入路) is too narrow for vehicle traffic (車輛通行), so we should establish (開設) a new access road. Also, the alleys are too narrow to carry long items on shoulder poles, so let's try widening the inner village roads (擴張).

**Jeong Jung-ik**: To create an access road (進入路), we'll need to build retaining walls (거랑뚝), but how will we manage that? Our villagers won't be able to farm at all if we focus only on this, and we'll have to finish it by the end of the year (입바이). And who will provide the land for the inner roads?

**Kim Hyung-bak**: As Jeong Jung-ik said, who will do all that work?

**Chairperson**: I think it's possible if our residents unite. Only then can we protect our farmland (農土) from flood damage (水害) and be able to pull our carts (리야카라) for farming.

**Kim Si-woo**: I agree with widening the inner roads (擴張) and creating an access road (進入路). However, the issue is how to promote (推進) the project (事業). From past experiences, only those who work do, and those who don't, don't, causing complaints (不平). Therefore, we should impose (賦課) a duty (義務) for everyone to participate (出役) daily. And to widen the inner roads (擴張), we need to obtain agreement (同意) for the incorporated land (編入敷地), right?

**Chairperson**: We will establish a participation plan (出役計劃) and announce (告知) the number of participation days (出役). But first, we need to decide whether to undertake the Saemaul Undong (새마을事業).

**Kim Byeong-seon**: No matter how difficult and hard it is, we must undertake the project (事業). So, it would be better to decide by a show of hands (擧手) for agreement (贊) or disagreement (反).

**Participants**: Silence (沈默).

**Chairperson**: If there are no other opinions, we will proceed to a vote (表決). Please raise your hands (擧手) if you think it's good to undertake the Saemaul Undong (새마을事業) for the access road (進入路) and inner road widening (擴張).

**Participants who raised hands (擧手者)**: 53

**Chairperson**: Since more than 2/3 of the attending members (參席) have agreed (贊成), we will consider this passed (可決). Now, please share your ideas on the participation (出役) method (方法) and land (敷地) solution (解決) plan (方案).

**Kim Hong-ro**: For participation (出役), let's calculate the total required area (所要面積) and allocate (配定) it equally per household (戶當). For the land (敷地), it would be good for the neighborhood chief (洞長) and a few others to persuade (說得) the landowners.

**Participants**: Silence (沈默).

**Chairperson**: If there are no other opinions, we will consider this issue passed (可決) as is. It's late at night, so let's conclude the neighborhood meeting (洞會) for today. Good night.

**<Attendees (參席者)>**
Kim Dong-sik, Kim Si-woo, Kim No-jin, Kim Sang-sul, Kim Jeong-ro, Lee Sun-deok, Kim Si-hwan, Kim No-hyeon, Bae Jae-sul, Hong Tae-won, Kim Si-wan


--- (p. 758) ---

Hong Geun-pyo, Lee Chun-bo, Kim Byung-se, Kim Hak-byeong, Kim Young-dal, Kim Si-gyeon, Kim Chi-dae, Kim Jae-ro, Kim Nam-ho, Kim Si-eok, Kim Myeong-guk, Kim Mun-gu, Kim Hyung-bak, Lee Nan-ho, Kim Dae-kyung, Hong Geun-pyo, Jang Gan-i, Lee Young-jun, Kwon Jae-cheol, Jang Bun-i, Kim Seong-won, Jeong Jung-eok, Lee Jang-jeong, Kim Si-gap, Kim Si-dong, Kim No-chun, Lee Chun-hwa, Kim Ji-won, Kim Hang-dae, Kim Won-mok, Kim Woo-bong, Kim Cheol-ho, Kim Seong-rak, Kim Byung-mo, Kim Yeon-byeong, Kim Si-won, Kim Seong-dae, Kim Byung-o, Lee Jeong-sul, Kim Si-hwan, Kim No-su, Park Jae-seon, Kim Hyung-ro, Lee Chun-bok, Lee Won-mok, Kim No-chun, Kim Si-cheon, Lee Dong-cheol, Kim Mun-gu, Kim Won-ho, Kwon O-bong, Kim Geun-dae, Hong Su-won, Kim Dong-han, Kim Ik-ro, Kim Hong-ro, Kim Byung-seon

◆ Minutes of Meeting (會議錄) (4)

*   **Date**: September 20, 1973, 21:00
*   **Venue**: Cheonjeon National School
*   **Attendees**: Kim Si-bang and 74 others
*   **Agenda**: Report on the settlement of the double loan income business (複借所得事業) and small stream (小河川) construction (工事), discussion on investment plans (投資方案) for the double loan fund (複借基金)
*   **Chairperson**: Dongjang (洞長) Kim Si-bang

**Chairperson**: Thanks to everyone's hard work, we have completed today's business and are able to present the settlement report. I don't know how to express my joy. We should all express our gratitude to the government and participate in the Saemaul Undong with even more enthusiasm. Now, let's hear the progress report from the business committee member Kim Seok-dae.

The total amount we received was 750,000 won, and we have completed 300m of stone embankment (石築). I will explain the expenditures by category. We paid 225,000 won for miscellaneous stone (雜石代金) and 262,000 won for labor costs (勞賃). The current balance in the account is 263,000 won for the double loan fund (複借基金) and 900 won in interest, totaling 263,900 won. Please refer to the attached payment records (取役) and labor cost payment ledger (勞賃支給臺帳) for the expenditure details. Please check the account book (通帳) number 105 in the village safe (金庫) for the financial records (帳係). If anyone has any objections, please raise them.

**All**: Reviewing the labor cost payment ledger (支拂臺帳), expenditure resolution (支出決議書), and account book (通帳) contents.

**Kim Hong-ro**: We, the audit committee (監査委員), have conducted a first inspection (檢査) and found no issues with the expenditures or the business. We will stamp our approval. If any villagers have any objections, please speak up.

**All**: Silence (沈默) (chatter (雜談)).

**Chairperson**: Since there are no objections, the settlement of this business is approved. Now, let's discuss how to invest the double loan savings (複借積立金).

**Kim Dong-han**: It would be good to buy cattle and lend them to farmers without livestock (無畜農家) for breeding. The breeder (飼育者) and the village (洞里) should share the profits equally.

**Kim Cheol-ho**: Cattle prices fluctuate greatly, and there are also cases of death (斃死). They are movable property (動産), which poses management issues. If the breeder goes bankrupt (倒産), it will cause problems. Therefore, it would be better to invest in real estate (不動産).


--- (p. 759) ---

I think so.
Kim Dong-hwan: There is a method to appoint a guarantor (保證人) so that if the breeder (飼育者) does not fulfill their compensation responsibility (辨償責任), the guarantor (保證人) will bear the joint liability (連帶責任).
Kim Si-hwan: Mr. Kim Dong-hwan's opinion (意見) is a good suggestion, but I agree with Mr. Kim Cheol-ho's opinion (意見).
Kim Hang-dae: I agree with the agreement (同意).
Kim Si-hwan: I agree (贊成).
All (一同): Casual talk (雜談).
Chairperson (司會): Please be quiet. Are there any other opinions (意見)? Since the majority (大多數) of opinions (意見) are to invest in real estate (不動産), we will decide to invest in real estate (不動산). Then, please tell us the method (方法) of how to do it.
Kim Byeong-seon: It would be good to purchase the 300 pyeong (坪) of land owned by Mr. Kim Hui-dae next to the copper coin (銅錢) at the head of the forest (숲). Let's make it into one field and decide what crop (作物) to cultivate (栽培).
Kim Hong-ro: That's a good suggestion.
Kim Dong-seon: I agree (同意).
All (一同): I agree (贊成).
Chairperson (司會): What would be a good purchase price (買入價格)?
Lee Dong-cheol: Please deliberate (熟議) among the development committee members (開發委員) and purchase (購入) it at an appropriate price (適切) (價格).
Bae Won-jik: That would be good.
All (一同): That's good.
Chairperson (司會): Then, the development committee (開發委員會) will take responsibility for purchasing (購入) the land (土地). Since Mr. Kim Hwa-dae is present, please deliberate (熟議) and decide the purchase price (購入價格). Please rest for a while, fellow villagers (洞民).
Chairperson (司會): We have decided to purchase the 300 pyeong (坪) of land for 200,000 won. If there are any objections, please speak up.
Park Jae-seon: It's a reasonable price (適當) (價格).
All (一同): No objections (異議).
Chairperson (司會): What crop (作物) would you like to cultivate (栽培)?
Kim Chi-dae: Since the price of silkworm cocoons is good now, it would be good to plant mulberry seedlings (桑苗) and have the Women's Association manage (管理) them. We can use part (一部) of the profit (利益金) for the Women's Association fund (基金) and part (一部) for the village (洞) fund (基金).
Hong Su-won: I agree (贊成).
All (一同): I agree (贊成).
Chairperson (司會): You have worked hard during this tedious time (時間) (苦生). I appreciate your serious deliberation (熟議). We will purchase the mulberry seedlings (桑苗) and report the results (結果) at the year-end general assembly (總會時) next year. Then, we will conclude today's meeting (會議).


--- (p. 760) ---

### Participants
Kim Si-bang, Kim In-ho, Kim Si-wan, Hong Geun-pyo, Hong Su-won, Lee Won-chang, Lee Won-mok, Kim Sung-won, Lee Bun-hwa, Lee Chun-bo, Kim Cheol-ho, Kim Sun-dae, Kim No-chun, Kim No-hyeon, Kim Jeong-tae, Kim Chang-hee, Kim No-jin, Kim Si-hwan, Kim Bun-do, Kim Dae-kyung, Kim Jong-seung, Kwon Oh-bong, Kim Neu-mi, Lee Chun-hwa, Kim Chi-gap, Kim Jong-seop, Ju Wiwon, Kim Mun-gu, Kim Dong-hwan, Heo Dong-pal, Kim Sang-yeol, Kim Jong-bal, Kim Byung-mo, Kim Young-dal, Kim Geun-dae, Kim Hyung-no, Kim Byung-seon, Kim Hong-ro, Kim Si-u, Kim Dong-seon, Jang Gan-i, Kim Hyung-sik, Jo Gyu-han, Lee Do-hak, Lee Chun-bok, Kim Gu-ik, Kim Jeong-dae, Park Jae-sung, Kim Ye-hwan, Yuk Deok-u, Kim Wi-seok, Bae Seok-du, Kim Si-seong, Kim Yeon-byeong, Kim Hak-byeong, Kim Sang-sul, Kim Gyun, Kwon Jae-yeon, Kim Dong-seok, Kim Si-eok, Kim Maeng-ho, Kim Seong-tae, Kim Si-won, Hong Seung-pyo, Kim Seok-dae, Kim Seong-dae, Kim Byung-pal, Kim Seong-ro, Kim Jae-won, Kim Heung-byeong, Kim Nam-ho, Kim Hyung-bak, Kim Hyung-tak, Kim No-su, Kim Si-u, Kim Chi-dae, Kim Wu-bong, Kim Sang-yeol, Kim Si-chang, Kim Ji-won, Kwon Sang-muk, Kim Young-jo

### Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (5)
*   **Date**: November 25, 1975, 19:30
*   **Location**: Dong Office
*   **Agenda**: Selection of Saemaul Business Sites for 1977
*   **Chairperson**: Saemaul Leader Kim Si-eok
*   **Attendees**: 72 people

**Chairperson**: Good evening, fellow villagers. The year is coming to an end. Thanks to your cooperation, all projects have been completed, and a clean environment has been created. I have called you all here today because, with the environmental projects largely finished, we now need to focus on projects that will directly improve our income. There are many tasks ahead, but we must tackle the most urgent ones first. Please share your thoughts on what should be prioritized.

**Kim Hang-dae**: The irrigation channel in the Gaemokjeong Farmland Management District is in poor condition, making it difficult to water the fields. I think we should build a retaining wall for this channel.

**Hong Su-won**: While other irrigation channels are also in need of repair, the Gaemok channel is the most urgent. I agree that we should prioritize building a retaining wall there.

**Lee Dong-cheol**: I agree.

**All**: Chatter.

**Chairperson**: Please quiet down. Projects must be carried out based on the collective will of the villagers. If anyone has different opinions, please speak up freely.

**Kim Dae-kyung**: The western irrigation channel is also low, and when water levels rise, it overflows, making it impossible to supply water to the lower fields. We should also address this channel.

**Chairperson**: Since the support from the central government is only 400 po, we cannot undertake many projects. Therefore, we must choose between the two locations.


--- (p. 761) ---

It would be better to focus on one place. If we have the ability to bear a significant portion of the burden ourselves, there won't be any problems....
**Kim Si-u**: Doesn't water flow from top to bottom? So, it would be better to start with the Gae-mok irrigation channel and postpone the Seon-yeok irrigation channel for later.
**Lee Chun-bo**: I agree.
**Kim Sang-yeol**: I concur.
**All present**: Silence.
**Chairperson**: If there are no other opinions, we will proceed with the Gae-mok irrigation channel first. Are there any objections? Then, I will explain the scope of work. According to our discussions with the local officials, we can complete approximately 150 meters with 400 bags of cement and 1.5 tons of steel reinforcement. However, I think we can manage around 200 meters without any defects, as the flow rate is not too severe. What are your thoughts?
**Hong Su-won**: I have some experience with manual labor, and I believe that amount is manageable without any defects. Even if the residents work a bit more, it would be better to increase the workload.
**Kim Si-hwan**: Let the experienced individuals, Saemaul leaders, and project promotion committee members handle the workload appropriately. Approximately how many days per household would be needed to complete the project?
**Chairperson**: If there are no other opinions on the workload, we will adjust it through discussions with those who have technical experience. We need about 360 people in total, and the formwork usage fee is 300,000 won. So, how should we handle the residents' financial burden and labor mobilization? Please share your opinions.
**Dongjang**: Our village has been allocated 300,000 won from the agricultural cooperative savings. We can use this to pay the formwork fee and have 90 households, excluding the 33 households without labor force out of 123 total households, contribute 4 days of labor each.
**Kim Young-dal**: It would be good to support households without labor force, but we should calculate the wages for all 360 people in cash and distribute them equally. For those who cannot participate, we should collect the cash equivalent. For those who contribute more than their share, we should compensate them with wages.
**Kim Si-u**: The spirit of Saemaul is self-help, self-reliance, and cooperation. The true meaning of cooperation is mutual support. Therefore, let us all act in the spirit of Saemaul and help those in difficult circumstances. It would be better for the 90 households to contribute 4 days of labor each.
**Kim Hong-ro**: I agree with Kim Si-u's opinion.
**Kim Maeng-ho**: I agree.
**All present**: We agree.
**Chairperson**: Then, we will proceed with 90 households contributing 4 days of labor each and prepare 90 output cards. Additionally, I would like to mention that in Saemaul projects, some days have too many participants leading to idle time, while other days have too few, hindering progress. Therefore, it would be better to form work teams and assign tasks by team.


--- (p. 762) ---

How should we organize the teams? Please share your opinions.

Kim Si-wan: I have experienced running businesses in the Saemaul. I think it would be best to organize work teams by class. Also, I think it would be good for the class president to come out and supervise the work together that day.

Lee Dong-cheol: I agree with the opinion of the 1st class president.
All: Agree.

Chairperson: I'm very sorry for keeping you all so late. We have prepared some alcohol for you, so please have a drink and go home. It's a small amount, but it's our sincerity, so please enjoy it. We will conclude the meeting here.

All: Hurrah (as happy as children).

### Attendees

Kim Geun-dae, Kim Hyung-sik, Heo Dong-pal, Kim Hak-byeong, Lee Jeong-sul, Kim Heung-byeong, Kwon Oh-bong, Kim Ye-hwan, Kim Seong-won, Kim Si-dong, Jo Gyu-hwan, Bae Won-jik, Kim Sang-sul, Kim No-chun, Kim Si-dae, Kim Jae-hyeok, Lee Won-mok, Shin Cha-hak, Kim Si-wan, Kim Myeong-dal, Kim Si-gap, Kim Si-seong, Kim No-sik, Kim Gi-su, Kim Si-woong, Bae Seong-yul, Kim Gyeong-ro, Kim Nam-ho, Kim Seong-rak, Kim Si-hwan, Kim Dong-hwan, Kim Hyung-bak, Lee Jin-hee, Kim Seong-tae, Lee Chun-bo, Kim Si-am, Lee Won-hak, Kim Sang-yeol, Kim Si-cheon, Kim No-jin, Kim Seong-gu, Kim Si-yang, Park Jae-seok, Kim Dong-seok, Kim Yeon-byeong, Lee Jae-won, Kim Jong-bal, Park Dae-il, Kim Hui-dae, Kim Woo-bong, Kim Jae-sik, Lee Chun-hwa, Kim Si-chang, Bae Seok-du, Im Tae-sul, Kim Jong-heon, Kim Byeong-se, Hong Geun-pyo, Kim Wi-seok, Kim Ji-won

◆ Minutes (會議錄) (6)

*   **Date**: 76. 11. 8. 20:15
*   **Venue**: Dong Office
*   **Agenda**: Selection of Saemaul Business for 1977
*   **Chairperson**: Saemaul Leader
*   **Number of Attendees**: 60

---

Chairperson: I'm sorry to have gathered you all when you're tired. Since more than 2/3 of the villagers are present, I declare the meeting open. Today, we will discuss the implementation of the Saemaul business for 1977. And I have one piece of good news to share. We have been designated as an excellent village and will receive a special support fund of 1,500,000 won from the President (大統領). All of this is thanks to the hard work and sweat of the residents. Now, please share your thoughts on what kind of business we should undertake in 1977 and how we should use the President's special support fund.

Kim Si-u: Our village has now achieved a certain level of appearance, but there are still many shortcomings. In particular, the Dong Office is too cramped and shabby, which is not visually appealing. I think it would be good to use the President's special support fund to construct a modern Dong Hall.

Kim Dae-gyeong: It would be good to build the Dong Office with the President's special support fund, but last year we completed


--- (p. 763) ---

Mr. Kim Ik-ro: While the irrigation canal repair project is a good initiative, our development committee members observed that the western irrigation canal does not currently present an urgent issue. The residents themselves can maintain and use it, so we believe constructing a community center is more pressing. During large resident assemblies, we face inconveniences such as moving to the school, and we also feel guilty for constantly relying on the school. I agree with the opinion to construct a community center.

Mr. Kim Si-hwan: Every time I see even smaller villages having modern community centers, I think: "Let's seize this opportunity and construct our community center this year."

Mr. Hong Ju-won: I agree.

Another attendee: I agree.

Chairperson: Then, we have decided that the special support project will be the construction of the community center. But what should be the scale? Please share your opinions.

Mr. Lee Dong-cheol: The development committee should decide the scale and details, considering the budget and residents' financial capacity, and notify the resident assembly of the contents.

Mr. Kim Si-wan: I agree.

Another attendee: I agree.

Chairperson: Then, let's recess for about 30 minutes until the scale and structure of the community center are decided.

---

Chairperson: (Drawing the community center layout plan on the blackboard)

![Diagram: Community Center Layout Plan](/images/page_763_img_1.png)

Community Center Layout Plan:

| Meeting Room | Storage | Kitchen |
|---|---|---|
| | Office | Room |

The development committee has decided to construct a community center in the form you see, with an area of about 30 pyeong. The construction cost is estimated to be around 3.6 million won, calculated at 120,000 won per pyeong.

Mr. Park Dae-il: We will use the special support fund of 1.5 million won, and the remaining amount will have to be covered in cash. The development committee has resolved to use the village savings fund to avoid cash burdens. We have made this decision because there are many self-funded expenses for temporary water supply and other environmental projects. We seek your agreement.

Another attendee: I agree.

Chairperson: How should we handle other business promotion, technical subcontracting issues, and fieldwork?

Mr. Kim Si-seong: It would be best for the development committee to resolve all issues and have the resident assembly approve them in the settlement report.

Mr. Kim Chi-dae: (Laughing) What if the development committee members deceive us?

Another attendee: Laughter.

Mr. Kim Jong-hun: For matters related to business promotion, it would be best for the development committee members and the Saemaul Undong leaders to deliberate and handle them together.


--- (p. 764) ---

Very well.

Attendee: Yes.

Chairperson: In that case, regarding the promotion of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) for the year 1977, I will adjust and promote it with the development committee members to suit the actual situation. I will ask for your cooperation. Each household should continue to promote self-help projects such as wall painting, fence improvement, toilet improvement, kitchen improvement, and roof painting from now on, and take measures to complete them all by the end of April next year. I appreciate your serious deliberation until late at night. In that case, I will conclude today's meeting. Please go home safely.

### Attendees

Kim Shibang, Kim Inho, Kim Maengho, Kim Siu, Kim Hangdae, Kim Shieok, Hong Suwon, Kim Ikro, Kim Byeongmo, Kim Sitaek, Kim Byeongseon, Kim Hongro, Kim Siwan, Kim Seongtae, Kwon Jaeyun, Kim Yongseok, Kim Hyungno, Kim Deokro, Kim Geundae, Kwon Obong, Kim Sidong, Kim Namho, Kim Nochun, Lee Wonmok, Lee Jaewon, Kim Nochun, Lee Chunhwa, Kim Dongran, Lee Wonhak, Kim Yeohwan, Lee Jeongsul, Lee Dongcheol, Kim Sicheon, Hong Geunpyo, Kim Hyungshik, Kim Shihang, Ju Giwon, Kim Yeongdal, Kim Jongheon, Kim Cheolho, Kim Gyeongshik, Kim Heungbyeong, Kim Shidae, Kim Shihwan, Kim Gisu, Heo Dongpal, Kim Hyunggeun, Bae Wonjik, Kim Wonho, Kim Sigaek, Kim Sibong, Kim Siung, Kim Nosik, Kim Gyeongro, Kim Taegyu, Kim Sichang, Kim Daegyeong, Kim Jongbal, Kim Jongguk, Kim Mungu, Kim Seonggu, Kim Ubong, Kim Inshik, Shin Sumok, Park Sanggyu, Kim Hyungbak

◆ Meeting Minutes (7)

| Item   | Content                      |
| ------ | ---------------------------- |
| Date   | 76. 11. 10. 19:00            |
| Venue  | Cheonjeon 1-dong Office      |
| Agenda | Application for Business Income Business |
| Chairperson | Dongjang (Neighborhood Chief) Kim Shibang |
| Attendees | 48 people                    |

Chairperson: Although the scheduled meeting time has arrived, the quorum has not been met. I will resume the meeting as soon as the quorum is met. I apologize for having to hold this meeting and then another one, but I called you all again to discuss business income business funds with a loan limit of 5 million won to carry out a business with productivity for the purpose of increasing income. This meeting is a particularly good opportunity for our neighbors, so I called you, so please bear with it and share your plans.

Kim Heungro: I think raising beef cattle would be suitable for our village. Some farms are already raising them. According to them, after deducting the expenses per head, a total of 20,000 won is generated, so I think it is a business with good income.

Kim Cheolho: I request to speak again.

Attendee: I agree.

Chairperson: In that case, we will decide on the business item as raising beef cattle. Please let me know how large the scale of the business should be.


--- (p. 765) ---

Kim Mang-ho: Currently, it costs around 300,000 won per head to raise a Hanwoo (Korean cattle) as a fattening cow. So, with a maximum of 5 million won, we can probably raise about 17 heads.

Kim Si-aek: All Saemaul projects must have resident burden (住民負擔). Therefore, it would be better to add a self-burden (自負擔) of 1 million won to raise 20 heads. It would be good to have the self-burden (自負擔) borne by the farming households that will raise the cows.

All present: Agree (贊成).

Chairperson (司會): The business plan (事業計劃) has been decided to raise 20 heads. Then, please explain the breeding method (飼育方法). Will you breed them through collective breeding (共同飼育) or individual allocation (個別分讓) breeding?

Kim Si-hwan: If we breed them collectively (共同), we don't have a large enough cattle shed (牛舍), so it would be better to breed them through individual allocation (個別分讓).

All present: Silence (沈默).

Chairperson (司會): Are there any other opinions (意見)? Then, please discuss the selection (選定) of breeders (飼育者).

Kim Ik-ro: Since the business funds (事業資金) are coming under the village's common name (共同名義), and as the village head (東長) initially mentioned prioritizing the creation (造成) of a village common fund (共同基金), it would be good for the farming households that breed through allocation (分讓飼育) to contribute 40% of the revenue (收益金) to the village and keep 60% for themselves.

Kim Hang-dae: The breeders (飼育者) should be those who do not have livestock (無家畜者) and are honest (誠實) individuals. Those breeders (飼育者) who do not have a cattle shed (牛舍) should be allowed to start breeding (入殖) only after constructing (建立) one.

Kim Si-u: I agree with the previous two speakers in principle (原則的). However, I have a slight objection (異議). The business funds (事業資金) have an annual interest rate (年利) of 5.5%. It would be good to receive 10% of the breeding funds (入殖資金) (loan portion (融資分)) from the breeders (飼育者), use 5.5% for interest (利子) repayment (償還), and deposit (積立) 4.5% into the village fund (基金). The principal (元金) should be repaid (償還) by the breeders (飼育者). Also, farming households (農家) that have not completed (完了) their cattle shed (牛舍) should prepare (準備) it within 2 months at the latest. Furthermore, it would be good to recommend (推薦) the candidates (對象者) in multiples (倍數) and provide (支援) funds (資金) in the order (順序) of cattle shed (牛舍) completion (完了). However, we still don't know when the funds (資金) will be available...

All present: Agree (贊同).

Chairperson (司會): Breeders (飼育者) must pay the principal repayment amount (元金償還額) and an annual (年) 10% interest (利子). It has been decided to deposit (積立) 4.5% of the interest (利子中) into the village fund (同基金). Please recommend (推薦) the breeding candidates (飼育對象者).

Kim Ik-ro: I recommend Kim Si-bang for 3 heads, Kim Young-dal for 3 heads, and Kim Jong-bal for 3 heads.

Kim Cheol-ho: I recommend Kim Mang-ho for 3 heads and Kim Si-ran for 3 heads.

Kim Si-chang: Kim No-sik for 3 heads.

All present: Silence (沈默).

Chairperson (司會): Are there any other opinions (意見)?

All present: None.

Chairperson (司會): Then, the breeders (飼育者) are decided to be the above 9 individuals. It would be good to deposit (拂入) the accumulated funds (積立金) into the village at the same time (同一) as the repayment (拂入) of the repayment amount (償還金額).

All present: Agree (好습니다).
