Shim Jae-sook, Kim Young-hwan, Son Seong-mo, Oh Il-young, Choi Man-seok, Jo Seong-gi, Lee Byung-mun, Shim Jae-ho, Son Mal-sul, Shim Ui-seop, Oh Han-young, Choi Pan-gae, No Seong-gi, Hyun Chang-seop, Lee Byung-mun, Yeo Un-sul, Son Byung-mo, Son Mu-gyeong


--- (p. 802) ---

# Agenda(議題): Roof Improvement (改良) Project (事業)
# Date(日時): March 26, 1972
# Location(場所): O Il-young's (吳一泳) main room
# Attendees(參席 人員): Shim Ui-seop (沈義燮) and 28 others
# Absentees(不參 人員): Lee Bok-deok (李福德) and 1 other
# Chairperson(司會): Saemaul Leader (指導者)

**Leader (指導者):** It's quite cold today, and I'm truly sorry to have gathered you all here. The matter is that other villages are improving their roofs, building block walls, and fixing their sewers. We need to change our village environment as well, which is why we've convened this neighborhood meeting (洞會).

**Neighborhood Chief (洞長):** With the Saemaul Movement (事業) unfolding nationwide, we must pour our hearts into it. Our village has many thatched roofs, so we should prioritize roof improvements.

**Leader (指導者):** The neighborhood chief and I have called you all here, and we apologize for always bringing up concerning matters. However, we're not asking you to work for our own benefit.

**Shim Ui-seop (沈義燮):** We've carried out projects every year, so perhaps we should take this year off and resume next year when our circumstances improve.

**Leader (指導者):** Your words are kind, but delaying by a year means falling a year behind in development. Even if some households are facing difficulties, working together on roof improvements will be less burdensome than doing it alone. As the saying goes, "Once you've started making rice cakes, you might as well hold a ritual."

**Choe Pan-sul (崔判述):** Even if it's difficult now, once it's done, there's a satisfying feeling. We should tackle it while it's on our minds.

**Shim Jae-suk (沈在淑):** Can we receive some government (政府) support for the roof improvements?

**Leader (指導者):** Yes. I believe the government (政府) provides loans for materials.

**Neighborhood Chief (洞長):** During the neighborhood chief (洞長) meeting (會議), it was mentioned that if there are difficulties during the project (事業), you should report to the myeon chief (面長), who will then propose solutions to the county magistrate (郡首). Please don't hesitate to visit. The leader (指導者) and I will take responsibility for the loan (融資) issue.

**Son Mu-gyeong (孫武庚):** I improved my roof with tiles, and now it's not only pleasant to look at but also keeps out pests and requires no worry during rain. It's truly satisfying.

**Leader (指導者):** We will go to the myeon (面) office to gather detailed information about the loan (融資) support and get back to you.

**Jang Seok-hwan (張錫煥):** Shouldn't we first determine the number of target neighborhoods (對象洞數) before reporting?

**Neighborhood Chief (洞長):** We aim to improve all households (全戶) regardless of the number of target neighborhoods (對象洞數).

**Jang Seok-hwan (張錫煥):** Isn't that unreasonable?

**Neighborhood Chief (洞長):** It may be unreasonable, but for households unable to improve their roofs, the only option is to demolish and rebuild with mud bricks.

**Leader (指導者):** Let's plan to complete the roof improvement (事業) project within a year. When improving the roofs, we'll divide into groups so that all neighborhood residents (全洞民) can participate.


--- (p. 803) ---

We are currently planning this.
Village Leader: This village has awakened, but who among us is related by four inches, eight inches, or even twelve inches? If we're twelve inches apart, we should even share ancestral rites.
Leader: The saying "my field hurts when your field hurts" is now outdated.
Moon Chil-gyu: If you, the Leader and the Village Leader, can take responsibility for the loan relationship, we can give it a try.
Kim Young-hwan: Should we demolish and improve every single house, including yours and mine?
Leader: Yes, of course. Every single household must be improved.
Kim Young-hwan: What about Auntie's house in Utgol? She doesn't have any property. What will you do about that?
Village Leader: For now, we should either invite her to the community center or have Kim Young-hwan take care of her since he's the closest.
Leader: Once we invite her, the rest must be done through collective work by the entire village.
Kim Young-hwan: Even the cost of materials?
Leader: Yes. Then, the Village Leader and I will go to the town and come back with concrete details. We'll hold another village meeting after that and conclude for today.

◆ Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (7)

Date: March 28, 1972
Location: O Il-young's large room
Agenda: Loan support for roof improvement
Attendees: O Il-young and 29 others
Absentees: None
Chairperson: Village Leader

Village Leader: I went to the town today. While our village has been allocated 21 households for roof improvement, it's not enough. I asked the town mayor for special consideration, and he said we can get a loan of 25,000 won per household. Attached buildings are excluded.
Leader: I heard from the Village Leader, but when have we ever received help from the town for the Saemaul Undong? If it doesn't work out, I'll go to the agricultural cooperative and get a low-interest loan.
Lee Byung-moon: It might be difficult to improve every single household. We can improve the main buildings with the allocated 21 households, but the attached buildings are the problem.
Village Leader: Let's first improve the main buildings, and we'll see about the attached buildings based on the results of the Leader's agricultural cooperative loan. We plan to complete all improvements within this year.
Leader: Let's make a list of those who hope to receive support.
Village Leader: Those who hope to receive support will use the loan for roof improvement, and we'll use the agricultural cooperative loan to collectively purchase materials for the remaining attached buildings.


--- (p. 804) ---

# List of Applicants (希望者  명단)
Kim Gab-sul (金甲術), Shim Ui-seop (沈義燮), Shim Won-seop (沈元燮), Roh Seong-gi (盧聖基), Jang Won-hwan (張元煥), Shim Ju-seop (沈周燮), Lee Ryung-mun (李領文), Mun Chil-gyu (文七圭), Jang Seok-hwan (張碩煥), Shim Gyu-seop (沈奎燮), Oh Tae-young (吳泰榮), Son Jin-hae (孫振海), Oh Han-young (吳漢泳), Choi Pan-sul (崔判述), Kim Jin-gyu (金鎭圭), Son Bong-cheol (孫奉哲), Kim In-bo (金仁寶), Lee Bok-deok (李福德), Shim Gwang-seop (沈光燮), Choi Man-seok (崔萬石), Yeo Un-sul (呂雲述) (21 people)

**Dongjang (洞長):** I will report that the loan (융자) recipients have been decided as 21 people. With this, I will conclude the Donghoe (洞會).

## Meeting Minutes (會議錄)
*   **Date (日時):** September 10, 1974
*   **Location (場所):** Village Community Center (마을회관)
*   **Agenda (議題):** Selection of the 1st Presidential (大統領) Special Support Project (特別支援事業) in 1974
*   **Attendees (參席人員):** Oh Il-young (吳日永) and 25 others
*   **Absentees (不參者):** Kim In-bo (金仁寶) and 1 other
*   **Chairperson (司會者):** Son Seong-mo (孫聖模) (Leader (指導者))

**Leader (指導者):** Through our hard work and efforts, we have been honored to receive the Presidential (大統領) Special Support Fund (特別支援金) of 1,000,000 won (萬圓). We have convened this Donghoe (洞會) to select a suitable business (事業) for our village with the granted funds (下賜金).
**Shim Jae-suk (沈在淑):** 1,000,000 won (萬圓) is not a small amount of money. I suggest we engage in an income-generating business (所得事業) for our village, such as medicinal herb (藥草) cultivation (栽培). What do you think?
**Kim Young-hwan (金永煥):** How about increasing our income (所得) through Hanwoo (韓牛) breeding (增殖)?
**Leader (指導者):** We have two proposals: medicinal herb (藥草) cultivation (栽培) and Hanwoo (韓牛) breeding (入式).
**Kim Gab-sul (金甲術):** Given the soil quality (土質) of our village, I suggest ginseng (人蔘) cultivation (栽培). What do you think?
**Son Bong-cheol (孫奉哲):** Ginseng (人蔘) cultivation (栽培) is good, but with 1,000,000 won (萬圓), we could buy a field and purchase ginseng (人蔘) seeds (種根) with the village fund (基金) to cultivate ginseng (人蔘).
**Leader (指導者):** We have four proposals to consider. We will decide by show of hands (擧手). Proposal 1: Medicinal herb (藥草) cultivation (栽培), Proposal 2: Hanwoo (韓牛) breeding (入式), Proposal 3: Ginseng (人蔘) cultivation (栽培), Proposal 4: Buy a field with 1,000,000 won (萬圓) to increase village (Hangeul) assets (資産) and cultivate ginseng (人蔘) on the field.
2 people agree with Proposal 1, 8 people agree with Proposal 2, 2 people agree with Proposal 3, and 15 people agree with Proposal 4.
**Leader (指導者):** We will decide to buy a field with the Presidential (大統領) granted funds (下賜金) of 1,000,000 won (萬圓) and cultivate ginseng (人蔘) on the field.
**Shim Jae-suk (沈在淑):** Ginseng (人蔘) cultivation (栽培) requires technical skills (技術). How will you proceed? And whose field will you buy?
**Kim Gab-sul (金甲術):** My sixth cousin in Busan (釜山) is selling a field. Shouldn't we buy that?
**Leader (指導者):** How many pyeong (坪) is it?
**Kim Gab-sul (金甲術):** About 1,000 pyeong (坪).
**Leader (指導者):** How much is he asking for it?
**Kim Gab-sul (金甲術):** Shouldn't we pay according to the market price (時勢)?


--- (p. 805) ---

**Village Head** : Lately, the field rent is between 900 won and 1,000 won per pyeong. For that field, we should pay 900 won per pyeong.
**Kim Gab-sul** : If we agree to pay 900 won per pyeong, I will go to Busan and sign a sales contract (賣買契約) and come back.
**Leader** : Let's do that. Villagers (洞民), do you agree (同意)?
**Villagers** : All (全員) agree (同意).
**Leader** : Then, we have Mr. Wi Yong-deok from Geumsan who is currently cultivating ginseng (人蔘) in our village. We can consult (問議) him.
**Jang Seok-hwan** : While we can consult (問議) about the technology (技術), it's like we're creating a collective farm (共同農場). Do you think it will work?
**Kim Gab-sul** : As Mr. Seok-hwan said, cooperation (協業) is a difficult business (事業).
**Village Head** : It's not our place to discuss (論議) this. Let's bring the main person (張本人) and consult (問議) with them.
**Wi Yong-deok** : Cultivating ginseng (人蔘栽培) shows that the soil quality (土質) is quite good. The problem is how much effort the villagers (洞民) are willing to put in. To cultivate ginseng (人蔘栽培) on about 1,000 pyeong (坪), we first need around 500,000 won.
**Leader** : Did everyone hear what he said?
**Kim Jin-gyu** : Let's entrust Mr. Wi Yong-deok with the facilities (施設) and seed purchase (購入).
**Leader** : That's a great idea. What do you all think?
**Villagers** : It's good. (All (全員))
**Wi Yong-deok** : If the villagers (洞民) want this, I will do my best. First (于先), we need 500,000 won in cash (現金).
**Leader** : Then, we will transfer the village's own fund (自體基金) of 500,000 won to Mr. Wi Yong-deok by tomorrow. With that, we will conclude the village meeting (洞會). (All attendees (參席者) applaud (拍手))

### ♦ Minutes (會議錄) (9)

*   **Date** : October 23, 1974
*   **Venue** : Village Hall (會館)
*   **Agenda** : President (大統領) Special Support (特別支援) for Small Stream (小河川) Improvement Project (整備事業)
*   **Attendees** : Oh Il-young and 26 others
*   **Absentees** : Lee Bok-deok and 2 others
*   **Chairperson** : Son Seong-mo (Leader (指導者))

**Leader** : I apologize for asking you to come to the meeting room (會議場) in this cold weather. The reason is that the President's (大統領) special support (特別支援) for the small stream (小河川) improvement project (整備事業) in 1974 is being given to our village as a reward for our hard work. I have called this village meeting (洞會) to hear your opinions (意見) on where we should improve (整備).
**Sim Ui-seop** : The small stream (小河川) next to the village is very dirty and unsightly. Even though we have improved the village road and roofs, the stream is still ugly. Let's improve (整備) it on this occasion (機會).
**No Seong-gi** : How much is the project cost (事業費)?
**Leader** : The project cost (事業費) seems to be supported (支援) based on the design (設計).


--- (p. 806) ---

Leader: You all have been working hard on the ginseng project. The question now is how to sell it. If we dig it up to sell, we lack manpower during the farming season, and if we sell it as is in the field, it feels a bit unfair, which is why I called this meeting.

Shim Jae-suk: Selling it as is in the field would be more advantageous. Since we can't dig up everything that's underground, if we fail, it would be a problem.

Kim Jin-gyu: If we leave it in the field to sell, we might not get a fair price.

Village Head: We're not experts, so let's ask Mr. Wi Yong-deok who is here with us.

Wi Yong-deok: I'm truly sorry to the villagers. The ginseng hasn't grown well. Of course, it's partly due to my lack of technical skills, but since this is a long-term cooperative income project, we can't say the harvest is good. Even in Geumsan (錦山), experts are selling to Seoul merchants as is in the field.

Oh Yong-geon: Let's sell it as is in the field.

Shim Ui-seop: How much will we get?

Leader: A merchant came by recently and offered 1.9 million won.

Wi Yong-deok: Then let's sell it right here in the field.

Villagers: Let's sell it right here. (All members (全員))

Leader: Do you agree?

Villagers: We agree. (All members (全員))

# Gyeongbuk (慶北) Mungyeong County (聞慶郡) Jeomchon-eup (店村邑) Heungdeok Village (興德마을)

## 1. Overview of the Village (槪況)

### Ga. History (沿革)

O Approximately 360 years ago (光海君), the ancestor of the Go (高氏) family, Taechon (泰村) Gosang-eon (高尙顔), settled in the area and has continued to reside here to this day.

O Taechon (泰村) was born in 1553 (明宗 9年) in Wangtae-dong (旺泰洞), Yeongseon-myeon (永順面), and in 1577 (宣祖 10年), he passed the civil service examination (文科). He served as a magistrate (縣監), judge (判官), and county governor (郡守) in various regions including Hamchang (咸昌), Jirye (知禮), Saga (四嘉), Hamyang (咸陽), and Ulsan (蔚山). During the Imjin War (壬亂), he led the righteous army (義兵) as a commander (大將) alongside the Yangban (士族) of Sangju (尙州) and Hamchang (咸昌), achieving significant merits. He was also recommended as an examiner (試官) for the naval examination (舟師試) held in Tongyeong (統營) during his tenure as the magistrate of Samga (三嘉縣監), where he exchanged poems (唱酬) with Yi Sunsin (李忠武公). Additionally, he submitted the "Eight Strategies Against the Wokou (倭寇)" (御倭八策) to Seoae (西涯) Yu Seokryong (柳式龍), which were implemented.

O During the corrupt reign of Gwanghae (光海昏政), Taechon (泰村) retired from official duties (棄官) for over 40 years. Around 1614 (光海 6年), he returned to the land in Yedong (芮洞), Hoseonam-myeon (戶西南面) (now Heungdeok 2-ri (興德 2里)), where he authored the "Farmer's Almanac (農家月令)" in one year, promoting diligent farming (勤農) and making it accessible to common farmers (一般農民) through vernacular interpretation (諺解).

### Na. Location (位置) and Conditions (與件)

#### <Location (位置)>

O The village is located approximately 1 km northeast of the Mungyeong County Office (聞慶郡廳) and is a suburban village (都市近郊) with relatively convenient transportation (交通).

O Surrounded by low hills (野山) on the south (南), west (西), and north (北) sides, the village is not easily visible from the national road (國道邊).

#### <Conditions (與件)>

O The village is a flatland (平野地) suburban (都市近郊) village divided into an upper (윗 마을) and lower (아랫마을) section.

O The Yeonggang River (榮江) flows in front of the village, with the Jeomchon (店村)—Yeongju (榮州) railway (鐵道) running between the river and the village. Behind the village, across the hills (野山), lies the national road (國道) connecting Jeomchon (店村) to Yeongdeok (盈德).

## 2. Village Development Process

### a. Situation Before 1970

1) Basic Environment

*   Out of the 59 households in the village, apart from 2 old tiled-roof houses and 3 modern tiled-roof houses that had been passed down from ancient times,
*   The rest were thatched houses, and during the rainy season in summer, red ash water would make the bedding unusable, and the village roads were narrow and overgrown with weeds.


--- (p. 810) ---

The wall was either half-destroyed or completely absent, and most outhouses were open-air (露天便所). There was no proper entrance road to the village, making it look like a primitive Oriental painting (東洋畫).

## 2) Income Level (所得水準)
O For generations, the 24ha of limited farmland (農地) inherited from ancestors was primarily cultivated with rice and wheat. The cultivated area per household was 0.4ha, and the total farmland area per farming household was 0.6ha. The annual income of the residents was 350,000 won (千원). Additionally,
O Besides rice and wheat, small income sources included 30 boxes of silkworms (箱子) per year, 8 head of Korean cattle (韓牛), and 20 head of pigs (頭), etc. (等).

## 3) Living Conditions (生活狀態)
### a) Consciousness Structure (意識構造)
O Since over 80% of the population in the same region consisted of the Gaekseong (開成) high-born Go (高氏) clan, there was a strong sense of neighborly affection and cooperation. However, this also led to an excessively feudalistic mindset,
O The village had been steeped in conservative customs and stubborn traditions for so long that they could not even fathom the spirit of pioneering. They held extremely conservative views.

### b) Culture (文化) and Daily Life (衣食住生活)
O Despite being close to Jeoncheon town and having convenient transportation, the village only had 10 old radios, as electricity (電氣) was fully installed (全戶架設) in 1969.
However, the village suffered from the urban fringe's drawbacks, such as extravagance and excessive consumerism, leading to significant wealth disparities.
O As a traditional yangban (양반) area, the village was dominated by the Confucian ideology of "respect for officials and contempt for the common people" (官尊民卑). Parents had high expectations for their children's education, sending them to study in Seoul, Daegu, and other cities, often selling their farmland (田畓) to fund their education.
O The villagers looked down on physical labor (肉體勞動), puffing on long pipes and carrying burdens on their backs while bossing others around, living in a state of complacency.

## b. Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (運動)
### 1) Motivation (動機) and Trial Project (試驗事業) Results (成果)
O News spread that the "Saemaul Undong (運動)" initiated by President (大統領) on April 22, 1970, was taking place across the country. However, no signs of reform appeared in this village throughout 1971.
O The government (政府) provided 335 bags of cement (袋) for trial projects. With forced labor (賦役), the villagers repaired 3 communal wells, built 2 communal laundry areas, and constructed a 500m road between the lower and upper villages. They also made and buried 9 water pipes.
O Due to a lack of technical skills and the fact that the Saemaul projects were not self-initiated but carried out through forced labor (賦役), the projects were poorly executed. However, the villagers began to subconsciously feel that they could accomplish tasks by working together and started to appreciate the value of their efforts.
O Despite the villagers' stubbornness (固執) and indifference, a year was wasted, leading to the embarrassing consequence of being excluded from the 1972 Saemaul support (支援) program. The villagers remained satisfied with their reality, living day to day without concern for the future.


--- (p. 811) ---

## 2) Leader's Activity Situation

After graduating from Konkuk University's College of Law through hard study and briefly working as an educational civil servant, Go Du-won, who had repeatedly failed the bar exam despite his aspirations to become a judge, returned to his hometown and spent days in despair. During this time, he would sometimes resent his own inadequacies and his poor neighbors, and other times dream of the glamorous city life and sudden wealth. Eventually, he took a chance and entered a bituminous coal mine, but failed and only gained a case of neuralgia. He spent his days in idleness, recuperating from his illness. These days of reflection and self-reproach made him ponder the true meaning of life and the purpose of living.

As the educated youth left for the city, who would take responsibility for the development of this region where only the uneducated remained to guard the farmland passed down by their ancestors? Go Du-won firmly resolved to cultivate his hometown, where his ancestors were buried and where he too would one day be laid to rest, and volunteered to become a Saemaul leader.

## 3) Overcoming Difficulties

After volunteering as a Saemaul leader, Go Du-won realized that to change the consciousness of the residents, an organization was needed to work together. He attempted to reorganize and strengthen the existing development committee by convening several village assemblies, but the residents showed little interest.

He visited households whenever he had time, but deeply rooted habits and customs could not be easily transformed into a sense of participation. Left with no choice, he consulted with teachers and civil servants residing in the village and decided to establish and operate a "study room." With the help of three teachers living in the village, he guided residents in their personal lives and schoolwork, encouraged them to start their days with early morning cleaning and weeding around the village paths, and placed children's storybooks in the village library for them to read and share.

As the living environment became cleaner and the laughter of students filled the houses, the once cold village began to change. Grandfathers came to visit the "study room" to see their grandchildren studying hard and became familiar with the teachers. One by one, they even started participating in the early morning cleaning.

During this time, the development committee was reorganized into departments such as the Youth Guidance Division, Environmental Affairs Division, Income Affairs Division, and Life Guidance Division, with tasks adjusted and participation encouraged in each field.

On Sundays, middle and high school students were gathered in the village square to play soccer and improve the village paths, planting flowers to revitalize the stagnant village atmosphere. As the number of students in the "study room" increased, it became increasingly inconvenient to move from one house to another for guidance.

In August 1972, he decided to build a village community center and, after consulting with the development committee members, agreed to sell part of the clan land to secure some of the construction materials. After much persuasion, he finally obtained the consent of the village elders and firmly resolved to start the project.

On October 19, 1972, with the students leading the way, they began building the village community center by digging sand from the nearby Yeonggangcheon Stream, making bricks, and laying the foundation.

As if to say that good deeds invite trouble, the weather turned cold, and the project funds ran low. In November, the senior leader suffered from neuralgia.


--- (p. 812) ---

Due to infectious conjunctivitis, I had to be hospitalized at Dongsan Hospital in Daegu. Even some villagers who had been uncooperative with neighborhood affairs when I was healthy started visiting me one by one, and they also promised to actively participate in the Saemaul Undong after my discharge.

After being discharged in 18 days, without even having time to cook at home due to the need to raise funds for the project, while rushing around, Kim Han-yeop, the county magistrate, who had come to see the village road expansion project on January 22, 1973, promised 200,000 won in support after seeing the project site. The joy at that time was indescribable. On the day the Saemaul flag was raised at the village community center, students who had been running around in the narrow study room rejoiced, and even the elderly who had been mere spectators until then held the leader's hands and shared in the joy.

## 4) Developmental Promotion of the Saemaul Undong

*   Taking the establishment of the village community center as a model, we improved the roofs of 106 houses with a loan of 615,000 won, expanded a 1,200m agricultural road from the entrance of the broadcasting relay station to the entrance of Hongdeok 4-ri to a width of 5m, and built a stone wall. Around the time the agricultural road project was completed on April 6, 1973, we had the honor of a visit from Governor Gu Ja-chun. The village was in a festive atmosphere with all the villagers. Even now, that memory is fresh.
*   The 3,000m of crooked earth walls have been neatly improved, which shows that our villagers have become the vanguard of the Saemaul spirit of diligence, self-help, and cooperation!
*   The roofs have been painted in bright colors, and the mud-walled houses that were collapsing in places have been improved, with the walls painted, and even the 3,060m of walls have been neatly painted, resulting in Jeoncheon-eup winning first place in the environmental improvement achievement review in the second half of 1977.
*   As the environmental improvement project was nearing completion, we promoted collective farming and income-generating businesses to increase the residents' income.
    1.  Collective farming of Tongil rice: 560kg per 1000m²
    2.  Garlic collective farming: Before the establishment of the collective, most residents unanimously opposed garlic farming in this area, saying it was not suitable. However, the leader, with the technical support of the Rural Guidance Center, successfully grew Tongil rice as a post-rice crop. In 1973, the first 3ha of the collective was established. After consulting with the agricultural cooperative and securing a loan of 750,000 won, 2,000 seeds of new varieties were purchased and distributed to 28 hopeful residents. With careful attention and technical guidance from the Rural Guidance Center and the agricultural cooperative, the production was a great success. However, due to unfavorable market conditions, it was difficult in 1973 and 1974. But by firmly believing and continuing to farm, in 1977, 12,000 seeds were produced, generating 30 million won in income.
    3.  Pig collective farming: Utilizing the geographical advantages of being near a city, we raised 42 pigs collectively and 305 pigs individually (4 pigs per household) with loans of 1.2 million won in 1973 and 1.15 million won in 1974 from the agricultural cooperative. However, there are plans to expand and establish a large collective in the future.
    4.  Hanwoo (Korean cattle) farming: Since this village is in a plain area near a city, it is extremely lacking in pastures. Abandoning the traditional farming methods, we are currently raising 35 head of cattle using rational farming methods. In the future, we plan to introduce dairy cows and are currently consulting with relevant agencies. As a result, income increased, the village environment was renewed, and women's association activities became lively. In 1977, the county designated the village as a model village for business income and lent 2 million won from the county income savings fund to purchase 2,000 seeds of Ulleungdo garlic, which, together with the seeds already in storage, totaled 4,500 seeds that were planted. In 1978, the

## Ba. Achievements (成果) of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

### 1) Spiritual Aspect (精神面)

*   Through Saemaul projects, people were transformed into new human beings characterized by diligence, self-help, and cooperation;
*   They gained confidence (自信感) in their ability to achieve;
*   Through neighborhood assemblies (住民總會), they experienced Korean-style (韓國的) democracy (民主主義) firsthand; and
*   They developed a sense of gratitude (感謝) towards their country (祖國) and appreciation for their neighbors.

### 2) Lifestyle Aspect (生活面)

*   With the reform of farming techniques, seed renewal, and the expansion of Hanwoo breeding businesses, incomes increased, leading farmers to adopt a progressive attitude towards studying and researching;
*   They practiced thrift and saved money;
*   They helped their less fortunate neighbors, understanding that the well-being of all was key to their own prosperity.

### 3) Production Aspect (生産面)

*   The expanded cultivation of unified rice varieties increased income;
*   The Hanwoo breeding business, funded by grants, doubled residents' income; and
*   Cooperative management income businesses significantly improved income.

### ◆ Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (1)

*   **Date (日時)**: December 23, 1974, 19:00~22:00 (3 hours)
*   **Location (場所)**: Saemaul Community Center
*   **Attendees (出席人員)**: Go Geun-hwan (高根煥) and 34 others
*   **Agenda (議案)**: Selection of Projects for President (大統領) Grant in 1974 (年度)
*   **Host (社會者)**: Saemaul Leader (指導者) Go Du-won (高斗遠)
*   **Observer (列席官)**: Chief of General Affairs, Township Office (總務係長)

**Host (社會者)**: We will now begin the Residents' Assembly (住民總會) to discuss the selection of projects for the President's (大統領) special support fund (支援金) for outstanding villages (優秀). This support fund (支援金) has been granted to outstanding Saemaul villages since 1973 by the special consideration of President Park (朴大統領), amounting to 1 million won each. This time, our village has been granted this honorable support fund (支援金) of 1 million won. The money will be transferred to our account, allowing us to easily purchase necessary items for our projects. While Saemaul materials (資材) such as lime and reinforcing bars are provided as materials (資材), this support fund (支援金) is given in cash (現金), making it very convenient. I would like to hear your valuable opinions (意見).

**Go Jae-in (高在寅)**: I think it would be good to build a communal warehouse (共同倉庫). It is a good project (事業) that can increase income (所得) without much difficulty or risk.

**Host (社會者)**: That is a good idea. I would like to hear another opinion (意見).

**Go Young-pil (高永弼)**: Let's develop an orchard (果樹園). It is close to the town and has good marketability (市場性), so it would be a truly great project (事業).

**Go Bong-rim (高奉林)**: I agree (贊成).

**Host (社會者)**: There was agreement (贊成) on the orchard (果樹園) proposal.

**Go Young-bong (高永奉)**: Currently (現在), when it is harvest time in our village, a combine harvester comes from Taidong to thresh (脫穀) for us. This is a shame for our village. At a time when we are advocating the modernization (近代化) of agriculture (農村), wouldn't it be a good idea to purchase important agricultural machinery (農機具) and use it jointly (共同) for the village (利用)?


--- (p. 818) ---

Host: Mr. Go Young-bong, that's a good opinion.

Host: Please, let someone else speak.

Host: If there are no other opinions, we will proceed to the vote. Those in favor of Mr. Go Jae-in's opinion on the communal warehouse, please raise your hands (5 hands raised). Next, those in favor of Mr. Go Young-pil's orchard proposal, please raise your hands (4 hands raised). Those in favor of Mr. Go Young-bong's opinion on purchasing farming equipment, please raise your hands (25 hands raised). The project has been decided as the purchase of farming equipment. **Date (日時)**: January 18, 1975, 14:00~16:00

Host: I apologize for asking you all to come here at the beginning of the year, but since this is for the development of our neighborhood and directly connected to the interests of the residents, I hope you understand that we are holding this Donghoe (Neighborhood Meeting). We will now hear from Choi Yong-soon, who requested this general meeting.

Choi Yong-soon: Last year, I purchased one Daedong-style (大同式) tractor, one fully automatic rice threshing machine, one bundled rice threshing machine, and one bundled barley threshing machine, all new. I have been using them for a year, but due to my circumstances, I need to sell these agricultural tools. Wouldn't it be better for the village to purchase my machines?

Ko Jae-gu: If Choi Yong-soon is selling, how much does he expect to get?

Choi Yong-soon: To purchase these machines and all their accessories new, you would need at least one million won. However, since I have used them for a year, the minimum I would accept is 700,000 won.

Ko Jae-bong: Are you talking about just the machines, or does that include all the accessories?

Ko Young-bong: Of course, that includes all the accessories.

Choi Yong-soon: That's right.

Ko Young-bong: While it would be good for the village to buy and sell among ourselves, the technical market value of the agricultural tools is important.

Ko Jae-wan: If we purchase them in our village, it would be problematic if the price is too high or too low. I think it would be appropriate to request an appraisal from an agricultural tool dealer and purchase them based on the appraisal.

Jeong Seong-jin: That method seems good.

(Unanimous approval)

Host: Which dealer should we request the appraisal from? Does anyone here have a reliable place they do business with?

Ko Young-bong: I think it would be best to request the appraisal from the Rural Guidance Center.

Host: So, we will request the Rural Guidance Center to appraise the market value of Choi Yong-soon's agricultural tools. What do you think, Choi Yong-soon?

Choi Yong-soon: That's fine. But it would be troublesome if it takes too long. I also have my circumstances to consider.

Host: We will request the appraisal soon and purchase the tools based on the appraisal. What do you all think?

All: That's fine.

Choi Yong-soon: Even if the appraisal is accurate and fair, there should not be a huge difference between the appraised value and what others are willing to pay. If it's similar, I will offer them to the village.

Host: So, even if we purchase one tractor and two rice threshing machines and one barley threshing machine from Choi Yong-soon, we still need to purchase one more tractor.

Ko Jae-wan: In that case, out of the one million won in support funds, if we use some to purchase Choi Yong-soon's machines, we will have 300,000 to 400,000 won left. It would be good to use this remaining amount and our own funds to purchase a tractor supplied by the Agricultural Cooperative.

# Meeting Minutes

**Ko Young-bong:** Managing communal property is quite a challenging task. What if we entrust the management to an individual, charge a certain amount of rent, and use that to repay the loan?

**Jeong Tae-won:** The leaders and the village head should take responsibility for management. We should lease the tractor and thresher to a villager and have the lessee bear all operational costs. The rent collected can then be used to repay the loan. If the village manages these, there will be no one to inspect for damages, and we would need a separate manager, so it's better to lease them out.

**Moderator:** There's a suggestion to lease out the tractor and thresher and use the rent to repay the loan. Are there other opinions?

**Ko Byung-mo:** It's a bit odd to lease out communal farming equipment to a specific individual for the benefit of the whole village. What if other villagers want to use it?

**Jeong Tae-won:** I understand your point. Even if we lease it to a specific individual, the tractor will always be available to the village for a fee, so it shouldn't be a big problem.

**Ko Byung-mo:** But if something breaks down or an accident occurs during operation, who will be responsible?

**Jeong Tae-won:** The lessee should be responsible for repairs and maintenance.

**Ko Byung-mo:** Well, that seems reasonable.

**Moderator:** Let's vote on whether to manage the equipment communally or lease it to an individual for operation. First, raise your hand if you think communal management is appropriate (7 people). Next, raise your hand if you think leasing to an individual is better (20 people). It's decided to lease to an individual for management and operation. Now, let's discuss the rent.

**Jeong Tae-won:** We should repay at least the minimum loan amount within the loan period.

**Leader:** The loan period is one year grace and two years repayment.

**Lee Dong-hee:** Since no one is available to lease it immediately, perhaps the Development Committee can decide and ensure the loan is fully repaid within the loan period. That would be appreciated.

**Jeong Tae-won:** That's a good idea.

**Moderator:** What do the villagers think?

**All Villagers:** We agree.

**Moderator:** Please do your best to consider the village's interests and consult with the Development Committee members. Are there any further comments regarding the settlement?

*(None.)*

**Moderator:** Then, we will conclude the settlement. Due to busy farming schedules, attendance is low. Please inform your neighbors and participate together in the next meeting. Thank you.

## 4. Future Development Plan (發展構想)

*   Based on the experience of the 1977 (年) model village (示範마을) for income-generating businesses (經營所得事業), we will expand the garlic cultivation area (마늘栽培團地) to 10 hectares, renew the seeds, and rationalize management (經營) through collective work (共同作業) and systematic distribution (系統出荷). We will also construct a joint warehouse (共同倉庫) for storage (保管) and management (管理).
*   We will increase pig farming (養豚) to 320 heads (頭) and expand the joint pigsty (共同畜舍) from 30 pyeong (坪) to 120 pyeong (坪).
*   We will increase the number of Hanwoo (韓牛) cattle to 78 heads (頭), expand the joint cattle shed (共同牛舍) from 20 pyeong (坪) to 156 pyeong (坪), and cultivate feed crops (飼料作物) such as sweet potatoes and corn for self-sufficiency (自給) in feed (飼料). We will also install silos and feed grinders (飼料粉碎機).
*   Starting from 1978 (年), we will implement an annual plan (年次計劃) to raise 15 heads (頭) of dairy cows (乳牛). We will construct a cattle shed (畜舍) of 50 pyeong (坪) and strive to develop this into a model site (示範團地) for income-generating businesses (經營所得事業). We will surely achieve the modernization (近代化) of the village and the construction (建設) of a welfare-oriented rural community (福祉農村), and pass this on as a legacy (遺産) to future generations (後孫).

# Gyeongbuk (慶北) Yeongju-gun (榮州郡) Punggi-eup (豊基邑) Baeksin1-ri (白新1里) Settermaeul

### 1. Overview of the Village (槪況)

#### a. History (沿革)

*   The exact period when this village was formed is uncertain, but judging from the age of the zelkova tree at the village entrance, it is estimated that settlers lived here about 200 years ago.
*   Around 1910, the vast plains around the area were reclaimed by settlers from the Gwons of Andong and the Kims of Andong, who named the village Sinji (新基) (Setter).
*   During the Korean War (6.25), the entire village was destroyed as it was a fierce battleground. In 1977, the village was reconstructed as a cultural rural community through the settlement improvement project.

#### b. Location (位置) and Conditions (與件)

**\<Location (位置)\>**

*   The village is located about 14 km northwest of the Yeongju County Office.
*   The national road from Masan (馬山) to Junggangjin (中) runs in front of the village, and the central line (中央線) railway runs behind it. About 9 km northwest along the national road is Jukryeong (竹嶺), the border between Gyeongsangdo and Chungcheongdo.

**\<Conditions (與件)\>**

*   This village is formed in the hilly area of Sobaek Mountain (小白山麓). Due to the influence of the cold northwest monsoon coming over Jukryeong (竹嶺), the village experiences unusually cold winters.
*   The region has many stones, making the soil barren. Therefore, special crops such as fruits and ginseng are mainly cultivated rather than general crops.

<Village Characteristics (特性)>
In 1977, the village underwent modernization through a settlement structure improvement project. The main road is 7 meters wide, and the secondary roads are 4 meters wide, arranged in a perfect square. The village is known for its orchards, ginseng, and medicinal herb cultivation, making it the wealthiest in the area.

2. Village Development Process (發展過程)
a. Situation Before 1970 (以前)
1) Basic Environment (基礎環境)
- Piles of stones left from land clearing were scattered around the village, creating an unsightly appearance.
- The village's stream, running alongside, was filled with waste and emitted a foul odor.
- The winding roads were so narrow that one could barely pass with a load of firewood.
- The 40-some thatched houses with mud walls required sweeping the dirt floor daily, and the thatched roofs, rotted and sunken, were overgrown with weeds. During rain, several buckets had to be placed inside to catch dripping water.
- There were no farm roads, let alone a village access road, forcing residents to walk along the ditches beside the central railway line. The village was an eyesore.
- With the efforts of the leader and all residents, the village was transformed into a modern rural community.

2) Income Level (所得水準)


--- (p. 827) ---

Inherited from ancestors for generations, the village had only 35 hectares of farmland, primarily cultivating grains. However, only about 40 households were actual farmers, while the rest relied on selling their labor to nearby villages or working day jobs in the town of Punggi to make a living. The village's per household income was around 249,000 won, making it one of the poorest in the region.

## Situation Before 1970 (以前)

### 1) Mental State (精神狀態)

Living in ignorance and poverty, the villagers had never even considered the idea of improving their lives. They were content with their dilapidated homes, resigned to their fate, and spent their days drinking and gambling. Most worked as day laborers in Punggi town, only to squander their daily earnings on alcohol and gambling, often leading to fights and frequent visits to the local police station. There was no hope for the future or pioneering spirit among these residents, who lived indifferent and expressionless lives.

### 2) Culture (文化) and Daily Life (衣食住生活)

Living by the light of lanterns, the villagers could barely afford a decent life. They had no access to newspapers or magazines, and a single radio at the village head's house was their only source of news. Most wore clothes made of plain cloth, and owning a pair of mixed fabric pants was considered a luxury. After repaying their debts with the autumn harvest, many households had nothing left but straw. During the spring famine, wild greens, mugwort, and millet chaff were staple foods. Despite their hardships, the villagers raised 5-6 children in a single room, tearing up old books for wallpaper, and lived in a cycle of poverty, oblivious to shame or sorrow, as if it were their destiny.


--- (p. 828) ---

## Da. Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

### 1) Motivation and Achievements of the Pilot Project

* On April 22, 1970, President Park Chung-hee proposed the "Saemaul Undong," which sparked like a wildfire in neighboring villages, while in the most backward village around, there was no movement at all, as if watching from across the river.
* The government supported a pilot project with 300 bags of cement to construct one underground passage and improve the fence, but due to the residents' lack of cooperation, it turned into a shoddy construction that only consumed the cement. As a result, the village was disqualified from the 1972 Saemaul support, a shameful outcome. The residents continued to sit around the tavern, complaining and spending their days.
* However, seeing their neighboring village, Changnak 1-dong, designated as the best village in the county, with central and provincial officials frequently visiting to encourage the residents, and the village's environment completely transformed within a year, the residents began to feel a sense of shame and thought that they should do something.

### 2) Activities of the Leader (指導者)

* After graduating from middle school, the leader, An Jeong-won (安正元), had worked as a police officer and served as the chairman of the village office before running a business in Daegu. He returned to his hometown to farm, and when he looked at his neighbors living like animals compared to his glamorous city life, he blamed his ancestors for passing down poverty, and he several times decided to leave for the city again.
* However, he scolded himself, thinking that leaving this village, which someone must transform into a prosperous one someday, would be a sin against all the residents. He firmly resolved to become a Saemaul leader elected by the general assembly of residents and to create a better life for future generations with his own hands.
* However, in the vague midst of wondering what and how he should do to live well and how to conduct the Saemaul Undong, the road expansion project launched as a pilot project in 1971 failed, and the village was also disqualified from the 1972 support.
* The leader, together with the village head, went on a field trip to advanced villages, visiting excellent villages in the county to listen to success stories, project promotion methods, and situations of overcoming difficulties, and then
* He firmly resolved to make the construction of a wealthy village his lifelong mission and to achieve it no matter what.

### 3) Overcoming Difficulties (克服狀況)

* After being elected as the Saemaul leader, An Jeong-won first thought that he should stop the practice of gambling away the fruits of a year's hard work in farming in a single evening. Realizing that he could not achieve this alone, he decided to cooperate with the women of the village. He visited places where women gathered, asking for their cooperation.


--- (p. 829) ---

Initially, the men who frequently appeared at gatherings of women were often criticized. However, these men gradually took the lead in initiatives such as refusing to provide late-night snacks at gambling dens and removing playing cards from their homes. They also informed others about locations where gambling was taking place.

The enthusiastic leader who eventually succeeded in eradicating gambling from the village took the lessons from the first project's failure in 1971 to heart. In 1972, he pushed for the urgent matter of road expansion as a self-reliant project. He convened several village assemblies, but the residents were divided: those whose land would be incorporated into the road strongly opposed it, while others supported it. It was difficult to reach a consensus. Through persistent persuasion, visiting each opposing household whenever time allowed, it was agreed that the output would be reduced by 2-3 days depending on the area of land incorporated. On December 10, 1971, a resolution was passed at the village assembly.

However, when the buildings to be demolished—three main structures and eight auxiliary buildings—were confirmed as part of the road expansion, the residents stubbornly refused, stating that while they could donate their land, they could not demolish their buildings.

Fortunately, the residents convinced each other to jointly construct new buildings for those affected by the demolitions, and the project was successfully completed.

Inspired by this, the villagers decided not to merely envy the progress of neighboring villages but to actively pursue the Saemaul Undong to create a leading village. They voluntarily resolved to address their own issues and successfully expanded the main village road to 570 meters.

Following the successful road expansion, the villagers initiated self-reliant projects such as improving 12 roofs and 300 meters of walls.

In 1973, they completed a 950-meter-long sewer system, improved the roofs of all households, and painted them, thereby concluding the basic environmental improvement project. By the end of the year, the village was upgraded to a self-reliant village at the Saemaul Undong general assembly.

At the Gwangju National Saemaul Undong Leader Conference, an outstanding village received a special support fund of 1 million won. The entire village celebrated this achievement and, through a general assembly of residents, decided to introduce 15 head of Korean cattle, initiating the village's first joint income-increasing project.

In 1974, with 500,000 won in government support, an 18-pyeong village hall was constructed, serving as a purchasing and selling market and a meeting room. A small stream was cleaned up, and facilities such as a children's playground, a temporary water supply system, and a communal laundry area were installed.

However, when residents opposed the temporary water supply system due to a lack of water sources, the village head and the Saemaul Undong leader dug a 40-meter-long, 2-meter-deep, and 1-meter-wide trench to find underground water, completing a simple water supply system for 43 households. Through this persistent effort, 43 households could now turn on their taps to access water.

By 1974, cultural and welfare facilities, flower bed creation, basic environmental improvement projects, and production income base projects were nearly completed. In 1975, to increase income, the village borrowed 1 million won from the income savings bank of the military government to establish a flour mill. They also jointly constructed a 100-pyeong warehouse with the agricultural cooperative and actively promoted the planting of fruit trees and medicinal plants such as peonies and herbs.

In 1976, with 1 million won in county support, they reclaimed 800 pyeong of riverbank land and added it to the existing 1,200 pyeong of communal farmland.


--- (p. 830) ---

Combined with the new variety of apple trees, 130 saplings were planted, and with the support of 1.5 million won from President (大統領) O, a 180-meter section of the small stream was completely cleaned up. As a result, within just five years, the village, once the poorest and most backward in the county, transformed into the richest and most outstanding village in the county. This achievement is the result of the relentless determination of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) leaders and the sweat and toil of the residents.

In 1977, 82,336,000 won (38,808,000 won supported, 43,528,000 won by residents) was invested to push forward the first village infrastructure improvement project in the county. This transformed the naturally formed village into a completely modern, scientifically planned community with 28 relocated or reconstructed houses, 10 repaired houses, 32 reconstructed annexes, 2,600 meters of improved fences, 1,400 meters of widened lanes (4m~7m), 1,200 meters of sewer systems, and 300 trees for shade. On September 23, 1977, a historic moving-in ceremony was held, and during the Chuseok (秋夕名節) festival on September 27, everyone could silently express gratitude to their ancestors for passing down a prosperous village to future generations.

### 4) Land and Cash Donations

Encouragement and comfort were extended to the hardworking residents of this village from various sectors, and the residents also generously contributed their land and cash without hesitation for the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement).

5) Heartwarming Stories (美談佳話)

a) First Story (第一話)

In December 1971, to carry out the village road expansion project (事業), the existing 2m narrow alley was to be expanded to 6m. Resident Lee Jae-won generously donated his 50-pyeong land to the project, deeply moving others and significantly influencing the village residents' general meeting (住民總議) for the road expansion.

b) Second Story (第二話)

- In April 1977, when planning the cluster structure improvement project (改善事業), there was a lack of residential land (住宅地) for reallocation (換地) at 70〜120 pyeong. Saemaul Undong (新村運動) leader An Jeong-won donated 350 pyeong of his farmland (答), Jo Jae-jin donated 170 pyeong, Yoon Jae-gwan donated 50 pyeong, and Baek Nam-su donated 340 pyeong, meeting the residents' (住民) demands and allowing the project to proceed smoothly as planned.
- Notably, Park Hae-won from 2-dong, Seobu (西部) in Bungi-eup (豊基邑), 3km away from the village, heard that his 80 pyeong farmland (答) was crucial for the cluster structure improvement project (改善事業), small stream (小河川) stone wall (石築), and main road stone wall (石築). He selflessly donated the land. Park Hae-won had also donated 15 pyeong of land for the road expansion (擴張) in 1971. On October 5, 1977, Hong Seok-gi, the representative (代表) of Namyang Progress Corporation (南陽進興工業株式會社) in Seoul (서울), sent 760,000 won (千원) for cement expenses (代金) while requesting a sisterhood alliance (姉妹結緣).

## 7) Special Items (特記事項)
### Enjoyable Events
*   When women (婦女子) cooperated (協助) to completely eradicate (完全根絕) gambling (賭博)
*   When residents (住民) who strongly opposed (頑强反對) were persuaded (說得) to complete the expansion of An-gil by 570m and the residents (住民) themselves resolved (決議) to create a leading village
*   When the village was promoted (昇格) to a self-reliant village (自立마을) in 1973 and received a special (特別) support (支援) of one million won (壹百萬圓) from President (大統領閣下) at the National (全國) Saemaul Leadership (指導者) Conference (大會)
*   When a simple (簡易) water supply (上水道) was installed (設置) in 1974 and water (水道物) gushed out (湧出)
*   When a flour mill (製粉工場) was established (建立) in the village in 1975
*   When the village was selected (選定) as an excellent (優秀) Saemaul village in 1976 and KBS-TV broadcasted (放映) a talk show (談放送) with Kwon Myeong-heum (權明欽), the County Magistrate (郡守) of Yeongju (榮州), and Saemaul leaders (指導者)
*   When 1 million won (百萬圓) was supported (支援) by Kwon Myeong-heum (權明欽), the County Magistrate (郡守) of Yeongju (榮州) in 1976 to reclaim (開墾) 800 pyeong (坪) of riverbed (河川敷地) and create (造成) a communal (共同) orchard (果樹園) for the village

# b) Joyful Moments

- On June 20, 1977, when we received two heads of Korean cattle (worth 300,000 won) as a donation from the Younghusband Club in Yeongju
- On September 23, 1977, when the village improvement project was completed and we held a housewarming ceremony
- On September 27, 1977, when we held our first Chuseok ancestral rites in a modern rural environment

## b) Sad Moments

- In 1971, when our first demonstration project supported by the government with 335 sheets of corrugated iron for fence improvement was crude and we were excluded from the 1972 support village
- When I visited women's gatherings to ask for cooperation in eradicating gambling and was misunderstood
- In 1976, when we aimed to win the compost production competition with the women's association, cutting grass 9 km away at Jukryeong, but did not even receive an inspection
- In 1977, when 23 households had to live homeless for 3 months as part of the village improvement project

## 3. Residents' Assembly (住民總會)

♦ Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (1)

*   Date (日時) : December 10, 1971 19:00〜21:00
*   Venue (場所) : Village Community Center (會館)
*   Agenda (議提) : Village Road (安길) Expansion (擴張)
*   Attendees (參席) : Jeong An-gyeong and 47 others
*   Absentees (不參) : Kim Guk-bo and 4 others
*   Chairperson (司會) : Dongjang (洞長) Park Dal-dae


--- (p. 835) ---

**Chairperson**: Everyone, the weather is very hot today. I apologize for making you sit in such an uncomfortable place for this meeting. Today's meeting was called to gather the collective will of the residents for this year's Saemaul Undong projects. As you know, our village is located by the national road and also by the railway, a busy thoroughfare where many travelers pass through. It is somewhat embarrassing to show the current state of our village. Starting this year, the government is supporting our Saemaul Undong projects with funds, which is a grateful and much-needed opportunity. We must begin improving our village one step at a time. Our village is about 200 meters from the national road, but the entrance road and inner lanes are quite narrow. Currently, the inner lane has a width of 2 meters, and I would like to propose a plan to expand it to 6 meters to allow cars to pass through freely.

**Lee Won-jae**: To expand the inner lane, how much planning is required? And how should we address the issue of walls and houses built along the road?

**Chairperson**: That is indeed the problem. To be frank, protruding houses must be demolished, and walls must be removed. With the support of Saemaul Undong funds, some assistance is possible for rebuilding the walls on either side of the inner lane. Therefore, we kindly ask for your cooperation in approving the use of the land.

**Lee Kyung-jae**: That would be very difficult. My house has two rooms, and if the upper room is demolished, I cannot agree to it.

**Kim Bo-guk**: My house also needs to have a room demolished. I cannot compromise on this.

**Saemaul Leader**: I understand the concerns of those who oppose this. If there were no difficulties, we would not have held this meeting in the first place, and the village chief would not have explained the situation at the beginning. The Saemaul Undong currently being implemented nationwide is a movement initiated by President Park Chung-hee last April as a historic spiritual reform to improve our lives. Although there may be personal difficulties and losses, the neighborhood will understand, and future generations will remember this gratitude forever.

**Kwon Eung-hwa**: Please provide the list of affected residents and discuss the plan to expand the inner lane from 2 meters to 6 meters so that the meeting can proceed concretely.

**Chairperson**: The affected residents are Hwang Jae-soo, Lee Ho-seon, Kim Sun-yong, Kwon Ki-ha, Kim Yong-hae, Lee Won-jae, and Kim Kuk-bo. For the inner lane expansion, I propose expanding it by 2 meters on each side, which seems fair.

**Kim Kuk-bo**: My house has a long passage, and about 30 pyeong (100 m²) of the inner lane will be incorporated. Will there be no compensation?

**Chairperson**: You must make a sacrifice for the benefit of the entire village.

**Kim Kuk-bo**: I cannot give up my land for free, not even if I die. The current road is sufficient for living, so why must we undertake such a difficult task?

**Lee Won-jae**: True, we can live with the current situation. However, this is not just for today; it is for making our rural village more convenient to live in. This is a long-standing wish of all residents that must be fulfilled someday. Although my land, about 30 pyeong, will also be incorporated into the inner lane, I willingly agree to it here.

**Kim Kuk-bo**: I have also lived in this village for 40 years. If this is a long-standing wish of the entire village, I will not oppose it to the end.


--- (p. 836) ---

♦ Minutes of Meeting (會議錄) (2)

*   **Date**: November 25, 1973, 19:00
*   **Location**: Community Center
*   **Agenda**: President (大統領) Special Donation Business Plan
*   **Attendees**: 50 people

---

Although I can't do much, I have one request. As you know, only my grandmother lives in my house, so please consider my house for the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) work mobilization.

**Host**: Good. If you donate the land, we will try to reconcile the opinions so that you won't have to work.

**Lee Daesik**: I also strongly support differentiating the mobilization efforts for the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) for those who donate land from others.

**Host**: Now, things seem to be progressing smoothly. Before we hold the village assembly today, the village head, Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) leader, and development committee members have actually talked to several potential land donors multiple times and received approval from a few people, but let's reaffirm that here today.

**Leader**: Kim Gukbo, do you have any objections? Lee Jaegyung also yielded to me. I appreciate Wonjae Lee, Hosun Lee, Jaesoo Hwang, Kihwa Kwon, and Yonghae Kim.

**Host**: Then, the land issue is resolved. I didn't expect it to be donated so easily. Let's discuss the work issue now.

**Leader**: First, we need to set an age criterion and consider differences between men and women.

**Im Byeonghyeok**: Let's set the age range to 18-60 years old and consider 2 days for men and 3 days for women as equal.

**Kim Jaejin**: We should consider the household situation and the number of family members.

**Leader**: We absolutely cannot do that for village community projects. However, let's exclude the two households that are subjects of livelihood protection and impose a fine of 500 won per day for those who do not participate.

**Yoon Gisoo**: I agree. We should not make exceptions for work unless it's a special case.

**Leader**: The case of the seven land donors is also a special case, so let's finalize it. It would be even more appreciated if they participate voluntarily, but those who donate 10 pyeong or more will not have to participate.

**Lee Seongho**: Agreed.

**Host**: One more thing I would like to mention before moving on is that although there is no support from both sides for the road widening and wall improvement next year, we will support it somewhat in 1973. Since the current walls must all be demolished, it is only natural.

**Leader**: Then, let's decide on the road widening as next year's business plan and create a 6-meter-wide village inner road with our own strength.

**Host**: If there are no objections, I will consider this as decided and ask for your active cooperation. I appreciate your hard work until late at night. This concludes today's meeting.


--- (p. 837) ---

**Host**: I apologize for calling this meeting after a long day of work in the fields. The reason I asked everyone to gather tonight is that a few days ago, our village's Saemaul leader, Jeong Jae-won, attended the Saemaul Leaders Conference in Gwangju and brought back a special grant of one million won from President (大統領) for our outstanding village. I would like to hear your opinions on how we should use this money for our village's communal projects.

**Saemaul Leader**: Thanks to all of you, I was able to attend and return from the Saemaul Leaders Conference in Gwangju. I would like to share one thing: our village is still far behind. We need to improve our village and pursue income-generating projects simultaneously. When I heard the success stories of the Saemaul movement and the President's (大統領) instructions, the conference hall was filled with excitement and applause. The Saemaul Undong is an inevitable movement of our time, and it is built on the principles of diligence, self-help, and cooperation. With this philosophy, we should carry out the Saemaul movement in line with the President's (大統領) wishes. How about using the one million won grant to invest in Hanwoo (Korean cattle) breeding? Let's purchase them together, place them in homes with stables, and settle accounts after one year.

**Lee Won-jae**: The village hall is quite cramped. Could we build a new one?

**Kim Young-jin**: Let's plan to construct the village hall in the next Saemaul project or through other support. With the one million won grant, let's focus on income-generating projects and expand our funds.

**Lee Dae-sik**: Let's proceed with the Hanwoo breeding. Tomorrow, around five of us— the Dongjang (洞長), Saemaul leader, and development committee members (開發委員)—should go to the market day and purchase 2-3 month old calves, which should cost around 70,000 won each.

**Dongjang**: Then it is decided that we will purchase the cattle. Please decide on the breeding methods and select the breeders.

**Lee Won-jae**: Before accepting applications from breeders, let's first decide on the breeding methods. Yes, that's right. Usually, when we breed cattle for others, we divide the profits equally after one year. However, this time, let's agree to repay one-third of the principal and interest (元利金) and set aside one-tenth as interest (利息). When we settle accounts (精算) after one year, we can make a decision at the general meeting (總會).

**Im Dal-soo**: That sounds good.

**Host**: Let's decide on the breeding methods and then accept registrations from those who wish to participate. As I mentioned earlier, the cost per head is around 70,000 won. We plan to purchase 15 heads, so please register 15 participants and we will make the purchase on the next market day.

**Lee Mu-ho**: I would like to participate in the breeding.

**Lee Mun-ho**: I would like to register as well. Yoon Gi-su, Kwon Yong-yeol, Kim Yong-hae, Jeong Jae-won, Go Ho-gyu, Lee Jae-deok, Kim Young-ja, Jang Bok-rae, Shin Hyeon-hwan, Im Ju-taek, Kim Jae-ja, Bae Geum-seok, Jeon Cha-mok all register.

**Lee Ho-seon**: While registering for breeding is good, let's create some rules to prepare for any accidents and appoint guarantors (保證人).

**Host**: That's a excellent suggestion.

**Leader**: Then, on the next market day, the Dongjang (洞長), leader, and development committee members (開發委員) will go to the cattle market to make the purchase and distribute the cattle. For other administrative matters, the Dongjang (洞長) will prepare the necessary forms for you to submit. Please keep me informed of any updates.


--- (p. 838) ---

We will make efforts to promote efficient income-generating businesses.

**Chairperson (社會) (동장)**: With this, we will conclude the meeting.

### Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (3)

* **Meeting Time**: January 20, 1974, 20:30~22:00
* **Location**: Village Community Center (會館)
* **Agenda (議際)**: Settlement of Accounts for the Purchase of Hanwoo (韓牛) with President (大統領) Special Grant (特別下賜金)
* **Attendees (參席人員)**: 50 people including Park Dal-dae
* **Absentees (不參人員)**: 2 people

**Chairperson (社會者)**: Starting now, I will report on the settlement of accounts for the purchase of Hanwoo (韓牛) following the residents' general meeting held on November 25, 1973, regarding the President's (大統領) special grant (特別下賜金) cattle introduction (韓牛入式). Over the past two months, the Dongjang (洞長) and the development committee members (開發委員) have purchased suitable cattle at the cattle market (牛市場) every market day. On January 13, we purchased 5 heads at 66,600 won per head and introduced them to residents Jeong Jae-deok, Kim Young-jin, and Kim Jae-jin. On January 8, we purchased another 5 heads at 66,600 won per head and introduced them to Lee Mun-ho and four others on January 15, January 18, and January 20, purchasing them at the market for 66,600 won or 67,600 won each. We have now completed the introduction of Hanwoo (韓牛) to all 5 households. Are there any comments?

**Kim Sun-yong**: I heard the settlement report well, but why didn't you purchase any cattle in January?

**Kwon Eung-ha (Development Committee Member (開發委員))**: We went to the cattle market (牛市場) in December but there were no cattle. We traveled to Yeongju, Busuk, Yecheon, and Sunheung to purchase cattle, but there were no suitable ones.

**Lee Gyeong-jae**: You traveled around several times. How did you use the expenses (經費)?

**Saemaul Leader (指導者)**: To be honest, it was self-funded (自負擔). We went down together as we had other business on market days. Once again, I would like to ask the Hanwoo (韓牛) breeders (飼育者) to raise them with all your heart. If there are any other opinions (意見), please let us know (there are none).

With this, we conclude the settlement report. Please proceed as discussed during the Hanwoo (韓牛) introduction residents' general meeting (住民總會). Goodbye.

### Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (4)

* **Date (日時)**: November 10, 1975
* **Location (場所)**: Village Community Center (會館)
* **Agenda (議際)**: Formulation of Saemaul Undong (事業) Plan for 1976
* **Attendees (參席人員)**: 48 people, Absent (不參): 10 people
* **Guest (臨席者)**: Kim In-sun, Local Administration Secretary (地方行政書記)
* **Chairperson (社會)**: Saemaul Leader (指導者) Jeong Jae-deok

**Chairperson (社會)**: Now that we have finished harvesting (秋收) and threshing (脫穀), we have some spare time, but we need to prepare for winter (越冬用) fuel collection (燃料採).


--- (p. 839) ---

It seems that our reality is such that we have no time to rest, day or night. I know you must be tired from working during the day, so I apologize for calling this village assembly at night. Although not everyone could attend today, many of you are here. Once again, I ask that you attend these meetings unless there are special circumstances, and if possible, have the head of the household attend. Today, we will discuss and decide what projects we should undertake for next year's Saemaul Undong.

**Park Dal-dae**: Since our village has completed environmental improvements at 100%, I think it would be good to focus on income-generating projects. I suggest we properly organize the dike construction for the main waterway and the small stream.

**Yun Gi-su**: I think we should perfectly place the culvert in front of the mill.

**Im Byung-sam**: The main waterway and small stream dike construction projects are too large in scale to be Saemaul Undong projects. Let's select something with a smaller scope.

**Chairperson**: The support for this project is 500 units of steel reinforcement bars and 1 ton of steel. Please share your opinions.

**Kwon Eung-yeol**: Can't we take a break from Saemaul Undong this year?

**Chairperson**: If there is a suitable project, let's do it. Everything we do benefits our neighborhood. In my opinion, our village entrance road is not paved with stones, so it collapses when it rains, freezes in the winter, and thaws in the spring, constantly deteriorating. If we properly pave it with stones, it will look better and be much safer and more convenient to travel on. Of course, it will be hard work.

**Lee Ho-seon**: It's 200 meters long, so it will be too difficult.

**Im Byeong-su**: I estimated it to be about 150 meters last time.

**Yun Jae-gwan**: We can bring the stones from the nearby stream and use cement to push this project forward as part of next year's Saemaul Undong.

**Chairperson**: A few of the development committee members met before and couldn't reach a conclusion. Let's make a decision here today.

**Kim Sun-yong**: Let's do it.

**Lee Gyeong-jae**: I agree.

**Im Gil-sang**: I second that.

**Lee Dae-sik**: Is the business plan only for the village entrance road paving?

**Yun Gi-su**: What should we do about the culvert I mentioned earlier?

**Park Dal-dae**: Let's postpone the main waterway and small stream projects and decide on the road paving and one culvert.

**Yun Jae-man**: That's fine.

**Kim Yong-hae**: Let's do that.

**Leader**: Then, let's finalize next year's Saemaul Undong business plan as 150 meters of entrance road paving and one 3-meter culvert. I will report this to the township office with the signatures of the village chief and the Saemaul Undong leader and development committee members by tomorrow. One more thing: please carry out housing improvements as a self-help project. The overall appearance of the village is


--- (p. 840) ---

Relatively clean and well-organized, but once you enter the house, it is as filthy as can be. Please make each household beautiful and clean, and especially, I urge you to implement a household water supply of 10 tons or more next year. Please prepare yourselves firmly and get ready for the New Community beautification project next year. With that, I will conclude today's meeting.

## Meeting Minutes (會議錄)

Agenda: 4th Special Support Project for 1976
Date: November 5, 1976, 19:30~20:30
Venue: House of Dongjang Park Dal-dae
Attendees: An Jeong-won and 50 others
Chairperson: Dongjang Park Dal-dae

**Chairperson**: The weather has suddenly turned cold. We were planning to hold the meeting at the village community center (會館), but considering the space is cramped and inconvenient, I thought it would be better to hold it at my house despite the cold. Today, we need to discuss how to use the special support fund of 1.5 million won, as our village has been selected as an outstanding village in this year's New Community Movement (總決算) final settlement. Please share your good ideas.

**New Community Leader**: The special support fund is to be brought back after attending this year's New Community Leader Conference. Starting this year, we must begin the project, and 20% of the wages must be deposited into the welfare (福祉) fund. Let's first decide on the business plan.

**Im Byeong-ho**: First, I would like to express my gratitude to Dongjang, the New Community Leader, and the Development Committee for creating this opportunity. With farming work almost done and the season changing, it is a joy to be able to earn wages. I think any business would be good.

**Yoon Gi-su**: Let's build a stone embankment for our village's Secheon Stream. The stream is too narrow and lacks an embankment. If left as is, our house and the entire neighborhood will be in danger, and it will look very unsightly.

**Im Byeong-ho**: Yes, I think it's a good project. I agree.

**Jang Bok-bae**: I agree as well.

**Kim Young-jin**: I second the motion. (Unanimous decision (萬丈一致) to build the Secheon Stream stone embankment)

**Chairperson**: Then, let's decide that the 4th Special Support Project for 1976 will be the construction of the Secheon Stream stone embankment, and we will draw up a business plan. Let's also decide on the welfare (福祉) fund issue here.

**New Community Leader**: Women cannot participate in the Secheon Stream embankment work. However, it would be good if each person could carry a certain number of stones. Although we cannot be sure of the exact amount of work, if we are to build a 150-meter-long stone embankment, we must work hard, and it is thought that the efficiency (能率) of the work will increase if only men (男子) do it.

**Gwon Gi-seok**: Still, there are households where only women live, and there are households where the women themselves want to work. Let's decide on the wages and give them the opportunity to work as well.


--- (p. 841) ---

**Lee Sang-ho (李相厚)**: That is a meaningful statement. Let's do as you say.
**Bae Sun-ung (裵淳邕)**: I think it would be appropriate to decide on wages at 1,000 won for men and 700 won for women.
**Moderator (社會者)**: Please share any other opinions you may have.
**Lee Jae-nam (李在男)** (President of the Mothers' Association): Please create opportunities for women to earn money and keep the wages as they are.
**Saemaul Leader (새마을指導者)**: That's good. Before we proceed with the project, I would like to emphasize that this project is one bestowed upon us by His Excellency the President (大統領閣下). Therefore, we should not treat it as a burden but rather approach it with enthusiasm like we do our daily tasks. Your cooperation would be greatly appreciated.
**Moderator (社會者)**: Is there any objection to deciding on the wages as such?
**Kwon Eum-hee (權音姬)**: No objection (unanimous decision).
**Moderator (社會者)**: There is one more thing. Should we not decide on the deduction and usage of the welfare fund for the wages?
**Bae Geum-seok (裵今錫)**: Where can the welfare fund be used?
**Moderator (社會者)**: It can be used for any communal projects as decided by the residents.
**Saemaul Leader (새마을指導者)**: Since it's getting late, how about we decide on the welfare fund issue at the next meeting?
**Lee Won-jae (李源載)**: Let's do that. There might be other necessary things to discuss.
**Kwon Gi-ha (權基河)**: I agree.
**Moderator (社會者)**: I ask all residents. Shall we proceed according to the leader's opinion? (Yes, unanimous decision) Alright. We will convene another meeting at a later opportunity. Today's meeting is adjourned. Thank you.

## ◆ Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (6)

*   **Date (日時)**: April 3, 1977, 10:00 AM
*   **Location (場所)**: Village Community Center (마을會館)
*   **Attendees (參席人員)**: 39 people (35 men, 4 women)
*   **Guests (臨席官)**: The mayor (邑長) and 2 others
*   **Agenda (案件)**: Formation of the Promotion Committee for the Improvement of Village Structure (聚落構造改善事業) Project

**Moderator (社會) (Dongjang (洞長))**: Despite the inconvenience, we have gathered here with the mayor and related officials to discuss and form a promotion committee with the residents to transform our village into a model village for the 1980s through the Improvement of Village Structure project.
**Saemaul Leader (새마을指導者) (An Jeong-won (安正源))**: Today's meeting topic is to confirm the village as an Improvement of Village Structure model and to seek the residents' opinions to form a promotion committee without a single dissenting voice. Once the plan is confirmed, we should aim to achieve the intended results through the promotion committee. Therefore, the chairperson of the promotion committee should be someone who is respected in the village, has knowledge, and is currently in a position to


--- (p. 842) ---

The position of the village leader (동장) who is already a Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) guide should be excluded, and someone else should be elected. In this regard, we recommend Kim Young-jin (金永鎭), who has lived in this village for a long time, graduated from a certain middle school (일정시 중학교), and has a strong sense of national identity (국가관).

**Kwon Eung-ha (權應夏)**: I agree. At the age of 54, he is a middle-aged man who has contributed greatly to the development of the village. **Master of Ceremonies (Village Chief)**: Deputy Mayor, Mayor, Chief, thank you for visiting our humble village. And to all villagers, thank you for gathering here in the middle of your busy day. 3. Free loan of construction equipment for the annex.
4. Full support (100%) for all village projects.
5. Approval of land exchange and division settlement.
6. For housing improvement, 20 units will be loaned 600,000 won and subsidized 150,000 won.
7. All houses should use standardized materials (Korean timber).
8. Land exchange will be mixed, ranging from 70 to 120 pyeong.
9. Land prices: 2,500 won per pyeong for land, 3,000 won per pyeong for fields, and 3,500 won per pyeong for farmland. The price of above-ground structures will be applied at the current market price.
If there are any amendments or supplements to the above resolution of the promotion committee, please let us know.
