## 4. Future Development Plan

Since the village improvement project was completed in 1977, the modernization of rural living standards has already reached a cultural level comparable to that of urban areas. We must now focus on raising the income level.
- Each farm household should solidify the given foundation and continue to increase income through special crops such as ginseng, peony, peony, and fruit tree cultivation. We should plant the Milyang No. 21, which achieved great success in 1977, in all plots to achieve a harvest of more than 500 kg per 1/1000 are (反當).
- With the 2,000 pyeong of orchards secured through the joint income business, we will continue to increase annual income to over 1,000,000 won if we cultivate them for 4-5 years. If we receive land reclamation loans in 1978, we will reclaim about 1 hectare of riverbed.
- We will receive loan funds from the income bank for the joint ginseng garden of 1,000 pyeong and expect a harvest of 5,000,000 won in four years.
- We will promote the introduction of 20 head of Hanwoo (韓牛) as a village income business. Today's reality, looking ahead to the 1980s, is bright. We expect to easily achieve an average annual household income of 2,500,000 won in the 1980s, up from the current 1,500,000 won.


--- (p. 848) ---

# 1. Village Overview

## a. History

During the Joseon Dynasty (李朝時代), this area was known as Jikhyeon-dong (直峴洞) in Pyeonghae-gun (平海郡), Gangwon-do (江原道), serving as the town's administrative center. It is said that six scholars (六進士) and six wealthy families (六富者) settled here, forming a large community of over 300 households. At that time, power struggles between these influential figures made life difficult for poor farmers and fishermen. Government officials also found the seaside location unsatisfactory, leading to their relocation, and consequently, the households that depended on them also moved to distant mountainous villages. This resulted in the village's decline, reducing the number of households to just over 30. These remaining households, unable to access the deep interior, rebuilt the abandoned village with the spirit of mutual aid (隣保相助). They erected a round pillar made from a large pine tree on the southern embankment (南山 制方) to establish a community center (洞會舘), which still stands today as a 12-pyeong (坪) building on a 65-pyeong plot, passed down through generations and preserved until 1975. The village is surrounded by a rocky coastline shaped like a scholar (선비사), said to resemble dancing figures, a testament to the intense power struggles of the past. After the Japanese colonial period (日帝時), the village was administratively reorganized under Uljin-gun (蔚珍郡), Pyeonghae-myeon (平海面), Jiksan-ri (直山里), and has been known by this name since liberation (解放).

## b. Location and Conditions

### <Location>

* Located 40 km south of Uljin County Office (蔚珍郡廳), the village is situated 4 km east along the coastline at the foot of a mountain.
* Due to Typhoon Sara, severe waves destroyed 7 houses and sank 5 ships, highlighting the village's proximity to the sea, just 50 meters away. The villagers have lived with the constant threat of fierce waves.

### <Conditions>

This seaside village is backed by a high mountain densely covered with pine forests, resembling a screen. In front, the East Sea (東海) stretches out with its shimmering horizon, where fishing boats come and go, making it a typical coastal fishing village.

* Night School Hall (夜學會堂) (130 years ago (年前), by ancestors (先代祖上), Dong Community Center (洞會舘), plaque (懸板))

"Jiksan (直山) Hwahyang (華鄕) is originally (本來) the land of talented people (人傑) of Namsan (南山). 70 years ago (年前), literary culture (文風) flourished, and there were many Confucian scholars (さみさ). Even children did not know how to recite poems (詩). Later, due to decline (衰運), they could not find work, which is a sad thing. Later, education (校學) revived, and the children of the village (洞里 村童) were intelligent (聰明) and pure (純粹), all entering public schools (公立學校) and developing (發展) with great effort. However, some could not achieve their goals due to difficult family circumstances (家庭形便), and as time passed, they still could not achieve their goals, which was unfortunate (不幸) even in happiness (幸福). How can we call this their fate (意理)? The villagers (洞民) must unite (一體) to revive (復興) the ruined village (廢墟) based on the spirit of mutual aid (隣保相助), and all should go on the path of learning (學問). Therefore, we must establish (設立) a night school (夜學) to save them. Thus, the elderly (年老) and outstanding (優秀) young people (靑年) discussed (議論) and built a six-room house (六間) in the village (洞里), naming it the Night School Hall (夜學會堂)."


--- (p. 850) ---

'May our descendants learn and practice this without regret. Kim Yunhwa (金允和) took on the task, and Yi Yonggi (李龍起) was in charge of writing. Without hesitation, they even composed a song to sing. The song goes: "The school stands at the foot of the mountain, by the bamboo grove. The green of the pine trees in the courtyard. The bamboo is lush, and we study by day and by night. In the twilight, the lamplight shines with the autumn moon. The path to the school shines. The pheasant flies in the mountain, and the whale lives in the sea." (Written on the 3rd day of the 3rd month of the Dingchou year (丁丑年) at Donghyeonbang (東賢坊) while sitting and discussing)'

※ The above is a translation of Chinese characters (漢字) into Hangul (한글).

## 2. Village Development Process (發展過程)

### 가. Situation Before 1970 (70年 以前의 情況)

#### 1) Basic Environment (基礎環境)
- The village had irregular, winding paths and sandy roads where even a cart could not pass. Behind the village, the Namdaecheon (南大川) River would flood even with a little rain, blocking students' commute. Agricultural and marine products were transported using weak stretchers. The mountains behind the village were so barren that not a single green tree could be found. Firewood had to be fetched from dozens of miles away, and women had to carry it on their heads.
- Small sailboats caught fish, which women divided and carried to sell door-to-door around the villages, centering on the administrative center of Pyeonghae-myeon (平海面). This lifestyle had accumulated over time. Fishermen, known for their ignorance, could not live a day without alcohol, a trait of coastal people.

#### 2) Income Level (所得水準)
- For generations, the village had cultivated 52ha of farmland, primarily growing rice and wheat.
- The average farm size per household was 0.45ha, with an annual average income of approximately 320,000 won (千원).
- Income from farming and natural seaweed during the spring famine period were the main sources of income.
- Among the 30 villages in Pyeonghae-myeon, this village was notorious for its poor living conditions. Rumors even spread that one should not marry into Jiksan-ri (直山里) for fear of poverty.

### 3) Mental State (精神狀態)
O Half-farming (半農), half-fishing (半漁業) life, singing and dancing with liquor after catching fish while battling fierce waves, sometimes losing precious lives (生命) due to severe storms (風波), witnessing colleagues (同僚) meet such fates, yet having to fight the sea again the next day (來日), borrowing money for rice during the spring famine (春窮期), unable to even think about tomorrow (來日)'s worries, living in such a world (世上). Sometimes, with good fortune (運), the village would celebrate all night with liquor upon the return of a full ship (滿船).

O On the other hand, people of ambition gathered to form a village prosperity association (繁榮會) and began village development (開發) in 1965 (年). To straighten the winding village roads (路), they demolished 12 houses (棟) and successfully built a 6m-wide road (幅) through the center of the village, stretching 1,200m. This was a significant achievement (成果).

## B. Promotion of the Saemaul Movement (事業)

### 1) Motivation (動機) and Trial Project (試驗事業) Results (成果)
O This village organized a village prosperity association (繁榮會) in 1964 (年) and, with Kim Bukhak (金北鶴) as the chairman (會長), decided to develop the village (開發). They first succeeded in building an 80m-long, 16m-wide bridge (橋梁) over the Namdaecheon (南大川), which would be flooded even with a little rain, using 100 million won (萬) from government support (政府支援) and 700 million won (萬) from the village's own funds (自負擔) over four years (年間).

O When the "Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)" initiated by President (大統領) on April 22, 1970 (年), spread across the country (全國), this village drew on its experience with road expansion (擴張) and bridge construction (橋梁架設) to launch the Saemaul project (事業) in 1971 (年) with the support of 335 bags (袋) of cement (洋灰). Although the project ended up being crude (粗雜) due to a lack of technical skills (技術) and foresight (眼目), the sincerity (誠意) behind it was remarkable (大端).

### 2) Leader (指導者) Activity (活動狀況)
O Kim Jaesung (金在成) was elected as the Saemaul leader (指導者) in 1971 (年). Although Kim (金氏) was talented (才能) and gained the trust (信任) of the residents (住民) as a writer (文筆家), the lack of driving force (推進力) and the residents' (住民) lack of awareness (認識) prevented the Saemaul movement (運動) from developing (發展), and his four years (年間) of service (奉仕) came to an end.

O In 1974 (年), Lee Byunghwa (李炳華) was elected as the leader (指導者), becoming the second-generation (代) leader (指導者). Lee Byunghwa (李炳華), a young man (靑年) who would not yield to any task (事), accelerated (加) village environmental improvement (環境改善), which had been stagnant (沈滯) for 2-3 years (年), and completed roof improvement (地붕改良) and roof painting (地붕塗色) by the end of the year (年末). He was then elected as the village head (里長), leading to a change in leadership (更迭) in 1975 (年).

O The current leader (指導者), Park Byeongryeong (朴丙玲), has been the village head (里長) since 1972 (年) for four years (年間) and was decided by the neighborhood association (洞會) to take over the village affairs (里事) from Lee Byunghwa (李炳華).

### O Activity (活動狀況)
After graduating from Seoul National Railway High School (鐵道高等) and working at the Samcheok Railway Bureau (三陟鐵道局), he returned to his hometown (故鄕) in 1969 (年度) and found the village residents (住民) living in a primitive (原始的) and miserable (悲慘) state (狀態), which moved him deeply. He decided to build a prosperous rural village (農村) and began serving as the village head (里長) in 1972 (年). At that time (當時), he worked hard to eliminate factionalism (派閥意識) and unite (團結) the residents (住民) as one, successfully bringing them together (總和).


--- (p. 852) ---

However, concerned about the village leader position (里長職), which comes with some compensation, he resigned after four years and was re-elected as a Saemaul leader by the consensus of the residents. When the first project, a wall improvement project using 335 bags of cement, failed due to lack of cooperation and joint effort in 1972, the village was dropped from the support list the following year (1973) and stagnated, while the neighboring village of Wolsong 3-ri achieved the glory of being an outstanding Saemaul. This news was a tremendous spiritual shock, and they vowed to lead their village to become an outstanding Saemaul through the strength of the residents themselves. They submitted the proposal to the village general assembly and decided to build a village hall, a place for dialogue, by consensus. In November 1974, they completed the renovation of 134 roofs and 92 houses, including painting, erasing the old appearance of Jikgo-dong.

### Construction of the Donghwegan (洞會舘)

Although there was a 12-pyeong Donghwegan inherited from their ancestors, it was too small for a public hall serving 138 households. In this village that revered good customs, fathers and sons could not sit together, naturally excluding the participation of the younger generation, and public opinion was always lagging behind other villages. They always wanted to build a modern village hall to find developmental and productive opinions in a broad space for dialogue.

In 1975, with the President's award of 1 million won for outstanding Saemaul villages and an additional 1.5 million won from the village, the construction of the hall was confirmed, boosting the residents' morale. To reduce the heavy burden of the total construction cost of 8.3 million won, they transported sand and gravel even in the bone-chilling cold, piled them up like Mount Tai, worked late into the night under the moonlight, and from March to April, they mobilized everyone, including children, to work on the white sandbank. As a result, they completed a two-story, 55-pyeong modern concrete village hall, a joy beyond measure. However, the village's debt increased to 5.8 million won due to the hall's construction, but the residents themselves donated happily at the completion ceremony, settling the accounts neatly, a truly heartwarming event.

### Temporary Water Supply Facility (簡易給水施設)

With a total construction cost of 4.5 million won (2 million won from the government and 2.5 million won from the residents), a complete water supply system was established for all 138 households.

### Repair of Breakwater (防波堤) and Wharf (物揚場)

As part of the Saemaul beautification project, they received support of 500 bags of cement to repair the damaged port and filled the stones inside the port using manpower alone. This project also required a significant amount of labor, comparable to the village hall construction. As a result, 23 ships were safely protected from the large waves last summer.

### Village Communal Bathhouse (共同沐浴湯)

With a total construction cost of 3.7 million won, a refreshing 17-pyeong bathhouse for men and women was built, funded by a 2 million won subsidy from the Hupo Fisheries Cooperative and a 1.7 million won contribution from the village. This was another overwhelming achievement.

The above four projects were completed in 1976, involving a total of 12,700 person-days of work, equivalent to an average of 120 people per household working non-stop for four months. The residents' bloody participation led to the success of the Saemaul projects.


--- (p. 853) ---

### Breakwater (防波堤)
Following the success of 1976, in 1977, the village constructed a 200-meter-long coastal breakwater to protect against high tides, using 1.5 million won in Outstanding New Village Special Support Fund and the labor of the residents. Additionally, with 2 million won in support from the Thick Water Supply Cooperative and 2.9 million won from the village, they completed unfinished projects including a 50-pyeong fish market, a communal restroom, and 1,000 meters of sewer lines.

### All These Projects
All these projects were initiated after the Development Committee drafted the project plans, which were then approved by the General Assembly of Residents. Progress reports were made throughout the projects, and upon completion, a public financial statement was presented at the General Assembly of Residents to ensure transparency. Completed projects were then managed by designated responsible parties, who were tasked with thorough operation and management.

### 3) Overcoming Challenges (隘路 극복)

### As a New Community Leader (새마을지도자)
After being elected as a New Community Leader, I realized that the success of the New Community Movement depended on the unity of the residents. I prioritized appointing Development Committee members from each surname group, seeking advice and cooperation from capable and innovative senior members to eliminate factionalism and encourage active participation and unity. This required immense effort and dedication.

### 4) Progressive Promotion of the New Community Movement (새마을사업의 발전적 추진)
Efforts were made to ensure all projects were decided upon at the General Assembly of Residents. Additionally, various civic matters (birth registration, death registration, marriage registration, copies of resident registration, etc.) were handled promptly, and problems were resolved to gain the trust of the residents, thereby increasing their participation in the New Community Movement.

### However, Fishing at Sea
However, fishing at sea often required immediate action, making it difficult to involve women in the projects. Together with the village chief and the prosperity association president, we persevered through daily tasks and persuasive efforts to overcome these challenges and unite the residents' spirits for the New Community Movement.

### 6) Heartwarming Stories (美談)

< Episode 1 (제1화) >
One morning in June 1976, under the bright sunshine, a large turtle that had lived in the East Sea for several hundred years crawled up to the front of the newly built village community center. The villagers gathered, each offering their opinions. Some suggested catching the turtle and selling it at Changgyeongwon, while others believed the turtle's appearance foretold the village's ruin. However, an elder present said that in ancient times, turtles were depicted to symbolize happiness, and this was surely a good omen. The elder then offered the turtle some alcohol and sent it back to the sea. The turtle swam away smoothly. This incident lightened the villagers' hearts and motivated them to work harder. Eventually, on December 10, 1976, at the National New Community Leader Conference held in Daejeon, the village was recognized as a model for the New Community Movement.


--- (p. 854) ---

Village leader Park Byung-young (朴丙玲) had the honor of receiving the prestigious Saemaul Medal (勲章) Cooperation Medal (協同章).

〈Chapter 2 (第2話)〉
This village has a village agreement (洞規約) consisting of 48 articles (條) based on the principles of Samgang-oryun (三綱五倫), which further solidifies the fundamental order (秩序) of the villagers (洞民) and aims for the happiness (幸福) and prosperity (繁榮) of future generations. The preamble (全文) states that it was unanimously (萬場一致) resolved (決議) and enacted (制定) at the general village meeting (住民總會) to be strictly adhered to (嚴格히 遵守). The Elder's Association (老班會), a gathering of village elders (洞首 以上), serves as the village's highest decision-making body (最高의 決議機關) and has handled village affairs smoothly (一事不亂) without hindrance (蹉跌) to the current Saemaul Undong (運動) progress (推進).

**b. Sad Events**


--- (p. 855) ---

*   Having spread out about 20 sacks of rice to dry in the field and gone out to the Saemaul Undong site, when they rushed back due to a sudden downpour, they found the rice and straw mats soaked, and saw a 9-year-old child crying while filling the sacks with rice, feeling their own loneliness at that moment.
*   The incident where a 60-year-old elder was dragged around by having their leg caught while their name was called out on the broadcast for not participating in the Saemaul Undong.
*   When the owner threatened to cut their own throat with a sickle during the demolition of pigsties, walls, and auxiliary buildings to create a village road, and all the villagers just stared at the leader's face,
*   The time when a couple visited the leader's house after a quarrel upon hearing that the existing wall was demolished at 10 PM, and had to flee while sleeping.

**When they felt a sense of accomplishment**

*   When Corporal Yun Il-byeong, who was serving at the front line, could endure the freezing cold without feeling it, thanks to the pride of being an excellent Saemaul Undong resident after seeing the village landscape in the military newspaper, and came home on leave to be comforted for his hard work.
*   When constructing the neighborhood center, they saw the faces of elderly people gazing at the rising smoke from the ondol room of the senior center, filled with joy.
*   When constructing a public bathhouse, everyone from young to old felt refreshed after their first bath and laughed with delight.

## Ba. Achievements from the Saemaul Undong (事業)

### 1) Spiritual Aspect (精神面)
- Through the Saemaul Undong (事業), a spirit of cooperation and service was established.
- The lesson that there is nothing we cannot achieve through cooperation and unity was learned.
- The town hall meetings (住民總會) became a forum for practicing the ideals of the Yushin (維新理念).
- The spirit of mutual aid (相扶相助), which our ancestors valued, was put into practice.

### 2) Livelihood Aspect (生活面)
- With the innovation of agricultural technology (農業技術) and the development of marine resources (資源), income increased.
- Farmers began to think and research, adopting a proactive attitude (進取的姿勢) and the will to live well.
- The spirit of thrift and savings (勤儉節約) grew stronger.
- Moving away from individualism (個人主義), the practice of cooperation (協同單位) and mutual aid (協助體制) was established, leading to the realization that everyone should live well.

### 3) Production Aspect (生産面)
- Banryeonghoe (繁榮會長) Kim Gang-ryeon, village chief (里長) Lee Byeong-hwa, fishing village chief (漁村契長) Kim Jong-seong, and Saemaul leader (指導者) Park Byeong-ryeong united (渾然一體) to develop marine resources (資源). They started with kelp farming (養食事業), setting up 20,000m with the guidance of the Fisheries Promotion Institute (水產振興院). Although they achieved great success in production (大成功), they faced failure due to the decline in kelp prices (時勢) and were unable to even recover labor costs (人件費).
- They then decided to implement stationary net fishing (停置網漁業) and applied for a fishing permit (漁業免許) from the county magistrate (郡守), who approved it promptly. They established four fishing grounds: cooperative fishing ground (協同漁場), self-help fishing ground (自助漁場), diligent fishing ground (勤勉漁場), and Saemaul fishing ground (漁場). Each fishing ground (漁場) was composed of 15-36 fishing village members (漁村契員) and practiced joint management (共同漁場管理), achieving an annual catch of over 60 million won (漁獲高). Meanwhile, agricultural production (農事) also saw a doubling of income due to the expanded cultivation (栽培) of unified rice (通一벼) and the dissemination of technology (技術).

# 3. Residents' General Assembly (住民總會)

## Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (1)

*   **Agenda (議題):** Construction of the Neighborhood Community Center (洞會舘建立)
*   **Date (日時):** December 31, 1975
*   **Location (場所):** Old Neighborhood Community Center (舊洞會舘)
*   **Attendees (參席人員):** Byung-Hwa Lee (李炳華) and 106 others
*   **Absentees (不參人員):** Dong-Taek Seo (徐童澤) and 26 others
*   **Chairperson (司會者):** Boom-Young President Kim Gwang-Ryeon (繁榮會長金光錬)

**Chairperson (司會者):** Ladies and gentlemen, the year 1975 is drawing to a close. Tomorrow will not come if today does not exist, and today is the last day of this year. With a sense of longing, I hope that today will be particularly meaningful. I ask for your sincere participation in the following discussion. It is truly a pleasure to see everyone gathered here after such a long time. It is especially heartwarming to see this small community center filled to capacity with members. The matter we must discuss with you today is the construction of a new neighborhood community center.

Currently, you are all gathered in this cramped community center filled with cigarette smoke. Up until now, this community center was built as a night school (夜學堂) by our ancestors during the late Joseon Dynasty (李朝末葉) as a place of learning, as they were concerned about the future. They had 300 households (戶) in the village, but most moved away, leaving only about 30 households. Our ancestors had such noble intentions, already putting the Saemaul spirit (新村精神) into practice.

The community center left to us by our esteemed ancestors is far too small to serve as a public meeting hall (公會堂) for our 134th generation (世帶). Therefore, we have gathered here today to discuss the construction of a new community center on this very site, to create a plaza for dialogue (對話廣場) as we move towards the 1980s.

What do you all think?

**Kim Bok-Hak:** Chairman Kim's words are truly moving. Our ancestors built a night school and taught illiterate people to read and write, which shows how great they were. However, constructing a modern building (現代式建物) would require a considerable amount of construction costs (工事費). I am worried about how we will afford it.

**Jang Wan-Sik:** Well, building a two-story house (二層屋) in a rural village (農村) like ours is unheard of. I believe we should preserve our ancestors' legacy (遺產) and not damage it.

**Jeong Young-Mun (Left Elder):** Well said, Wan-Sik. This neighborhood community center (洞會舘) was built as a night school (夜學堂) to teach people, and it is where six scholars (六進士) and six wealthy individuals (六富者) emerged. Who dares to touch this place? It is absolutely unacceptable. If you must build, do so elsewhere.

**Leader (指導者):** Left Elder's words are indeed wise. The reason we are trying to build a new community center today is to honor the intentions of our esteemed ancestors and to-


--- (p. 859) ---

We aim to further illuminate our village, striving to achieve as much as our ancestors did. We plan to build a two-story house in the center of the village. On the second floor, we will create a venue for ceremonies and an environment where children can study. On the ground floor, we will establish a senior center for elders to rest and a space for neighbors to openly discuss and share their thoughts, fostering a constructive and genuine democratic political arena. Please, esteemed village head, kindly grant your generous approval.

**Kim Haedong**: Truly an excellent response. If the youth all share the leader's vision, the elders will not oppose it. Let us hear the opinions of the young people.

**Lee Byunghwa**: I also support this idea. However, according to the design, the total construction cost is 8.3 million won, and the floor area is 55 pyeong. I am concerned about the funds. It would be better to build a single-story structure.

**Lee Youngman**: Let us carry on the spirit of mutual aid from our ancestors and, with today's Saemaul spirit, build a magnificent two-story building, just like urban residents.

**Kim Dowoon**: How much is the current village fund?

**Park Byungryeong**: Approximately 1.5 million won.

**Kim Dowoon**: How do you plan to establish a community center with that amount?

**Village Head**: I believe that funding is not an issue for establishing a village community center. If our neighbors can unite, we can accomplish anything. First, if we have the passion and sincerity to achieve our goals, we can secure support. We can also utilize funds from the Fisheries Cooperative, among others. If residents transport sand and gravel and bear the labor costs, it will not be a difficult task.

**Lee Gyusik**: If we can secure the funds, let's give it a try. If it can be accomplished through the residents' efforts, what is there to fear? Let's do it.

**Kim Hangshik**: We will bear the labor costs, so go ahead and do it. But don't ask for money later. Do you understand, Village Head?

**Village Head**: Yes, I understand. If everyone participates diligently and works hard, I won't mention money. What do you all think?

The young side agrees.
The elders remain silent.

**Moderator**: Today, on this meaningful last day of 1975, we have made an important decision. Do we all unanimously agree? Especially, we need the elders' agreement.

**Lee Byungdoo**: Today, the younger generation is taking the lead. Although we lack strength, we will support from behind, so please proceed with careful consideration.

**Moderator**: Thank you very much.

It is late at night. This concludes our meeting. Goodnight on your way home through the dark night.


--- (p. 860) ---

As reported above by the accountant (會計員), if there are any questions regarding the financial settlement (決算), please feel free to ask.
Lee Young-man : Thank you very much for your hard work. Initially, I understood that the construction cost (工事費) was planned to be 8,300,000 Won, but the actual expenditure (支出) was 5,776,600 Won, leaving a surplus of 2,522,400 Won from the construction cost (工事費), isn't that correct?
Leader (指導者) : Of course (勿論) it is. This is due to the tremendous effort and labor contribution (勞力負擔) of the Dongmin (洞民) who directly provided gravel and sand;


--- (p. 861) ---

It was because they worked with their own hands that the labor burden (勞力負擔) was covered.

**Kim Jae-sung:** To build the Donghoe Hall (洞會舘), we borrowed 1,000,000 won from the Agricultural Cooperative (農協). How do you plan to repay this loan?

**Kim Do-woon:** Let's sell the village's paddy fields to pay it back.

**Kim Kwang-ryeon:** No, that's not acceptable. The funds borrowed from the Agricultural Cooperative (農協) should be repaid by cultivating medicinal herbs, such as Chinese wormwood (藥草 방풍), on the barren beach (不毛地 白沙場) this autumn and using the income (所得金) generated.

**Kim Chung-hak:** That is indeed an excellent idea. Let's all do that.

**Chairperson (司會者):** Are there any other questions? None.

**Myeon Total Affairs Chief (面總務係長):** While we are all here, I would like to say a few words. On behalf of the Myeon Chief (面長), I would like to express my gratitude for your tireless efforts. When the President (大統領) first decided to provide special support (特別支援) for this project, there were concerns about the immense task planned for this village. We requested reconsideration (再考) several times, but you insisted on completing it. From the report (報告) afterward, we were genuinely worried until its completion, but seeing the whole community (全住民) working together (協同團結) and pushing forward (推進) at every guidance session (指導次), we never doubted that today's results would be achieved. Now, we have a rare dialogue plaza (對話의 광장) in the entire country (全國). I kindly ask you to manage and utilize this fruit of your hard work (努力) wisely to achieve the intended purpose (所期의 목적) and to continue to put effort into its operation (運營). Once again, I thank you for your efforts (勞苦).

**Chairperson (司會者):** Then, today's meeting (會議) is adjourned. Please sign and stamp if you are a representative (代表者) of each class (班別).

♦ Minutes of Meeting (會議錄)(3)

Agenda (議題): Simple Water Supply Facility (簡易給水施設)
Date (日時): June 10, 1976, 23:00
Location (場所): Village Hall (마을會館) 2nd Floor Conference Room (會議室)
Attendees (參席人員): Kim Gwang-il (金光日) and 110 others


--- (p. 864) ---

Absent: Lee Deok-jun (李得俊) and 24 others
Chairperson: Village Head Lee Byung-hwa (李炳華)

Chairperson: Thank you for attending today despite your exhaustion from the busy farming season. Although 24 people could not attend due to unavoidable circumstances related to fishing work, I hope you understand and help us proceed with today's meeting. Now that the community center has been completed, we need to discuss the installation of a simple water supply facility. As you know, our village's water situation is not good. Those living near the sea have pump water with high salt content, and the stream water is unclean, which is not only unhygienic but also insufficient during droughts. Uljin County has offered to support the installation of a simple water supply facility if the residents wish, so shall we push forward with this?

Kim Kwang-il: While the water supply facility is good, we just completed the community center, and we are short-handed during the busy farming season. How can we carry out this project? Moreover, the men are working at sea, and it would be too much for the women alone to handle.

Kim Nok-man: It's not just about the project, but let's think about our spirit. Can we really do so many projects in one year? Let's do it next year.

Kim Kwang-ryeon: Such projects don't happen every year, and we should do it when the county budget is available. It's not like there's always money set aside for our village. Although it's tough and requires effort, I believe we should start and keep going without stopping.

Seo Hae-su: How much is the budget, and what exactly is a simple water supply facility?

Leader: The total construction cost is 4.5 million won. Out of this, 2.5 million won will be supported by the county, and the rest will be borne by the village. The project involves building a water collection well by the Namdaecheon stream, using electricity to pump water up to a high place on the mountain, and connecting pipes to supply water to each household. It is a project that requires a lot of manpower. Once the facility is installed, it will help with the women's chores, and they won't have to carry water buckets anymore. They can just turn on the tap in the kitchen and use water freely.

Jeong Bok-yong: In that case, the women members would benefit the most.

Village Head: Of course, it's great to be able to drink clean water as much as you want.

Jang Wan-sik: Then, let's hear the opinion of the women's club president since she is present.

Women's Club President (Lee Bong-geum (李鳳今)): I'm sorry. I attended today's meeting as the village head told me to, not knowing what it was about. It seems it's about this matter. It's a tough request, but please install the facility.

Kim Jong-sung: If funds are insufficient, I will go to the Hupo Fisheries Cooperative and request financial support. I will discuss the cooperative's returned business funds with the cooperative head.

Kim Seo-hak: Please ask for a lot of financial support. Our village is in a difficult situation.

Jeong Yeon-mun (鄭淵文) (Elder at the table): Financial support is good, and the women's club president's words are also good, but we need people who can work to

---


--- (p. 865) ---

To the women's association president: Can women come out and do men's work?
Women's Association President: Yes, we can. Although we are weak women, we will actively work on this in the women's association.
Host: How about it, everyone? The women's association president is pleading with us.
Seo Jeong-mo: Let's do it. I'm fine with it.
Kim Man-sik: Seo Jeong-mo doesn't have a pump in his own house, so he says let's have running water. (Everyone laughs)
Leader: Of course, a full person cannot understand the feelings of a hungry person. There may be some people who don't lack water. But let's think about working for the entire village, not just ourselves, and muster up the courage to work again.
Host: Does everyone agree?
All: We agree.
Host: I am greatly thankful.

First, the 500,000 won in cash contributions must be deposited into the agricultural cooperative (農協) account.

**Chairperson (司會者):** Everything will be carried out as you have decided. I ask for your continued cooperation and participation. The meeting is adjourned.

# Gyeongnam (慶南) Uiryeong County (宜寧郡) Bulim-myeon (富林面) Yeobae-ri (餘背里) Haya (下餘) Village

## 1. Village Overview (槪況)

### a. History (沿革)

*   Approximately 580 years ago, the monk Muhak (舞鶴禪士) passed through this area and, finding the mountains and water clear and the stream water exceptionally pure, named the river flowing through the village Okcheon (玉川) and established a temple called Yuhaeksa (留鶴寺).
*   As eminent monks (高僧) like Muhak (舞鶴禪士) were always present, the village was traditionally called Yeobul (餘佛).
*   Around 1924, during the Japanese colonial period (倭政), the village name was changed to its current administrative name, Yeobae-ri (餘背里). Administratively, the village is divided into Sangyeo (上餘) and Haya (下餘), with this village being Haya (下餘).

### b. Location (位置) and Conditions (與件)

<Location (位置)>

*   Located 30 km northeast of the county seat (郡所在地) and 6 km northeast of the Bulim-myeon (富林面) seat (所在地), along the provincial road (地方道) between Jinju (晋州) and Daegu (大邱).
*   The village is situated along a valley following the slopes of Mitaesan (山), which has an elevation (海拔) of 680 meters, at the back of the village.

<Conditions (與件)>

*   As a mid-mountain village (中山間), the soil quality (土質) is generally infertile, with an average cultivated area (耕地面積) of 7.7 pyeong (反步) per household (戶當), characterized by a scarcity of fields (田) and an abundance of paddies (沓).
*   Transportation is relatively good, with eight daily scheduled buses operating between Jinju (晋州) and Daegu (大邱).
*   Agricultural sideline (農家副業) activities include sericulture (養蠶) and holchigi, generating an annual income (收入) of approximately 300,000 won (萬원) per household (戶當).

### c. Basic Status (基本現況)

### La. Village Characteristics (特性)

Located in a mid-mountain (中山間) area, the village has convenient transportation (交通) but relatively low income (所得) compared to the residents' (住民) education level (學力). In front of the village, there is about 10 hectares of abandoned wasteland (荒無地) consisting of national mixed-breed land (國有雜種地) that is prone to flooding during the rainy season (雨期浸水地帶). This land could be developed (開發) for agricultural use (農耕地) in the future.

### 2. Village Process (過程)

#### Ga. Situation Before 1970 (以前)

#### 1) Basic Environment (基礎環境)
* Out of a total of 198 houses (棟), only 3 were tiled-roof houses (기와집), while the remaining 195 were thatched-roof houses (초가집). The alleys were so narrow, with some less than 1 meter wide, that residents could barely pass each other carrying shoulder poles (지게).
* The embankments (堤防) of the small streams (小河川) and village brooks (細川) had been washed away (流失) by floods (洪水) long ago, leading to annual flooding (浸水) and burial (埋沒) at the lower reaches (下端) of the small streams. This made it nearly impossible to expect any harvest (收穫) from the surrounding farmland (田沓).

#### 2) Mental State (精神狀態)
* Due to low income (低所得), livelihoods (生計) were uncertain (莫然), and residents often gambled (賭博) and drank excessively (술타령) in winter, squandering (蕩盡) their household finances (家事).
* Neighbors often harbored jealousy (猜忌) and envy (嫉妬), engaging in fights and living idly on credit (外上술) while struggling to get through the hungry gap (보릿고개).


--- (p. 872) ---

The situation was dire and struggling.

### 3) Cultural Life (文化生活)
- Education (教育) for children (子女) was not even considered to be sent to the national school (國民學校) in the village (本部落), nor was it financially feasible (形便).
- Only 5 out of 96 households (戶) owned a radio (라디오), and there was no capacity (能力) to afford (保有) electrical facilities (電氣施設) or other cultural facilities (文化施設).

### 4) Daily Life (衣食住生活)
- Every year (每年), crops (農作物) were damaged by flooding (浸水), buried (埋沒), or lost (流失), preventing normal harvests (正常的收穫). During the hungry gap (보릿고개), people survived on ferns (쑥).
- Clothing (衣生活) consisted of worn-out rags (헌 누더기).
- Without electricity (電氣), nights were desolate (寂寞江山).
- The thatched roofs (草家) were typical (典型的) of a mountainous village (山間農村), often infested with snakes (뱀) or centipedes (지네).

### 5) Income Level (所得水準)
- Agriculture (營農) focused on rice and wheat (米麥) using traditional methods (在來式) that relied on the heavens (하늘만 쳐다보는). Income was meager, around 300,000 won (萬圓).

## II. Development Process (發展過程)

### 1) Motivation (動機) and Trial Project Results (試驗事業의 성과)
#### a) Development Motivation (開發動機)
- Some (一部) leaders (指導層) wanted to awaken the lazy and disorderly (無秩序) spirit (精神) through communal village projects (共同事業), but most residents (住民) refused to work, deterring any action.
- When Park Chung-hee (朴正熙), the President (大統領), launched the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) nationwide on April 22, 1970 (1970年4月22日), this village remained asleep.
- In the autumn of 1974 (74年 가을), the current Saemaul leader (指導者) Cho Seon-gyu (趙善奎) convinced the residents (住民) to complete a 320-meter expansion of An-gil Road (安吉擴張) and improve the roofs (地붕개량) of 20 houses (棟).
- By early 1975 (75년 초), 250 meters of farm roads (農路) were completed (完成), sparking Saemaul enthusiasm (意慾) among the residents (住民).

### 2) Leader Selection Process (指導者選定過程)
- Annual spring and autumn (春秋) meetings (大洞會) were held twice a year (每年 2回). The current Saemaul leader (指導者), Cho Seon-gyu (趙善奎), after ending his long life away (客地生活) and returning home (歸鄕) in the autumn of 1974 (74年 가을), led the village development (開發) despite not being an official leader (指導者).
- On October 23, 1974 (74年 10月 23日), during the autumn meeting (秋季大洞會), he was unanimously (萬場一致) elected (選定) as the leader (指導者) by the residents (住民).

### 3) Leader Activities (活動) and Replacement (交替狀況)
- First leader (初代): Lee Daejin (李大鎭) (Nov. 1, 1970 ~ Dec. 20, 1972)
  - Expanded An-gil Road (安吉擴張) by 100 meters (100m).
- Second leader (2代): Jo Ilgyu (趙一奎) (Dec. 21, 1972 ~ Oct. 22, 1974)
  - Expanded An-gil Road (安吉擴張) by 320 meters (320m).


--- (p. 873) ---

Choe Sang-gwi (74.10.23~Present)
- Complete roof improvement
- Road construction: 1,600m
- Apple orchard development: 5,000 pyeong
- Communal compost shed: 1 building, 30 pyeong
- Communal purchasing and selling facility: 1 building, 12 pyeong
- Communal warehouse: 1 building, 30 pyeong
- Temporary water supply facility: 96 households
- Small stream embankment repair: 600m

## 4) Overcoming Difficulties

### Road Construction Project

Due to the excessive amount of work, residents' complaints never ceased. Although we could have used the foundation stones for stone walls by breaking the locally called "deungkkokji" rocks, the superstition that damaging those stones would bring misfortune to the entire village prevented residents' cooperation, making it impossible to obtain stones for the stone walls. During the construction, the vibrant Saemaul Undong came to a complete halt due to the injury of village youth leader Jo Yong-gil.

*   Although the development committee and all residents said the amount of work for road construction was too much, only leader Choe Sang-gwi had the firm belief that he could accomplish it alone. He visited each household whenever he had time and eventually persuaded all residents,
*   To break the locally called "deungkkokji" rocks, a village meeting was held for three consecutive days, and after earnest appeals, the consensus of all residents was obtained to break the rocks.
*   At that time, all residents thought that if they lived well in the future, the Saemaul leader alone would not live well either. Seeing the leader working tirelessly day and night, they decided to break the deungkkokji rocks together, share the benefits, and if any misfortune befell, share it together. The leader first broke the rocks, and all residents cooperated enthusiastically. However, one day, while Jo Yong-gil was working with all his might on a mountain slope, he suddenly rolled down with the rocks he had broken, suffering a spinal fracture and was hospitalized at Daegu Hae-tae Surgical Hospital, hovering between life and death.
*   Family, relatives, and residents gathered at the Saemaul leader's house, shouting that the Saemaul Undong was ruining the neighborhood. The leader, unable to find a solution, almost stopped eating and drinking. However, a few days later, a message came from Jo Yong-gil, who had regained consciousness: "Leader, please forget about my concerns and make sure our long-cherished goal of completing that road succeeds."
*   The leader's feelings at that time were indescribable, and upon hearing this, all villagers were deeply moved and accelerated the project period with doubled enthusiasm and sincerity. As a result, an excellent embankment and 1,600m of roads were completed simultaneously, solidifying the livelihood of this village.

## 5) Heartwarming Stories

*   During the construction of roads and small stream embankments, an unexpected accident injured the village youth leader Jo Yong-gil (then youth leader)


--- (p. 874) ---

When Mr. Yong-gil Cho (趙鏞吉) was hospitalized at Daegu (大邱) Uihwae External Hospital (外科病院), the entire village (全住民) was filled with despair, abandoned their work, blamed their leader, and severely criticized him. At that moment, when Mr. Cho wished for the continuous promotion of farm road construction (農路開設) even in the face of life-and-death situations, the entire village was moved and successfully completed the project through cooperation and unity. As a result, 24,000 pyeong (坪) of abandoned land was transformed into fertile soil (沃土). Meanwhile, the villagers voluntarily collected 200,000 won (萬圓) as a gift and handed it over to Mr. Cho for his hospital expenses (入院費). Even now, as Mr. Cho is bedridden (不具者) and recuperating (療養) at his home (自宅), the entire village takes turns to console (慰勞) and encourage (歡勵) him.

6) Land and Cash Donation (現金喜捨) Status (狀況)

They generously donated land (土地喜捨) for the farm road construction without hesitation. Moreover, many villagers lined up to donate cash (現金) to cover Mr. Cho's hospital expenses (入院費).

### Ba. Achievements through Saemaul Undong

1) Spiritual Aspect
*   Through spiritual reform fostering cooperation and unity, a firm belief in the power of diligence and honesty was instilled;
*   The spirit of helping neighbors and other community service movements became a way of life.
2) Livelihood Aspect
*   To increase non-farming income, the women's club actively promoted sericulture and other ventures, raising non-farming income per household to over ₩30;
*   As income improved through cattle farming, various cultural facilities like TVs were introduced;
*   The realization that the prosperity of neighbors contributes to one's own well-being was put into practice.
3) Production Aspect
*   Expanded cultivation of unified rice strains doubled production;
*   The cultivation of special crops like onions and tobacco, along with various side businesses, increased residents' income.
4) Income Aspect
*   Improved farming methods and expanded farm side businesses significantly increased farm income;
*   Storing various agricultural products in communal village warehouses generated storage fee revenue;
*   Through cooperative farming, per household income reached ₩1,402,000 by the end of 1976.

# 3. Residents' Assembly (住民總會)

*   Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (1)

| | |
| :---------- | :------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Date (日時)** | December 3, 1975, 14:20 ~ 17:30                              |
| **Location (參席)** | Hyeo Village (下余部落) Cho's House (趙氏 宅) |
| **Attendance (人員)** | Total 76 people (名)                                         |

Following the opening remarks by the village head (里長), the meeting proceeded with the following agenda:
1. National Ceremony (國民儀禮), 2. Opening Remarks (開會辭), 3. Report on Dongjeong (洞政) Progress (經過報告) for 1975, 4. Additional Settlement Report (精算報告) on Wage-for-Work Project (勞賃就勞事業), 5. Exploring Effective Operation Plans (運營方案) for Village Purchase and Sale Center (購販場), 6. On the Establishment of Saemaul Cooperative Farm (協同農場造成事業), 7. Telephone Business (電化事業) Promotion Funds (推進資金) and Post-Management Report (事後管理報告), 8. Adoption of Village Cooperative Prohibition of Alcohol (禁酒案), 9. Other Discussion Items (討議事項), 10. Closing (閉會)

**Key Points of Opening Remarks (開會辭 要旨)**: Today's Donghoe (洞會) is being held again because the last autumn Donghoe (洞會) had a low turnout, which did not sufficiently reflect the residents' opinions. At the village development committee meeting on November 16, it was decided to hold this Donghoe (洞會) today, December 3. I ask that your sincere opinions be fully reflected in today's Donghoe (洞會) and that you provide guidance for the Dongjeong (洞政) moving forward.

Following the village head's report on Dongjeong (洞政) progress, the following questions were raised:

**Jeong Seon-seok (鄭先石)**: Our Hyeo Saemaul warehouse (下余新村倉庫) often stores grain (糧穀) from other villages and government grain (政府糧穀). How is the storage fee (保管費) handled in these cases?

**Village Head (里長)**: We plan to charge storage fees in the future. I am currently negotiating this with the relevant authorities (有關當局).

**Han Tae-hyeon (韓台炫)**: I understand that a large amount of National Agricultural Cooperative Federation (農協) fertilizer (肥料) is being stored in our Saemaul warehouse (新村倉庫). How is the storage fee (保管費) handled in this case?

**Village Head (里長)**: I have never given permission for fertilizer (肥料) to be stored in the Saemaul warehouse (新村倉庫), and of course, we are not receiving any storage fees (保管料).

**Lee Hak-mun (李學問)**: How was National Agricultural Cooperative Federation (農協) fertilizer (肥料) able to be stored in our village warehouse (村倉庫) without the village head's (里長) consent (同意) or permission (承諾)? I would like an answer to this.

**Village Head (里長)**: (No response, 默默不答)

**Cho Yun-gyu (趙潤奎)**: The National Agricultural Cooperative Federation (農協) has separate storage businesses (保管業者) and warehouses (保管倉庫). How was our village warehouse (村倉庫) used for storage (入庫), and who opened the warehouse door (倉庫門) to allow the fertilizer (肥料) to be stored (積載)?

**Lee Dae-ho (李大鎬)**: In response to Cho Yun-gyu's (趙潤奎) question, I will explain. I am handling the storage (保管), but I cannot be responsible for the payment of storage fees (保管料支拂). You should ask the unit cooperative leader (單位組合長) about the storage fee (保管料) issue. The storage (保管) was clearly instructed through the village head (里長).

**Leader (指導者)**: Alright, let's do this. We will thoroughly investigate (徹底히 究明) who authorized the storage (保管) and whether storage fees (保管料) were paid. We will report back in a few days (數日). (Note: A few days later, it was clarified that while the village head (里長) was away, a National Agricultural Cooperative Federation (農協) employee came and asked the village head's (里長) wife for the warehouse key (保管倉庫 열쇠).)


--- (p. 878) ---

,it was simply stored and kept, and since the woman did not mention this fact to the village head, it was a fact unknown to the village head. (The storage fee was to be paid soon by the agricultural cooperative.)

**Leader (指導者)**: Fellow villagers, I believe you are curious about the Saemaul Cooperative Farm establishment project. However, we cannot start the project without concluding conditional contracts with all individual landowners within the farm establishment area. Please wait for a while, and I will inform you of the results.

**Villagers (洞民一同)**: Alright, we understand.

**Lee Dae-ho (李大鎬)**: I would like to mention the post-management issue of the electrification project's savings. On November 11 last year, the development committee decided to entrust me with this matter. I have changed the account name of the project funds, issued by the local agricultural cooperative in the name of Cho Sun-gwe (趙善奎), to my name, Lee Dae-ho (李大鎬). I have also taken responsibility for managing the 278,100 won project funds with a 2% monthly interest until January 30, 1976.

**Villagers (洞民一同)**: Alright, we understand.

**Han Tae-hyeon (韓台炫)**: Our village has been visited twice by the tax office authorities, and illegal liquor has been discovered, even resulting in fines. Such cases are not only shameful but also violate the Yushin ideology. Therefore, our villagers should firmly decide to ban makgeolli (rice wine).

**Villagers (洞民一同)**: Let's resolve to do so. That's a great suggestion.

**Leader (指導者)**: Then, let the village head draft a resolution and convene a neighborhood meeting to have it signed and stamped.

**Villagers (洞民一同)**: Alright, let's do that and rid our village of decadent customs, making it a bright and cheerful place.

**Village Head (里長)**: Then, today's neighborhood meeting is adjourned. To record the contents of today's meeting for future reference, I will first receive the stamps of the village development committee members representing everyone's intentions.

**Villagers (洞民一同)**: We agree.

**Village Head (里長)**: Then, the meeting is adjourned.

## Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (2)

| Item       | Contents                                                                                     |
| :--------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Date**   | March 8, 1976, 9:00 AM ~ 11:00 AM                                                         |
| **Venue**  | East side of the village's communal apple orchard complex                                   |
| **Agenda** | Interim settlement of President (大統領) His Excellency's support project and request for completion of village communal apple orchard complex |
| **Host**   | Saemaul Leader (指導者) (Cho Sun-gwe (趙善奎))                                             |
| **Attendees** | 61 people                                                                                 |

**Host (司會者)**: Fellow residents! Thank you very much for participating in this residents' general meeting held in the communal apple orchard complex, which will plant dreams for our future, despite your busy schedules. We convened the village development committee on March 6 and March 3 last month, but we did so to consult with you, the residents.


--- (p. 879) ---

Today, I have convened this meeting. As you all know, the agenda for today is to discuss the settlement of accounts for the apple orchard complex, which was promoted through the special grant from His Excellency, and the issues related to post-management. I believe you are all aware, but if you have any questions about the promotion of the special grant business or have good opinions regarding post-management, please share them.

**Leader:** Since February 4th, we have been continuously working to complete a 5,000-pyeong apple orchard complex in our village. If there are any points you, the residents, are curious about, I will take your questions.

**Kim Sang-beom:** Although some residents say that the business selection was wrong or that it is shoddy, the leader thinks there is no need to pay attention to such words. Those people are clearly playing intentional tricks to hinder the development of our village. The more so, let us cooperate and unite, centering around the leader, and work even harder.

**Oh Gi-man:** As the old saying goes, "If a cousin buys a field, it hurts the stomach," right? The joint apple orchard complex construction is a business promoted for the entire village to live well. The leader should not pay any attention to such words at all.

**Leader:** Yes, thank you very much for your kind words. Then, I will explain to you, the residents, about the apple orchard complex construction.

First, the business selection for the special grant was made by the residents at the village general meeting held at the new village classroom of Dongrim Elementary School immediately after I received the funds at the National Saemaul Leader Conference last December. Therefore, I believe there should be no objections to this business.

Second, regarding the management of the funds for this business, the account is jointly named by the face chief, the village chief, and myself and deposited in the agricultural cooperative. Is there any room for distrust here? I have handed over all matters related to the business funds and related documents to the village chief to be handled exclusively, with the approval of the committee members at the Development Committee meeting on March 6th. And even now, the funds have not been executed at all.

**All Residents:** We understand. We have no distrust or doubt about that. Let's plant either apple trees or fruit trees to bear more fruit.

**Leader:** Yes, I understand. Then, I would like to discuss with you all about the joint apple orchard complex construction business in the village. How should we proceed with the planting and soil preparation work in the future?

**Jo Yong-so:** Since we are currently busy with barley field maintenance, let's postpone the joint work for about 4-5 days.

**Jo Il-gyu:** That's a good idea, but what about adjusting the number of working days for those who have not come out even once so far?

**Leader:** First, let's decide on the proposal made by Mr. Jo Yong-so. It would be good to start full-scale mobilization from 4-5 days later.

**Kim Sang-woo:** That would be good. (All residents agree)

**Leader:** Then, I will answer the question raised by Mr. Jo Il-gyu. Regarding the adjustment of the number of working days for participation, since we will continue to work together in this complex, it is not something that will be finished in one or two days. We will stop the participation of those who have participated a lot and continue the participation of those who have participated less.


--- (p. 880) ---

We will adjust the number of days.
All residents: We understand.
Cho Yoon-gyu (趙潤奎): There is an individual land share within our village's collective apple orchard area belonging to Mr. Lee Gwang-gi (李光基). Before the formation of the orchard, Mr. Lee Gwang-gi had agreed at the village development committee meeting to contribute 30% of his land to the village. I've heard there's much discontent among residents about this issue, so please clarify this matter.
Leader: We discussed this at the development committee meeting on March 6th and 7th but couldn't reach a solution. Mr. Lee Gwang-gi proposed to contribute 35% of his land to the village in advance, on the condition that the village manages it together until the first harvest. If anyone has good suggestions, please share them.
All residents: (Silent)
Leader: Why are you silent? Please speak up here and now without holding back.
Lee Dae-ho (李大鎬): Rather than discussing this and that about planting apple trees in the collective orchard, please speak frankly here about Mr. Lee Gwang-gi's land share and the portion to be transferred to the village.
Kim Sang-yul (金相律): Mr. Lee Gwang-gi has made many concessions so far, but let's ask him to make more concessions. I asked him, and he said he has consistently maintained his initial conditions without any changes.
Lee Dae-ho (李大鎬): Gwang-gi asked me to meet him and said he would contribute 40% to the village and that the village should manage the future orchard together with the collective apple orchard.
Leader: Residents! Just now, Mr. Lee Gwang-gi conveyed that he will donate 40% of his land to the village. Is this acceptable to everyone?
All residents: Yes, it is.
Lee Gwang-gi (李光基): In fact, I do not oppose the village's activities, but my contribution of 40% is actually more than 50%. This is because the stream area I'm contributing to the village is also my land. Anyway, I hope you all understand my feelings and use this as an opportunity to further dedicate yourselves to the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement).
All residents: (Applauding to express welcome)
Leader: Although the village development committee members and I have had many concerns that residents were unaware of until today's general meeting, we are very pleased that the matter has been resolved satisfactorily as residents wished. That concludes today's meeting.

# Minutes (會議錄) (4)

*   Date (日時) : March 25, 1976
*   Location (場所) : Village Community Center (會館)
*   Agenda (議題) : Meeting on the Construction of Farm Roads (農路)
*   Attendees (參席人員) : 75 people (名)
*   Chairperson (社會者) : Saemaul Leader (指導者) Cho Seon-gyu (趙善奎)

**Chairperson (社會者)** : Before we begin, I would like to wish a speedy recovery to Cho Yong-gil (趙鏞吉), who is currently hospitalized in Daegu due to an unexpected accident during the farm road construction project. I, along with a few village representatives, have conveyed your heartfelt donations to him, and he has promised that the farm road will be completed.
**Chairperson (社會者)** : Now, please share your opinions on how we should proceed with the farm road construction project, which was temporarily halted due to Cho Yong-gil's accident.
**Lee Dae-ho (李大鎬)** : As I mentioned during my visit to Cho Yong-gil, we should strive to complete the project despite any difficulties that may arise. This will not only benefit our village but also be a way to repay his request.
**Cho Dae-gyu (趙大奎)** : Last time, we started with the "gi tteumkkokji" rock. Should we start with that rock again this time as well?
**Chairperson (社會者)** : As before, I will be the first to tackle that rock. I feel guilty that Cho Yong-gil was injured instead of me. We should do our best to ensure that he is the first to ride a taxi on the farm road we have constructed.
**All Residents (住民一同)** : Yes, let's do that.
**Chairperson (社會者)** : What is the best way to proceed with the mobilization (出役)?
**Kim Sang-yul (金相律)** : As before, let's have all able-bodied residents (全住民) participate and complete the project before the busy farming season (農繁期).
**All Residents (住民一同)** : That sounds good.
**Chairperson (社會者)** : Are there any other comments?
**All Residents (住民一同)** : None.
**Chairperson (社會者)** : Then, we will adjourn today's meeting. Let us all pray for Cho Yong-gil's (趙鏞吉) speedy recovery... and we will start immediately tomorrow (來日).

## 4. Future Development Plans

*   There is a temple called Yuhaksa (留鶴寺) at the upper end of Sangyeo (上餘) Village, which attracts many visitors. However, buses do not currently operate to the temple. In the future, plans are to construct an 8-meter-wide road along the remaining 3.5 km section (excluding the existing 1.6 km agricultural road from Sangyeo Village) to attract tourists and also to facilitate the movement of residents and students.
*   Plans are to promote livestock farming by utilizing the abundant meadows of Yangpyeonsan (兩便山) to improve income.
*   Negotiations are underway with the Canadian Children's Relief Fund to secure a promise of 50 dairy cows (6-month-old) for free support, and plans are to promote dairy farming.
*   Plans are to cultivate approximately 10 hectares of abandoned mixed national land in front of the village to expand farmland.

Residents dedicated to increasing fertilizer production

# 1. Village Overview

## a. History

*   Located beneath the 1,200-meter-high Sinbul Mountain (神拂山), the village was established on wasteland formed by mixed forests, rocks, and wetlands.
*   After the liberation of Korea on August 15, 150 households of refugees settled here in 1947, marking the village's inception.
*   Subsequently, the settlers formed a tent village and relied on relief grain for sustenance.
*   During the day, they engaged in land reclamation and farming. However, when the government ceased grain distribution in March 1950, 135 households dispersed in search of livelihoods, leaving only 15 households. The village became subordinate to the neighboring Sangcheon (象川) village.
*   In 1960, 37 impoverished households resettled in the area, increasing the population to 52 households. The village was named "Sinan" (新安) and became an independent hamlet.
*   Between 1960 and 1968, the villagers reclaimed 50 hectares of farmland for agriculture. The construction of the Gyeongbu Expressway (京釜高速道) led to the consolidation of the village.

## b. Conditions and Location

### <Conditions>

*   Adjacent to the Gyeongbu Expressway (京釜高速道), this plain village has poor soil quality, making it highly susceptible to drought. The village also faces water shortages, posing challenges for crop cultivation.
*   The village has completed its settlement structure improvement. Its layout is zoned, livestock barns are consolidated, and communal facilities, cultural welfare facilities, and housing have been upgraded to rural standard homes.
*   The village operates pig farming, silkworm farming, Hanwoo (韓牛) cattle, persimmon, and pear orchards to increase farmers' income.

### <Location>

*   Located 32 km northwest of the county office, a 60-minute drive away.
*   6 km south of the Unyang (彦陽) Interchange, which connects the Gyeongbu Expressway (京釜高速道路) and the Ulsan Industrial Complex (蔚山工業團地), a 30-minute drive away.
*   4 km from the Tongdosa (通度寺) Interchange heading towards Seoul, a 15-minute drive away.

## Ra. Characteristics of the Village (特性)

*   After liberation (解放), as a settlement (定着村) for repatriates (歸還同胞) who overcame all difficulties (難關) and hardships (逆境) to achieve self-reliance (自立)
*   Along with the opening (開通) of the Gyeongbu Expressway (京釜高速道), the village promoted settlement structure improvement (聚落構造改善) and in 1975, the village structure (構造) was divided into sections (區劃化)
*   The access road (進入路) was widened to 5 meters, the inner road to 4 meters, and a new livestock barn (畜舍) of 120 pyeong (坪) was built to collectively raise Hanwoo (韓牛)
*   Communal facilities (共同利用施設), cultural and welfare facilities (文化福祉施設), and self-defense facilities (自衛施設) were established
*   Standard farming houses (農家住宅) of 24 buildings (棟) were constructed, with rooms (房) equipped with hot water heating (溫水煖房器), and toilets (便所) were improved to be covered and disinfected (有蓋消毒式)


--- (p. 885) ---

* The village wall was made of natural hedges (生울타리) and was selected as a promotional village (弘報마을) for foreigners.

## 2. Village Development Process (發展過程)

### 가. Situation Before 1970 (70年 以前 的 狀況)

#### 1) Environmental Aspect (環境面)

* As a resettlement village (定着村) for repatriates (歸還同胞), the village was scattered and desolate.
* The village consisted of thatched houses (草家) and shacks, with households struggling to escape poverty (貧困).
* The alleys were only 2 meters wide, barely enough for a single cart (리어카) to pass.
* The walls were made of crooked earthen fences, with many parts collapsed or damaged.
* There was no simple water supply system (簡易上水道), and residents relied on wells (井戶) for drinking water.
* Only 16 out of 53 households had improved roofs, leaving 37 households with thatched houses. There was no electricity (電氣), telephone facilities (電話施設), or TV sets, making it a backward village.

#### 2) Income Aspect (所得面)

| Crop Name (作物名) | Scale (規模)         | Production (生產量) | Production Value (生產額)    | Remarks (備考)                  |
| :------------- | :----------------- | :------------- | :---------------- | :-------------------------- |
| Cereals (米穀)     | 21.4ha             | 140%           | 41,500,000 won (千元) |                             |
| Wheat (麥類)     | 12.6"              | 65"            | 5,200"            |                             |
| Beans (豆類)     | 1"                 | 5"             | 1,000"            |                             |
| Misc. Grains (雜穀)     | 2"                 | 7"             | 1,300"            |                             |
| Fruits (果樹)     | 2,600 pyeong (坪)        | 30"            | 2,050"            |                             |
| Hanwoo (韓牛)     | 32 heads (頭)           | 32 heads (頭)       | 3,200"            |                             |
| Total (計)         | -                  | -              | 27,250"           | Per household income (所得) 5,140,000 won (千元) |

#### 3) Spiritual Aspect (精神面)

* Residents lived recklessly, indulging in drinking (飮酒) and gambling (賭博), with no thought for the future.
* There was no spirit of self-reliance (自立) or creative movement (創造的 精神運動) to forge new paths for life.

#### 4) Production Aspect (生産面)

* The village focused on main grain (主穀) production (生産), but due to lack of water source (水源) development (開發) and severe drought (旱魃), it could not increase unit production (單位 生產量).
* The soil quality (土質) was poor, and efforts to enhance soil fertility (地力 增進) were neglected, leading to poor results in other crop productions.
* During the farming off-season (農閑期), residents showed no interest (意慾) in producing straw crafts (藁工品), leading to low adoption (普及).
* High-value vegetables (高等 菜蔬) were not produced due to unfavorable geographical conditions (立地的 与件).
* Overall, the village's production was poor, keeping residents' income at a low level.


--- (p. 886) ---

## 5) Cultural Aspect
*   The village had no electricity, so there were no TVs or refrigerators.
*   There were only 22 radios, 6 copies of central newspapers, and 2 copies of local newspapers.
*   Occasionally, the county would screen mobile traveling films.

## B. Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

### 1) Development Motive
*   In December 1969, with the opening of the Gyeongbu Expressway, the nearby village of Sangcheon in Gyeongsangnam-do began its first cluster improvement project.
*   The scattered village was organized into a collective, and the nearby hill was developed into residential land. In 1972, 67 units of standard rural housing were newly built in the Asrael Gibbs style.
*   The village was equipped with a community center, a purchasing and selling market, a warehouse, a communal kitchen, etc.
*   A communal cattle barn and a communal pigsty were newly built, leading to increased farm income through Hanwoo fattening and pig farming.
*   However, the village of Sinan, located just 500 meters away from Sangcheon, witnessed the prosperity of Sangcheon and always yearned to create a similarly comfortable village.
*   Due to its location near the expressway, the village was designated as the optimal site for promoting the development value and achievements of the Saemaul Undong.
*   The cluster improvement and housing renovation projects were promoted, and the village was developed as a model for foreign promotion.

### 2) Activities of the Leader
*   Appointed as a Saemaul leader on January 10, 1975, the leader began the Saemaul cluster improvement project in April of the same year.
*   Day and night, the leader devoted all efforts to the Saemaul project, dividing the village into sections, and building a livestock barn, a children's playground, a communal laundry area, 24 units of standard rural housing, a community center combined with a warehouse, simple water supply facilities, a communal pigsty, and a camellia housing complex.
*   The village, which was initially a settlement for returning compatriots, was improved to become a model village for foreign promotion.
*   In December 1976, the leader received the Saemaul Medal of Cooperation at the National Saemaul Leaders Conference.
*   From 1977, the leader was appointed as a lecturer at the Gyeongsangnam-do Local Government Training Institute to present successful cases.
*   Every Thursday, the leader would spend 2 hours sharing success stories about completing the cluster improvement project, widely introducing personal experiences of the Saemaul Undong.
*   In June 1977, the leader was selected as one of the outstanding Saemaul leaders nationwide and visited Japan for two weeks to broaden their understanding of the Saemaul Undong.
*   Invited to the Ulsan Industrial Complex, the leader presented successful cases and was also invited to present at reserve forces training and civil defense education, dedicating all efforts to instilling the basic direction and spirit of the Saemaul Undong into the nation.

### 3) Overcoming Difficulties


--- (p. 887) ---

*   As there was no community center (會舘), villagers had to squat in layers in the thatched cottage (草堂房) for every meeting. Thus, constructing a spacious and bright community center became the villagers' strong desire. During this time, former Prime Minister (國務總理) Kim Jong-pil (金鍾泌) donated 700 bags of cement (洋灰), which enabled the villagers to build a community center. However,
*   The 300-pyeong (坪) site for the community center was 1 meter lower than the surrounding area. Men filled the area with soil, while the women's association carried children on their backs, oblivious to the cold, as they sorted and transported gravel and sand. Through two months of arduous work,
*   The community center was completed on February 22, 1976. However, as the building had two floors with 25 pyeong on the second floor designated as the community center and the first floor as a warehouse, the excessive construction left them with a debt of 1,350,000 won.
*   The contractor demanded payment daily, and as the village had no funds, the leader (指導者) and the village head (里長) used their property as collateral to borrow 1,350,000 won from the agricultural cooperative (農協) to pay the construction costs. However, the interest accumulated daily, and
*   The villagers' parents despaired, saying they were ruined, and repaying the debt seemed impossible.
*   In November 1976, a general village meeting was held to discuss the debt. As a result, the villagers agreed to work mandatory 15 days per household at the nearby Young Shin Textile new factory site during the winter to resolve the community center debt.
*   In order to improve the village structure and construct 24 new houses, demolition of the 24 houses began on May 14, 1965. However,
*   Suddenly, with their houses demolished, the villagers had nowhere to live. In the heat of June, they had to sleep on straw mats in the barn. Moreover, as it was the busy farming season for transplanting rice seedlings, the villagers' complaints and frustrations grew as they had to both transplant rice and build houses.
*   On June 21, 1976, as a drizzle fell, a truck carrying cement arrived in front of the community center.
*   An announcement was made to unload the cement, but no one from the fields transplanting rice seedlings came to help. The cement got wet in the rain, and as the rain continued, the leader, driven by a sense of duty, had to endure the humiliation of single-handedly unloading 300 bags of cement into the warehouse.
*   The next day, June 22, continuous heavy rain and strong winds turned the entire village into chaos.
*   The tarpaulins covering the houses flew away, water accumulated on the ceilings, walls collapsed, and rainwater filled the rooms. The villagers lost their rationality and blamed the leader for persuading them to build these unwanted houses. They grabbed the leader by the collar and beat him.
*   Feeling a sense of responsibility, the leader ran from house to house in the rain without even wearing a raincoat, covering the houses with tarpaulins and setting up supports. Despite the difficulties, he vowed with tears in his eyes to complete the houses.
*   Through such unwavering belief, the 24 houses were completed two months after the start of construction on July 20. However,
*   The challenge of building the annexes (附屬舍) emerged as a more difficult issue, and with the new houses constructed, the annexes remained.


--- (p. 888) ---

The traditional (在來式) barn house looked very unsightly as it was.
- Building (新築) a new main building (建物) with a loan (融資) of 600,000 won (萬圓) and additional debts (負債) of 200,000 to 300,000 won (萬圓) made it financially (財政上) impossible to construct an annex (附屬建物) by purchasing new materials (資材).
- After discussion, it was decided to use the old wooden materials (木材) from the demolished structure to build an annex (附屬舍). However, it was found impossible (不可能) for small-scale farmers (零細農家) to build an annex (附屬舍).
- After consulting with the village head (里長), a visit was made to the Hyundai (現代) Automobile (自動車) Company in Ulsan (蔚山) to discuss obtaining discarded wooden boxes (廢木箱子) used for importing automobile parts (附屬品) as a donation (喜捨) for the New Community Movement.
- In July 1976, a visit was made to the company (會社), and the factory manager (工場長) was appealed to for the village's difficult situation, successfully obtaining a truckload of discarded wood (廢木).
- By appropriately processing (製材) the wood (木材), it was distributed evenly to struggling farmers (農家), enabling the completion of the annex (附屬舍) with minimal difficulties (難關).

### 5) Good Deeds and Heartwarming Stories (美談가화(佳話))

a) Story 1 (第 1話)
*   Mrs. Kang Sun-bun (姜順粉), the women's association president of Sinan (新安) Village, led a rice-saving campaign through the village women's association and saved 1 cheongbo (合式) of rice daily in a rice-saving box.
*   The 22 members of the association worked together for 5 days to earn 60,000 won from weeding work, adding their own money to make it 80,000 won.
*   The women's association then provided 50 chairs for the community center.
*   News of this cooperative spirit reached Lee Jae-hyuk, the manager of Youngshin Textile Factory nearby, who donated a podium for meetings.

b) Story 2 (第 2話)
*   By being the first in the province to improve the village layout, Sinan Village attracted approximately 7,000 visitors from all over the country by November 1977.
*   It was quite challenging to explain the village's situation to the numerous visitors who came several times a day, and the leaders had little time for household chores, which took a significant economic toll on their private lives. However, their sense of mission helped them endure.
*   In the summer of 1976, basic village leaders who were receiving education at the Gyeongnam Civil Servant Training Institute visited Sinan Village for a field trip.
*   At that time, one leader, upon seeing the developed appearance of Sinan Village, came up to the village leader and asked if this was indeed the village where repatriates had lived.
*   The person was a repatriate who had lived in the village 30 years ago and regretted leaving due to hardship. Overwhelmed with emotion and nostalgia, the repatriate could hardly believe the dramatic transformation of their old village. With tears of gratitude, they firmly grasped the village leader's hand.

### 7) Special Notes

#### a) Memorable Events
* On August 16, 1975, Prime Minister Kim Jong-pil (金鍾泌) personally visited Sinan Village, toured the village, and passionately encouraged the residents, calling it a model village where overseas Koreans had created something from nothing. This speech remains etched in the hearts of the residents forever.
* On December 8, 1976, during the National Saemaul Leaders Conference, the leaders received the Saemaul Cooperation Medal directly from the President (大統領).
* In June 1977, when the Interior Ministry sent Saemaul leaders to observe Japan, it was the Sinan leaders who conducted the inspection.

#### b) Sad Events
* On June 21, 1976, during the village infrastructure project and the improvement of 24 houses, heavy rains continued while the existing houses were being demolished and standard housing construction was underway.
* Since the project started in April, furniture was stacked in the barn, and residents had to sleep on sacks in the barn. The heavy rain and strong winds caused thatch to fly away, walls to collapse, and water to accumulate in the rooms. Residents blamed the leaders for their struggles in building houses and taking on debt during the rainy season.
* The residents' frustration and resentment exploded, leading to confrontations with the leaders, even resulting in elderly residents slapping the leaders. This was the saddest moment in the leaders' lives.

## Ba. Achievements (成果) from the Saemaul Undong (新村運動)

### 1) Spiritual Aspect (精神面)
O Through the Saemaul Undong (新村運動), we have acquired the philosophy (哲學) of diligent (勤勉) and self-reliant (自立) living,
O Gained confidence (自信感) in our abilities,
O And learned to prioritize the community (我們) over the individual (나) through cooperation (協同) and unity (團合).

### 2) Living Aspect (生活面)
O With the expansion (擴大) of agricultural (農家) side businesses (副業) and increased income (所得),
O We have come to understand and practice (實踐) the idea that helping (도우고) and wishing for the well-being (잘 사는) of our neighbors (이웃) is key to our own prosperity (내가 잘 사는).

### 3) Production Aspect (生産面)
O The expansion (擴大) of rice (벼) cultivation (栽培) in unified (統一) varieties (계(系)) has doubled (倍加) our income (所得),
O And the establishment (造成) of livestock (畜産) and orchard (果樹) complexes (단지(團地)) has brought about a dramatic (劃期的) improvement (向上) in income (所得).
