### Meeting Minutes (會議錄)

**Date:** November 19, 1976
**Location:** Ri Office (里事務所)
**Agenda:** Recognition and Use of Funds for President (大統領) Grant and Promotional Village Support Project in 1976
**Attendees:** Kim Dae-yeon and 10 others

**Ri-jang (Village Leader) Oh Seong-su (吳晟秀):** Thank you for attending the meeting despite your busy schedules. Today's meeting is convened to select projects for the President's (大統領) special support project worth 1.5 million won and the promotional model village support project worth 2 million won. Please listen to everyone's good opinions, discuss, and make a decision.

**Saemaul Leader (Kim Seok-jung (金碩重)):** This President's (大統領) special support project and promotional model village support project should be the most necessary projects for our village. Please select them.

**Kim Du-man (金斗萬):** It would be best to establish a communal warehouse, which our village currently needs, with the President's (大統領) special support project.

**Kim Su-gwon (金壽權):** It would be better to establish a senior citizen center where the elderly can enjoy themselves.

**Saemaul Leader (Kim Seok-jung (金碩重)):** Are there any other good opinions? If not, we will proceed with establishing a communal warehouse and a senior citizen center.

**All Attendees:** We agree.


--- (p. 940) ---

Kim Bong-hyun (金奉鉉): For the project selection, it would be best to construct a communal warehouse (共同倉庫) and a senior citizens' center (敬老堂), and then convene a temporary village assembly (臨時總會) to make the final decision.

Saemaul Leader (金碩重): In that case, we will hold a temporary assembly soon to make the final decision on the project. With that, we will conclude the Development Committee (開發委員會) meeting.

**Attendees (開發委員)**
Kim Dae-yeon (金大淵) and 10 others

♦ Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (4)

| Date      | November 23, 1976                                                                                               |
| :-------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Venue      | Village Office (事務所)                                                                                        |
| Agenda      | Confirmation of the Plan for the Selection of Projects Supported by the President (大統領) Special Support Fund and Foreign Promotion Village Support Project |
| Attendees | 63 people                                                                                                    |

Village Head (吳晟秀): Thank you for attending this meeting despite your busy schedules during the tangerine (柑橘) harvest season. We have received 1.5 million won for the President (大統領) Special Support Project and 2 million won for the Foreign Promotion Demonstration Village Support Project. We held a Development Committee (開發委員會) meeting on November 19 to discuss the project selection, and now we would like to make a decision based on the collective opinion of everyone here. Please engage in a serious discussion to determine the best project.

Saemaul Leader (金碩重): As you all know, we have received 1.5 million won for the President (大統領) Special Support Project and 2 million won for the Foreign Promotion Demonstration Village Support Project. First, let's select the projects that our village needs based on the times, through the collective opinion of everyone here.

Oh Mun-suk: What projects were decided upon at the Development Committee (開發委員會) meeting?

Saemaul Leader (金碩重): At the Development Committee (開發委員會) meeting, it was resolved to construct a communal warehouse (共同倉庫) (30 坪) with the President (大統領) Special Support Fund, as our village lacks one and our current one is leased to a local agricultural cooperative, making it inconvenient to use freely. Additionally, it was resolved to construct a senior citizens' center (敬老堂) (20 坪) with the Foreign Promotion Demonstration Village Support Fund, as there is no recreational facility for the elderly to enjoy.

Kim Dae-eon (金大彥): It seems best to proceed with the projects as decided by the Development Committee (開發委員), constructing a communal warehouse (共同倉庫) and a senior citizens' center (敬老堂).

All Attendees: Agreed.

Saemaul Leader (金碩重): As Kim Dae-eon (金大彥) suggested, we will proceed with constructing a communal warehouse (共同倉庫) of 30 坪 with the President (大統領) Special Support Project and a senior citizens' center (敬老堂) of 20 坪 with the Foreign Promotion Demonstration Village Support Project, with unanimous approval. Now, where would be the best location for these constructions? Currently, the palanquin house is expected to be in contact with the urban plan, so considering management and usage, how about constructing the communal warehouse (共同倉庫) on the first floor and the senior citizens' center (敬老堂) on the second floor across from the village office (事務所)?


--- (p. 941) ---

All attendees: We agree.

Saemaul Leader (Kim Seok-jung): Then, with everyone's agreement, it is decided to construct the village office on the opposite side of the village office.

The construction of the community warehouse and the senior citizens' center requires more funding than the support funds can provide, so residents will need to bear some of the cost. How should we calculate the required funds for this project?

Kim Chang-man: If we collect the full amount for this year's road paving project, we could use the remaining funds from this year's road paving project to cover the cost.

Saemaul Leader (Kim Seok-jung): If the outstanding amount for the road paving project is not paid, it will hinder the funding for this project. Those who have not paid should pay the full amount as soon as possible. Does everyone agree to use the outstanding amount from the road paving project to cover the funding shortfall for the community warehouse and senior citizens' center?

Saemaul Leader (Kim Seok-jung): Then, we will use the outstanding amount from the road paving project to cover the funding shortfall for the construction of the community warehouse and senior citizens' center. With that, we will conclude the meeting. Finally, I would like to ask for your cooperation in promoting this project. Thank you.

### 4. Future Development Plans (發展構想)

*   Improve the citrus (柑橘) variety to double income and establish and operate a self-processing plant for citrus processing. Improve the village-owned communal ranch (共同牧場) (270ha) to enhance livestock (畜產) income.
*   Expand the beekeeping (養蜂) business, which was supported by Your Excellency's special support fund, into a major income-generating business. The increased income will be spread through the production teams (作目班). The women's association (婦女會) will further expand its purchasing and sales (購販) business to supply daily necessities (生必品) at low prices.
*   Through these efforts, we will achieve the goal of becoming the highest-income village in the nation and a welfare collective village (集團마을) where human relations flourish. We will surely accomplish this and proudly leave it as a legacy for future generations.


--- (p. 943) ---

# Jeju (濟州) Najeju-gun (南濟州郡) Andeok-myeon (安德面) Sagye-ri (沙溪里)

## 1. Overview of the Village

### a. History

* During the Joseon (李朝) Dynasty, this area belonged to Jung-myeon (中面) of Daejeong-hyeon (大靜縣). However, 138 years ago in 1839 (경자년 (庚子年)), it was named Jinnam-ro (今勿路), and
* In 1914, as part of an administrative district reorganization, it was named Sagye-ri (沙溪里) in Andeok-myeon (安德面). This village was first settled by Kim Jin-si (金珍氏), an ancestor of the Gimhae Kim (金海 金氏) clan, 340 years ago. At that time, Sagye-ri (沙溪里) was a forested area with dense trees. After these settlers established themselves, they cleared the land to create farmland and began living there, thus forming the village.
* The tourist attraction Sanbanggulsa (山房窟寺) and Daejeong Hyanggyo (大靜鄕校) are located here. Sanbanggulsa (山房窟寺) was established over 1,000 years ago during the Goryeo (高麗) Dynasty by the monk Hyeil (慧日法師), who enshrined a Buddha statue. The dripping water from the ceiling of the cave, which is over 100 pyeong (坪) in size, is said to be the sad tears of love from "Sanbangdeok" (山房德), the guardian spirit of Sanbang Mountain (山房山).
* Daejeong Hyanggyo (大靜鄕校) was founded 326 years ago in the year of Gyeosa (癸巳年) by Lee Moksa (李牧使). It has been spreading Confucian ideology throughout the entire village ever since.

### b. Location and Conditions

**＜Location＞**

* Located 28 km west of Seogwipo (西歸浦), the site of the Najeju County Office (南濟州郡廳), along the One-week Road (一週道路). It is also 4 km west of Hwasun-ri (和順里), the site of the Andeok-myeon (安德面) office, following the access road to Sanbanggulsa (山房窟寺). The village is situated between Sanbang Mountain (山房山), which is 395 meters tall to the northeast, and Daejeong Hyanggyo (大靜鄕校), which was built 326 years ago to the northwest. To the south, there is a coastal area featuring the famous fishing spot Hyeongjedo (兄弟島) and a 4 km coastline, making it a plains village.

**＜Conditions＞**

As a coastal village, it is situated between Sanbang Mountain (山房山) and the South Sea (南海), with a wide plain in between. The village has favorable conditions for agriculture and is rich in marine resources.

## 2. Village Development Process (發展過程)

### A. Situation Before 1970 (70年 以前의 상황)

#### 1) Basic Environment (基礎環境)

*   The three natural hamlets (自然部落) of Yonghae (龍海), Songjuk (松竹), and Daejeon (大田) were connected by three winding and narrow village access roads (마을進入路), which were the only means of passage (通行) and transportation (交通手段);
*   There were no farm roads (農路), so agricultural products (農產物) had to be transported using ox carts (소 길마), reflecting a primitive (原時的) farming method (營農手段);
*   Thatched-roof houses (초가집) passed down for several generations (代) were barely more than shacks (오두막집), with overgrown weeds (雜草), rotten and crooked wooden pillars (나무기둥), and a structure that seemed ready to collapse (내려앉을 것 같은 상태) with any heavy rain (폭우);
*   Behind the village, there was an abandoned military road (軍事道路) opened during the Japanese colonial period (日帝當時), which resembled ruins (廢墟).

#### 2) Income Level (所得水準)

*   Relying on ancestral farmland (農土) of about 700 jeongbo (情報) for generations (祖上代代), the villagers depended on wheat (麥類),杂粮 (雜穀), and sweet potatoes (고구마) for food crops (食糧作物) to sustain their livelihoods (衣),


--- (p. 945) ---

Living conditions were barely sufficient for subsistence, with agriculture as the primary means of livelihood.
*   The average cultivated land per household was only 1.3 hectares, and farm income was 301,000 won.
*   Livestock farming and seaweed harvesting were common side jobs, and the village was relatively better off compared to others in the area.

### 3) Spiritual Aspect

*   Despite living in extreme poverty, the idea of improving one's life was never considered.
*   The natural hamlet was divided into three neighborhoods: Daejeon (大田), Songjuk (松竹), and Yonghae (龍海), and the residents were constantly fighting, envying, and insulting each other in a state of ignorance.

### 4) Cultural Life

*   There wasn't a single television, only a few radios, and about ten newspapers, allowing residents to hear the news.
*   In 1969, electricity was installed, providing a foundation for cultural life, but
*   Winters were spent in thatched houses with earthen walls, heating rooms with straw bundles instead of coal, living a primitive life without bathhouses, unable to take a proper bath all winter.
*   Summers were spent sewing under the scorching sun and harvesting seaweed to sell at the five-day market to buy rice for meals.
*   Garbage and waste were scattered everywhere, flies and mosquitoes swarmed like a market dump, and pigs ate human waste in traditional outhouses, reflecting the ignorant and pitiful living conditions.

## B. Implementation of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

### 1) Motivation and Experimental Project Results

*   The "Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)" initiated by President Park Chung-hee began to spread like wildfire across the country from April 23, 1970, and the news reached Saegye-ri (沙溪里), the southernmost village.
*   However, in 1970, the local residents only wondered what their neighboring villages were doing.


--- (p. 946) ---

, passing just one year
O In 1971, with the cement (洋灰) provided by the government (政府) as a trial project (試驗事業), we were able to complete 6 communal wells (共同우물), 4 communal laundries (共同빨래터), 1 water supply facility (수발세월), and 2 waiting rooms (待合室).
O However, as it was our first cooperative work (協同作業), there was no order in the work, and due to a lack of technical skills (技術不足), the construction (工事) was not perfect.
O But the villagers planted a firm belief (信念) in their hearts that "We can do it if we try."
O Thus, in 1972, with government (政府) support and self-reliant projects (自力事業), we were able to easily complete the expansion of the village road by 200m, the improvement of the fence by 500m, the construction of 1 dock (船着場), the paving of the inner road by 90m, the opening of 1,000m of farm roads (農路), the improvement of 445m of small streams (小河川), and the installation of 520m of sewers (下水溝).

## 2) Leader's (指導者) Activities (活動)
O Born in Sagae-ri (沙溪里) of this area, graduating from Daejeong (大靜) High School (高等學校), and living by farming (農事) the ancestral land (農土) passed down through generations (代代), tending to it as one would to ancestors (祖上),
O In 1973, on September 5th, with a firm resolve (信念) to develop this hometown (故鄕) where my ancestors' bones lie and where my own bones will one day rest, I took on the role of a leader (指導者).
O However, I was at a loss as to what to do or how to turn the Saemaul Undong (運動) into a nationwide movement (汎國民的運動) to create a prosperous hometown (故鄕). Everything seemed dark and daunting.
O Leader Lee (李指導者) declared 1974 as the "Year of Total Effort for Saemaul Projects (事業)" and
O No matter what, I vowed several times to raise the self-help village (自助村) to a self-sufficient village (自立村) and make it a truly prosperous village (村).

## 3) Overcoming Difficulties (隘路克服)
O After being appointed as a Saemaul leader (指導者), Leader Lee (李指導者) decided, after much deliberation, to promote sweet potato (고구마) farming (栽培) on a large scale (大大的) as the most suitable and profitable (最適合且最有利) agricultural practice (農事) for this area to increase the income (所得) of the villagers (住民).
O However, the most crucial (最重要) aspect of promoting sweet potatoes (奬勵) was solving the problem (問題) of seed potato (種感) storage (貯藏).
O The decay (腐敗) of seed potatoes (種感) during planting (播種) was a major obstacle (難關).
O To find a solution (方案) for safely storing (保管) seed potatoes (種感), he visited Kim (金), the agricultural (農村) guidance officer (指導士) at the Namjeju County (南濟州郡) Rural Guidance Center (指導所) in Ilgwa-ri (日果里), Daejeong-eup (大靜邑).
O Kim explained in detail (詳細) the necessary (必要) special techniques (特殊技術) and basic knowledge (基礎知識) required to build a multipurpose (多目的) seed potato (種感) storage facility (貯藏庫).
O That night, Leader Lee (李指導者) convened a meeting (會) of the entire village (全部落) development committee (開發委員) and team leaders (班長) to discuss (論議) the plan (方案) for building a sweet potato (고구마) storage facility (貯藏庫).
O The entire village (全住民) then petitioned (建議) the local government (行政當局) to support this initiative (事實).
O The government (行政當局), impressed by the village's diligence (勤勞), granted a subsidy (下賜金) of 1,000,000 won (元).
O With this support, in August 1974, following the decision (議決) of the village general assembly (總會), he successfully completed the construction of a 30-pyeong (坪) multipurpose (多目的) sweet potato (고구마) storage facility (貯藏庫).


--- (p. 947) ---

That autumn, a multipurpose storage facility was created by the power and will of the residents, and 30 tons of seed sweet potatoes were stored there.
However, there were concerns about whether the stored seed sweet potatoes could be safely managed so that the residents' hopes would not be dashed.
That winter was unusually cold, with half the days dropping below 5°C.
He decided to become the storage facility caretaker, preparing five stoves and lighting them every night to share the "joys and sorrows of life" with the storage facility. He was a "sweet potato storage facility caretaker" who guided the community through the harsh winter.
Despite the complaints of his family, he managed the storage facility for four months, enduring many difficult days.
In mid-March of the following year, it was time to take out the seed sweet potatoes. His hands trembled and he felt afraid as he removed them.
The 30 tons of seed sweet potatoes that had been stored were fresh and waiting for their owner.
His chest swelled with pride and his heart pounded with joy—a feeling that only those who have experienced it can understand.
In March of that year, a communal seedbed was carefully set up, and the guide's heart was filled with indescribable emotions.
All the residents, having directly experienced the success of the seed sweet potato storage, felt gratitude for the guide's persistent determination.
Proposals were made to build a second and third storage facility, and in the fiscal years of 1976 and 1977, facilities of 20 and 25 square meters (20 and 25 pyeong) respectively were constructed. This resulted in a total of three storage facilities covering 75 square meters (75 pyeong), resolving the seed sweet potato storage issue in Sagye-ri and contributing to increased farm income.

### 4) Developmental Promotion of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

Using the successful momentum of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement),
In March 1974, with 110,000 won of government support and 287,000 won of residents' own funds (more than double the support funds), a 150-meter irrigation channel was constructed to contribute to increased food production.
At the time of its construction, the landowners objected unanimously, claiming that their land was being occupied by the irrigation channel.
However, the promotion committee and Mr. Lee, the guide, persuaded all the landowners persistently, eventually gaining their agreement. As a result, the 150-meter irrigation channel project was successfully completed in April of that year.
Additionally, through the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) beautification project, a 30-square meter (30 pyeong) communal warehouse was built through cooperative work by all residents. This allowed agricultural products from farms to be safely stored and managed collectively.
His Excellency the President also supported the village, which was well-managed and united, by providing a special grant of 1,000,000 won.
The 1,000,000 won contributed to the success of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) in this village.
In August 1974, following a resolution at the general assembly of residents, opinions aligned on the need to establish a storage facility for safely storing sweet potatoes for multiple purposes. It was selected as a model project, with construction beginning that August and completing a 30-square meter (30 pyeong) slab storage facility by October 30. This allowed for the safe storage of 30 tons of seed sweet potatoes annually, generating an annual income of 750,000 won.
In 1975, in addition to paving 510 meters of roads, a secondary grant of 500,000 won was received from His Excellency the President for the construction of a water source pond.


--- (p. 948) ---

A facility of 20 pyeong (坪) was constructed in early October and completed by the end of the month, providing living water for 3,014 residents of Saegye-ri (沙溪里) and agricultural water for 28.9ha of farmland, contributing to grain production.

In 1976, the village tourism access road connecting Sangmo-ri (上毛里) in Daejeong-eup (大靜邑) and Hwasun-ri (和順里) in Andeok-myeon (安德面) was paved for 2,500m as a cooperative circle project, with a subsidy of 3,125,000 won (千원). However, this was only 23% of the total construction cost of 14,000,000 won (千원), with residents bearing the burden of 10,875,000 won (千원). Despite this substantial amount, all residents, rooted in the Saemaul spirit (精神), did not hesitate to support with cash or labor, and through their tireless efforts, they created a pristine 4m-wide asphalt road for the 2,500m access road.

Additionally, a 30 pyeong (坪) communal warehouse and a 20 pyeong (坪) communal storage facility were completed.

In 1977, as part of the beautification project, the government provided 300 units of cement and 1 ton of rebar, with residents contributing 2,175,000 won (千원) to build a 25 pyeong (坪) sweet potato storage facility.

A 17 pyeong (坪) daycare center where children could play freely, a 35 pyeong (坪) senior center, and a 50 pyeong (坪) communal warehouse were completed as part of the 1976 4th special support project by the Prime Minister (閣下). Thus, many grand projects were completed in the first half of 1977.

Furthermore, in 1977, Yonghae-dong (龍海洞) in the main village was selected as a village for improving the village structure (聚落構造改善). The 51 households and 239 residents of Yonghae-dong (龍海洞) formed a promotion committee (委員會) to carry out the improvement project, centered around the promotion committee chairperson (委員長). They expanded the main road by 480m, opened 600m of new roads, improved 1,960m of walls, improved 19 houses, built a 25 pyeong (坪) village community center, planted 135 trees, landscaped one area, built 350m of stone fences, relocated three graves, built 800m of sewers, and paved 480m of the main road, among other extensive projects. Through these efforts, the village became one of the best in the county (郡), worthy of pride.

Due to these numerous projects, in the first half of 1977, the village was selected as the best in Jeju Province (濟州道) for the Saemaul beautification project, receiving a commendation from the Minister of Interior (內務部長官) and a prize of 2,000,000 won (萬원). This fund was used for the long-desired project of paving 600m of the main road between Daejeon (大田) and Songjukkan (松竹間). As a reward for these tireless efforts, leader Lee Chang-sik (李昌植) received the Saemaul paving award at the 1977 National Saemaul Leaders Conference (새마을指導者大會), becoming a true pillar of the nation (役軍).

### Good Deeds and Heartwarming Stories

#### Story 1

* In January 1977, when constructing a new senior center in Songjuk-dong (松竹洞), Mr. Lee Gi-Cho (李己礎), aged 80, expressed that the establishment of a senior center, which would serve as a cradle for the lives of the elderly and a place for them to enjoy themselves, was his lifelong wish. He generously donated his lifetime savings of 1,500,000 won (千원) on January 20, 1977, as the construction fund, deeply touching the hearts of the local residents. Additionally, Grandmother Kang Yu-Saeng (姜有生), aged 70, from this village, donated her land of 50 pyeong (坪) in front of her house as the site for the senior center on January 25, 1977, setting a good example for the entire village's Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) efforts.

#### Story 2

* Jo Gwan-Ok (趙官玉), a 36-year-old president of a company residing in Busan and originally from Bonri (本里), visited his hometown in 1975 and heard that the villagers were struggling to raise funds for constructing a 30 pyeong (坪) communal warehouse in Yonghae-dong (龍海洞) as part of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement). He generously donated the construction of a 30 pyeong (坪) warehouse in cooperation with the village, enabling the safe storage of agricultural products.

#### Story 3

* In 1968, when the village was struggling to secure funds for electrical (電氣) installation, Dr. Kang Si-Hong (姜時弘), a medical doctor (醫學博士) and head of the Red Cross Hospital (赤十字病院長) in Dae-Pan (大板) who was also a Korean resident in Japan, donated 3,500,000 won (千원), making it possible to easily install the long-desired electricity.

#### Story 4

* In January 1977, Lee Seok-Ho (李錫鎬), a Korean resident in Japan and a businessman, visited the village and, aware of the inconvenience of walking at night due to the lack of streetlights, donated 1,280,000 won (千원) to install 33 streetlights and 3 streetlight poles, illuminating the dark night paths. Additionally, on June 3, 1977, he attended the comprehensive completion ceremony of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) and donated a reception set worth 25,000 won (千원) to this office.

#### Story 5

* In 1977, the construction of the senior center in Songjuk-dong (松竹洞) as part of the village's Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) was completed early thanks to the donations of 166 people, including the founding committee chairman Lee Young-Jun (李泳駿), and the free technical services of carpenters such as Lee Si-Hun (李始勛) and several others. In particular, the women's association of this village used the savings collected through frugal living to provide lunch for the technical staff.


--- (p. 950) ---

Free services were provided until completion, setting an example for neighboring villages.

### 바) The Sixth Episode (第6話)

*   In 1963, Lee Cheon-hoon (李千勛), the president (社長) residing in Seoul, visited his hometown and noticed the absence of a communal warehouse (共同倉庫). He generously built a sturdy 40-pyeong (坪) warehouse next to the village office (里事務所).
    **Other (其他)**
*   In 1971, a 200-pyeong warehouse site in Yonghaedong (龍海洞) donated by Cho Nam-sang (趙南祥)

*   In 1974, Kang Moon-sam (姜文三) residing in Seogwipo (西歸浦) donated 500,000 won for the construction of a speaker (스피커) and storage facility (저장고)

## 8) Special Items (特記事項)

### 가) Joyful Events

*   The completion of a multipurpose sweet potato (고구마) storage facility, successfully storing 30 tons of sweet potatoes (종감) without any spoilage when opened the following March
*   In 1975, the village was promoted from a self-help (自助) village to a self-reliant (自立) village
*   In the first half of 1977, the village was selected as the best village in the province, receiving a commendation from the Minister of the Interior (內務部長官) and a prize of 2,000,000 won
*   In 1974, 1975, and 1976, the village received special support funds (特別 支援 事業費) from the government
*   In 1976, during the National Saemaul Leaders Conference (全國 新村指導者 大會), the village received a commendation from the Prime Minister (國務總理). In 1977, during the Saemaul Leaders Conference, the village received the Saemaul Badge (新村 포장)

### 나) Difficult Times

*   In 1974, during the construction of farm roads (農路) and road expansion projects (安길 擴張 事業), strong opposition from some landowners (土地主) delayed construction for 2-3 months, causing sleepless nights
*   In 1976, illegal fishing boats (不法 漁船) intruded into the communal fishing ground (共同漁場) and illegally harvested marine products (海産物). However, due to a lack of patrol boats (動力船 不足), the village was unable to drive them away

The anxious situation of not being able to secure a site for the construction of a communal warehouse (共同倉庫) and community center (會舘) in 1977

2) Living Aspect (生活面)
O With environmental improvement (環境改善), welfare facilities, and income-increasing projects (所得增大事業), farm income (農家所得) improved, allowing farmers (農民) to learn and realize the habits of thrift, frugality, and savings, and
O Gained the motivation (意慾) to live well.

3) Production Aspect (生產面)
Through seed storage and the introduction of new varieties (新品種) for cultivation, farm income (農家所得增大) increased, and productivity (生產性) per unit area improved. Mass production and systematic sales doubled residents' income.

3. Residents' General Assembly (住民總會)

♦ Meeting Minutes (會議錄)(1)

Agenda (議題): Selection (選定) of 74 Excellent New Community Special Support Project (特別支援事業) (President (大統領) His Excellency's (閣下) Gift (下賜金) Project (事業))
Date (日時): August 5, 1974, 21:00~23:00 (3 hours (時間))
Location (場所): Village Office (里事務所)
Attendees (參席人員): Kim Seong-nam (金性南) and 392 others (名)
Absentees (不參人員): 281 (名)
Attending Officials (臨席公務員): Mun Sun-bu of Anduk-myeon

Chairperson (司會者): Thank you very much for attending despite the hot weather. We will now begin the meeting to discuss the selection (選定) of the President (大統領) His Excellency's (閣下) gift (下賜金) project (事業) of 1,000 thousand won (千원) for the 74 excellent new communities.


--- (p. 954) ---

I now declare the meeting open.
As the funds we are receiving are support funds (支援資金) from Your Excellency, we must proceed with caution (愼重) and select a project (事業) that is most suitable for our village (部落).
**Lee Won-taek (李元澤)**: Our village (部落) has made some progress in environmental improvement projects (環境改善事業), so we should select a project (事業) that can contribute to increasing income (所得增大). We must contribute to increasing the income (所得增大) of our residents (住民).
First, what about a facility (施設) for safely (安全) and multipurpose storage (貯藏) of sweet potatoes?
**Lee Seong-hoon (李性勛)**: That is a good suggestion (發言). I agree (同意).
(The attendees (參席者) unanimously (滿場一致) express agreement (同意).)
**Master of Ceremonies (司會者)**: Please suggest ways to promote this project (事業) more efficiently (效率的).
**Cho Nam-sang (趙南祥)**: I understand that this construction project (工事) requires construction (施工) and technology (技術), and is a special support project (特別支援事業), so we must proceed with caution (愼重).
First, what if we elect an executive responsible for the project (事業執行責任者) and an executive promotion committee (執行推進委員) who can take responsibility (責任) for promoting the project (事業推進) and have them handle it exclusively (專擔)?
**Ko Chang-mun (高昌文)**: I agree (同意).
(All attendees (全員) agree (同意).)
**Master of Ceremonies (司會者)**: Then, please explain how to promote (推進) it.
**Lee Seong-hoon (李性勛)**: It would be good to make the executive responsible (執行責任者) the village head (里長) and the Saemaul leader (指導者), and the promotion committee (推進委員) the development committee (開發委員).
(All attendees (全員) agree (同意).)
**Master of Ceremonies (司會者)**: To promote this project (事業), 1 million won from Your Excellency's gift (下賜金) will not be enough to complete (完工) it.
Self-raised funds (自體資金) are the most needed, so please explain the method of raising funds (調達方法).
**Lee Soon-shin (李淳信)**: For the remaining funds of 950,000 won, it would be good to cover 150,000 won through resident (住民) effort construction (努力施工) and 800,000 won in cash (現金) through the village fund (部落基金) and resident contribution (住民醵出) method (方法).
(All attendees (全員) agree (同意).)
**Master of Ceremonies (司會者)**: Thank you. No matter what happens, we must start construction (着工) this month and complete (完工) it by October, so that this year's mountain harvest (山 終感) can be stored (貯藏) safely (安全). All villagers (全里民) must unite (一心同體).
Thank you for your hard work in the hot weather for a long time (長時間).
(Declare closure (閉會) of the meeting. The representative of the attendees (參席者代表) signs (署名) and stamps (捺印).)
Kim Seong-nam, Lee Chang-sik, Cho Ik-hyeon, Im Se-hwa, Lee Won-taek, Yu Myung-guk, Gu Don-hyeon, Lee Seong-hoon, Cheon Se-wan, Lee Soon-shin, Lee Buk-sun, Lee Shin-hun, Cho Nam-sang, Ko Chang-mun, Yu Gye-hong, Lee Young-sik, Kim Bong-pil, Kim Yong-sam, Kim Bong-min, Lee Jong-ho


--- (p. 955) ---

### ♦ Minutes (會議錄)⑵

*   **Agenda (議案)**: Settlement (決算) of the 1974 Excellent Saemaul Special Support Project
*   **Date (日時)**: November 1, 1974, 20:00~22:00
*   **Location (場所)**: Village Community Center
*   **Attendees (出席人員)**: Kim Seong-nam (金性南) and 375 others
*   **Absentees**: 298
*   **Chairperson (社會者)**: Village Head Kim Seong-nam (金性南)

**Chairperson (社會者)**: We will now hear the settlement (決算) report regarding the construction of a communal storage facility (共同貯藏庫) funded by the special support funds (特別支援資金) granted by His Excellency (閣下), which was selected by the residents (住民) on August 5th.

**Leader (指導者) Lee Chang-sik (李昌植)**: I will now present the settlement (決算) report.

Out of the total construction cost (總工事費) of 1,950,000 won, 1,000,000 won was supported by His Excellency (閣下), and the remaining 950,000 won was covered by the residents' effort burden (住民努力負擔) of 150,000 won and 800,000 won in cash (現金). With these funds, we completed a 30-pyeong (建坪) multipurpose storage facility (多目的貯藏庫).

**Chairperson (社會者)**: Please raise any objections to the facts (事實) reported by the leader (指導者).

**Cho Nam-sang (趙南祥)**: I have heard the settlement (決算) report, but could you please elaborate (詳細) more on the progress (推進過程)?

**Leader (指導者) Lee Chang-sik (李昌植)**: I apologize. We started construction (着工) at the end of August and completed it on October 25th. Initially (當初), it was difficult (困難) to secure (調達) the necessary cash (現金) from our own funds (自體資金). However, after approaching several prominent individuals (人士), Chairman Kang Moon-sam (姜文三) of Samhyeop Industry (三協産業) (전분공장 (專粉工場)) generously donated (喜捨) 400,000 won, which enabled us to finish the project.

**Ko Chang-ha (高昌河)**: Thank you for your hard work (努力) in promoting (推進) the project (事業). I agree (同意) with the settlement (決算) without any objections (異議).
(All attendees (出席者) express (表明) their agreement (同意).)

**Chairperson (社會者)**: With this, we conclude (閉會) the meeting (會議) on the settlement (決算) report of the 1974 multipurpose communal storage facility (多目的共同貯藏庫) funded by His Excellency's (閣下) special support funds (特別支援資金). Thank you. (The chairperson declares (宣言) the closure (閉會) of the meeting (會議). Representatives (代表) of the attendees (出席者) sign (署名) and stamp (捺印) the document.)

Lee Seong-hoon, Lee Won-taek, Ko Chang-ha, Lee Eul-saeng, Ko Bong-jun, Cho Nam-sang, Lee Ye-beom, Kang Gyeong-jin, Im Se-hwa, Ko Young-nam, Kang Dal-ho, Gu Dong-hyeon, Yu Myeong-guk, Kim Dae-chon, Lee Chang-sik, Kim Seong-nam

### ♦ Minutes (會議錄)⑶

*   **Agenda (議案)**: Selection (選定) of the 1975 Excellent Saemaul Special Support Project (事業) (His Excellency's (閣下) Donation (下賜金) Project (事業))
*   **Date (日時)**: October 1, 1975, 20:00~22:00 (2 hours)
*   **Location (場所)**: Ri (里) Office (事務所)
*   **Attendees (出席人員)**: Lee Chang-sik (李昌植) and 367 others
*   **Chairperson (司會者)**: Lee Won-taek (李元澤)

**Chairperson (司會者)**: Thank you for attending (出席) despite your busy schedules (忙中). I appreciate (感謝) the presence (出席) of many residents (住民). As in 1974, we have been selected (選定) as an excellent village (優秀村) this year as well, and have received support (支援) of 500,000 won from His Excellency's (閣下) donation (下賜金). We must once again express (感謝) our gratitude (感謝) to President (大統領) His Excellency (閣下).


--- (p. 956) ---

Please carefully consider the projects to be selected.

**Kim Seong-eun (金性銀)**: As you all know, our village (部落) is always struggling due to a shortage (不足) of both living water (生活用水) and agricultural water (農業用水). If we establish a water source area (水源地) in Amkaji-gu, I believe our worries about living water (生活用水) and agricultural water (農業用水) will be somewhat alleviated.

**Host (司會者)**: What do you think of Kim Seong-eun's (金性銀) statement?

**Lee Gae-bong (李桂奉)**: I agree.

(All attendees (全員) unanimously (滿場一致) agree.)

**Host (司會者)**: How can we complete the water source area (水源地) facility as soon as possible?

**Gang Man-ho (姜萬鎬)**: I think this project (本事業) won't be as difficult as last year's storage facility. First, I suggest selecting promotion committee members (推進委員) as we did last year and have them take charge (專擔).

**Gu Dong-hyeon (具東玄)**: What if we entrust (委任) the members who promoted last year's project with this year's water source area (水源地) project?

**Lee Eul-saeng (李乙生)**: I agree.

(All attendees (全員) agree.)

**Host (司會者)**: Please discuss the method of raising internal funds (自體資金).

**Lee Seong-hun (李性勛)**: Let's cover the remaining 583,000 won with 390,000 won from the residents' efforts and the rest from the village fund (部落基金).

**Go Chang-mun (高滎男)**: I agree.

(All attendees (全員) agree. The meeting is adjourned (閉會). The attendees sign and stamp (署名捺印) on behalf of the representatives.)

**Date (日時)**: December 15, 1976, 19:00-21:00

**Location (場所)**: Ri Office (里事務所)

**Attendees (參席人員)**: Lee Won-taek (李元澤) and 387 others (名)

### 4. Future Development Plans (發展構想)

* In 1978, we will focus on increasing productivity (生産性) and income (所得) by:
  * Adding a 20-pyeong (坪) communal storage facility (共同 貯藏庫) to store more sweet potatoes (種甘).
  * Introducing an additional 100-plus head (餘 頭) of fattening cattle (肥肉牛) and 50 head (頭) of breeding cattle (育成牛), as well as raising black goats (黑山羊) around Sanbang Mountain (山方山).
  * Establishing an aquaculture farm (水產養殖場) to develop marine resources (水產 資源) and actively promoting the cultivation (栽培) of special crops (特用作物) such as sweet potatoes (고구마), rapeseed (유채), and hops (맥주맥).
  * Purchasing a large quantity (多量) of agricultural machinery (農機械) to mechanize farming (機械化 營農).
  * Planning to beautify (淨化) the Sanbanggulsa Temple (山房窟寺), one of the 10 scenic views (10景) of Jeju, develop Yongmeoru, and preserve the Daejeong Hyanggyo School (大靜鄕校).
  * Actively addressing the development (開發) of the fishing spot (낚시터) at Hyongjeseom Island to attract more tourists (觀光客).
  * Purchasing a patrol boat (監視船) to crack down on illegal fishing boats (不法 漁船) entering our communal fishing grounds (共同 漁場) and increase marine income (水產 收入).
We plan to accelerate the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) even further.

# Jeju (濟州) Namjeju-gun (南濟州郡) Pyoseon-myeon (表善面) Gasiri (加時里)

## 1. Overview of the Village

### a. History

- Approximately 600 years ago (around 1368 AD), the Byeon clan (邊氏) settled in Anjwa-dong (安坐洞) (Anjwa Oreum: distance from the village office is 1.2km) and later, around 550 years ago (around 1400 AD), the Han clan (韓氏) settled in the main village and named it "Gasi Oreum."
- In the 16th year of King Taejong's reign during the Joseon Dynasty (李朝 太宗 16年), it belonged to Jung-myeon (中面) of Jeongui-gun (旌義郡), and at the same time, Gasi Oreum was renamed Gasiri (加時里), and Anjwa Oreum was renamed Anjwa-ri (安坐里).
- In 1964, the administrative district was changed to Dongjung-myeon (東中面) of Jeollado (全羅道) Jeju-do (濟州島), and Gasiri (加時里) was renamed Gasiri 1-gu (加時里 1區), and Anjwa-ri (安坐里) was renamed Gasiri 2-gu (加時里 2區). Each gu (區) had its own gujang (區長), and due to population growth, households spread to areas like Durimul-dongne, Pongnammaru, Yeongmeoriwat, Maegareumdongne, etc., totaling over 350 households.
- Starting August 1, 1946, the administrative district was separated from Jeollado (全羅道) to Jeju-do (濟州道), and the 1st and 2nd gu (區) of the village were merged into Gasiri (加時里) of Pyoseon-myeon (表善面).
- Due to the April 3 Incident (4.3사건) in 1948, this peaceful village became a complete ruin with 350 households destroyed and 1,500 villagers scattered, leaving no houses in the village.
- In May 1949, after the April 3 Incident was suppressed, the villagers returned from their refuge and rebuilt the village.
- As the population and number of households increased, the village naturally divided into six dong (洞): Dusu-dong (頭水洞) (Durimul-dongne), Pongnam-dong (暴南洞) (Pongnammoru Saenggaengigol), Yeokdu-dong (逆頭洞) (Yeongmeoriwat), Saenggi-dong (生起洞) (Restored Housing Cluster), etc.
- In 1971, through the government policy of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), the village transformed completely from a basic village to a self-help village by 1973. Currently, the village consists of 6 natural dong (自然部落) and 8 ban (班).

### b. Location and Conditions

#### Location

- Located 30km east of Seogwipo (西歸浦), the site of the Namjeju-gun (南濟州郡) office, along the Ilju-daero (一周道路), and 8km northwest of Pyoseon (表善), the site of the myeon (面) office, at an altitude of 120m where houses are sporadically visible amidst dense trees.
- Behind the village lies the vast Noksanjang (녹산장), where deer roam freely, and several communal pastures, giving the village a cozy feel.


--- (p. 962) ---

# Conditions

*   The area surrounding the village has, since time immemorial, been composed of abandoned hills and rocky fields forming cultivated land
*   The vast grasslands have been improved through the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) to create a 160ha communal pasture, where improved grasslands have been seeded with cattle for breeding
*   With the village at its center, the Ga-si-cheon (加時川) and Song-cheon (松川) rivers flow on either side. During heavy rainfall, these rivers can flow violently, occasionally causing loss of farmland

# 2. Community Development Process

## a. Situation Before 1970

### 1) Basic Environment

O The village access road, 8 km from the new road (national road), and the village paths were stony, causing significant inconvenience for pedestrian and horse-drawn carriage traffic. Moreover, student commuting and resident movement requiring bus traffic was almost unthinkable, and while many farmlands were owned and agricultural production increased, transportation was severely restricted.
O Due to the desolation caused by the April 3rd Incident, residents' living conditions were dire. Residents carried goods on their backs or used horse-drawn carts to travel from the mountains to the county market 5 days away to barter for daily necessities.
O Without proper rooms or verandas, residents slept on straw mats on earthen walls. When the wind blew, they would light a bonfire to ward off the cold.
O The thatched roofs, hastily put together, were overgrown with weeds, and during heavy rains, diverting water flows was a priority.
O In our region, carrying goods on one's back was common, and there were only a few farm roads suitable for horse-drawn carts.
O Even obtaining kerosene for oil lamps required traveling 20 ri, making for a grueling lifestyle.

### 2) Income Level

O On average, each household owned about 1 hectare of farmland, primarily cultivating grains and sweet potatoes, but this did not generate significant income. Residents struggled to get through the spring famine season.
O The average annual income per resident was 356,000 won.
O Traditional livestock farming and agriculture were insufficient to overcome poverty, making this village one of the poorest in the county.


--- (p. 964) ---

3) Mental State (精神狀態)
a) Consciousness Structure (意識構造)
- After the brutal 4.3 Incident (事件) caused by the communist bandits in 1948, the 480 households of the 98 local residents (現住民) who returned to the ruins of Gasri found it impossible to achieve stability due to extreme poverty.
- Day by day, men turned to alcohol and gambling, while women succumbed to superstition and mistrust, leading to discord and laziness in families and the village.
- There was no will among the residents to forge a new life or improve their situation.
- Occasionally, a clever young person would attempt to live wisely, but such individuals were often ostracized for their actions.

b) Cultural Life (文化生活)
- The residents here lived without electricity, relying on oil lamps.
- Struggling to make ends meet, they had no recreational facilities, and only a few households owned radios or subscribed to newspapers.
- Babies were raised in bamboo cradles, and water was drawn from natural springs. Transportation was done using shoulder poles, leading to unsanitary living conditions.
- In summer, people wore clothes dyed with citrus fruits.
- The diet consisted mainly of plain rice or barley, with little to no side dishes, reflecting a very meager lifestyle.

## B. The Launch of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

1) Motivation and Experimental Project Results
- On April 22, 1970, the Saemaul Undong (運動) initiated by President (大統領) Park Chung-hee resonated across the nation.
- Kim Han-seok (金漢錫), the current Saemaul leader, began encouraging villagers to gather grass from around the village to produce fertilizer starting from the end of 1970. This effort led to Gasri being awarded as an outstanding village in the first Jeju Provincial (濟州道) Excellent Village Competition (競進大會) on February 19, 1971.
- The villagers used the prize money to build a communal market (1동 15평) operated by the village women's association. However, initially, the women faced complaints from their husbands and jealousy from other residents, causing some to


--- (p. 965) ---

After one month, the door was closed.
- Although 335 bags of cement (支援) donated to this village arrived a few days ago, no one paid any attention to them, and there was no interest in where to use them.
- However, leader Kim Han-seok (金漢錫) organized a leaders' conference (指導者協議會) by summoning each Dongjang (洞長) and concluded the first Saemaul project (事業) by deciding on the use of the cement.
- Residents' cooperation (協同) and participation in joint projects (共同事業) were extremely limited, especially with almost no youth participation.
- The village head (里長) had anticipated these issues from the beginning, so he started persuading and requesting cooperation from the youth first. By the end of that year, he eventually organized the Ga-si-ri New Village Youth Association (加時里維新靑年會) (35 members) and a women's association (婦女會), promoting agricultural improvement (農事改良), lifestyle improvement (生活改善), and simplification of family rituals (家庭儀禮).

## 2) Leader's (指導者) Activity (活動) Situation (狀況)

- Kim Han-seok (金漢錫), a leader who was managing a small business in a foreign land and returned to his hometown due to a herniated disc, was reporting village affairs as the Myeonjang (面長) while recuperating.
- Seeing the desperately poor village with conflicts between clans (部落間) and residents wasting time on alcohol and gambling,
- He wondered how to improve the village's living conditions and promote harmony between clans, but he was at a loss as to what to do.
- However, he firmly resolved to cultivate his hometown, where his ancestors' bones were buried and where he would one day be buried himself, and volunteered to be a Saemaul leader (指導者).

## 3) Overcoming Difficulties (隘路克服) Situation (狀況)

- After volunteering as a Saemaul leader (指導者), he thought that to stimulate residents' cooperative spirit (協同心) and participation awareness (參與意識), cooperative projects (協同事業) should be promoted first.
- A plan for the residents' long-standing project (宿願事業) of electric power installation (電氣架設) was established, and a general assembly of residents (住民總會) was held. However, due to the excessive resident burden (住民負擔), installation was not feasible. Undeterred, the leader petitioned the governor (知事) for a loan (融資) and subsidy (補助), which was approved. A promotion committee (推進委員會) was formed, and after persuading the residents, it was decided that residents would bear a burden of 14,730,000 won (千원). The project was completed three months after the start of construction.
- Taking advantage of this opportunity, the leader proposed asphalt paving (鋪裝) of the access road (進入路) (8.3 km) to the general assembly of residents, but the issue of securing 480,000,000 won for the construction cost was a challenge. With over 340 households, it was doubtful whether they could accomplish this. Moreover, comparing the entire province (道全體), no village had undertaken access road paving (進入路鋪裝) as a self-funded project (自體事業).
- However, the leader, who had experience in civil engineering (土木工事), appealed to the residents that if they decided unanimously and cooperated, it would be manageable.
- Nevertheless, the residents were skeptical, saying it was impossible and that their private lives would be threatened. Facing the residents' resignation, the leader went to Seoul and appealed for financial support to An Jae-woo, the chairman of the resident Koreans in Japan.


--- (p. 966) ---

The residents' response was good, and if the company president could just provide 10 million won, it would be possible.

If we can solve this remaining problem, we have obtained a promise of help. The leaders proposed to the heads of the neighboring village of Sehwa-ri that they should push forward with this cooperative circle business, and after persuading them, the villagers held their own village meeting and discussed this issue.

The leader thought that if they created a problem, a solution would emerge, so they consulted with the village promotion committee members and had the residents bear 50% of the cost of the access road by piling up base course materials along the roadside. However, this made bus travel difficult, leading to the suspension of bus routes. As a result, the residents' complaints and criticism toward the promotion committee members and the leader increased, prompting a village meeting to address the issue.

The promotion committee members pleaded that this effort was part of developing and improving our village, and that this was an opportunity for residents to understand how important roads are. They asked for cooperation, saying that they would proceed with the project if the residents would help.

Thus, the residents decided at a general meeting that if they could raise 12 million won, with each household contributing 2 million won in two installments, they could cover the residents' share. They collected donations day and night, raising 40% of the funds, and entered into full negotiations with the neighboring village.

When the neighboring village said they would proceed with the project independently if there was no response, the neighboring village also held discussions for several days, formed their own promotion committee, and established a cooperative asphalt paving promotion committee.

However, the issue of the financial burden led to daily changes and objections the next day, despite initial agreements. The joint promotion committee had 1-6 members attending from the neighboring village of Sehwa-ri, but only the leader from Gasiri attended, leading to repeated deadlocks and time-wasting despite concessions.

Eventually, it was agreed that Gasiri would bear an additional 6 million won and pave an additional 300 meters within the village, allowing the paving work to commence.

However, due to physical disabilities, the leader was unable to be active and had to undergo spinal surgery at Gwangju National University Hospital. At that time, the leader was too weak to be active and was bedridden while recuperating. The leader was falsely accused of wrongdoing and received a named complaint from the village chief, claiming that the leader's wrongdoing was the reason the construction had not started.

Although it was too painful and infuriating to bear, the leader endured it. Moreover, the leader was subjected to a police investigation regarding all account books and passbooks.

Although there was no suspicion of wrongdoing, the shock and anger were too great. However, the leader vowed to complete this project even if it cost their life. Using crutches, the leader commenced the construction and completed it in four months (January 10, 1975 - May 20, 1975).

With the completion of the access road paving from Pyoseon to Gasiri, the bus travel time to the town center, which previously took 40 minutes, was reduced to 10 minutes. This improvement brought convenience in transportation, saved time and labor, and opened up new markets, among other effects. The residents felt the fulfillment of the Saemaul Undong and created a new opportunity for cooperation.

Gasiri, located in a mid-mountainous area, discussed a project to reduce the travel time to Jeju City from 2 hours to 1 hour.

Jeju Province has the May 16 Road, a west-to-east crossing road, but lacks an industrial road in the east. Therefore, this industrial road project...


--- (p. 967) ---

Connecting the 9.5 km road would extend it to 18 km, making it suitable as an industrial road. Along this road, 4,000 ha of forested land could be developed, enabling not only livestock development but also agricultural expansion and the formation of a quasi-urban center that would serve as a focal point for transportation in eastern Jeju. Based on this strategic location, the idea of paving the 9.5 km industrial road was conceived. However, due to the substantial financial burden, a council of six natural village leaders deliberated for a month but found no solution.

Even if the residents' response was poor and their cooperation was minimal, it was decided to proceed. After several discussions with a wealthy Korean resident in Japan, a pledge of 3 million won was secured. Following consultations with the county magistrate, it was agreed that if 10 million won could be secured—including the 1 million won prize for outstanding villages and 2 million won prize for outstanding counties from the first half of 1975—assistance would be provided. At a general meeting of the residents, the progress and plans were seriously discussed, and it was stated that securing an additional 50 million won would make the project possible. However, the residents were taken aback and did not respond positively. It was explained that if 27 million won in cash could be secured, the residents could each contribute 70,000 won per household, with the remaining 23 million won to be covered by labor. However, it was impossible to pass the resolution, so the promotion committee began visiting each household to seek cooperation and persuasion, emphasizing that even if 70,000 won was not available, the current lifestyle would not change, and decided to proceed with the venture.

No matter how impossible it seemed, the Saemaul Undong project is about "creating something from nothing." If there is money, it is called a construction project, but since this project starts with no money, it is a Saemaul Undong project. The power to turn the impossible into the possible is an element of the Saemaul Movement, a common truth. The promotion committee recognized that their mission was to turn this venture into a possible project through the residents' persuasion.

Therefore, all members of the promotion committee decided to cooperate with a sense of shared destiny. The leader also decided to stake his life on this project, thinking that even if the project failed, it would not be solely his debt, despite his physical limitations.

Initially, the design through the county resulted in a cost of 100 million 762,000 won. It was a very challenging project. The belief that "it can be done" is what this is about. The term "impossible" exists because "possible" exists. Such a plan was made by a leader who was obsessed with the whole rather than personal matters.

To start the road construction, negotiations were held with Jeongdong Ranch to rent equipment at a lower price, and it was felt that road construction was possible. First, two promotion committee members were scheduled to work with the road construction team on a rotating basis each day. On November 3, 1975, despite the bitterly cold winter, the first impossible shovel was dug.

Even if the residents did not help or respond, the determination was to proceed, come what may. With the help of a friend, 5 million won in cash was borrowed, and a trip to Busan was made to purchase asphalt.

At that time, the purchase was impossible due to the oil price hike. Attempts were made to have gangsters purchase black-market goods, and stays of 5-6 days in Busan were made, but all in vain. Sometimes, it was said that there were goods available, but


--- (p. 968) ---

I was introduced to a man named Yoon Hoejang of the Ulsan Hotel by some thugs who claimed that I could purchase asphalt at a low price, but I almost fell victim to a scam when his associates claimed to be relatives of my nephew from Mogogwan. However, since it was impossible to purchase, I was able to secure a contract through Jeju Oil for 1,500 tons. Although I had to rely on friends to pay the remaining balance for the asphalt, I later faced bankruptcy. I then consulted Mr. An Jae-u, a Korean resident in Japan and the president of a company, who generously donated 20 million won, allowing me to settle the asphalt payment.

Without his help, this business might have been impossible. After the asphalt was delivered and transported, the residents, centered around their leaders and the promotion committee, even attempted to kill them, causing great despair. With 20 trucks in operation, the residents dug mountains with "doja" and loaded them with "paeroida," pushing forward despite the cold. Just as the road subgrade was nearly complete, KAL Ranch, which had initially promised to route through the area, began to avoid the route and unilaterally started road construction using heavy machinery at night, which was very disappointing and left us with no one to appeal to. During this time, Kim Jun, the director of Yeonsuwon, Jang Dong-hwan, and Park Jin-hwan, special advisors to Cheong Wa Dae, visited the site and resolved the road issue between Jedong Ranch. They praised and encouraged the residents who were working hard on the 9.5km site.

The joy and relief of that time must be a unique satisfaction that only leaders who have experienced hardships through the Saemaul Undong can feel.

In the end, the residents collected 23 million won in cash and successfully completed the project. For 90 days, despite rain, snow, or wind, they silently collected and transported ballast over 14-15km, leading to the historic completion ceremony on October 20, 1976.

After the project was completed, the residents purchased a 1,200-pyeong plot of land, formerly a national school, for 9.6 million won through their own efforts. They built a welfare center, a small park, a gymnasium, a library, and a daycare center, and additionally paved six natural hamlet connections with asphalt. The residents felt even more accomplished and became more ambitious, leading to various successful outcomes of the Saemaul Undong. Visitors for on-site learning never cease to come.

On January 2, 1977, His Excellency the President visited Gasiri and toured the Saemaul Undong site, offering encouragement and praise. He donated 10 million won, with which the residents purchased one truck and one tractor, improving 160ha of the 2,000ha pasture. They are now hastening the introduction of 2,000 head of beef cattle in the 1980s.

### 3) Developmental Promotion of Saemaul Undong
Taking the successful completion of village road paving as an opportunity,
In 1974, they continued paving 400m of the main road;
In 1975, they completed paving 370m of the main road, expanding 1,200m of the main road, paving 20m of Seweol, constructing a 40-pyeong livestock watering place, and completing one 30-pyeong building for the purchasing and selling market;
The Pyeoseon-Sehwa-Gasiri access road paving, which began construction on January 20, 1974, was completed as a cooperative business of three hamlets, spanning 8.3km.


--- (p. 969) ---

Road paving was carried out with a total construction cost of 48,000 thousand won (support: 4,000 thousand won, overseas Korean donation: 15,000 thousand won, local residents' share: 29,000 thousand won), resulting in the completion of a road paving revolution.
- For this purpose, An Jae-woo (安在祐), president of a company in Japan, donated 10,000 thousand won, and 32 people including Kang Chung-nam donated 5,800 thousand won, which reduced the residents' share.
- In 1976, taking this as an opportunity, a total of 100,762 thousand won (support: 20,000 thousand won, overseas Korean donation: 40,000 thousand won, local residents' share: 40,762 thousand won) was spent to pave the industrial road (9.5km from Gasri to Jedong Farm), achieving a landmark road revolution through thorough improvement.
- With special support funds, a 30-pyeong (坪) communal warehouse was built, a 1,200-pyeong small park was developed, and a children's playground was set up, contributing to the improvement of child welfare.
- In 1977, with special support funds, a 30-pyeong communal warehouse was built, playing a significant role in storing agricultural products. Moreover, with the 10 million won donated by President (大統領) during his visit in early January, one tractor and one truck were purchased, greatly contributing to the procurement of agricultural products, the reclamation of heavy farmland, and the development of grasslands. These have become a significant source of management income.

## Achievements through Saemaul Undong

### 1) Spiritual Aspect

- Through the Saemaul spirit, village residents have first become a cooperative body (the laziness and disorder before the Saemaul Undong are nowhere to be found)
- Secondly, there is the diligent and self-help Saemaul spirit. In particular, the improvement of farming by young people, the management of greenhouses, and the creation of citrus groves for special crops have made them aware of themselves and compete with each other's diligence, achieving an income source equivalent to 3,500,000 won to 2,200,000 won.

### 2) Lifestyle Aspect

- The lifestyle has changed 360 degrees. Increased income from citrus production, radish sprouts cultivation, economic crops, and livestock has led to improved housing and cultural life.
- The poor houses and lifestyle before the Saemaul Undong are nowhere to be found, and with the improvement of income, savings have increased, eliminating the harshness of the old "borrowing pass" (spring hunger period).
- Road paving has made transportation more convenient, allowing daily trips to be completed in a couple of hours, saving labor and costs, transforming the impoverished life into a prosperous village.

### 3) Production Aspect


--- (p. 974) ---

* Before the Saemaul Undong (運動), only Kimjangyong radish was cultivated, but now we process it with air to make "radish malrangi" and produce 525 tons on 120 hectares of farmland, earning 136,000 thousand won in income;
* We used to raise native Korean cattle only for farming purposes, but now we have introduced improved breeds and increased the number of cattle to 807 heads through cattle breeding;
* By improving farming practices, we have built 3 seedling greenhouses and raised 620 groups of bees, significantly boosting our income;
* We have established 90 hectares of citrus orchards and increased sweet potato production to 3,700 tons, earning 25,900 thousand won, among others;
* The income from agricultural and fishery products alone has reached 757,500 thousand won, showing a dramatic increase in production. The residents' hope to create a livestock village through the expansion of livestock farming in the vast fields continues to grow.

### 3. Residents' General Assembly (住民總會)

♦ Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (1)

* Date (日) and Time (時): 75.10.2. 18:50 ~ 20:00
* Venue (場 所): Village Community Center (會館)
* Agenda (議 題): Road Paving Project (鋪裝事業) Section Selection (區間選定)
* Attendees (參席 人員): 223 people (名)
* Chairperson (司會者): Village Head (里長)

Chairperson (司會者) Village Head (里長) (Kim Han-seok (金漢錫)): I believe that the successful completion of the road paving project from Pyoseon (表善) to Sehwa (細花) to Gasiri (加時里) as a cooperative (協同圈) project, resulting in an 8.3km revolutionary road, is due to everyone's cooperation and the strong spirit of Saemaul (精神). With the paving of the access road, we have seen an increase in bus routes in this village, from just one or two buses a day, and facilitated the smooth transportation of agricultural products, saving time and labor. Seeing our hard work, Chairman An Jae-u (安在祐), a Korean resident in Japan (在日僑胞), generously donated 40,000 thousand won for the road paving, which has motivated us even more and provided the driving force for our project.


--- (p. 975) ---

Today, we will discuss the agenda item of using the honest money (誠金) and self-funding (自體負擔) for the paving project (鋪裝事業). We will seek your opinions on the project sections (事業區間) and the methods of promotion (事業推進方法).

First, let's discuss the selection of the project sections (事業區間).
An Heung-gyu: I think it would be good to pave the unpaved village roads as part of the Saemaul Undong (事業) and the road to Je-dong Ranch (濟東牧場) via Jeungsan Road (增產道路) to expand and develop livestock production (畜產).
All attendees (參席全員) agreed.

Chairperson (司會者): We will decide to pave the village roads in Gasi-ri (加時里) and the section from Gasi to Je-dong Ranch (濟東牧場區間). Now, let's discuss the methods of promotion (事業推進方法).
Kim Gwang-chu: We will have one person from each household apply and work together at the same time to secure gravel and assist in the paving project (鋪裝事業). (53 people agreed (同意))
Oh Mun-seon: Since there are 325 households (家口), it would be good to equally divide the road (道路) and secure the required gravel (所要). (12 people agreed (同意))
Chairperson: Alright. We will decide to complete the gravel securing based on the amount each household is responsible for.
For labor mobilization (勞力動員), mobilizing one person per household for the 325 households daily would be fair and prevent misunderstandings. Moreover, for a sturdy paving (鋪裝), we should use volcanic ash soil for the subbase, and the base layer should consist of broken stones, gravel, and macadam, while the surface layer should be penetration-type asphalt. We think it would be good to receive technical support from the technical support team for any technical issues (問題). All attendees (參席人員全員) agreed and decided to follow the chairperson's opinion (司會者의意見).

Chairperson: When should we start the project?
An Woo-cheon (安又天): It would be best to start from late October before it gets colder. (All agreed (全員賛同))
Chairperson: We will start securing gravel and transporting and laying volcanic ash soil from late October. If any issues (問題點) arise, we will address them as they come. We will conclude this emergency general meeting here.

## Minutes (會議錄) (2)

**Date:** 76.6.10
**Venue:** Community Center (會舘)
**Agenda:** Settlement (決算) of Industrial Road Paving (產業道路鋪裝) (Gasi to Je-dong Ranch (濟東牧場間))
**Attendees (參席人員):** 172 people (名)

Chairperson (司會者): Although it was during the severe winter, we have completed the road paving project (道路鋪裝事業) from Gasi to Je-dong Ranch (濟東牧場間) thanks to your generous support. While promoting the project,


--- (p. 976) ---

There were countless difficulties and hardships, but now that the project has been completed, I am content, and I believe all of your hearts are even more joyful. I will now provide a concrete explanation of the paving project that has been promoted so far.

*   Section: Paving of Gashiri Inner Road and Gashiri~Noksanjang (Jeongdong Ranch)
*   Length: 9.5km, Width: 4m
*   Construction Method: Subbase - Volcanic Ash 30cm
*   Base Course: Crushed Stone, Macadam 15cm
*   Surface Course: Penetration Grade Asphalt 4cm
*   Participating Villages: 6 Natural Villages in Gashiri (325 Households, 1,653 People)
*   Construction Cost: Total 100,762,000 Won
    *   Support Fund 20,000,000 Won
    *   Overseas Korean Donation 40,000,000 Won
    *   Resident's Share 40,762,000 Won
*   Project Period: Construction Start 1975.11.3 (Surface Course 76.4.15) • Completion 76.7.10
*   Resident Participation: Total 25,400 People (80 Days per Household)
*   Donation Details: An Jae-woo, Chairman (재일(在日) 안재우 사장(社長)) 40,000,000 Won

**Project Motivation and Effects:**
a) Convenience of transportation and formation of the eastern business district to promote development
b) Development of 4,000ha meadows along the road for full utilization of farmland and livestock development
c) Formation of a sub-urban area as the focal point of the western and eastern regions of Seongsan-myeon (城山面)
d) Halving the distance to Jeju City (濟州市), saving time, labor, and opening up markets for agricultural products
e) Reducing travel time between the eastern region and Jeju City (濟州市) to within one hour and ensuring smooth traffic in the mountainous areas during the snowy season
f) Model of Saemaul Cooperation District

After reporting the above project settlement to the residents, everyone was satisfied with thunderous applause, and at this opportunity, they decided to further accelerate the Saemaul project and adjourned the temporary general meeting.

### Meeting Minutes (會議錄) (3)
*   Date: 77.1.17. 19:00~22:00
*   Venue: Community Center (마을회관(會館))
*   Agenda: Selection of Projects for President (大統領) Gift Fund and Fundraising
*   Attendees: Oh Mun-seon (吳文善) and 253 others


--- (p. 977) ---

Head of the Village, Kim Han-seok (金漢錫), who is also a Saemaul Undong (指導者) leader, takes his seat at the chairperson's seat and asks the attending residents to express their opinions on the selection of projects and the use of the funds from the 1,000,000 won (萬) donated by the President (大統領) after his visit to the village earlier this January, while also expressing his gratitude for their attendance at the temporary general assembly (臨時總會).

**O Moon-seon (吳文善):** In my opinion, although the access road (進入路), village road, and industrial road (產業道路) are fully paved, the lack of convenient transportation makes it difficult to distribute the sweet potatoes, rapeseed, tangerines, and radishes produced in our village (本里). Moreover, the distance to the market (市場) prevents us from receiving appropriate prices (價格). Therefore, I believe the most urgent task is to purchase a car (自動車) to alleviate the residents' difficulties in transporting agricultural products (農產物). Considering our village's situation, which jointly owns a thorny pasture and vast grasslands, we should purchase large agricultural machinery (農機具) to improve traditional pastures and promote livestock farming (蓄產). Additionally, joint work (共同作業) or land reclamation work will help save costs (經費節約), and purchasing a tractor (트럭타) for joint operation and management (共同運營管理) would be beneficial. Although purchasing one truck and one tractor with 1,000,000 won (萬) would require a significant amount of self-funding (自體負擔金), I believe it is necessary to use the village fund (部落基金) for this purpose.

**An Heung-gyu:** That is an excellent opinion. I agree. (Unanimously agreed without objection.)

**Head of the Village, Kim Han-seok (金漢錫):** Then, let's decide to purchase a truck and a tractor. Next, please share your thoughts on how to proceed with the purchase.

**O Guk-jeong (吳國禎):** I believe it would be best for the Head of the Village (里長) and the village development committee members (開發委員) to fully take charge and purchase them in the best possible way.

**Kim Gwang-chu (金光秋):** I agree with that opinion. (Unanimously agreed without objection.)

**Head of the Village, Kim Han-seok (金漢錫):** Then, with the project selection for the donated funds decided and the people to handle the purchase also selected, I will conclude this temporary general assembly (臨時總會).

### ♦ Minutes of the Meeting (會議錄) ⑷

Date and Time: May 11, 1977, 19:00
Number of Attendees (參席人員): 227
Agenda (會議案件): Equipment Operation (運營)

Chairperson (司會者): Thank you for attending today despite the hot weather and busy household chores. Let us now proceed to the main topic (論題) of today's meeting. First, we will decide on the truck usage fee (使用料). When using the truck in the future, we need to decide whether to charge a usage fee (使用料) or not, and if so, how much to charge.


--- (p. 978) ---

Kim Gwang-chu (金光秋): It would be appropriate to allocate around 3,000 won for a visit to the communal cemetery (共同墓地).
Voting results (擧手結果): 110 people (名) agreed (同議).
Kang Gab-jin (康甲珍): It would be better to allocate around 5,000 won per session (回).
Voting results (擧手結果): 80 people (名) agreed (同議).
Chairperson (司會者): The first proposal (案) has been agreed upon by 110 people (名), so it is decided that 3,000 won per session (回) will be allocated.
Now, how much should the rental fee (貸切) for a funeral (葬禮) be decided to be?
Kim Gwang-chu (金光秋): 15,000 won would be good.
Attendees (參席者): It was unanimously (滿場一致) adopted by all attendees (全員) that it is agreed upon (同議). However, waiting (待機) will be initially (一旦) considered as rental (貸切).
For other general (一般) working days (作業日), it will be decided (決定) according to other vehicles (車).
Chairperson (司會者): As the truck usage fee (使用料) has been decided (決定), next, we will decide (決定) on the truck driver's usage fee (使用料). Normally (平常時), it is based on time (時間), so in the village as well, it would be more accurate to base it on time (時間). All attendees (全員) agreed (同議), so it is decided (決定) that the usage fee (使用料) will be per hour (時間當).
Chairperson (司會者): For personal (個人) vehicle days (車輛日), it is currently 4,000 won per hour (時間當), so it would be better to set it proportionally (比例).
Oh Geun-hwan (吳根煥): It would be better to set it at 3,000 won per hour (時間).
An Jae-mun (安在文): It would be better to set it at 3,500 won per hour (時間).
An Jae-mun's (安在文) proposal (案) was agreed upon (贊成) by all attendees (全員), so it is decided (決定) that the fee (料金) will be 3,500 won per hour (時間當).
Chairperson (司會者): How much should the rental fee (賃貸) for a full day (大切) be decided (決定) to be?
Kim Gwang-chu (金光秋): 26,000 won would be good. (65 people (名) agreed (同議))
Oh Geun-hwan (吳根煥): 25,000 won would be appropriate. (127 people (名) agreed (同議))
Oh Geun-hwan's (吳根煥) proposal (案) was agreed upon (同議) by 127 people (名), so the rental fee (貸切) is decided (決定) to be 25,000 won, and the same will be applied to mature fields (熟田) and new fields.
Chairperson (司會者): With that, the matter of equipment (裝備) is concluded. Are there any other matters (案件) to discuss under "Others (其他)"?

### <Joint Equipment Usage Fee Collection Regulations>

**Article 1 (Purpose)** These regulations are enacted to stipulate necessary matters concerning the management and usage fees collection of the equipment (truck, tractor) owned by Ga-si-ri (加時里) (hereinafter referred to as "equipment").

**Article 2 (Management)** The equipment shall be centrally stored by the management committee chairperson (里長), who shall be responsible for its operation and management with the help of the committee members.

**Article 3 (Usage)**
1. The aforementioned equipment shall be primarily used for Ga-si-ri's joint Saemaul projects and income-generating projects.
2. If the management committee chairperson deems that the execution of the projects specified in Article 1 does not pose any obstacles, they may lease the equipment to individuals or other villages.

**Article 4 (Usage Application)**
1. Any civilian (民間人) (hereinafter referred to as "civilian") wishing to use the equipment must submit an equipment usage application form (使用申請書) in accordance with the format specified in Appendix 1 and conclude a lease agreement (賃貸借契約).

**Article 5 (Usage Decision, etc.)**
1. Upon receiving an application form as specified in Article 3, the equipment lease decision notice (決定通知書) in accordance with the format specified in Appendix 2 shall be sent to the lessee (賃借人), and the management committee member (管理委員) shall be instructed to deploy the equipment.

**Article 6 (Deployment and Retrieval of Equipment)**
1. The deployment and retrieval of the equipment must be carried out on the designated date and location as specified in the usage approval notice (使用承認通知書).
2. The management committee chairperson (管理委員長) may request the lessee (賃借人) to return the leased equipment in the following cases. The lessee must comply even before the expiration of the lease period:
   a) When the lessee violates the permitted items (許可事項).


--- (p. 980) ---

### Article 7 (Use of Equipment Loss or Damage)
1. If the lessee (賃借人) loses or damages equipment during use due to their negligence (過失), they must immediately submit a statement of reasons (事由書) to the management committee chairperson (管理委員長).
2. The lessee (賃借人) who has lost or damaged the equipment must restore it to its original condition (原狀回復) as directed by the management committee chairperson (管理委員長).
3. In the following cases (各 號), compensation (變相金) can be collected from the lessee (賃借人):
   a) When the lessee (賃借人) fails to fulfill the obligation to restore the equipment to its original condition (原狀回復) as stipulated in Article 2 (第2項)
   b) When restoration to the original condition (原狀回復) as stipulated in Article 2 (第2項) is impossible (不可能)
   c) When it is deemed inappropriate (不適當) to have the lessee (賃借人) restore the equipment to its original condition (原狀)

### Article 8 (Basis and Payment of Usage Fee)
1. Equipment usage fees (使用料) must be collected based on the criteria attached (別紙).
2. Part or all of the rental fee (賃貸料) stipulated in Article 1 (第1項) can be paid in advance (先納).
3. The calculation of the rental period (期間) for equipment rented out based on the decision in Article 3, Paragraph 2 (第3條 제2項) shall be as follows:
   a) The usage time (時間) of the equipment is based on 10 hours per day (日). However, if it is less than one day (日), the actual usage time (時間) shall be applied.
   b) Periods during which the equipment was not used due to return before the expiration of the usage period (期間) as stipulated in Article 6, Paragraph 2 (第6條 제2항), breakdowns, natural disasters (天災地變), climate conditions (氣候), or force majeure (不可抗力) shall be deducted (控除).
   c) Waiting time (待機) at the work site (現場) for work (作業) shall be considered as usage time (時間).
   d) The transportation period (期間) for equipment delivery (引渡) and return (返納) shall not be included in the usage time (時間).

### Article 9 (Settlement of Usage Fee)
If the usage period (期間) is shortened or extended after renting out the equipment, the fee must be settled (精算) based on the number of days (日數) of overuse (超過).

### Article 10 (Reduction of Usage Fee)
The usage fee (使用料) is waived (免除) when used for Ga-si-ri Saemaul Community Business (共同事業).

### Article 11 (Application)
For matters related to the collection of equipment usage fees (裝備使用料) and other matters not covered in these regulations, the regulations on the collection of equipment usage fees (裝備使用料) in Namjeju-gun (南濟州郡) shall apply (依한다).

### Supplementary Provisions
1. Date of Enforcement: This regulation shall enter into force (施行) on the day it is decided (議決) by the residents' assembly (住民總會).
